articles.title: Today I learned a single Google Gemini query uses about five drops of water, but that's not the whole truth
articles.text:
Today I learned a single Google Gemini query uses about five drops of water, but that's not the whole truth
Google's per-prompt figure skips the water power plants use
Asking Gemini to rewrite your email costs about five drops of water. At least, that's what Google says.
In an August 2025 technical paper, the company estimated that a median Gemini Apps text prompt uses 0.24 Wh of energy, emits 0.03 grams of CO2 equivalent and consumes 0.26 mL of water.
Google compared the energy use to watching TV for less than nine seconds. It also claimed that over a 12-month period, the energy and carbon footprint of a median prompt fell by 33x and 44x respectively. Those are big efficiency gains, assuming the math holds up.
A technically correct figure
Credit where it's due, Google's method counts more than most. Alongside the AI chips themselves, it includes host CPUs and memory, idle machines kept on standby, plus data center overhead like cooling. If you count only active TPUs and GPUs, the numbers drop to 0.10 Wh and 0.12 mL, which Google itself calls an underestimate.
By Google's own breakdown, the AI accelerators account for 58% of the energy behind each prompt. Host CPUs and memory take another 24%, with spare capacity and data center overhead making up the remaining 18%.
The catch is in the water. Google's figure covers only the water consumed on-site to cool its data centers, calculated from its 2024 fleetwide average. The fine print also notes that the data hasn't been verified by an independent third party.
Reading the fine print
Power plants drink water too, for cooling and for making the steam that spins their turbines. That's the part Google skipped, according to Shaolei Ren, a UC Riverside associate professor whose research the paper cited. "They're just hiding the critical information," Ren told an interviewer.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Google said its five drops were far below a previous estimate of about 50 mL per prompt drawn from Ren's work. But Ren says his figure already included that off-site water. His 2023 study estimated GPT-3 consumed a 500 mL bottle of water for every 10 to 50 medium-length responses, depending on when and where it ran.
That off-site share is far from a rounding error. A 2024 Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory report found the water used to generate electricity for US data centers in 2023 was about 12 times what they used for cooling. Meta, the only hyperscaler that discloses this figure, puts its own indirect water use at more than 20 times its direct use.
Ren and Alex de Vries-Gao, founder of Digiconomist, also took issue with Google comparing its median prompt against their averages. Both argued Google should have reported location-based emissions, which reflect the actual power grid near each data center, rather than market-based figures that credit its clean energy purchases.
Then there's scale. The Gemini app passed 1 billion monthly active users in August 2026. Meanwhile, Google's latest environmental report shows its total water consumption rose 34% to 10.9 billion gallons in 2025.
Five drops per prompt might be technically accurate. It just isn't the number that matters most.

Ritoban Mukherjee is a tech and innovations journalist from West Bengal, India. These days, most of his work revolves around B2B software, such as AI website builders, VoIP platforms, and CRMs, among other things. He has also been published on Tom's Guide, Creative Bloq, IT Pro, Gizmodo, Quartz, and Mental Floss.

articles.title: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
articles.text:
The suspected Chinese advanced persistent threat (APT) group behind the sophisticated EggStreme malware has rebuilt its toolkit as it continues to target government organizations in the Philippines.
"When attackers are exposed, the cheap response is to rotate," Bitdefender said in a technical report shared with The Hacker News. "A file hash changes with every recompile, a domain costs a few dollars, and a new IP address costs less."
"The EggStreme operators did more than rotate – the agent we now see uses a different network protocol, has an enhanced command set, and comes in a passive variant that never beacons out. The infrastructure appears to be moving away from the one certificate authority that tied its older servers together."
The end result is that the changes allow it to bypass static signatures and heuristic detections built around the EggStreme malware framework when it was first exposed in September 2025.
Delivered via an as-yet-unknown initial access vector, EggStreme's defining characteristic is the use of DLL sideloading to execute payloads. It features multiple components as follows -
- EggStremeFuel (aka RawCookie), which conducts system profiling and deploys EggStremeLoader
- EggStremeLoader, which sets up persistence and decrypts and executes EggStremeReflectiveLoader
- EggStremeReflectiveLoader, which executes EggStremeAgent
- EggStremeAgent (aka Gorem RAT), the core component and a full-featured backdoor that enables system reconnaissance, lateral movement, data theft via an injected keylogger called EggStremeKeylogger, and reverse shell and file upload/download capabilities via a secondary backdoor called EggStremeWizard
It's worth noting that some components of the framework, such as EggStremeFuel and EggStremeLoader, have been put to use by another cluster tracked by Palo Alto Networks as CL-STA-1048 between March and September 2025.
Martin Zugec, technical solutions director at Bitdefender, told The Hacker News that CL-STA-1048's targeting of a Southeast Asian government entity and its associated tooling is "consistent with what we have observed" but emphasized that their research is more focused on the malware's capabilities and its evolution rather than attribution.
As is often the case with Chinese-aligned activity, the same tools can be used by more than one threat actor, Zugec noted, adding they have not compared infrastructure or victim data to determine if the two sets of activity constitute the same threat cluster as CL-STA-1048.
The latest findings from Bitdefender show a significant retooling of EggStreme's capabilities, including removing the keylogger from every agent build observed since then. Within two weeks after public disclosure, the threat actors are also said to have made other changes -
- The method EggStremeFuel uses to protect its configuration
- EggStremeLoader's cryptography and payload format, moving from RC4 to RC5 and to a custom cipher by the end of October 2025
- Added commands in EggStremeAgent that facilitate Active Directory reconnaissance, Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) querying, TCP traffic forwarding, and execution of PowerShell, Portable Executable (PE), .NET assembly payloads
- Moving from a single certificate authority to campaign-specific certificate authorities
In addition, where lateral movement previously relied on Impacket-like tooling and on EggStremeAgent itself, newer incidents make use of an unmanaged system that sits outside of the organization's endpoint management but is still reachable by other workstations to stage the payloads and launch them via DLL sideloading using a Visual Basic Script (VBScript) file remotely run over Server Message Block (SMB).
Exactly how the operators gain access to the target is still unclear. "Our first investigation began with a logon script on a network share, and we could not determine how that script got there," Zugec said. "In the later activity we analyzed, the operators used valid credentials and a script staged on a host that the organization did not manage. That tells us how they moved once inside, not how they got in."
Some of the newer builds have been found to run in passive mode by opening a listening port and waiting for the operator to connect in as opposed to contacting an external command-and-control (C2) server.
Bitdefender also noted that there is no evidence at this stage to indicate EggStremeWizard has been discontinued by the attackers.
"The newer EggStremeAgent samples we analyzed do not show whether it is still being deployed because it is not part of the agent," Zugec said. "EggStremeWizard was an additional tool used alongside EggStremeAgent, not the primary implant, and the framework works without it. The keylogger is a separate component. Its absence from the newer agent builds reflects what the operators chose to compile into those builds, so we do not interpret its absence as evidence that the tool has been retired."
There is also some evidence that the attackers have also targeted Taiwan, but it has been treated with low to medium confidence.
"The speed of the loader changes says as much about the operators' maturity as about the cost of exposure," Bitdefender concluded. "The build-time design appears to be what makes rebuilds this fast. What they did not change is how they operate: sideloaded DLLs under system library names, staging through file shares, running from memory, and requiring mutual TLS."
Mustang Panda Targets Philippine Government Using ASEAN Summit Lures
As of late October 2026, Philippine government officials have also been targeted by Mustang Panda, a prolific China-aligned cyber espionage group, using ASEAN Summit lures to deliver PlugX using established tactics like DLL sideloading.
| Mustang Panda attack chain | 
"The package impersonated a Laos–Philippines bilateral meeting agenda from the Lao Ministry of Foreign Affairs," Dream Research Labs said in a report published last week.
"It named five officials and referenced plausible diplomatic priorities, requesting that the reader provide confirmation before the summit. Behind it was a delivery chain that installed PlugX remote-access malware while displaying the decoy agenda."
Earth Alux Uses Stealthy Tradecraft to Strike Southeast Asia
The disclosure comes as a China-nexus threat actor tracked as Earth Alux (aka Ink Dragon, Jewelbug, REF7707, and UAT-11587) has been attributed to a fresh set of attacks targeting Southeast Asian government entities since at least July 2025. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has assigned the activity the designation TGR-STA-0049 (formerly CL-STA-0049).
"The defining signature of the threat actor behind the activity is the targeting of government entities, combined with the use of advanced custom payloads that are designed for high-stealth intelligence collection operations, with an emphasis on evading security detection tools," Unit 42 researcher Tom Fakterman said.
Attacks mounted by the group have historically deployed an advanced backdoor known as FINALDRAFT (aka Squidoor) since 2023. However, it has since expanded its malware arsenal to include two previously undocumented remote access trojans (RATs) called PerfectPioneer RAT (in July 2025) and KUKURAT (in March 2026).
Initial access to target networks is achieved via exploitation of vulnerable, unpatched Microsoft Exchange servers to deploy web shells like ASPXSpy and Godzilla, which are then used to deploy the RAT payloads. Alternatively, Earth Alux has leveraged phishing emails using decoy PDFs and lookalike domains to compromise victim hosts.
PerfectPioneer RAT is a Go-based malware that's launched via three different methods -
- DLL sideloading to launch a malicious DLL that reads, decrypts and executes XOR-encrypted shellcode containing the RAT
- Decoy installers for Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect that installs the legitimate program but also writes the malware to disk and executes it in the background
- Disguising executable files as PDF documents in phishing emails that, once launched, opens a decoy PDF document while the malware is launched in the background
The malware supports a number of features that enable the operator to gain remote control of the infected host. It facilitates file operations, shell execution, process management, keylogging, SOCKS5 proxy, screenshot capture, Window enumeration and manipulation, and CPU and memory utilization monitoring.
| PerfectPioneer RAT execution chain | 
It also ensures a connection to the C2 server remains active at all times and systematically cleans up temporary files and runs garbage collection if memory usage exceeds 100 MB to minimize forensic traces.
Furthermore, select variants of the malware come with an "isDangerousCommand" feature to avoid running administrative commands that would be highly destructive or noisy, thereby allowing it to be detected by security programs installed on the host. These include rm, curl | bash, wget | bash, and powershell -e, among others.
KUKURAT, in contrast, functions as a modular implant that's executed in networks already compromised by PerfectPioneer RAT. Written in C++, the backdoor implements its functionality as a separate DLL module that's loaded dynamically at runtime directly from the C2 server.
This allows the malware to be highly evasive and adapt its capabilities on the fly in response to shifting operational objectives. It supports the following features -
- Send system information and receive a configuration from the C2 server
- Take screenshots
- Log keystrokes
- Enumerate and terminate processes
- Perform file operations
- Execute shell commands via cmd.exe and PowerShell
- Conduct lateral movement via PsExec
- Carry out SMB credential brute-forcing
- Run Beacon Object Files (BOF)
- Facilitate local privilege elevation
- Ensure the malware remains active by means of a standalone watchdog executable
What's more, KUKURAT initiates bogus, legitimate-looking activity on the endpoint to camouflage and cover up its tracks based on a command issued by the threat actor. This includes -
- Generate 10 decoy HTTP requests per operational cycle to randomly selected domains that are extracted from a hard-coded list of 15 popular websites using randomly generated URL paths with an aim to blend C2 communications
- Mimic legitimate Google Chrome browser behavior by writing random data to the registry path HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome\BrowserCrashRecovery, reading the data back, and deleting the key
- Create temporary files with random names and randomized content inside the system %temp% directory, and delete them
"Both PerfectPioneer RAT and KUKURAT use HTTP/3 as the primary method for communicating with C2 infrastructure," Unit 42 said. "While the adoption of HTTP/3 is rare across the broader malware landscape, its deployment in this campaign reflects an emerging trend among advanced threat actors."
The attacks have also been found to leverage established tools like PsExec, WMI, and Windows Remote Management (WinRM) to move laterally across compromised enterprise networks; collect credentials using Mimikatz, ProcDump, and SharpDPAPI; compromise Domain Controllers to deploy KUKURAT on local endpoints; and exfiltrate sensitive data such as files and emails.
"Through the deployment of KUKURAT and the PerfectPioneer RAT, the attackers behind this activity are actively evolving to stay ahead of traditional network defenses by implementing protocol-level evasion via HTTP/3 and QUIC over UDP," Unit 42 concluded.
"What makes this group particularly evasive is the extensive effort invested in maintaining operational security and remaining hidden on compromised endpoints. The group demonstrates a mature understanding of modern defensive ecosystems. They have even gone so far as to embed hard-coded administrative safety switches within their binaries to prevent their own operators from running loud or destructive commands that might trigger security alerts."

articles.title: Qwant, Shadow, EUSP et OVHcloud unissent leurs forces pour bâtir une IA européenne de bout en bout
articles.text:
Chez Qwant, les réponses flash reposent désormais sur Olala mini, un modèle français qui traite trois millions de requêtes par jour. Une première réalisation concrète pour une alliance qui entend réunir toutes les compétences nécessaires au développement d'une IA européenne, de la recherche web à la puissance de calcul.
Un modèle de langage français, un index web européen, des infrastructures GPU souveraines… Les ingrédients pour bâtir une IA moins dépendante des géants américains étaient déjà là ; ne restait plus qu'à les réunir. C'est tout l'objet du partenariat technologique et commercial qu'officialisent, ce jeudi 19 novembre, Qwant, Shadow, European Search Perspective (EUSP) et OVHcloud, et qui pourrait bien changer la donne pour l'autonomie numérique de l'UE.
De l'index web aux GPU, une alliance pour bâtir une IA européenne
Pour donner corps à cette ambition, EUSP, la coentreprise créée par Qwant et Ecosia, apporte son index web indépendant, développé et exploité en Europe, auquel les modèles d'IA peuvent accéder grâce à Staan, son service de recherche par API. OVHcloud fournit quant à elle les modèles de langage conçus par son laboratoire OVHai LLM, ainsi que les services permettant de les exploiter.
À leurs côtés, Shadow mobilise Blade, sa plateforme de services GPU dédiée à l'entraînement et à l'exécution des modèles d'IA, dont les capacités profitent déjà au moteur de recherche Qwant. Un rapprochement entre acteurs déjà étroitement liés, puisque Qwant et Shadow appartiennent au groupe Synfonium, dont Octave et Miroslaw Klaba, les cofondateurs d'OVHcloud, sont les actionnaires majoritaires.
Au-delà de cette répartition des rôles, le partenariat prévoit également de croiser les catalogues de modèles proposés par OVHcloud et Blade. Les utilisateurs et utilisatrices de Blade auront ainsi accès aux grands modèles open-weight de plus de 70 milliards de paramètres proposés par OVHcloud, aux différentes versions d'Olala et aux modèles de transcription audio de Gladia.
À l'inverse, les modèles compacts open-weight exécutés sur les GPU de Shadow rejoindront OVH AI Endpoints, le service d'OVHcloud permettant d'exploiter des modèles d'IA via une API. Tous ces modèles seront hébergés et exécutés dans les datacenters européens d'OVHcloud. Un choix qui permet de maîtriser leur exploitation sans garantir une indépendance technologique totale, puisque l'offre comprend également des modèles développés hors d'Europe et qu'Olala mini a lui-même été entraîné sur des GPU NVIDIA.
Cette coopération est déjà à l'œuvre chez Qwant, dont la fonctionnalité de réponse flash, affichée en tête des résultats de recherche, repose désormais sur Olala mini 7A1B, exécuté sur Blade. D'après les partenaires, le modèle traite trois millions de requêtes par jour, avec des réponses 20 % plus rapides et des coûts de fonctionnement divisés par trois par rapport à la solution précédemment utilisée. OVHai LLM s'était également appuyée sur Blade AI Fabric, le service de calcul GPU à la demande de Shadow, pour la phase d'apprentissage par renforcement d'Olala.
Un index européen pour connecter les modèles d'IA au web
Si les modèles de langage savent produire du texte à partir des connaissances acquises pendant leur entraînement, ils ont besoin de sources extérieures pour répondre à des questions portant sur des événements récents. Grâce à Staan, les modèles d'OVHai LLM, accessibles via OVH AI Endpoints, pourront donc interroger le web et récupérer des informations actualisées pour enrichir leurs réponses.
Staan propose pour cela plusieurs API permettant de rechercher des pages web et d'en récupérer le contenu. Les modèles peuvent ainsi produire des réponses fondées sur des informations récentes et accompagnées de leurs sources, selon une approche appelée RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), qui consiste à fournir à une IA des documents externes récupérés au moment de la requête pour alimenter sa réponse.
Cette capacité doit aussi profiter à OVH AI Agents, la nouvelle plateforme de création d'agents IA d'OVHcloud, dont l'ouverture en version alpha est prévue pour décembre 2026. Grâce à Staan, les agents pourront rechercher des informations sur le web et les exploiter dans l'exécution de leurs tâches.

articles.title: Un jugador consiguió que su esposa firmara un acuerdo para dedicar diez días a GTA 6
articles.text:
El documento establece restricciones sobre interrupciones, tareas domésticas y conversaciones mientras el jugador completa misiones de GTA 6.
Algunos usuarios han empezado a organizar sus actividades al rededor del lanzamiento de GTA 6. Ese es el caso de Julian Tay, un youtuber de Singapur que decidió tomar una medida poco habitual: conseguir que su esposa, Lisa Chan, firmara un documento que le permitirá jugar durante diez días sin interrupciones.
La historia se hizo viral después de que Tay compartiera un video en redes sociales en el que muestra cómo le presenta el acuerdo a su pareja. Antes de entregarle el documento, el creador de contenido le explicó algunos detalles de la franquicia, sus personajes y los acontecimientos de los videojuegos anteriores.
Durante la conversación, le recordó cuánto tiempo llevaba esperando esta entrega y expresó: “He esperado 13 años”. Después de esa introducción, le presentó el contrato para que lo firmara.
Según se puede ver en las publicaciones que compartió, el periodo autorizado comprende del 19 al 29 de noviembre de 2026. Durante esos diez días, Tay podrá dedicar tiempo al videojuego sin que su esposa interrumpa sus partidas.
Las condiciones que debe cumplir la pareja durante GTA 6
El documento establece varias reglas que buscan garantizar que el jugador pueda concentrarse en las misiones. Una de las principales condiciones indica que Lisa no deberá distraerlo mientras esté realizando una actividad dentro del videojuego.
El acuerdo también contempla situaciones particulares. Si Tay pierde una misión, es arrestado o termina borracho dentro del mundo virtual, tendrá un tiempo para recuperarse antes de continuar jugando.
Otra de las cláusulas prohíbe temporalmente algunas expresiones que podrían interrumpir su experiencia, como “Es solo un juego” o “¿No has jugado suficiente?”.
Además, las actividades habituales de pareja, como los abrazos, los besos y las conversaciones, deberán esperar hasta que el jugador termine una misión o encuentre un momento adecuado para detenerse. Las tareas domésticas también quedan sujetas a estas condiciones durante el periodo establecido.
Aunque el contrato está planteado como una broma, su contenido refleja la expectativa que existe alrededor del nuevo título de Rockstar Games.
Las críticas que recibió la pareja en redes sociales
Después de publicar el video, Julian Tay y Lisa Chan recibieron comentarios de usuarios que cuestionaron el acuerdo. Algunos interpretaron las condiciones como una señal de problemas en su relación e incluso recomendaron a la mujer terminar el matrimonio.
Ante las reacciones, el youtuber explicó que el documento forma parte del humor que comparte habitualmente con su esposa y que muchas personas interpretaron la situación de manera demasiado seria.
También aclaró que los diez días no significan que abandonará sus responsabilidades familiares y laborales. De hecho, la pareja tiene previsto participar en una actividad de escalada durante ese periodo.
Cuando le preguntaron si su esposa tendría la oportunidad de disfrutar de un tiempo similar para realizar alguna actividad sin interrupciones, Tay respondió que estaría dispuesto a firmar otro acuerdo. Incluso mencionó la posibilidad de que Lisa organice un retiro de yoga.
La expectativa por el lanzamiento de GTA 6
El caso refleja el impacto que genera la próxima entrega de Grand Theft Auto entre los seguidores de la franquicia. GTA 6 llegará después de más de una década desde el lanzamiento de GTA V, publicado originalmente en 2013.
El nuevo videojuego de Rockstar Games trasladará a los jugadores a Leonida, un estado ficticio inspirado en Florida, con Vice City como uno de sus principales escenarios.
La expectativa también está relacionada con las novedades en su mundo abierto, los personajes protagonistas y las posibilidades de interacción. Para algunos seguidores, la llegada del título representa un acontecimiento que merece reservar varios días en el calendario.

articles.title: 8BitDo Unveils GameCube-Inspired Controller for Switch 2 and PC
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
8BitDo Unveils GameCube-Inspired Controller for Switch 2 and PC
8BitDo has unveiled the GC Bluetooth Gamepad, a GameCube-inspired controller for the Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, and Windows PCs. It keeps the shape of the original and the same ABXY button layout, along with a matte finish and a familiar shell texture. The controller measures 140.1 x 102.95 x 67.6 mm and weighs 218.1 grams. The joysticks are TMR with octagonal gates and a 10-bit ADC sampling chip. 8BitDo's goal was to deliver precise directional input while keeping the eight-direction movement of the original GameCube stick. The triggers use Hall Effect sensors, and the Z and ZL shoulder buttons have a symmetrical layout.
The rest of the feature list covers a classic D-pad, a single-rotor rumble motor, a Capture button for screenshots and gameplay recording, and a Turbo function. Connectivity includes Bluetooth 5.0, 2.4 GHz wireless, and wired USB-C. Bluetooth is supported on the Nintendo Switch, while the 2.4 GHz and wired modes work with both Switch consoles and Windows PCs. 8BitDo offers the GC Bluetooth Gamepad in Orange and Purple editions, both priced at $49.99.

articles.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years
articles.text:
On AMD-based PCs and some Intel PCs, the TPM lockout for Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs can be reset by someone who opens the PC's case, researchers at Technische Universität Berlin say.
That leaves short PINs open to guessing. In lab tests, the researchers found a four-digit Hello PIN on an AMD laptop and a 6-digit BitLocker PIN on an Intel laptop this way.
Both PINs were set by the researchers and found within 236 tries. From the speeds they measured, they calculate a worst-case of 40 hours for a four-digit Hello PIN, compared to 69 days with the lockout working as documented. For a default six-digit BitLocker PIN, the worst-case time drops from 19 years to 20 days.
AMD confirmed yesterday that its processor firmware has a flaw that allows the attack on some PCs with its chips. It plans fixes for most of those chips between November and February 2027. For now, the researchers advise adding at least two digits to Hello and BitLocker PINs.
The TPM in these PCs is a firmware TPM, built into the processor. Unlike a separate TPM chip, it has no secure storage of its own, according to the research paper the researchers posted late last week. So it keeps its saved state, including the count of wrong guesses, encrypted on the mainboard's flash chip.
If someone copies that saved state and later writes the old copy back, the count goes back too, unless the PC detects it. Newer PCs try to catch this with counters inside the flash chip, called RPMC, that can only go up.
On AMD PCs that use these counters, the processor's firmware never verifies that a counter actually increased. A small board placed between the processor and the flash chip can block the update and report success, causing the PC to accept the old state.
RPMC chips from flash maker Winbond have a different weakness, the researchers found. A brief drop in the chip's power supply, called a voltage glitch, can cause the chip to reveal the secret key that signs its counter values. With that key, which took about a second to extract with their best settings, the board can forge any counter value.
On the Intel laptop they tested, one glitch was enough: the laptop's firmware feeds the chip the same value at every boot, so the leaked key kept working after each restart.
For the Hello test, the researchers attacked a locked HP OmniBook 3 with an AMD Ryzen AI 5 330 processor and a BitLocker-encrypted drive. Their setup typed PINs from 1000 upward and reached the correct one, 1235, after 236 tries in 57 minutes.
Windows still forced a restart after every 5 incorrect PIN attempts on that laptop, but no lockout delay was applied. Microsoft's lockout defaults lock the TPM after 32 wrong tries and forget one failure every 10 minutes.
The BitLocker test ran on a Framework Laptop 13 with an Intel Core Ultra 5 125H processor and Winbond flash. BitLocker's startup prompt adds no limit of its own, so each reset gave a fresh 32 tries. The setup found the PIN, 123457, after 236 tries in 6 minutes and 55 seconds.
In both tests, the researchers took the flash chip off the mainboard and wired in their own board. A script read the screen, typed PINs, and restarted the laptop through a KVM switch. They also changed firmware settings to slow each laptop's link to the flash chip, because their board could not keep up at full speed.
The researchers make two further claims that their tests did not cover. Either method could be used against either PIN. A recovered Hello PIN can also unlock keys tied to the device and enable Hello-based single sign-on at work, and, in some configurations, pass a multi-factor check.
The researchers have published their attack firmware, board designs, and scripts. They say reproducing the RPMC attacks is not plug-and-play and needs one of their boards. Neither the paper nor the vendor notices published so far describe attacks outside the lab.
Which PCs the Attack Works On and What Vendors Say
Whether the attack works depends on the processor and the flash chip:
- AMD-based PCs with RPMC flash: open to the board that blocks counter updates. The chipmaker has confirmed the firmware flaw behind this and plans to fix it.
- AMD-based PCs without RPMC flash: on two AMD desktops in the researchers' tests, writing an old copy back with an ordinary flash programmer reset the count, requiring no board. They conclude that AMD processors likely have no other protection against this, though two desktops may not be representative of all AMD systems.
- PCs that rely on Winbond RPMC flash: the researchers say these are open to the leaked-key method whatever the processor, and that only a new chip design can fix it.
- Intel PCs without RPMC-like flash: three Intel systems detected the same write-back in those tests.
The researchers expect the AMD firmware flaw to affect AMD PCs that use the Microsoft Pluton security core as their TPM, but did not show this.
On an AMD PC, the owner can boot Linux, for example from a live USB stick, and run the command grep . /sys/bus/pci/drivers/ccp/*/rpmc_* from the researchers' exposure check. The output indicates whether RPMC flash is present and enabled, which tells the owner which of the two methods applies. Missing files do not mean the PC lacks RPMC.
For Intel PCs, the researchers know of no such check. Owners would have to open the PC and look for a Winbond chip marked 25R or 74M.
AMD tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-43613 and assigns it a CVSS score of 5.1 in a security bulletin published yesterday.
The chipmaker says attacks requiring physical access fall outside its product security threat model, but that "RPMC is intended to stop this type of interposer attack." The researchers first told it about the flaw in February.
The chipmaker's fix targets run from November to February 2027 across Ryzen, Ryzen AI, Ryzen Threadripper, Athlon and EPYC chips, and one unnamed product has no date yet. These are planned dates for its own firmware, not updates already out for PCs.
The bulletin does not cover AMD PCs without RPMC flash. It also does not say whether the update will prevent an attacker from installing older, unfixed firmware on the PC, which the researchers say a fix must prevent.
Intel, whose processor was in the BitLocker test laptop, said in a security announcement earlier this week that the research "did not demonstrate a vulnerability in an Intel component". That matches the tests, in which the attack on the Intel laptop needed the Winbond chip's flaw.
According to the researchers, Intel's security team called the reused value a weakness rather than a vulnerability.
The researchers told Microsoft in April. According to them, the company rated the Windows Hello report as "moderate severity" and below its bar for an immediate fix, issued no CVE or bounty, and committed to raising its recommended minimum Hello PIN length to six digits.
At the company's request, the researchers filed the BitLocker finding as a separate report for a different team. The company declined to give them any further written statement for the paper.
Separately, a Windows 11 test build released late last week makes six digits the minimum for personal-account Hello PINs, with an option to use four. The release notes give no reason, and features in that test channel may never reach regular releases.
According to the researchers, Winbond was first told about its chips' weakness to voltage glitches in January 2025 and received a second report in April showing that a glitch also leaks the key. The flash maker is studying the issue, possibly including a new chip design, but has not committed to a fix or a date.
What Owners and Admins Can Do
Two extra digits make a large difference in the researchers' figures:
| Worst-case time to find a numeric PIN |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| PIN length | With the documented lockout | Hello attack (AMD laptop) | BitLocker attack (Intel laptop) | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 digits | 69 days | 40 hours | 5 hours* | 
| 6 digits | 19 years | 168 days | 20 days | 
| 8 digits | 1,903 years | 46 years | 6 years | 
* BitLocker accepts a four-digit PIN only if an admin lowers the six-digit minimum. The times are worst cases calculated from speeds measured on one laptop each.
In May, Microsoft advised moving BitLocker from TPM-only to TPM+PIN to block the YellowKey bypass, as part of its YellowKey mitigation. The same TPM lockout guards that PIN.
Steps for each setup:
- Windows Hello for Business: raise the Minimum PIN length policy, under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > PIN Complexity. If it is not set, Windows requires six digits, a worst case of 168 days in the table above, and admins can set it as low as four. The PIN policy settings page lists it on the PIN settings tab.
- BitLocker: raise the Configure minimum PIN length for startup policy, which allows 4 to 20 digits and requires six by default. Turning on "Allow enhanced PINs for startup" lets letters and symbols, which the BitLocker PIN guidance recommends for older hardware.
- AMD-based PCs: install the firmware update with the chipmaker's fix when one is available for your PC. Until then, the chipmaker advises keeping PCs under physical control and watching for signs of tampering.
- PCs that rely on Winbond RPMC flash: the flash maker has not committed to a fix, according to the researchers. Intel advises its customers to ask their PC maker about updates.

articles.title: La CNIL inflige 5 millions d’euros d’amende à la Macif
articles.text:
Macif Vie stockait en clair les mots de passe d’environ 1,8 million de clients, et la CNIL lui a infligé 5 millions d’euros d’amende. La filiale d’assurance-vie de la Macif conservait aussi des messages de ses clients depuis plus de treize ans.
Le rappel est parfois nécessaire. Un mot de passe stocké en clair est enregistré tel que vous l’avez tapé. Normalement, le site le transforme en une suite de caractères illisible, impossible à retraduire, et compare cette empreinte à chaque connexion. La CNIL ne nomme pas l’assureur dans sa délibération publiée le 18 novembre, mais l’agence spécialisée Mlex avait révélé l’identité de Macif Vie dès l’audience du 15 octobre, et la Macif a reconnu auprès de BFM Tech être concernée. Macif Vie paiera autant que France Travail, sanctionné en janvier après le vol des données de 36,8 millions de personnes, alors que l’assureur n’a subi aucune fuite connue. Mais il a mis près de deux ans à protéger correctement les mots de passe de ses clients.
Macif Vie a protégé les mots de passe de ses clients deux ans après le contrôle
Alertée fin 2023, la CNIL a contrôlé Macif Vie dans ses bureaux de Niort en mai 2024. Ses agents ont trouvé environ 1,8 million de mots de passe d’accès aux espaces clients stockés en clair, dont 730 289 apparaissaient aussi dans le journal où l’assureur enregistrait chaque tentative de connexion. Si vous avez un contrat chez Macif Vie, votre mot de passe faisait peut-être partie du lot.
Deux mois plus tard, l’assureur a transformé ces mots de passe avec ora_hash, une fonction du logiciel de bases de données Oracle, mais sans sel. Pour la CNIL, cette fonction est obsolète. Depuis 2013, l’ANSSI recommande une fonction lente à calculer et un sel, c’est-à-dire une valeur aléatoire ajoutée à chaque mot de passe. Avec ces deux protections, le voleur d’une base de données doit tester les mots de passe un par un, sans pouvoir s’aider de tables de correspondance calculées à l’avance. Macif Vie n’est passée à Argon2, avec un sel, que le 25 avril 2026, après avoir reçu le rapport de sanction. La CNIL recommande cette fonction dans son guide pour les développeurs.
L’assureur a fait valoir qu’aucun incident de sécurité n’avait compromis ces données. Pour la formation restreinte, l’organe de la CNIL chargé des sanctions, ces mots de passe en clair rendaient vulnérables toutes les informations des espaces clients, parfois financières, « peu important que cette vulnérabilité ait été exploitée ou non par un attaquant ».
Huit salariés se partageaient aussi un seul compte pour consulter la base des 1,3 million de clients titulaires d’un contrat d’assurance-vie en cours. Avec ce mot de passe commun, impossible de savoir qui avait consulté, modifié ou supprimé une donnée.
Macif Vie gardait les messages de ses clients depuis 2010
Depuis leur espace personnel, les clients de Macif Vie écrivent à leur gestionnaire grâce à un formulaire de contact. L’assureur gardait tous ces messages et leurs pièces jointes dans sa base active, y compris après la fin du contrat. Le plus ancien datait du 27 novembre 2010, et certains clients avaient tapé leur IBAN complet dans leur message. Une fois la demande traitée, Macif Vie aurait dû anonymiser ces données, les archiver si la loi l’exigeait, ou les supprimer.
Le journal des connexions remontait jusqu’en 2003, alors que l’assureur avait prévu de l’effacer au bout d’un an. Il contenait encore les mots de passe de 8 628 clients, enregistrés depuis juillet 2019. Macif Vie s’est montrée « à tout le moins, particulièrement négligente », tranche la CNIL.
L’assureur a purgé ces historiques en juillet 2024, et il efface aujourd’hui les messages du formulaire au bout d’un mois. Grâce à ces corrections, la CNIL ne lui a imposé aucune injonction sous astreinte. Son rapporteur avait d’abord réclamé une amende de 9 millions d’euros, calculée sur le chiffre d’affaires du groupe Macif, puis de 7 millions. Il demandait aussi que la décision nomme l’assureur pendant deux ans. La Macif a contesté cette publicité au nom de sa réputation et de la confiance de ses épargnants, et la CNIL a publié sa délibération sans la nommer, « à des fins pédagogiques ». Pour l’autorité, il est surtout « important de rappeler aux acteurs économiques les règles applicables en la matière ».
La Macif se dit « attachée au respect de la protection des données de ses clients ». « Nous tenons à rassurer nos clients sur le fait qu’aucune de leurs données n’a été divulguée », ajoute l’assureur. Il peut encore contester l’amende devant le Conseil d’État, dans un délai de deux mois.

articles.title: GTA 6 en Google: Argentina, Brasil y Chile entre los más “obsesionados” por saber cuándo sale
articles.text:
Países Bajos encabeza la lista de naciones más “obsesionadas” con GTA VI en el mundo, según un análisis de búsquedas en Google. Con el lanzamiento del juego fijado para el 19 de noviembre de 2026, el interés se multiplica en distintas regiones luego de 13 años de espera desde el último título de la saga.
El estudio, elaborado por ActionNetwork.com, midió el promedio mensual de búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes en 150 países, entre los que se destacan Chile y Argentina para nuestra región. Para ello combinó cuatro términos de búsqueda: GTA VI, GTA 6, Grand Theft Auto VI y Grand Theft Auto 6, a partir de datos de Google Keyword Planner correspondientes a los últimos 12 meses.
El top 10 mundial de interés por GTA VI
Los Países Bajos lideran el ranking con 2,045 búsquedas mensuales por cada 100 mil habitantes, equivalentes a 369,900 búsquedas totales sobre una población de 18.1 millones. Francia ocupa el segundo lugar con 1,594 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes, y Finlandia completa el podio con 1,514.
El resto del top 10 se compone de Suiza (1,490), Bélgica (1,483), Reino Unido (1,469), Polonia (1,436), Alemania (1,386), Suecia (1,378) e Irlanda (1,362). La totalidad de las diez primeras posiciones corresponde a países europeos.
Para calcular el ranking, se dividió el total de búsquedas combinadas por la población de cada país y se multiplicó por 100 mil. Esa metodología per cápita explica por qué naciones con poca población, como los Países Bajos, superan a países con mercados mucho más grandes en volumen absoluto de búsquedas.
El interés de búsqueda por GTA VI, medido en búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes, indica qué tan intensa es la curiosidad de una población hacia el juego en relación con su tamaño, no cuántas copias comprará. Por eso los Países Bajos, con apenas 18 millones de habitantes, superan a mercados mucho más grandes como Estados Unidos.
Aunque Estados Unidos registra el mayor número absoluto de búsquedas mensuales del mundo, con 3,066,500, al dividir esa cifra entre su población cae hasta el puesto 22 del ranking per cápita, con 897 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes.
El patrón se repite con otros mercados grandes. Brasil aparece segundo en volumen total con 1,317,900 búsquedas mensuales, seguido de Alemania (1,157,400), Francia (1,095,400) y Reino Unido (1,021,100). India, pese a sus 943,900 búsquedas mensuales, queda en el puesto 106 del ranking per cápita debido a su enorme población.
Cómo quedaron los países de Latinoamérica
Entre los países de habla hispana, España es el que muestra mayor interés relativo, con 1,166 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes, lo que lo ubica en el puesto 14 del ranking mundial.
En América Latina, Chile encabeza la región en el puesto 28 global, con 710 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes. Le sigue Uruguay en el puesto 33, con 614 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes.
Argentina se posiciona en el lugar 35 con 561 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes, mientras que Costa Rica aparece en el puesto 40 con 452. México, pese a registrar 577,600 búsquedas totales mensuales (el séptimo volumen más alto del mundo), queda en el puesto 41 per cápita con 438 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes.
Colombia se ubica en la posición 52 con 326 búsquedas por cada 100 mil habitantes, y Perú cierra el grupo de los países más consultados de la región en el puesto 59, con 273. Más abajo en la tabla aparecen Ecuador (puesto 62, con 262), Paraguay (puesto 63, con 249) y Bolivia (puesto 73, con 182).
Qué miden realmente estas cifras
El volumen de búsquedas refleja curiosidad, no necesariamente intención de compra. Por eso el análisis aclara que las estimaciones de preventas funcionan como un indicador complementario de la demanda real del juego.
Aun con esa salvedad, el patrón geográfico resulta contundente: los cinco primeros puestos del ranking mundial están ocupados exclusivamente por países europeos, mientras que Estados Unidos, pese a generar el mayor número de búsquedas en términos absolutos, se ubica recién en el puesto 22 cuando se ajusta por población.

articles.title: AI Pentesting Checklist for Web Apps: 15 Questions to Ask Before Choosing a Vendor
articles.text:
TL;DR
- Attackers move first. On average, exploitation now starts before a patch exists (Mandiant M-Trends 2026). In 1H 2026, 23% of vulnerabilities VulnCheck added to its exploited list were hit on or before disclosure day.
- AI pentesting vendors aren't interchangeable. Most look convincing in a demo. The gaps show up in your logged-in flows, your coverage, and your production safety.
- Make them prove it on your own web apps. Score each vendor on context, reach, validated findings, guardrails, and retests.
Choosing an AI pentesting vendor? Get 15 questions, red flags, and a scorecard to test what vendors deliver, not just what they demo. Download the free checklist →
AI is speeding attackers up
For the first time, Google's Threat Intelligence Group identified a threat actor using a zero-day exploit it believes was developed with AI: a 2FA bypass rooted in a logic flaw that conventional fuzzing and static analysis can easily miss (GTIG).
Agentic pentesting can close that gap, and 87% of US security leaders surveyed are planning, piloting, or using it. Choosing the agent is the hard part.
Every Demo Looks Good. Your App Is the Real Test.
Picture three agents that all demo well. The first finds real flaws but stops at your login page. The second navigates your app but can't answer a basic question: coverage of what? The third exploits real issues but has no hard limits for production.
Each looks impressive on the vendor's target. The difference shows up on yours. A structured bake-off surfaces it before you sign.
Ask What the Agent Knows Before It Attacks
Every tester has to learn your site before the first payload. That recon is real attack work. The cost is redoing it from scratch on every engagement, when most of the map hasn't changed. In CyCognito's model, recon and analysis take 20 to 30 of a manual pentest's 63 to 95 hours.
Agents differ here. Some start from a blank URL and rebuild the map on every run. Others start from an existing model of your site and keep it current between runs. Ask which one you're buying, what carries over between runs, and whether the agent keeps discovering beyond its starting map. A starting map should be a head start, not a boundary.
Without context, an AI agent behaves like a smart scanner. With context, it can reason about your application. That changes what it finds, not just how fast. When a security researcher hunted for flaws in Apache Airflow, their AI assistant called the search a dead end. Testing how the deployment’s parts trust each other, instead of reading the code, turned up an unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-68982).
Ask for Proof, Not Suspicion
A suspicious pattern is not an exploitable vulnerability. Ask whether the agent exploits what it suspects, reproduces its findings, and hands over evidence your team can verify. A list of suspected issues is not a validated pentest.
Here is what proof looks like. During an authorized assessment of a major insurer's production website, an AI pentesting agent found that the one-time passcode request could send login codes to any email address. It proved the flaw by logging in with a code sent to its own inbox, and guardrails then stopped the test. The insurer said it had pentested the site about six months earlier (Reflectiz case study on The Hacker News).
Three Questions That Expose a Weak AI Pentesting Vendor
A demo can look convincing without proving that the agent reaches your logged-in workflows, validates what it finds, or confirms your fixes. Here are three of the 15 checks to run before you choose.
The other 12, covering starting context, coverage proof, attack chaining, access across roles, data handling, and guardrails, are in the full checklist.
Run a Bake-Off, Not a Demo
Demos run on the vendor's target. Bake-offs run on yours.
- Same target, same week. Same app, test accounts, and scope for every vendor.
- Log three timestamps. Access granted, discovery complete, first test.
- Score every check. The checklist's scoring sheet weights what matters and gates on safety.
What's Inside the Checklist
- 15 checks, each with the question to ask and the red flag
- Checks for attack chaining, roles, guardrails, and retesting
- A 36-point scorecard and a per-check scoring sheet
The best AI pentesting agent isn't the one with the best demo. It's the one that can show what it tested, prove what it found, and run safely on your application. Use these 15 questions to find it.
Download the free AI Pentesting Checklist and vendor scorecard →

articles.title: GTA 6 Reportedly Plays Best on PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S Struggles
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
GTA 6 Reportedly Plays Best on PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S Struggles
Digital Foundry has published its detailed platform comparison for GTA 6 based on over 100 hours of testing. Rockstar has officially confirmed that every console targets 30 FPS, and even the PS5 Pro misses out on a 40 FPS or 60 FPS mode. The PS5 Pro, PS5, and Xbox Series X all render at 1440p, but only the PS5 Pro reconstructs that into a 4K-like image using PSSR. The other two get a softer spatial upscale through Rockstar's own TAA. The Pro is also the only version with ray-traced shadows, while the other consoles have to make do with RT global illumination and RT reflections only. 
In DF's technical analysis, the PS5 Pro was able to hold 30 FPS across roughly 75 hours of play, briefly dropping to 24 FPS in scenes with intense explosions. The base PS5 and Xbox Series X bounce between 30 FPS and the high 20s during combat and fast traversal, but they can also dip into the low 20s in very intense scenes. DF notes that the Xbox Series X feels slightly smoother thanks to Xbox's 120 Hz VRR container. The PlayStation does not benefit from VRR at all, since it only kicks in above 48 FPS. Still, Digital Foundry's verdict is that both versions look and play well. Then there's the Xbox Series S…Xbox's "little brother" console is the hardest to recommend for Grand Theft Auto 6. It renders at 720p and uses FSR 4 to reach roughly 1080p, which also makes GTA 6 the first Xbox Series game to ship with that upscaler. As for the framerate, much of the game reportedly runs in the mid-to-high 20s, and heavy explosions can even pull it down to around 20 FPS. Some very specific scenes saw the Series S dip to the high teens momentarily. Visually, the lighting, reflections, shadows, and textures are all a step below the other consoles, and apparently pop-in is also an annoyance. PC players are still in the dark about when GTA 6 is coming to the platform, with the latest rumors pointing to a Q1 2027 window.

articles.title: The five-star Samsung 990 PRO 2TB SSD gets a massive $250 discount at Newegg ahead of Black Friday
articles.text:
The five-star Samsung 990 PRO 2TB SSD gets a massive $250 discount at Newegg ahead of Black Friday
It’s seriously fast storage for gaming and creative workloads, and now Samsung’s SSD is available with a decent discount
Samsung’s 990 PRO has been around for a few years, but it’s a sign of its quality that it remains one of the most impressive PCIe 4.0 SSDs we’ve tested.
In Newegg’s Black November sale, the 2TB model is currently available for $389.99, down from its listed price of $639.99. That’s a $250 discount on a high-performance drive that can handle gaming, video editing, and workstation workloads with ease.
Today’s best Samsung 990 PRO 2TB deal
Newegg is selling the 2TB Samsung 990 PRO for $389.99 with free shipping. That’s a 39% reduction against its advertised regular price. This is the non-heatsink version, so check that your motherboard has suitable M.2 cooling - and if you do want the heatsink version, Newegg has that on sale for $483.45.
Why we recommend the Samsung 990 PRO
The 990 PRO is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD that serves up sequential read speeds of up to 7,450MB/s and write speeds of up to 6,900MB/s. It also features 2GB of DRAM cache and Samsung’s V-NAND technology.
We awarded it five stars and a Best in Class award in our review, praising its stunning performance and reliability. Our testing recorded sequential read and write speeds of 7,465MB/s and 6,888MB/s respectively. It also transferred a 10GB folder of smaller files in just over seven seconds.
That makes it appealing for creative professionals handling large projects, although gamers should also appreciate its rapid loading times.
There are two things to consider: this is a slightly older drive that doesn’t support PCIe 5.0, so you should consider a newer SSD if you’re running tougher workloads and want to extract every ounce of speed. Also bear in mind that it can run hot under sustained workloads, so you’ll need appropriate cooling - whether that’s from the drive’s own heatsink or from your motherboard.
Read our full Samsung 990 PRO review
Price context and historical value
At $389.99, the 990 PRO is easier to justify - it’s still a premium SSD, but it’s a few years old now, and there are plenty of PCIe 5.0 models on the market.
That $250 discount is very attractive, and this drive looks even better if you don’t have a PCIe 5.0 motherboard and would rather invest in proven PCIe 4.0 technology than pay extra for bandwidth you might not use.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Samsung 990 PRO if… you want exceptionally fast PCIe 4.0 storage for gaming, video editing or demanding creative workloads.
❌ Skip the Samsung 990 PRO if… you need PCIe 5.0 performance, want a cheaper everyday storage upgrade or don’t have suitable M.2 cooling.

articles.title: GTA 6 sort à minuit : après la panne du PSN ce soir, préparez vite votre PS5
articles.text:
Des joueurs ont eu du mal à se connecter mercredi soir. Les services de Sony sont repassés au vert vers 20h30, à temps pour les derniers préparatifs sur PS5.
La soirée a commencé par des messages d’erreur sur PS5. Ce mercredi 18 novembre, les signalements visant le PlayStation Network (PSN) ont grimpé dès 18h30 sur Downdetector France, avec un pic autour de 19h. Les problèmes remontés par les joueurs concernaient surtout l’accès aux serveurs et la connexion à leur compte.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Que vérifier sur sa PS5 avant minuit ?
Sur sa page d’état, Sony a signalé des difficultés à lancer des jeux, des applications et certaines fonctions en ligne. Vers 20h30, tous les services étaient de nouveau indiqués comme opérationnels. La cause de la panne reste inconnue. Côté calendrier, Rockstar prévoit toujours de débloquer GTA 6 à minuit, dans la nuit du mercredi 18 au jeudi 19 novembre en France métropolitaine, sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S.
Si la connexion coince de nouveau, consultez la page d’état du PSN. Même si GTA 6 est déjà préchargé, vérifiez qu’il est à jour. Un deuxième patch, la version 01.002.001, est déployé depuis le 16 novembre et pèse environ 600 Mo sur PS5. Sélectionnez le jeu sur l’écran d’accueil, appuyez sur la touche Options de la manette, puis choisissez Vérifier si des mises à jour sont disponibles.
Le support PlayStation précise également que la mise à jour système 26.07-14.23.00 doit être installée pour jouer à GTA 6. Si elle ne se lance pas automatiquement, vous la trouverez dans Paramètres > Système > Logiciel système > Paramètres et mise à jour du logiciel système.

articles.title: ‘La rebelión’ de Joe Arroyo suena en GTA VI: un colombiano en la estación de radio
articles.text:
El clásico de salsa ‘La rebelión’ del colombiano, Joe Arroyo, quedó incluido en la banda sonora de Grand Theft Auto VI y suena dentro de La Ola, la estación dedicada a la salsa y la música tropical del videojuego.
El tema se volvió viral luego de que jugadores con acceso anticipado compartieran fragmentos de sus partidas antes del lanzamiento oficial, previsto para el 19 de noviembre de 2026, lo que generó sorpresa entre la comunidad latina al reconocer el himno cartagenero en las calles de Vice City y Leonida.
El hallazgo se dio en medio de la expectativa que rodea el estreno del videojuego, uno de los más esperados a nivel mundial, y puso en el centro de la conversación digital la presencia de un clásico colombiano en una producción de alcance global.
‘La rebelión’ de Joe Arroyo suena en la estación La Ola de GTA VI
Dentro de la programación musical de Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar incorporó una emisora dedicada a los sonidos latinos tradicionales llamada La Ola, que reúne clásicos de la salsa y la música tropical. Allí es donde aparece ‘La rebelión’, uno de los temas más representativos de Joe Arroyo.
El descubrimiento se hizo público a través del streamer Sebasberon, quien mientras conducía un vehículo dentro del juego sintonizó la emisora y escuchó, entre otras canciones, el tema del artista cartagenero. El momento quedó registrado en video y se difundió rápidamente entre los seguidores del videojuego y de la música colombiana.
La inclusión de ‘La rebelión’ en el repertorio de GTA VI representa la presencia de un referente de la salsa colombiana en una de las franquicias de videojuegos más influyentes del mundo, lo que explica la reacción inmediata de usuarios latinoamericanos al reconocer la canción durante las transmisiones en vivo.
La viralización del clip respondió, en gran medida, a que se trata de un lanzamiento con expectativa mundial y a que el acceso anticipado permitió a ciertos jugadores explorar contenidos del juego antes de su fecha oficial de estreno.
Qué otras canciones y estaciones integran la banda sonora de GTA VI
Además de La Ola, Rockstar difundió un listado parcial de las canciones que sonarán en cada una de las emisoras del juego. En Flash FM se confirmaron temas de Charli xcx, MGMT y la colaboración entre Zara Larsson y PinkPantheress.
Cocoteo FM, por su parte, incluirá música de Bad Bunny, un remix de Axel Rulay junto a Farruko y El Alfa, y una canción de Romeo Santos con El Chaval de la Bachata. En Back Country Radio sonarán artistas como David Allan Coe, Loretta Lynn, y el dúo conformado por Hank Williams Jr. y Waylon Jennings.
La emisora AfroBank FM contará con canciones de Asake, Pat Thomas junto a Ebo Taylor, y una colaboración entre DJ Lag, Robot Boii y Kamo Mphela. Para los seguidores del metal, The Chamber 106.6 reproducirá temas de Black Sabbath, Pantera y Slayer.
Dirty South Classics, en tanto, incluirá canciones de David Banner junto a Lil’ Flip, JT Money con Solé, y una colaboración de DJ Khaled con Trick Daddy, Rick Ross y Pitbull.
Quiénes son los famosos que presentan las estaciones de radio del juego
Rockstar sumó seis emisoras conducidas por figuras reconocidas para reforzar la identidad de cada estación dentro de GTA VI. Entre los nombres que prestan su voz aparecen Bad Bunny, bajo el personaje de El Martillo en Cocoteo FM, y RaiNao, como La Gata en esa misma emisora.
Flash FM está presentada por Robyn y Alex Consani, mientras que Dirty South Classics es conducida por Trick Daddy y Trina. En AfroBank FM, la conducción corre por cuenta de Burna Boy y Palms Trax, y Back Country Radio tiene como presentadores a Morgan Wallen y Lana Del Rey.
The Chamber 106.6, la emisora dedicada al metal, está conducida por Kerry King y Tom Araya, integrantes de la banda Slayer. Esta selección de conductores acompaña la decisión de incorporar emisoras específicas para sonidos latinos, africanos y estadounidenses, en línea con la diversidad cultural que Rockstar buscó representar en Leonida.

articles.title: Disney a créé des robots Star Wars qui décident seuls quoi vous dire, grâce à l'IA d'AWS
articles.text:
Les équipes de Walt Disney Imagineering ont présenté mercredi les Anzellans, trois robots Star Wars dont l'intelligence artificielle repose sur AWS. Ces animatroniques réagissent seuls aux visiteurs, mais ils ne prononcent que des répliques écrites et enregistrées à l'avance.
Disney a dévoilé, ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026, les Anzellans, de nouveaux robots animatroniques inspirés de Star Wars et dotés d'une intelligence artificielle construite avec Amazon Web Services (AWS). Le prototype, conçu par la division R&D de Walt Disney Imagineering, réagit en temps réel aux visiteurs, sans opérateur, et rompt avec des décennies de spectacles rejoués à l'identique. Avant de rejoindre un jour un parc Disney, le trio sera présenté au salon AWS re:Invent de Las Vegas dans une quinzaine de jours, où Clubic sera présent.
Trois robots Star Wars qui ne jouent jamais deux fois la même scène
Vilo Vele, Kado Bre'a et Jibu Bre'a sont des Anzellans, une espèce extraterrestre minuscule de l'univers Star Wars, aperçue récemment à l'écran dans The Mandalorian and Grogu, un long métrage de l'univers Star Wars qui se laisse regarder. Pour donner une idée de l'expérience, Disney raconte une rencontre type. Dès que vous vous approchez, les trois personnages se tournent vers vous en même temps. Le premier engage la conversation en mélangeant l'anglais et l'anzellan, la langue de son espèce. Le deuxième cligne des yeux et penche la tête. Le troisième vous observe longuement, puis finit par vous annoncer que le petit groupe a quelque chose de spécial pour vous.
C’est un sacré virage pour les audio-animatronics. Sous ce nom, Disney désigne les personnages robotisés qui bougent et parlent dans ses parcs depuis plus de soixante ans, de l'Abraham Lincoln de Great Moments with Mr. Lincoln au pirate nouvelle génération de l'attraction Pirates of the Caribbean. Jusqu'ici, ces figures jouaient une partition écrite à l'avance, un peu comme un film qu'on relance sans arrêt, avec les mêmes gestes, les mêmes répliques, dans le même ordre, à chaque passage. Les Anzellans, eux, perçoivent ce qui se passe devant eux. Si vous faites un signe de la main ou dites quelques mots, ils réagissent assez vite pour que l'échange paraisse naturel, sans personne pour les piloter en coulisses. Chacun garde son caractère bien à lui, et les trois compères réagissent les uns aux autres autant qu'aux visiteurs. Du coup, aucune rencontre ne ressemble tout à fait à la précédente.
Techniquement, tout repose sur un cerveau à deux étages, propulsé par AWS. Des modèles taillés pour la vitesse gèrent les réactions immédiates, à la manière de réflexes, tandis que des modèles plus imposants prennent du recul pour saisir la situation dans son ensemble. Qu'il s'agisse de percevoir, raisonner, répondre, tout doit aller vite, et chaque composant du système a été optimisé pour réduire la latence, ce petit délai entre le geste de l'utilisateur, et la réaction du robot. Un Anzellan qui mettrait trois secondes à vous saluer perdrait vite tout son charme.
Une IA qui choisit ses mots, mais sans jamais les inventer
Ne cherchez pas de ChatGPT dans ces petites têtes. Les Anzellans n'inventent aucune phrase. L'intelligence artificielle sélectionne la bonne réplique parmi des enregistrements audio réalisés en amont, puis la joue en l'accompagnant d'animations dynamiques. Le partage des rôles est net, et ainsi chaque mot, chaque geste et chaque trait de personnalité sortent des ateliers d'Imagineering, tandis que l'IA construite avec AWS aide les personnages à percevoir, réfléchir et agir sur le moment. Disney résume l'idée d'une jolie formule, en évoquant des personnages qui surprennent le visiteur, sans jamais surprendre leurs créateurs.
Voilà une prudence bienvenue, quand on sait qu'une IA générative peut dérailler, et qu'un parc Disney grouille d'enfants, qu'ils soient grands ou petits, n'est-ce pas ? Le vice-président senior de la R&D d'Imagineering, Kyle Laughlin, assume vouloir avant tout provoquer la surprise, et parle du prochain défi, qui est de donner vie à des personnages de façon innovante, à l'échelle qu'attendent les visiteurs. Côté AWS, fournisseur d'infrastructure cloud de Disney+ de longue date, Samira Panah Bakhtiar, qui pilote notamment les activités médias et divertissement, évoque le parfait exemple d'une « IA physique », qui on le rappelle est un peu l'intelligence artificielle qui quitte l'écran pour agir dans le monde réel, pour schématiser.
Il faudra toutefois patienter avant de leur dire bonjour pour de vrai. Les Anzellans ne sont pour l'instant qu'un prototype, AWS évoque bien leur future installation dans un parc Disney, mais aucun nom ni aucune date n'ont encore été communiqués, il est bien trop tôt. Les participants à re:Invent, la grande conférence annuelle d'Amazon Web Services, pourront en revanche les rencontrer à Las Vegas du 30 novembre au 4 décembre, au Caesars Forum. Quant à savoir s'ils poseront un jour leurs valises à Disneyland Paris, mystère.

articles.title: Voltage glitch unlocks 80GB on Nvidia's CMP 170HX, but 'faster than an A100' rests on a single benchmark
articles.text:
Voltage glitch unlocks 80GB on Nvidia's CMP 170HX, but 'faster than an A100' rests on a single benchmark
Nvidia built the CMP 170HX to be a worse A100
- Researcher uses voltage fault injection on Nvidia's GA100 die to blow normally locked fuses and re-enable memory and compute on the crippled CMP 170HX mining card
- An 8GB card can be pushed to a full 80GB of HBM and 120 to 126 working SMs, more than the 108 Nvidia currently enables on a retail A100
- The "faster than an A100" claim, however, rests on a single FP16 benchmark and leaves tensor performance, ECC, NVLink, and MIG untested or incomplete
Nvidia spent the better part of a decade teaching its silicon to keep secrets from its own owners, but a new piece of hardware research argues that, on at least one chip, those secrets were only ever a power glitch away.
Writing on her personal blog, a researcher known as Kate published a voltage fault injection attack on Nvidia's GA100, the Ampere die at the heart of the A100 data center accelerator.
Her claim is blunt but one backed by proof: by disrupting the chip's power delivery at the right moment during boot, she can write fuses that Nvidia designed to be unwritable, and in doing so re-enable the memory and compute the company switched off at the factory, resulting in a card that behaves as an 80GB A100, assembled from a mining accelerator that was never meant to be anything of that sort.
The card Nvidia built to be worse than it is
The subject of the work is the CMP 170HX, a passively cooled mining card Nvidia introduced in 2021 to steer harvested GA100 dies toward Ethereum and away from the GeForce stock gamers were fighting over as GPU prices skyrocketed because of their potential for cryptomining.
The company was explicit about the segmentation at the time, pairing the CMP line with a hash-rate limiter on the RTX 3060 under the banner "GeForce Is Made for Gaming, CMP Is Made to Mine." The 170HX shipped with 8GB or 10GB of HBM2e exposed to software, 70 streaming multiprocessors, a PCIe Gen1 link, and no video output.
Underneath, it carries the same die that powers accelerators costing many thousands of dollars, and a nominal 8GB card physically holds closer to 80GB of HBM, with firmware and fuses doing the hiding.
That gap is why a five-year-old mining card has become an unlikely object of desire. The industry is in the grip of a memory shortage severe enough that HBM is effectively sold out, so hardware that hides usable high-bandwidth memory behind a software lock is suddenly worth prying open.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This isn't the first attempt to do so: a community project called cmpunlocker, built on earlier work by Amogh Munikote and others, had already shown that patched drivers could expose 64GB on the 8GB card and restore compute, though it stopped at PCIe Gen2 and left NVLink, ECC and Multi-Instance GPU partitioning untouched. Kate's contribution goes past the point where a pure software mod runs out of room to eke out more from the accelerator.
A voltage glitch that writes the unwritable
The mechanism is voltage fault injection, a well-worn technique in hardware security rather than a niche one. In a nutshell, a small microcontroller board taps the signal line between the GPU and its voltage regulator and briefly disturbs the supply while the chip is starting up, nudging the fuse controller into a state where normally locked fuses can be burned.
This is not exclusive to Nvidia's hardware; the same class of attack was used to bypass AMD's secure processor and jailbreak the AMD-based computers inside Tesla's cars to switch on paid features for free. Kate reports that she had OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra design the glitching board. It's interesting to consider: an AI model helped pry open the very class of accelerator that trains AI models.
Faster than an A100? Based on one benchmark
In Kate's testing, an unlocked card reached about 85.9 TFLOP/s of FP16 fused-multiply-add throughput against roughly 72.5 for a retail A100, a gain of about 1.2x. The reason is straightforward. A production A100 enables 108 of the die's 128 SMs for yield, whereas Kate's unlocked cards report between 120 and 126, so a healthy specimen simply has more working silicon than Nvidia ever ships.
That number, however, is non-tensor FP16 throughput from a single OpenCL benchmark. It says nothing about the tensor-core performance, the ECC, the NVLink, and the MIG partitioning that actually define what an A100 is for inside a data center, and Kate marks ECC, MIG, and the video engines as untested.
NVLink also isn't fully working, requiring further board surgery she hasn't completed, even though PCIe can be pushed to Gen4 only with additional hardware modification. A card that wins one synthetic test win is therefore arguably not the same object as a card that can drop into an A100's slot and do its job. The honest description is a GA100 running close to its native potential, which is remarkable to recover from a mining castoff that many wrote off years ago, but not a $20,000 accelerator cloned for pocket change.
A flawed design?
The more durable finding is interestingly not the free compute: it is the flaw underneath it. Kate's argument is that a secure fuse scheme should only let a blown fuse make a chip more restricted, because a fuse cannot be unblown once set.
On the GA100, she says, the opposite can be true, and an operator can "relax restrictions by blowing more fuses." She reports disclosing the vulnerability to Nvidia's product security team before publishing, and going public only after another researcher independently found the same issue. Nvidia has not commented publicly, and for the cards already in the field there is little it can do, since the problem sits in silicon that has long since shipped.
That places the work within a wider run of Ampere-era security research rather than on its own. Academic teams have spent the past two years demonstrating Rowhammer bit flips on Nvidia GPUs and, more recently, defeating the ECC that Nvidia had recommended as the fix.
Kate's own write-up builds directly on Arizona State researcher Jon Pry's June 2026 paper "A Canary in the Crypto Mine," which defeated stack protection in the GPU's security coprocessor. The common thread is a generation of Nvidia silicon whose protections keep proving softer than the marketing implied.
For anyone reading this as a cheap route to an AI box, the caveats matter more than the TFLOPS. Kate reports that unlocking a single card takes somewhere between one and 48 hours, and that of ten cards she examined, one had only 64GB of healthy memory rather than the full 80.
The procedure needs physical rework and per-card tuning, and the fuse burns are permanent, so a mistake isn't something you can walk back. One analyst, Ken Ashe, captured this well, calling the work "silicon archaeology with a soldering iron" and noting that one success is a hack while ten repeatable cards would be infrastructure.
The economics are softer than they look, too. The street prices that make the comparison dramatic- a mining card at a couple of thousand dollars against an A100 near $20,000- come from volatile secondhand listings rather than any stable supply, and they have already climbed as word spread. The 170HX traded for as little as $250 before the first software unlock, then surged past $1,000 once buyers realized what was inside.
What the research really demonstrates here is less a bargain than a warning. In a market this starved of memory, the hardware people already own may be concealing far more than its vendor cares to admit, and the locks keeping it hidden are not as solid as they appear, especially when it comes to last-generation hardware that repurposed higher-end die and memory configurations into lower-end packages regularly.

Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.
