articles.title: Researchers Claim Two RCE Exploits That Bypass Telegram’s New Android Defenses
articles.text:
A malicious widget can bypass the security filter that Telegram added to its Android app last week and run code outside it, according to NebuSec, a security company.
Widgets are small interactive blocks that bots send inside chat messages, and their JavaScript runs on the user's phone. The researchers ran their demonstration on a Telegram test server, because only approved bots can send widgets on the live service now.
Bots could start sending widgets last week. Two days later, an account called V12 posted a video on X claiming that any Telegram message could now be used to execute remote code.
Telegram then put QuickJS, the small engine that runs widget JavaScript, into its own process on Android. It also added a seccomp filter, which can block or record the system calls that the process makes. Both changes appear in the source code it published for Telegram for Android 13.2.2 (7303).
NebuSec said in a technical analysis published earlier this week that its researchers got code running outside that filter in two separate ways. One uses a widget bug the filter does not cover, and the other chains a widget bug the filter does cover with a kernel bug.
In their video, a bot's Telegram widget on Android 13.2.2 (7303) bypasses the filter and opens the phone's calculator app, the researchers say.
Their write-up and their demonstration post on X do not say what the code could reach beyond that, such as the app's messages or the rest of the phone. They also do not say whether the user had to start the bot or tap the widget first.
The researchers are holding back the details for now. Their write-up names no CVE identifier and does not say whether the bugs were reported to the app's developers.
The widget documentation says widgets run in a sandbox, with rules such as no network access. Those rules live in the engine's own code, the researchers say. A single use-after-free or out-of-bounds write bug in QuickJS lets a script read and write the process's memory, and then the rules no longer protect anything.
The new filter names a few dozen system calls, such as ptrace, bpf, and mount, and lets every other call through. The filter's source code leaves ioctl unfiltered. The filter sits on top of Android's own limits on the engine process.
One process also runs every widget, so a hijacked widget from one bot shares memory with the widgets of every other bot, the researchers say.
In the published source code for Telegram for Android 13.2.2 (7303), that filter is set to an audit mode, The Hacker News found. In audit mode, it still blocks attempts to start new programs or processes, but it only records the other listed calls and lets them run.
A comment above the setting says how long that will last: "Audit until the logs from the devices say the engine never makes them." The published code does not show whether the version people install uses the same setting.
"Yes, currently, general bots aren't allowed to use widgets even in private chats," a contributor to the telegram-bot-api project wrote late last week in a bug report thread on GitHub. As of this week, no later message in the thread says which bots are still allowed or that the limit has been lifted.
The researchers' write-up lists no fixed version, and the published Android source code is no newer than 13.2.2 (7303) as of this week.
"No one could be hacked just by receiving a message," Pavel Durov, Telegram's chief executive, wrote late last week in a channel post. His post addressed reports of code execution through widgets in the Android and Windows apps, and came before the researchers' demonstration. He added that a user first had to start a third-party service, and that even that was fully patched on the server side.
The company had earlier said that the problem in V12's first demonstration was fixed and that the fix had reached all users.
Separately, the security vendor Kaspersky said late last week that it had detected suspected exploitation of a flaw in Telegram widgets when people visited some Telegram channels.
In that activity, a PowerShell script ran without the user noticing and downloaded and launched WebRAT, also known as Salat Stealer. The malware allows attackers to control the infected system and steal data from crypto wallets and Telegram accounts.
The vendor's malware warning does not identify the flaw or the Telegram version, does not report the number of victims, and does not link the activity to either demonstration. It advises not running widgets until a fix is released.

articles.title: Tout ça pour ça ! NVIDIA annulerait la GeForce RTX 5080 24 Go : la GDDR7 est trop chère
articles.text:
Finalement, NVIDIA aurait décidé de laisser de côté cette hypothétique version 24 Go de la GeForce RTX 5080 et conservé le « simple » modèle doté de 16 Go, moins onéreux à produire.
Cruel univers que celui des cartes graphiques. Alors que l'on commençait à vraiment croire que NVIDIA envisageait le lancement d'une version 24 Go de la GeForce RTX 5080, nos espoirs sont douchés par ce qui serait un problème de coût de production. Alors là, quelle surprise !
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Une RTX 5080 dotée de 24 Go de VRAM…
Les GeForce RTX série 50 en déclinaison « SUPER », on en parle depuis des mois. En réalité, on en parle pratiquement depuis le lancement des RTX 5090 et RTX 5080, c'est dire.
Cela dit, le nombre de rumeurs autour d'un produit est loin d'en faire une réalité et si vous suivez un tant soit peu l'actualité de la carte graphique, vous êtes bien placés pour savoir que les bruits de couloir autour des GPU d'AMD, d'Intel ou de NVIDIA sont loin de tous devenir réalité. Les « SUPER », on les avait ainsi presque oubliées quand la rumeur – seule cette fois – est revenue à la charge alors que NVIDIA semblait retirer les RTX 5080/5090 de sa boutique.
Cette fois, il n'était plus nécessairement question de l'appeler RTX 5080 SUPER, mais simplement « 24 Go » pour insister sur le fait qu'un modèle en chassait un autre. La GeForce RTX 5080 16 Go devait disparaître pour céder la place à un modèle doté de 8 Go de mémoire vidéo en plus. De quoi lui donner un peu plus de peps afin de convaincre les joueurs déçus par l'inaccessibilité de la RTX 5090.
… finalement annulée et retour à la version 16 Go !
Alors que les indices commençaient à se multiplier et que l'on envisageait même une sortie en tout début d'année prochaine, tout porte à croire que NVIDIA a complètement changé son fusil d'épaule.
Relayée par nos confrères du site VideoCardz, la nouvelle de l'annulation de cette version 24 Go de la GeForce RTX 5080 serait à mettre en lien avec le coût de la GDDR7. Remarquez, ce n'est pas franchement une surprise, c'est en partie la raison pour laquelle le prix des cartes gaming haut de gamme et des cartes professionnelles crève le plafond.
À en croire notre confrère, il ne serait donc plus question de se fournir en puces de 3 Go pour concevoir cette variante 24 Go et NVIDIA préfère continuer avec les puces GDDR7 de 2 Go afin de maintenir en vie la GeForce RTX 5080 16 Go telle que nous la connaissons. Nous avons d'ailleurs testé la variante signée ASUS/Noctua il y a seulement quelques jours. Si l'information clarifie un peu la situation, cela ne résout cependant pas les problèmes du prix.
La GeForce RTX 5080 16 Go – et pas seulement le modèle ASUS/Noctua – a effectivement bien augmenté depuis son lancement il y a bientôt deux ans et personne ne voit aucun signe d'amélioration à court terme.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: The US grounded all domestic flights for four hours due to an HPE router fault
articles.text:
Two HPE Juniper routers were reportedly behind the FAA nationwide ground stop, which grounded all US flights
The US grounded all domestic flights for four hours due to HPE router fault
- Two newly installed routers reportedly overwhelmed the FAA's aging communications network
- FAA controllers lost communications, forcing an unprecedented nationwide flight suspension
- TCAS remained unaffected despite failures in controller-pilot communications
Recently installed HPE Juniper routers reportedly triggered the recent US nationwide aviation disruption after overwhelming the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) aging communications infrastructure.
The incident forced the FAA to suspend flights across the United States while technicians investigated interruptions affecting communications between air traffic controllers and pilots.
Although the equipment itself reportedly remained operational, excessive network traffic exposed vulnerabilities within infrastructure that the agency has been gradually replacing.
New routers reportedly overwhelmed the FAA communications infrastructure
The disruption reportedly originated at two locations where HPE Juniper routers started transmitting unusually large volumes of data.
Investigators traced the affected equipment to an FAA radio facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, and a radar installation in Amarillo, Texas.
The problem initially emerged at the Indianapolis Center, which is responsible for managing aircraft movements across northern Kentucky, southern Indiana, southern Ohio, and parts of West Virginia.
Personnel experienced difficulties communicating with flight crews, prompting investigators to examine the agency's nationwide communications network.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“We saw two places that were actually pinging our network at a very high rate, a thousand connections over every four to five seconds,” said Rebecca Guy, FAA technology chief.
Although such traffic volumes would ordinarily present limited difficulties for modern networking infrastructure, the FAA operates an aging communications system.
Consequently, the equipment struggled to accommodate the incoming traffic, resulting in communication interruptions that prevented controllers from coordinating aircraft movements.
The disruption reportedly did not affect aircraft collision-avoidance equipment, including the Traffic Collision Avoidance System (TCAS), which uses onboard transponders.
Nevertheless, communication difficulties between controllers and pilots left the agency unable to coordinate air traffic safely, necessitating an emergency nationwide ground stop.
FAA investigates router configuration as HPE defends its equipment
A nationwide ground stop remains an exceptional measure, with the FAA having invoked it only twice before the latest incident.
Those previous occasions involved the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks and a January 11, 2023, outage affecting its Notice to Air Missions system.
The agency needed approximately four hours to restore its communications network after identifying the problematic equipment.
Technicians subsequently disabled a particular router feature across the network's installed Juniper devices, preventing further disruption.
HPE, the manufacturer of the affected networking equipment, maintained that its routers were operating according to their intended specifications.
The company disputed suggestions that hardware failure directly caused the communications breakdown.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford nevertheless indicated that investigators were examining several possible explanations for the incident.
These included installation problems, configuration errors, and potential shortcomings associated with the router technology itself.
“Was it a faulty installation? Was it a faulty configuration? Or was it just a bad piece of router technology that we put into this system that propagated these errors?” said Bedford.
The FAA is already transitioning from decades-old copper connections to fiber-optic technology, an extensive modernization program costing taxpayers billions of dollars.
Via Tom's Hardware

articles.title: Instagram vous laisse enfin éditer vos stories
articles.text:
Qui n’a jamais publié un peu trop rapidement une story sur Instagram avant de le regretter, quelques secondes plus tard, à cause d’un oubli ou d’une vilaine faute ? Jusqu’à présent, Instagram n’offrait aucune solution permettant de corriger ce que vous aviez publié en story, vous obligeant ainsi à supprimer votre publication pour la recommencer ensuite. Mais les choses sont sur le point de changer.
Un délai de 15 minutes pour éditer vos stories
La bonne nouvelle a été annoncée officiellement par Adam Mosseri, le patron d’Instagram en personne sur son compte.
 Voir cette publication sur Instagram
 « Si vous avez déjà remarqué une faute de frappe juste après avoir posté une story, celle-ci est pour vous. Vous pouvez maintenant éditer du texte, de la musique, des autocollants et des dessins pendant 15 minutes maximum après le partage, sans perdre vos vues, vos likes ou vos réponses. » a-t-il ainsi expliqué en commentaire de sa publication.
Cette option d’édition, attendue de longue date par les utilisateurs, est accessible en tapotant le bouton Plus affiché en bas de la story, puis en sélectionnant Éditer la story. Attention toutefois, la possibilité de modifier une story n’est possible que dans les 15 minutes après la publication de celle-ci. Passé ce délai, vous n’aurez donc pas d’autre choix que d’adopter l’ancienne méthode, c’est-à-dire supprimer votre publication pour en refaire une nouvelle.

articles.title: Una plataforma india de cobro de deudas con IA dejó expuestos datos de 6,6 millones de cuentas
articles.text:
Dos fallas de seguridad en CreditNirvana, una plataforma india que usa inteligencia artificial para cobrar deudas, dejaron expuestas 6,6 millones de cuentas de deudores y unas 315.000 grabaciones de llamadas. El investigador independiente Eaton Zveare las descubrió, y WIRED las dio a conocer el 18 de noviembre.
CreditNirvana pertenece a Perfios, una empresa india de tecnología financiera. Su sistema decide cuál es el siguiente paso con cada deudor y lo ejecuta sin intervención humana, según la propia descripción citada por WIRED.
Zveare informó los problemas a CERT-In, el equipo de respuesta a emergencias informáticas de India, el 30 de mayo. Según su cronología, las fallas se corrigieron el 2 de junio, un día después de que la empresa las conoció. CERT-In emitió la nota oficial con los identificadores de las vulnerabilidades el 26 de octubre.
CERT-In clasificó una falla como de gravedad alta y la otra como crítica. WIRED informó que CreditNirvana y Perfios no respondieron a sus pedidos de comentarios.
Un código mal protegido abría el centro de llamadas
La primera falla afectaba al centro de llamadas con agentes de IA que usa la financiera Aditya Birla Capital Finance. El sitio pedía iniciar sesión, pero una clave de acceso estaba escrita en el código de la página y daba control total, según el informe de Zveare.
Con esa clave se podían escuchar y leer 315.000 llamadas grabadas, ver las recomendaciones que el sistema generaba después de cada una y crear campañas de llamadas automáticas. Un atacante también podía administrar a los agentes de IA de la plataforma, según WIRED.
La segunda falla estaba en la plataforma principal y, para CERT-In, era la más grave. Permitía iniciar sesión como cualquier usuario, incluidos los administradores, y acceder o modificar información con los permisos de esa persona. Zveare precisó que bastaba con alterar el código de la página que se ejecuta en el navegador para saltarse la autenticación.
Documentos de identidad, informes de crédito y rastreo de cobradores
Esa segunda falla expuso las cuentas de tres clientes de CreditNirvana: Aditya Birla Capital Finance, con más de 3,4 millones, y la plataforma de pagos BharatPe y la International Asset Reconstruction Company, que sumaban otros 3,2 millones.
Cada cuenta contenía datos de contacto, recibos de pago, cartas de reclamo y avisos legales. En los casos con acuerdos de pago, Zveare encontró documentos de identidad e informes de crédito completos de TransUnion CIBIL, uno de ellos de 26 páginas con el historial de la persona. Había más de 161.000 acuerdos de ese tipo.
El sistema también mostraba millones de mensajes de texto, correos y WhatsApp enviados a los deudores. Solo en mayo de 2026 figuraban 214.000 llamadas hechas por el robot de voz y 119.000 avisos legales. Además, registraba el recorrido de los cobradores que visitan a los deudores en persona: dónde fueron, a quién vieron y con qué resultado.
Zveare dijo a WIRED que las vulnerabilidades pudieron existir durante años y que el caso es “un ejemplo importante” de un servicio con IA que concentra datos muy delicados. También señaló que la corrección en un día fue una buena respuesta de la empresa.
No hay constancia pública de que alguien más haya aprovechado las fallas antes de su corrección. El informe del investigador no lo afirma, y WIRED tampoco aporta pruebas de ello.
Zveare indicó además que publicará en diciembre otra vulnerabilidad que podría explotarse de manera similar en otras aplicaciones web, ligada a la misma técnica contra el sistema de identidades Keycloak, y que aún no divulgó.

articles.title: Microsoft to Use Intel's EMIB Advanced Packaging Technology
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
Microsoft to Use Intel's EMIB Advanced Packaging Technology
Microsoft announced today that it will officially adopt Intel Foundry's Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB) advanced packaging technology for its custom silicon used in Azure. Specifically, Microsoft will use Intel's EMIB-T, which includes through-silicon vias (TSVs) to enable vertical power delivery across multiple stacked chips, supporting the concept of vertical power delivery for 3D silicon modules at the package level. As a reminder, Microsoft's fleet of custom silicon solutions includes valuable accelerators, such as the current Maia 200, which powers AI inferencing workloads like large-scale reasoning, and the Cobalt 200 CPUs, designed for agentic workloads. The next-generation versions of these silicon projects will be packaged at Intel Foundry, supported by EMIB and its variants like EMIB-T.
Additionally, Microsoft confirmed its commitment to using Intel's Xeon processors and the upcoming "Diamond Rapids" Xeon 7 CPUs to power Azure infrastructure. The company will collaborate with Intel to integrate Intel Xeons on Compute Express Link (CXL) to achieve greater memory efficiency and system-level control across its data centers. Microsoft will also utilize Intel QuickAssist (Intel QAT) and confidential computing through Intel Trust Domain Extensions (Intel TDX). The company has measured a 2.5x increase in performance and flexibility on some workloads, such as SQL backups, thanks to CXL and other optimizations.
Naga Chandrasekaran, EVP, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel FoundryMicrosoft and Intel share a clear view of where AI infrastructure is headed-increasingly complex systems designed through the co-optimization of silicon, packaging, compute memory and software. Through use of our advanced packaging capabilities with EMIB to scale future generations of Azure infrastructure, Intel and Microsoft can combine the flexibility of heterogeneous integration with the manufacturing scale required for the AI era—giving customers new levels of performance and economics when interacting with Azure.

articles.title: Google's latest midtier model Gemini 4 Neon is three times faster than Carbon and wins on some metrics - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google’s latest midtier model Gemini 4 Neon is three times faster than Carbon and wins on some metrics
After laying low during the summer while competitors Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC unleashed powerful new frontier models, Google LLC is hitting back.
Having released its latest flagship model Gemini 4 Carbon one month ago, followed by the cost-effective Gemini 4 Hydrogen, it’s now striking a balance between the two with Gemini 4 Neon. Google announced its latest artificial intelligence offering in a blog post today, saying that Neon is a general-purpose model designed to handle complex coding tasks, multistep agentic workflows and analytical reasoning.
Surprisingly, though Carbon is positioned as the company’s strongest model, Neon’s performance surpassed it on some tasks, according to benchmarks the company published today. Google also said Neon completes most tasks about three times as quickly as Carbon at costs of about 60% lower, making it “competitive with the leading models in its class.”
Here’s Google’s official benchmarks:
Digging deeper into Google’s benchmarks, the company said Neon outranked the midtier Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol models on tests such as knowledge work, reasoning, automation, multimodal understanding, cybersecurity, science and math.
Those numbers were from Google’s own tests, but independent research by Artificial Analysis shows that Neon achieved an impressive score of 61 on the Intelligence Index, putting it third overall, just behind Anthropic’s most powerful model, Claude Fable 5.2, which scored 65, and OpenAI’s leading model GPT-6.2 Astra, which achieved a score of 62.
Google continues to accelerate its release cadence with Gemini 4 Neon, delivering a small Intelligence gain over Gemini 4 Carbon at a ~17% lower Cost per Task@GoogleDeepMind has released Gemini 4 Neon, its fourth model in just seven weeks. Neon (xhigh) scores 61 on the… pic.twitter.com/L76oKwyxXa
— Artificial Analysis (@ArtificialAnlys) November 18, 2026
With regard to cost, Neon isn’t quite so impressive. Google said it’s priced at a cost of $3 per million input tokens, 15 cents per million cached input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. That means it falls right in between GPT-6.2 Sol, which costs $2 per million input tokens, 10 cents per million cached tokens and $10 per million output tokens, and Claude Opus 5.5, which is priced at $4 per million input tokens, 20 cents per million cached tokens and $20 per million output tokens.
Google’s choice of pricing is interesting because there’s a lot of debate around which model provider can achieve a genuine competitive advantage over its competitors. Given that these midtier models are so comparable in terms of performance, cost efficiency is becoming a more significant factor for enterprise customers. Although Neon appears to edge out GPT-6.2 Sol and Claude Fable 5.2 in terms of its ability to process several important workloads, many organizations might decide that’s not really enough to justify paying more to use it.
Google said it’s making Neon available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers from today in the Gemini application. Developers can also access it through the company’s paid application programming interface, the Google Antigravity platform and other business offerings.

articles.title: « Improbable et grave » : l’IA a découvert une faille planétaire dans un langage informatique « dont nous dépendons tous »
articles.text:
Une nouvelle faille critique fait trembler le monde de l’informatique. Ce 17 novembre, la start-up californienne Calif a dévoilé une brèche dans le cœur du code de Java, un langage de programmation omniprésent dans le monde entier. Baptisée Java4Shell, la faille permet à un pirate de prendre le contrôle de certains serveurs à distance. Elle touche surtout les serveurs des entreprises équipés de processeurs Intel ou AMD récents. Les puces ARM, présentes dans la plupart des smartphones, ne sont pas concernées.
À lire aussi : « Un faux sentiment de secret » – face à l’IA, Google prend une décision qui divise le monde de la cybersécurité
Une faille découverte par l’IA… en une heure
L’affaire a commencé il y a quelques semaines quand Quang Luong, chercheur chez Calif, a décidé de se pencher sur le code de Java. Conscient de la difficulté de la tâche, il s’est tourné vers Codex, l’assistant d’OpenAI propulsé par GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle d’IA spécialisé dans la recherche de failles.
 Since the vulnerability has leaked: Calif discovered and reported Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938).
We’re publishing technical details by 1 PM Pacific today, after Oracle releases a patch.
Stay tuned!
— Calif (@calif_io) November 17, 2026
Au début, l’IA n’a proposé que des pistes inutiles. Moins d’une heure après le début des recherches, l’intelligence artificielle a mis le doigt sur une vraie faille de sécurité, bien plus préoccupante que prévu. Selon Calif, il n’a fallu qu’une heure pour trouver la faille, puis deux heures pour mettre au point une attaque, le tout pour moins de 200 dollars de frais de calcul.
« Je suis venu chercher du cuivre et j’ai trouvé de l’or », résume le chercheur.
64 lettres « A » pour pirater un serveur
La faille se cache dans une fonction très banale de Java qui sert à décoder du texte au format Base64. Ce format sert à transformer des données en suites de lettres et de chiffres pour qu’elles circulent facilement sur Internet. La fonction est notamment utilisée pour envoyer des identifiants de connexion ou des fichiers. Sur les processeurs récents, Java utilise une version accélérée de cette fonction. C’est dans cette fonctionnalité que l’IA a déniché une faille de sécurité.
Pour déclencher la brèche, il suffit d’envoyer 64 lettres « A » suivies d’un signe « = » à la fonction. Celle-ci se met alors à déborder et à écraser certaines des données de sa mémoire. Un pirate peut alors en profiter pour lire des informations secrètes, comme des mots de passe ou des clés de chiffrement, explique Calif. C’est la porte ouverte à des vols de données sensibles, susceptibles de compromettre des comptes en banque. Un attaquant peut aussi en profiter pour envoyer ses propres commandes par le biais de la fonction. Lors de ses tests, Calif a piraté plusieurs logiciels très utilisés en entreprise, comme Jira, Confluence ou Jenkins.
« Corriger immédiatement » la faille Java4Shell
L’annonce devait rester secrète jusqu’à la publication du correctif, conformément aux meilleures pratiques du monde de la cybersécurité. Selon Calif, l’information a été divulguée quelques heures trop tôt, alors qu’aucun correctif n’avait encore été annoncé. Le 17 novembre, la start-up a donc publié le résultat de ses travaux.
Le jour même, le géant américain Oracle, propriétaire de Java ,et OpenJDK, la version libre de Java, mettent en ligne un correctif pour colmater la vulnérabilité dans l’urgence. Dans la foulée, la CISA, l’agence américaine de cybersécurité, a appelé toutes les organisations à « corriger immédiatement » la faille pour éviter une explosion des cyberattaques.
 🚨We urge orgs to immediately patch the recently disclosed Oracle Java vuln CVE-2026-114938. This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as “Java4Shell,” affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot JVM, part of the Java Development Kit. 🔗https://t.co/SwrhdPFlZF pic.twitter.com/3QGldeAerV
— CISA Cyber (@CISACyber) November 17, 2026
L’alerte fait rapidement le tour du monde. En Allemagne, le BSI (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik), l’agence fédérale de cybersécurité, met lui aussi en garde contre les attaques exploitant la faille de Java, rapporte Reuters. Le Canada et l’Inde ont rapidement publié des avis similaires, exhortant toutes les entreprises à agir dans les plus brefs délais.
Une faille jugée « improbable et grave »
Interrogé par la BBC, le chercheur Toby Walsh juge la faille « improbable et grave ». Il rappelle que Java est justement conçu pour protéger la mémoire à l’encontre de ce genre d’erreur. Selon Walsh, « l’IA met désormais au jour davantage de failles, bien plus rapidement ». Le chercheur Pedram Hayati ne cache pas son inquiétude. Il estime que la brèche dans Java pourrait compromettre « des systèmes financiers critiques ».
Pour Fouad Matin, le responsable de la préparation aux cybermenaces chez OpenAI, les travaux de Calif montrent que l’IA peut aider les chercheurs à débusquer des failles graves « dans des logiciels dont nous dépendons tous », selon des propos rapportés par le New York Times.
Bonne nouvelle, aucune cyberattaque n’a encore été détectée. Dans une réaction envoyée à 01net, les chercheurs de Group-IB révèlent n’avoir « trouvé aucune preuve d’exploitation » pour le moment. Comme le souligne le Centre canadien pour la cybersécurité, « cela peut changer rapidement ». C’est également l’avis de Cisco Talos, qui s’attend à voir les tentatives d’attaque se multiplier prochainement.
Avant Java, le chaos PHP
L’histoire de Java4Shell rappelle celle de PHP2Shell. En octobre, Calif avait déjà utilisé l’IA pour dénicher deux failles critiques dans PHP, un autre langage très répandu, plongeant une partie d’Internet dans le chaos. La faille a aussi été divulguée un peu trop tôt, ouvrant la porte à des tentatives d’intrusion. Des pirates chinois se sont rapidement servis de la faille pour mener des attaques. Les versions touchées sont Java 17 (à partir de la 17.0.6), 21, 25 et 27. Comme pour PHP, le plus dur sera de retrouver toutes les copies de Java cachées dans les logiciels et les machines à travers le monde. De facto, des systèmes risquent de rester vulnérables pendant un long moment…

articles.title: Los mejores memes del lanzamiento de GTA VI: Jensen Huang de Nvidia fue protagonista
articles.text:
GTA 6 ha estado envuelto en memes desde hace muchos años. Sus continuos retrasos y la espera por más de una década han hecho que las redes sociales bromeen con su lanzamiento continuamente. Ahora, con su estreno, Instagram, X, TikTok y Facebook están llenos de referencias a esa espera y lo importante que es para los jugadores este momento.
Su lanzamiento para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S ha servido para que surjan diferentes memes hablando del impacto que tendrá en las parejas, el tiempo que se le dedicará y hasta bromeando con que el título de Rockstar es el verdadero motivo por el que Jensen Huang renunció como director ejecutivo de Nvidia.
Así son los memes del lanzamiento de GTA 6
Pasaron 13 años desde el estreno del último título de la saga de Grand Theft Auto, aunque sobre GTA 6 se viene hablando específicamente desde 2021, cuando Rockstar confirmó su desarrollo. Durante estos años de espera se presentaron diferentes retrasos, por lo que se creó una categoría de memes para esa larga espera: “Antes de GTA 6”, en la que se hacían referencias a acontecimientos históricos que podrían suceder antes del lanzamiento del juego.
Con eso cerrado, ahora las redes hablan de cómo el juego impactará en la vida personal de los usuarios, quienes esperan dedicar una gran cantidad de horas, lo que podría afectar su vida sentimental.
Incluso algunos memes intentan explicar la importancia de este lanzamiento con hechos casi imposibles, como: Crepúsculo 6, una nueva gira de One Direction, regalos en Shein, comer sin engordar o tener uñas y pestañas gratis para siempre.
Los jugadores de PC también son víctimas de los memes. Rockstar decidió que su juego salga, por ahora, solo en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, por lo que la versión para computadoras no ha sido mencionada y no se conoce la fecha de su lanzamiento.
Cuándo sale GTA 6 y cómo será su lanzamiento
GTA 6 llega este jueves 19 de noviembre, con disponibilidad desde las 00:00 horas de cada país. El nuevo título de Rockstar Games ubica la historia en Vice City, dentro del estado ficticio de Leonida, y sigue a Jason y Lucía como protagonistas.
Rockstar fijó dos precios: la edición estándar cuesta US$80, mientras que la Ultimate Edition llega a US$100, con contenido adicional. Sin embargo, la versión física no contará con disco, sino con un código para canjear de manera digital.
La instalación requiere unos 212 GB de espacio, por lo que se recomienda liberar almacenamiento y descargar con anticipación. Así que los usuarios deberán tener paciencia durante el proceso de instalación y quizás borrar otros juegos de sus consolas.
Las primeras reseñas de la prensa especializada fueron muy positivas. Un análisis previo al lanzamiento, tras varias semanas de prueba en PlayStation 5 Pro, calificó al juego como una obra maestra. En Metacritic, GTA 6 obtuvo 99 sobre 100 puntos, con base en 147 reseñas, una marca que lo coloca cerca del récord histórico atribuido a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
Entre los puntos más elogiados figuran el detalle del mundo abierto y la ambientación. La recepción inicial refuerza las expectativas sobre uno de los estrenos más esperados de los videojuegos en los últimos años.
Cómo jugar GTA 6 antes de su lanzamiento
El truco de Nueva Zelanda permite adelantar el acceso a GTA VI porque ese país recibe el juego a medianoche según su horario, antes que el resto del mundo. En Xbox Series X|S, el cambio es sencillo: desde Configuración, Sistema e Idioma y ubicación se selecciona Nueva Zelanda y se reinicia la consola.
En PlayStation 5, Sony no permite modificar la región de una cuenta existente, por lo que exige crear un perfil nuevo y comprar el juego otra vez. Usuarios reportaron baneos en PlayStation por declarar un país falso, aunque ni Sony ni Rockstar Games confirmaron sanciones oficiales por esta práctica.

-VPN chiffré : sécurisation de la connexion, notamment sur les réseaux Wi-Fi publics.
-Protection anti-phishing : détection des liens et sites web potentiellement dangereux.
-Analyse des téléchargements : recherche de logiciels malveillants dans les fichiers récupérés.
-Blocage des publicités et traqueurs : limitation des annonces intrusives et du suivi en ligne.
-Jusqu'à 10 appareils : un seul compte pour plusieurs équipements.

Le fournisseur met également en avant une politique sans journaux d'activité et une bande passante illimitée. Le service couvre aussi bien les ordinateurs que les mobiles, avec des applications pour Windows, macOS, Linux, Android et iOS. La compatibilité s'étend également à certains téléviseurs connectés et routeurs.
Une réduction de 78 % et trois mois offerts pour le Black Friday

NordVPN laisse également 30 jours pour essayer son service. Cette garantie laisse un mois pour découvrir le service. Si l'expérience n'est pas concluante, un remboursement peut être sollicité dans les conditions prévues.
Au final, NordVPN Premium ne se limite pas au chiffrement de la connexion. L'offre associe un VPN, des fonctions de détection des menaces et un bloqueur de traqueurs, avec une couverture allant jusqu'à 10 appareils.La réduction du Black Friday et les trois mois offerts rendent la formule plus accessible, à condition de bien prendre en compte les modalités de renouvellement.

articles.title: BMW dit non à Apple CarPlay Ultra, mais ouvre la porte à un autre retour très attendu dans ses voitures
articles.text:
Apple CarPlay et Android Auto ont révolutionné notre rapport à l’infodivertissement automobile. Les deux interfaces proposent en effet de répliquer en toute simplicité les écrans de nos smartphones afin d’utiliser nos applications préférées à bord. Une belle avancée qui va encore plus loin avec CarPlay Ultra faisant des combinés d’instrumentation de nouveaux territoires de conquête.
Mieux que cela, le système prend aussi la main sur certaines commandes du véhicule. C’est le cas de la ventilation et des aides à la conduite. Intéressant, mais encore rare : à ce jour, seul Aston Martin intègre le dispositif. BMW, de son côté, confirme que CarPlay Ultra n’arrivera pas de sitôt sur ses modèles. L’ensemble ne pourra d’ailleurs s’afficher sur aucun écran à bord du véhicule. La marque évoque des risques sur la confidentialité.
Le vrai motif du refus de la marque à l’hélice
Cela veut-il dire qu’aucun changement ne sera à prévoir pour les années futures ? Claudia Maier, responsable du numérique chez BMW, affirme que rien n’est fixé et que le constructeur pourrait éventuellement procéder à des ajustements sur l’interface des modèles Neue Klasse. Toujours pas de CarPlay Ultra, donc, mais les classiques connectivités Apple CarPlay et Android Auto. Et pourquoi donc ?
Maier explique que CarPlay Ultra ne correspond pas à la stratégie, ni à la philosophie portée par la marque à l’hélice. BMW souhaite conserver toutes ses données dans ses propres logiciels en interne afin de les sécuriser au maximum. Il faut dire que le constructeur a également investi du temps et de l’argent pour développer son Panoramic iDrive. Tout changer dans l’immédiat avec CarPlay Ultra serait un immense gâchis.
Ce revirement ergonomique que les conducteurs attendaient
En outre, un retour en grâce des boutons physiques pourrait être envisageable. Sur les i3 et iX3, les commandes de ventilation logées dans les écrans peuvent déjà déranger, même si elles sont constamment affichées en accès direct. Cependant, orienter le flux d’air impose aussi une manipulation sur l’écran tactile, ce qui commence à poser d’évidents problèmes d’ergonomie. Un revirement est donc plausible.
Plausible ne veut cependant pas dire certain. Maier a en effet indiqué que BMW est sûr que ses clients finiront par s’habituer au Panoramic iDrive utilisant massivement les commandes tactiles et vocales. La disparition de la mythique molette contrôlant l’infodivertissement au profit d’un environnement complètement numérique, est-ce vraiment une évidence pour tous ?
La fin de la mythique molette iDrive fait grincer des dents
Permettez-nous de douter, car une telle adaptation ne se fera pas sans douleur pour les habitués. Si changement il y a, il faudra ainsi attendre la prochaine génération de véhicules qui arrivera encore dans très longtemps. Heureusement que la Neue Klasse assure côté technique avec d’excellents scores d’autonomie et de recharge. De quoi faire avaler la pilule…

articles.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128 GB of unified memory and NVIDIA's AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work.
Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark—all on one Windows PC.A Windows PC Built for Local AI
As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session—from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. 
RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system.
Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks.
RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128 GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage.
This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including:
- Running massive 120-billion-parameter large language models locally
- Rendering 90 GB+ 3D scenes in real time
- Smoothly editing 4:2:2 video in real time
New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box.
From Local Agents to AI Creation
Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth.
RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions.
NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows.
These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device—from isolating a subject and defining its motion to generating the finished video.
The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark.
Adobe Accelerates the Full Creative Stack for RTX Spark
NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe's creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark.
Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX, including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe—so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting. 
GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables.
Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters.
Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required.
Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark.
Blender 5.3 Adds DLSS Ray Reconstruction to the Viewport
Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work. 
The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time. 
DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software.
Windows Server 2028 Coming to DGX Station for Windows
Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data.
Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip is expanding to include support for Windows Server 2028.
New accelerator platforms and the breadth of the Windows silicon ecosystem provide customers options at different capability levels and price points for advanced AI development, local inference, and agent workloads at scale.
Windows ML Updates Give Developers More Options
Also announced at Microsoft Ignite, developers can now bring any GGUF model from Hugging Face and run it within Windows ML using the llama.cpp backend.
The DxCGC backend, now available as an experimental release, is an integration for game developers that compiles and runs machine learning models through DirectX 12, allowing them to execute AI workloads alongside graphics.
Windows APIs let applications integrate platform-provided AI capabilities adding GPU support for AION Instruct and VSR.
Developers can also build high-performance AI models for Windows ML using the command line interface.

articles.title: App do Gemini agora funciona até em celulares Android com pouca RAM • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
App do Gemini agora funciona até em celulares Android com pouca RAM
Google otimizou aplicativo do Gemini para funcionar em celulares Android básicos com pelo menos 2 GB de RAM.
O aplicativo oficial do Gemini para Android foi lançado no começo de 2024, logo após o serviço deixar de se chamar Bard (lembra disso?). Mas usuários de celulares Android mais simples ficavam restritos ao Google Assistente Go, com comandos básicos. Bom, não mais: o Google tratou de otimizar a ferramenta para que ela funcione até com aparelhos Android básicos, com 2 GB de RAM ou mais.
É importante deixar claro desde já que não estamos falando de um aplicativo alternativo do Gemini voltado especificamente a dispositivos de entrada. O que o Google fez foi tornar o aplicativo oficial do serviço capaz de funcionar a contento mesmo quando houver capacidade reduzida de memória RAM ou armazenamento.
O Google explica que, até recentemente, as limitações de hardware impediam que esses dispositivos rodassem o app do Gemini, deixando o usuário acessar, no máximo, comandos básicos de voz no antigo assistente.
Com a otimização do aplicativo, o Gemini passa a atender os usuários desses aparelhos com funcionalidades que já são conhecidas por quem usa celulares Android mais avançados:
Em vez de digitar frases longas, você pode conversar ou praticar para uma entrevista em voz alta em mais de 45 idiomas com o Gemini Live, apontar a câmera para anotações ou formulários para aprender e traduzir, ou criar imagens personalizadas com o Nano Banana — como um folheto para a venda de uma padaria no fim de semana.
Google
O Google não divulgou uma lista de celulares que serão beneficiados com a novidade. A companhia revelou, porém, que o app reformulado visa atender especialmente dispositivos que rodam o Android Go, uma versão enxuta do sistema operacional criada para dispositivos de entrada.
Também é preciso que o aparelho tenha pelo menos 2 GB de RAM, como já informado, bem como que o usuário acesse o Gemini com sua Conta Google.
A novidade é universal, valendo para todos os países onde o serviço de IA está disponível. Para o Brasil, podemos presumir que usuários de aparelhos como Motorola Moto E14 e Samsung Galaxy A03 serão beneficiados.
Ainda há algumas limitações. Por exemplo, a ativação por voz (“ok, Google”) e a leitura contextual da tela podem não funcionar em dispositivos Android básicos. Neste caso, o usuário tem a opção de acionar o Gemini pressionando o botão Inicial (Home) ou a tecla Liga/Desliga.

articles.title: Everpure beats expectations as AI accelerates revenue growth for ninth straight quarter - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Everpure beats expectations as AI accelerates revenue growth for ninth straight quarter
Data center infrastructure company Everpure Inc. posted third-quarter earnings and revenue that surpassed analysts’ expectations and raised its full-year forecast for the third successive quarter, and its stock gained just over 4% in after-hours trading today.
The storage and data management hardware firm reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of 86 cents per share, easily beating Wall Street’s consensus estimate of 77 cents. Revenue for the period rose 51% from a year earlier to $1.5 billion, surpassing the analyst’s target of $1.33 billion by a comfortable margin.
Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Giancarlo (pictured) said the results reinforce the company’s status as a trusted partner for enterprises. “As organizations work to break down data silos and modernize their data estates, our growth across both core and new, high-growth markets shows we are uniquely equipped to solve their most complex data challenges at scale,” he added.
Everpure, formerly known as Pure Storage, is a pioneer of all-flash data storage hardware and unified data management software for applications, cloud environments, analytics workloads and, increasingly, artificial intelligence workloads. Specifically for AI, it provides enterprises and cloud infrastructure providers with the high-speed, cost- and power-efficient data storage and management solutions they need to keep pace with the high-end accelerators that process model training and inference workloads
The company rebranded in February 2026 as part of an effort to emphasize its vision of “data primacy,” which positions its products as the central data intelligence and governance layer for AI. By integrating closely with Nvidia Corp.’s graphics processing units and using tools such as its Data Intelligence software and its FlashBlade servers, it claims to be able to prepare data, speed up inference and lower GPU and storage costs.
AI has helped Everpure to accelerate its momentum this year, and it beat the Street’s targets across all major metrics in the last quarter. Adjusted operating income reached $345 million, an impressive $70 million above its prior guidance. Product revenue, derived from the sale of storage systems, came to $948 million, up 77% from a year earlier, while subscription services revenue was up 20%. Net income for the quarter came to $100.4 million, up from $54.8 million in the same period one year ago.
The company said its remaining performance obligations, which refers to the value of contracts already signed but not yet realized as revenue, ended the quarter at $4.2 billion, up 44%.
NAND Research analyst Steve McDowell told SiliconANGLE that a primary reason for Everpure’s growth is the rising cost of memory and flash storage, which has allowed the company to bump up the prices of its storage products quite substantially this year without any negative impact on demand. “But it’s notable that Everpure continues to outperform the broader storage market, and the numbers it’s putting up suggests it’s taking market share away from its rivals,” he said.
Everpure’s growth has been accelerating for more than two years now. In August, the company said its revenue had grown for eight successive quarters, and today’s report makes that nine. Over the last five quarters, it has grown by 16%, 20%, 35%, 38% and 51%. “It’s the third consecutive quarter of growth above 35%,” McDowell said. “At the same time, it has been growing its product margins even in the face of those rising component costs and supply chain challenges. Everpure’s team is demonstrating strong execution to do this.”
Giancarlo said on a conference call that much of that momentum has to do with AI. During the quarter, it won a design contract with one of the top five largest hyperscale cloud companies, he added.
According to McDowell, the only real blot on Everpure’s results was the slight drop in its subscription margins, but even this was more than offset by its increased product margins. “This was not addressed on the conference call, and it’s something I’ll be watching going forward.”
However, there are serious questions regarding whether Everpure’s growth momentum has peaked. For the current quarter, it’s forecasting sales of between $1.5 billion and $1.52 billion, which would amount to growth of between 42% and 43%.
The forecast is still ahead of the Street’s target of $1.49 billion in sales, but in order to keep accelerating its growth, it would need to generate fourth-quarter revenue of at least $1.6 billion, which is about $83 million higher than the top end of its forecast range. That’s not impossible, because Everpure actually beat the top end of its range by $125 million in the quarter just gone.
McDowell said one reason to be optimistic that Everpure can keep accelerating is that it has spent the last year expanding its offerings, without showing any material impact on its bottom line from those efforts. “Its hyperscale business is only just starting to impact revenue, so most of this growth has been from its traditional products,” the analyst said. “That tells me there’s still significant upside to come.”
Even if Everpure’s momentum slows, it’s still on track to deliver an impressive financial year. The company also raised its full-year revenue guidance from a prior range of $5.03 billion to $5.07 billion to a new range of $5.2 billion to $5.21 billion. Wall Street analysts are modeling full-year sales of $5.06 billion.

articles.title: Hackers target big brands like McDonald’s, Bayer, CarMax in new phishing scam
articles.text:
Hackers target big brands like McDonald’s, Bayer, CarMax in new phishing scam
Typosquatted attacks just became a lot more dangerous
- Attackers rapidly registered lookalike domains matching newly launched brand campaigns to capture mistyped traffic
- Typosquatting targeted major brands including McDonald’s, Bayer, CarMax, and Procter & Gamble
- Researchers warn these domains can enable phishing, credential theft, malvertising, and other scams before detection
Cybercriminals have reportedly found a way to make typosquatted domain scams more convincing, and are already trying out new campaigns, researchers are saying.
Security experts Symantec have outlined how they saw attackers targeting victims with typosquatted names of popular companies such as CarMax, McDonald’s, and Procter & Gamble.
Many people don’t pay close attention to spelling or typos, and threat actors turned it into a criminal enterprise. A malicious executable called Excsel.exe has a higher chance of being launched compared to one called malware-v2.exe. The same goes for websites - Goggle.com or, Facebook.com can be typed and navigated to without a second thought, and visitors who do that often risk losing their sensitive files or infecting their computers with malware.
The practice is called typosquatting and can be found all over the web - on websites, in file names, email addresses, social media profiles, and even mobile applications. But typosquatted domains have a rather short lifespan - they get flagged by users rather quickly and taken down by either domain registrars, or even law enforcement.
Typosquatting with a twist
But what if the victims couldn’t tell if the domain was typosquatted? What if the legitimate one is so fresh that it hasn’t yet established itself in the eyes and the browsers of its target audience? The idea obviously crossed some cybercriminals’ minds, since Symantec recently uncovered just that - typosquatted domains that were registered within a day of the legitimate one.
Symantec says it saw legitimate businesses registering a new domain through a corporate brand-protection registrar, and the crooks following up a day later with a registration of their own - on a Chinese domain registrar.
“Each time a client of CSC (Corporation Service Company) or MarkMonitor registered a new campaign domain, a one-letter lookalike was registered the next day through a China-based registrar. The pattern repeated 27 times, across domains belonging to Abbott Laboratories, Bayer, CarMax, McDonald’s, Procter & Gamble and Sanofi, among others,” Symantec explained.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“In one case, CarMax registered carmaxclaims[.]com and kmxclaims[.]com through CSC on August 26. The next day, carmaxclaim[.]com and kmxclaim[.]com, each one letter shorter, were registered through a registrar in China. The campaign has not stopped. The same pattern appeared again as recently as November 11, 2026.”
The scam is genius on a number of levels. Not only are these domains infinitely harder to spot as being fake, but visitors who open them expect to hand over sensitive, personally identifiable data. “Most were campaign sites rather than corporate home pages, including patient-savings programs, sweepstakes, rebates, claims portals and legal settlements,” the researchers said.
What's the point?
Some of the names being abused in this campaign include Abbott Laboratories, Arlo Technology, Bayer, Beam Suntory, Bristol-Myers Squibb, CarMax, Greystar, Immunovant, Ipsos, Kroll, McDonald’s, Procter & Gamble and Sanofi.
Another reason why these scams are dangerous is the fact that these addresses are often printed, shown on television advertisements, distributed through pharmacy leaflets, or court-ordered settlement notices. As such, visitors often end up typing the addresses by hand, increasing the chances of landing on the wrong page.
In all 27 examples Symantec observed, the changes were in a single letter. The majority were simply singular versus plural - if the legitimate domain is ‘fyzadasavings’, the attackers would register ‘fyzadasaving’. Same goes for mypgsweeps, or healthspringproducers. Some added a single letter, while others dropped it.
The full list can be found on this link, but since the researchers said the scam was ongoing, it most likely is not exhaustive.
The endgame of the campaign is up for debate. All sites served one of three kinds of content - either a placeholder page that earned money via pay-per-click advertising feeds, scam blogs written around the typosquatted name, or fake search engines. But Symantec believes low-grade scam traffic may not be the end goal, and that advertising networks of this kind can be abused for malvertising and credential harvesting, as well.

articles.title: Nvidia buscó al jefe de Arm, Rene Haas, para reemplazar a Jensen Huang
articles.text:
La firma de reclutamiento Heidrick & Struggles contactó a Rene Haas, director ejecutivo de Arm, para ofrecerle el puesto más alto de Nvidia, según informó Bloomberg el 18 de noviembre. El directorio de la empresa de chips contrató a la consultora para buscar al sucesor de Jensen Huang, que renunció la semana pasada.
Bloomberg citó a una persona familiar con el proceso. La consultora también empezó a consultar a otros ejecutivos que podrían ocupar el cargo. Ni Nvidia ni Arm confirmaron públicamente el contacto con Haas.
El contacto no implica que Haas haya aceptado ni que Nvidia haya decidido. El proceso de selección sigue abierto, según los reportes.
El presidente del directorio, Harvey Jones, confirmó el 17 de noviembre, en la llamada de resultados trimestrales, que la empresa contrató a Heidrick & Struggles. Dijo que evaluarán candidatos internos y externos y que la búsqueda será “minuciosa”, sin apresurar la elección antes de encontrar a la persona exacta.
Jones también afirmó que el directorio “no tiene intención de reincorporar” a Huang. Horas antes, Huang había escrito en la red social X que se sentiría honrado de volver si el directorio lo decidiera.
Un candidato con pasado en Nvidia
Haas dirige Arm desde 2022. Según el Financial Times, trabajó unos siete años en Nvidia antes de irse a Arm en 2013, mantiene buena relación con Huang y con algunos miembros del directorio, y fue mentoreado por el fundador de Nvidia.
El diario británico, que ya había informado el 13 de noviembre de un acercamiento del directorio a Haas, lo describió como uno de los pocos candidatos externos posibles, junto con Lisa Su, directora ejecutiva de AMD, rival de Nvidia. Entre los internos mencionó a la directora financiera Colette Kress y a Ian Buck, responsable del negocio de centros de datos.
The Wall Street Journal informó el 17 de noviembre que la búsqueda la lidera Jeff Sanders, socio de Heidrick, y que Haas figuraba entre los candidatos con los que la firma estaba en conversaciones.
Nvidia intentó comprar Arm por USD 40.000 millones en 2020, pero la operación se cayó por objeciones de los reguladores, según el Financial Times. Arm, cuya tecnología está presente en la mayoría de los chips de teléfonos y también en equipos de Nvidia, lanzó este año su propio chip completo para inteligencia artificial, lo que la puso a competir con parte de sus clientes.
Haas también se acercó a SoftBank: el Financial Times informó que su jefe, Masayoshi Son, lo puso a cargo del negocio internacional del grupo japonés en abril.
Una transición bajo presión
Huang renunció el 12 de noviembre como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del directorio, después de que la empresa hablara de conductas personales incompatibles con su código de conducta. El Financial Times informó que mantuvo relaciones con una subordinada y con una ejecutiva de Megaspeed, cliente de Nvidia con sede en Singapur, a quien los servicios de inteligencia de Estados Unidos consideran una posible espía de China.
Kress es directora ejecutiva interina sin dejar la dirección financiera. En la misma llamada, Nvidia informó ingresos trimestrales de USD 115.800 millones y la creación de un comité de seguridad nacional y control de exportaciones dentro del directorio. Huang debe declarar ante legisladores estadounidenses el 1 de diciembre, según The Verge.

articles.title: Hey, you stuffing cash into your mattress — this series of unfortunate tech outages is not connected, nor is it the end of our digital world
articles.text:
Hey, you stuffing cash into your mattress — this series of unfortunate tech outages is not connected, nor is it the end of our digital world
Fear-mongering isn't helping anyone
"What's going on?!" my commuter friend asked me, wild-eyed. "They told us to start stockpiling water, go to the bank, take out our money!" When I asked her who, she mentioned a mainstream media outlet.
I locked eyes with her to make sure I had her full attention: "Don't do that. This is not a calamity. It's not the end of the tech world."
"But… but… it's all happening. How could it all happen at once?"
"I know, it's an incredible coincidence, but that's also all it is, a coincidence."
She breathed a sigh of relief, and I could actually see the stress leaving her face. For the moment — perhaps until the next outage — she was soothed.
There's no arguing that this has been an unprecedented couple of weeks as we daisy-chained our way through one seemingly massive tech outage after another.
One damn thing after another
It started with Microsoft, and notably Microsoft Outlook, an email platform used by, according to some measures, half a billion people. Considering that Windows is still, according to StatCounter, used by over 76% of desktops, it stands to reason that many would also be using Outlook and other affected Microsoft services like Teams and Copilot.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
A day later, the US Fedral Aviation Authority called a very rare total US ground stop because of a telecommunications issue.
And hours after that, several US banks, specifically Chase (one of the biggest), were reporting that customers could not access their accounts via the app, and sometimes while physically at the bank locations.
But wait, there's more.
United delayed many departing flights while it worked out a tech issue. Then Apple's online services, including iCloud and some access to in-store services, were out for hours.
It's a lot, and people can be forgiven for thinking this all has to be connected.
In a way, they were, but not by a coordinated cyberattack, or even by the growing use of AI. No, they were all connected by the human- and built-in frailties of large-scale digital systems serving millions of people, and because we now live our lives digitally, any disruption is felt instantly by seemingly everyone.
In almost every instance, the companies and governing bodies reported that their hardware and/or software failed because of updates. Apple said its outage was due to an "internal update," while the FAA is now pointing to system-wide updates and one very overactive router.
Chase Bank blamed a software release that broke its own hardware, and United called its outage that impacted flight crews a "technology outage".
Finger, point at yourself
Basically, for all of these outages, the call was coming from inside the building. There were zero signs of cyberattacks or, say, a denial of service attack, where hackers try to overload servers with requests in order to bring down systems and sometimes gain access. No one reported malware attacks or ransomware.
While there's been some conjecture that the FAA outage was related to it trying to apply artificial intelligence to its antiquated system, the real culprit — that router — was far more mundane.
People, however, do not like coincidences. They were raised, after all, on the axiom: where there's smoke, there's fire. It does not help that some media, including TMZ, The New York Post, and the outlet my friend was watching, are stoking these fears with alarming and unfounded headlines.
Look at this front page (below). I honestly feel for the guy they dressed up as a prophet of doom; he looks like he's 15. At least they included the line "...but don't panic, experts say."
Speaking of alarmists, I don't know what TMZ was thinking with this story. Basically, it took a relatively hidden hack of Optimizely, which is apparently used by many sites, and turned it into a massive, global cyberattack. Except no one saw or felt it. As this story was running, I was on a very unhacked Zoom.
Running such a story when tensions, confusion, and anxiety are so high goes well past the point of irresponsible.
If there is a lesson in what's happened here, it's that these systems are fragile, and that we're still doing a poor job of QA testing before releasing updates into the wild.
Microsoft apparently did what it needed to do to test its Outlook update, but those tests didn't account for the scale of activity the patch would face in the wild. The FAA, meanwhile, apparently made the rookie error of applying an update during the busiest working hours.
This isn't the end... it's the beginning
The other lesson I take from this is that we're likely to see more of these outages. After all, infrastructure continues to age, and we have to swap out the old for new.
The age of AI means we'll be deploying powerful new patches that will be more efficient than ever, but, being AI, they may be slightly unpredictable, interacting with systems we didn't expect, or test for.
There's also the concept of shared infrastructure. Over the past few years, we've seen dozens of sites and services go down because a widely shared platform went offline. The best example might be cloud services. Many services do not host their sites and leave it to, for instance, Amazon Web Services. If AWS goes down, so do so many websites.
We've also seen patches that sit between services and widely used platforms like Windows take hundreds of sites and services down with them.
Finally, the power of AI is open to everyone, including hackers, who have been using it to scale up their cyberattacks. What once took a team of hackers now takes one and a legion of AI agents to find previously hidden vulnerabilities in — yes — ageing software.
So, we're not out of the woods. If anything, we're entering the digital age's forbidden forest. But for now, despite the past calamitous tech week, I think we can rest easy. This was not coordinated. This was not an attack. It was just a combination of sloppiness, and some very bad luck.
