articles.title: Supermicro Ships First All-Flash Storage Servers, Delivering PCIe Gen 6 Performance and Broad Software-Defined Storage Support
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
Supermicro Ships First All-Flash Storage Servers, Delivering PCIe Gen 6 Performance and Broad Software-Defined Storage Support
Supermicro, Inc., an AI, Enterprise, Storage, and 5G/Edge Total IT Solution Provider featuring Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS), today announced new extensions to the broad portfolio of AMD EPYC based all-flash storage servers. The first systems, now shipping, include the Petascale system powered by the 6th Gen AMD EPYC 9006 Series processors (formerly codenamed "Venice"), with more products to follow as AMD launches new SP8 CPU versions. These are the first storage products supporting the PCIe Gen 6 I/O specification with 100% greater sequential read bandwidth over PCIe Gen 5.
Vik Malyala, chief business officer at Supermicro"Expanding AI and HPC workloads require storage that can match the performance of today's CPU and GPU clusters," "With our new all-flash storage servers based on AMD EPYC processors, and the flexibility of the DCBBS architecture, we are delivering improved PCIe Gen 6 bandwidth, high density, and scalable capacity. These platforms can be customized for HPC, AI training, and inference workloads, while providing software-defined storage partners with proven, validated systems they can rely on."
Supermicro will be showing the new Petascale all-flash storage server in booth #4017 at Supercomputing 2026, in Chicago, November 15-20.
The first system in the new family packs exceptional density into a 2U chassis with support for up to 32 E3.S NVMe SSDs—delivering as much as 3.93 PB of capacity with 122 TB drives. Its balanced I/O architecture supports up to four x16 high-performance networking cards, enabling the sustained bandwidth required for AI data lakes, large-scale analytics, and high-throughput storage networking while giving customers the flexibility to optimize for their specific workload and fabric requirements.
Supporting Partner Quotes
AMD
"We have worked with Supermicro for years, bringing AMD EPYC processing capabilities to Petascale all-flash servers," said Dan McNamara, senior vice president and general manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD. "As software-defined storage architectures demand greater energy efficiency, high single-socket performance, and large numbers of PCIe lanes, the AMD EPYC family is ideally suited. The latest Venice SP7 and SP8 platforms deliver the core density and PCIe Gen 6 connectivity that modern storage workloads require."
Hammerspace
"The future of AI infrastructure is about maximizing performance per dollar, per watt, and per rack," said Gregg Machon, SVP Business Development & Worldwide Partners Hammerspace. "Supermicro's new Petascale platform delivers exceptional NVMe performance density and efficiency. With Hammerspace's standards-based Data Platform, customers can easily incorporate this high-performance storage into a single global namespace alongside existing, cost-optimized capacity storage. This gives organizations the performance AI workloads demand, while maximizing infrastructure utilization, avoiding costly over-provisioning, and delivering better overall price-performance." 
IBM
"AI inference is no longer a single workload - it's a pipeline that spans data ingest, model loading, retrieval, and KV cache and each stage must maximize GPU utilization efficiency," said Vincent Hsu, IBM Fellow, VP & CTO of IBM Storage. "IBM Storage Scale on Supermicro's newest AMD-based Petascale server is designed to give customers a high-performance, resilient platform for the entire inference pipeline, with PCIe Gen 6 bandwidth and greater headroom for both performance and capacity growth.
MinIO
"Supermicro's new Petascale platform offers a compelling foundation for the full AI data pipeline," said Ugur Tigli, MinIO CTO. "Combined with MinIO AIStor and MemKV, it becomes a data and memory foundation for modern AI infrastructure. Enterprises can put its dense flash capacity and PCIe Gen 6 bandwidth to work across ingestion, training, and inference, serving all of their throughput, IOPS, and latency needs. Together, we're helping customers build a compact foundation that delivers performance and capacity from every rack unit."
Nutanix
"Unlocking the value of agentic AI requires seamless optimization across compute, networking, and storage. Nutanix is thrilled to expand its full-stack agentic AI collaboration with Supermicro and AMD," said Ketan Shah, SVP, Product Management, Nutanix. By bringing together AMD EPYC processors, Supermicro's high-density Petascale all-flash platform, and Nutanix software-defined storage with built-in data security, we are giving customers a secure validated AI platform that fuels real-time inference, retrieval, and data-intensive enterprise workloads at scale.
Scality
"Scality has recently introduced new storage solutions for AI, including Autonomous Data Infrastructure (ADI) and AI Inference Factory, building on our ongoing collaboration with Supermicro," said Paul Speciale, chief strategy officer, Scality. "The latest Petascale platform provides an ideal foundation for these solutions, delivering the performance and scalability our customers require."
VAST Data
"AI infrastructure is not one-size-fits-all, and our longstanding partnership with Supermicro is built around giving customers the flexibility to deploy the right infrastructure for their workloads," said Phil Manez, vice president, Global Partnerships at VAST Data. "With Supermicro's latest AMD EPYC-based systems, we're expanding that choice, combining the performance and efficiency of the VAST AI Operating System with next-generation hardware to help customers optimize for performance, cost, power, and scale."
VDURA
"VDURA's software-defined data platform runs on Supermicro's latest Petascale systems built on AMD's Venice CPU," said Ken Claffey, CEO of VDURA. "With Supermicro's broad all-flash and HDD platforms unified in a single VDURA namespace, together we deliver more performance per watt and per rack unit at the best cost per terabyte, so customers can maximize the efficiency of their AI infrastructure."
WEKA
"AI labs and neoclouds want more performance for less power in the smallest footprint, and that's where our partnership with Supermicro truly delivers. WEKA NeuralMesh is fully software-defined and distributed, so it scales uniformly across Supermicro's new Petascale server and puts the full bandwidth of PCIe Gen 6 and AMD EPYC 9006 processors to work from day one, with no hardware tiers to create bottlenecks. That's how NeuralMesh keeps pushing throughput higher and latency lower as AI workloads evolve. Together, we're giving customers the performance density that large-scale training and inference demand," said Ajay Singh, chief product officer at WEKA.

articles.title: ¿Hay que dejar la puerta de la lavadora abierta tras sacar la ropa? La respuesta la tiene la microbiología
articles.text:
Cuando la lavadora acaba y se saca la ropa para tenderla, hay una pregunta que puede rondar muchas cabezas: ¿hay que dejar la puerta de la lavadora abierta para que 'respire' o es mejor cerrarla? Aquí podemos decir que hay dos filosofías muy diferentes, ya que hay gente que por estética o por el hecho de no tropezar cree firmemente que lo mejor es mantenerlo cerrado.
Es un debate. Ante una pregunta que es bastante recurrente en el día a día, los fabricantes como Miele o Siemens se han pronunciado, al igual que también lo ha hecho la propia OCU. Y aquí la opinión es bastante unánime al apuntar que, tras sacar la ropa mojada, lo mejor es dejar tanto la puerta como el cajetín del detergente abiertos para que se seque todo el interior.
El miedo. El principal freno para muchos usuarios es la presión a la que se someten las bisagras cuando la puerta se queda abierta durante mucho tiempo. Pero aquí los fabricantes apuntan a que estos componentes están preparados para soportar la carga de la puerta cuando está abierta sin ningún tipo de problema.
Pero además de pensar en la puerta, los fabricantes también han tenido en cuenta la posibilidad de que alguien se apoye ligeramente sobre ella al cargar o descargar la ropa. Es por ello que dejarla abierta no supone ningún esfuerzo.
En microbiología. Una vez tenemos en cuenta que la bisagra no va a sufrir por dejar la lavadora abierta, la pregunta que debemos hacernos es: ¿por qué? Aquí es donde entra el miedo de que aparezcan unos invitados indeseados en la lavadora, como son los hongos. Pero el problema aquí no es el tambor, que suele quedar prácticamente escurrido, sino que debemos fijarnos en la parte inferior de esa goma donde queda atrapada una pequeña piscina de agua residual mezclada con restos de detergente, suavizante, fibras y hasta grasa.
Y es algo que tiene todo el sentido, porque si se cierra la puerta inmediatamente después del lavado, esa mezcla de agua y materia orgánica se evapora a un ritmo muy lento. Esto hace que los microorganismos tengan un auténtico paraíso para poder proliferar e ir pasando de colada en colada.
Lo que vive. Cuando esa humedad se cronifica, la goma deja de ser un simple aislante para convertirse en un ecosistema complejo dominado por biopelículas, hongos y bacterias. En 2015, un estudio publicado en Fungal Biology analizó 70 lavadoras domésticas en Eslovenia y detectó hongos en el 79 % de ellas, destacando especies como las especies Fusarium, Exophiala o Candida parapsilosis, hongos oportunistas capaces de provocar infecciones en la piel, las uñas o los ojos en personas que estén inmunodeprimidas.
Pero es algo que se ha seguido viendo, ya que un estudio publicado en 2023 elevó la presencia de hongos al 82% de las lavadoras analizadas, señalando los pliegues internos de la goma como el punto de mayor densidad de colonización. Además, un análisis comparativo publicado en Frontiers in Microbiology en 2025 observó que las lavadoras de carga frontal albergan una carga microbiana notablemente superior a las de carga superior, aunque puede existir algún sesgo de fondo.
El olor. En el terreno bacteriano, el protagonista indiscutible del clásico olor a «trapo húmedo» en la ropa recién lavada tiene nombre propio desde que investigadores de la compañía japonesa Kao publicaron un estudio clave: Moraxella osloensis. Esta bacteria sobrevive bien al lavado y metaboliza los restos de sebo y proteínas, liberando compuestos volátiles responsables de ese olor tan característico.
Hay una excepción. Aunque dejar la puerta abierta es el hábito más eficaz para frenar este ciclo, los especialistas apuntan a que si la lavadora está instalada en un sótano húmedo, un garaje cerrado o un cuarto de lavado sin ventilación, dejar la puerta abierta de par en par puede resultar ineficaz e incluso contraproducente si la humedad ambiental es más alta que la del propio tambor.
Pero además, en ambientes muy secos, calurosos o expuestos al sol directo, mantener la goma completamente al aire durante meses sin usar el aparato puede acelerar su resequedad y agrietamiento a largo plazo. En esos escenarios basta con dejar la puerta simplemente entornada para permitir un mínimo intercambio de aire sin castigar el elastómero.

articles.title: AMD’s Twitter brag that it ‘loves gamers’ met with savage Community Note
articles.text:
AMD’s Twitter brag that it ‘loves gamers’ met with savage Community Note — post met with backlash over the company’s pivot to AI
The company said it 'values its interactions with gamers above all else'
AMD Japan's X account has been met with sharp reproach after claiming the company loves gamers and values its interactions with gamers above all else, with commenters and even a community note expressing dissent at the sentiment, owing to AMD's comments on its "data center-first" ethos and a commitment to AI that has driven the price of consumer PC gaming up to nearly unaffordable levels.
Quoting a Tom's Hardware post on the X social network discussing CEO Dr. Lisa Su meeting gamers and autographing a GPU, the AMD Japan account was quick to seize the moment. "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else," the post read, but it was met with a stark reminder that gamers don't feel the same way. The post soon received a new community note that pointed out that AMD's own CEO doesn't agree. In fact, Su was quoted as saying that AMD is now "a data center-first company," with the note also pointing to the fact that AMD's data center revenue increased 97% year-over-year, as per its Q3 2026 earnings report. That equates to around $8.5 billion in revenue, while client and gaming revenue fell 8% to $3.7 billion. Gaming alone was down 40%.
At the time, Su said that AMD expected its server revenue to double year over year in 2027, with its data center AI revenue growing at an even faster rate. "As a result, we expect data center to be more than eighty percent of our total revenue in 2027 and to drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth," the CEO said during the company's earnings call.
By comparison, the same call heard Su say that, in 2027, AMD was "planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage." With this all in mind, it's perhaps no surprise that the AMD Japan X account stirred such a strong response from gamers who feel that AMD has left them behind in search of a more lucrative data center market. AMD is certainly not alone in that regard. Nvidia, once the darling of the PC component enthusiast, is now focused on AI data center components instead. The company's high-performance AI chips are so capable that they're export-controlled, something that, among other reasons, will put former CEO Jensen Huang in front of a House Foreign Affairs panel in December.
As for AMD, its ill-timed, misjudged X post ended with "AMD loves gamers." Gamers would appear to disagree.

Oliver Haslam has written about technology of all shapes and sizes for over 15 years, both online and in print. He's fascinated by how personal computing continues to change as tower PCs give way to foldable phones and beyond.

Even after the AI growth blows, AI datacenters will have to be maintained and updated that will turn into a more consistent and predictable revenue, which may keep AMD AI focused, but not gamer focused despite the internal staff's passion. articles.title: Google alerta: era de ataques cibernéticos autônomos já começou • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google alerta: era de ataques cibernéticos autônomos já começou
Relatório de segurança identificou sistemas de IA que encontram falhas e criam ataques sem intervenção humana.
A era dos ataques cibernéticos autônomos já começou, segundo o Google. Em um novo relatório de segurança, a empresa afirma que criminosos estão utilizando agentes de inteligência artificial capazes de identificar vulnerabilidades em programas, desenvolver códigos maliciosos e executar ataques sem depender de comandos humanos.
O alerta foi divulgado pelo Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) na segunda-feira (16/11). O grupo identificou uma evolução no uso de IA por hackers, que passaram de consultas a chatbots para sistemas capazes de coordenar diferentes etapas de uma invasão.
Para o Google, a velocidade dessas ferramentas representa um desafio para equipes de segurança que ainda dependem de análises e respostas manuais. Uma das descobertas envolve um sistema chamado exploit_agent, encontrado pelos pesquisadores em um servidor de testes exposto na internet. A ferramenta utilizava diferentes modelos de IA para analisar atualizações de softwares e identificar possíveis vulnerabilidades.
Na prática, o sistema comparava versões antigas e atualizadas dos programas para descobrir quais falhas haviam sido corrigidas. A partir dessas informações, criava códigos para explorar as brechas e executava testes automaticamente, sem exigir aprovação humana a cada etapa. O Google também encontrou dados extraídos de vítimas e ferramentas que poderiam ser utilizadas após a invasão.
Os indícios apontam para interesse em sites franceses dos setores de mídia, entretenimento e educação. O relatório também cita as ferramentas CAIRN e PentAGI, que coordenam diferentes agentes de IA. Segundo o Google, elas já foram identificadas em atividades de invasão e busca por vulnerabilidades nos Estados Unidos e na Ásia.
O avanço representa uma mudança em relação aos malwares com IA identificados anteriormente pelo Google. Na ocasião, especialistas apontaram limitações nas primeiras tentativas de usar modelos generativos para modificar códigos maliciosos. Agora, a preocupação é que agentes consigam reduzir o intervalo entre a divulgação de uma vulnerabilidade e a sua exploração por criminosos.
Para enfrentar as novas ameaças, o Google está ampliando o uso de ferramentas automatizadas de segurança visando identificar riscos e acelerar a correção de falhas. A ideia é permitir que sistemas de defesa analisem programas, priorizem vulnerabilidades e respondam a incidentes em uma velocidade próxima à dos ataques automatizados.
O tema já havia aparecido em uma investigação anterior. Em maio, o Google afirmou ter bloqueado uma tentativa de ataque desenvolvida com auxílio de IA. Outras empresas também identificaram o uso da tecnologia em ataques reais. A Anthropic relatou uma campanha envolvendo o Claude, na qual criminosos teriam automatizado grande parte das operações contra organizações de diferentes países.
Apesar dos avanços, o relatório do Google ressalta que as ferramentas autônomas ainda apresentam limitações e podem produzir códigos ineficazes, cometer erros e deixar rastros que facilitam a identificação das invasões. Ainda assim, a capacidade de executar mais ataques em menos tempo reforça a importância de corrigir vulnerabilidades rapidamente.

articles.title: La Macif écope d'une amende de 5 millions d'euros : les mots de passe étaient laissés à la merci des pirates
articles.text:
La Cnil, soit le gendarme des données personnelles, a annoncé une amende de cinq millions d’euros infligée à une société qui n’a pas été nommée. Cependant, selon les informations de BFMT Tech, il s’agit de la Macif, la société de groupe d’assurance mutuelle. Pourquoi une telle amende ? Lors d’un contrôle, la Cnil a constaté deux manquements importants au RGPD, le règlement européen sur les données personnelles.
Des mots de passe stockés en clair et des données conservées pendant plus de 10 ans
Avant toute chose, précisons que la Cnil a anonymisé la société qui s’est vue infliger une amende de cinq millions d’euros, car elle voulait que sa délibération soit publiée « à des fins pédagogiques ». En fin de compte, il semble y avoir peu de doute quant à l’identité de cette société. En effet, BFM Tech a contacté la Macif, qui reconnaît être concernée et « prend acte » de la décision de la Cnil.
Qu’est-il reproché à la Macif ? D’une part, l’entreprise française a stocké en clair les mots de passe de ses clients et leurs réponses aux questions de sécurité, sans aucune protection donc. Selon BFM Tech, 1,8 million de mots de passe étaient stockés en clair. Les identifiants, adresses e-mail et mots de passe étaient par ailleurs partagés sur des plateformes non sécurisées. Un employé de la société pouvait donc avoir accès à ces données confidentielles simplement en accédant à l’une de ces plateformes. À ce titre, le site spécialisé Cyberattaque.org assure qu’un compte administrateur a été partagé entre huit salariés.
D’autre part, la Cnil a constaté que la société conservait des données confidentielles de certains de ses clients (provenant notamment de formulaires de contact) depuis « plus de dix ans ». Le gendarme des données personnelles a estimé que cela « est excessif une fois la demande du client traitée ». De son côté, la plateforme Cyberattaque.org rapporte que certaines données confidentielles ont été conservées durant 21 ans. Selon BFM Tech, la Macif aurait dû garder ces données durant un an au maximum.
La Macif assure avoir pris des mesures
Contactée par BFM Tech, la Macif s’est dite « attachée au respect de la protection des données de ses clients » et assure avoir collaboré « pleinement et entièrement » avec la Cnil durant son contrôle. L’entreprise précise ensuite : « Nous tenons à rassurer nos clients sur le fait qu’aucune de leurs données n’a été divulguée ». De son côté, la Cnil précise que la Macif a pris les mesures nécessaires « en cours de procédure », notamment en supprimant l’historique des données.
Il reste un point particulièrement important à souligner : aucune fuite de données n’a été constatée à ce jour. Si de sérieux manquements ont bel et bien été constatés par la Cnil, la Macif n’a pas été victime de cyberattaque et n’est donc pas dans l’obligation de contacter ses clients.

articles.title: GTA 6 podría vaciar oficinas en su lanzamiento: uno de cada cinco trabajadores planea pedir el día libre
articles.text:
El estreno de GTA 6 podría traducirse en ausencias laborales: el 18% de los trabajadores consultados en Estados Unidos planea pedir el día libre para jugar. Tras 13 años sin una nueva entrega principal, Grand Theft Auto VI llega a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S con una expectativa que ya se refleja en calendarios de vacaciones y decisiones de empresas.
Un análisis de BambooHR detectó que las solicitudes de tiempo libre para el 19 de noviembre son casi un 13% superiores a las registradas en jueves equivalentes de 2024 y 2025. La expresión “GTA flu”, o gripe GTA, comenzó a circular para describir posibles ausencias relacionadas con el estreno.
El mayor salto, sin embargo, se concentra el viernes 20 de noviembre, antes del fin de semana. Para esa fecha, el 6,04% de los empleados solicitó tiempo libre, un incremento cercano al 28% frente al 4,73% de 2025 y casi el doble del 3,04% de 2024. Las cifras reflejan que el interés por uno de los lanzamientos más esperados de la industria del entretenimiento no solo impacta en el día de su llegada, sino también en la jornada posterior.
Uno de cada cinco trabajadores planea pedir vacaciones
El estudio de BambooHR examinó información de más de 3,4 millones de empleados en Estados Unidos y realizó una encuesta a más de 1.500 trabajadores asalariados. El 18% de las personas consultadas indicó que planeaba solicitar el día libre para el lanzamiento.
El porcentaje aumenta entre los grupos más jóvenes. El 32% de los integrantes de la generación Z consultados dijo que tenía previsto ausentarse del trabajo el 19 de noviembre. Entre los millennials, la cifra llega al 27%.
Las solicitudes de vacaciones también muestran un aumento respecto de otros años, aunque los datos disponibles no permiten determinar cuántas estarán ligadas exclusivamente a GTA 6. La coincidencia entre la salida del juego y el pico de pedidos de tiempo libre alimentó el debate sobre el impacto del entretenimiento digital en las rutinas de trabajo.
El lanzamiento ocurrirá después de una espera de 13 años desde Grand Theft Auto V, publicado en 2013. La longevidad de aquella entrega ayudó a mantener la franquicia presente durante más de una década a través de ventas, actualizaciones y actividad en línea.
Compañías que ofrecerán una jornada adicional a sus empleados
Algunas empresas decidieron incorporar la expectativa por los videojuegos a sus beneficios internos. Logitech, fabricante de accesorios y dispositivos tecnológicos, anunció una jornada adicional de descanso para más de 7.000 empleados en todo el mundo.
La compañía denominó el beneficio Logi Game Day. El día libre no estará limitado a GTA 6: cada trabajador podrá emplearlo para jugar al título que elija.
La medida reconoce una práctica que muchas personas realizan con sus vacaciones personales: reservar jornadas para estrenos de cine, conciertos, eventos deportivos o videojuegos. En este caso, el alcance de la franquicia llevó a una empresa tecnológica a formalizar esa posibilidad dentro de su esquema de descanso.
El fenómeno también llegó a una instalación militar de Georgia. El 9.º Batallón de Ingenieros de Brigada, ubicado en Fort Stewart, ofreció cuatro días adicionales de permiso a soldados elegibles que renovaran su contrato por al menos dos años.
Una unidad del Ejército vinculó permisos con la fecha de salida
La licencia especial coincidió con el lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto VI. Según Associated Press, al menos 20 militares habían aceptado el incentivo hasta agosto, dentro de un grupo de cerca de 130 soldados que podían acceder a la propuesta.
La decisión muestra cómo el estreno se convirtió en una referencia incluso fuera de la industria del ocio. En España, un docente aplazó un examen del 23 al 30 de noviembre y eliminó deberes y trabajos de la semana para no coincidir con la salida del videojuego.
También se prevén efectos en sectores vinculados al consumo doméstico. La jornada de estreno podría aumentar la demanda de servicios de comida a domicilio, mientras que la ambientación del juego en una versión ficticia de Miami puede reavivar el interés por esa ciudad.
Las estimaciones que calculan pérdidas de productividad o ausencias masivas no han sido confirmadas por empresas ni autoridades. Por eso, los datos de BambooHR ofrecen una referencia más concreta sobre las intenciones expresadas por trabajadores consultados, aunque no anticipan con certeza el comportamiento real del jueves.
La franquicia Grand Theft Auto comenzó en 1997 y se aproxima a 480 millones de unidades distribuidas en todas sus entregas. GTA V ha distribuido cerca de 235 millones de copias en el mundo, según los resultados financieros más recientes de Take-Two Interactive, empresa matriz de Rockstar Games.

articles.title: Flipper One raises more than €10 million on Kickstarter in just 24 hours
articles.text:
Linux Hacking FTW: Earlier this year, Flipper Devices announced a brand-new cyberdeck aimed at power users and hacking enthusiasts. Now that the Flipper One has launched its Kickstarter campaign, customers are pouring millions of dollars into pre-orders. The crowdfunding price is discounted, but quantities are limited, so get yours while you still can.
The Flipper One Kickstarter campaign is now live, and the developers have already raised more than €10,700,000 against an initial funding target of €272,981. Interest in the new Linux-based hacking tool is clearly strong, but Flipper Devices warns that it is not simply a more powerful replacement for the previously released Flipper Zero.
The company describes the Flipper One as a portable, standalone Linux computer based on the Arm architecture and designed to support a wide range of security-focused applications. The device can be used to build custom computing projects, analyze network signals, experiment with wireless communications, watch an MKV movie in a hotel room, and much more.
Flipper Devices emphasizes that the Flipper One and Flipper Zero are two fundamentally different devices designed for distinct security and hacking workflows. The Zero features a low-power microcontroller and functions as a "layer zero" networking multi-tool, offering access to various protocols and technologies including NFC, RFID, sub-GHz radio, and UART.
The Flipper One, meanwhile, is a "layer one" tool designed to work with virtually anything that offers IP connectivity. The new device supports Wi-Fi, Ethernet, 5G, and satellite communications. It also offers full support for the mainline Linux kernel and enough computing power to handle software-defined radio applications and local AI models.
The Flipper One combines a high-performance Arm system-on-chip (Rockchip RK3576) with a low-power Raspberry Pi microcontroller (RP2350). This architecture allows the device to remain operational even if users manage to completely break its embedded Linux system.
Some of the Flipper One's capabilities include a desktop mode accessible through USB-C, a network scanner and multi-tool for traffic tunneling and packet analysis, and support for custom cellular antennas and modems in underserved areas. The device also offers several expansion options through external hardware modules and an internal, high-speed M.2 expansion slot.
Flipper One pre-orders are currently priced at $399 (€364), representing a 25% discount off the estimated $550 retail price. Flipper Devices said the Kickstarter price leaves the company with no profit margin, citing the ongoing memory shortage driven by AI demand. Still, the more than €10 million raised in just 24 hours will likely keep the company happy for the time being.
Shipping is expected to begin in July 2027 in most parts of the world. However, the team warns that ongoing component and chip shortages could significantly affect production schedules and delivery dates.

articles.title: 'Hey Copilot, Outlook.com isn't working. Can you fix that?': Microsoft shows off AI troubleshooting a Windows 11 PC — and the haters are out in force
articles.text:
Microsoft shows off Copilot troubleshooting Windows 11 — but this will be for Copilot+ PCs only (and here's why that's a good thing)
New video clip is our first glimpse of AI-based 'local PC diagnostics' in action
- Windows 11 is bringing in a feature for Copilot+ PCs that will troubleshoot problems
- We've heard about this before, but Microsoft has shown off a new demo of the feature working in a video clip
- Because it uses the NPU, this 'PC diagnostics' functionality can stay local, and not tap the cloud, which is good news from a privacy perspective — but doubters remain
Microsoft is working towards a world where if there's a problem with your Windows 11 PC, Copilot will be able to help solve it (or it'll try to, anyway).
Windows Central reports that Microsoft's Ignite conference is underway, and the company has written a blog post about 'Building Windows for the next era of work' that touches on a whole host of topics pertaining to AI and Copilot.
While aimed at the business world, the 'local PC diagnostics' capabilities of Copilot will be usable by consumers, at least if they own a Copilot+ PC, as this feature will run by locally leveraging the NPU (and not via the cloud).
We knew that this was what Microsoft had been angling towards, but the below YouTube clip is the first time we've seen Copilot in action troubleshooting a PC issue — in this case, a problem with Bluetooth headphones.
The user must give the AI permission to access files and read system information, and then it runs a scan on the system (with no changes being made) in an attempt to find the root of the problem.
This can be a multi-step query session (a running troubleshooting conversation) on alternative fixes if the initially proposed solution doesn't produce the goods.
As you may have seen, Microsoft is working on integrating Copilot with the Windows 11 search box (in the taskbar), albeit as an opt-in choice (it won't be on by default, in other words).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Alongside this, Microsoft has a plan for allowing Copilot to deal with files on your local drives, so you can ask the AI in natural language to find, copy or rename files and so on.
As Microsoft puts it: "Tidying a cluttered Downloads folder or pulling project files together takes a sentence."
It's hard to imagine how that might go wrong.
These features are "coming soon" for Copilot+ PCs, we're told.
Analysis: steering clear of the cloud — but not the broader risks that some fear
The idea of Copilot troubleshooting a PC has mainly provoked a mixture of mirth and cynicism on social media. It's worth bearing in mind, though, that you must give Copilot explicit permission to carry out these tasks — and it's also good that the work is done locally. This is because if the AI was carrying out these tasks in the cloud, that would raise concerns around privacy and where the various bits of system information that Copilot is using might end up.
As for that negative reaction, it includes comments from those on Reddit such as: "Hey Copilot, Outlook.com isn't working. Can you fix that?" (A reference to the recent huge Microsoft outage, of course).
Another Redditor jokes about the best possible fix they could envisage for Windows 11: "So it [Copilot] can remove itself?"
Even if the AI is working locally, and on a read-only basis – without any ability to change system settings, so it's just providing advice – there will continue to be Windows 11 users who don't want anything to do with Copilot on their PC. A lot of that is down to much broader trust issues relating to AI in general, but it's also about Microsoft's penchant for bugs (with its monthly updates) — the combination of which is enough to make some folks feel very uncomfortable.

articles.title: Comment libérer de l’espace sur son PC avec ChatGPT ou Claude
articles.text:
Avant de désinstaller un jeu ou de vous lancer dans le tri de vos photos, demandez à ChatGPT ou à Claude ce qui encombre votre PC. Sur le nôtre, une démo avait laissé à elle seule près de 60 Go de fichiers dont on pouvait se passer.
On sait assez bien ce qui prend de la place sur un PC qu’on vient de monter ou d’acheter. Quelques années et quelques dizaines d’installations plus tard, on a une idée beaucoup plus vague de ce qui se cache sur le SSD. Au moment de faire le ménage, c’est souvent un jeu qui en fait les frais, pour la simple raison qu’on sait où le trouver et combien sa désinstallation va rapporter. On pense moins volontiers aux fichiers qu’un logiciel a mis de côté pour gagner du temps la prochaine fois qu’on l’ouvrira. C’est pourtant là qu’on a fait la plus belle trouvaille de cet essai.
L’idée nous est venue en demandant à Hermes, notre agent IA, de regarder ce qui remplissait le disque. Il nous avait proposé plusieurs lots de fichiers à nettoyer, en expliquant pour chacun ce qu’on pouvait gagner et ce qu’on risquait de perdre. On a voulu voir si l’on pouvait obtenir le même coup de main avec ChatGPT, plus accessible qu’Hermes. Voici comment s’y prendre sous Windows, avec ChatGPT ou avec Claude, que votre PC soit équipé d’un SSD ou d’un disque dur.
Peut-on le faire avec un compte gratuit ?
Si vous utilisez ChatGPT, votre compte gratuit suffit. La petite différence avec vos conversations habituelles, c’est qu’il faut ouvrir l’application Windows et y choisir Codex pour que ChatGPT puisse examiner les dossiers de votre PC.
- Assistant IA extrêmement polyvalent
- Fonctionnalités gratuites nombreuses
- Automatisation de tâches complexes
Si vous préférez Claude, l’outil équivalent s’appelle Claude Code et demande au minimum un abonnement Claude Pro. Si vous avez déjà cet abonnement, suivez le parcours Claude ci-dessous. Sinon, le parcours ChatGPT vous évitera de payer pour cet essai.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace
Lancer l’analyse avec ChatGPT
Ouvrez ChatGPT pour Windows, choisissez Codex et démarrez une conversation sur votre ordinateur. Copiez-y le message proposé un peu plus bas. Si l’application vous demande l’autorisation de lire un dossier, regardez lequel et donnez votre accord au fur et à mesure. À ce stade, il s’agit simplement de faire le tour du propriétaire.
Lancer l’analyse avec Claude
Ouvrez Claude pour Windows et cliquez sur « Code » dans la colonne de gauche. Sous la zone où vous écrivez d’habitude, choisissez « Local », puis « Ouvrir un dossier ». Dans la fenêtre qui s’affiche, cliquez sur « Ce PC », puis sur le disque « C: ». C’est là que Claude fera ses recherches. Vous pouvez maintenant lui envoyer le même message qu’à ChatGPT. Le guide de Claude détaille cette étape si les boutons se présentent autrement chez vous.
Le message à copier pour savoir ce qui prend de la place
Avant de commencer, ouvrez l’Explorateur de fichiers de Windows et cliquez sur « Ce PC ». Sous le disque « C: », vous verrez combien de place il reste. Notez le chiffre ou faites une capture d’écran pour pouvoir comparer après le ménage. Dans le message ci-dessous, on laisse de côté les documents personnels et les dossiers synchronisés en ligne, comme OneDrive. Le nom et la taille des fichiers suffisent pour ce premier tri, et une partie des informations communiquées à l’IA peut être traitée en ligne.
Le prompt :
Analyse mon disque C: pour repérer ce qui prend de la place et ce qui pourrait être nettoyé. Pour l’instant, ne supprime, ne déplace et ne modifie rien. Mesure les volumes avec les outils locaux disponibles, sans installer de logiciel supplémentaire.
Présente les principaux dossiers et fichiers volumineux, puis propose des lots de nettoyage numérotés, classés par priorité selon la place récupérable et les conséquences de leur suppression. Pour chaque lot, précise les emplacements, la taille mesurée, l’utilité probable des fichiers et la méthode de nettoyage. Demande-moi si j’utilise encore les applications avant d’en proposer la désinstallation.
Appuie-toi sur les noms, tailles et dates sans ouvrir mes documents personnels. Laisse de côté les dossiers synchronisés avec le cloud et les fichiers uniquement en ligne. Ne propose aucune suppression manuelle des composants Windows, des pilotes, des sauvegardes ou des fichiers de récupération.
Indique les zones que tu n’as pas pu examiner et les mesures incertaines, sans compter deux fois le même espace. Termine par tes recommandations et attends que je choisisse les lots à nettoyer.
La première réponse peut réserver quelques surprises. Sur notre PC, Codex a repéré deux gros fichiers que Windows utilise pour compléter sa mémoire et pour retrouver notre session au réveil de l’ordinateur. Ensemble, ils pèsent près de 35 Go. Ils expliquent donc une bonne partie de l’espace occupé, et on les a laissés là où ils étaient. Si un nom vous laisse perplexe, c’est justement le moment de poser la question qui manque à une simple liste de fichiers : « Si j’efface celui-ci, qu’est-ce qui changera la prochaine fois que j’utiliserai mon PC ? »
Ce qu’on a supprimé, et ce qu’on a préféré garder
Chez nous, le choix a été vite fait pour Electric Dreams, une démo d’Epic. À elle seule, elle avait laissé près de 60 Go de cache, autrement dit des données que le logiciel garde sous la main pour éviter de refaire le même travail au prochain lancement. On a autorisé Codex à vider ce cache ainsi qu’un second, puis à effacer de vieux fichiers temporaires et des comptes rendus de plantage. En revanche, on a tiqué devant un nom que l’on reconnaît moins facilement dans une liste : LLVM. Après explication, il s’agissait d’outils de développement logiciel, qui pouvaient encore être utiles sur cette machine. Pour les quelque 3 Go en jeu, on les a gardés.
Dans notre essai, on a répondu : « tu peux nettoyer les lots 1, 3 et 4. » et nous avons demandé des précisions sur la nature de LLVM. Reprenez les numéros qui correspondent à votre propre liste. Si la liste contient une application que vous n’utilisez plus, désinstallez-la depuis les paramètres de Windows, ou demandez à l’agent de le faire pour vous. Pour ses propres fichiers, Windows propose aussi des recommandations de nettoyage dans Paramètres > Système > Stockage.
Et si vous en profitez pour mettre à la Corbeille quelques vieux téléchargements, pensez à vérifier son contenu avant de la vider. Tant que les fichiers y sont, ils prennent toujours la même place sur le PC.
Après le nettoyage, retournez dans « Ce PC » sur l’explorateur Windows et comparez l’espace libre avec votre premier relevé. Chez nous, Codex annonce 63,9 Gio récupérés, soit environ 69 Go pour les trois lots réunis. Le détail qu’on retiendra, c’est que près de 60 de ces 69 Go dormaient dans le cache d’une seule démo. On aurait pu passer un bon moment à trier nos photos avant d’arriver au même résultat !

LG Electronics USA announced the U.S. launch of the LG gram Book 14, a new Windows 11 Home laptop that combines long battery life, an ultra-light design and a 14-inch display in an accessible package for work, school and entertainment. Available in touchscreen (14U40V-H.AR51U3 and 14U40V-H.AA65U1) and standard (14U40V-G.AR51U3 and 14U40V-G.AA65U1) configurations, the gram Book 14 comes in Titan Silver and Black and is available now at LG.com, starting at $799.99.
Thin, Light and Built to Last
Designed for users who want a slim, lightweight Windows laptop without stepping up to a premium price tier, the gram Book 14 weighs 2.86 pounds and measures just 0.59 inches thick. Its compact design makes it easy to carry between home, school, office and travel.With up to 30.5 hours of video playback from a single charge, it is built to help users stay productive through long workdays, classes and travel without frequently reaching for a charger.
Built for Everyday Productivity
Both gram Book 14 models start from the same strong foundation: the 14-inch WUXGA IPS display at a 16:10 aspect ratio (1920 x 1200), a wider, taller screen format that gives users more room on screen for documents, emails, spreadsheets and web pages without having to scroll as often. The anti-glare coating and 350-nit brightness keep the image comfortable and clear whether working by a window or under office lighting.
AI-enabled features further support productivity, with features like Windows 11 Home with Copilot helping users work smarter and create faster. With the LG gram Link app, users can connect and share content across up to 10 compatible iOS, Android and webOS devices for a more seamless multi-device experience.
Under the hood, both models are powered by the Intel Core 5 processor with 8 GB/16 GB of RAM and 256 GB/512 GB of fast SSD storage, providing enough power to handle everyday multitasking, demanding AI tasks, video calls and creative work without slowdown. A Mega Cooling System keeps everything running smoothly inside the 0.59-inch chassis, so performance stays consistent even during longer work sessions. When users are ready to connect to a bigger screen, HDMI 2.1 handles external displays at up to 4K resolution.
All models feature strong security features, including FHD IR webcam with dual microphone, Windows Hello facial recognition support, Secure Lock and a hardware privacy camera shutter. The gram Book 14 also delivers audio through a stereo speaker with SoundWire audio technology and Dolby Atmos support, providing spatial audio enhancement for video conferencing, content streaming and music playback directly from the built-in speakers.
Multiple Configurations to Match How You Work
The touchscreen configuration adds full touch input and 100% sRGB color coverage, supporting vivid color and direct interaction for photo editing, design work, document annotation and touch-based navigation.
The non-touch models feature the same 14-inch WUXGA IPS with 45% NTSC color coverage anti-glare display with 350-nit brightness and a 60 Hz refresh rate. They share the same processor, two memory configurations (8 GB or 16 GB), storage, battery capacity, connectivity and chassis dimensions as the touchscreen models.
The standard 14U40V-G.AR51U3 and 14U40V-G.AA65U1 gram Book 14 models retail for $799.99 and $1,099.99, while the touchscreen 14U40V-H.AR51U3 and 14U40V-H.AA65U1 gram Book 14 models retail for $829.99 and $1,199.99, respectively, with additional holiday promotions available for a limited time on LG.com. During Best Buy's holiday promotion from November 16 to November 30, the 14U40V-G.AR51U3 and touchscreen 14U40V-H.AR51U3 will be offered at promotional prices of $499.99 and $529.99, respectively. For more information on the full 2026 LG gram lineup, visit LG.com.

articles.text:
Como baixar vídeos de qualquer site
Fazer download de vídeos de sites da internet permite criar uma biblioteca offline no seu dispositivo, ficando menos dependente de conexões
Você pode guardar suas mídias favoritas offline ao utilizar ferramentas especializadas para baixar vídeo de um site. Hoje, existem diferentes meios de fazer download de vídeo de qualquer site diretamente para seu dispositivo e salvar o conteúdo da internet.
Entre as alternativas mais populares, vale instalar uma extensão para baixar vídeos diretamente no navegador Google Chrome ou utilizar sites conversores online. Contudo, barreiras como direitos autorais protegidos, criptografia de streaming e players restritos podem impedir a captura do arquivo.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te explica como baixar vídeo de qualquer site pelo PC.
Usar uma extensão para baixar vídeos no navegador Chrome facilita o download de qualquer mídia direto no computador. Confira o passo a passo para utilizar a ferramenta 4Saved no PC.
Abra o Google Chrome no computador e visite a loja de extensões do navegador: chromewebstore.google.com.
Use a barra de pesquisa no topo da página e digite “4Saved” para encontrar a extensão para baixar vídeos compatível com o Google Chrome.
Clique no botão azul “Usar no Chrome” no canto direito e, na janela pop-up, selecione “Adicionar extensão” para concluir a instalação.
Acesse a página onde está o arquivo que deseja salvar e dê o play para que o 4Saved identifique o fluxo de mídias disponível para baixar vídeo de um site.
Clique no ícone do 4Saved, ícone preto e amarelo ao lado da barra de endereço, e selecione a opção com seta para baixo para fazer o download da mídia.
Importante: vídeos no formato .mp4 são baixados automaticamente e salvos na pasta “Downloads” do PC. Em outros formatos, será necessário seguir para o passo seguinte do guia.
Caso o arquivo esteja no formato .m3u8, uma nova aba será aberta. Aguarde o carregamento atingir 100% e clique no botão “Save” para baixar o vídeo do site.
Você também pode utilizar ferramentas online direto no navegador como uma opção prática para fazer download de vídeo de qualquer site sem instalar programas. Confira como usar o SnapWC para baixar vídeo de qualquer site pelo PC:
Use o navegador do dispositivo para acessar snapwc.com. Esta página permite baixar vídeo pelo link de qualquer página na web.
Copie o endereço da página onde está o arquivo, cole no campo central e clique em “Obter links de download” para o sistema extrair o vídeo.
Na seção “Vídeo”, selecione a qualidade e o formato do arquivo que será baixado e clique no botão de seta para baixo para iniciar a conversão.
Aguarde a exibição de um breve anúncio na nova janela, retorne à aba anterior para liberar o botão final e conclua o processo para baixar o vídeo de um site.
Sim, o método via link em plataforma web permite fazer o download de vídeo de qualquer site diretamente pelo celular, sem precisar instalar aplicativos extras. Assim como no PC, basta copiar o endereço da página com a mídia e colar no site conversor usando o próprio navegador do aparelho.
Durante o processo, pode ser necessário ajustar as permissões de segurança e downloads nas configurações do navegador para autorizar o salvamento de conteúdo de terceiros.
Existem algumas barreiras técnicas e de segurança que podem impedir você de baixar vídeo de qualquer site, mesmo usando extensões ou plataformas de conversão. Confira os principais motivos que bloqueiam a captura e o salvamento desses arquivos:
Sim, as extensões e sites conversores costumam funcionar com redes sociais, mas o ideal é dar preferência às funções nativas para baixar vídeos do Instagram ou fazer download de vídeos do TikTok. Quando o criador de conteúdo deixa essa permissão ativa, você salva o arquivo original direto no dispositivo sem depender de plataformas externas.
Já a forma oficial de assistir no modo offline do YouTube exige uma assinatura do plano YouTube Premium. Caso você queira ter uma cópia dos arquivos, é necessário usar as ferramentas de terceiros para baixar os vídeos do YouTube.
Baixar vídeo de qualquer site sem permissão traz riscos legais, pois pode violar direitos autorais e os termos de uso das plataformas, mesmo para consumo próprio. Quebrar travas digitais de serviços de assinatura ou redistribuir o material agrava a situação, gerando desde o banimento da sua conta até processos judiciais.
Na prática, o maior perigo está no uso de sites conversores e extensões de navegador pouco confiáveis. Essas plataformas podem esconder anúncios maliciosos, golpes de phishing e softwares espiões capazes de roubar senhas e comprometer a segurança do seu dispositivo.

articles.title: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO priced at $83 per share, higher than expected - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO priced at $83 per share, higher than expected
Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic PBC today priced one of the most eagerly anticipated initial public offerings in history at a price of $83 per share, setting the stage for the biggest stock market listing ever.
The pricing, which has been reported by multiple news outlets including Bloomberg, Reuters and the Financial Times, is even higher than the company’s expected range of $70 to $78 per share.
If that price is correct, and if Anthropic sells all of its shares, it would raise in excess of $68 billion from the sale. Including the $26 billion in private placements, that puts Anthropic’s offering at more than $94 billion, surpassing even Space Exploration Technologies Corp. blockbuster $86 billion listing back in June.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission last week, Anthropic had said its expected price range would give it a valuation of $1.4 trillion, but its market capitalization could well be even higher than that. The company’s shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq exchange on Thursday under the ticker symbol “ANT.” Its debut might help the AI industry to push back against growing concerns that it’s entering into unsustainable bubble territory after years of breathtaking technological advances that has seen investors pour billions of dollars into almost any AI bet they can.
The listing is a major test for the AI industry, which has recently been beset by numerous setbacks, including the U.S. population’s backlash against data center building that was evident during the midterm elections, and then the ousting of Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Jensen Huang last week. Those events raised concerns even higher in a market that was already jittery about the prospect of rising interest rates that could put debt financing out of the reach of many smaller AI infrastructure companies.
Some of the technology industry’s biggest companies have significant exposure to Anthropic, as customers, partners and shareholders. For instance, both Amazon.com Inc. and Google LLC have sizable stakes in the company, and others including Microsoft Corp., Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. have invested billions into its IPO. Meanwhile, the company is one of the biggest buyers of AI chips from those firms.
“If we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia,” Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei (pictured) said in a roadshow video last week. “We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time.”
Anthropic has been surrounded by immense hype and equally sizable controversy, generating billions of dollars in revenue while raising even more, and sparking serious concerns over the safety of the technology it has pioneered. Amodei has emerged as one of the biggest sources of the numerous doomsday stories surrounding AI, writing essays and repeatedly warning anyone who will listen of the dangers of humans losing control. In addition, he has attracted the ire of U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after refusing to let the Pentagon do as it pleases with the company’s tools.
“If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian,” Amodei wrote in a viral essay in September.
Industry analyst Dan Ives told the New York Post that most investors view Amodei’s comments as “background noise” relative to the growth opportunity Anthropic has as one of the perceived leaders in frontier model development. “It’s a white-knuckle period and it’s a vote of confidence that Anthropic could have a successful IPO with the black cloud around Nvidia, Jensen and the AI trade,” he said.
Going forward, Amodei and his team will try to defy a stock market that has looked increasingly volatile this year. But even if they fail, they will walk away from this as incredibly rich men, with some reports suggesting that he and his six co-founders could each earn around $18 billion from today’s sale.
“Anthropic’s IPO will test just how much value frontier AI companies can capture as the industry moves from building increasingly capable models to putting them to work,” DatologyAI Inc. CEO Ari Morcos told SiliconANGLE.
Wall Street anticipates massive growth for the company in the coming years. Anthropic has been engaged in a titanic struggle with OpenAI Group PBC and Google LLC to develop the best AI models and recruit enterprise customers, and it appears to be winning, at least for now. It has enjoyed a rapid rise this year driven by the success of its popular AI coding tool Claude Code.
According to its IPO prospectus, it generated revenue of $33.24 billion in the nine month period ending Sept. 30, up about 1,200% from the same period one year earlier. During that period, it recorded a staggering $104 billion net loss, though most of that was the result of a change in the value of convertible notes issues to investors and its derivative liabilities, the Financial Times said. Over the same stretch in 2025, Anthropic’s total losses came to $25.1 billion.
In a recent amendment to its IPO filing, the company said it had achieved a revenue run-rate of $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the prior month.
Regarding projections, some analysts have forecast Anthropic’s revenue to hit $53 billion by the end of its fiscal year, rising to between $135 billion and $137 billion in fiscal 2027 and between $270 billion and $280 billion by 2028.
Anthropic’s rival OpenAI had originally hoped to beat it to the public markets, but its founder and CEO Sam Altman later delayed its listing. Though it has confidentially filed paperwork for an IPO, it’s not expected to make its market debut until sometime next year.

articles.title: Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour
articles.text:
Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour — users trace massive idle wear to background service, newer driver reportedly still affected
That would use up to 5% of a typical 1TB SSD’s rated endurance each year.
Nvidia’s GeForce driver 621.14 is reportedly causing excessive background writes on idle PCs, inducing extra wear on SSDs. One user measured about 3GB an hour on the susceptible driver, and another mentioned estimated up to 30GB/hour on the newer 621.24. This follows a similar-looking bug from AMD’s video driver discovered last month.
The bug is described by user Andergraude in an Nvidia forum post as “new in 621.14,” which came out on Nov. 4, who says it operates by “continuously [rewriting] the binary log file” with “real writes” to the drive. The writes are coming from the NVDisplay.Container.exe process, or the “NVIDIA Display Container LS” service, which logs to the nvlog.nvlgstg file. This background service is necessary for running the Nvidia Control Panel and App. It’s not clear what’s written in the log, and not every system is necessarily impacted.
The “real writes” point comes from the fact that a per-process write counter is not the same as writes reaching the drive. The measurements came from Windows Resource Monitor, Windows performance counters, and CrystalDiskInfo. The Data Units Written counter matched Windows’ reporting. This test showed 515MB of process I/O coming with 270MB of total writes to the C: drive over five minutes. That works out to roughly 3GB per hour, in line with the user’s own estimate.
Worse, “the write volume increases as the file grows.” Stopping the service and deleting the log can temporarily reduce the writes. With the previous driver version 621.01, the writes totaled less than 2MB per five minutes, and a second user in the thread confirmed that a rollback helps.
Mitigation attempts, such as three clean reinstalls with the help of DDU from that second user, did not fix the problem. The writing process also impacted gaming and video performance, potentially causing hitching, which suggests it gets worse under load.
Another user, AyzekUorren, in a separate thread about driver 621.24, which came out Nov. 12, says that it could get up to “about 30gb per 1h” or even “70gb or even more” with longer sessions. This is even with telemetry disabled in the Nvidia App. Noted is that every Alt+Tab added 500MB to 1GB of writes, at least for this user.
In AMD’s case, it was the External Events Utility, or atieclxx.exe, that exhibited constant writes on an idle PC. In that case, the AMD utility was reportedly copying its own executable every second. To put the impact into context, the AMD bug had rates reported between 0.3 and 5MB/s while total drive writes in the 621.14 test measured around 0.9MB/s.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The Nvidia numbers are somewhat alarming, given that a typical 1TB SSD is rated for 600TB of writes over a standard five-year warranty. Even at 270MB per five minutes, this could be about 28TB per year — for a never-sleeping PC — which is reaching toward 5% of the drive’s rated endurance, although the writes include everything the system is writing and realistic uptime will be less. However, at the higher end — 30GB per hour, at eight hours a day — one could see 15% of drive endurance worn every year for nothing.
This doesn’t make it a drive killer, but given how much users value drive endurance, especially with SSD prices as they are, avoiding unnecessary writes like this is certainly a priority. To see if you’re affected, check Resource Monitor and look for the telltale NVDisplay.Container.exe and the nvlog.nvlgstg file in the list. You can also check the SMART Data Units Written value with CrystalDiskInfo or equivalent, such as your drive’s SSD toolbox.
At this time, no fix or hotfix has been announced, and the best workaround is to do a rollback. A similar issue in the past, fixed with driver update 471.96 back in 2021, was covered by Nvidia’s release notes. As it stands, Nvidia has “N/A” for 621.24’s Open Issues, and the company has not acknowledged the bug. For the AMD bug, the driver wasn't fixed for over three weeks (and came as an optional update).
Follow Tom’s Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Intel vuelve a despedir trabajadores: “evaluamos nuestra fuerza laboral para garantizar prioridades y recursos”
articles.text:
Intel volvió a recortar puestos de trabajo en medio de los esfuerzos por recuperar su posición en la industria de los semiconductores. La nueva ronda de despidos fue reportada por Business Insider, que recogió testimonios de trabajadores que comunicaron en redes sociales que habían sido afectados por la decisión.
Los recortes se concentran en la fuerza laboral global de tecnología de la información de la compañía. Sin embargo, Intel no confirmó cuántas personas perderán sus empleos ni identificó los equipos específicos involucrados en esta nueva reducción.
Un portavoz de la empresa explicó a Business Insider que la organización revisa continuamente su plantilla como parte de una estrategia para convertirse en una compañía más enfocada y eficiente.
“Como parte de nuestra estrategia más amplia para convertirnos en una empresa más enfocada y eficiente, evaluamos continuamente nuestra fuerza laboral para garantizar que las prioridades y los recursos estén adecuadamente alineados”, señaló el representante.
Aunque la declaración no confirma expresamente el alcance de esta nueva ronda de despidos, los testimonios de los empleados apuntan a que las notificaciones ya comenzaron. La decisión se suma a otros ajustes realizados durante los últimos años.
Lip-Bu Tan busca reducir costos y reorganizar Intel
La nueva reducción de personal responde al plan de reestructuración de Lip-Bu Tan, quien asumió como director ejecutivo de Intel en 2025. Desde su llegada, el empresario estableció como una de sus prioridades disminuir los gastos operativos y simplificar la estructura interna de la compañía.
Su estrategia contempla reducir los niveles de gestión, eliminar proyectos considerados secundarios y trasladar recursos hacia iniciativas que puedan generar mejores resultados para el negocio.
La intención es que Intel tenga una organización menos compleja y pueda tomar decisiones con mayor rapidez. Para conseguirlo, la compañía también revisa sus equipos de trabajo y la distribución de sus recursos humanos.
Los despidos reportados en noviembre representan otro capítulo de este proceso. No obstante, la empresa no explicó si los puestos afectados corresponden exclusivamente a funciones administrativas o si también involucran actividades técnicas relacionadas con sus productos y servicios.
Intel ya había eliminado miles de puestos de trabajo
La reducción de personal no es una medida nueva para Intel. En 2024, cuando Pat Gelsinger todavía dirigía la compañía, se anunció un plan para eliminar más de 15.000 empleos, aproximadamente el 15% de su plantilla de ese momento.
Desde entonces, la empresa continuó con diferentes ajustes para reducir sus costos y adaptar sus operaciones a las condiciones del mercado.
Los documentos corporativos más recientes muestran que Intel tenía 81.100 trabajadores al cierre de septiembre de 2026. Esta cifra representa una disminución frente a los 85.100 empleados registrados al finalizar 2025.
La diferencia equivale a 4.000 trabajadores menos en ese periodo. Sin embargo, este número no corresponde exclusivamente a los despidos anunciados en noviembre, ya que incluye los cambios acumulados en la plantilla durante varios meses.
La compañía tampoco ha publicado una cifra específica sobre cuántas personas serán afectadas por esta última ronda.
Los problemas de Intel en la industria de los semiconductores
La reestructuración ocurre mientras Intel intenta recuperar terreno frente a otros fabricantes de procesadores. Durante los últimos años, la empresa enfrentó dificultades en sus procesos de fabricación y perdió participación en el mercado de chips utilizados para desarrollar inteligencia artificial.
Este escenario aumentó la presión para revisar sus inversiones, reducir gastos y concentrar sus esfuerzos en productos y proyectos estratégicos.
La competencia en el sector también se intensificó por el crecimiento de la inteligencia artificial, que elevó la demanda de procesadores especializados y aceleradores utilizados en centros de datos.
Bajo el liderazgo de Lip-Bu Tan, Intel busca recuperar su capacidad competitiva mediante una organización más eficiente y una mejor distribución de sus recursos.
Por ahora, la empresa no ha informado cuántos puestos adicionales podrían desaparecer ni si habrá nuevas rondas de despidos antes de finalizar el año. La evolución de su plantilla y los próximos resultados permitirán evaluar el impacto de una reestructuración que todavía continúa.

articles.title: Six Indian startups selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi
articles.text:
Six Indian startups selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi
The winners were chosen from among ten finalists in the areas of AI, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and digital finance.
Six Indian startups have been selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi, following the UAE-India Start-Up Series 2.0 finale in Bengaluru.
Hub71, Abu Dhabi's global tech ecosystem, is the cross-border partner which will connect the startups with investors, corporate and government partners, regulators, and prospective customers.
Convened by the UAE Embassy in New Delhi, the series drew more than 11,000 applications this year. The winners were chosen from among ten finalists in the areas of artificial intelligence, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and digital finance.
Since the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement came into force in 2022, bilateral trade between India and the UAE has grown from about $73 billion to more than $101 billion, it added. Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of UAE, and Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, have set a target of $200 billion by 2032.
According to a statement, the series seeks to help Indian companies expand globally, with the UAE as their gateway to investment and growth, said a statement.
H.E. Abdulla Saif Al Nuaimi, Ambassador of the UAE to India, announced the winners. Three of them will be shortlisted for Hub71's Access Programme; one startup will join the programme and receive AED 250,000 in in-kind incentives and AED 250,000 in cash through a SAFE note, the statement said.
Al Nuaimi said, “The UAE and India have set themselves the goal of doubling bilateral trade to $200 billion by 2032. Innovative companies like the ones we celebrate tonight will be central to reaching it. The UAE offers Indian founders a gateway to new markets, capital, and partnerships, and we will support these winners as they grow there. I congratulate all ten finalists on the standard they set.”
Ahmad Ali Alwan, CEO of Hub71, said, “India is an important source of technology innovation and entrepreneurial talent, and our collaboration with the UAE-India Start-Up Series is helping more ambitious founders connect with investors, partners, and market opportunities through Hub71.
"Through Hub71's Immersion Programme, startups can deepen their understanding of the market, build meaningful relationships, and access opportunities that support their growth in the UAE and internationally.”
The finale in Bengaluru brought together 10 startups for two days of investor meetings, mentorship and live pitching: CYRAN AI Solutions, Nawgati, KoinX, Onsite, Forthcode, Flo Mobility, Pointo, Econovus, XYMA Analytics, and Sustvest.
The jury comprised Al Nuaimi; Tushar Ved, President of Apparel Group; and members of the UAE-India business community. Al Nuaimi also unveiled a Top 50 Investment Dossier profiling 50 leading applicants.
The six winners will take part in a two-week hybrid programme, comprising a week of virtual preparation, followed by a one-week in-person session at Hub71 in Abu Dhabi from December 7. The programme includes mentorship, curated introductions, and knowledge sessions on Abu Dhabi's business and regulatory environment.
The first edition in 2025 opened a pathway for Indian startups to explore the UAE through Hub71. Endimension, an AI-powered radiology platform, later joined Hub71's Access Programme as part of Cohort 18. BioReform, Docket Run, Data Sutram and SBNRI are the other startups that have completed the Immersion Programme.
Here's a look at the six winning startups this year.
CYRAN AI Solutions (New Delhi, NCR)
The deeptech company uses AI to help aerospace and precision manufacturers catch defects before a part ships, an engine returns to service, or a satellite launches. Founded by IIT Delhi professor Manan Suri, it also builds edge AI for Industry 4.0 and geospatial customers.
Nawgati (Noida, Uttar Pradesh)
The AI and IoT platform helps fuel companies, dealers and governments monitor and run fuel stations from one real-time view. Founded by Aalaap Nair, Vaibhav Kaushik and Aryan Sisodia, the startup raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Ajay Upadhyaya, and has deployments in Sri Lanka and the UAE.
KoinX (Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
This crypto tax and accounting platform helps investors and businesses calculate their tax, track their holdings, and keep compliant books. Founded in 2022 by Punit Agarwal, its CEO, the startup raised $1.5 million in seed funding from investors including Polygon founder Sandeep Nailwal, and later attracted investment from CoinDCX Ventures.
KoinX Founder and CEO Punit Agarwal, told YourStory that he has been active in crypto for about 10 years and had previously led the Crypto Relief Fund, a UAE-domiciled fund of close to $500 million. He said India has the most stringent crypto tax regime in the world, and the crypto market would grow in the country with regulations.
Agarwal said KoinX first earned revenue in the June-July 2023 tax season. Revenue grew from about $140,000 in its first year to about $700,000 in the third. He expects about $1.5 million this financial year, aided by B2B contracts.
In the UAE, KoinX sells B2B software to businesses. Agarwal said a local presence, through Hub71's Immersion Programme, would help build trust.
Onsite (New Delhi, NCR)
The AI-powered construction management platform helps contractors and developers control cost and time from site to office. Founded in March 2021 by Sumit Garg, Dheeraj Anand, and Akshansh Agarwal, the startup raised $1.5 million in 2022 in a round led by Foundamental.
Forthcode (Bengaluru, Karnataka)
The aviation technology company helps airlines grow ancillary revenue and automate operations at the airport, on board, and after the flight. Its platform automates inflight retail, services, and catering management. It has partnered with Worldline for inflight payments in India.
Founder and CEO Ajith Balakumar, told YourStory that Forthcode has built an AI model for aviation on Core42's sovereign AI models. Core42 is an Abu Dhabi-based technology company.
On seatback screens in planes, passengers can search for films or ask advanced questions, such as what a city they are flying over looked like 2,000 years ago. He said the software is isolated from avionics and flight controls, and guardrails limit questions to movies, food and the destination.
Balakumar said AI can also answer queries from ground staff on matters such as dangerous goods compliance and support ancillary revenue and disruption management.
Forthcode is a winner of AviationX Labs by Emirates, Thales, Collins, GE and Airbus, has completed a paid pilot with Emirates, and works with Thales as its go-to-market partner.
Flo Mobility (Bengaluru, Karnataka)
Founded by Manesh Jain and Pratik Patel, the construction robotics company helps builders and contractors move materials across large sites using autonomous electric vehicles.
The startup's Flo Hauler robot can carry up to 1.5 tonnes. More than 60 of its robots are deployed across 10 states for developers including L&T and Godrej Properties. Flo Mobility raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round co-led by Mela Ventures and Arali Ventures.

articles.title: Can a VPN help you play GTA VI early?
articles.text:
Can a VPN help you play GTA VI early? The truth about risky purchases, quicker downloads, and early access rumors
The latest Grand Theft Auto (GTA) is nearly out in the US and UK, and after a 13-year wait, hype is at its peak.
Several VPNs have used the excitement to promote themselves as 'gaming VPNs' — offering higher download speeds, less latency and even early access.
The issue is a VPN will not help you access GTA VI early. What's more, there are no online elements at launch that require the 'improved ping' some providers claim.
Not all the claims are bogus. Higher download speeds are a possibility, and VPNs can help protect you from fake storefronts or phishing traps.
Here's everything you need to know.
Will a VPN give me safer downloads and help avoid scams?
Yes, for some.
While console gamers only have hours to wait for GTA VI to arrive, PC gamers have a far longer wait before they can play. As a result, lots of fake storefronts offering 'early PC access' are cropping up, keen to take advantage of eager PC gamers.
According to Surfshark, over 200 new GTA-themed domains had emerged by August, with more than a quarter appearing to contain scam links. NordVPN also found a 'scam kit' listed on the dark web for just $200 that contains everything someone might need to earn money maliciously from the launch.
VPNs can help protect you from dangerous sites in several ways.
Many come equipped with malicious link blocking or scam detection features, which can warn you of threats before a site loads.
You can also use email alias tools — offered by the likes of Surfshark, Proton and ExpressVPN — to mask your real email address if you're asked to sign up to any sites you're unsure of.
However, email security may be the least of your concerns if you've just submitted your credit card details to a scam site.
As usual, the best thing to do is to use common sense when approaching any site advertising GTA VI access: does the price seem too good to be true? Is it offering access to something earlier than you expected?
If the answer to either of these questions is yes, then steer clear.
NordVPN Complete: the best GTA VI VPN plan
Was: $4.49/month
Now: $3.99/month
NordVPN's Complete plan is the best way to keep yourself safe when buying and playing the new Grand Theft Auto. It includes scam detection and identity defense tools such as dark web monitoring to keep you safe from scam sites. It also has protocols quick enough to keep your gaming smooth (but secure) once GTA Online launches in 2027. Try it risk-free with NordVPN's 30-day money-back guarantee.
Can a VPN help me get faster download speeds?
Possibly. 
Grand Theft Auto VI is over 200GB to install, so it naturally takes a long time to download.
Some Internet Service Providers (ISPs) throttle your connection to preserve capacity for others when they spot a large download or during peak times.
In these specific situations, a VPN can help because it means your ISP can't determine what you're doing online. However, this is only likely to work if your connection is being significantly impacted.
For normal use, a VPN actually slows your internet connection because of the encryption overhead.
So for most, the best option is just to connect your console to your router via an Ethernet cable instead.
Can a VPN help me get GTA VI early?
No.
While in the past you could trick your computer or console into thinking you were in New Zealand by editing your time zone or connecting to a VPN, this method doesn't work these days.
Major game stores like Steam, PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store lock accounts to a specific region when you sign up. So, if you originally signed up from the UK, it won't make a difference if you connect to a router running a VPN.
While some people online have suggested creating a New Zealand-based account, it's worth remembering that you'd be violating the service's Terms of Service and could lose access to the game as a result.
Will a VPN improve online play?
Not yet.
GTA VI online is not available at launch. However, once it arrives, a VPN can help in a couple of ways:
- DDoS attacks: Previous online modes from Rockstar have left users' IP addresses exposed, leaving them vulnerable to DDoS attacks. With a VPN connected, your real IP address is hidden, which keeps you protected.
- Routing stability: Playing with a VPN connected to a local server can also help streamline ISP peering and remove packet loss issues so you don't experience an unstable connection when you're online.
How to stay safe
Keeping your personal data safe in the run-up to the GTA VI launch comes down to common sense.
Don't click links without checking they're safe, don't sign up for websites making promises they can't keep and don't let your excitement cloud your judgment about any supposed 'discounts' or early access opportunities.
A VPN can offer a useful extra layer of protection. NordVPN, for example, includes malicious link blocking and scam detection, as well as dark web monitoring for all your personal details.
Combined, that's everything you need to stay safe against malicious GTA VI links, which is why it's my recommendation if you're considering a VPN for launch day.
By signing up now, you'll also be protected for GTA Online when it eventually launches. NordVPN offers the security you need to protect against DDoS attacks and has fast connections to ensure lag-free gaming.
While a VPN won't give you exclusive early access to GTA VI, or guarantee faster downloads, it does give you the peace of mind that you're not being scammed and added security for the future.
