articles.title: Pourquoi GTA 6 tourne à 30 fps sur toutes les consoles, même sur PS5 Pro : les explications de Rockstar
articles.text:
Rockstar vient de répondre à la question que se posent les joueurs sur console : pourquoi GTA 6 reste verrouillé à 30 images par seconde sans mode intermédiaire à 40 fps ? Tout se jouerait notamment dans les 33 millisecondes dont dispose le moteur graphique pour calculer chaque image. Décryptage.
Inutile de chercher un mode Performance dans les réglages de GTA 6 à sa sortie. Le jeu arrive le 19 novembre avec un seul mode graphique et la même cadence cible sur toutes les consoles, de la Xbox Series S à la PS5 Pro, en passant par la Series X et la PS5. À la veille du lancement, Rockstar a expliqué à TechRadar pourquoi il s’en tenait à 30 images par seconde (fps), y compris face à l’option intermédiaire des 40 fps.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Ce que Rockstar fait de ses 33 millisecondes
À 30 fps, le jeu doit livrer une image toutes les 33,3 millisecondes. À 40 fps, il lui faudrait en produire une toutes les 25 ms. Dix images de plus chaque seconde, c’est un gain de fluidité à l’écran, mais aussi un quart de temps en moins dans le budget de calcul par image. Sur les consoles de cette génération, certains jeux proposent ce compromis entre un mode Qualité à 30 fps et un mode Performance à 60 fps. À 120 Hz, chaque image d’un jeu qui tourne à 40 fps reste affichée pendant exactement trois rafraîchissements.
Pour Jonathon Ashcroft, vice-président senior chargé de la technologie chez Rockstar, le calcul dépasse la seule qualité d’image. Le studio doit répartir le travail entre le processeur central et le processeur graphique pour simuler le monde et produire son rendu. Les différents systèmes du jeu interagissent en permanence, et le studio juge que le temps disponible à 30 fps lui permet de préserver l’équilibre entre la simulation, le rendu et le gameplay.
Marc Chambers, directeur de la production technologique, souligne de son côté que les outils et la technologie du jeu ont été développés en interne. Rockstar a ainsi pu les adapter à ce qu’il voulait faire de son monde ouvert.
Sur PS5 Pro, les améliorations portent sur le rendu
Les rumeurs d’un mode à 40 fps avaient entretenu l’espoir d’une option plus fluide sur les consoles les plus puissantes. La PS5 Pro conserve la même cadence cible que la PS5 avec toutefois des améliorations visuelles propres à la console. Sony annonce une image plus nette grâce au PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) et des ombres calculées en ray tracing.
Pour les joueurs, la régularité de cette cadence d’affichage comptera autant que le chiffre annoncé. C’est en traversant Vice City à toute blinde qu’on saura si ces 30 fps se font oublier.

articles.title: AI is now finding bugs in the code that runs banks, airlines, and hospitals
articles.text:
The takeaway: An AI model built for security research has uncovered a series of vulnerabilities in Java, the Oracle programming language used in the systems of airlines, banks, hospitals, and government agencies. The flaws were discovered by cybersecurity startup Calif using OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model. Now, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency urged companies to update every system running Java.
Oracle released what it called a "critical security patch update" the same day and urged customers to install it. The company declined to comment further. Applying the fix could be a major undertaking: 90% of Fortune 500 companies use Java, which is deeply embedded in the software that keeps large organizations running.
Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif, said the language's widespread use is what makes the discovery so serious. "Java is basically critical infrastructure," he told The Financial Times. "It's so central to the technology that we depend on . . . [and] a lot of big companies are going to have their work cut out to get it fixed."
Calif said it notified Oracle about the vulnerability last month. It then worked with government agencies through the Five Eyes intelligence-sharing alliance, which includes Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK and the US. Amazon, Apple, Google, and Microsoft also helped coordinate fixes. That kind of cooperation is intended to ensure patches are ready before details of a vulnerability spread widely enough for attackers to exploit it.
The Java findings are the latest in a growing list of software vulnerabilities discovered with the help of AI models in recent months. In October, researchers used models from OpenAI and Google to identify two security flaws in PHP, a programming language used by 70% of websites. The bugs had gone undetected for more than a decade. After they were disclosed, companies and government agencies took websites offline as a precaution.
These cases illustrate a shift in how vulnerability research is conducted. AI models can now analyze large, established codebases and uncover flaws that years of human review have missed. That gives defenders an advantage, but it also puts them in a race against potential attackers.
Security researchers are trying to identify and patch weaknesses before malicious actors can exploit them. Advances in AI make that race more challenging because the same capabilities could help attackers discover the same vulnerabilities.
The CISA advisory comes during a period of unusual instability affecting digital services in the US, adding to concerns about further disruptions. Microsoft experienced a widespread outage last week that disrupted its services. The company said a system malfunctioned during a routine effort to reroute user traffic and ruled out a cyberattack. JPMorgan and United Airlines are among the other companies that have experienced outages in recent weeks.
Air travel has also been affected. A five-hour disruption to the country's aging air traffic control system caused a weekend of travel chaos for American passengers. Separately, Norwegian oil and gas group Equinor said it had been targeted in a cyberattack.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio sought to ease concerns that the outages were connected. Speaking to reporters in Manila during President Donald Trump's three-day trip to Asia, he rejected the idea of a coordinated campaign. "We are not under systemic attack. These events, one has nothing to do with another, they are not interrelated, they are all separate and distinct," he said.
"Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country," Rubio added.
The outages have not been linked to the Java vulnerabilities. Still, the timing puts additional pressure on organizations that rely heavily on Java. With Oracle's patch released and CISA's warning issued, companies using Java must now identify every place the language is embedded in their systems and apply the necessary updates.

articles.title: Nvidia va cesser d'exporter ses puces les plus puissantes vers la Chine
articles.text:
Nvidia ne vendra plus ses puces Hopper à la Chine. Colette Kress, la dirigeante temporaire de Nvidia, en a fait l’annonce ce mercredi 18 novembre. L’entreprise américaine semble vouloir montrer qu’elle prend maintenant des mesures concrètes, alors que certains la suspectent d’avoir laissé passer jusqu’à 1,5 million de puces interdites vers la Chine, sous l’ère de Jensen Huang.
Nvidia prive la Chine de ses puces les plus puissantes
Pour rappel, il s’agit de puces particulièrement puissantes, conçues pour les centres de données et l’intelligence artificielle. Aucune information n’a été communiquée pour justifier clairement cette décision. Nvidia a pourtant annoncé avoir vendu pour 2,4 milliards de dollars de produits Hopper sous licence à la Chine au troisième trimestre.
La raison se situe bien entendu du côté de l’affaire Jensen Huang, accusé d’avoir entretenu une relation extraconjugale avec Alice Huang, suspectée par Washington d’être une espionne au service de la Chine. Mais surtout, Nvidia, sous la direction de Jensen Huang, est soupçonnée d’avoir laissé passer jusqu’à 1,5 million de puces interdites vers la Chine.
Nvidia, sous l’ère Colette Kress, veut maintenant montrer que les choses ont changé avec le départ de Jensen Huang. Plus de suspicion d’affaires de contrebande : l’entreprise interdit dorénavant l’accès à la Chine à certaines de ses puces de pointe. Nvidia espère bien montrer qu’elle remet maintenant de l’ordre dans ses affaires, alors que Washington envisage de nouvelles restrictions contre la Chine. Rappelons au passage que les exportations de composants Nvidia étaient déjà très limitées depuis un moment. En ce qui concerne les expéditions de puces Hopper vers la Chine, Donald Trump avait autorisé leur commercialisation auprès de certaines entreprises chinoises, avec en contrepartie une taxe de 25 % sur les ventes.
Nvidia annonce la création d’un comité chargé de s’assurer de la sécurité nationale
Un jour avant de mettre fin aux expéditions de ses puces Hopper vers la Chine, Nvidia a indiqué que son conseil d’administration avait créé un comité chargé de surveiller les questions de sécurité nationale et de contrôle des exportations. Selon l’entreprise, ce comité fera appel à des experts indépendants et externes « pour fournir une expertise juridique, en matière de sécurité nationale et de conformité commerciale ».
Pour rappel, Jensen Huang a fait part de sa volonté de récupérer son poste de PDG de Nvidia, mais le conseil d’administration de l’entreprise lui a gentiment fait comprendre que cela n’arrivera pas. À la place, Nvidia semble vouloir montrer qu’une page s’est définitivement tournée, en insistant sur la question de la sécurité nationale et en limitant encore davantage ses relations avec la Chine.

Pour un bon robot cuiseur multifonctions à prix abordable, privilégiez...
Le robot cuiseur multifonctions Silvercrest Monsieur Cuisine Smart s'affiche aujourd'hui à 466,02 € chez Amazon. C'est actuellement le meilleur robot cuiseur multifonctions à prix abordable de notre comparatif, selon les 15 modèles testés dans notre laboratoire.
Deux ans après la sortie de son Monsieur Cuisine Connect sous sa marque Silvercrest, Lidl améliore et enrichit son robot-cuiseur star avec le Monsieur Cuisine Smart. Ce modèle gagne un moteur plus puissant, un écran plus grand et plus de fonctionnalités.

Bon en mixage et respectueux des cuissons, le Monsieur Cuisine Smart s'impose comme la meilleure référence à moins de 400 €, même si tout n'est pas parfait. articles.title: NVIDIA Expands Commitments With Supply Chain Partners to Support AI Infrastructure Buildout
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
NVIDIA Expands Commitments With Supply Chain Partners to Support AI Infrastructure Buildout
NVIDIA today announced expanded commitments with supply chain partners to support sustainable long-term growth, aligning supply and manufacturing capacity with demand for its accelerated computing and AI infrastructure platforms.
Working with Amkor Technology, Foxconn, Kinsus Interconnect Technology, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and TSMC, NVIDIA is expanding manufacturing capacity across substrates, advanced packaging, wafer and contract manufacturing to scale production of its current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms."Our supply chain is a strategic advantage," said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations at NVIDIA. "Our work with these partners builds on our manufacturing foundation for long-term growth, expanding capacity across components, advanced packaging and system production to deliver the accelerated computing platforms our customers need."
Increasing Substrate Capacity and Production Capabilities
NVIDIA is expanding its substrate supply commitments with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, adding manufacturing capacity and improving production capabilities at existing factories.
Under a new agreement with NVIDIA, Kinsus plans to expand its advanced ABF package substrate manufacturing capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5x over current levels from its Youth campus in Taoyuan, Taiwan.
Production is expected to begin in the second half of 2027, with the additional capacity targeted for the third quarter of 2028. This multiyear agreement builds on the companies' existing supplier relationship and supports NVIDIA's long-term supply planning for its accelerated computing platforms.
"We believe AI will be one of the most important technology transitions of our lifetime," said Scott Chen, CEO and president of Kinsus. "After more than a decade of partnership with NVIDIA, we are excited to continue building the future together."
NVIDIA and Samsung Electro-Mechanics have amended their existing substrate supply agreement to improve operational capabilities at existing factories in support of increased production of NVIDIA's accelerated computing platforms.
The amendment builds on the companies' previously announced multiyear collaboration supporting substrate manufacturing in Sejong and Busan, South Korea, for NVIDIA's compute and high-speed networking technologies.
"By combining our world-class substrate fine-processing technology and high-reliability MLCC technology, we will perfectly fulfill our role as a total solution provider so that NVIDIA's AI platform can be supplied to the global market on time, with the highest performance and quality," said Duck-Hyun Chang, CEO of Samsung Electro-Mechanics. 
Scaling Advanced Packaging Through Multiyear Agreements
NVIDIA's advanced packaging plans include a new capacity expansion with SPIL and previously announced agreements supporting Amkor's manufacturing expansion in the U.S. and South Korea.
NVIDIA is supporting Amkor's expansion of advanced packaging capacity in Arizona and South Korea through multiyear agreements announced in July and October 2026, totaling nearly $3 billion. The agreements include prepayments to help Amkor scale manufacturing capacity for NVIDIA's long-term production needs.
"Our agreements with NVIDIA support investments in Arizona and South Korea that will serve multiple generations of AI platforms," said Kevin Engel, president and CEO of Amkor. "That long-term planning allows us to advance our packaging technologies and add manufacturing capacity as NVIDIA's production needs grow."
NVIDIA and SPIL are expanding advanced packaging operations in Taiwan under a multiyear agreement supported by multibillion-dollar funding from NVIDIA. The expansion will increase contracted advanced packaging capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by mid-2029.
The project includes new production lines with turnkey support spanning bumping, interposer wafer fabrication, assembly and testing. These capabilities support semiconductor products with demanding requirements for computing performance, bandwidth, power efficiency and system integration.
"SPIL is proud to strengthen our collaboration with NVIDIA," said C.W. Tsai, CEO and chairman of the board of SPIL. "This agreement enhances our ability to support next-generation packaging technologies and deliver the performance and reliability required for future AI systems."
Next-Generation Technologies for Agentic AI
The third quarter marked the first volume shipment of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs for agentic AI. These products take advantage of TSMC's 5 nm, 3 nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies.
"TSMC and NVIDIA share a longstanding partnership built on semiconductor innovation," said Dr. Kevin Zhang, senior vice president and deputy co-COO at TSMC. "This deep collaboration allows us to plan for future technology requirements and prepare our manufacturing capabilities as NVIDIA brings new platforms to market."
Leveraging Global Manufacturing Footprint for GPU and Networking Platforms
"Foxconn continues to deepen its collaboration with NVIDIA across next-generation GPU and networking platforms," said Young Liu, chairman of Foxconn. "By leveraging its integrated global production network spanning Asia, North America, and Europe, Foxconn is well-positioned to support the volume ramp-up of next-generation AI infrastructure."
Building on Global Supply Chain Expansion
These commitments build on NVIDIA's decades-long partnerships and recent commitments announced in October for manufacturing expansions with Amkor, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL and Unimicron. Those plans included an aggregate 2.5x increase in substrate capacity over three years, expanded advanced packaging, a doubling of semiconductor testing capacity from 2026 to 2027 and a 15x increase in SPIL's optical-engine capacity by mid-2027, with aims for another doubling by the end of 2028.
"Our strong and long-standing collaboration with NVIDIA has continued to develop in the area of high-performance IC package substrates," said Koji Kawashima, president and chief executive officer at IBIDEN. "Through the expansion of our Ono Plant, we will continue to strengthen our production capabilities and meet growing demand."
"Our work with NVIDIA demonstrates the value of close collaboration between chip design and semiconductor testing," said Gauss Chang, president at KYEC. "Expanding our testing operations into the United States builds on that relationship and brings our capabilities closer to NVIDIA's growing U.S. manufacturing supply chain."
"As AI reshapes industries and societies around the world, trusted partnerships and supply chain collaboration have never been more important," said SC Chien, chairman of Unimicron. "The advanced substrate capacity investment underscores the strength of our partnership with NVIDIA and our shared commitment to support the rapid growth of AI infrastructure. By investing in advanced substrate technologies and manufacturing capabilities, Unimicron is well-positioned to help customers unlock new opportunities and share in the tremendous growth of the AI era."

articles.title: En mitad del caos ferroviario, Renfe pintará sus trenes de azul, rojo y morado
articles.text:
Dice Raquel Elices en RTVE que Azuloscurocasinegro es "una tonalidad que nos recuerda que muchas veces nos equivocamos y, a veces, las cosas no son exactamente cómo las vemos". Habla, por supuesto, de la película de Daniel Sánchez Arévalo, que en 2006 contaba la historia de un joven que no podía escapar de sus problemas y responsabilidades familiares y de un amigo cuyo descubrimiento de cómo es realmente su padre le ayudaba a comprenderse a sí mismo.
Quizás eso tiene algo de lo que busca Renfe con su cambio de imagen: comprenderse a sí mismo y recordar que, a veces, nos equivocamos. La compañía ferroviaria está inmersa en una renovación de su imagen. El pasado mes de septiembre, la compañía ya anunció que recuperaba su histórica galleta volviendo medio siglo atrás. Esa nueva seña de identidad, se apuntó, sería uno de los primeros pasos que se darían en su camino para redefinir su imagen.
Ahora, el siguiente gran cambio apunta a cambiar la identidad visual de los trenes. Renfe quiere simplificar sus productos dotando de una imagen clarificadora del servicio que presta para cada tren. La nueva identidad la ha presentado Álvaro Fernández Heredia, quien era presidente de Renfe hasta hace unos días, posteando en la red social X la imagen que llevarán los próximos trenes.
Reimaginando en un momento complicado
El cambio en la imagen de Renfe llega tras un trabajo intenso en la renovación de la identidad de la marca pero también en cambios más profundos que afectan a su funcionamiento en el día a día. Por ejemplo, la compañía ya tiene lista una nueva aplicación para la compra de billetes. Hasta el día 25 de enero convivirá con la actual pero a partir de entonces no quedaremos con esta nueva versión que, prometen, será más sencilla.
Ese ejercicio de simplificación es el que se ha querido hacer con la identidad visual de los trenes. Éstos irán pintados en diferentes colores dependiendo del servicio que presten, quedando divididos de la siguiente manera:
- Alta velocidad: azul muy oscuro (casi negro) que se extenderá por todos los coches. Los trenes AVLO llevarán estas siglas en grandes dimensiones escritas en un azul más claro para contrastar y dejar claro que estamos ante el servicio "barato" de la alta velocidad. Por lo tanto, dejaremos de ver los AVLO morados como hasta ahora.
- Larga y media distancia: la larga y media distancia tendrá trenes morados que contrastarán con detalles naranjas.
- Cercanías: se combinará el blanco y el rojo compartiendo la mitad del peso en la carrocería del vehículo. En el lateral será más preponderante el rojo y en los extremos el blanco.
Estos cambios en la imagen llegan en un momento complicado para la compañía, castigados en parte por todo el caos ferroviario que se está viviendo. Y es que aunque el trabajo para crear una nueva identidad visual no es, ni mucho menos, un ejercicio que se lleve a cabo de un día para otro, la noticia llega en momentos difíciles para el sector.
Y es que el 2026 ha sido un año para olvidar. Probablemente estamos ante uno de los peores años (si no el peor) en la historia del ferrocarril español, con más de un centenar de fallecidos en la suma de dos accidentes que se producen con nueve meses de diferencia.
El accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba) ya puso en duda cómo se estaba invirtiendo el dinero en el sector ferroviario español pero ha sido el de Urda (Toledo) el que ha hecho saltar por los aires la confianza que quedaba en el sistema, dejando al descubierto un amplio abanico de problemas que hay que atacar (mantenimiento de las vías, falta de personal cualificado, presión excesiva sobre los controladores...), que ha terminado con la dimisión de Óscar Puente como ministro de Transportes y la promesa de que se blindarán 19.000 millones de euros para que se lleven a cabo las reformas necesarias para devolver la confianza a los clientes.

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks bets $4.5B on AI startup Applied Compute as earnings top forecasts - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks bets $4.5B on AI startup Applied Compute as earnings top forecasts
Cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks Inc. today announced that it has agreed to acquire artificial intelligence model training and inference startup Applied Compute Inc. in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.
The news came alongside fiscal first-quarter earnings and revenue that were well ahead of Wall Street expectations. Shares of Palo Alto Networks rose more than 8% in late trading, adding to a gain of nearly 10% during the regular session.
The acquisition, subject to regulatory clearance, is expected to close in Palo Alto Networks’ fiscal third quarter. Once the deal closes, Applied Compute co-founder and Chief Executive Yash Patil will become co-chief AI officer at Palo Alto Networks, with the startup’s research team also joining the company.
Founded in 2025 by former OpenAI Group PBC researchers Patil, Rhythm Garg and Linden Li, Applied Compute offers a platform for post-training and inference of open-weight models. The platform is designed to make it easier for companies to train, serve and improve their own models, with an autoscaling inference engine and a model router called Shift-1 also included.
Applied Compute raised $350 million at a $3.25 billion valuation earlier this month in a round led by Elad Gil, with Nvidia Corp., Shopify Ventures and HubSpot Ventures also participating. At the time, the company said that its annualized recurring revenue had topped $100 million. Notable customers include Microsoft Corp. and DoorDash Inc. Coming into its acquisition, Applied Compute had raised more than $500 million in total.
Palo Alto Networks is pitching the deal as a bet that enterprise AI will be hybrid, as a large share of companies run open-weight models tuned to their own data. According to the company, no large provider is currently delivering those models securely. With Applied Compute, enterprises will be able to train and deploy open-weight models with security built in, either in the public cloud or in sovereign environments.
“Every enterprise is going to run a mix of open and closed models, and every one of those models needs to be secured,” Chairman and Chief Executive Nikesh Arora said. “Applied Compute has built the best post-training and inference platform we’ve seen, and its research team is exceptional.”
The deal came on the same day Palo Alto Networks reported what Arora called a record first quarter. For the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, the company reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.05, up from 93 cents in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $3.44 billion, up 39% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting earnings of 97 cents per share on revenue of $3.31 billion.
Next-generation security annual recurring revenue grew 66% from a year earlier, to $9.73 billion. Remaining performance obligations rose 35%, to $21 billion. Helped by a tax benefit of $457 million, net income on an unadjusted basis came to $482 million, up from $334 million in the same quarter a year ago.
Chief Financial Officer Dipak Golechha said that given the current threat environment and the demand ahead, the company is “materially raising” its full-year guidance.
For its fiscal second quarter, Palo Alto Networks expects adjusted earnings per share of $1.01 to $1.03 on revenue of $3.53 billion to $3.55 billion. Full-year revenue is now forecast at $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, up from the $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion guided in September, with adjusted earnings of $4.26 to $4.30 per share ahead of the $4.18 expected by analysts polled by FactSet.

articles.title: Tela grande e custo-benefício: TCL QLED 75" atinge menor preço na Black November • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Tela grande e custo-benefício: TCL QLED 75″ atinge menor preço na Black November
TCL P7L de 75" possui painel QLED de até 120 Hz em games; smart TV recebe desconto de 36% em até 12x sem juros com cupom em oferta do AliExpress
A P7L de 75″ está em oferta por R$ 4.019 em até 12x sem juros com cupom AEMEGA18 na loja do Magazine Luiza no AliExpress. A smart TV da TCL, com painel QLED e taxa de atualização de até 120 Hz para jogos, recebe desconto de 36% sobre o preço original de R$ 6.299 durante a Black November 2026.
A P7L é uma TV de entrada com um amplo painel QLED, que usa pontos quânticos para reproduzir cores com até 93% da gama DCI-P3, e a tecnologia HVA para um contraste superior ao de modelos LCD. O resultado é uma experiência próxima de um televisor OLED, mas sem risco do temido burn-in.
O aparelho suporta tecnologias de imagem como HDR10+ e Dolby Vision, e embora possua uma taxa de apenas 60 Hz, ela usa o recurso DLG para emular mais quadros em games, chegando a 120 Hz. O som, embora provido por duas caixas de 15 W, suporta Dolby Atmos e DTS Virtual:X para mais qualidade.
Seu processador AiPQ usa recursos de inteligência artificial em funções como upscaling de conteúdos legados para 4K sem perdas, otimização de imagem, e agentes dedicados a melhorar a experiência ao rodar games e filmes, e até mesmo soluções corporativas, ao conectar um PC ao televisor.
O controle remoto da P7L é igual ao embarcado na linha 2025 de TVs da TCL, com acesso rápido a apps de streaming e microfone integrado para comandos de voz.
O sistema Google TV oferece vasta compatibilidade com serviços, como Netflix, Apple TV, Prime Video, Spotify, Crunchyroll e outros.
A TCL T7L (R$ 4.019 em até 12x sem juros com cupom AEMEGA18) possui três entradas HDMI, uma porta USB-A, uma Ethernet e uma saída de áudio óptico, além de suporte a Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth 5.4.
A Black Friday 2026 chega só dia 27 de novembro, mas a campanha Black November está a todo vapor, com o AliExpress e outras lojas oferecendo cupons de promoções em eletrônicos com condições especiais durante todo o mês.

articles.title: Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal — at first all-hands meeting since CEO’s departure, staff offered perks, told ‘we’re going to be fine'
articles.text:
Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal — at first all-hands meeting since CEO’s departure, staff offered perks, told ‘we’re going to be fine’
Money isn't everything, but it sure can help.
Nvidia today held its first all-hands meeting since the resignation of co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. According to Wired, interim CEO Colette Kress offered more money and equity on a faster-than-expected schedule to calm staffers' nerves.
"So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” Wired reports Kress said.
The pay and equity bumps are set for December, far ahead of the company's normal raise cycle. Kress said that compensation and more clarity from the board were the most common topics in questions submitted ahead of the meeting.
Keeping current employees happy will be one of Kress' most important short-term challenges. One director-level employee has already written to the board and top executives, warning that failure to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could lead to the loss of ‘irreplaceable talent.’
A potential exodus of talent could also spook investors, despite standout earnings on Thursday. A leadership crisis could make the company seem less stable, and Huang had placed himself as the anchor point for many decisions and the company's overall vision.
Huang has expressed interest in returning to Nvidia, saying he would be "honored" to lead the company again if asked by the board. The board was clear in yesterday's earnings call that it did not intend to bring Huang back, though there is reportedly a pro-Huang faction.
Nvidia cofounder Chris Malachowsky was also on the call, explaining that the company lives its values rather than simply plastering them on posters.
“We’re going to be fine,” he said.

articles.title: NVIDIA ferme publiquement la porte à un retour de Jensen Huang
articles.text:
On parle beaucoup d'un potentiel retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de NVIDIA. Mais le conseil d'administration n'a clairement pas l'air très chaud pour cette possibilité !
L'énorme polémique autour de la liaison de Jensen Huang avec une femme qui pourrait être une espionne chinoise n'a pas été éteinte par sa démission. Car de nombreuses personnes au sein de NVIDIA, ainsi qu'à l'extérieur - à l'instar d'Elon Musk - poussent pour que le fondateur de la boîte reprenne son poste de PDG. Mais pour le moment, ça ne semble pas avoir d'effet sur la direction.
Le président du conseil d'administration de NVIDIA réfute publiquement la possibilité d'un retour de Jensen Huang
Jensen Huang aimerait pouvoir reprendre les rênes de NVIDIA. Mais le conseil d'administration n'est clairement pas très chaud pour cette option, comme nous l'apprend une information de Reuters.
D'après ce dernier, le président du conseil d'administration de NVIDIA, Harvey Jones, a ainsi déclaré que la société ne réengagerait pas Jensen Huang. Une communication qui a eu lieu ce mardi 17 novembre, à l'occasion d'une conférence téléphonique avec les investisseurs.
NVIDIA a engagé le cabinet Heidrick & Struggles pour trouver un nouveau PDG
Preuve de sa volonté de tourner définitivement la page, il a aussi indiqué durant la même conférence qu'il ne répondrait pas aux questions relatives à Jensen Huang. Pour lui, l'avenir se trouve ailleurs, et il l'a montré en se faisant accompagner durant cette intervention de la patronne par intérim Colette Kress et du vice-président et directeur général chargé du calcul hyperscale et haute performance, Ian Buck.
Pour ce qui est du futur patron, NVIDIA a fait appel au cabinet de recrutement de renommé mondial Heidrick & Struggles afin de trouver un remplacement à Jensen Huang. « Nous souhaitons nommer le PDG, le PDG permanent, dès que possible, mais nous ne précipiterons pas cette nomination avant d’avoir trouvé la personne idéale » a assuré Harvey Jones. Alors, la porte est-elle définitivement fermée ?
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Dos hombres desarrollaron psicosis y manía tras suspender un fármaco tipo Ozempic. La coincidencia inquieta a los médicos, aunque no demuestra nada
articles.text:
Los fármacos GLP-1 tienen muchas luces, pero también muchas sombras. Llevan años ayudando a pacientes con diabetes a controlar sus niveles de glucosa y desde hace un tiempo también están ayudando a algunas personas a perder peso. Esto último ha llegado a rozar la obsesión en algunas personas, por lo que se advierte a quienes recurren a estos fármacos sin realmente necesitarlos que pueden tener un amplio abanico de efectos secundarios. La mayoría son leves, pero dos reportes de caso publicados recientemente en una revista de psiquiatría nos recuerdan que, en pacientes con problemas previos de salud mental, se debe reforzar la atención.
Ambos casos coinciden en que los pacientes dejaron de golpe un medicamento GLP-1 llamado tirzepatida y, poco después, desarrollaron síntomas psiquiátricos graves. Es cierto que tenían otros factores de riesgo y que, con solo dos casos, no podemos saber con seguridad si fue el medicamento el que causó el problema. Aun así, son una llamada de atención que nos recuerda la importancia de hacer un seguimiento aún más estricto en algunos pacientes receptores de los fármacos GLP-1.
Varón, 61 años. El primer caso es el de un hombre que dejó la tirzepatida, conocida comercialmente como Mounjaro, en agosto de 2025. Comenzó a sentir náuseas, así que abandonó el fármaco de golpe. Dos meses después, se presentó en las urgencias psiquiátricas de un hospital con síntomas de confusión, paranoia, alucinaciones auditivas y visuales y empeoramiento de la depresión que ya padecía. Además, padecía un delirio de Cotard, que se da cuando los pacientes creen que están muertos o que les faltan algunas partes del cuerpo.
Varón, 52 años. El otro paciente había abandonado de golpe el Mounjaro en septiembre, después de perder 45 kg en seis meses. Se presentó en urgencias en octubre con un episodio maníaco caracterizado por irritabilidad, impulsividad, grandiosidad y habla desorganizada. Si el otro paciente sufría de depresión, este lo hacía de ansiedad previa. Además, tenía los niveles de vitamina B12 muy bajos y consumía cannabis, una droga que puede aumentar el riesgo de padecer síntomas psiquiátricos.
Receptores en el cerebro. Los medicamentos GLP-1 imitan una hormona con el mismo nombre, cuyo papel es controlar los niveles de glucosa y reducir el apetito. Esto último es el motivo por el que suele usarse para perder peso. Por un lado, ralentiza el vaciado del estómago, por lo que la sensación de saciedad dura más tiempo. Por otro, reduce el hambre dirigiéndose directamente al cerebro. Esto último nos indica que en el cerebro hay receptores para GLP-1. Se ha visto que el medicamento puede atravesar la barrera hematoencefálica e introducirse en algunas regiones del cerebro. Una vez ahí no se sabe qué hace exactamente, pero podría aumentar el riesgo de ciertos síntomas psiquiátricos.
Muy pocas personas. Antes de este estudio se habían publicado otros en los que señalan que los medicamentos GLP-1 pueden afectar a los niveles de dopamina. Esto puede ser útil para tratar las adicciones, pero también podría generar síntomas depresivos más o menos graves. En los peores casos, se han visto pacientes con ideaciones suicidas y autolesiones. Es cierto que estos casos psiquiátricos son muy poco frecuentes. Por ejemplo, en una base de datos europea se registraron 481 eventos psiquiátricos con semaglutida, liraglutida y tirzepatida, algo más del 1% de los informes. Los casos muy graves serían aún menos. No obstante, dada la gran gravedad que suponen, es importante estudiarlos a fondo para evitar males mayores.

articles.title: Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote
articles.text:
A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote.
All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee’s 13 Democrats were absent. “We’re going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs,” Cruz said at today’s hearing.
Nominees are vetted in committees first, and then seek require majority approval from the Senate. Republicans are hoping to get Thumann confirmed before Democrats take Senate control in January.
Although the Senate Commerce Committee generally requires one minority member to be present for nomination votes, a spokesperson for Cruz said Senate rules allow the nomination to be advanced for a vote in the entire chamber. A spokesperson for Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on the committee, said in response that “since 2005, Commerce Committee rules required that a quorum include one member of the minority for official action on bill, resolution, or nomination.”
Technically, the committee has operated with no rules during Cruz’s chairmanship because Cruz “failed to pass committee rules” for the current session of Congress, Cantwell’s spokesperson said. “Nevertheless, in practice it has operated in line with rules from the last Congress (and this provision, specifically, since 2005), including that a quorum with a member of the minority party must be present for official action on a nomination or legislation. Until today.”
False testimony allegation
At a hearing last week, Thumann said she never worked with Carr on media-related topics, leading to accusations that she provided false testimony. “I have not worked with the chairman on any media-related issues,” Thumann said after Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) asked, “Do you support Chairman Carr’s illegal campaign to remove Jimmy Kimmel from the nation’s airwaves?”

articles.title: Vous utilisez l'un des 20 pires mots de passe de France ? Changez-le immédiatement
articles.text:
Comme chaque année, NordPass dévoile le classement des mots de passe les plus utilisés dans le monde. Pour cette huitième édition, le gestionnaire de mots de passe édité par Nord Security a analysé, avec des chercheurs indépendants, « les récentes fuites de données rendues publiques et les référentiels du dark web ». Les chercheurs se sont concentrés sur les mots de passe exposés entre septembre 2025 et septembre 2026, dans 44 pays.
À lire aussi : Fuites de données – la France sort du top 3 mondial, mais 18 comptes sont encore piratés chaque minute
Les 20 mots de passe les plus utilisés au monde
Sans surprise, « 123456 » reste le mot de passe le plus répandu sur la planète. D’après NordPass, il a été repéré plus de 7,2 millions de fois dans les fuites de données. Pour rappel, ce mot de passe est aussi répandu que dangereux. Récemment, un pirate s’est d’ailleurs introduit dans le registre central des personnes du Danemark grâce au mot de passe « 123456 ». En exploitant la négligence d’un employé, le pirate s’est emparé des données de millions de Danois.

- Pass@12345
- Admin@123
Cette année, les caractères spéciaux gagnent du terrain. En effet, 39 mots de passe du classement mondial en contiennent, contre 32 l’an dernier, ce qui cadre avec les pratiques recommandées en matière de cybersécurité. Néanmoins, la plupart des restent encore trop simples, comme « P@ssw0rd » ou « Admin@123 ».
« Si vous devez créer un mot de passe non aléatoire, par exemple un mot de passe maître, mieux vaut opter pour une phrase de passe longue composée de deux ou trois mots plutôt que pour un mot de passe court et commun comportant des caractères spéciaux », conseille Karolis Arbaciauskas, responsable produit chez NordPass.
Les chercheurs ont aussi repéré des mots de passe par défaut de routeurs, comme « ALC#FGU » et « adminHW ». Ils sont si répandus qu’ils figurent dans le classement mondial des mots de passe les plus compromis. Autrement dit, d’innombrables box Internet et objets connectés restent exposés aux cyberattaques
Les 20 pires mots de passe de France
En France, « 123456 » reprend la tête du classement. L’an dernier, il avait été détrôné par « admin », qui se contente cette fois de la deuxième place du top français. On trouve aussi plusieurs variantes liées au clavier AZERTY, avec « azerty », « azertyuiop » et « Azerty123 ». On note aussi des choix plus personnels, comme « bebe2012 », « loulou », ou « Marseille13 ».

De « metallica » à « skibiditoilet »
Cette année, NordPass s’est aussi intéressé à l’influence de la culture pop sur nos mots de passe. Chaque époque laisse son empreinte sur les codes employés par les internautes, comme « metallica » et « corleone13 » pour les années 80 et 90, « sasuke » et « eminem2004 » pour les années 2000, « minecraft » et « neymar10 » pour les années 2010, ou encore « skibiditoilet » et « squidgamethebest » pour la décennie actuelle.
« Les mots de passe inspirés de la culture pop nous rappellent que ce que l’on aime nous rend prévisibles. Les pirates n’ont pas besoin de vous connaître personnellement : il leur suffit de connaître vos centres d’intérêt », met en garde Karolis Arbaciauskas, ajoutant que le nom d’un groupe préféré associé à une année de naissance peut ainsi être « piraté en moins d’une seconde ».
On vous recommande évidemment de ne jamais vous servir d’un des mots de passe épinglés ci-dessus. Plus un mot de passe est répandu, plus les pirates peuvent le deviner en très peu de temps. La meilleure défense contre les cyberattaques consiste à utiliser des mots de passe longs, d’au moins 14 caractères, et différents pour chacun de vos comptes. Pensez également à activer la double authentification dès que celle-ci est disponible. Ce mécanisme de sécurité bloque les pirates, même si votre mot de passe et votre nom d’utilisateur ont été compromis.

articles.title: You can now opt out of AI training in Gemini without losing your chat history
articles.text:
The big picture: Google is rolling out new Gemini privacy settings that let users keep their chat history even after opting out of AI model training. The change is likely to be welcomed by tech-savvy users and privacy advocates, who have long clamored for their chats to be excluded from generative AI training.
The new settings were reported by 9to5Google, which noted that the Gemini app now splits chat history saving and consent for generative AI model training into separate sections. The change allows users to switch off generative AI training on their data while still saving their chat history for future reference.
Google is dividing the existing Keep Activity setting into a History section, which lets users control how long their chats are saved, and an AI training section, which lets them independently control whether their chat content is used to train AI models.
If Keep Activity is already turned off when the change reaches an account, both new options will be disabled by default.
Once the change takes effect, if users turn off History, Gemini will save future chats for around two months, using them to "respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public, with help from human reviewers." Before the update, with saving disabled, chats were kept for only 72 hours to protect Google, its users, and the public, and only the last 24 hours were used for context.
Google clarified that temporary chats are not used to train its AI models, so users who have switched off History and don't submit feedback won't have their chats used for AI training.
If History is off but the user submits feedback, Google will use that feedback and the last 24 hours of chat history, including attachments and data from connected apps, to improve Gemini.
The second AI training setting, meanwhile, lets users keep their chat history while independently controlling whether their chat content, including text and attachments, can be used for generative AI model training.
Google says it is notifying users of the changes by email, and that they will roll out globally over the coming weeks. It's unclear whether the new settings can be configured on both desktop and mobile, but the official emails will likely provide more details.

articles.title: Anitta debuta en GTA VI como la Dra. Nita en un pódcast exclusivo sobre relaciones e intimidad
articles.text:
Anitta se suma al elenco sonoro de Grand Theft Auto VI, el título de Rockstar Games que llega este jueves 19 de noviembre de 2026 a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X/S. La cantante brasileña presta su voz para interpretar a la Dra. Nita, conductora de un pódcast ficticio dentro del juego llamado Ask Dr. Nita, que forma parte de la programación de la emisora The Wipe.
El espacio, que combina humor adulto con un tono satírico, aborda temas vinculados a la sexualidad, las relaciones de pareja y la intimidad. Entre las invitadas que participan del segmento aparece la actriz Barbie Ferreira, en escenas donde Anitta habla en portugués.
Qué es el pódcast de Anitta en GTA 6 y cómo funciona dentro del juego
Ask Dr. Nita es un pódcast ficticio incluido en la emisora The Wipe de GTA VI, conducido por Anitta bajo el personaje de la Dra. Nita. El programa combina humor adulto con consejos sobre sexo e intimidad, y puede escucharse mientras los jugadores recorren el mapa en auto o desde el teléfono de los personajes.
Un video difundido por VOXL, medio digital de entretenimiento de Brasil, muestra un fragmento de la trama en el que Jason y Lucia, los protagonistas del juego, permanecen dentro de un auto descapotable rojo estacionado mientras escuchan la radio. En ese momento suena el segmento de la Dra. Nita, que mantiene una conversación íntima y cómplice con una invitada.
El diálogo comienza en inglés y rápidamente pasa al portugués. La invitada abre la charla con una frase directa: “Siento la sangre subiéndome al clítoris”. Anitta responde entre risas, con la intención de moderar el nivel de detalle al aire: “Está bien, pero no vamos a contarlo todo aquí”.
La invitada acepta el límite propuesto y murmura de forma cómplice: “Ajá, ajá... Solo para nosotras”. Anitta insiste en la misma idea y repite que no hace falta revelar todo el relato en el programa.
El tono de la conversación cambia cuando la invitada le dedica un halago personal a la conductora: “Ay, qué linda estás. Vaya, te extrañaba tanto, Anitta”. La Dra. Nita corresponde el gesto con coquetería y la llama “ricura”, al tiempo que vuelve a autorizarla a compartir solo una parte de la historia: “Qué nostalgia, ricura. Puedes hablar un poquito, pero no todo”.
Es menester señalar que el clip se corta en el instante en que la invitada comienza su relato con la frase “Fue aquí...”, dejando el resto de la confesión sin revelar.
Las 22 estaciones de radio confirmadas para GTA 6
Más allá del pódcast de Anitta, Rockstar incorporó a GTA VI un total de 22 estaciones de radio, la cifra más alta registrada hasta ahora en la saga. La oferta musical recorre géneros como pop, rap, metal, salsa, jazz, música clásica y country, disponible tanto al conducir por Leonida como desde el teléfono de los personajes.
Entre las emisoras confirmadas aparecen Flash FM, con pop conducido por Robyn y Alex Consani; Emotion 98.3, de soft rock; Vice City FM, con pop de los años 80; y Stockyard FM, centrada en indie y electrónica. También figuran Dirty South Classics y VCRR, ambas dedicadas al rap, en sus variantes sureña y moderna.
La lista incluye además Honey FM, con R&B y soul de los años 90; Cocoteo FM, de reggaetón, dembow y bachata; Radio La Ola, con clásicos latinos; y Radio On-U, orientada al dub y al reggae. A ellas se suman V-Rock, que regresa con rock clásico, y The Chamber 106.6, dedicada al metal.
El resto del listado lo completan Back Country Radio, de country; Gloriana Blues Radio; Leonida Jazz Radio; Symphony FM, de música clásica; Worldwide FM, que vuelve desde GTA 5 y GTA Online; CircoLoco Records Radio, vinculada a un sello cofundado por Rockstar; AfroBank FM, de música africana; Kaleidoscope FM, con mezclas poco convencionales; WKTT, de formato satírico político que regresa desde GTA 4; y The Wipe, el programa de charla donde se emite el segmento de la Dra. Nita.
Qué famosos conducen estaciones de radio en GTA VI
Rockstar sumó seis estaciones con conductores famosos para reforzar la identidad de cada emisora dentro de GTA VI. Entre los nombres que prestan su voz aparecen Bad Bunny, bajo el personaje de El Martillo en Cocoteo FM, y RaiNao, como La Gata en la misma emisora.
Flash FM está presentada por Robyn y Alex Consani, mientras que Dirty South Classics es conducida por Trick Daddy y Trina. En AfroBank FM, la conducción corre por cuenta de Burna Boy y Palms Trax. Back Country Radio, por su parte, tiene como presentadores a Morgan Wallen y Lana Del Rey.
The Chamber 106.6, la emisora dedicada al metal, está conducida por Kerry King y Tom Araya, integrantes de la banda Slayer. Esta selección de conductores se suma a la decisión de incluir emisoras específicas para sonidos latinos, africanos y estadounidenses, en línea con la diversidad cultural que Rockstar buscó representar en Leonida.
Principales canciones que sonarán en las estaciones de GTA 6
Junto al anuncio de las emisoras, Rockstar difundió un listado parcial de las canciones que integrarán cada estación. En Flash FM ya se confirmaron temas de Charli xcx, MGMT y la colaboración entre Zara Larsson y PinkPantheress.
Cocoteo FM incluirá música de Bad Bunny, además de un remix de Axel Rulay junto a Farruko y El Alfa, y una canción de Romeo Santos con El Chaval de la Bachata. En Back Country Radio sonarán artistas como David Allan Coe, Loretta Lynn, y el dúo formado por Hank Williams Jr. y Waylon Jennings.
AfroBank FM contará con canciones de Asake, Pat Thomas junto a Ebo Taylor, y una colaboración entre DJ Lag, Robot Boii y Kamo Mphela. Para los seguidores del metal, The Chamber 106.6 reproducirá temas de Black Sabbath, Pantera y Slayer.
Dirty South Classics, por su parte, incluirá canciones de David Banner junto a Lil’ Flip, JT Money con Solé, y una colaboración de DJ Khaled con Trick Daddy, Rick Ross y Pitbull.

articles.title: Tor hit by major DDoS attack, forced to release emergency update to users
articles.text:
Tor hit by major DDoS attack, forced to release emergency update to users
Users are reporting slow and unresponsive Tor networks
- The Tor Project releases urgent updates after large-scale DDoS attacks overwhelmed relay operators across the network
- Attackers flooded relays with circuit requests, causing resource exhaustion, degraded performance, and lost relay functionality
- Maintainers say the attacks are ongoing and adaptive, urging operators to upgrade immediately and watch for further fixes
The Tor Project seems to be experiencing major Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks which have gotten so disruptive that they forced the release of an update in order to address it.
Now, Tor Project says “most relay operators” were affected by an ongoing DDoS attack.
“This release comes in rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack on the network, which has affected most relay operators,” the patch notes read. “This is not an easy problem to address, as relays across the network are being overwhelmed by a massive flood of client circuits. We are actively evaluating additional defenses and so expect further releases in the near future.”
Second patch
Tor is a privacy-focused network that routes internet traffic through multiple relays (servers operated by volunteers), allowing users to hide their identities and online activities. The relays work by receiving and forwarding encrypted traffic between users and other parts of the network, and are divided into three categories: Guard (or entry) relays (the first point of contact between a Tor user and the network), Middle relays (these pass traffic between them and add layers of separation), and Exit relays (these send traffic from the Tor network back to the regular internet and the user’s final destination).
The patch brings Tor to version 0.4.9.17 and includes a series of security fixes, including, according to the patch notes, one “especially important for relay DoS defenses related to IPv6 handling."
The project now urges relay operators to upgrade to the latest version as soon as possible, and to keep an eye out for additional updates. It did not share any details about the ongoing DDoS attack.
This doesn’t seem to be the first patch the Tor Project released in response to the DDoS attacks, either.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Approximately three weeks ago, Tor version 0.4.9.15 was introduced, also in response to attacks.
This version, however, seems not to have worked properly. “Tor relay operators are reporting renewed denial-of-service (DoS) attacks despite security mitigations introduced in Tor 0.4.9.15 on October 28,” a Reddit user said in a thread on “renewed DoS attacks”.. “On November 9, one operator reported that two relays lost their HSDir flags after attacks caused severe CPU and memory exhaustion. Another operator reported similar activity on November 10, including thousands of circuit creation requests per second.”
The operator said the reports suggest whoever is behind these attacks managed to bypass Tor’s recent protections. “The full scope of the attacks and their impact on the wider Tor network are not clear,” they said.
Reddit activity
Reddit has quite a few threads from different Tor users complaining about nodes being saturated and the network being slow or outright unresponsive. On November 9, a person on the Tor Project’s forum said the attacker “successfully stripped the HSDir flag from two [of their] relays” in a few hours, and that one attack saw “high asymmetric egress and one saw high asymmetric ingress (although not nearly as much as the old attacks).”
Both relays lost their HSDir flags as a result.
At press time, no threat actors claimed responsibility for the attacks, so we don’t know who they are or what their motives are. What we do know is that the attacks appear persistent and adaptive, and that relay operators reported multiple waves of attacks and changes in attack patterns.
Whether or not the latest patch finally addresses the attacks in full, remains to be seen. The project maintainers seem to be confident about it.
“Thank you to all… except our attacker(s),” they said in conclusion.

articles.title: AI can write code, but knowing what to build still matters
articles.text:
AI can write code, but knowing what to build still matters
At TechSparks 2026, Srinivas Chamarthy of Diligent India, Madhusudan N. Murthy of EY GDS, and Arun Kalyanaraman of Target discussed why domain expertise, engineering skills, and human judgement remain important as AI makes software development more accessible.
AI is making it easier to build software. Product managers, designers, and domain experts can now turn ideas into prototypes without necessarily knowing how to code. But turning those prototypes into reliable products that solve real problems remains a challenge.
At TechSparks 2026, Srinivas Chamarthy, Senior Vice President of Engineering, Site Lead and Country Head at Diligent India; Madhusudan N. Murthy, Digital Engineering and Tech Strategy Leader at EY GDS; and Arun Kalyanaraman, VP of Engineering at Target in India, discussed these changes during a panel titled ‘From Who Can Code to Who Can Build’.
The discussion was moderated by Chhavi Mahajan, Chief Content Officer at YourStory.
From prototypes to production
AI-assisted development allows business teams to test ideas, demonstrate concepts, and gather feedback much earlier. However, a prototype that shows an idea can work is not necessarily ready for production. Applications still need to meet security, scalability, and reliability requirements.
Murthy said that AI is making experimentation easier, but companies must distinguish between a proof of concept and a production-ready application. Engineering teams still need to identify vulnerabilities, put safeguards in place, and ensure systems can handle real-world use.
“It's good, it's a very positive development, but it also has to have its guardrails,” he stated.
Kalyanaraman said AI can do more than help developers write code faster. It can also speed up the entire development process, from defining a problem and testing a solution to getting stakeholder approval. However, strong engineering fundamentals, architectural thinking, and technical depth will remain essential, even as AI changes how solutions are built.
He gave the example of a product owner, an engineer, and a UX professional who used AI tools and large language models to prototype a complex concept and present it to leadership within a week. Without these tools, the process could have taken six weeks to two months.
The benefit was not just faster coding, but the ability to test an idea and make a decision sooner.
Chamarthy said coding is becoming a commodity in the generative AI era, shortening the path from prototype to customer feedback to production, with a nine-month cycle potentially coming down to a month or two. As speed increases, he said, knowing what not to build becomes more valuable, so ideas should be tested in a sandbox while experienced engineers harden them for security, scalability, and privacy.
Deciding where human oversight is needed
As companies move from using AI to assist developers to deploying agents that can complete tasks with limited supervision, they must decide how much autonomy to allow.
Chamarthy said this should depend on the risks involved, the potential impact of a decision, and whether its outcome can be reversed.
He suggested organizations consider whether a decision is a two-way-door or a one-way-door call, with significant financial or strategic decisions needing human oversight and contextual judgment.
Chamarthy cautioned that access to AI coding tools cannot replace engineering experience. Experienced engineers understand the architectural decisions that affect security, scalability, and long-term maintenance, including risks that may not be apparent in a prototype.
His advice was to encourage experimentation, but within controlled environments.
“Don't stop the code. Sandbox it.”
This allows more employees to test ideas while giving engineering teams the opportunity to review the applications, address weaknesses, and prepare them for production.
Why domain expertise matters
As AI makes it easier to generate code and find answers, knowing which problems to solve becomes more important.
Kalyanaraman compared using AI to consulting a genie that grants only three wishes. Getting a useful result depends on asking the right questions and understanding the constraints.
“In a world where maybe getting answers are easy, asking the right questions is going to be a really, really critical skill,” he said.
People who understand customers, business processes, and operational requirements are better placed to identify solutions that create value.
Engineering teams will also need systems thinking and platform expertise to help non-engineers develop applications without putting production systems at risk.
The shift also has implications for workforce development.
Murthy said EY GDS is preparing employees for an AI-driven workplace by bringing experienced professionals and younger talent together. Existing employees bring knowledge of customers and systems, while newer team members contribute fresh approaches and develop emerging technical skills.
Chamarthy said teams need a mix of strengths: organizations should upskill existing employees, who understand their products and customers, while bringing in fresh graduates who can work with AI tools.
He also added that engineering performance should be measured by the problems teams solve for customers, rather than only by metrics such as lines of code written or tickets closed.
As AI takes over more routine work, the outcomes delivered by engineering teams become a more useful measure of their contribution.
A workforce of people and AI agents
The panellists expect employees and AI agents to work increasingly closely together.
As agents take on more complex tasks, companies will need to rethink workflows, accountability and performance expectations. They will also need to ensure safeguards keep pace with what the technology can do.
Murthy described a future in which managers will oversee AI agents alongside human employees.
“The future I see is getting used to agents reporting to you and not just humans,” he said.
Kalyanaraman added that The New Tech Order is not just about what AI can do for us. It is about how we evolve our thinking, engineering practices, and decision-making to make the most of it.
While AI is making software easier to build, companies will still need engineering expertise, domain knowledge, and human judgement to decide which ideas are worth pursuing and which prototypes are ready for production.

articles.title: Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) on SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) on SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization
Fine-tuning is the process of continuing to train a pretrained large language model (LLM) on a company’s own data so it adapts to a specific domain, task, or style rather than relying on general-purpose knowledge alone. For businesses, the value is twofold. A fine-tuned model delivers measurably better accuracy on domain-specific work while reducing costs: a smaller specialized model can match or exceed a frontier model on your task at a fraction of the per-token inference price. Those savings compound across millions of requests. Fine-tuning has therefore become an essential process for businesses looking to get more value from LLMs at lower costs.
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods like Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) have emerged as a practical solution for fine-tuning LLMs to downstream tasks, reducing GPU capacity requirements by updating only a small subset of LLM parameters. LoRA aims to strike a balance between efficiency and expressiveness, however, the low-rank nature of the weight update inherently limits the representation power of LoRA fine-tuned models, potentially compromising performance on complex tasks. This trade-off hampers the ability of LoRA methods to capture complex patterns needed for diverse tasks. To address these challenges, Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) updates model parameters simultaneously, overcoming the low-rank limitations so LLMs can fully absorb complex domain-specific knowledge.
Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization now supports Full Fine-Tuning (FFT), so you can achieve superior model quality without managing infrastructure. There is no GPU provisioning, cluster setup, or distributed-training configuration required. In this post, we explore when and where FFT consistently outperforms LoRA across key benchmarks, examine the spectral properties of model weight matrices that explain this quality gap, provide practical hyperparameter tuning guidelines backed by controlled experiments using SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization, and show you how to get started with FFT on SageMaker AI.
Full Fine-Tuning: Why it matters
Model customization types like LoRA reduce trainable parameters by freezing the pre-trained model’s weights and injecting small, separate pairs of replacement matrices (called low-rank matrices) into the model layers. This works well for simple adaptations, but the low-rank structure inherently limits the representation power of the fine-tuned model. As tasks grow more complex and datasets scale beyond tens of thousands of examples, LoRA hits an accuracy plateau where increasing rank (and thus trainable parameters) fails to bridge the accuracy gap with standard fine-tuning. This plateau reveals that the performance gap isn’t simply because of fewer parameters. It’s caused by rank deficiency itself. The low-rank update can’t capture the full complexity of the weight changes needed for deep task adaptation.
However, for complex tasks and domains where large, good-quality datasets exist, full-rank fine-tuning excels by updating model parameters simultaneously. FFT modifies the model’s weight matrix uniformly, using the full representational capacity of the model’s weight matrices rather than restricting updates to a small subspace, and without introducing the abrupt, localized distortions characteristic of low-rank methods. The result is stronger model convergence, better activation alignment across model layers, and a model that faithfully captures both the target task distribution and the richness of its pre-trained knowledge. FFT’s quality advantage grows with dataset scale: at 100K+ training examples, FFT achieved 90.0 percent on LLM-as-Judge semantic correctness across code generation tasks, as shown in the following chart.
Furthermore, the following radar chart provides a holistic view: the base model (inner polygon) shows consistently low scores across all axes. LoRA (middle polygon) shows strong, balanced improvement. FFT (outer polygon) extends further on every dimension, with particularly pronounced leads on BLEU and ROUGE-2 scores. This multi-dimensional quality lead confirms that it isn’t a metric-specific artifact but a fundamental advantage of full-rank optimization.
The details of how we arrived at these results, the coding datasets used for model customization, and the experimentation process are explained in detail in the following sections.
Experimentation and benchmark results
In this post we used the Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) technique on a Qwen3-4B base model offered within Amazon SageMaker AI Studio and performed all the fine-tuning experiments using SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization across LoRA and FFT training methods. Within each experiment, both methods received the same prompts, targets, and evaluation code.
Dataset: Code generation 110K instruction pairs
For all the experimentation, we fine-tuned the Qwen3-4B base model on the Magicoder-Evol-Instruct-110K dataset, a curated corpus of 110,000 coding instruction-response pairs spanning algorithm design, debugging, data structures, and systems programming. We applied a 90/5/5 split to the dataset: 99,000 records for training, 5,500 for validation to monitor convergence and training loss during the customization job, and 5,500 reserved as a held-out test set for unbiased evaluation of the final model, as registered in SageMaker AI dataset assets and shown in the following figure.
Serverless Model Customization job
All the model customization experiments in this post were performed on Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization. Serverless Model Customization on SageMaker AI lets data scientists and machine learning (ML) engineers focus on model fine-tuning without managing infrastructure or GPU capacity planning. You specify the base model, dataset, and hyperparameters, and the service handles compute allocation and checkpoint management automatically in a serverless fashion. The following code snippet shows one such experiment for launching a Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) job on Serverless Model Customization using the SageMaker Python SDK.
The code triggers a serverless model customization job, shown in the following screenshot, with training performance metrics tracked in the job and viewable in the linked MLflow app.
Switching from Full Fine-Tuning to LoRA requires only one change: set TrainingType.FULL to TrainingType.LORA. The rest of the code remains identical:
Model evaluation and benchmarking
We tested the resulting customized models across three diverse evaluation methods built into SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization: LLM-as-Judge, PRIMECODE, and MMLU, shown in the following image. Each targets a different dimension of model quality: semantic correctness, code generation fidelity, and general knowledge retention. Together they provide a comprehensive picture of the model customization quality.
The LLM-as-Judge metric uses a frontier model (in this post, Amazon Nova Pro) as an automated evaluator that reads the model’s generated code alongside the original prompt and judges whether the solution is logically correct. On serverless model customization you can evaluate both the customized model alongside the base model, as shown in the following figure.
PRIMECODE is a custom scorer evaluation that measures how closely the model’s generated code matches reference solutions using deterministic text-similarity metrics: BLEU (n-gram precision), ROUGE-1/2/L (recall-oriented overlap), and F1 (precision-recall balance). These metrics are fully reproducible, making them ideal for controlled ablation studies. We used PRIMECODE as our primary metric for surface-level code quality because it quantifies how well the model has learned the coding patterns, formatting conventions, and implementation style present in the training data. A high BLEU score means the model generates code that looks structurally similar to expert-written solutions, as shown in the following results.
MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding) is a built-in benchmark that tests the model across 57 academic subjects from abstract algebra and anatomy to Nutrition and Philosophy. It measures whether the model retains its broad general knowledge after domain-specific fine-tuning, as shown in the following figure. We used MMLU as our forgetting detection guardrail. Fine-tuning on code can overwrite general capabilities stored in the model’s weights. By tracking MMLU accuracy before and after fine-tuning, we can quantify exactly how much general knowledge the model sacrifices for code generation improvement, and whether our hyperparameter choices accelerate or mitigate this trade-off.
Rapid experimentation at scale
The ease of setup and use of SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization let us perform rapid experimentation without re-provisioning infrastructure. We changed training types between LoRA and FFT, swept hyperparameters, and tested across multiple base models. Over a short time window, we ran tens of model customization experiments across multiple supported base models (Qwen3-4B, DeepSeek-R1-1.5B, Nemotron-30B, Gemma-4-26B), systematically ablating learning rate, batch size, warmup ratio, epoch count, and dataset scale. Each experiment, from job submission to evaluation results, completed in a few hours and the resulting fine-tuned models were automatically registered in SageMaker Model Registry as versioned Model Packages, ready for review or deployment.
Hyperparameter options
SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization supports many hyperparameters. In this section, we explain a few important ones, informed by the series of experiments that we ran across multiple hyperparameter configurations within the previously mentioned code generation task. While effective values will vary by task, the patterns observed across these experiments provide useful starting points when configuring FFT model customization jobs. For more information about the hyperparameters that you can configure before launching an FFT model customization job, see the hyperparameters documentation page.
1. learning_rate
In full fine-tuning, the learning rate controls how aggressively every weight is updated. Unlike LoRA, where only small adapter matrices change, an FFT learning rate that is too high permanently overwrites pretrained knowledge. In our experiments, the following LR × dataset-size risk map shows that an LR of 2e-5 on a large dataset (over 100 thousand) was the safe zone.
2. max_epochs
Epoch count in FFT is fundamentally a forgetting question, not a loss-curve question. Training loss will keep falling and your held-out validation will look healthy because it shares a distribution with training data, but capabilities on everything you didn’t train on quietly degrade. The LLM-as-Judge correctness score rose to 90.0 percent at 3 epochs, and extending beyond 3 epochs degraded every variant we experimented with.
3. global_batch_size
Batch size determines how many examples contribute to each gradient step. At a fixed learning rate, smaller batches produce more noisy updates that behave much like a higher learning rate, increasing forgetting risk. Larger batches reduce noise but also reduce the number of optimization steps, potentially underfitting.
Catastrophic forgetting risk
FFT modifies every parameter in the model, including the parameters that encode general knowledge acquired during pre-training. When fine-tuning pushes these parameters too aggressively toward a narrow domain, the model can “forget” its broader capabilities, a phenomenon known as catastrophic forgetting. We tested for this systematically using MMLU, measuring general knowledge retention across all our fine-tuning configurations. A baseline configuration with warmup=5 percent, batch size 8, and LR=2e-5 best preserved general knowledge (MMLU), as shown in the following figure.
Hence, it is important to note that FFT isn’t universally superior to LoRA, and its effectiveness is extremely sensitive to hyperparameter choices. For example, in our experiments, both FFT and LoRA underperformed the base model on MATH exact match, underscoring the challenge of preserving reasoning capabilities during domain-specific fine-tuning. Aggressive learning rates (LR ≥ 5e-5) in FFT proved particularly destructive, causing MATH scores to plummet to 2–3 percent and MMLU accuracy to drop to 3.6 percent, clear evidence of catastrophic forgetting. Additionally, LoRA slightly outperformed FFT on the LLM-as-Judge metric (81.5 percent compared to 79.5 percent), demonstrating that parameter-efficient methods can still hold an edge on subjective quality assessments. These findings reinforce that the choice between FFT and LoRA should be guided by careful experimentation, dataset characteristics, and a clear understanding of the trade-offs involved.
Conclusion
With Full Fine-Tuning on Amazon SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization, your model can fully absorb domain-specific knowledge when task complexity and data scale demand it. If your use case requires deep adaptation, such as specialized reasoning, code generation, or domain-specific language understanding, and you have sufficient high-quality training data, FFT delivers measurably stronger results.
You can get started with FFT on SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization with serverless training, built-in evaluation, and without infrastructure or compute capacity planning, so you can focus on your data and hyperparameter choices. You can use the SageMaker Python SDK to configure and launch your training and evaluation jobs programmatically. You can see the documentation for supported base models available for Full Fine-Tuning on Serverless Model Customization.

articles.title: Global OLED Monitor Shipments Double YoY in 3Q26
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
Global OLED Monitor Shipments Double YoY in 3Q26
Global OLED monitor shipments maintained strong momentum in the third quarter of 2026, rising 13% QoQ and doubling compared with the same period in 2025, according to TrendForce's latest research. Growth was driven not only by continued product launches from major brands, which helped boost shipment volumes, but also by ample upstream panel supply. The latter has enabled second-tier and emerging brands to significantly expand their shipments.
ASUS retains top spot as MSI climbs to second place for the first time
TrendForce reports that competition in the OLED monitor market intensified in the third quarter as brands adjusted their strategies and product portfolios. Rankings shifted considerably among the second- through fifth-largest vendors, highlighting the increasingly fierce competition among brands vying for positions just below the market leader.Amid this competitive landscape, ASUS maintained its position as the world's leading OLED monitor brand, capturing a 21.7% market share. Shipments rose a steady 6% QoQ, supported by an easing of supply constraints on its key high-end 27-inch QHD 540 Hz panels. The launch of new models commemorating the brand's 20th anniversary also helped stimulate demand.
MSI climbed to second place globally for the first time, with its market share increasing 1.7 percentage points QoQ to 14.5%. Its cumulative shipments over the first three quarters were roughly on par with Samsung's. MSI's third-quarter growth was primarily driven by increased orders for its 27-inch QHD monitors ahead of the holiday shopping season, alongside the successive launches of several new models, including 27-inch QHD 320 Hz monitors.
Samsung slipped to third place, with its market share declining to 11.3%. Although the company's shipments remained relatively stable throughout the first three quarters of 2026, its share was diluted by the rapid expansion of the overall market. In response to mounting competition, Samsung plans to ramp up shipments aggressively in the fourth quarter, targeting the year-end holiday shopping season in Europe and North America. This push could help the company reclaim its position as the world's second-largest supplier.
LGE rose one position to fourth place, securing an 8.6% market share in the third quarter. Aggressive promotional campaigns for select 27-inch QHD 240 Hz models successfully stimulated demand and supported the brand's improved ranking.
Dell also moved up one position to fifth place, as its shipment performance recovered and its quarterly market share reached 8.2%. Growth was primarily fueled by continued shipment expansion of its mainstream 27-inch QHD 240 Hz models, together with accelerating shipments of a new 39-inch model introduced in the second quarter.
