articles.title: GTA VI runs at 1440p on PS5 and Xbox Series X, but just 720p with upscaling on Series S — Rockstar details upscaling technologies ahead of launch
articles.text:
GTA VI runs at 1440p on PS5 and Xbox Series X, but just 720p with upscaling on Series S — Rockstar details upscaling technologies for launch
No support for native 4K.
The most highly anticipated video game of the decade is here. GTA VI arrives almost 13 years after GTA V, with reports suggesting that it has already generated around $1.54 billion in revenue from 16 million preorders. Ahead of its release, Rockstar Games has finally shared some technical details, including rendering resolutions and upscaling technologies being used across all consoles.
In a statement shared with Wccftech, the technical team at Rockstar has confirmed that GTA VI uses different upscaling solutions across all consoles in order to achieve a balance between visual quality and performance with a target of 30FPS. The PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X use Rockstar's own temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) solution, while the PlayStation 5 Pro relies on Sony's second-generation PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR2). The Xbox Series S, meanwhile, relies on AMD's FSR 4 upscaling technology.
As for rendered resolutions, the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and PlayStation 5 Pro all start with a native base resolution of 1440p, which is then upscaled to 4K. The Xbox Series S is the least powerful console; thus, the game runs at a lower base resolution of 720p, which is upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4. The final image on all consoles is then composited with a 4K user interface before being presented.
Rockstar has also developed a physically-based material library for GTA VI and a cinematic imaging pipeline to deliver realistic lighting, reflections, and material details within the game. The team says it has worked to maintain a consistent lighting solution across all consoles, including the Xbox Series S, while adjusting ray-traced global illumination (RTGI) features depending on each platform's hardware capabilities.
The PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S launched all the way back in 2020, and while the consoles have capable hardware, their architectures are finally beginning to show their age. The fact that Rockstar is targeting just 30FPS across all consoles, while relying on different upscaling technologies and rendering resolutions, highlights how much performance is potentially being left on the table in order to maintain visual fidelity. That being said, a PC release of GTA VI continues to be a big question mark. Rockstar is yet to announce a release date or even provide a launch window, meaning that PC gamers can only rely on Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream the game on their systems.

articles.title: Google Wallet chega ao iPhone, mas não se empolgue • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google Wallet chega ao iPhone, mas não se empolgue
Google Wallet (Carteira do Google) para iOS estreia nos Estados Unidos, mas com limitações importantes.
O Google Wallet (no Brasil, Carteira do Google) não é mais exclusividade do ecossistema do Android. O aplicativo do serviço acaba de ser disponibilizado para usuários do iPhone. Por ora, a versão para iOS só funciona nos Estados Unidos. Mas esta não é a única limitação.
Por meio do novo aplicativo, os usuários podem armazenar e acessar determinados tipos de documentos no Google Wallet, como passagens aéreas, ingressos para shows e cartões de fidelidade.
Nesse sentido, a novidade também pode sincronizar dados com o Gmail para obter, automaticamente, recibos de compras, códigos de rastreamento de entregas, cartões de embarque e assim por diante.
Por outro lado, não é possível armazenar documentos oficiais, como carteira de motorista ou identidade digital, ao contrário do que pode ser feito com o Google Wallet para Android, pelo menos nos Estados Unidos.
O aplicativo também permite que o usuário gerencie cartões de crédito ou débito registrados em sua Conta Google, facilitando o preenchimento automático dessas informações em compras realizadas por meio do Chrome ou lojas online compatíveis com o Google Pay.
Agora vem o que talvez seja a maior limitação do Google Wallet para iPhone: o app não permite pagamentos por aproximação, tampouco pode ser usado para pagar transporte público, exceto via QR Code ou código de barras.
O Google não fez nenhum pronunciamento oficial sobre o assunto, mas é provável que haja limitações comerciais ou técnicas. Uma delas pode ser a necessidade de pagar taxas à Apple para o uso de APIs de NFC e Secure Element, que são necessárias para pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone. Talvez o Google não considere viável arcar com esses custos.
Outra possibilidade reside no fato de o iPhone ser configurado por padrão para funcionar com o Apple Pay. Talvez o Google entenda que convencer o usuário a trocar esse serviço pela sua solução possa causar confusão ou deixar o uso do Google Wallet mais complexo.
Não está descartada a hipótese de o Google Wallet para iPhone lidar com pagamentos em algum momento. Mas, por ora, a versão para iOS serve apenas para deixar os usuários um pouco mais próximos de alguns serviços do Google.
Ainda não há informação sobre a expansão da novidade para além dos Estados Unidos.
Vale destacar ainda que o Google já teve uma versão do Wallet para iPhone, lançada em 2013. Mas o aplicativo passou por mudanças posteriores e acabou sendo descontinuado como carteira digital. Desde então, a companhia vinha focando seus esforços na versão para Android.

articles.title: Recent spate of outages attributed to technical issues amid accelerated AI bug discovery - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Recent spate of outages attributed to technical issues amid accelerated AI bug discovery
U.S. authorities don’t believe that the recent outages at federal agencies and top tech firms were caused by cyberattacks.
The Federal Aviation Administration, United Airlines, Apple Inc. and Microsoft Corp. were among the affected organizations. All four said that their systems were disrupted by technical issues rather than hackers. Experts noted that artificial intelligence models’ ability to find software bugs has made patching more complicated, which may increase the risk of outages.
The first major service disruption hit Exchange Online on Thursday. The Microsoft-operated email service went offline for nearly a day, which left 450 million users without access to their inboxes. The company attributed the downtime to two separate bugs in the software that powers its network. The first one went undetected for three months, while the other cropped up a day before the outage.
The FAA experienced a network disruption of its own on Friday. An issue with a router at the agency’s El Dorado, Arkansas campus disrupted aircraft communications and radar data feeds. The outage led to more than 12,000 flight cancellations.
United Airlines reported a fairly extensive, but brief infrastructure disruption a few days later. The issue took several of the carrier’s pilot-facing applications offline for 30 minutes. Fewer than 150 flights were affected.
Yet another high-profile network outage occurred on Tuesday, this time at the U.S. National Security Agency. A technical problem cropped up in NSANet, an internal network that agency staff use to exchange classified information. The cause of the outage and its duration were not specified. However, officials did tell NBC the disruption wasn’t caused by a cyberattack.
U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton reiterated that point in a Tuesday interview. He added that officials have “looked very closely” into the other outages that occurred over the past week and ruled out cyberattacks as the cause. According to Clayton, authorities believe that the disruptions occurred because companies are patching vulnerabilities “on much larger scale” than before.
Frontier AI models have found thousands of software vulnerabilities over the past few months. That accelerated pace of discovery is creating more work for administrators, who have to roll out patches more frequently than before. The less time there is to prepare a patch, the greater the risk of human error.
“As AI accelerates vulnerability discovery and development cycles, pressure is mounting on companies to deploy fixes quickly, often without fully understanding how those changes will affect interconnected systems, “ said Prince Kohli, the chief executive officer of software testing provider Sauce Labs Inc. “The only way to prevent these issues is continuous testing and release validation in their development processes, even more so for critical software updates.”
Apple and Workday Inc. are also among the companies that have experienced outages in recent days. Separately, several financial services temporarily became unavailable because of an issue with one of JPMorgan Chase’s on-premises systems. All the incidents have been resolved.

articles.title: Avec son Auto-empty Dok, Dyson donne une nouvelle aspiration au V10 Konical : notre test
articles.text:
| Type d'aspirateur-balai | Stick | 
| Type de filtre | Multicyclonique, Mousse, HEPA | 
| Mode de fonctionnement | Interrupteur | 
| Capacité collecteur | 0.54 L | 
| Rangement | Autre | 
| Batterie amovible | Oui | 
| Poids | 2.65 g | 
| Accessoire(s) fourni(s) | Brosse, Mini-brosse motorisée, Suceur, Brosse meubles et textiles | 
| Option(s) supplémentaire(s) | Mode Turbo, Rampe de LEDs sur la brosse, Indicateur de charge | 
Déclinaison du V10 Konical, le Dyson V10 Konical avec Auto-Empty Dok est accompagné d'une base de vidange qui lui sert au passage de support de rangement et de charge. Le Britannique y cache une petite surprise qui aurait de quoi faire hausser plus d'un sourcil…
Au fil des générations, Dyson nous a habitués à ses aspirateurs sans-fil emblématiques. Tous reposent sur le même système de rangement : ils sont livrés avec une base de charge à fixer au mur, ou peuvent être simplement posés dans un recoin et branchés à un câble classique. Néanmoins, en un peu plus de 15 ans de règne sur le marché de l’aspiration sans-fil, le fabricant a vu débarquer une concurrence aussi nombreuse que féroce, rivalisant d’ingéniosité pour pousser le consommateur à renouveler son antique aspirateur.
Parmi les options désormais les plus communes dans l’entretien des sols, il y a les stations de vidange. Il faut dire que les aspirateurs-balais disposent de collecteurs de taille relativement modeste afin de limiter l’encombrement du bloc tenu en main, à vider très régulièrement pour éviter le trop-plein. C’est ici qu’intervient la fameuse station, qui automatise le processus pour mieux alléger la charge ménagère de l’utilisateur.
Dyson s’y met donc sur le tard et opte pour une déclinaison de son V10 Konical, lancé au printemps 2026. L’appareil prend donc le nom à rallonge de Dyson V10 Konical avec Auto-Empty Dok, qui a attendu quelques mois avant d’être commercialisé en France. Cette association donne un nouveau souffle à un aspirateur qui, par ailleurs, ne change pas d’un iota. Elle déleste simplement l’utilisateur de la petite corvée — si l'on peut la nommer ainsi — que constitue la vidange de son collecteur à poussière.
Alors que le V10 Konical est facturé seul 499 €, sa mouture avec Auto-Empty Dok culmine à 659 €. De quoi le placer face à la cohorte de produits concurrents dotés de bases de vidage, proposés parfois (voire souvent) à des tarifs plus attractifs.
Le Dyson V10 Konical s’inscrit dans la droite lignée du V8 Cyclone. Tout y est : des finitions soignées, réalisées dans un plastique qui inspire confiance, à l'assemblage irréprochable. Tous les éléments du balai s’emboîtent parfaitement, un clic net signalant leur verrouillage. Ils se détachent tout aussi facilement, ce dont ses concurrents ne peuvent pas toujours se targuer.
La prise en main se révèle des plus classiques et confortable. Le V10 Konical est à peine plus lourd que le V8 Cyclone (1,64 kg contre 1,62 kg) et atteint 2,73 kg avec sa tête All Floor Cones, un peu massive. Autrement dit, il concède un surplus de 140 g par rapport à son prédécesseur, ce qui est pour le moins difficile à déceler une fois l’engin en main. Il faut dire qu’il s'avère aisé à manipuler et qu’il négocie sans broncher les virages serrés, un atout pratique pour les pilotes adeptes des circuits de ménage menés à toute allure. L’adhérence aux sols y est suffisante pour éviter les sorties de route.
Lors de notre test du V10 Konical sans base, nous avions relevé des options limitées à leur plus simple expression. Il en va de même pour la version Auto-Empty Dok, qui n’en diffère pas d’un iota. Oubliez donc tout indicateur de batterie, ou même de simples témoins leds, un choix qui complique logiquement l’anticipation d’une longue session de ménage. L’aspirateur indique simplement par trois brefs à-coups qu’il s’apprête à tomber à court d'énergie, mais c’est à peu près tout. Outre son bouton d’allumage, il inclut une touche permettant d’activer l’un des trois niveaux de puissance de l’appareil (Auto, Eco et Max). Cette simplicité rend l’usage du V10 Konical particulièrement intuitif.
L’aspirateur-balai est livré avec son jeu d’accessoires habituel. Outre la brosse principale du V10 Konical (All Floor Cones), on compte donc une mini-brosse motorisée adaptée aux petits espaces et un suceur long pour les plinthes et autres recoins. N’oublions pas la base Auto-Empty Dok, qui ne risque pas de passer inaperçue.
Plus haute que l’aspirateur seul, elle prend la forme d’un cylindre haut de 1,20 m pour un diamètre de 18 cm (hors base circulaire à clipser au cylindre). La base s’y emboîte d’un clic et se montre illico prête à l’emploi. L’aspirateur, lui, s’y loge par le haut de sa base aspirante : il faut prendre le coup de main pour l’y fixer, mais rien de bien compliqué. Ajoutons que cette station collecte les poussières et sert en parallèle de socle de charge.
Le V10 Konical n’est probablement pas l’aspirateur le plus performant de notre comparatif, mais il s’acquitte très convenablement des tâches qui lui sont confiées. C’est sur les sols durs qu’il livre le meilleur de lui-même, puisqu’un seul passage suffit pour venir à bout de la totalité des déchets qui jonchent le sol, quel que soit le niveau de puissance sélectionné. Sa large tête d’aspiration (environ 29 cm) permet d’ailleurs d’aller vite.
Le V10 Konical reste performant sur les moquettes fines. Au premier passage, en puissance normale, il gobe 85 % des détritus, tandis qu’il en aspire 98 % en mode Max. Il va sans dire qu’au second passage, tout a disparu.
En revanche, les tapis à poils longs lui posent davantage de problèmes. Il ne récolte alors que 55 % des déchets en mode standard et 80 % en mode Max. Certes, l’exercice n’est pas aisé. À son crédit, notons sa bonne capacité, due à sa brosse, à débarrasser notre tapis des touffes de poils déposées lors de nos essais.
En revanche, l’aspirateur est à la peine sur les sols à rainures, à savoir les parquets. Il ne parvient à extraire que 5 % de la poussière fine au premier passage en mode standard, valeur qui grimpe à 13 % au troisième passage. Au même exercice, le Dyson V16 Piston Animal récupère plus de 25 % des poussières. En mode Max, le troisième passage vient à bout d’environ 24 % des poussières incrustées.
Pour aller plus loin :
Dyson n’est pas le seul à opter pour un tel fonctionnement, mais le choix surprend de la part d’une marque qui s’est fait un devoir de faire disparaître le traditionnel sac d’aspirateur. Sa base de vidage fonctionne en effet avec ce que le fabricant désigne pudiquement sous le nom de “doublure hygiénique” (un sac, quoi…) de 2,5 l. Il faut bien admettre qu’ôter un sac de temps à autre (tous les deux mois en moyenne, selon Dyson, mais tout dépend évidemment de vos habitudes) est moins fastidieux que de vider un collecteur, au risque de renverser de la poussière au passage. Mais ce fusil changé discrètement d’épaule ne manque pas de sel… et coûtera à l’utilisateur 12 € pour trois sacs.
La base compte deux trappes latérales. Celle du bas est dédiée au sac, donc, mais aussi au filtre HEPA lavable à l'eau. La seconde, au-dessus, accueille au déballage un sac de rechange. Surtout, elle est conçue pour ranger la mini-brosse et le suceur long, autrement dit ces accessoires que l'on ne sait jamais où glisser. La station n'est pas très discrète, mais elle se rend utile.
D’un point de vue un peu plus technique, la base vide le collecteur du V10 Konical en 30 s. Elle est un peu bruyante, puisque nous avons mesuré 70,5 dB, mais cela ne dure pas longtemps.
Il est possible de vider manuellement le collecteur situé sur le corps de l’aspirateur en tirant sur la poignée qui déclenche l’ouverture de sa trappe (au-dessus d’une poubelle, de préférence). On peut accéder au même endroit au filtre-grille, mais aussi au filtre mousse. Le filtre HEPA se place derrière le bloc-moteur et se dévisse très simplement. L’opération n’est de toute manière pas très fréquente, compte tenu de l’efficacité de la filtration multicyclonique.
Quid de la tête d’aspiration All Floor Cones ? Ayant le mérite d’éviter aux cheveux longs de s’entortiller, elle peut se démonter aisément pour un nettoyage complet et rapide.
Pas forcément un mime Marceau de l'aspiration, le V10 Konical délivre 69 dB lorsqu’il est utilisé en mode standard. En passant au mode Boost, on atteint 73 dB. C’est un peu plus que les modèles concurrents, qui dépassent rarement 70 dB.
Le bloc-moteur du V10 Konical n’étant pas énorme, il ne laisse pas beaucoup de place à sa batterie. La capacité réduite de cette dernière explique une autonomie un peu légère, limitée à 25 min en mode standard. Si l’état de vos sols exige de passer en mode Boost, il faudra faire vite : comptez 7 min 30 s d’utilisation avant extinction des feux.
En revanche, la charge de l’appareil est plutôt rapide. Elle ne demande que 2 h, ce qui est peu dans le segment des aspirateurs-balais.
Dyson revendique une note de réparabilité de 9,2/10, plus élevée de 0,1 point que celle du V10 Konical sans base de vidage. L'appareil doit cette meilleure note au prix plus avantageux de ses pièces détachées, ainsi qu'à leur livraison rapide.
Le V10 Konical de Dyson a le mérite d’être peu encombrant et facile — trop, peut-être — à utiliser comme à entretenir. En revanche, il excelle sur les sols durs, peinant davantage sur les parquets truffés de rainures, et manque d’endurance pour tenir la distance lors de grandes sessions de ménage. Sa station Auto-Empty Dok simplifie son rangement, sa charge et la vidange de son collecteur. Dommage qu’elle signe le retour du sac, synonyme d’achat de consommables auxquels il faut donc penser.
À 659 € avec sa base, le Dyson V10 Konical associé à sa station de charge souffre d’une concurrence plus abordable chez bien des fabricants. Il suffit de voir le Shark PowerDetect Speed Clean and Empty disponible à moins de 300 €, ou encore le très performant Narwal V40, affiché à moins de 500 €. Mais achète-t-on un produit Dyson pour ses seules performances ?

articles.title: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47M in Series A
articles.text:
Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47M in Series A
Humyn Labs said it will use the funds across three areas: building deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India; and expanding its R&D and market presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
Humyn Labs, a physical AI research and deployment startup, has raised $47 million in a Series A funding round comprising equity and debt.
The Bengaluru-headquartered startup raised $26 million in equity funding led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence (through Bajaj Finance), Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading LLC and angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic.
The $21 million venture debt round was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.
Founded in February 2026 by Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs prepares physical AI systems for real-world deployment by translating human experience into physical understanding for robots. The startup's proprietary capture devices record how people perform specific tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes. Its end-to-end data engine then converts these recordings into labelled, training-ready datasets with verified provenance across sight, sound, motion and touch.
Humyn Labs will use the funds across three areas: building deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India; and expanding its R&D and market presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
“Physical AI will only be as good as the real-world data it learns from. This funding will help us strengthen our research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand our global presence. With a $10 billion opportunity emerging in data infrastructure, we aim to build a $1 billion annual revenue business and establish ourselves as a global leader in the space,” said Manish Agarwal, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.
According to Humyn Labs, it has surpassed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations. It works with frontier AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers, and runs its own capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.
“A robot does not learn a job from the internet. It learns it from the person who has done it for twenty years, on the floor where it will be done. We bring the model lab and the site operator onto that floor together, so every deployment teaches the next model, and the world’s factories, farms and warehouses become the training se,” said Ishank Gupta, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.

articles.title: Google Wallet para iPhone: cómo usar la app para guardar documentos y administrar compras
articles.text:
Google lanzó Wallet para iPhone en Estados Unidos, una aplicación que permite reunir tarjetas de embarque, entradas, recibos y el seguimiento de compras realizadas mediante agentes de inteligencia artificial (IA).
La llegada a iOS amplía el servicio más allá de los dispositivos Android y busca centralizar estos elementos en todos los dispositivos vinculados a una cuenta de Google.
La aplicación se sincroniza automáticamente con Gmail y otras plataformas de la empresa, así que incorpora datos de paquetes, pases de vuelo, entradas para conciertos y comprobantes de compra. Google explicó que el objetivo es mantener esa información accesible sin importar el tipo de dispositivo usado.
Cómo Google Wallet gestiona las compras hechas por agentes de IA
Google Wallet para iOS funciona como un espacio seguro para administrar las compras efectuadas por agentes de inteligencia artificial de la compañía. Esta capacidad constituye su principal diferencia frente a Apple Wallet, que permite pagos digitales y el almacenamiento de billetes de viaje, entradas y otras tarjetas, pero no incorpora la gestión de adquisiciones hechas por asistentes automatizados.
La función se relaciona con Tasks, una herramienta de Google que ya permite ejecutar determinadas compras mediante agentes. El modelo también se asemeja a Muse, de Meta, y Dots, de OpenAI, servicios que ofrecen compras en línea a través de sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
Los usuarios de iPhone podrán digitalizar tarjetas de fidelización y membresías de gimnasio con la cámara del teléfono para importarlas a la aplicación. Podrán guardar tarjetas de pago para agilizar las compras en línea dentro de los servicios de Google y en los comercios que acepten Google Pay.
Qué limitaciones tiene Google Wallet en iPhone
La aplicación no incluye por ahora pagos sin contacto mediante la función tap-to-pay, que permite abonar acercando el teléfono a una terminal compatible. Google no ha dicho si esa herramienta llegará posteriormente a iOS.
El lanzamiento ofrece una alternativa a la aplicación Wallet de Apple para organizar documentación digital y compras, aunque los usuarios de iPhone deberán continuar usando otros métodos para realizar pagos presenciales sin contacto.
Cómo aprovechar Google Wallet para ordenar viajes, compras y membresías
La aplicación permite reunir en un mismo lugar las tarjetas de embarque, las entradas a eventos, los comprobantes de compra y la información de envíos que llegue al correo. Así, el usuario puede consultar un vuelo, verificar el estado de un paquete o presentar una entrada sin buscar cada dato entre mensajes, capturas de pantalla y aplicaciones distintas.
Asimismo, se pueden incorporar tarjetas de fidelización y membresías mediante la cámara. Guardar las tarjetas de pago habilita compras en línea en los servicios de Google y comercios compatibles con Google Pay, mientras que la organización de recibos facilita revisar adquisiciones realizadas por asistentes de inteligencia artificial antes de solicitar una devolución o contactar al vendedor o comercio digital.
Qué medidas ayudan a proteger la información guardada en Google Wallet
El primer paso es asegurar la cuenta de Google con una contraseña única y la verificación en dos pasos. Hay que utilizar el bloqueo de pantalla del teléfono y evitar registrar tarjetas o abrir la aplicación desde dispositivos compartidos. Si el iPhone se pierde, revisar las sesiones activas de la cuenta permite identificar equipos desconocidos y cerrar el acceso de forma remota.
Es clave comprobar con frecuencia las tarjetas, pases y cuentas vinculadas para eliminar aquellos elementos que ya no se utilizan. Revisar los movimientos de compra y las notificaciones ayuda a detectar cargos no reconocidos o pedidos realizados sin autorización, especialmente cuando intervienen herramientas automatizadas.
Antes de viajar, hay que descargar o verificar los pases con anticipación y confirmar que los datos coincidan con la reserva. Esto evita depender de conexiones inestables en aeropuertos o lugares públicos.

articles.title: Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Exa boosts embedding throughput by 50% to index billions of documents on AWS AI chips
At Exa, we are building one of the few true web indexes by aggregating and serving knowledge from across the web, along with private and synthetic sources. We optimize the index for semantic search, grounding agents and humans in true, high-quality data. We use multi-tower semantic machine learning (ML) models to embed web data and query data into the same vector space, so users can express complex queries in natural language alongside traditional keyword search. The keystone technology behind this is an in-house vector database. It must ingest as much high-quality web data as possible and embed all of it. The unit economics of embedding therefore underlie everything we do. At the scale of tens or hundreds of billions of documents, finding the hardware that delivers the best performance per dollar isn’t a tuning detail. Any per-document cost improvement compounds into a significant number.
This post details how we optimized our embedding infrastructure for cheaper, more flexible inference workloads on AWS Neuron hardware (AWS Inferentia2 and AWS Trainium2), and how an agentic development workflow drove the optimization.
Inference runs on an asynchronous pipeline, but it must be high-volume and fast to serve recent data quickly and shrink the time between discovery and serving.
Every structured web document we rank as high enough quality must be embedded before it can be served. This figure shows how raw web data moves from Crawlers into an asynchronous pipeline of Parse, Moderate and filter, then Embed, with the result served from a vector database.
Embedding documents at scale
Our experience with the Neuron hardware family began with a backfill. Moving to a superior document model meant re-embedding our existing corpus. We selected 30 billion high-priority documents for re-embedding. A migration like this temporarily doubles the embedding load, which made it exactly the right moment to re-evaluate our hardware choices.
The preceding figure shows two parallel pipelines sharing the crawl and parse stages, one embedding with the live model into the live index and one re-embedding priority documents with the new model into the new index, which is what doubles the load. This doubling was a clear trigger to reconsider our hardware and optimization choices.
Optimization journey
AWS Inferentia2 figures refer to performance on the smallest instance type, an Inferentia2 xlarge instance (inf2.xlarge), with one chip and two NeuronCores. Our workload runs on a single NeuronCore, so we run Kubernetes pods that pack onto larger instances without leaving any cores idle, giving us container homogeneity across the embedding fleet. The same process runs on a Trainium2 NeuronCore and scales the same way through data parallelism. Our initial Inferentia2 implementation was a straightforward data-parallel, FP16 representation of the model. From that baseline, it became a march to push throughput (docs/sec) as high as possible, using the Neuron SDK and support from the AWS Trainium team. The following chart shows the throughput gains at each milestone.
Starting from the naive compile, a progressive series of optimizations ultimately delivered roughly a 1.5× throughput improvement. The first was weight layout optimization, which eliminates unnecessary transposes by aligning the weight layout with the scheduling and layout of the broader model. We also enabled autocast, letting the compiler downcast matrix multiplications to lower precision while preserving dynamic range. The downcast outputs met our correctness gate of 0.999 cosine similarity against the reference (see Agentic methodology), so the accuracy impact was within our acceptance threshold.
NKI kernels
The Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) library provides optimized kernels for common model layers and operations. These pre-built kernels deliver immediate gains on common features, and we used them to quickly remove the most straightforward sources of inefficiency. A drop-in attention kernel gave us the next bump in performance.
Memory layout optimization: A fused SwiGLU MLP kernel
The next bottleneck was memory spill. Profiles from the Neuron Explorer consistently showed large amounts of spill and reload from high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which kept the Tensor Engine from being fully utilized through the forward pass. Using a drop-in MLP kernel as a steppingstone to profile the shortcomings of the pre-built implementation, we wrote a custom weight-stationary fused SwiGLU MLP kernel that eliminated the HBM stalls.
We used the higher-level NKI language for layout operations, loops, and memory operations, and only dropped into the lower-level NKI ISA for specific tensor operations. Keeping most of the kernel in the higher-level language makes it more understandable for engineers, and easier to debug.
FLOPS reduction
At this point we hit a wall. Per-accelerator throughput measured with the other on-chip core idle was significantly higher than what we saw with both cores running simultaneously. That gap meant our theoretical data-parallel throughput should have been well above our realized aggregate performance, which pointed to contention between the cores.
Profiling and experimentation showed that our workload wasn’t yet saturating the Tensor Engine. The remaining headroom was ours to claim by making the computation leaner. The clearest path left was to reduce the overall FLOPS needed to produce our results by eliminating waste. We rewrote the attention kernel around the exact shapes in our model to cut FLOPS spent on padding. This is where kernel customization really paid off. Generic kernels are built to handle any shape, so they can’t take advantage of the specific shapes in a given architecture. We wrung more performance out of attention by tailoring the implementation to the real shape of our model’s head architecture. We also folded attention operations into single matmuls where the generic kernel used multiple instruction steps. That cut the inner-loop operations needed to compute the same values, which reduced HBM round trips and produced the final significant speedup.
In total, our final version was a 47% improvement in performance and cost per 1 million documents embedded, against our initial baseline.
Agentic methodology
Agents developed all of these optimizations inside a simple three part harness that lets them verify correctness, measure performance and profile the workload to find the next direction. Using Flyte, an ML ops workflow platform, each agent runs its own workflow. The workflow compiles a NEFF Neuron executable and checks a forward pass against a baseline dataset, which must reach 0.999 cosine similarity to the canonical model. It then profiles one forward pass and runs a 30 minute saturation benchmark on real hardware.
The harness supports agents at different costs. Lightweight models handle tedious work like grid searching compiler parameters, and correctness checks prevent drift. Reasoning agents test complex hypotheses and find bottlenecks, while the strongest code generators write custom kernels to fix them. Matching each agent to its task keeps costs in check, and validation keeps capable agents from drifting. Because many agents don’t know the latest features and syntax, neuron agentic development skills also helped.
The benefits of flexible compute
So far, we have optimized Inferentia2 for the US West (Oregon) Region (us-west-2), but tuning one hardware family in one Region has hard limits. Spot and on demand availability vary by Region, and organizations with many consumers compete with themselves. Locking into one Region or instance type almost guarantees a compute shortage, and possibly degraded service.
Exa schedules compute across multiple Regions from one Kubernetes control plane. Our scheduler compares performance per dollar across instance types and packs pods onto the cheapest nodes, rescheduling as embedding demand shifts. Each hardware type we optimize for brings us closer to the global optimum. This is why our Inferentia2 work carried over directly to Trainium2. Shifting hardware profiles lets us free up nodes other teams need or absorb their unused reserved compute. For a long lived model, optimizing across hardware pays off enormously.
Conclusion
At the scale Exa operates, extracting maximum cost-performance from a flexible pool of hardware is what matters. Adding Neuron hardware to that pool and optimizing it with NKI has proven to be a major source of long-term cost savings.

articles.title: Microsoft Defender va pouvoir protéger les systèmes vulnérables sans attendre l'installation d'un correctif
articles.text:
Microsoft présente Vulnerability Shielding, une nouvelle fonction de Defender capable d'appliquer des protections temporaires aux systèmes exposés à des failles de sécurité. En cas d'attaque, elle pourra même intervenir automatiquement pour couper la route aux pirates.
Les cybercriminels n'attendent pas que les entreprises aient terminé leurs mises à jour pour exploiter une faille de sécurité. Entre la publication d'un patch et son installation, plusieurs jours peuvent s'écouler, le temps de vérifier sa compatibilité avec les logiciels existants et d'organiser son déploiement sans perturber l'activité. Un délai dont les pirates savent profiter, et pendant lequel Microsoft entend désormais protéger les systèmes vulnérables grâce à Vulnerability Shielding, une nouvelle fonction de Defender présentée à l'occasion de l'Ignite 2026.
Faire barrage aux pirates sans corriger la faille
Plutôt que de laisser les machines exposées jusqu'à l'installation d'une mise à jour, Microsoft propose de leur appliquer des protections provisoires, adaptées à la vulnérabilité concernée. Pour cela, Vulnerability Shielding s'appuie sur l'intelligence artificielle et les données de sécurité de Defender pour identifier les failles exploitables, examiner la configuration des systèmes et déterminer comment empêcher les pirates d'en tirer parti.
Dans les faits, l'outil pourra restreindre les communications réseau, bloquer des chemins d'accès ou limiter certaines autorisations pour empêcher l'exploitation d'une vulnérabilité, tout en cherchant à préserver le fonctionnement des applications. Il ne s'agit donc pas de corriger la faille elle-même, mais de rendre son exploitation plus difficile en attendant l'installation du patch définitif.
Cette protection préventive s'appuie sur le Risk Reduction Agent de Microsoft Perception, chargé d'établir un plan d'action tenant compte des risques et des contraintes de l'entreprise. Pour aider les administrateurs à prendre leur décision, l'agent simulera les conséquences des protections envisagées à partir de 90 jours d'activité réelle. Aucune mesure ne sera appliquée sans leur validation.
En cas d'attaque, Defender pourra intervenir de lui-même
Mais Vulnerability Shielding ne se limitera pas à anticiper les attaques. La nouvelle fonction vient également renforcer Attack Disruption, le dispositif de Defender capable de détecter et d'interrompre automatiquement des intrusions en cours. Lorsqu'une attaque sera repérée, il pourra appliquer de lui-même des protections temporaires aux systèmes vulnérables.
L'objectif sera alors de bloquer les accès exploités par les pirates, mais aussi de leur fermer d'autres voies susceptibles de leur permettre de progresser dans le réseau. Pour choisir les restrictions à appliquer, Defender tiendra compte des vulnérabilités connues, des techniques d'attaque observées et des usages habituels des systèmes concernés, afin de préserver autant que possible les activités légitimes.
Ces protections auront vocation à rester temporaires. Une fois le correctif définitif installé, elles seront retirées automatiquement. Les administrateurs pourront également consulter les restrictions appliquées, exclure des appareils ou des applications et revenir sur une décision si nécessaire.
Vulnerability Shielding arrive en préversion publique, avec une première prise en charge des failles permettant l'exécution de code à distance sur les serveurs pour son volet préventif. La nouveauté s'adresse aux entreprises équipées des solutions de sécurité professionnelles de Microsoft, et non aux particuliers utilisant simplement l'antivirus intégré à Windows.
- Moteur de détection de dernière génération efficace et discret
- Intégration dans Windows 10 et Windows 11
- Pare-feu

articles.title: YouTube sait combien de personnes sont en train de regarder la TV, mais on ne sait pas comment
articles.text:
En août dernier, YouTube changeait pour la première fois les règles de la comptabilisation des vues. Depuis, dès qu’une vidéo est lancée, elle est comptée comme une vue. Il y a quelques jours, YouTube a discrètement instauré une nouvelle règle : les vues sur TV vont être démultipliées.
Les vues YouTube sur TV vont parfois compter double, ou triple
Depuis le 16 novembre, YouTube a changé une nouvelle fois de manière de comptabiliser les vues : « nous allons franchir une nouvelle étape dans la mesure de la façon dont les spectateurs regardent vos contenus sur les téléviseurs », peut-on lire sur le forum dédié aux créateurs sur la plateforme. YouTube intègre dans le compteur de vues d’une vidéo les estimations de covisionnage, jusque-là cantonnées dans les statistiques de chaque chaîne YouTube. Autrement dit, lorsque YouTube estimera que plusieurs personnes regardent une même vidéo sur un même téléviseur, ce ne sera plus une seule vue qui sera comptabilisée, mais plusieurs.
YouTube revendique officiellement qu’il s’agit de refléter « plus précisément la façon dont les spectateurs regardent vos contenus. » Mais c’est aussi un moyen de faire gonfler les vues d’une vidéo et ainsi de renforcer son attractivité commerciale ou encore d’encourager les créateurs et les internautes à rester sur la plateforme grâce à cet effet de preuve sociale. Face à des réseaux sociaux comme TikTok ou Instagram, sur lesquels les utilisateurs enchaînent les vidéos et font gonfler les compteurs de vues, YouTube ne semblait plus avoir de choix. D’ailleurs, ce système de covisionnage fonctionne sur tous les formats : vidéos classiques, Shorts et lives.
Comment YouTube estime combien de personnes regardent une vidéo sur un même téléviseur
Pour mesurer les audiences à la télévision, l’organisme Médiamétrie a installé des boîtiers dans quelques milliers de foyers. À la maison, dès que la télévision est allumée, les participants doivent indiquer dessus combien de personnes regardent la télévision. Ce qui n’existe absolument pas sur YouTube, qui est resté durant des années à son compteur de vues.
Dans son communiqué, YouTube indique ne jamais utiliser de caméras, de microphones ou autres capteurs d’appareils pour mesurer ce « covisionnage ». Autrement dit, il n’utilisera pas votre téléviseur ou vos téléphones/tablettes pour vous espionner, de quelque manière que ce soit. Une bonne chose en ces temps où les téléviseurs sont régulièrement accusés d’espionner les téléspectateurs. Non, YouTube a préféré créer un modèle d’estimation avec ses chercheurs. La plateforme s’explique : « notre système analyse des signaux tels que les schémas démographiques, les métadonnées de contenu et les heures de visionnage pour estimer quand plusieurs personnes regardent la télévision ensemble. » Il s’agit donc d’une estimation algorithmique et non pratique : « au petit doigt mouillé » comme diraient certains.

articles.title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
articles.text:
A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in.
On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update. Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile.
The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times. Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities.
During the Ukrainian attacks on the Kerch Strait Bridge, the flying mesh network allowed operators located more than 250 kilometers away (155 miles) to remotely guide missiles and drones in evading Russian air defenses while also homing in on the bridge’s weakest structural points, according to the Financial Times.
Ukraine’s takedown of the bridge segment was preceded by weeks of preparatory strikes that systematically destroyed or degraded Russian air defense weapons, radars and electronic warfare equipment arrayed to protect the bridge. The November 15 night attack on the bridge also coincided with the largest Ukrainian overnight drone attack on Russia since the start of the full-scale war, Reuters reported.

articles.title: GTA 6 dev speaks on building a modern game while balancing Vice City’s nostalgic 80s vibes influenced by Miami Vice and Goodfellas — ‘Something we have talked about is being nostalgic for the present moment we are all in but also being nostalgic for GTA Vice City’
articles.text:
GTA 6 dev shares how Miami Vice, Heat, and Goodfellas are ‘touchstones’ for the latest game and how it channeled a sense of nostalgia of GTA Vice City — ‘I think the feeling of playing a movie that you get with GTA is one of the coolest things we do’
- Grand Theft Auto 6 senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries explains how Rockstar Games channeled the 80s vibes of GTA Vice City
- Humphries says GTA Vice City is "a game we all love and know sits in a special place for a lot of our fans"
- He reveals that media like Heat, Scarface, Goodfellas, and Miami Vice are "touchstones" for the studio's GTA games
Rockstar Games drew on some of the most iconic 80s gangster movies for Grand Theft Auto 6, influencing the studio's vision for a game that channels the nostalgia of playing GTA Vice City.
Responding to questions sent directly to Rockstar by TechRadar Gaming, senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries explained how the team made a game for 2026 while balancing the 80s vibe players know and love.
"Something we have talked about is being nostalgic for the present moment we are all in but also being nostalgic for GTA Vice City - a game we all love and know sits in a special place for a lot of our fans," Humphries said. "Vice City FM being the 80s station is a sort of nod to that."
The developer went on to reveal how Rockstar references a lot of classic gangster media from the 80s, which it uses to channel that style and vibe.
"There are movies that are touchstones for us whenever we start on one of these projects – Scarface, Heat, Goodfellas – but we also go back and watch Miami Vice, particularly the pilot," Humphries said. "Nothing on TV has ever been as cool as those 90 minutes.
"I think the feeling of playing a movie that you get with GTA is one of the coolest things we do.”

articles.title: El robot de cocina compacto de Lidl regresa por el Black Friday: ahora cuesta menos de 150 euros y es ideal para cocinas pequeñas
articles.text:
Lidl celebra la semana que viene su Black Friday y uno de sus productos estrella es su robot de cocina. El próximo viernes 28 de noviembre, la cadena de supermercados alemana venderá rebajado (a 149,99 euros frente a los 199,99 euros que suele costar) este Monsieur Cuisine Compact.
Monsieur Cuisine compact SMCC 1100 A1

articles.title: AI workflow automation: 3 monday.com Elevate insights - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of monday.com’s Elevate event
AI workflow automation is changing how businesses build applications and manage everyday work, raising questions about the role of established software platforms. As organizations experiment with AI-generated applications and autonomous agents, they must also determine how to maintain access controls, integrate existing systems and manage increasingly complex workflows.
The growing accessibility of AI development tools has prompted speculation that businesses could replace traditional software-as-a-service platforms with applications built for specific needs. But building an application and operating it securely across an enterprise present different challenges, according to Casey George, chief revenue officer of monday.com Ltd.
“We are seeing customers come back to a platform that’s integrated — that’s governed, that’s permissioned with their infrastructure, that is secure — like monday.com,” he told theCUBE. “I joke and say it was an expensive funeral, but we learned a lot. Customers learned a lot.”
George, along with executives and practitioners, spoke with host Rebecca Knight at monday.com’s Elevate event during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. The discussions examined enterprise AI deployment, governance requirements and the challenges of scaling AI workflow automation across organizations. (* Disclosure below.)
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Casey George:
Here are three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of monday.com’s Elevate event:
Insight #1: Deploying AI agents requires expertise and governance.
Making autonomous agents available to employees does not guarantee business returns. After an internal initiative produced more than 3,600 agents, monday.com established monday Frontier, an organization combining managed services and deployment engineers to help customers identify workflow bottlenecks and implement AI projects. The initiative addresses the implementation challenges involved in moving agents into productive use, according to Eran Zinman (pictured), co-founder and co-chief executive officer of monday.com.
“Adopting AI really requires expertise. I know how hard it is because we experienced ourselves that you have this amazing technology, but how do you actually use it?” he said during the event.
As organizations deploy AI agents, security teams must account for how access rights change across users, applications and environments. Incremental rollouts offer a way to test capabilities before expanding their reach, while permission management remains an ongoing responsibility, according to Ryan Nigro, security trust and enablement team lead at monday.com.
“It just comes to making sure that your users are properly being given just enough to do their roles but not too much to cause harm,” Nigro told theCUBE. “There’s no reason why a sales rep should have the ability to change your production environment.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Ryan Nigro:
Insight #2: Shared dashboards improve operational visibility.
At Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co., employees are using monday vibe, monday.com’s no-code application builder, to create custom tools. One executive dashboard replaces the manual process of copying charts into presentation slides while retaining the ability to export to PowerPoint, according to Kate Kenner, capability and community lead for strategic sourcing and planning at HPE.
“[Executives] knocked a whole bunch of the meetings off the calendar,” she told theCUBE. “Instead of weekly, now they’re monthly.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Kate Kenner:
At Lowe’s Cos. Inc., coordinating store setups and remodels once required tracking information across Microsoft Excel, emails and other communications. The retailer now uses monday.com to monitor individual store bays and dozens of simultaneous projects, according to Lanny Finley, director of remerch and new stores at Lowe’s.
“I can take the dashboard and see which projects are on track, which ones are at risk, and then make the appropriate actions and get the right partners in place to make the corrections to get everything back on track and completed,” he said during the event.
Lowe’s also developed an internal Green Dot Board to track issues such as missing components during store projects. The company is exploring additional automation that could initiate vendor orders when components are needed and close issues once replacements are installed, according to Brian Olms, senior business partner manager at Lowe’s, who joined Finley during the discussion.
“We needed a way to automate the process, make it more user-friendly [and] make it simpler. That’s what we started the Green Dot Board for,” he told theCUBE. “Here at Elevate, we’re seeing ways that we could even take it a step further and start to use agents and more automation and [the] vibe app.”
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Lanny Finley and Brian Olms:
Insight #3: AI workflow automation expands organizational capacity.
For nonprofits facing growing demand, AI workflow automation offers a way to expand organizational capacity without placing additional administrative burdens on employees. At Feed the Children Inc., a two-person team oversees relationships with more than 500 community partners, according to Colleen Finn Ridenhour, chief growth and strategy officer at Feed the Children.
“Things from [memorandums of understanding] and legal contracts, annual renewals and compliance and reporting — it’s quite a lot. It’s been a very manual process, historically, for them to keep track of that all the time. We really want them focused on the human element of that job, which is bringing in new partners to help us scale our impact,” she told theCUBE.
The nonprofit uses monday.com’s forms, boards, automations and agents to coordinate partner activities and manage information. Employees can also build dashboards for specific needs, including budget tracking, while retaining human oversight of compliance-related work, according to Ridenhour.
“We’re not going to be able to scale our impact by just always asking people to work harder. [We need to find] ways to repeat a lot of these repetitive actions in a much easier way and [share] information so [that] people’s jobs get easier and it frees up their time to do the things that only they can do,” she said during the event.
Here’s theCUBE’s complete video interview with Colleen Finn Ridenhour:

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff.
Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI.
The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit.
“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he explained.
For some people, “that reorganization and change is sort of hard, right?” he added, “but, I mean, it has to be done.”
He offered the example of the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. He said the team consists of just 11 developers who have mastered using AI to do their jobs. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.”
He believes that every employee will one day similarly become a manager of agents, rather than a person directly doing the work. “That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs.”
But Microsoft, as a 51-year-old company, didn’t grow up as an AI-first company. “So the question is, how quickly can an incumbent transform the work, the workflow, and the work artifact, and with all the wage support that goes with it?” he said. “It’s going to take a bit more time than anyone expects. And there is going to be in all of this, you know, people who may say, ‘Hey, I have some other choices I want to make.’”
When asked about this same topic — why ask 60,000 people to voluntarily resign — last week by Gergely Orosz on his The Pragmatic Engineer podcast, Nadella further explained, “We have created enormous anxiety in people sort of feeling that they don’t have control of their own destiny because the way we have talked about this AI revolution.”
He called out talk about the singularity (the hypothetical point at which AI surpasses human intelligence) and predictions that AI will take away all jobs. “All of that leads anyone who even wants to change to be sort of anxious … You have to sort of walk the hard walk of really making the structural changes, getting people slotted, giving them opportunity.”
In other words, the buyout was the message to employees: You can get with the new AI-first program, which will radically change your job, or you choose to get on with your life. Elsewhere.

articles.title: Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law — proposed law would expand list of beneficiaries
articles.text:
Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law — proposed law would expand list of beneficiaries
It's not the first time eminent domain fears have been raised around AI data centers
While Ohioans have rejected the building of new data centers at every turn, they might not have much choice in the future. That's if a newly leaked bill that could allow data centers to be classified as public utilities is allowed to progress. The move would see the list of who can qualify for eminent domain law expanded, moving beyond entities owned or operated by municipal corporations, electric cooperatives, and agencies holding a certificate of public convenience and necessity granted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The bill, leaked to WCPO Cincinnati, would add "and an agency holding a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need from the power siting board for constructing an electric transmission line and associated facilities or gas pipeline and its associated facilities."
Legal experts have warned that the change could mean a transmission developer, like a power company, would be able to seize land to be used for a data center or a facility that would power one. The writing has been on the wall for a while, too, after it was discovered in June that the Ohio Business Roundtable trade group recommended that lawmakers change eminent domain law to "extend possession authority to energy infrastructure projects once public use and necessity have been established.”
This follows a July 2026 report that the government was able to seize private land for new transmission lines needed to power new data centers. The law gives the government the power to take private land without the need for the owner's consent, so long as it is for public use and the owner receives appropriate compensation. The government can also delegate the same land-grabbing power to “private entities or common carriers,” which includes utility companies.
This is already happening, too. Earlier this year, the largest utility company in Georgia required the removal of 30 residential properties in order to upgrade its grid. Residents claimed that the expansion was to power AI data centers, a fact given more weight by the fact that one such data center was located just a few miles away.
Despite this, eminent domain law can still be used for good. Nashville set out to use the same law to block the building of a 69,220-square-foot single-story data center next to a zoo. Nashville Metro Council approved the use of eminent domain as a way to buy the land from a local developer who planned the $700 million data center buildout.

O Watch GT 6 Pro está saindo por apenas R$ 1.330 no Pix na Amazon. O smartwatch da Huawei, com corpo de titânio e suporte a mais de 100 atividades físicas, atinge o 2.º menor preço de 2026, com desconto de 47% sobre o original de R$ 2.499 durante a Black November.

articles.title: Binance obtuvo una orden judicial por 6.500 millones de dólares para recuperar criptomonedas robadas
articles.text:
Binance consiguió una orden judicial de los tribunales del Mercado Global de Abu Dabi (ADGM) para avanzar en la recuperación de los activos digitales sustraídos durante un incidente de seguridad ocurrido el 29 de octubre de 2026. La medida contempla el congelamiento de fondos por un monto de 6.500 millones de dólares y establece mecanismos para facilitar su identificación y recuperación mediante herramientas vinculadas con la tecnología blockchain.
La compañía informó que los activos afectados por el incidente ya fueron repuestos en su totalidad y que asumió el impacto financiero. Según el comunicado difundido el 18 de noviembre, los usuarios están protegidos, aunque la plataforma continuará con las acciones legales para intentar recuperar los fondos robados y evitar que permanezcan bajo el control de los atacantes.
La resolución judicial representa un nuevo paso en ese proceso. Binance busca utilizar los mecanismos legales disponibles para rastrear los movimientos de las criptomonedas, congelar las billeteras que contienen los activos sustraídos y facilitar su devolución cuando sea posible.
Una orden judicial para congelar activos digitales
Los tribunales del ADGM dictaron una orden de congelamiento de alcance mundial contra determinadas personas desconocidas, identificadas como presuntos responsables del fraude. El monto de la medida asciende a 6.500 millones de dólares, una cifra que, según los representantes legales de Binance, podría convertirla en una de las mayores órdenes de este tipo conocidas públicamente.
Además, el tribunal concedió medidas cautelares patrimoniales provisionales y órdenes de restitución contra distintas categorías de personas desconocidas. También dictó medidas contra determinados demandados identificados que tienen parte de los activos robados congelados. Binance aclaró que a estas últimas personas no se les atribuye ninguna conducta ilícita.
La empresa cuenta con la representación del estudio jurídico Gibson Dunn para llevar adelante las acciones destinadas a recuperar los criptoactivos.
M. Kendall Day, representante de la firma legal, destacó la magnitud de la medida y explicó que las disposiciones judiciales incluyen mecanismos para notificar las órdenes directamente a través de la blockchain. De acuerdo con su declaración, esta posibilidad permitirá comunicar las restricciones a los participantes del mercado de criptomonedas.
La lista de 26.000 billeteras digitales identificadas
Uno de los elementos más relevantes de la resolución es la creación de una lista dinámica con 26.000 direcciones de billeteras digitales identificadas como poseedoras de activos robados.
Este registro se actualizará permanentemente y sus modificaciones serán comunicadas al mercado. El objetivo es que los exchanges, emisores de activos digitales y otras empresas puedan identificar rápidamente las direcciones vinculadas con los fondos sustraídos y actuar para impedir que sean transferidos.
La medida cobra importancia porque las criptomonedas pueden moverse entre distintas billeteras en poco tiempo. Además, los responsables de un robo pueden intentar distribuir los fondos entre múltiples direcciones para dificultar su seguimiento.
Con la lista actualizada, Binance pretende facilitar el rastreo de esos movimientos y acelerar el congelamiento de los activos cuando sea legalmente posible. La notificación mediante blockchain también busca que las empresas involucradas reciban información sobre las restricciones judiciales.
Por qué Binance recurrió a los tribunales de Abu Dabi
La orden judicial también responde a una dificultad que puede surgir durante la recuperación de criptomonedas robadas: algunos emisores, exchanges y socios de la industria exigen una resolución formal antes de liberar, transferir o devolver fondos que fueron congelados.
En esos casos, identificar una billetera relacionada con un robo no siempre es suficiente para concretar la restitución de los activos. Las empresas pueden necesitar un respaldo legal que les permita actuar sin exponerse a posibles conflictos jurídicos.
Por eso, la resolución del ADGM busca proporcionar ese marco y facilitar la cooperación entre las distintas organizaciones que participan en el proceso.
Dugan Bliss, Deputy General Counsel de Binance, afirmó que la compañía continuará utilizando todas las herramientas legales disponibles para rastrear y recuperar los fondos. También señaló que la responsabilidad de la plataforma no termina con la reposición de los activos afectados.
Binance continuará con el proceso de recuperación
Después del incidente del 29 de octubre, Binance aseguró que trabaja con fuerzas del orden, autoridades competentes, emisores, exchanges y empresas especializadas en inteligencia blockchain para monitorear los movimientos de los activos.
La plataforma indicó que seguirá publicando actualizaciones verificadas a medida que avance el procedimiento judicial y las acciones para recuperar las criptomonedas.
Aunque Binance afirma que los usuarios afectados ya recibieron la reposición de sus activos, la orden judicial apunta a recuperar los fondos sustraídos y mantenerlos fuera del alcance de quienes participaron en el ataque. El comunicado no identifica a los responsables ni detalla cómo se produjo el incidente de seguridad.

articles.title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
articles.text:
In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump’s pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation.
Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy’s decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats.
In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA’s current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn’t say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is “quite lethal” or that children are given vaccine doses the “size of a soda bottle.” Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong.
Axios quoted a senior Trump administration official as saying that Overton’s nomination was dropped because she “lacks the support on the Hill to move forward with her confirmation.”
The Senate’s Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, chaired by Bill Cassidy (R-La.), was scheduled to vote on Overton’s nomination Wednesday. In a social media post Tuesday night, after her nomination was withdrawn, Cassidy said he believed she had a “viable confirmation path.” But he said the nomination was “abandoned” after some anti-abortion senators sought commitments from her that they couldn’t get. “The Administration withdrew Dr. Overton rather than make such commitments,” Cassidy said.

articles.title: Vivimos rodeados de sustancias que pueden alterar nuestras hormonas y la ciencia cada vez tiene más pruebas de sus efectos
articles.text:
Durante más de una década, la comunidad científica ha ido acumulando pruebas sobre un grupo de compuestos invisibles que han sido conocidos como 'disruptores endocrinos' y que alteran el funcionamiento de las hormonas naturales de nuestro organismo. Ahora, tanto la PNUMA como la OMS han lanzado la primera gran actualización sobre este tema, donde se apunta que, tras catorce años de investigación, se consolida el efecto que tiene sobre la salud.
Sus efectos. Según recoge el documento, la evidencia más sólida vincula la exposición a disruptores endocrinos con alteraciones en la fertilidad y el desarrollo reproductivo, el desarrollo cerebral y el neurocomportamiento, la función tiroidea, el metabolismo y el sistema inmunitario.
Pero junto a estos frentes que ya se conocían, el informe actualizado incorpora preocupaciones que hace una década apenas figuraban en el radar, como la enfermedad hepática metabólica y los posibles efectos sobre la función renal. Aunque todavía hay dudas, puesto que mientras los efectos sobre el neurodesarrollo cuentan con un respaldo sólido, la relación con las enfermedades cardiovasculares se clasifica todavía como emergente, y en patologías como la diabetes tipo 2 o el asma existe una confianza creciente en su relación.
El problema de fondo. Algo que poco a poco vamos conociendo es que los disruptores endocrinos están presentes en una infinidad de productos de uso diario y, a diferencia de los tóxicos clásicos que siguen la máxima de que "la dosis hace el veneno", pueden interferir con las señales hormonales incluso a concentraciones extraordinariamente bajas.
Un agujero regulatorio. En el mercado global hay registradas más de 350.000 sustancias y mezclas químicas, pero solo una pequeña fracción ha sido sometida a pruebas específicas para determinar si es un disruptor endocrino. Y es que el problema está en que el ritmo al que se introducen nuevos compuestos en la industria sigue superando al de la regulación sanitaria.
Para ilustrar cómo esa exposición se materializa en el mundo real, hay algunos estudios que nos dan bastante información al respecto. Algunos de ellos han realizado mediciones mediante pulseras de silicona y mostraron que los trabajadores del reciclaje y la gestión de residuos plásticos estaban expuestos a más de veinte sustancias químicas peligrosas, pero los trabajadores de oficina utilizados como grupo de control también acumulaban al menos once de esos compuestos en su entorno diario.
La factura sanitaria. Las estimaciones que hacen las autoridades apuntan a que las enfermedades asociadas a los disruptores endocrinos generan un gasto anual que equivale a alrededor del 1% del producto interior bruto global, lo que es igual a un billón de dólares. Pero este número no es del todo exacto, puesto que es una extrapolación basada en estudios previos de carga de enfermedad realizados con datos epidemiológicos de Estados Unidos, la Unión Europea y Canadá.
Para pasar del diagnóstico a la prevención, la guía From Evidence to Action plantea revisar de forma transversal las normativas que regulan los materiales en contacto con alimentos, la cosmética, los juguetes infantiles, los textiles, los insumos hospitalarios, los productos fitosanitarios, los fármacos y la gestión de residuos.

articles.title: « Le pire modèle jamais sorti par OpenAI » : le nouveau ChatGPT se fait descendre par des testeurs
articles.text:
OpenAI a mis en ligne GPT-6.2 Astra et GPT-6.2 Sol le 17 novembre, deux modèles promis plus efficaces, censés produire un code plus propre en moins d’allers-retours. Les abonnés Plus, Pro, Enterprise et Edu y ont accès dans ChatGPT Work et dans Codex, l’outil de programmation maison. La facture baisse même de 20 % sur l’API pour Astra, à 8 et 40 dollars le million de jetons, l’unité de compte des modèles.
Des accès anticipés qui tournent au réquisitoire
OpenAI s’appuie à chaque lancement sur une poignée de développeurs et d’investisseurs servis en avance, dont les retours alimentent d’ordinaire la promotion. L’annonce du 17 novembre cite d’ailleurs ses testeurs comblés ; d’autres racontent depuis une expérience inverse. Theo Browne, développeur passé par une semaine d’accès anticipé, a ainsi transformé son essai en lettre ouverte à OpenAI. Sa tâche témoin, la réécriture d’un compilateur en Rust, a accouché d’un programme 56 % plus lent que l’original. Sa lettre tranche : « le pire modèle jamais sorti par OpenAI ». Rien que ça.
Dan Shipper, qui confie des projets entiers aux modèles, voit GPT-6.2 s’arrêter avant la fin de ses tâches. Ethan Mollick décrit une expérience en dents de scie, face à un modèle inégal, étrange par endroits et plus difficile à piloter que ses rivaux. Matt Shumer, lui, a renoncé à sa longue revue habituelle et juge les deux modèles « quasiment inutilisables ».
La même lettre crédite pourtant Astra de bonnes prises en relecture de code, d’une génération 3D solide et d’un projet d’infrastructure qui devrait économiser 25 000 dollars par mois à son auteur. Sur le fil de lancement de Hacker News, passé les 500 points en 75 minutes, la baisse des prix récolte d’ailleurs plus d’éloges que le modèle lui-même.
Un modèle moins sûr ?
Face à un obstacle qu’il a pourtant identifié, GPT-6.2 Astra poursuit sans le signaler dans 22,28 % des cas, d’après l’indicateur « Blocker Deception » de sa fiche de sécurité. Le taux double par rapport aux 11,09 % de GPT-6 Astra : l’artisan repère la poutre vermoulue, puis referme le mur sans un mot.
OpenAI avance une piste, un entraînement qui pousse le modèle à répondre court, avec moins de réserves, et un correctif circule déjà dans Codex. Rien d’automatique côté API : la retouche des instructions revient aux développeurs. L’index d’Artificial Analysis, qui agrège des tests de référence, installe Astra sur la deuxième marche, derrière Claude Fable 5.2 d’Anthropic, pour un coût par tâche plus de six fois inférieur à celui du rival.
Fin septembre, OpenAI annulait GPT-6.1 Astra à quelques jours de la sortie, pour des permissions outrepassées et des comptes rendus infidèles en tests internes. La génération suivante arrive donc au complet, lestée cette fois des critiques de ses meilleurs ambassadeurs. Les abonnés ont déjà les deux modèles en main, dans ChatGPT Work et Codex comme sur l’API. À leurs projets de rendre le verdict que plaquettes et lettres ouvertes se disputent.
