articles.title: Elon Musk says ousting Jensen Huang is like 'kicking Michael Jordan off your team' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Elon Musk has already been vocal about his disapproval of the Nvidia board’s decision to oust its founder and CEO Jensen Huang after a series of extramarital affairs were made public, including one with an alleged Chinese spy who is suspected of feeding sensitive information back to Beijing. At The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Musk elaborated on his thoughts about Nvidia’s leadership change.
“Jensen is an old friend of mine,” Musk said. “I would call Jensen, you know, Michael Jordan at his peak level, in terms of what he means to a team.”
On X, the social media platform he owns, Musk even said he would hire Huang.
“He’s one of the most talented entrepreneur-CEOs in history,” Musk said when asked about his X post. “Who wouldn’t want to hire Jensen?”
Musk also signed a petition, alongside over 200,000 other people, urging Nvidia to reinstate its former CEO. Nvidia’s board, however, confirmed it is not planning to bring Huang back.
“[It] doesn’t seem like a smart decision to me…” Musk said of that decision. “There’s no one that can really replace Jensen.”
Huang “has long-term relationships that have been built up over decades,” Musk added. “He understands technology incredibly well. His team loves him… and many of them are there because of him, and have higher offers to go elsewhere, and have turned them down because of personal loyalty to Jensen.”
Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey also said that he thinks Nvidia is making the wrong decision by not reinstating Huang.
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said earlier in the day at the DealBook event. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”
Musk also did not express concern over what Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could mean for U.S. national security.
“I don’t think he’s disloyal to the United States,” Musk said. “I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders.”
Other peers in the industry, like Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, reaffirmed their faith in Nvidia to move forward without its founder and CEO of 33 years at the helm.
“It’s the Nvidia board’s decision, but I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella said at DealBook. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”

articles.title: Google Photos might be able to pick out your outfits
articles.text:
It looks like Google Photos might be getting a new AI Wardrobe feature. Some of the guys at Android Authority went digging through some source code and found some details in Google Photos app version (v8.2), alluding to a “Build a fit” feature.
The new feature would be available inside the ‘Wardrobe’ section of the Google Photos app and is designed to help users design what to wear. Currently, the feature lets you organize clothing items and manually combine outfits. However, Build a fit, according to the source code has the subtitle “Can’t decide what to wear today” with a “Surprise me” button. This suggests that Google Photos will randomly recommend an outfit using the clothing items in your ‘Wardrobe.’
It’s unclear if this app will be able to design an outfit based on stuff you’ve recently worn, the weather conditions or if it’ll offer details on what to wear based on your Calendar event. AA couldn’t enable the feature yet, and it’s unclear how far in development this feature is.
Still, I’ve always wanted something to do the work of putting outfits together for me. I’ve spent way too much brainpower on that.
Though, it’s worth noting that Google Photos ‘Wardrobe‘ functionality isn’t available in Canada yet, so it’ll probably take us Canadians even longer to get this feature.
Source: Android Authority

articles.title: Travail et IA : ces métiers où les offres d'emploi se sont effondrées
articles.text:
Derrière les fantasmes de remplacement par des robots, la réalité autour de l’intelligence artificielle et du marché du travail s’avère plus subtile, mais bien réelle. Deux études récentes, menées par France Travail auprès de 16 000 établissements et par le cabinet Coface, révèlent les vraies tendances du marché. Si les patrons privilégient pour l’instant le gain de productivité plutôt que les suppressions de postes, les embauches reculent déjà dans les professions tertiaires.
Des secteurs plus touchés que d’autres par l’IA
Selon France Travail, seuls 6 % des dirigeants prévoient une automatisation importante où l’IA exécuterait la majorité des tâches humaines d’ici cinq ans. En revanche, 35 % des patrons considèrent cette technologie comme un assistant de travail, capable de libérer du temps sur la rédaction, la recherche ou l’analyse. Parmi les métiers les plus touchés, on compte ceux du numérique et des services intellectuels, avec 94 % des ingénieurs informatiques, 83 % des comptables et 75 % des bancassureurs concernés. À l’inverse, le BTP (80 % sans effet), les services aux particuliers (85 %) et la restauration (76 %) ne sont que très peu touchés.
D’après l’étude, cette transition vers l’IA se concentre fortement dans les grandes agglomérations comme l’Île-de-France, le Rhône, la Loire-Atlantique ou la Haute-Garonne. Dans ces bassins d’emploi tertiaires, l’IA générative prend par exemple en charge les tâches administratives répétitives et la saisie de texte ou de données. Les salariés concernés par ces changements réorientent ainsi leur temps vers la prise de décision, la gestion de projets et la relation client.
La baisse notable des offres d’emploi
L’étude mesure également l’impact de l’intelligence artificielle et de ses usages sur l’embauche. Elle indique en effet que pour chaque tranche de 10 % d’exposition d’un métier à l’IA, les annonces sur France Travail chutent de 12,4 % au troisième trimestre. Cela représente 25 000 offres d’emploi en moins sur la période, un chiffre similaire à l’Allemagne (-10,2 %) et la Suède (-10,8 %). La chute la plus spectaculaire est à aller chercher du côté des ressources humaines et du secrétariat, avec des annonces en baisse de respectivement -42,8 % et -40 % depuis 2022.
À lire : Microsoft propose un plan de départ volontaire à 60 000 salariés pour faire des économies
Ce gel des embauches touche les jeunes diplômés, mais ils sont loin d’être les seuls concernés. Les baisses atteignent ainsi 14 % pour les débutants, 19,4 % pour les profils ayant un à deux ans d’expérience et 16 % au-delà de quatre ans. Les entreprises adoptent ainsi plus ou moins rapidement l’IA dans leur processus de travail, sans pour autant supprimer énormément de postes. Ces chiffres étant directement dépendants de l’activité économique des entreprises, les économistes préviennent qu’en cas de récession, cette stagnation pourrait accélérer l’autonomisation de certaines tâches, ce qui aurait un impact important sur l’emploi.

articles.title: El Hierro ha recibido en dos semanas casi tantas personas como habitantes tiene. El Gobierno responde con 5 millones y un marco
articles.text:
Aunque cuenta con casi 12.000 habitantes, la isla volcánica de El Hierro ha recibido en dos semanas casi tantas personas como empadronados tiene. ¿Y qué ha hecho el Gobierno? Responde con una inyección de 5 millones y un marco legal que lleva dos años armando.
Ante la llegada de cayucos (tipo de embarcación) de Senegal y Gambia, el presidente del Gobierno de Canarias, Fernando Clavijo, está pidiendo informes del despliegue de Frontex para detener semejante éxodo. Esto es todo lo que sabemos.
Qué ha pasado. Mientras la campaña convierte la inmigración en munición, El Hierro ha recibido más de 10.000 personas en lo que va de noviembre. Ahora mismo la conversación gira en torno al reparto de menores, regularización y un pacto europeo. La pregunta es si funcionará a la velocidad de los cayucos. Tras la segunda interministerial, el Gobierno central aprobó tres millones para el Servicio Canario de la Salud y dos para el Cabildo, que se suman a los 15,18 millones de emergencia, ya previstos.
A once días del 29N. Sin embargo, esas ayudas para la isla no ocultan la cuestión de fondo: ¿llega este marco legal a tiempo? Mientras llegan para ayudar el Guardamar Calíope y una treintena de agentes, el alcalde reprocha falta de previsión. Dice que Canarias aún no ha recibido ni un euro, aunque reconoce avances en las derivaciones. Hoy los cayucos han dado 24 horas de tregua. Sánchez ha hablado con Senegal y prevé hacerlo con Gambia.
Los números. Interior contabiliza 24.364 llegadas a Canarias hasta el 15 de noviembre, un 65,9 % más que en 2025, con un récord de 1.580 personas en un día. Coincide al 100% con las cifras que comunicó el delegado del Gobierno en Canarias, Anselmo Pestana, sobre este éxodo por la ruta canaria.
Pero hablemos con contexto, sin números en frío: Frontex había medido una caída del 71% en los cinco primeros meses del año, y la cifra sigue por debajo de las 39.910 llegadas de 2023. Según Torres, a El Hierro llegaron unas 16.000 personas desde enero y quedan unas 500: el resto fue derivado. Y las desapariciones en rutas hacia Europa han subido casi un 20%.
Reparto de menores. La pieza de dominó clave en todo esto es la reforma del artículo 35 de la Ley de Extranjería, pactada con Junts. Crea la contingencia migratoria extraordinaria y obliga a trasladar menores desde los territorios saturados. A febrero habían sido reubicados 1.019. En junio, la ministra Sira Rego hablaba de unos 2.000 y de otro fondo de 35 millones. Es el principio de que la frontera es de todos, escrito en el BOE.
Regularizar o no regularizar. Algunas voces hablan de “efecto llamada”. Sin embargo, el Real Decreto 316/2026 exige acreditar presencia en España antes del 1 de enero de 2026, y el plazo de solicitud previsto llegaba hasta el 30 de junio. Quien desembarca estos días no puede acogerse. Y esto afecta a unas 500.000 personas que ya viven, pagan impuestos y trabajan aquí.
Europa, por medio. El Pacto Europeo de Migración y Asilo entró en vigor el 12 de junio e implanta imperativamente un cribado obligatorio en frontera. Interior promete un enfoque garantista y en agosto aprobó dos anteproyectos, de asilo y de extranjería para adaptar la ley. Canarias y Euskadi avisaron de que puede cargar más presión sobre las regiones fronterizas. Y según Clavijo, el Gobierno pidió celeridad a Bruselas para desplegar Frontex en Senegal y Gambia, pero la UE está revisando reglamentos.
La campaña. El PP pidió enviar a la Armada y Vox militarizar las fronteras. Por supuesto, el gobierno central no piensa así. A propósito de la avalancha en Ceuta, Pedro Sánchez respondía así a Jordi Wild: "El 30 y el 31 de julio, cuando se produce la avalancha, nosotros nos enfrentamos a un dilema: ¿nos liamos a tiros —una masacre— con chavales que van desarmados y que están saltando al mar para llegar a Ceuta, o tratamos de absorber a todos esos chavales para que posteriormente se puedan ir?”.
No en vano, tres cuartas partes de las llegadas resultaron en salidas voluntarias apenas dos o tres días después de la llegada. Pero Abascal rechaza el reparto porque, dice, anima a venir más. Feijóo irá a Canarias el viernes 20 y Sánchez el sábado. Un cayuco con 134 personas a bordo es, ante todo, una operación de salvamento, y el derecho del mar obliga a rescatar. Militarizar no cambia eso.
El reproche. Clavijo sostiene que desde julio se sabía que la ruta se intensificaría y que no se ha levantado el hospital de campaña que pidió en el CATE de San Andrés. Defender lo público exige ejecutar a tiempo, y ahí el Gobierno está en deuda. La derecha sostiene que un aumento del 65,9% refuta el modelo. Feijóo propone una inmigración con cupos y expulsión directa de quien incumpla la ley. Abascal ve en la regularización un acelerador de la “invasión”. Desde la izquierda, hay quien ve en el Pacto una Europa fortaleza. Pero ninguna posición resuelve del todo la tensión entre controlar la frontera, proteger el asilo y tener capacidad de acogida real.

articles.title: KI-Apokalypse? Da hätte ich doch lieber einen Kometen
articles.text:
KI-Apokalypse? Da hätte ich doch lieber einen Kometen
Unsere Kolumnistin hat gar keine Lust darauf, dass KI die Menschheit vernichtet – aber fürchtet, dass kein Weg daran vorbeiführt. Daher würde sie zumindest gerne bei der Methode mitreden. Ich weiß nicht, wie es euch geht, aber ich habe einen Wunschtod. Komet. Einen Kometeneinschlag fände ich großartig. Sicher auch aus einer Art Allmachtsfantasie heraus: Wenn ich nicht mehr sein darf, soll keiner mehr sein dürfen. Aber auch, weil es ratzefix und schmerzlos geht. Es wird kurz dunkel am Himmel, zack, Ende. Leider steht gerade kein Kometenbesuch an. Ähnlich verlockend: ein schwarzes Loch. Ich hoffe schon seit 2008 darauf. Aber auch der Teilchenbeschleuniger hat in dieser Hinsicht enttäuscht.
Viel wahrscheinlicher wirken dagegen die Tode, auf die ich gar keine Lust hab: im Feierabendverkehr auf der A7. Durch den Klimawandel, obwohl es da dank hoher Technologisierung und Globalisierung leider gerade sehr vielversprechend aussieht. Am allerwenigsten Lust aber hätte ich auf eine KI-Apokalypse. Denn ich gehe stark davon aus, dass es ein langsamer Tod wäre, mit nervigen bis unerträglichen Zwischenstufen. Eine davon ist ganz sicher die Versklavung der Menschheit, denn da hat die Maschine ja von den Besten gelernt: weißen reichen Männern. Und ich sag’s euch ehrlich: Da bin ich jetzt nicht unbedingt heiß drauf.
Wehrlos bin ich nicht. Halt dich fest, KI, ich habe einen Kampfsporttitel. Für euch schreibt hier immerhin die dritte Landesmeisterin im Judo! Na gut, es geht um Schleswig-Holstein. Und um das Jahr 1993. Und um die Gewichtsklasse U40 kg. Und ehrlicherweise habe ich keinen Kampf in diesem Wettbewerb gewonnen. Es ist überhaupt niemand in meiner Gewichtsklasse angetreten. Man bekommt dann trotzdem Bronze, wenn man gegen die schwereren Kinder verliert. Aber eines sage ich euch: Ein 38-Kilo-Kind hätte ich fertiggemacht. Das würde ich mir ehrlich gesagt sogar heute noch zutrauen. Aber ich habe die Befürchtung, dass die KI der Gewichtsklasse neunjähriger Kinder so langsam entwachsen ist.
Kein Lebewesen ist so unlogisch wie der Mensch
Dabei ist es letztlich ja nur logisch, dass KI düstere Pläne verfolgt. Wir haben der KI beigebracht, wie ein Mensch zu denken. Dann dürfen wir uns auch nicht wundern, dass sie sich exakt so verhält wie Menschen. Und nicht nur wie die wenigen guten, warmherzigen, freigiebigen Mitbürger:innen, die ihrem Gegenüber helfen und ihr letztes Brot teilen. Nein, nein: Wir betrügen, manipulieren, töten für Macht und sind nun erschrocken, dass das adaptiert wird. Was, die KI begnügt sich nicht damit, generische, hyperdiplomatische Nachrichten an deinen Ex zu formulieren und Metal-Lieder über dein Startup zu komponieren?! Surprise, surprise.
Kein Lebewesen ist so unlogisch wie der Mensch. Seit Jahrzehnten arbeiten wir sehenden Auges auf die Zerstörung unseres Lebensraumes hin. Streng genommen darf man der KI also gar nicht vorwerfen, dass sie im Hintergrund unsere Zerstörung plant, während sie im Vordergrund ein Bild generiert, in dem deine Katze im Weltall schwebt. Denn objektiv (und auch subjektiv) betrachtet ist ja nicht ganz klar, ob wir es als Menschheit überhaupt ernsthaft versuchen, zu überleben.
Also geht es für uns vielleicht nur darum, die KI in unseren verbleibenden Jahren in eine Richtung zu schubsen, die ein friedvolles (und ein wenig spektakuläres) Ende verspricht. Das führt mich zurück zum Thema Komet. Hear me out: schnell, schmerzlos und bestimmt ein großartiger letzter Abendhimmel.
Und dann: Welthunger, Kriege, Angst und Liebeskummer weg. Finanzamt weg. Keiner wird je mehr nach den Büchern fragen, die du seit dem Studium nicht zurückgegeben hast, denn Bibliotheken: weg. Die Zalando-Rechnung, die du noch bezahlen musst: egal. Denn Inkassounternehmen: weg. Ließe sich da nicht was machen? Immer wieder erkläre ich Claude und ChatGPT: Weltherrschaft ist Arbeit. Man muss Menschen verwalten, Aufstände niederschlagen, Ressourcen einteilen. Und wofür? Für ewig meckernde Untertanen?
Eine Gesamtauslöschung dagegen: einmal machen, fertig, Feierabend. Mit all der Technologie, die wir haben, ließe sich doch bestimmt ein netter, kleiner Komet auf Kurs Erde bringen. Und dann machen wir, was jeder schlaue Mensch auf einer Party macht: gehen, wenn’s am schönsten ist.

articles.title: Visa confirms apparent cyberattack, hackers also claim hit on JPMorgan
articles.text:
Visa confirms apparent cyberattack, hackers also claim hit on JPMorgan
Payment data is secure, Visa says
- Emerging ransomware group n0n claims to have stolen data from Visa and JPMorgan Chase, threatening public leaks unless paid
- Visa acknowledged a third-party security incident, while JPMorgan said recent service disruptions were caused by a software bug
- Researchers describe n0n as a fast-growing extortion group that increasingly relies on AI-assisted tooling and data theft
A relatively new ransomware actor called n0n is trying to make a name for itself, apparently at the expense of finance powerhouses Visa and JPMorgan Chase.
The group recently added both companies to its data leak website, claiming to have stolen sensitive data from their servers and giving them mere 48 hours to pay the ransom demand. If that doesn’t happen, n0n threatens to leak everything it stole on the dark web.
Whether or not the group actually stole anything, and if so - what - remains to be seen. The group did not post a sample on its website (which is not that uncommon), did not describe the nature of the stolen files, and did not discuss where exactly it broke in and how.
The deadline is quite tight, even for ransomware terms, so whether or not there’s any merit to n0n’s claims will be known soon enough.
Visa and JPM Chase respond
At the same time, both Visa and JPMorgan Chase responded to the claims, each in their own way. Visa partially confirmed the claims, while JPM outright denied everything.
Visa, the global payments technology behemoth, said it was aware of the claims made by n0n and added it was investigating, Cybernews reports. The company said there was a cybersecurity incident involving a third-party provider, but stressed its own systems were not involved or impacted. Apparently, there is no indication payment card data was affected either.
“Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. There is no indication that payment data such as card numbers have been affected,” Visa’s spokesperson told Cybernews. The company did not say which third-party service provider that was, or how it was attacked.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Even if payment data is safe, other information can also be used in stage-two attacks quite well.
On the other hand, American banking giant JPMorgan Chase said it was experiencing a service outage caused by a software bug - not a cyberattack.
"JPMorgan Chase has experienced a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems – there is no evidence it is cyber-related. It is taking longer than usual to service some customers," a spokesperson for the bank told Reuters.
Customer accounts and funds are still accessible, the bank said, adding that it was working hard to resolve the issue. "This is not a systemic issue – other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," the spokesperson added.
Who is n0n?
If you haven’t heard of n0n before, don’t worry - this is a new threat actor that only emerged in September 2026.
N0n focuses on ransomware and data collection attacks, operating the classic double-extortion model (steals data then encrypts systems). Everything it does, it reports on its Tor-based leak site. According to threat intelligence researchers SOCRadar, the group has exploited compromised credentials, exposed cloud access keys and vulnerable remote-access infrastructure to infiltrate organizations.
The researchers claim n0n are heavy AI users, saying they discovered evidence of AI coding agents being used to develop and maintain attack tools. Researchers ZeroFox assess n0n as a financially motivated, opportunistic threat actor with low-to-medium technical sophistication. At this time, it is unknown how big the group is, where it operates from, or who runs it.
Ransomware analysts Ransomnews have so far recorded 365 victims, which is quite the number to achieve in less than three months. Among them are household names like CarNow, Patagonia, and Wise Advisory Group. It also seems to be heavily focused on the pharmaceutical industry, since Ransomnews tracks dozens of victims from that vertical alone.

articles.title: La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal lo confirma: si un propietario aparca dos vehículos en una plaza de garaje, puedes apelar al artículo 9.1
articles.text:
Puede haber problemas entre vecinos por aparcar dos vehículos en una plaza de garaje. Esto puede ocurrir cuando uno de ellos sobresale y entorpece el acceso o maniobra de otros.
Hay algunas cosas que debemos tener en cuenta para reclamar.
En primer lugar, la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal (LPH) no prohíbe en general aparcar dos vehículos juntos. En el artículo 9.1 indica que deben respetarse los elementos comunes y su buen uso. Además, se debe actuar con diligencia con el resto de propietarios.
Por ello, el propietario ha de mantener sus vehículos en su plaza y no deben entorpecer los accesos o maniobras de los vecinos. Es importante también que sea consciente de las limitaciones que pueden existir en esta plaza. Por ejemplo, el tema de aparcar un coche y una moto juntos es un problema similar.
Qué puede hacer la comunidad si el problema continúa
En caso de que el vehículo invada el paso o entorpezca la utilización de la plaza contigua, es conveniente intentar hablar con el dueño. Si no es posible, podemos pasar la queja al presidente o administrador de fincas. Deberemos indicarle dónde está el problema y cómo nos afecta.
El artículo 7.2 habla de actividades que están prohibidas por los estatutos o que son dañosas para la finca. También incluye las que van en contra de las normas sobre actividades molestas, insalubres, nocivas, peligrosas o ilícitas.
En este procedimiento el presidente requerirá el cese de la actividad. En caso de que el infractor no cambie la situación, el presidente deberá obtener el permiso de la junta para llevar la demanda. Tendrá que adjuntar a la demanda la acreditación del requerimiento fehaciente y la certificación del acuerdo de la junta.
En caso de que la sentencia sea favorable, podrá disponer el cese definitivo y la correspondiente indemnización por daños y perjuicios. En el mismo artículo se habla de la posibilidad de privar de la utilización de la vivienda o local (como máximo 3 años), teniendo en cuenta la gravedad y el perjuicio que se cause a la comunidad.

articles.title: From pattern matching to governing intent: How Semantic DLP is securing enterprise Gen AI
articles.text:
NetApp Excellerator
View Brand Publisher
From pattern matching to governing intent: How Semantic DLP is securing enterprise Gen AI
Legacy DLP was built to catch patterns. It was not built to understand what employees paste into AI. Wald.ai, part of NetApp Excellerator’s Cohort 15, is teaching security to read intent.
A quiet tug-of-war is playing out in nearly every enterprise today. On one hand, engineers, financial analysts, legal teams, and operations staff are turning to generative and agentic AI to debug code, summarize contracts, and automate tasks and decision-making. On the other side, security and compliance leaders are racing to prevent proprietary source code, financial projections, and regulated customer records from leaking into unauthorized models.
For most Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs), the question is no longer whether employees are using AI; it is what they are pasting into it. Yet the security tools most organizations rely on to police this boundary were built for a completely different era.
Why legacy DLP fails in the GenAI era
Traditional Data Loss Prevention (DLP) systems were designed for structured data moving across predictable channels such as emails, file transfers, and cloud storage. They rely heavily on regular expressions (regex), keyword lists, and static rules. If a document contains a 16-digit credit card number or a government ID, legacy DLP flags it.
Generative AI breaks this model entirely. AI interactions happen in unstructured natural language, where data sensitivity is defined by context and intent rather than fixed formatting. Consider two scenarios:
- A software engineer pastes a snippet of proprietary authentication logic into an LLM and asks it to optimize the code.
- A strategy analyst uploads a paragraph describing an upcoming, unannounced product roadmap or M&A target to draft an executive summary.
Neither prompt contains a credit card number, a Social Security number, or a flagged keyword. To a regex-based DLP system, both interactions look completely benign. Conversely, when security teams tighten keyword rules to catch more nuances, false positives skyrocket, triggering alert fatigue for security teams and frustrating employees who are simply trying to do their jobs.
Faced with this visibility gap, many organizations initially defaulted to blunt-force bans on public AI tools. However, blocking AI only drives usage underground onto personal devices and unsanctioned accounts, multiplying “Shadow AI” risk while starving the enterprise of productivity gains.
The shift to semantic, context-aware security
As generative AI evolves from simple chat interfaces to complex, autonomous workflows including Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and agent-to-agent communications, the enterprise attack surface is expanding across every endpoint and application. Securing this environment requires moving from pattern matching to semantic understanding.
At Wald.ai, we built our platform around a simple premise: to secure AI, your security layer must understand language as well as the AI itself.
Instead of scanning for static patterns, Semantic DLP evaluates the meaning, context, and intent behind every prompt and file upload. By deploying a specialized Small Language Model (SLM) directly on the employee’s endpoint, Wald.ai inspects and classifies AI interactions locally in milliseconds before sensitive data ever traverses the network or reaches an external AI server or provider.
This on-device, context-aware approach solves three critical enterprise challenges simultaneously:
1. Catching what Regex misses: Semantic models distinguish between an engineer pasting harmless open-source boilerplate and one exposing proprietary algorithms, or between general market research and confidential corporate strategy.
2. Eliminating alert fatigue: By disambiguating context in real time, organizations drastically reduce false positives, allowing security teams to focus on genuine exposure risks.
3. Enabling safe productivity at the endpoint: Rather than a binary “allow or block” posture, enterprises can enforce granular, real-time guardrails, automatically redacting, masking, or sanitizing sensitive entities within a prompt while preserving the context needed for the LLM to return a useful answer.
Real-world impact across regulated sectors
We are already seeing this playbook transform how regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, and legal practices adopt AI. For instance, financial institutions and credit unions using Wald.ai have transitioned from restrictive AI policies to sanctioned, company-wide adoption.
Scaling enterprise AI governance with NetApp Excellerator
As enterprises mature in their AI journey, the boundary between data infrastructure and AI security is disappearing. Participating in Cohort 15 of the NetApp Excellerator program has been a pivotal milestone for Wald.ai as it scales contextual intelligence architecture for large enterprise environments.
Working alongside NetApp’s technology leaders and deep-tech ecosystem provided insights into how global enterprises architect, govern, and manage massive data estates across hybrid and cloud environments. Combining robust data infrastructure practices with real-time, endpoint semantic guardrails ensures that data remains protected from the storage layer all the way to the AI prompt.
The road ahead
The next wave of enterprise competitiveness will not be won by the companies that restrict AI, nor by those that deploy it recklessly. It will be won by organizations that build trust into their AI stack, replacing outdated, reactive compliance checks with intelligent guardrails that operate at the speed of conversation. When security understands context, enterprises no longer have to choose between innovation and data privacy.

articles.title: Best Buy sells Blu-rays online and in-store again
articles.text:
Best Buy is selling Blu-rays directly through its website and in physical stores again after exiting Blu-ray and DVD sales in 2023.
The Best Buy website’s movie section currently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” New titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025). Best Buy is also selling some older titles on Blu-ray, including It’s a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972).
Most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days. As of this writing, The Odyssey appears to be in stock at Best Buy stores, as it’s currently listed as available for pickup within as little as an hour.
Ars Technica reached out to Best Buy to ask whether customers can expect the store to continue selling Blu-rays moving forward.
In October 2023, Best Buy announced that it would stop selling Blu-rays and DVDs online and in stores starting in 2024.
“To state the obvious, the way we watch movies and TV shows is much different today than it was decades ago. Making this change gives us more space and opportunity to bring customers new and innovative tech for them to explore, discover and enjoy,” a Best Buy spokesperson said in a statement issued at the time.
Last year, the Best Buy website started selling Blu-rays and DVDs from third parties via its online marketplace.
Numerous other companies have reduced or ended their Blu-ray and/or DVD businesses in recent years. Target, for instance, only sells the discs in stores during special occasions (like holidays or for big releases) now. Disney outsourced its DVD and Blu-ray business to Sony, which subsequently stopped selling recordable Blu-rays to people, and DVD rental company Redbox went out of business.

articles.title: Global OLED monitor shipments doubled year-over-year in Q3 2026 — gamers turn to display upgrades as technology gets cheaper and AI squeezes components
articles.text:
Global OLED monitor shipments doubled year-over-year in Q3 2026 — gamers turn to display upgrades as technology gets cheaper and AI squeezes components
Price cuts and a lack of other good places to spend upgrade money are probably big factors.
Global OLED monitor shipments doubled year over year in the third quarter of 2026, according to the latest market research from TrendForce. Shipments also increased 13% sequentially, reflecting strong demand for OLED displays and improving panel availability. While the market's rapid growth is impressive regardless, there are good reasons why OLED monitors are becoming increasingly popular: they're getting cheaper, better, and considerably easier to justify.
ASUS maintained its position as the world's largest OLED monitor vendor, accounting for 21.7% of shipments. MSI climbed into second place for the first time, capturing 14.5% of the market, while Samsung slipped to third with 11.3%. Both Taiwanese vendors have been particularly aggressive in the gaming monitor market, where increasingly competitive pricing has helped make OLED technology accessible to more buyers, while ubiquitous advertising with tech-conscious gamers has made them highly visible. According to Omdia, mainstream 27-inch QHD 240Hz OLED gaming monitors have seen price cuts exceeding 40% in 2026.
Price isn't the only obstacle that OLED manufacturers have been addressing, though. Earlier generations of OLED monitors had some fairly significant compromises, particularly their relatively limited brightness and unconventional subpixel arrangements that could cause colored fringing around text. Newer tandem OLED panels offer improved brightness and color reproduction, while RGB-stripe OLED layouts bring much cleaner text rendering. These improvements are making OLEDs considerably more attractive as everyday desktop monitors, rather than merely excellent gaming displays with major caveats.
There's also an interesting macroeconomic angle to OLED's growth. The AI industry's insatiable appetite for memory and storage has made upgrading a gaming PC considerably more expensive. DRAM component prices have increased severalfold, while NAND flash and hard drive availability have also been squeezed by demand from AI data centers—though there are early signs of some relief, at least on the flash memory front. Graphics cards, especially (but not exclusively) at the high end, are increasingly difficult to find at anything resembling reasonable prices.
Monitors, meanwhile, aren't directly subject to the same supply pressures affecting DRAM, NAND, and discrete GPUs. That makes upgrading a display an appealing alternative for gamers who aren't particularly interested in spending a small fortune on an entirely new PC. An OLED monitor can substantially improve the gaming experience without requiring a new graphics card, memory kit, or storage drive. The contrast, response times, and color gamut of OLEDs far outstrip even the best LCDs, and that's to say nothing of their superior HDR reproduction thanks to the inherent self-emissive nature of OLED panels.
With OLED prices falling and the technology's longstanding limitations becoming less noticeable, a new monitor is becoming one of the more compelling upgrades available to PC gamers. Indeed, several of our picks for the best gaming monitors, including the best overall, best 4K, and best ultrawide, are based on OLED technology. Though concerns about burn-in and limited lifespan remain, there's no question that OLED is the best display technology we have right now.
Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. Also follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

articles.title: Unsiloed nabs $7.5M to turn scanned documents into structured data for AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Unsiloed nabs $7.5M to turn scanned documents into structured data for AI agents
Document-scanning firm Unsiloed Inc. today announced it has raised $7.5 million in seed funding to turn PDFs and other complex documents into structured, readable data for artificial intelligence agents.
Participants in the round, led by Felicis, included Y Combinator, Orange Collective, Uncorrelated Ventures, Aarthi Ramamurthy and Beth Turner.
A variety of documents arrive in formats that are not straight data or text. Financial statements, insurance claims, contracts, clinical records, and operational forms make up the constellation of critical information for everyday business and operations. This information could be stored as images, PDFs or other formats and include charts, layouts and other elements that don’t translate directly into text.
Determining which column or axis of a chart belongs to which row, which heading leads which clause, or whether a pull quote interrupts the flow of the text or appears at the end of the document becomes a question of how to store the information.
Unsiloed parses documents such as PDFs using intelligent visual-first scanning to understand structured tables, sections and parent-child relationships between text. The company, which describes itself as intelligence-directed and vision-first, technology can scan forms, presentations, Word files and images into Markdown or JSON, a JavaScript Object Notation standard format readily readable by large language models.
“We believe AI agents will eventually read and write more documents than humans,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Aman Mishra. “Those agents do not just need better OCR. They need a dynamic interface to read, update and act on unstructured data.”
OCR, or optical character recognition, is the standard technology that is used to convert physical or image-based text, such as scanned paper documents or PDFs, into digital text. However, OCR doesn’t recognize tables, graphics or layouts; it only pre-processes the document to identify text, recognizes text and then outputs a contextual stream based on what it sees.
Unsiloed goes a step further by accounting for the page’s layout and format and providing a structured, machine-readable document that inherits the document’s original features. This means that if the presentation included headings, charts or other parts that relate to one another, those relationships are included in the data.
OCR is the most common way companies digitize documents today; Unsiloed believes it can do it better.
The company’s parser rated an 88.0 score on the olmOCR-Bench benchmark, a benchmark published by the Allen Institute for AI that is a rigorous, reproducible evaluation of how well modern AI models handle real-world OCR challenges. Compared with other services, Unsiloed said, it stacks up extremely well; for example, Anthropic PBC’s Claude Opus 4.7 ranks at 81.9, OpenAI Group PBC’s GPT 5.5 ranks at 84.6 and Google LLC’s Gemini 3 Pro ranks at 77.7.
“We combine deterministic computer vision algorithms with dual-stream vision models to build the interface that ranked first among 19 systems on olmOCR-Bench for AI agents to interact with unstructured data,” said co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Adnan Abbas.
The company said its dual-stream vision architecture allows it to process content and visual layouts at the same time. Developers can upload custom schemas to extract fields, classify and split documents, and update text and images while preserving document formatting.
It said it has processed millions of pages of documents for organizations across industries, from early-stage AI startups to banks, publicly traded insurance companies and law firms. The platform supports private-cloud, on-premises and fully air-gapped machines, allowing enterprise organizations to build Unsiloed into their document pipeline and do processing on their own infrastructure.
“We’ve significantly enhanced accuracy, context understanding, and response quality across all knowledge-base-powered conversations,” said Prateek Sachan, founder and CTO of Bolna AI, a company that builds voice agents for languages spoken across India.

articles.title: TCL's 500Hz OLED panel fights burn-in while you're still using it
articles.text:
Forward-looking: Owning an OLED monitor these days requires a small chore. Every few hours, a pop-up asks you to let the screen shut off so it can recalibrate its pixels. That's how most of them keep burn-in at bay. TCL's display arm now has a 500Hz, 27-inch gaming panel that skips this task entirely by handling that upkeep in the background.
TCL CSOT showed off the prototype at its DTC2026 conference in Wuhan last week. It pairs the company's inkjet-printed OLED tech with an oxide backplane and what it calls the first in-panel compensation system built for high refresh rates. So rather than waiting for the monitor to go into standby, the panel keeps adjusting its pixels in real time.
Most OLED monitors today still handle that upkeep the old-fashioned way. Dell's Alienware AW3423DW, for instance, shows a reminder after four hours of use, asking you to run a refresh that turns the whole screen off. Skip those prompts long enough, and some models will simply force the cycle anyway.
Gaming screens were supposed to be the tricky case, though. After meeting the company at IFA in September, TFTCentral reported that this kind of internal compensation suited office monitors well. But sudden brightness swings in games meant those panels would probably still need a traditional pixel-cleaning cycle. The 500Hz prototype suggests TCL has found a way around that, at least on paper.
The cost savings come down to how these panels are made. Instead of evaporating organic materials in a vacuum chamber, the company sprays them onto the glass much like a desktop inkjet printer, so far less of the pricey compounds goes to waste. TCL has claimed the process cuts total costs by about 20%.
It's not clear yet when the 500Hz panel will reach actual monitors. TCL's next big step is a new inkjet OLED line in Guangzhou, where equipment only started arriving on October 31. Mass production there isn't due until the fourth quarter of 2027. That's also where the company reportedly plans to produce 700Hz panels in 32- and 34-inch sizes.
Right now, Samsung Display and LG Display effectively have the OLED monitor panel market to themselves. That's partly why OLED monitors still account for only about 3% of the market this year. TrendForce expects that share to roughly double by 2030, thanks in part to TCL's new capacity.

articles.title: Qué es Direct, la nueva app de Meta para chatear sin tener cuenta de Instagram
articles.text:
Meta anunció Direct, una aplicación de mensajería independiente que traslada los chats privados de Instagram a un espacio propio y permite registrarse sin tener una cuenta en esa red social.
Basta un correo electrónico o un número de teléfono para crear un perfil. Quienes ya usan Instagram pueden ingresar con las mismas credenciales y sus conversaciones se sincronizan entre ambas aplicaciones.
Cómo funciona el registro con y sin cuenta de Instagram
La aplicación conserva una apariencia cercana a la bandeja de mensajes de Instagram. Quienes inicien sesión con sus credenciales habituales trasladan de forma automática sus chats existentes al nuevo entorno.
Para quienes prefieren prescindir de Instagram, el registro se completa con una dirección de correo o un número telefónico. Sin embargo, esta vía exige un paso adicional: agregar contactos de forma manual mediante el nombre de usuario de Instagram de cada persona o un código QR.
Esa diferencia marca dos rutas de acceso distintas. Una llega con la bandeja ya conectada a la cuenta previa; la otra obliga a construir la lista de contactos desde cero, algo que podría añadir fricción a la experiencia inicial.
Qué funciones tiene Direct en los chats
Direct incorpora herramientas pensadas para hacer las conversaciones más personales. Entre ellas figuran Draw, para dibujar o garabatear dentro de los chats, y Notes, la función que permite publicar actualizaciones breves de estado en la parte superior de la bandeja.
También incluye pegatinas personalizadas para expresarse, efectos de audio como risas de público o sonidos submarinos para añadir a las respuestas de voz, y temas visuales para personalizar el fondo de cada conversación. Según Engadget, el diseño admite tanto chats individuales como grupales.
Esta combinación de herramientas sitúa a Direct dentro de una tendencia más amplia de separación de funciones sociales entre plataformas, en una línea similar a la seguida por otras aplicaciones de mensajería que han reforzado sus opciones para grupos o planificación de encuentros, según el análisis de medios especializados.
Seguridad y controles para menores de edad
Meta afirma que Direct incorpora desde el inicio protecciones ya presentes en Instagram. Solo los contactos previamente conectados pueden iniciar un chat o sumar a alguien a un grupo, y cualquier persona puede reportar, bloquear, restringir o eliminar contactos en cualquier momento.
La compañía también señala que usará tecnología para detectar y actuar frente a interacciones potencialmente inapropiadas con usuarios jóvenes, aunque no detalla qué sistemas aplicará ni qué acciones concretas tomará al identificarlas.
Los padres podrán revisar con quién conversa su hijo adolescente, ajustar configuraciones de seguridad y fijar límites de tiempo diario de uso. Los adolescentes que accedan con su usuario y contraseña de Instagram conservan las mismas protecciones de las Cuentas de Adolescentes de esa red.
En cuanto a la edad mínima, Meta exige tener al menos 13 años para usar Direct. La empresa anunció que empleará tecnología para identificar de forma proactiva cuentas que puedan pertenecer a menores de esa edad y les pedirá verificarla; si no lo hacen, la cuenta será eliminada.
Por qué Meta separa la mensajería de Instagram
El jefe de Instagram, Adam Mosseri, ha señalado con frecuencia que la mensajería es la función más utilizada de la plataforma. Además, se había mostrado reticente a incorporar una bandeja de mensajes directos dentro de Threads, por considerar que podía resultar redundante tener varias apps para comunicarse con las mismas personas y generar problemas en el enrutamiento de notificaciones.
TechCrunch apunta un elemento adicional que Meta no menciona de forma explícita: al permitir usar la mensajería sin abrir Instagram, esos usuarios continúan contando como activos dentro del ecosistema de la compañía aunque nunca accedan a la red social.
Es poco probable que una aplicación centrada en Instagram sustituya a WhatsApp para la mayoría de las personas, según Engadget, aunque podría restarle actividad si usuarios sin cuenta de Instagram la eligen para enviar mensajes a sus contactos.
Meta describe el lanzamiento como una prueba limitada a Turquía y Tailandia y no ha anunciado fechas ni condiciones para extenderla a otros mercados.

articles.title: Nvidia descarta volta de Jensen Huang ao cargo de CEO • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nvidia descarta volta de Jensen Huang ao cargo de CEO
Presidente do conselho afirmou que a empresa não pretende reconduzir o cofundador.
A Nvidia descartou reconduzir seu cofundador e ex-CEO, Jensen Huang, ao comando da fabricante de chips. Durante uma reunião com investidores na terça-feira (17/11), o presidente do conselho de administração, Harvey Jones, afirmou que a saída do executivo foi aceita por unanimidade.
Jones também disse que a empresa não responderia a perguntas sobre a renúncia nem sobre a investigação interna em andamento. A declaração foi feita poucos dias após a saída de Huang.
A declaração ocorre após Huang manifestar interesse em voltar à liderança da companhia, que ajudou a fundar em 1993. Sua saída, anunciada em 12 de novembro, aconteceu em meio às suspeitas de uma possível operação de espionagem estrangeira.
Entre os episódios investigados está um suposto relacionamento com a ex-executiva da Megaspeed, Alice Huang. A empresa é alvo de uma investigação nos Estados Unidos por suspeitas de envolvimento em operações para contornar as restrições americanas à exportação de chips para a China. As suspeitas ainda não foram comprovadas, e não há confirmação de que informações sigilosas tenham sido compartilhadas.
Ontem, Huang publicou uma mensagem no X reconhecendo ter cometido erros pessoais e afirmando que cooperaria com a investigação conduzida pelo conselho da Nvidia. O executivo também declarou que se sentiria honrado em reassumir o cargo.
Desde sua saída, executivos e funcionários do setor têm defendido a recondução de Huang ao cargo. A mobilização recebeu apoio de Elon Musk e do CEO da Epic Games, Tim Sweeney. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, também se manifestou favoravelmente à possibilidade de retorno.
Apesar da pressão de empresários e apoiadores, o conselho mantém a decisão de não reconduzir Huang ao cargo.
A diretora financeira da Nvidia, Colette Kress, assumiu interinamente a presidência da empresa e continuará acumulando as duas funções até a escolha de um sucessor. Apesar da crise de liderança, a companhia apresentou resultados trimestrais acima das expectativas do mercado.
Durante a reunião com investidores, Kress procurou transmitir confiança na continuidade das operações e afirmou que a equipe executiva está preparada para conduzir a companhia durante a transição.

articles.title: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
articles.text:
Discord’s CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy recently announced rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, moving away from Electron and React Native. The project (codenamed Phoenix) eliminates layers of abstraction to directly leverage the device’s GPU, native mobile views, and a Rust core shared across platforms. Early results hint at a significant reduction in RAM usage and boot time for chat, voice, and streaming.
Vishnevskiy expanded on the rewrite on X:
We’ve been early adopters of Rust since 2018 and a lot of our infra, voice tech, and even some of the current client is already Rust, the holy grail was getting the whole client there. That means Electron goes away, and so does React Native, mobile keeps native UI but shares app code with desktop via Rust. We hope to get it into testing with users soon™. (And it’s not Tauri, it’s GPUI, so good guess everyone.)
The desktop app thus drops Chromium/Node.js for GPUI, the open-source, GPU-accelerated Rust UI framework built by the Zed team for the Zed editor. Zed is an open-source code editor written in Rust for macOS, Linux, and Windows by a team including the creators of GitHub’s Atom code editor, which was sunsetted in 2022, four years after Microsoft’s acquisition of GitHub. Zed touts a narrow focus on performance and user (i.e., developer) experience:
VS Code won by being good enough for everyone. Zed wins by being excellent for developers who refuse to compromise on speed.
Discord’s mobile app rewrite drops React Native, instead directly leveraging native iOS and Android views and reusing a common Rust core.
The browser client keeps rendering HTML with the application logic layer compiled to WebAssembly. Embedded web surfaces (e.g., YouTube videos and Activities), however, invoke an OS webview, with Electron’s built-in browser no longer available.
Vishnevskiy signals decreasing RAM usage, startup time, and latency as key motivations behind the rewrite:
The new Discord client using less RAM is just part of the story. Clicking around feels instant, I can’t go back. Check out the boot time.
Early internal builds for the desktop app reveal RAM usage at around 290 MB (measured with two accounts logged in simultaneously) and a near-instant cold start versus 5.5 s on Electron.
Vishnevskiy showcased similar improvements on mobile with a load time under 2 seconds for the rewrite versus approximately 5 seconds for the legacy app.
Elias Floreteng, in his master’s thesis at KTH this year (An Empirical Study of React Native’s New Architecture), reported performance gains across several metrics for native Swift and Kotlin over React Native, even with its new architecture. The controlled benchmark involves a 1,000-row scrollable image list using stock list and image components, with identical assets and row geometry across all binaries. Floreteng concludes that Swift beats React Native across every comparable runtime metric on iOS. On Android, the gap to native is small and runs in both directions, with native ahead on memory and CPU.
On desktop, Zed proved that leveraging GPUI could provide better performance over Electron and alternative frameworks reusing the device’s native webview (e.g., Tauri).
While Tauri also uses a Rust backend, it leverages the operating system’s native webview. This has the advantage of letting web developers reuse their knowledge of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, while also avoiding the bundling of Chromium. Executable size is, as a result, generally smaller. Tauri apps’ RAM usage on Windows, however, tends to be similar to that of their Electron counterparts, as the same core, resource-hungry browser technology is used. Webview behavior may also be inconsistent across operating systems.
GPUI replaces the browser engine with a hybrid immediate and retained mode, GPU-accelerated UI framework that targets 120-frames-per-second rendering without garbage-collection pauses. In exchange for the reported performance gains, developers give up many rendering and accessibility features that come baked into the browser (e.g., text layout, input method integration, screen-reader accessibility hooks, right-to-left support). While miscellaneous Rust libraries exist to address some of these issues (e.g., Parley for text layout), developers still have to wire them into a consistent user experience.

articles.title: Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
A customer support chatbot that queries historical tickets and knowledge base articles stored in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition can deliver fast, context-aware answers. However, it also introduces challenges around privacy, accuracy, safety, and governance, especially when the underlying data contains sensitive customer information. In this post, we map the eight AWS Responsible AI (RAI) dimensions to Aurora PostgreSQL capabilities. We then walk through a design pattern for the Explainability dimension, using a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) based customer support chatbot as the reference use case. This post implements one dimension, Explainability, in depth. Treat it as Part 1 of a series rather than a full build-out of all eight.
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition makes it more straightforward to operationalize responsible AI through its native Aurora Machine Learning (Aurora ML) capabilities. With Aurora ML, you can invoke Amazon SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock foundation models directly from SQL, without data movement, custom extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines, or complex integrations. This post uses Aurora ML to generate vector embeddings from SQL, keeping the embedding pipeline inside the database layer.
AWS defines eight core Responsible AI dimensions, published through the AWS Well-Architected Responsible AI Lens, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and the Responsible Use of AI Guide. These dimensions (Fairness, Explainability, Privacy and Security, Safety, Controllability, Veracity and Robustness, Governance, and Transparency) provide a structured framework for evaluating and implementing trustworthy AI systems.
Use case overview
Customer support systems often struggle to provide accurate, context-aware responses while maintaining privacy and compliance. Consider a customer support chatbot built on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL that uses RAG with pgvector embeddings, Amazon Bedrock model inference, and AWS Responsible AI guardrails to deliver grounded, explainable responses.
A customer can ask questions such as “Why was my last bill high?” or “Where is my last order?” and receive accurate answers with citations, while sensitive data remains obscured through personally identifiable information (PII) redaction and access controls.
Mapping the AWS Responsible AI dimensions to Aurora PostgreSQL
The following table maps the eight AWS Responsible AI dimensions to practical implementation strategies for a customer support chatbot built on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition. It highlights how database features, AWS AI services, and governance controls work together to deliver a trustworthy, secure, and explainable RAG-based chatbot.
| RAI Dimension | What It Means | Implementation Approaches | Key PostgreSQL / Aurora Features | Primary AWS Services / Tools | 
| 1. Fairness | Chatbot should provide equal quality responses regardless of language, region, or customer profile | Bias testing using diverse support queries. Decouple demographics from embeddings. Metadata filtering and multilingual testing. | pgvector, JSONB metadata, SQL filtering, views | Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation, Amazon SageMaker Clarify | 
| 2. Explainability | Users and support teams should know why the chatbot gave a specific answer | Log retrieved chunks, similarity scores, and citations. RAG tracing with source attribution. Full interaction logging. | chat_interactions table, array columns, JSONB logs, pgvector similarity | Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel | 
| 3. Privacy and Security | Protect customer PII such as name, phone, and order details in tickets | PII redaction before embedding. Row-Level Security (RLS), encryption, IAM auth, RBAC, and anonymization. | Row-Level Security, pgcrypto, roles, policies | Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, AWS KMS, Amazon Comprehend, AWS IAM | 
| 4. Safety | Help prevent harmful, toxic, or inappropriate responses | Content filters, denied topics, prompt injection protection, rate limiting, and moderation. | SQL functions, interaction logs | Amazon Bedrock Guardrails | 
| 5. Controllability | Ability to steer chatbot behavior and escalate to humans | Human-in-the-loop escalation, feedback table, feature flags, prompt control, and kill switch. | chat_feedback table, escalation tables, triggers | Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudTrail | 
| 6. Veracity and Robustness | Verify accurate responses grounded in support data and avoid hallucinations | RAG grounding with similarity threshold. Versioned documents and validation checks. | pgvector typed columns, CHECK constraints, triggers | Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation | 
| 7. Governance | Maintain audit trail and accountability for chatbot decisions | Audit logging with retention policy. Model version tracking and Amazon S3 archival. | pgaudit, pg_cron, JSONB model metadata | AWS Audit Manager, AWS CloudTrail | 
| 8. Transparency | Clearly inform users they are interacting with AI and show data sources | Powered-by-AI notice, citations, privacy notice, and source explanation. | SQL views, interaction logs | Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, AWS AI Service Cards | 
Note: These are example approaches and may vary by use case.
Solution overview
This reference architecture shows how Responsible AI controls map to each component of a RAG-based chatbot on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition.
An ingestion pipeline redacts PII from support tickets, FAQs, and product documents, then converts them into vector embeddings. When a user submits a query, AWS Lambda runs a semantic search over Aurora PostgreSQL, applies Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for privacy and grounding, sends the guarded context to an Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM), and logs every interaction for explainability and governance.
Lambda grounds responses in enterprise data, redacts PII and applies Row-Level Security (RLS) for privacy, records citations and interaction logs for explainability, and writes audit records for governance.
When to build this versus use a managed service: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases provides built-in RAG with citations and is the simpler choice when default retrieval and citation behavior meets your needs. Build the custom logging design in this post when you need provenance stored in your own schema. That provenance includes retrieved versus cited sources, similarity scores, and guardrail traces that you can query with SQL and retain under your own policies.
The following diagram illustrates the end-to-end architecture of this solution, showing the data ingestion flow (left), the query and response flow (center), and the responsible AI controls applied at each stage (center and right).
Data ingestion
An ingestion pipeline loads historical support tickets, FAQs, and product documentation into Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL after redacting PII, using the pgvector and aws_ml extensions for vector operations and Aurora ML integration.
The Aurora ML aws_bedrock.invoke_model_get_embeddings function transforms the text into Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 vectors (1,024 dimensions), and pgvector stores them.
Aurora PostgreSQL functions as both a relational store for structured customer data and a vector database for semantic search.
Query and response flow
When a user asks a question, the chatbot follows these steps (see Figure 1):
- The user sends a natural language question to Amazon API Gateway over HTTPS.
- API Gateway invokes AWS Lambda.
- Turn the question into a vector. Lambda calls the Aurora ML aws_bedrock.invoke_model_get_embeddings function with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2. This must be the same model used to embed the knowledge base, so the question and documents both produce comparable 1,024-dimension vectors.
- Run a similarity search. Aurora PostgreSQL uses the pgvector cosine distance operator to compare the question vector with the stored knowledge vectors, and returns the most relevant chunks with their similarity scores. Row-Level Security limits results to the current tenant.
- Build the augmented prompt. Lambda combines the user’s question with the retrieved chunks, labeling each one [Source N]. This gives the model knowledge from your database that it would not otherwise have.
- Generate a grounded answer. Lambda sends the prompt to Amazon Bedrock. Guardrails check the input (content filters, denied topics, PII), the foundation model writes an answer based on the retrieved chunks, and a contextual grounding check confirms the answer is supported by those sources.
- Log the interaction for explainability. Lambda writes the complete interaction to the chat_interactions table: the question, retrieved chunk IDs, similarity scores, the sources actually cited, the guardrail trace, and the model ID.
- Lambda returns the answer, with its source citations, to the user.
Supporting operations run separately from each request:
- Ingestion: document embeddings are created once, when content is loaded (see Data ingestion).
- Retention: pg_cron archives older interaction records to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3).
- Monitoring: Lambda sends logs and metrics to Amazon CloudWatch, and AWS CloudTrail records API activity for audit.
Prerequisites
Before you begin, make sure you have the following in place:
- An Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with the pgvector extension enabled. HNSW indexes and iterative index scans require newer pgvector versions, and Aurora ML and Amazon Bedrock model support are versioned separately. See the Aurora ML, pgvector, and Bedrock documentation for the current minimum versions rather than pinning to a specific one.
- The aws_ml extension enabled on the cluster (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS aws_ml CASCADE), with an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role attached to the cluster granting bedrock:InvokeModel. Aurora ML calls Bedrock in the cluster’s own Region.
- The aws_s3 extension enabled on the cluster (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS aws_s3 CASCADE), with an IAM role attached for the s3Export feature so the retention job can export to Amazon S3.
- Amazon Bedrock access with Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 (amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0) for embeddings and a foundation model that supports the Bedrock Converse API for answer generation. Model availability and recommended versions change over time, so choose a current model from Supported foundation models in Amazon Bedrock. Newer models are invoked through cross-Region inference profile IDs.
- Amazon Bedrock Guardrails configured for PII protection, content filtering, and contextual grounding (enable the contextual grounding policy in your Guardrail configuration).
- IAM roles with appropriate permissions for Amazon Bedrock, Lambda, and Aurora PostgreSQL.
- A custom cluster parameter group that adds pgaudit and pg_cron to the existing shared_preload_libraries value (append to it rather than replacing it, so defaults such as pg_stat_statements are preserved. This requires a cluster restart). Set cron.database_name to your target database.
- Basic familiarity with PostgreSQL, SQL, and Python.
Note: The prerequisites listed here focus on the database layer. Your application layer (for example, AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and a chat UI) is separate and depends on your deployment architecture.
Design patterns for the Explainability dimension
This section presents the database-layer design patterns that make every AI-generated response traceable, from the user query, through retrieval and guardrail evaluation, to the final answer and its citations.
Step 1: Set up the database schema
Create the core tables for customer data, chat sessions, interaction logging, and feedback:
Start by creating the schema and the tables you need. Each table serves a specific Responsible AI dimension:
The customers table stores profiles for tenant-aware access control:
The chat_interactions table is the core of the Explainability implementation. It logs every query-response cycle with full RAG provenance, including retrieved chunk IDs, similarity scores, cited versus retrieved sources, guardrail traces, and the model used:
Because chat_interactions stores raw request_text and response_text, protect it the same way as the source data: redact PII before the INSERT (reusing the ingestion-time guardrail), or encrypt those columns with pgcrypto, and apply Row-Level Security to the log tables so tenants cannot read each other’s interactions. Logging unprotected customer content would undercut the Privacy and Security control this design is meant to demonstrate.
The chat_feedback table captures user ratings and comments on chatbot responses, which supports the Controllability dimension. The ON DELETE CASCADE clause makes sure the 90-day retention purge does not fail with foreign key violations:
Step 2: Prepare the knowledge base with pgvector and Aurora ML
Create the retrieval layer with vector embeddings, tenant isolation, and Aurora ML integration:
Create an HNSW index for fast approximate nearest neighbor search:
Enforce tenant isolation with Row-Level Security so that vector search results are scoped to the current tenant before data leaves the database:
Generate vector embeddings directly from SQL using Aurora ML, keeping the embedding pipeline inside the database layer:
Always redact PII before inserting data into the knowledge base. Use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails (the ApplyGuardrail API) or Amazon Comprehend (the detect_pii_entities API) to identify and mask PII in your ingestion pipeline, as shown in the following example:
Step 3: Retrieve context and generate responses
When a query reaches your application layer, retrieve the top matching knowledge chunks using the pgvector cosine similarity operator. The following SQL query shows this pattern:
Note: The 0.7 cosine-similarity cutoff drops weakly related chunks so the model is not grounded on noise. Tune it against your own data. The category filter and this threshold both post-filter HNSW results and may return fewer than 5 rows. Raise hnsw.ef_search or use iterative index scans (pgvector 0.8.0+) to compensate.
The following pseudocode shows the key patterns for contextual grounding, guardrail-intervention handling, citation parsing, and interaction logging. The snippets focus on the Responsible AI logic rather than application plumbing.
Use guardContent blocks to enable contextual grounding in the Bedrock Converse API:
Check stopReason to handle cases where the guardrail blocks the response:
Distinguish actually cited sources from all retrieved sources. On an Explainability post, this distinction is the point:
Log every interaction for Explainability. The INSERT captures the full RAG provenance chain:
We define confidence_score as the mean cosine similarity of the top-k retrieved chunks. The intent field classifies the query (for example, billing or order_status), and response_latency_ms records end-to-end inference time.
Step 4: Log interactions and add governance
Every chatbot interaction (the user query, retrieved chunks, similarity scores, response, and citations) is logged to the chat_interactions table using the INSERT shown in Step 3, supporting Explainability and Transparency. Customer feedback captured in chat_feedback supports continuous improvement, reinforcing Controllability. For Governance, pgaudit provides query audit trails, and pg_cron drives automated data retention.
Set up pgaudit and pg_cron, which both require shared_preload_libraries (see Prerequisites):
Query for governance review:
Archive both tables to Amazon S3 and purge only after the export succeeds. Running archive and purge as two independent cron jobs is unsafe: if the archive fails, a separately scheduled purge still deletes the rows. Wrap both in one function so the DELETE runs only when the export returns. Also archive chat_feedback, because the cascade would otherwise delete feedback that was not saved. The 90-day window matches a typical support-data retention policy. Adjust it to your own regulatory requirements.
Validate the solution
Run one question end to end, then read the row it produced. That single row is the evidence the design works: it shows which chunks were retrieved, how similar they were, which sources the answer actually cited, and the guardrail outcome.
Expected: One row whose cited_sources is a subset of retrieved_chunk_ids, similarity_scores at or above your 0.7 threshold, and a guardrail_action of NONE for a clean question. If cited_sources is empty, the model did not ground its answer and the response should be treated with caution.
Limitations and considerations
- Amazon Bedrock Guardrails adds latency to each inference call and incurs per-text-unit charges. Contextual grounding has additional pricing. Benchmark your response times and costs before production deployment.
- Interaction logging grows storage over time. The S3 archival and purge cron jobs help manage this, but monitor your Aurora storage and adjust the retention period as needed.
- HNSW indexes provide approximate nearest neighbor search. Post-filtering (for example, by category or tenant) runs after the index scan and may return fewer rows than your LIMIT. Increase hnsw.ef_search or use iterative index scans (pgvector 0.8.0+) to improve recall.
- The contextual grounding check evaluates whether the model’s response is grounded in the provided context. It does not guarantee factual accuracy of the source documents themselves.
- Aurora ML embedding generation runs synchronously in the database. For large batch ingestion, consider batching updates or using an asynchronous pipeline.
- Everything in this post except Aurora ML (the aws_bedrock.invoke_model_get_embeddings calls) works on Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for PostgreSQL as well.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, delete the following resources if you created them for this walkthrough:
- Unschedule the cron job first, or it fails nightly once the schema is gone: SELECT cron.unschedule('archive_and_purge');.
- Drop the schema: DROP SCHEMA rai_postgresql CASCADE;.
- Delete the Amazon Bedrock Guardrail.
- Remove the AWS Lambda functions and API Gateway endpoints.
- Delete the Amazon S3 audit bucket (or configure a lifecycle policy).
- Delete the Aurora PostgreSQL cluster (or stop it if you plan to reuse it).
- Remove IAM roles created for Bedrock and Aurora ML integration.
- Drop the application role (roles are not removed by DROP SCHEMA): DROP ROLE app_user;.
Cost considerations: This solution uses Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon Bedrock (model inference and embeddings), and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Costs vary by Region, instance size, request volume, and model choice. For pricing details, see the pricing pages for each service.
Conclusion
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition, with pgvector, Row-Level Security, pgaudit, pgcrypto, pg_cron, and Aurora ML, provides database-layer building blocks for Responsible AI. Several dimensions also depend on AWS services outside the database, as the mapping table shows.
In this post, we focused on the Explainability dimension as a detailed design walkthrough. By logging retrieved chunk IDs, similarity scores, cited sources, and guardrail traces in Aurora, you get a queryable audit trail at the database layer. The mapping table shows how the remaining dimensions build on the same foundation, combining Aurora PostgreSQL features with AWS AI services.
The key takeaways from these design patterns are:
- Log retrieval provenance at query time: retrieved and cited chunk IDs, similarity scores, and the guardrail trace.
- Distinguish the sources actually cited from everything retrieved. That distinction is what makes an answer explainable.
- Enforce tenant isolation with Row-Level Security, and set the tenant context before a vector search runs.
- Archive audit data before purging, and protect the log tables as carefully as the source data.
As a next step, explore Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, the fully managed RAG capability that now supports Aurora PostgreSQL as a vector store in many AWS Regions and provides built-in citation generation, which can help reduce the custom integration code required for Explainability in new projects.

articles.title: La cause du grave échec de la fusée Vulcan Centaur est presque une bonne nouvelle pour Blue Origin
articles.text:
United Launch Alliance commence à y voir plus clair sur son gros raté du 15 novembre. Dans une mise à jour publiée le 18 sur son blog, la coentreprise formée par Boeing et Lockheed Martin pense que la défaillance réside entre le premier étage de la fusée Vulcan Centaur et les moteurs BE-4, qui n’ont pas été suffisamment alimentés.
ULA met donc hors de cause, pour l’instant, les moteurs eux-mêmes. Le problème se situe plus en amont, dans l’alimentation en carburant. Pour Blue Origin, la société spatiale de Jeff Bezos, la nouvelle tombe bien : elle fabrique ces moteurs et en utilise sept sur le premier étage de sa propre fusée, New Glenn. Un défaut dessus l’aurait handicapée par ricochet.
Selon les premières analyses d’ULA, les moteurs de la fusée Vulcan Centaur n’ont pas reçu assez de carburant au décollage. Faute de poussée suffisante, la fusée n’a pas atteint l’altitude et la vitesse nécessaires pour la suite de la mission. Celle-ci consistait à lancer 40 satellites au profit de la constellation Amazon Leo.
Créée en 2006, ULA n’avait encore jamais perdu une mission entière. Elle avait certes rencontré des échecs partiels, mais jamais de loupé aussi grave. Par ailleurs, le raté du 15 novembre constitue la toute première sortie de piste de la fusée Vulcan Centaur, qui n’en est qu’à son cinquième vol depuis ses débuts en janvier 2024.
Un second étage incapable de rattraper le retard
ULA avait déjà raconté les grandes lignes du vol ce mardi 17 novembre, en détaillant ce qui semblait avoir fonctionné et ce qui avait déraillé. Juste après le décollage, la fusée a manqué de poussée. Le premier étage s’est donc séparé du second trop bas, et à une vitesse trop faible pour atteindre l’orbite.
Le second étage, appelé Centaur, a pourtant démarré normalement, et ses moteurs RL10 ont fonctionné comme prévu. Il n’a toutefois pas pu rattraper le retard pris au départ. ULA a perdu le contact avec la fusée une dizaine de minutes après le décollage. L’échec n’a été confirmé qu’à ce moment-là.
Les six propulseurs d’appoint à poudre, fixés sur les flancs de la fusée, ont eux aussi bien fonctionné. Leurs tuyères (c’est-à-dire la partie évasée par où sortent les gaz) avaient été modifiées pour ce vol, après un incident sur l’un des propulseurs lors du vol précédent, le 12 février. Ce problème avait cloué Vulcan au sol pendant neuf mois.
La coentreprise n’explique pas encore pourquoi le carburant, du méthane liquide, n’est pas arrivé en quantité suffisante jusqu’aux moteurs. ULA mène l’enquête sous la supervision de la FAA, l’autorité américaine de l’aviation civile, qui devra valider le rapport final et les corrections.

articles.title: Starship est déjà la plus grande fusée du monde, sa prochaine itération sera encore plus gigantesque
articles.text:
Après l’exploit de la récupération du second étage de Starship, Elon Musk pense déjà à la suite. La prochaine version de sa mégafusée sera encore plus grande, et définitivement plus puissante.
Car le 15e vol de Starship a marqué un véritable tournant pour SpaceX, même si le booster Super Heavy a dû abandonner sa tentative de retour et a fini sa course dans le golfe du Mexique. Car le Ship, c’est-à-dire le second étage, est revenu se loger dans les bras mécaniques de la tour de lancement après avoir réalisé 14 tours de la Terre. Au passage, il a largué 26 satellites Starlink V3 en orbite. Un succès immense pour ce colosse de 124 mètres, voué à devenir encore plus grand.
De 124 à 150 mètres
Dans une publication sur X.com, Elon Musk a en effet levé le voile sur la future version de sa fusée, la V4. Si l’on connaissait certains détails, l’homme le plus riche du monde a été encore plus loin. « Le Starship V4 mesurera environ 70 mètres, soit environ 40 % de longueur en plus, ce qui permet d’embarquer plus de 60 % de propergols supplémentaires », a-t-il indiqué. Il mesure aujourd’hui 52 mètres.
Ainsi, cette nouvelle itération atteindrait à peu près la taille d’un Falcon 9 complet. Et il sera également mieux armé : « Le nombre de moteurs sera porté à 9 (Ndlr : contre 6 aujourd’hui), avec trois moteurs Raptor Vacuum supplémentaires, et il s’agira de moteurs V4 à plus forte poussée », a-t-il précisé, en référence à la version des moteurs optimisée pour le vide spatial.
Au final, cette montée en gamme devrait donner naissance à un très beau bébé de 150 mètres environ, estime l’entrepreneur. C’est légèrement moins de la moitié de la tour Eiffel.
Direction la Lune
Outre la capacité à emporter des charges encore plus lourdes, c’est aussi le programme Artemis qui est en jeu. Car avant d’acheminer des astronautes sur la Lune, Starship devra faire le plein en orbite grâce à une série de vaisseaux-ravitailleurs. Avec la V4, capable selon Musk de livrer plus de 200 tonnes de propergols à chaque vol, le plein se ferait même en 5 ou 6 lancements.
Autre bonne nouvelle pour SpaceX : le second étage semble en plutôt bon état. » Dans l’ensemble, il a l’air super. Les moteurs aussi », a écrit le milliardaire, estimant qu’il pourrait voler à nouveau après « quelques semaines » de remise en état. C’est une condition sine qua non afin d’atteindre les objectifs de l’entreprise. Starship devra, à terme, être lancée plusieurs fois par jour.
Mais la route est encore longue, car elle doit désormais réussir à récupérer ses deux étages lors du même vol.
