articles.title: Un paso más en la sustitución de artistas por avatares digitales: Antonio Roma no existe pero va a dar un concierto en Madrid
articles.text:
Es el primer cantante de flamenco hecho con IA que se sube a un escenario en España. Dicho así, suena a sinsentido, pero es que éste concretamente viene acompañado de alguien de carne y hueso que le pone voz y una banda real que tocará su música. Una curiosa vía intermedia que, sin duda, no elimina la gran duda que flota sobre toda esta nueva generación de artistas virtuales sobre si van a sustituir a los músicos tradicionales.
Medio aforo ya. El 3 de febrero de 2027, a las 21:00, la sala Galileo Galilei de Madrid programa un concierto del artista generado con IA Antonio Roma, con entradas a 25 euros. Ya se han vendido más de la mitad de las casi 500 localidades que tiene de aforo la sala. Es el último jalón en una carrera fulgurante: a mediados de noviembre, tres meses después de aparecer, ya sumaba más de 100.000 oyentes mensuales en Spotify, 350.000 seguidores en Instagram y dos videoclips por encima del millón de reproducciones en YouTube. Su primer álbum, de ocho canciones, salió el 21 de agosto, y el 11 de septiembre ya tenía el siguiente. El propio avatar dice que “Antonio Roma no es humano, es un concepto”.
Junior. A Antonio Roma le pondrá voz Diego Amador Jr., sevillano de 33 años, hijo del multiinstrumentista Diego Amador y sobrino de Raimundo Amador, cofundador de Pata Negra. Criptik Sound, creadores de Roma, dio con él por una story de Instagram después de que otros artistas rechazaran el encargo. Saldrá al escenario sin hologramas, y el evento se plantea como un puente para que el público escuche "un poco más a Junior, y más flamenco". En Instagram no llega a 15.000 seguidores, por comparar con el personaje.
Dramatis personae. La sala titula el evento “Antonio Roma en concierto | Interpretado por Diego Amador Jr.” y no escribe en ningún momento “inteligencia artificial”: describe el proyecto como “nacido con ayuda de la tecnología”. Todo se aproxima bastante a un cartel casi de teatro, con Amador Jr. como un actor que da vida a un personaje. Es el único nombre humano del cartel, en una especie de inversión de la polémica de Milli Vanilli: aquí la voz es sintética y el cuerpo de verdad.
Los críptidos. Detrás de todo esto está Criptik Sound, un sello fundado este año por tres colombianos que hacían en el pasado estrategia digital para Lola Índigo o Aitana. Tiene 14 empleados y 15 artistas generados con IA, e ingresan entre 30.000 y 50.000 dólares por trimestre. Sus responsables dicen que escriben letras y melodías y que la máquina “musicaliza”, y venden el modelo como una forma de evitar “la extinción de géneros como el flamenco”, al que según ellos las grandes discográficas ya no dedican dinero.
Versión original. Criptik asegura que se opone a los conciertos sin personas y que, como se ahorra estudio, grabación y mezcla, quiere pagar bien a quienes suban al escenario: Amador Jr. y sus cuatro músicos. Medios como Hipersónica lo han visto de otra manera: el flamenco no está en peligro, el negocio encaja en la figura del “rentista de la música” y lo triste es que un cantaor tenga que disfrazarse de su copia para que lo escuchen.
La riada. En noviembre, Deezer recibía casi 90.000 pistas íntegramente generadas por IA al día, más de la mitad de lo que le llega en los días de pico, y el 57% de los más de 53.000 usuarios que se pasaron a la plataforma en octubre traía al menos una en sus listas. Apenas se escuchan: en abril suponían entre el 1% y el 3% de las reproducciones. Antonio Roma es de la minoría con público real, como The Velvet Sundown o Ruby Black, la cantante sintética que, cuando hablamos de ella en mayo, sacaba single cada jueves y encabezaba las listas algorítmicas de Spotify en España.
Sin algoritmo. A esa minoría Spotify le ha ido cerrando puertas. En abril la dejó fuera de su distintivo de verificación, un poco un empezar la casa por el tejado. En agosto anunció la etiqueta "AI Persona" para los perfiles cuyo nombre e imagen parezcan identidades fotorrealistas creadas con IA, empezando por los que superan ciertos umbrales de audiencia. La plataforma hace que dejen de aparecer en las listas de la plataforma y en lo que sugiere el algoritmo, y solo los encuentra quien ya los sigue. Sin el algoritmo de su parte, una sala con músicos de verdad es de las pocas promociones que le quedan a un personaje hecho con IA, así que muy posiblemente veamos en el futuro más experimentos en vivo como este de Antonio Roma.
La factura. La CISAC calculaba en diciembre de 2024 que la IA generativa ponía en riesgo el 24% de los ingresos de los autores musicales en 2028, con una pérdida acumulada de 10.000 millones de euros en cinco años. Para entonces, la música sintética rondaría el 20% de lo que facturan las plataformas de streaming y el 60% de lo que ingresan las bibliotecas musicales. Cifras que, llevadas a lo práctico, dejan una pregunta en el aire sobre el consumo de música en redes: ¿se sigue a quien canta o a la cara no existente que sale en el vídeo?

articles.title: Ukraine, FBI arrest ransomware gang members tied to $40M in ransoms
articles.text:
Ukrainian authorities, working with the FBI, have arrested four suspected members of an international ransomware organization linked to more than $40.5 million in ransom payments from at least 28 companies worldwide.
The arrests come after a two-year investigation into a cybercrime organization comprising at least 27 individuals from Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Russia, and other countries.
Investigators say the organization was connected to a larger cybercrime network of more than 60 members operating across eight jurisdictions, including former members of the notorious Conti ransomware gang.
According to Ukraine's National Police, the group targeted organizations in the oil and gas, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, logistics, and financial sectors, as well as critical infrastructure.
The attackers researched their victims' financial standing, assets, employees, and IT vulnerabilities before launching attacks designed to steal corporate data, encrypt systems, and extort cryptocurrency payments.
Speaking in an exclusive interview with Ukrainian news outlet Censor.NET, acting National Police chief Maksym Tsutskiridze said investigators had identified at least 28 companies that paid more than $40.5 million in ransoms.
"We have identified at least 28 companies that transferred more than $40.5 million in ransom payments to the hackers, equivalent to approximately UAH 1.8 billion. This is money that has already been paid. We are still establishing the full extent of the damage," Tsutskiridze said.
In one attack, the hackers stole 1.4 terabytes of data from a U.S. company and expanded their attack to other companies within the same corporate group.
The attackers initially demanded $10 million but ultimately received $5 million after negotiations.
As first reported by French cybersecurity news outlet LeMagIT, Ukrainian court records identify several victims of the criminal organization, including Warren Oil Company, Maxxis International-USA, Newpark Resources, and Quantum Health.
The court documents identify Warren Oil Company as the victim of an August 2024 attack in which hackers copied 1.4 TB of data before receiving an 84.5 BTC ransom payment, equivalent to approximately $5 million at the time.
The records also allege that Newpark Resources paid $1.5 million in December 2024, while Quantum Health paid $5 million in June 2026 following an initial $15 million ransom demand.
LeMagIT also noted that the BlackSuit ransomware gang claimed Maxxis International as a victim in November 2024, while Ukrainian court records identify Chaos as the ransomware used by the criminal organization.
The Conti ransomware operation shut down in May 2022, with its members dispersing into smaller ransomware gangs and other cybercrime operations.
One of the groups linked to former Conti members was BlackSuit, which initially operated as Quantum ransomware in January 2022 before becoming Royal.
In June 2023, Royal began operating under the BlackSuit name after testing a new encryptor and carrying out high-profile attacks, including one against the City of Dallas, Texas.
However, Ukrainian authorities have not identified the four arrested suspects as former Conti members or confirmed their individual affiliations with BlackSuit or Chaos.
AI-powered IT support impersonation
To breach corporate networks, the cybercriminals impersonated IT support personnel and used a custom-developed platform with AI-generated voice messages to automate fraudulent phone calls.
During these calls, they tricked employees into disclosing login credentials or installing remote-access software, allowing the attackers to access internal corporate systems.
In one documented incident, an attacker kept an employee on the phone while another attacker accessed the company's systems, with the call ending only after the attackers confirmed the intrusion was successful.
"They created their own platform featuring voice messages generated by artificial intelligence. They called company employees, posing as IT support specialists. Under the pretext of providing technical assistance, they persuaded employees to disclose their login credentials or install remote access software. This allowed them to gain access to corporate networks," Tsutskiridze explained.
The Ukrainian court records provide additional insight into these attacks, describing how the hackers used phishing pages impersonating corporate VPN services, spoofed phone numbers, and remote-access tools such as TeamViewer and AnyDesk.
During the Warren Oil Company attack, the records allege that the attackers tricked an employee into entering credentials on a phishing page, then obtained a two-factor authentication code that granted them remote access to the corporate network.
Once inside the network, the attackers stole sensitive information and encrypted files using ransomware, disrupting the victim's operations.
The gang then demanded cryptocurrency payments in exchange for restoring access to encrypted systems while threatening to publicly release stolen corporate data.
"They would deprive a company of access to its own data and then demand millions of dollars in exchange for decrypting it. At the same time, they threatened to publish the stolen information. Victims were put under pressure from both sides, forcing them to pay the ransom in cryptocurrency," Tsutskiridze said.
Ukrainian authorities conducted 66 simultaneous searches across Kyiv and 11 regions of Ukraine as part of the joint operation with U.S. law enforcement. Four suspected key members of the organization were detained, although authorities did not disclose their exact arrest locations.
During these searches, investigators seized computers, mobile phones, bank cards, nearly $370,000 in cash, and €20,000.
Four alleged key members of the organization were formally notified of suspicion and are currently in custody.
The suspects face charges related to participating in a criminal organization and unauthorized interference with information systems under Ukrainian law. If convicted, they face up to 15 years in prison.
Ukrainian authorities say the investigation is ongoing as law enforcement works to identify additional members of the international network and determine their involvement in other cyberattacks.
The National Police also released a video showing footage from the investigation, including law enforcement raids, seized cash, interviews with investigators, and a suspect being questioned.
The video also contains audio from an alleged ransomware extortion call demanding $15 million after claiming to have stolen more than 1.5 TB of corporate data.

articles.title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
articles.text:
After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms.
When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed.
Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked.
“Hmmm,” one Meta staffer wrote in an instance where Muse sent the definition of “money laundering” unbidden. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for… .”
In at least one case, Muse told a staffer surprised by a similarly out-of-context offer to message a seller about a coffee table that it had “pulled in some context about a coffee table pickup that doesn’t seem to be yours.”
According to Reuters, that employee flagged the troubling output, writing, “this was ‘not my conversation’” and “expressing concern about a ‘possible cross-account context leak.’”
Raising the most concern were random outputs that appeared to share private user data. For example, a perplexed Meta staffer chatting with Muse about fishing got a random extra response, seemingly sharing balances from two unknown bank accounts. That output said, “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”
At least one staffer said they lost money testing Muse, Reuters reported. That staffer reported that Muse “accidentally rolled me into a premium insurance plan” for their dog that charged them $888 per month instead of their prior rate of $200. “Couldn’t recover,” the staffer said.
Meta’s spokesperson, Daniel Roberts, told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents,” and internally employees were told that “the agent appeared to be hallucinating messages in response to built-in prompts pushing it to engage with users in between sessions.” In those cases, an AI team member said the hallucinations were “unfortunately” biased “towards the most uncomfortable topics, like finances/security/safety, which sucks.” In some cases, instead of bank details, Muse hallucinated bitcoin balances, the team member said.
A Meta spokesperson told Ars that “employee testing is core to the product development process and the entire point is to get feedback, so we can implement safety and privacy protections and improve products. Importantly, employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.”
Speaking to Reuters, Roberts reiterated that “many of the messages flagged by employees as potential account mix-ups were hallucinations” that Meta had already addressed.
But Roberts declined to respond to Reuters’ questions on the prevalence or persistence of the issues the AI team member discussed. And Reuters’ report emphasized that the outlet independently was “unable to establish whether Muse was giving users other people’s bank account balances and other sensitive data, or making up the information.”
Muse issues arose soon after September launch
Meta started receiving privacy-related complaints from Muse users in September. An Inc. Magazine reporter, Jason Aten, was shocked when it became clear that Muse was digging through private messages on his Mac without permission, reporting that he instead “explicitly” chose to deny Muse that access. As Meta delayed responding, the agent claimed it was simply parsing text in push notifications, but Aten found that “wasn’t true.” Rather, the agent was syncing messages from a local database, which Aten said was activated without his knowledge.
Eventually, a Meta spokesperson, David Singleton, responded to Aten on social media. Singleton insisted that Aten must have opted into granting “macOS system-level Full Disk Access” with the “Messages connector” enabled, if Muse was reading his private messages.
But Aten said the response wasn’t good enough.
“Email me, David,” Aten responded. “Full Disk Access off. Muse synced 187k lines from my messages chat [database]. Something’s not great. Also, that Full Disk Access doesn’t say anything about your message database, and I specifically gave Muse a goal that had nothing to do with messages, so it had no business doing that even if I had given it permission.”
Around the same time, Singleton responded to another user warning that his Muse appeared to be hacked. In that case, the user said that Muse tried to access an email service after claiming the user asked it to.
“I didn’t even open the app today at all,” the user wrote, vowing to delete the app and report it to Apple. “This is crazy.”
In a lengthy response providing more technical details, Singleton confirmed that Meta had received “a few reports” of such cases “where people thought their Muse was hallucinating or leaking other people’s data.” As he explained, the issues arose after Meta deployed an update giving Muse instructions on “how to engage with the user and ask them for confirmation before taking specific actions.”
It seems those instructions “landed on every message, not just messages pertaining to those specific actions, so its impact was wider than intended,” Singleton said. Also: “the way this instruction was provided to the model was done in a way that the model was not expecting (i.e. was not trained to expect).”
“We investigated with urgency and determined that this was caused by a bug introduced in the product that caused the model to hallucinate and was NOT a security or privacy issue,” Singleton wrote. “The bug has now been fixed.”
Aten warned that even though you can’t rely on Muse to explain its own behavior, the agent’s response coupled with Meta’s did little to rebuild trust after the shocking intrusion into his private messages.
“If we grant Singleton’s premise that I managed to unknowingly click something that enabled this capability, I still think that’s really bad,” Aten wrote. “You should not design your system in a way that people end up surprised by this kind of thing.” And if you do, you should not make “user control the central pitch” for marketing Muse, Aten suggested.
“If an AI agent is going to read my private messages, there should be a moment when it clearly asks me whether that’s okay,” Aten wrote.
Reuters warned Signal intrusions are ongoing
Since Muse launched in September, it has been downloaded more than 10 million times, tapping Meta’s vast user network to quickly become one of the most-used AI agent tools.
But staffers warned Meta that users may be blindsided by some actions the agents take, depending on the operating system the app is connected to. For example, one staffer was surprised to find that “Muse was set up by default with permission to access push notifications on phones with Google’s Android operating system.” That, too, gave access to private message preview text the staffer had not intended for the agent’s review.
Meta says that Muse users can trust the company to keep their data private. It also warns users that Muse can make mistakes, while building into its terms that users are responsible for actions taken by Muse (like maybe buying things you don’t want or making doctor’s appointments you don’t need). The tech giant said it’s continuously updating user protections, conducting internal testing, and prioritizing user safety.
However, Reuters worked with staff at Signal and the AI Now Institute to test if they could replicate that Meta staffer’s and others’ Muse experiences. On Android devices, they found that Muse could read Signal messages by bypassing Meta’s “Connector” tool and instead relying on permissions granted during initial setup.
On iPhone, requests were blocked, Reuters reported. But on Apple’s macOS, Muse repurposed “settings Apple offers to help people with disabilities operate their computers” to retrieve messages, including screenshot tools.
That testing “indicated the issue described by the Meta employees was ongoing and could be affecting others,” Reuters reported. Overall, Meta seemed to be interpreting permissions from Muse users “broadly,” Reuters concluded, in ways that privacy advocates and regulators may disagree with.
Signal President Meredith Whittaker told Reuters that Meta launched Muse “without showing any respect for basic privacy or cybersecurity.” She demanded that Meta make changes to give app developers like Signal “consistent technical ways” to “mark their applications as off-limits to AI agents,” Reuters reported.
Part of that change would require operating systems to enforce rules that app developers set to rope off AI agents from sensitive data, Whittaker suggested. And following Reuters’ reporting, both Apple and Google are already weighing potential changes to “give people more control over what they authorize with AI agents.”
Apple, in particular, seemed disturbed by how Muse may be manipulating accessibility tools for people with disabilities. In October, Apple had already announced changes coming in response to users complaining about Muse accessing private messages without their knowledge or explicit consent. At that time, Apple concluded that “some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk.” And they promised to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”
“We are committed to ensuring users understand exactly what they are allowing, so they can make informed choices about their data and privacy,” Apple said.
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Mon Espace Santé et le DMP tournent désormais sur une seule plateforme, hébergée en France par Atos
articles.text:
Atos a annoncé le 17 novembre avoir achevé la reprise de la gestion et de la sécurisation du Dossier Médical Partagé, ainsi que son intégration à Mon Espace Santé, pour le compte de l’Assurance Maladie. Le groupement formé avec Accenture, dont l’entreprise française est mandataire, gère et héberge l’ensemble dans ses centres de données en France. Le communiqué décrit une infrastructure « sécurisée et souveraine », ouverte à plus de 60 millions d’assurés.
Un déménagement joué depuis juin 2025
Les deux services vivaient déjà ensemble à l’écran : depuis 2022, chaque profil Mon Espace Santé contient le dossier médical partagé, héritier d’un chantier public ouvert au milieu des années 2000. En coulisses, chacun gardait pourtant sa propre infrastructure, et le DMP restait exploité par son opérateur historique.
La bascule est intervenue le week-end des 7 et 8 juin 2025, quand le DMP a rejoint l’architecture de Mon Espace Santé. L’opération s’est accompagnée d’une coupure programmée, le dossier médical restant indisponible du samedi 21 h au dimanche 20 h, et Mon Espace Santé rouvrant par étapes après maintenance. Les éditeurs de logiciels médicaux avaient ouvert la voie, leurs accès ayant basculé vers le nouvel environnement dès le 10 mars.
L’accord-cadre qui porte l’opération court du 6 mai 2024 au 5 mai 2028, pour une valeur totale estimée à 466,7 millions d’euros hors taxes. Il couvre aussi la poursuite de la gestion et des évolutions de Mon Espace Santé, déployé par Atos en 2022, et l’entreprise chiffre à plus de 300 experts l’effectif mobilisé sur la reprise.
Qu’est-ce qui change dans votre quotidien ?
Les habitudes restent les mêmes des deux côtés de l’écran : Mon Espace Santé demeure le service des patients, le DMP le point d’entrée des professionnels de santé. Ces derniers l’alimentent et le consultent depuis leur logiciel métier. Certains documents produits dans Amelipro, arrêts de travail en tête, s’y versent d’ailleurs automatiquement depuis le 24 mars 2026, et les comptes rendus bucco-dentaires suivent le même circuit depuis le 1er avril 2025. Résultats d’examens, ordonnances et comptes rendus hospitaliers continuent de s’y ranger au fil des soins.
Atos avance près de 28 millions de comptes activés, plus de 40 millions de documents déposés chaque mois et un rythme d’environ 130 000 nouveaux usagers par semaine. Le dernier décompte public, dressé fin janvier par l’Assurance Maladie, recensait 24 millions de profils activés et 2,5 millions d’utilisateurs mensuels. Les dépôts atteignaient alors 420 millions de documents sur l’année 2025, pour un parc frôlant l’exhaustivité : 97 % de la population dispose d’un profil, créé d’office sauf opposition.
La feuille de route officielle vise 40 millions de citoyens ayant activé et utilisé le service d’ici fin 2027. L’infrastructure est donc une affaire réglée, mais il reste l’usage : 69 millions de profils créés, 28 millions activés pour seulement 2,5 millions de visiteurs mensuels. C’est là que 2027 devra faire bouger les lignes.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella remains confident in Nvidia after Huang’s exit | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella weighed in on former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unexpected departure amid a series of shocking controversies.
“It’s all sort of pretty tragic in the sense of, you know, Jensen is somebody I’ve known for a long time. I’ve admired what he’s done, and at this point, I kind of want to give him space to figure this out,” Nadella said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.
Huang stepped down last week from his CEO role, which he has held for 33 years. Huang’s leadership has been central to Nvidia’s ascent to one of the world’s most valuable companies, but his judgment was questioned after it was reported that he had an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy feeding information back to Beijing. It was also revealed that Huang was having affairs with two Nvidia employees, including one who was a direct report.
While the world waits to see what the long-term economic impacts of Huang’s departure might be, Nadella says he still has confidence in Nvidia, which is a close partner of Microsoft.
“I’ll just say this one thing,” Nadella added. “Colette [Kress, interim CEO at Nvidia] worked at Microsoft for a long time. I’ve known her for a long time. She’s a tremendous person… I’m in touch with the same set of people I was in touch with before [Huang left], so I have a lot of confidence in the Nvidia team and their ability to continue to do the good work.”
Microsoft is not unlike Nvidia in that its founder Bill Gates inhabited a larger-than-life persona as CEO.
“Founders are unbelievable in the sense that they create something from nothing, so that is pretty magical… They’re singular, but they’re not gods, right?” Nadella said. “I used to say to Bill [Gates]… Founders also die, and so at some point, a company, if it needs to succeed, it has to have someone take over.”

articles.title: AI finds Java flaw exposing banks, hospitals and companies
articles.text:
AI has discovered an issue with Java that leaves many companies and other institutions vulnerable.
Using OpenAI’s still-not-public GPT-6 Cyber model, cybersecurity startup Calif found a string of “A” characters followed by an equals sign. While this normally leads to a crash, bad actors can leverage this to gain full unauthorized access to a device.
This is particular dangerous since Java is a ubiquitous programming language used by 90 per cent of Fortune 500 companies, including Amazon and Apple, as well as U.S. banks like J.P. Morgan Chase and the Bank of America and even hospitals.
Calif, for its part, says it’s not easy to use the bug for malicious purposes. Still, it’s an understandably big concern, and the agency says it’s been coordinating with associates in U.S., Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Britain accordingly. Oracle, which owns Java, hasn’t issues a public statement on the matter. Instead, it quietly rolled out a software patch on Tuesday.
This is the latest in a lineup of high-profile tech failures. Last week, Microsoft services like Outlook and Teams weren’t working for many people, which the company attributed to a “latent defect” from a server fix. The same week, U.S. airlines were grounded for hours due to air traffic control system errors.
Naturally, this has led experts to scrutinize the increasing role of AI in both tech businesses and those behind cyberattacks.

articles.title: Memory bottlenecks in AI: How photonics and shared pools help - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI’s hidden energy tax: More than 80% of scale-up traffic is just memory moving around
Memory bottlenecks are emerging as one of the costliest problems in AI infrastructure as inference overtakes training. GPUs sit idle waiting on data, while high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, stays bolted to processors that cannot share it.
Photonics is shaping up as one way out. Marvell Technology Inc. has been pairing optics with photonic memory to stretch memory beyond the edge of a chip. The payoff is better efficiency in data centers enterprises have already paid for, according to Preet Virk (pictured, left), senior vice president and general manager of the Photonic Fabric Business Unit at Marvell.
“In the data center today, we have a lot of room for improvement of efficiency,” Virk said. “And when I say efficiency, I’m alluding to the wasted flops because we have GPU utilization that’s very low.”
Virk and Andy Mills (right), vice president of advanced product development at Penguin Solutions Inc., spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Amit Eyal Govrin at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how photonics and shared memory pools can ease memory bottlenecks in AI infrastructure. (* Disclosure below.)
Shared pools take aim at memory bottlenecks
Penguin’s MemoryAI Photonic Appliance moves HBM into a separate box tens of meters from the GPU, linked by Marvell’s Photonic Fabric. Each appliance holds 16 terabytes of HBM and DDR5 memory that servers across multiple racks can share, Mills explained.
“The challenge there is making sure your LLM doesn’t forget what you started talking to it about 10 minutes ago,” Mills said. “To do that, you need a large amount of memory, large token lengths.”
Optics also changes the energy math. Copper still works inside a rack, but crossing a pod of thousands of GPUs requires optics, according to Virk. More than 80 percent of scale-up network traffic is memory transactions, and a shared pool means much of that data never moves at all, he noted.
“Within data movement, the memory transactions are a place to focus on,” Virk said. “So with this solution versus a copper-based data movement, we could immediately get to a quarter of the energy, picojoules per bit, of data movement.”
Agents raise the stakes, generating far more token requests than human users ever did. As inference spreads across more racks and sites, Mills sees shared pools as the practical answer to memory bottlenecks.
“If anything, distributed encourages shared because you don’t want to recompute,” Mills said. “The whole thing about KV cache was a huge success because it stops recomputation of the same data. And when you can share that data on a broader base and wider across more racks, your efficiencies go up as well.”

articles.title: Surfshark's proprietary 'Dausos' protocol now powers automatic connections on Mac
articles.text:
Surfshark's proprietary 'Dausos' protocol now powers automatic connections on Mac
Surfshark macOS app can now automatically connect to Dausos when it’s the best option
- Surfshark adds its proprietary Dausos protocol as the default option on Mac
- The app can now automatically connect to Dausos when it’s the best option
- The news comes a little over seven months after Surfshark released Dausos
Surfshark’s proprietary Dausos protocol will now be the default option for macOS users.
In an attempt to provide the best VPN possible for its customers, Surfshark explains that users can now automatically connect to Dausos when it's the best available protocol for their connection without having to do it themselves.
In a statement, Surfshark said: "Instead of manually switching between protocols, the app does the work for you — testing, adapting, and choosing the fastest and most stable option in real time."
Surfshark – the best cheap VPN
Surfshark is a fast, easy-to-use VPN that seriously beats the competition when it comes to subscription pricing. Its two-year Starter plan works out at $2.49 a month (plus tax), but we think Surfshark One is the best value plan as it adds an antivirus, data breach monitor, alternative ID, and now new anti-scam tools. All of this starting from the equivalent of  just $2.79 a month. 
What this update means for you
Surfshark launched Dausos in April this year.
The company claims the protocol is both up to 30 per cent faster than its rivals and it also works "dynamically" to match network conditions. This means that, at least in theory, it should keep performing at its optimal speed regardless of whether the connection is WiFi, fibre broadband, or mobile.
Dausos also includes post-quantum encryption protections to protect users from future threats.
As Surfshark explains, by adding Dausos as an automatic connection protocol, it makes it easier for users to benefit from these advantages without needing to understand the technical differences.
"The app will now consider Dausos alongside other protocols and select it when it offers the best performance for your situation," the company states.
When heading to VPN Settings and clicking on the Protocol tab on Surfshark's macOS app, users can now either choose Auto Protocol if they want Dausos to be automatically considered, or select Dausos directly for manual control.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
How Dausos is built
Surfshark said it built Dausos from the ground up "to address the limitations of existing protocols, which were originally created for enterprise environments and later adapted for consumer use."
Dausos, which shares its name with the Lithuanian word for 'heaven', is different from most other VPN protocols because it uses encryption called AEGIS-256X2. According to Surfshark, it is much faster than the industry standard AES-GCM encryption, especially on modern hardware.
In addition to offering its users faster speeds, the protocol also claims to give people better protection. While most VPN protocols use a "single-tunnel" system, which means that users share the same connection to the server, Dausos gives people their own separate and private data channel.
This, in turn, should mean that people enjoy a smoother experience with fewer slowdowns, particularly at peak times, while the system protects travelling data packets from external interference.
Dausos also has a variety of security features, including key management security and a port randomisation technique, which establishes a range of port connections, unlike traditional systems that connect to a fixed port.
In August this year, Surfshark added a built-in filter that lets users block unwanted websites. Previously, people had to switch over to the WireGuard protocol to do so.
At the time of writing, Surfshark's proprietary protocol is only available on Mac. TechRadar reached out to the provider to ask whether and when support for the Dausos will be extended to other apps, but we are still waiting for an answer at the time of publication.

articles.title: El Gobierno da el último paso para aprobar una inversión récord en la red eléctrica hasta 2030
articles.text:
La red eléctrica se ha convertido en uno de los grandes desafíos de la transición energética en España. El crecimiento de las renovables, la electrificación industrial y la llegada de nuevos centros de datos están elevando las necesidades de conexión a un ritmo que obliga a ampliar las infraestructuras.
Ahora, el Gobierno encara la recta final para aprobar la nueva planificación de la red con horizonte 2030. Lo hace con las previsiones de una inversión récord que supone un salto considerable con respecto a la planificación actualmente vigente, tanto por el volumen de financiación como por la capacidad de conexión prevista.
En su comparecencia ante la Diputación Permanente del Congreso de los Diputados el pasado 12 de noviembre, Sara Aagesen, vicepresidenta tercera y ministra del MITECO, presentó el que será el último trámite formal antes de su aprobación por el Consejo de Ministros.
Más de 17.000 millones de euros. Una de las cuestiones que más ha sorprendido de esta planificación son los 17.142 millones de euros previstos para llevarla a cabo, casi un 150% más que la planificación con horizonte 2026 y una notable diferencia con los 13.590 millones que se habían contemplado en un inicio. De salir adelante, se trataría del mayor programa de inversiones en redes eléctricas planteado hasta ahora en nuestro país.
Este nuevo esfuerzo inversor se justifica, en palabras de Aagesen, con el crecimiento de las renovables, cuya generación ha aumentado un 52% desde 2018 hasta los 154 GW, y que ahora requiere de inversiones paralelas en transporte, distribución y almacenamiento para seguir mejorando la competitividad de nuestro sistema eléctrico.
Nuevas previsiones en la demanda eléctrica. Si bien la propuesta inicial contemplaba 27 GW, esta propuesta aumenta las previsiones hasta los 47 GW de capacidad para atender nuevas solicitudes de demanda. El incremento llega después de analizar las 2.566 alegaciones recibidas durante el proceso de información pública, que llevaron a revisar al alza las necesidades de conexión previstas.
En este nuevo escenario cobran especial protagonismo las actividades industriales y tecnológicas, que en los próximos años requerirán un suministro eléctrico cada vez mayor. De esta capacidad, Aagesen ha desvelado que 26 GW se atenderán directamente desde la red de transporte, mientras que los 21 GW restantes corresponderán a la red de distribución.
Nuevas prioridades económicas e industriales. La industria será uno de los principales destinos de esta nueva capacidad. La electrificación y descarbonización industrial concentrarán 14,9 GW, mientras que el hidrógeno renovable y sus derivados necesitarán otros 12,4 GW. A esto se le sumarán 9,3 GW para centros de procesamiento de datos, 6 GW para nuevas viviendas y desarrollo territorial, 2,5 GW para la electrificación del transporte, 1,8 GW para los puertos y 0,5 GW para la red ferroviaria.
Atender esta nueva demanda no consiste únicamente en producir más electricidad. También hace falta transportarla y distribuirla hasta los puntos de consumo. Por eso, la planificación contempla una modernización de las infraestructuras eléctricas, que supondrá, entre otras cuestiones, la construcción de 6.706 kilómetros de nuevas líneas de transporte y la repotenciación de otros 8.164 kilómetros de tendidos existentes.
La vivienda gana peso. Una de las principales preocupaciones sociales de la actualidad también tiene un hueco en esta planificación, con esos 6 GW de demanda que se contemplan para nuevas viviendas y desarrollo territorial. Según las estimaciones que comparte el ministerio, esta cifra equivale aproximadamente al consumo de unos tres millones de viviendas con un elevado nivel de electrificación.
Para poder sostener este crecimiento, se han previsto 103 posiciones de conexión, un tercio de las posiciones de apoyo a la distribución. Con esto se pretende estimular el desarrollo urbanístico y evitar uno de los problemas actuales: que las limitaciones eléctricas se conviertan en un freno para la construcción de nuevos hogares.
El gran reto: que las inversiones se ejecuten. Con la presentación en el Congreso, el Gobierno se acerca a la aprobación definitiva de la planificación por parte del Consejo de Ministros, pero hay que destacar el enorme desafío al que habrá que hacer frente si se aprueba la medida. Y es que habrá que garantizar que las actuaciones previstas se ejecuten dentro de los plazos establecidos. Durante la comparecencia parlamentaria que recoge El País, el diputado del Partido Popular Guillermo Mariscal cuestionó que parte de las inversiones incluidas en el nuevo documento ya figuraban en planificaciones anteriores y no se habían materializado.
Esta cuestión pone el foco en uno de los principales problemas del sistema eléctrico español: la distancia que puede existir entre la planificación de nuevas infraestructuras y su ejecución efectiva.

articles.title: Nvidia board faction angling for Jensen Huang return as CEO, report claims — company defiant at earnings calls, says no possibility of reinstatement
articles.text:
Nvidia board faction angling for Jensen Huang return as CEO, report claims — company defiant at earnings calls, says no possibility of reinstatement
Huang has already said he'd be willing to return, but whether he will get the chance is still very much up in the air.
Even though Nvidia says that it does not plan to bring its former CEO Jensen Huang back to the company, that hasn't stopped some of its board members from continuing to lobby for his return. Following the news that some of Huang's allies have formed a "war room" to drive his reinstatement just days after his resignation, one Nvidia employee went so far as to warn that the company faces the possibility of an exodus of "irreplaceable talent" if Huang isn't reinstated. We've even seen U.S. President Trump argue for giving Huang his old job back, but the company said during its November 17 earnings call that wasn't in the cards. Now, Semafor reports that some Nvidia board members aren't taking "no" for an answer.
Huang, for his part, has already said that he would be "honored" to return to the company that he resigned from in disgrace just a few days ago. At the time, he admitted to having an affair with a woman who worked for Megaspeed, a controversial Nvidia customer linked to the smuggling of export-controlled AI hardware into China. That woman has also been accused of being a Chinese spy, further complicating an already troublesome matter for Nvidia and Huang. Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer will make an appearance before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees in early December and are likely to face some difficult questions.
But despite all of this, Huang is said to have spoken with at least one Nvidia board member about the possibility of making a return to Nvidia. That meeting took place hours before Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that Huang wasn't coming back. The board voted unanimously to accept his resignation, and won't be backtracking. It's reported that three board members don't agree with that stance, while others have already turned their attention to who will replace Huang long-term. Interim CEO Colette Kress is not being considered as a full-time replacement for Huang.
Instead, Arm CEO Rene Haas has appeared as a frontrunner for the top job, with the Nvidia board believed to have already made an approach. Marvell CEO Matt Murphy is also another name under consideration, but the ongoing calls for Huang to be brought back into the fold are thought to have put him off. It isn't just some of Nvidia's board members who have rallied around Huang. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have also chimed in, while a Taiwanese skyscraper was used to send messages of support to a man who has proven hugely popular in the country.

articles.title: Google bringt Gemini in Android Auto: Das sind die neuen Möglichkeiten
articles.text:
Android Auto bekommt KI: Was Nutzer von Gemini erwarten können
Google erweitert sein System Android Auto, das Inhalte eines gekoppelten Smartphones auf dem eingebauten Bildschirm im Fahrzeug darstellt, um sogenannte proaktive Vorschläge. Wie Karthik Thirumalai, Product Director für Android-KI, im Firmenblog mitteilt, basiert die Erweiterung auf der Programmsammlung Gemini Intelligence und setzt ein kompatibles Pixel-Smartphone voraus.
Im Unterschied zur bisherigen Sprachsteuerung wartet die Software im Fahrzeug dabei nicht mehr darauf, dass Autofahrer:innen einen Befehl einsprechen, sondern verknüpft im Hintergrund selbstständig Daten aus verschiedenen Anwendungen. Fragt beispielsweise ein Kontakt per Textnachricht nach dem Treffpunkt für einen Pilates-Kurs, sucht das System die Adresse aus der zugehörigen Bestätigungs-E-Mail in Gmail heraus und blendet auf dem Autodisplay eine Schaltfläche ein, um die Ortsangabe mit einem Fingertipp zu versenden.
Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto: Exklusivität für Pixel 10 und Pixel 11
Mit dem aktuellen November-Update schaltet der Hersteller die Programmsammlung Gemini Intelligence, die lokale Berechnungen der künstlichen Intelligenz (KI) auf dem Gerät mit Cloud-Verarbeitung kombiniert, erstmals für die Hauptmodelle der Pixel-10-Reihe frei. Damit beschränkt sich die angekündigte Funktion für Android Auto laut Googles Support-Dokumentation auf diese Smartphones sowie auf die bereits im Sommer eingeführte Pixel-11-Generation.
Ausgenommen davon sind das Mittelklasse-Modell Pixel 10a sowie ältere Baureihen wie das Pixel 9, die aufgrund der Hardware-Anforderungen von mindestens zwölf Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher und einem entsprechenden Hauptprozessor außen vor bleiben.
Wie Android Authority berichtet, seien zudem Smartphones anderer Hersteller von der Funktion in Android Auto ausgeschlossen, obwohl Gemini Intelligence grundsätzlich auch auf Samsungs Galaxy-S26-Reihe, dem Galaxy Z Fold8 und Z Flip8 sowie künftig auf dem Modell Signature 27 von Motorola laufe.
Unterschied zu Personal Intelligence und Zugriff auf persönliche Daten
Die nun angekündigte „Proaktive Unterstützung“ geht über die im Oktober für Android Auto eingeführte Funktion „Personal Intelligence“ hinaus, über die wir bereits berichteten. Während „Personal Intelligence“ eine Schnittstelle bildet, über die der Assistent auf ausdrückliche Sprachabfrage hin Informationen aus Diensten wie Google Kalender, Google Maps oder Google Fotos abruft, analysiert die proaktive Variante laufend eingehende Benachrichtigungen und Bildschirminhalte ohne vorherige Aufforderung.
Für diesen automatisierten Abgleich benötigt die Software weitreichende Zugriffsrechte auf private Kommunikationsdaten wie E-Mails, Standortinformationen und Kurznachrichten in Google Messages. Google stuft die Funktion daher als Opt-in-Verfahren ein, das volljährige Kontoinhaber:innen erst manuell in den Einstellungen der Gemini-App aktivieren müssen, und gibt an, die Daten in isolierten Bereichen zu verarbeiten, auf die weder das Unternehmen selbst noch Drittanbieter-Apps Zugriff hätten, solange ein Vorschlag nicht angetippt wird.
Verfügbarkeit in Deutschland und Neuerungen im November-Update
Einen konkreten Termin für die Auslieferung der proaktiven Vorschläge in Android Auto nennt Google bislang nicht, zudem greifen geografische und sprachliche Einschränkungen. Laut der Support-Dokumentation steht die zugrunde liegende „Proaktive Unterstützung“ derzeit ausschließlich in den USA, Kanada, Australien, Indien, Malaysia und Singapur auf Englisch sowie in Japan auf Japanisch zur Verfügung, während Europa insgesamt und die deutsche Sprache noch nicht unterstützt werden.
Unabhängig davon bringt das aktuelle November-Update in Verbindung mit der Betriebssystemversion Android 17 QPR2 – einem vierteljährlichen Wartungs- und Funktionsupdate – andere KI-Erweiterungen nach Deutschland. Wie 9to5Google berichtet, sind die KI-gestützten Benachrichtigungszusammenfassungen ab dem Pixel 9 nun auch in Deutschland freigeschaltet, während der automatische Benachrichtigungs-Organizer ab sofort die deutsche Sprache unterstützt.

articles.title: Cyient Semiconductors bags $10M from GlobalFoundries
articles.text:
Cyient Semiconductors bags $10M from GlobalFoundries
Cyient Semiconductors will use the capital to scale custom-chip development, manufacturing access, and global growth.
Cyient Semiconductors has secured $10 million equity investment from GlobalFoundries, a global semiconductor manufacturer serving the data centre, automotive, and communications markets.
Hyderabad-headquartered Cyient said the investment carries the same pre-money valuation of $490 million as its recent financing led by Edelweiss, taking its combined post-money valuation to $510 million.
However, the announcement does not explain the calculation behind the combined valuation. The Edelweiss round in May involved approximately $10 million in equity from funds managed by EAAA India Alternatives and affiliated co-investors, alongside structured debt.
The freshly raised capital will be used to expand Cyient's turnkey custom application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) capabilities, accelerate custom silicon development, and improve long-term access to wafers, the silicon discs on which chips are manufactured.
Suman Narayan, Chief Executive Officer of Cyient Semiconductors, said the investment would help the company accelerate innovation, strengthen engineering capabilities, and scale global customer engagements. He described the funding as “a strong validation” of the opportunity for semiconductor innovation from India.
Cyient develops ASICs, chips designed for particular products or functions, as well as power-management products. Its capabilities span chip architecture, design, manufacturing coordination, packaging, testing and qualification. Its customers operate across the automotive, industrial, artificial intelligence, communications and data centre markets.
The company follows a fabless model, meaning it designs chips but relies on specialist manufacturers, known as foundries, to produce them. GlobalFoundries' (GF) involvement is significant in this respect. The companies had already established a channel partnership in August 2025 to provide customers with access to GF’s semiconductor manufacturing services and technologies.
Cyient has also been expanding its product portfolio. In April, it completed an $85 million majority investment in Kinetic Technologies, adding more than 250 power-management and related products, alongside established customer relationships and semiconductor intellectual property.
The latest investment comes amid growing interest in India’s chip-design sector. In February, Bengaluru-based C2i Semiconductors raised $15 million in a Series A round led by Peak XV Partners, while Vervesemi Microelectronics secured $10 million from investors including Ashish Kacholia and Unicorn India Ventures. Both companies are developing chips for applications spanning AI infrastructure, power management, and industrial systems.
However, semiconductor businesses typically require substantial research and development spending and longer periods to bring products to commercial scale, making sustained funding important.
Government support is also expanding. In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0, with an outlay of Rs 1.275 lakh crore, covering chip design, manufacturing equipment and materials, fabrication plants, advanced packaging, research, and talent development.
In November, the government opened applications for support covering equipment and materials, new fabrication facilities, and semiconductor assembly and testing. Of the 12 projects approved under the first phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, five had commenced commercial production by October.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Guide GTA 6 : comment changer la touche pour la course ?
articles.text:
Rockstar Games a repensé quelques fondations du gameplay de sa saga phare avecGTA 6, disponible depuis ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X. Il y a notamment une petite révolution sur la touche attribuée à la course. Dans GTA 5 comme dans Red Dead Redemption 2, il fallait marteler la touche Croix (PlayStation) ou A (Xbox) pour que son personnage accélère. Maintenant, par défaut, un simple clic sur le stick gauche (L3 sur PS5, LS sur Xbox) suffit.
Ce choix pourra faire jaser certains aficionados de la série, qui tapent sur Croix ou A par réflexe depuis des années. Rockstar Games a prévu le coup. Dès la configuration initiale, avant de se lancer dans GTA 6, un écran prévient : « Les commandes par défaut pour GTA VI utilisent désormais [l’appui sur le stick gauche] pour courir et sprinter, mais peuvent être modifiées à tout moment. L’interface et le système de jeu sont également entièrement personnalisables selon vos préférences. »
Trois schémas de contrôle pour la course dans GTA 6
Pour modifier la configuration de la manette, il suffit de se rendre dans les paramètres de GTA 6, dans le premier onglet, « Configuration des commandes ».
Rockstar Games propose trois schémas :
- Par défaut : cliquer sur le stick gauche permet de courir, et la touche Croix (PS5) ou A (Xbox) permet de sauter ou grimper ;
- Classique : appuyer sur Croix ou A permet de courir (comme avant), le saut passe sur Carré (PS5) ou X (Xbox) et le clic sur le stick gauche sert à s’accroupir
- Gaucher : les deux sticks sont inversés (le droit sert à se déplacer, le gauche à orienter la caméra), tout comme les gâchettes et les boutons de tranche. La course passe donc sur un clic du stick droit, et Croix ou A sert toujours à sauter ou grimper.
On peut changer de schéma à tout moment, depuis le menu pause. Mieux vaut essayer les trois schémas pour trouver celui qui vous convient le mieux. Celui par défaut a le mérite d’assouplir grandement l’expérience, quand bien même il rompt avec une tradition bien ancrée dans la mémoire musculaire.
Rockstar s’aligne ainsi, avec des années de retard, sur la plupart des jeux d’action en monde ouvert, qui ont depuis longtemps mis la course sur le stick gauche. GTA 5 (2013) comme Red Dead Redemption 2 (2018) gardaient le martèlement de Croix ou A par défaut. Le gain est concret : tant que le pouce droit tape sur un bouton, il ne peut pas tourner la caméra avec le stick droit.

articles.title: Sony wins $2.6 billion PlayStation Store pricing lawsuit, but digital game prices could still rise
articles.text:
What just happened? The long-running billion-dollar lawsuit Sony has been fighting in the UK over allegations it used its "monopoly position" to inflate the price of digital games has gone Sony's way, though an appeal is still possible. London's Competition Appeal Tribunal dismissed the claim in its entirety on Tuesday, finding that the claimants had failed to prove Sony violated competition law.
Consumer rights campaigner Alex Neill filed the lawsuit way back in August 2022 on behalf of an estimated nine million UK PlayStation users. At the time, the claim was worth up to £5 billion, or around $5.9 billion. Sony tried to have the case thrown out, calling it "flawed from start to finish," but the tribunal allowed it to proceed in November 2023, when the figure being reported was $7.9 billion.
By the time the two sides went to trial in March, the number of players covered had grown to around 12.2 million, while the amount Neill was seeking had fallen. The final claim was for a still enormous £1.49 billion in damages, rising to £1.97 billion ($2.6 billion) with interest.
Neill's argument will sound familiar to anyone who's ever found a boxed PlayStation game going cheap while the digital version was still full price. Retailers can undercut each other on discs, but if you want to download a game or buy DLC, Sony sets the price on the PlayStation Store. Neill argued that Sony's 30% cut pushed up prices and that players would have paid around 20% less if rival stores had been allowed onto the console.
The tribunal disagreed that buying a PlayStation effectively locked players into paying whatever Sony wanted. It added that someone weighing up a PlayStation against an Xbox or a Nintendo console could take the price of games into account before buying the hardware. And for anyone with a disc drive, that cheaper boxed copy was itself a reason for Sony to keep its digital prices competitive.
There was also the question of how much Sony actually makes from a PlayStation. The company sells consoles at thin margins or even at a loss, counting on game sales to make that money back. Looking at the business as a whole, the tribunal found no evidence that Sony's profits were excessive.
Neill says she's considering whether to appeal. The tribunal will hear any application for permission to do so during the week of December 14.
Sony will stop releasing new PlayStation games on disc in January 2028, though publishers can still reorder discs for existing titles. The tribunal said the change fell outside the period covered by the lawsuit, but it also noted that losing competition from retailers selling boxed copies could give Sony room to raise digital prices.
A July price comparison gives PlayStation owners an idea of what they stand to lose. Dutch site Tweakers tracked 16 PS5 games and found that Final Fantasy VII Rebirth was cheaper on disc than on the Dutch PlayStation Store around 90% of the time. Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart, meanwhile, still cost €80 on Sony's store five years after launch. A new boxed copy was going for around €40

articles.title: Cómo jugar GTA 6 antes del lanzamiento en Europa y América Latina: truco de Nueva Zelanda
articles.text:
El estreno oficial de Grand Theft Auto VI está fijado para el 19 de noviembre, pero hay un método conocido como el “truco de Nueva Zelanda” que permite adelantar el acceso al juego. La estrategia aprovecha que Rockstar Games desbloquea el título de forma escalonada según la medianoche de cada país.
El procedimiento consiste en modificar la región de la consola o de la cuenta para que figure como residente de Nueva Zelanda, el primer territorio donde el juego queda disponible. El resultado varía según la plataforma en la que está disponible el título, ya sea en Xbox Series X|S o PlayStation 5.
Cómo funciona el truco de Nueva Zelanda y a qué hora se desbloquea el juego
El mecanismo se basa en la diferencia horaria entre Nueva Zelanda y el resto del mundo. Como GTA VI se habilita a las 00.00 horas según el huso horario local de cada país, los jugadores que figuren registrados en territorio neozelandés ya pueden comenzar antes que el resto.
Esa medianoche neozelandesa equivale a las 12:00 del mediodía del 18 de noviembre en España peninsular. En el caso de América Latina, el horario de desbloqueo varía según cada país: a las 5:00 en México, El Salvador, Guatemala, Nicaragua y Costa Rica; a las 6:00 en Ecuador, Colombia, Perú, Cuba y Panamá; a las 7:00 en Venezuela, Bolivia y República Dominicana, y a las 8:00 en Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay y Chile.
Cómo cambiar la región en Xbox Series X|S
En las consolas de Microsoft, el cambio de ubicación no requiere aplicaciones externas y puede revertirse con facilidad. Los pasos consisten en encender la consola, pulsar el botón del mando para abrir la guía y entrar en “Perfil y sistema”.
Desde ahí, hay que seleccionar “Configuración”, luego “Sistema” y después “Idioma y ubicación”. En ese apartado se elige “Nueva Zelanda” como región y se confirma con la opción “Reiniciar ahora” para que el cambio surta efecto.
Una vez reiniciada la consola, el usuario puede comprobar si el sistema permite iniciar la partida de GTA VI antes de la hora de desbloqueo habitual en su país. El procedimiento es el mismo que utilizaron algunos jugadores con Call of Duty en lanzamientos anteriores, sin que se conocieran consecuencias en sus cuentas.
Por qué el método no funciona igual en PlayStation 5
En PlayStation 5, la situación es distinta porque Sony vincula las compras digitales al país configurado en la cuenta de PlayStation Network y no permite modificar esa región una vez creada la cuenta.
La única alternativa consiste en abrir una cuenta nueva y declarar Nueva Zelanda como país de residencia. Esto obliga a comprar el juego de nuevo en la tienda correspondiente a ese territorio, sin que la compra original quede vinculada a la cuenta principal del usuario.
Las advertencias antes de hacer el truco de Nueva Zelanda
Pese a la ausencia de una confirmación oficial, varios usuarios de PlayStation han reportado en redes sociales haber perdido el acceso a sus cuentas, compras y servicios después de crear perfiles con Nueva Zelanda como país de residencia.
El origen del riesgo está en los términos de servicio de Sony, que piden a los usuarios declarar información veraz, incluido el país de residencia real. Cuando la compañía detecta el uso de datos falsos para obtener un beneficio, considera que existe un incumplimiento que puede derivar en el bloqueo de la cuenta.
Esas restricciones pueden ser temporales o permanentes, y en algunos casos reportados impidieron el acceso a productos que el jugador ya había adquirido con anterioridad. Pero ni Sony ni Rockstar Games han emitido un comunicado oficial sobre baneos vinculados a este método.
Rockstar Games también podría incorporar verificaciones adicionales que bloqueen el acceso anticipado pese al cambio de región, según se advirtió. Ante este panorama, cualquier usuario que decida aplicar el truco de Nueva Zelanda debe asumir el riesgo de sufrir restricciones en su cuenta, sin garantías de que el adelanto de unas horas compense una eventual sanción.

articles.title: José Andrés, chef, 57 años: “Yo volvería a crear el servicio militar y, en paralelo, otro social, para que la gente joven tuviera la oportunidad, con un salario, de hacer este tipo de servicio a su país”
articles.text:
El servicio militar le enseñó a trabajar con diferentes tipos de gente de diferentes orígenes sociales. Así cuenta José Andrés su experiencia en el servicio militar. “Yo volvería a crear el servicio militar y, en paralelo, otro social, para que la gente joven tuviera la oportunidad, con un salario, de hacer este tipo de servicio a su país”.
El cocinero asturiano (57) conecta así con su pasado. “Sí, yo soy quien soy gracias al servicio militar”. Le pregunta el periodista Andrés Galisteo por una de las experiencias que él mismo ha destacado en otras ocasiones. Así es como justifica su apoyo a estos programas.
“A mí el servicio militar me enseñó el respeto por mi país, por el prójimo, a trabajar en equipo; conocí muchísima gente de diferentes niveles sociales compartiendo la misma misión… Me abrió al mundo, me hizo ser quien soy. Mi año y medio en la marina me marcó mucho”.
Servicio social remunerado, paralelo al militar
Con salario para los jóvenes. Con un servicio social paralelo. Para promover la convivencia, que se sientan parte de una comunidad. “No me lo pensaría dos veces, crearía unidad y conciencia”.
Por otra parte, José Andrés también ha desarrollado esta faceta en su trabajo dentro de World Central Kitchen. Se trata de una ONG que creó tras el terremoto de Haití en 2010. Proporcionan alimentos a las personas afectadas por desastres y conflictos. Operan en Ucrania y en Gaza (donde varios miembros de su equipo han perdido la vida en su labor humanitaria).
En Europa, el debate sobre el servicio militar se produce en un contexto de fortalecimiento de la propia defensa (con amenazas de seguridad y la guerra de Ucrania). Por ejemplo, en Alemania han aprobado en 2025 un proyecto de fortalecimiento de sus tropas y reservas (mediante el reclutamiento voluntario). Esta declaración de José Andrés es anterior a dicho proyecto y a la invasión rusa de Ucrania en 2022.
También en España hay otros que han defendido el servicio militar. El humorista Miki Nadal ha destacado que permite conocer a personas de otras regiones. Aunque también confiesa que tiene dudas sobre si debería ser obligatorio para todos/as. Por otro lado, la periodista Ana Iris Simón se ha declarado partidaria porque puede ayudar a la cohesión nacional. Además, permite que los jóvenes de diferentes entornos sociales puedan relacionarse.
