articles.title: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status
articles.text:
International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.
After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.
But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.
Lost status
The US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.)
For their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.)
According to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data shows that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.
The full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.
The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.
Private data
But Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer said the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.
In a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.
Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.
Brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas—that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.
“Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer said, and the national data shows multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.
Key question
For people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the big outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.
Data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in big outbreaks in Arizona and Utah. But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”
To date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.
For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.
But in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he said.
Bleak outlook
With the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action plan” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.
While the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.
A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. Meanwhile, non-medical exemptions from school vaccination requirements have never been higher, at 4 percent. Currently, 24 states have exemption rates at or above 5 percent, meaning that even if they are able to vaccinate every single non-exempt child, they would still not meet the 95 percent target. And this is just the data for young children. The vaccination coverage for adults is another concern, and the data there is scarce. In Pennsylvania’s massive outbreak, 1,055 of the 1,561 cases this year have been in adults ages 18 and older (less than 1 percent of the cases were fully vaccinated).
While some health officials have noted optimistically that 92.4 percent in children is just a few percentage points from the target, the reality of bringing up vaccination rates is more onerous.
PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa stressed the point in the press briefing Tuesday: It’s “not the national average or the average in the state or even the average in a big city, you need to guarantee that in every community, village, you have this vaccination coverage up to 95 percent. This is very important,” Barbosa said.
The point has been demonstrated in the US. In 2019, the US came very close to losing its measles elimination status. Unlike now—when the virus is on a nationwide rampage, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases—in 2019, the US nearly lost its status from a single, large outbreak that spread in New York. Though it didn’t explode on a national level, it took 11 months to stamp out in those undervaccinated communities. In that year, the US reported 1,274 measles cases total.
The situation in the US has only gotten worse, and the outlook is bleak, Brewer warns. “The measles outbreaks in Canada and Mexico are winding down,” he noted. “However, in the US, our measles problem continues to accelerate. There is no end in sight.”
Beth is Ars Technica’s Senior Health Reporter. Beth has a Ph.D. in microbiology from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and attended the Science Communication program at the University of California, Santa Cruz. She specializes in covering infectious diseases, public health, and microbes.

articles.title: AMD tease une annonce majeure au CES 2027 : Zen 6 enfin dévoilé ?
articles.text:
Le 5 janvier 2027, à Las Vegas, AMD aura des choses visiblement très intéressantes à nous dire et à nous montrer. C’est ce que l’on retient d’un post partagé par le vice-président du groupe sur X. Derrière ses tournures de phrases aussi alambiquées que cryptiques, la promesse d’une annonce majeure. Zen 6 peut-être ?
Que faut-il retenir du message de Jack Huynh, le vice-président d'AMD, sur X ? Qu’AMD sera bien présent au CES 2027, que la firme y tiendra une conférence au Mandala Bay de Las Vegas le 5 Janvier à 10h heure locale (19 heures en France) et que cet évènement sera l’occasion d’une annonce vraisemblablement majeure.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
« Quelque chose de spécial » pour AMD au CES 2027
L’intéressé évoque en effet rien de moins que le « la prochaine ère de l’informatique », ajoutant qu’il s’agira de « quelque chose de spécial » et qu’AMD s’apprête à « réinventer ce qui est possible, repousser les limites d’aujourd’hui, en façonnant un avenir riche en possibilités dont nous ne pouvions autrefois que rêver ». L’emphase est bien là, c’est certain, mais le mystère aussi car on n’en apprend pas plus à ce stade.
Le seul indice qu'AMD nous soumet en parallèle de ce message prend l'allure d’une figure lumineuse en forme de « A », qui apparaît sur la brève vidéo partagée par Jack Huynh avec son post. Cette dernière peut renvoyer à plusieurs hypothèses à prendre, évidemment, avec tout le recul nécessaire.
Vers une annonce de l’architecture Zen 6 ?
AMD pourrait en effet profiter de sa conférence au CES 2027 pour lever le voile sur au moins une partie de sa nouvelle gamme de processeurs sous architecture Zen 6. Cette forme lumineuse évoquerait par exemple la silhouette d’un ordinateur portable vu de profil, suggérant alors la présentation de la nouvelle gamme de puces Ryzen mobile. Pourquoi pas.
Certains observateurs laissent également entendre que cette forme lumineuse évoquerait le « A » d’Alpha Trion (AT), le nom de code employé en interne pour l’architecture graphique RDNA 5.
Difficile de trancher dans l’immédiat. À moins de fuites courant décembre pour nous éclairer un peu plus sur ce qu’AMD dévoilera à Las Vegas, il nous faudra attendre le 5 janvier prochain pour savoir ce que la firme nous réserve. Affaire à suivre !
Source : AMD / Overclock3D

articles.title: How Social Department built culture-aware video discovery | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
How Social Department built culture-aware video discovery
This post is co-written by Mariah Miller and Sirajus Salekin from AWS and Nicholas Chase from Social Department.
Entertainment marketing teams manage tens of thousands of video assets across studios, networks, and streaming applications. Most campaigns begin with the same video discovery problem: finding the one moment in the footage that will resonate with an audience. When a brief lands, the clock starts, and what they need is almost never something a database can describe.
Semantic search, on its own, has a ceiling: It answers the question you can articulate. Ask it for a character holding a coffee mug and it will find every coffee mug in a thousand episodes. The queries that actually drive entertainment campaigns look nothing like that. They are questions of judgment: which moment in a show will travel, which line is quotable, and which single frame will work as a meme.
Those questions can’t be typed into a search box. Answering them requires two things the search index doesn’t have: an editorial definition of what “quotable” or “memeable” means for a given library, and a continuously refreshed view of what is moving outside the library. Historically, answering them meant a person with deep knowledge of the show watching footage for a week, and that person doesn’t scale across a catalog.
In this post, we describe how Social Department, the AI operating system for entertainment marketing, set out to encode those editorial questions as executable retrieval pipelines. The result is QuickSearch, a set of single-action queries that return the clips a marketer is looking for without requiring them to describe it: Shareable Scenes, Quotable Quotes, Memeable Moments, and Trend Align.
The models in this solution run on Amazon Bedrock, so customer data stays within the AWS data boundary. It isn’t shared with model providers and isn’t used to train the underlying models.
Social Department’s approach to responsible AI is that AI proposes and people decide. In production, code checks generated output against the source material (for example, a quote is discarded if it isn’t in the episode transcript). Amazon Bedrock Guardrails helps screen customer search text for prompt attacks, and a person on the customer’s team approves every post before it publishes.
Social Department owns the pipeline architecture, the retrieval system, and the editorial criteria behind each action. TrackIt, an AWS Premier Tier Services Partner, implemented and delivered against that design. TwelveLabs’ Marengo 3.0 and Pegasus 1.2 models on Amazon Bedrock provide the scene-level video reasoning the pipeline builds on. AWS supplies the infrastructure, the model access including Anthropic’s Claude models, and Amazon OpenSearch Service, using its serverless option, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, for retrieval.
A note on scope: This post describes the AWS portions of the system: the ingest and indexing pipeline, the retrieval path, and the services that run them. The components Social Department owns, including its media and data backbone, content analysis and discovery engine, editorial criteria, and evaluation program, are described only to the depth needed to follow the architecture. The named services that follow are the ones this post is about, not an inventory of Social Department’s full system.
About Social Department
Social Department is the AI operating system for entertainment marketing, serving major studios, networks, streamers, and FAST applications. It automates campaign strategy, asset creation, publishing, and performance optimization across a client’s full content library. Most of those functions depend on locating the right moment inside the footage first, and semantic clip discovery has been core to the product from the beginning.
Why semantic search alone was insufficient
Entertainment marketing operates under two constraints that a general-purpose search layer can’t satisfy.
The valuable queries are the ones nobody can phrase
A marketer can describe an object, a location, or a line of dialogue, but not what will travel. That judgment, this moment lands and that one doesn’t, is the actual skill in the job. It was never automatable because it depends on knowing how an audience behaves rather than what a video contains. A search layer that only understands content requires a human to supply the intent, and supplying that intent well requires having already watched the show.
Trend signal lives outside the library and moves on a different clock
No amount of video understanding tells you what audiences are talking about this morning. That information is created outside the library and changes hourly, while a library changes only when new content is added. A system that answers these queries has to acquire trend signal continuously and reconcile it against the library at request time.
That distinction drove the core architectural decision: content understanding and trend acquisition run as independent pipelines on their own schedules and are joined only when a user selects a QuickSearch action.
Solution overview
With QuickSearch, teams can interact with a video library in a different way, one where the system proposes rather than waits. It provides four actions, each with its own retrieval strategy, editorial criteria, and ranking model. The walkthrough that follows describes how each is implemented. The list here introduces what they do.
- Shareable Scenes surfaces substantial, self-contained scenes such as extended confrontations, climaxes, and set pieces, biased toward developed sequences rather than quick reactions.
- Quotable Quotes finds punchy, quotable dialogue capped at short clip lengths, weighting up lines that have demonstrably circulated where that signal is available for the title.
- Memeable Moments identifies individual frames that will function as memes and generates a caption grounded in the actual frame. A dedicated extraction and scoring step chooses the frame rather than taking a thumbnail.
- Trend Align takes what is trending right now and finds the moments in the library that legitimately connect to it, so a title that finished airing years ago can re-enter a live conversation.
Alongside these, Social Department keeps natural-language search for everything the actions don’t cover, and image-based search, where a reference image returns visually similar content across the library.
The following diagram shows how the three parts of the architecture connect. The content understanding pipeline makes the library searchable, and the trend acquisition lanes pull in external trend signal. The QuickSearch job layer joins the two at request time.
Architecture walkthrough
The system has three parts that run on independent schedules. Two acquire and structure information. The third resolves a user’s single selection into a multi-stage retrieval operation across both.
Content understanding pipeline
This pipeline makes the library legible. It works asynchronously on ingest. An AWS Step Functions state machine orchestrates roughly two dozen Python AWS Lambda functions end to end. The following steps trace one video from upload to indexed clips.
- Upload and trigger – Video lands in a per-team Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket. The S3 Object Created event, routed through Amazon EventBridge, starts the Step Functions execution.
- Metadata – The first Lambda function resolves title, team, episode, and public identifiers against Social Department’s media and data backbone, writes video metadata to Amazon DynamoDB, and reports the asset as processing.
- Transcode – AWS Elemental MediaConvert transcodes the asset to 480p H.264 with adaptive deinterlacing, using a Step Functions task token so the state machine waits on the job rather than polling.
- Shot detection – Amazon Rekognition performs asynchronous segment detection with an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) callback. A second Lambda function merges and splits the raw shots into content-aware ranges of roughly 10–20 seconds. Those ranges are the unit the rest of the pipeline fans out over. Within a range, Social Department segments embeddings at a fixed interval, a design choice tuned to the pacing of episodic television. The indexed clip is short and fixed-length, but the range it sits in follows the cut.
- Embedding – Ranges are processed in a Step Functions Distributed Map. Each call passes a start and end time to TwelveLabs Marengo 3.0 on Amazon Bedrock through asynchronous invocation. The call produces multimodal embeddings across visual, audio, and transcript dimensions, with no file splitting needed on this path.
- Scene description – TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.2 on Amazon Bedrock runs per segment in a parallel Distributed Map, producing scene-level narrative descriptions, emotions, themes, dialogue type, and narrative position, which form the text layer the ranking models later reason over. Pegasus takes pre-cut files rather than time ranges, so a separate Lambda function cuts each range first, with a few seconds of padding on either side to preserve scene transitions.
- Transcription and enrichment – In parallel with embedding, the pipeline runs speech-to-text with automatic fallback, and Amazon Rekognition for on-screen text, visual labels, and face collections used in character grounding. Anthropic’s Claude models on Amazon Bedrock extract the show’s character map and generate show-level concepts and character roles.
- Indexing – Amazon Bedrock writes embedding output to Amazon S3. A final Distributed Map then indexes embeddings, transcript, on-screen text, scene description fields, and labels into Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.
The pipeline is event-driven end to end. Every Lambda task retries with exponential backoff. The scene-description stage adds a dedicated throttling retry with full jitter. Non-critical enrichment steps degrade gracefully rather than failing the run, and a hard failure routes to an error handler that records the reason and reports the asset as failed.
Same-Region staging for Marengo. Marengo is available in a specific set of AWS Regions. Asynchronous invocation in Amazon Bedrock reads input from and writes output to an Amazon S3 bucket in the same Region as the endpoint. The pipeline is built around those parameters. It stages each video into a dedicated bucket in US East (N. Virginia) before invoking Marengo, then reads the embedding output back from the same bucket. The rest of the infrastructure stays in its home Region while each embedding job runs alongside the model. For model availability by Region, see Model support by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock.
Trend acquisition
This pipeline operates continuously and independently of any library, and it is what makes Trend Align possible.
- Two lanes, one feed – Trend data is acquired through two lanes with deliberately different mechanisms. The daily lane uses an Amazon EventBridge cron, one scheduled fetch per region per day, timed to each region’s local morning rather than a fixed UTC hour. The heat lane (Heat Seeker) reads early-stage, momentum-ordered trends, and is fetched only when a user explicitly asks for it, reusing what is already stored if it is recent enough. The split is a cost decision. A cron pays for every region on every tick whether or not anyone is working, while a demand-shaped fetch behind a TTL costs nothing on a quiet day.
- Regional feeds are separate populations – Trends are acquired per geographic region, currently four feeds: worldwide, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. A region isn’t a filter over a global list. Each is discovered separately on its own schedule, so the same day’s trends genuinely differ between them.
- Interpretation and the editorial gate – Raw trend data isn’t shown to a customer. Anthropic’s Claude Haiku on Amazon Bedrock normalizes each trend onto Social Department’s own category schema, standardizes its description, deduplicates near-matches, and caps how many survive per category. In the same pass, an editorial gate drops trends whose primary subject is death, violence, self-harm, natural disaster, politics, protest, crime, or a public-health crisis. A marketing customer isn’t offered these, regardless of how large the trend is. Rejected trends are remembered so each fetch doesn’t re-screen them.
- Storage as first-class rows – Interpreted trends are upserted by stable fingerprint, so the same trend day-over-day reuses its row and its cached derivations. Trends that stop appearing age out and are eventually retired. Refresh runs take a claim so two cannot overlap.
Quotable Quotes draws on a second, narrower input: an external dialogue popularity signal, used strictly to weight lines that have already circulated. It’s optional by design, so if the signal is unavailable a line gets no boost rather than failing the job.
The QuickSearch job layer
This layer is where a single selection becomes a retrieval strategy. It executes each action asynchronously and returns a ranked set of clips.
- Request path – The web application is a React single-page application served from Amazon S3 through Amazon CloudFront. Its API is a Fastify service running on AWS Lambda behind an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API, with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition for relational data.
- Asynchronous execution – Selecting a QuickSearch action writes a job record to Amazon DynamoDB and enqueues an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message. A worker Lambda function picks it up and runs the pipeline for that action. Transient failures retry through Amazon SQS, and errors classified as non-retriable go straight to a dead-letter queue.
- Query formulation – Each action expands into a set of retrieval queries shaped by its editorial criteria. For Trend Align, this is where most of the proprietary work sits: A trend arrives as a cultural topic, and what a video index can match is what appears on screen and in the audio. Bridging those two is a translation problem, which Claude models on Amazon Bedrock handle. The output is a set of queries the index can act on.
- Multi-channel retrieval – Each query goes to the search Lambda function, which handles hybrid retrieval. Marengo embeds the query once, as text, an image, or a composed text-plus-image query. The embedded query then executes across six k-NN channels (visual, audio, transcript, on-screen text, scene description, and labels) and seven BM25 text channels. Per-modality weights come from the query itself. Query-type routing adjusts channel boosts so dialogue queries lean on transcript and emotion channels while visual queries suppress them.
- Fusion and reranking – The channels are combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, which uses rank positions rather than raw scores and so avoids the scale mismatch between k-NN and BM25 similarity. The top candidates then pass through the Amazon Rerank model, a cross-encoder called through the Rerank API in Amazon Bedrock, for a final text-to-text relevance pass, followed by a Claude validation step over the top results.
- Aggregation – The index stores short fixed-length clips. Before results are returned, adjacent clips with high visual-embedding similarity are merged into coherent moments, so a query for a scene returns one 20–60 second result rather than five fragments of the same scene.
- Editorial ranking – A Claude model on Amazon Bedrock ranks the deduplicated, enriched candidates against the action’s editorial criteria. The pool is capped so the model’s output can’t truncate. Model choice is per action: Claude Sonnet where cultural recall changes the answer, Claude Haiku where the task is bounded and cost-sensitive.
- Frame extraction – For Memeable Moments, a dedicated Lambda function extracts several candidate frames from the winning clip and scores them for face quality using Amazon Rekognition and for image sharpness. It then re-extracts the winner at full resolution, trims letterboxing, and returns a signed Amazon CloudFront URL.
- Caching – Completed results are stored in Amazon DynamoDB and reused for 30 days. The cache key includes a per-action pipeline version and, for Trend Align, a hash of the active trend set, so a criteria change, a model upgrade, or a refreshed trend catalog invalidates cleanly rather than serving a stale answer.
Design decisions
Three choices made culturally informed retrieval tractable.
Separating trend acquisition from content understanding
A library changes when new content is added. Trends change daily, and early-stage trends faster than that. Coupling the two would mean either reprocessing content against fresh signal, which is computationally untenable, or serving stale trend judgment. Keeping them as independent pipelines joined at request time means signal stays current without the library ever being touched again. A title that finished airing years ago can re-enter a live conversation.
Splitting each action into cheap retrieval and expensive judgment
The naive design puts one large model in front of the whole library. QuickSearch instead uses inexpensive, high-recall vector and keyword retrieval to build a candidate pool, then spends model budget only on ranking a capped set of real candidates. The caps are sized against the ranking model’s output token limit, because a ranker that truncates mid-response silently drops results. This also keeps the per-query cost of Amazon Bedrock predictable: one embedding call, one rerank call, and a small fixed number of Claude invocations, regardless of library size.
Making cache invalidation an explicit editorial act
Results are cached for 30 days. Without intervention, a change to an action’s criteria or model would stay invisible to users until the cache expired. Each action carries a pipeline version that is bumped in the same change that alters its behavior. That bump invalidates prior results immediately, so editorial judgment is refined as a versioned change to the product rather than relitigated on every query.
Results
Social Department reports the following outcomes from customer use of QuickSearch. These are the company’s own observations rather than a controlled benchmark.
- Queries that were previously impossible are now a single selection – Identifying the moments a fandom has canonized, or the frames that will function as memes for a specific audience, previously required a person with deep familiarity with the title watching footage, and it didn’t scale across a catalog.
- Discovery no longer depends on manual scrubbing – According to Social Department, campaign discovery work that used to take 3–4 days now takes about 10 minutes with QuickSearch. The time a marketer spent scrubbing through episodes for the right moment goes back to higher-value campaign work.
- Marketers reach candidate clips without composing a query – That removes the requirement that the person searching already knows the library well enough to describe what they want, the constraint that made discovery depend on the few people who had watched the show.
- Archived catalog becomes addressable – Content that was effectively unreachable, because it was finished, archived, and invisible to metadata search, becomes usable for campaign work, and titles that stopped airing years ago can re-enter live cultural conversations.
- Industry recognition – Social Department was showcased as a top startup at NAB 2026 and featured in the Entertainment Loft.
        “The hard part here was never the search. It was working out what to search for: how you take something a great marketer does on instinct, about which moment lands and why, and turn it into criteria a system can execute a thousand times. We spent a long time on that. Working with TrackIt on a compressed timeline, we went from spec to a live demo at NAB. TwelveLabs gives us the intelligence to understand what’s inside the footage and AWS gives us the infrastructure to do it at library scale. Our job is to know what to point it at.”
— Jonathan Verk, Founder and CEO, Social Department
        “Everyone in media talks about adding metadata to their libraries but tagging content doesn’t pay for itself. What I like about this project is that it closes the loop. It takes shows sitting in an archive and makes them useful for real campaigns, at a cost that makes sense to run every day. That’s the part the industry has been missing.”
— Chris Marchitelli, Vice President, TrackIt
What we learned
The following four lessons from the project stood out.
The hard problem was expressing judgment, not retrieving content
Retrieval is largely solved. What isn’t solved is specifying intent precisely enough for retrieval to be useful without an expert marketer in the loop. Most of the engineering effort went into defining what qualifies as a shareable scene or a memeable frame, tightly enough to execute repeatedly across libraries with different tones and audiences. That definition is the output of a standing evaluation program of numbered iterations, each measured against per-show ground-truth sets and a tracked baseline, that tunes the criteria against results rather than intuition.
A multi-model architecture on Amazon Bedrock
QuickSearch uses a multi-model architecture, with each model assigned to the work it fits best. Claude Haiku handles bounded, cost-sensitive output, and Claude Sonnet handles tasks where cultural recall changes the answer. TwelveLabs Marengo produces multimodal embeddings, TwelveLabs Pegasus provides scene-level video reasoning, and the Amazon Rerank model handles reranking. Amazon Bedrock made this architecture practical to build and run. Models from TwelveLabs, Anthropic, and Amazon are available through one API, so Social Department can change the model behind a task when measured quality moves, without building a new integration. Asynchronous invocation runs long video embedding jobs at library scale, and the Rerank API adds a relevance pass without separately hosted infrastructure. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails helps screen search input in the same service, and customer data stays within the AWS data boundary. Because Amazon Bedrock is fully managed, the team operates no model-serving infrastructure of its own.
Signal that decays needs its own architecture
Treating trend data as another input to the content pipeline would have failed, because the two have incompatible lifecycles. Recognizing early that library content and live culture are separate systems, with separate refresh rates, storage, and failure modes, was the decision the rest of the design depended on.
Clear layer boundaries made a multi-party project work
Social Department owned the pipeline architecture, retrieval system, and editorial criteria. TrackIt built and delivered against that architecture, and TwelveLabs supplied the video understanding models. AWS, with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, provided the infrastructure, model access, and solution architecture for the AWS components. Because each party had a clearly defined scope, the 8-week production timeline held.
Conclusion
We described how Social Department, working with TrackIt, TwelveLabs, and AWS, built culture-aware video discovery for entertainment marketing using its own pipeline and retrieval architecture. Several AWS components make up the layer this post describes. TwelveLabs Marengo handles multimodal embedding and TwelveLabs Pegasus handles scene-level video reasoning, both on Amazon Bedrock. Anthropic’s Claude models on Amazon Bedrock handle interpretation and editorial ranking, and Amazon OpenSearch Serverless handles hybrid retrieval. AWS Step Functions, AWS Lambda, AWS Elemental MediaConvert, Amazon Rekognition, Amazon DynamoDB, and Amazon SQS run the pipelines around them. The result is a set of single-action queries that return the clips audiences already care about, the lines they already quote, the frames that will work as memes, and the moments that connect to whatever is trending right now.
To get started with multimodal video understanding on AWS, explore Amazon Bedrock and Amazon OpenSearch Service. To learn more about the TwelveLabs models available on Amazon Bedrock, visit the TwelveLabs page on AWS Marketplace. To explore how the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center can help your organization, visit the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center page.
Acknowledgements: The authors would like to thank Katie Kenney, Pranay Duhan, Xiaoye Qian, Rinne Han, and Dahler Battle for their work on this solution. We would also like to thank the TrackIt and TwelveLabs teams for their support.

articles.title: Tesla inicia la venta del Cybercab sin volante ni pedales, pero se necesita un pago mensual
articles.text:
Tesla, compañía liderada por Elon Musk, ya permite la compra particular del Cybercab, su vehículo sin volante ni pedales, en Estados Unidos, pero la oferta inicial llega con condiciones que quitan el control de los propietarios sobre el uso del auto.
La compañía comenzó a invitar a un grupo limitado de clientes a reservar el Cybercab para uso personal en Estados Unidos. El modelo tiene un precio de partida de USD 29.990, sin impuestos, y las primeras entregas están previstas para diciembre de 2026.
Sin embargo, la compra exige una suscripción mensual para que el vehículo pueda circular y restringe su operación a zonas autorizadas por la empresa.
Cuál es el vehículo sin volante ni pedales de Tesla
El Cybercab, presentado por Tesla en octubre de 2024, es un vehículo de dos plazas concebido para desplazarse de manera autónoma. No cuenta con volante, pedales ni otros mandos destinados a la conducción convencional, así que sus dueños no disponen de una alternativa manual si el sistema autónomo deja de estar disponible.
Sumado al precio de compra, los usuarios deben contratar una suscripción de autonomía de USD 299 al mes. Los términos del servicio establecen que el vehículo no funcionará sin una suscripción activa. El primer mes está incluido, pero posteriormente el cobro se renueva de forma mensual.
El costo equivale a más de USD 3.500 al año. En cinco años, la cuota sumaría USD 17.940, con lo que el desembolso inicial y el servicio obligatorio alcanzarían USD 47.930 antes de impuestos, seguro, carga eléctrica y otros gastos de propiedad.
El consejero delegado de Tesla, Elon Musk, reconoció el 14 de noviembre de 2026 que la tarifa mensual era elevada. En una publicación en X, señaló que debería acercarse a los USD 115 mensuales que cuestan, aproximadamente, el sistema Full Self-Driving y la conectividad de otros modelos de la marca.
La empresa puede modificar el precio de la suscripción con un preaviso de un mes. Si el cliente cancela el servicio o Tesla lo suspende por una infracción de las condiciones, no recibe un reembolso proporcional por los días restantes del período ya pagado.
En dónde puede operar el vehículo sin volante de Tesla
Comprar un Cybercab no significa poder usarlo en cualquier calle o carretera. En esta primera etapa, el vehículo funcionará únicamente dentro de áreas geográficas habilitadas por Tesla, que coinciden o están vinculadas con los territorios de Estados Unidos en los que opera su servicio de robotaxis.
Las entregas iniciales se concentran en ciudades de Texas, entre ellas Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio y Fort Worth. Hay reportes de zonas de robotaxi de Tesla en ciudades de Florida, aunque la empresa puede ampliar, reducir o modificar los lugares donde permite circular al vehículo.
La delimitación geográfica no es la única condición. Tesla puede restringir el servicio por el clima, el tipo de vía o el estado de las carreteras. El propietario, por tanto, adquiere el auto, pero depende de una autorización remota y variable para utilizarlo.
Qué restricciones tiene los propietarios del auto de Tesla
La letra pequeña limita lo que el comprador puede hacer con el Cybercab. La reventa o transferencia del vehículo requiere autorización escrita de Tesla. Si un propietario incumple esa regla, la empresa puede reclamar una penalización de al menos USD 50.000 o el valor total de la operación, según cuál sea mayor, sumado a deshabilitar el vehículo.
Tesla prohíbe las modificaciones estéticas o técnicas que no sean realizadas por la compañía o por proveedores autorizados. La empresa se reserva el derecho de recomprar el vehículo en cualquier momento a un valor de mercado definido por ella.
Asimismo, el acuerdo limita el uso comercial. Los compradores no pueden integrar el auto en servicios de transporte de pasajeros, entregas o alquileres sin consentimiento escrito de Tesla.
La compañía tendrá acceso a información de ubicación y a imágenes obtenidas por la cámara interna del auto, según los términos conocidos del servicio. Esa capacidad forma parte de un esquema de asistencia, seguridad y supervisión remota que Tesla considera necesario para el funcionamiento del vehículo autónomo.

articles.title: Microsoft amplia linha própria de IA com sete novos modelos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft amplia linha própria de IA com sete novos modelos
Nova geração inclui IAs para código, cibersegurança, imagem e voz. Modelos devem ser integrados ao GitHub.
A Microsoft apresentou uma nova geração de modelos proprietários de IA chamados MAI. Os sistemas são especializados em tarefas como programação, cibersegurança e edição de imagens, e devem ser usados para reduzir o custo de tarefas sem recorrer aos modelos mais avançados do mercado.
O anúncio foi feito nessa terça-feira (17/11), durante a conferência Ignite e, segundo o CEO da Microsoft AI, Mustafa Suleyman, eles devem ser integrados ao GitHub. Ainda assim, a Microsoft não informou quando o uso do GitHub Copilot pretende migrar para a tecnologia própria.
Na ocasião, a empresa também anunciou o MAI Licensed Weights, para empresas que queiram adaptar os modelos da Microsoft dentro do Azure.
O MAI Code 2 é a principal aposta da nova geração para programação. O modelo foi treinado para tarefas comuns dentro do GitHub Copilot, como escrever código e fazer manutenção de sistemas. Ele, segundo a Microsoft, alcança 98% do desempenho do GPT-6.1 Sol por 40% do preço. Em comparação com o Claude Opus 5.5, da Anthropic, a empresa diz entregar 96% da performance por apenas 5% do custo.
Há ainda o MAI Code 2 Flash, versão mais leve para tarefas que exigem menos tempo de raciocínio. Segundo a companhia, ele alcança desempenho equivalente ao GPT-6 Luna por 65% do preço e ao Claude Haiku 5.5 por 20% do custo.
Além do lançamento voltado à criação e edição de código, a Microsoft também apresentou soluções para outras tarefas. Para criação visual, ela traz o MAI Image 2.7, que, segundo a companhia, assumiu o primeiro lugar no ranking de edição de imagens da Artificial Analysis.
Aproveitando o cenário de tensão em relação às IAs e a segurança digital, a companhia também lançou o MAI Cyber 2 Flash, voltado à defesa de sistemas. Segundo a companhia, o modelo pode executar verificações repetidamente e em segundo plano e teria igualado resultados do GPT-6 Astra no benchmark CyberGymE2E.
Ao todo, Suleyman apresentou sete novos modelos ou sistemas:
A aposta da Microsoft parte da ideia de que nem toda solicitação precisa ser enviada a um modelo de propósito geral que resolveria problemas muito mais complexos. Na avaliação de Suleyman, sistemas de fronteira carregam conhecimentos muito avançados que continuam presentes mesmo quando o usuário pede algo simples, aumentando o custo de processamento.
A proposta dos modelos especializados é concentrar capacidade em um conjunto mais restrito de tarefas. “Isso basicamente significa que você coloca mais tokens, conhecimento e especialização na mesma quantidade de parâmetros”, afirmou Suleyman ao Axios.
Outras companhias também têm investido mais nessa integração entre modelos de maior e menor capacidade de raciocínio. O Google, por exemplo, desenvolveu uma ferramenta para o Google Antigravity — chatbot de programação da empresa — para que o usuário possa atribuir tarefas mais ou menos pesadas entre seu modelo mais avançado, o Gemini 4 Carbon, e outros modelos mais básicos como a versão Hydrogen, lançada em seguida.

articles.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anthropic has priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in the industry. The Claude maker sold 980 million shares in the offering, up from the 825 million initially planned, generating $81.3 billion in proceeds and surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion record to become the largest IPO in history by proceeds raised.
At the IPO price, Anthropic is valued at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, a significant increase from the $965 billion the company reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private market round, but below the $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for several months ago.
Anthropic will begin its life as a public company on Thursday, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” A strong first day of trading would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption, despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks.
The company’s performance is expected to set expectations for private AI companies, including Anthropic’s main rival OpenAI, which was last reportedly valued at $1.25 billion but has yet to announce plans for an IPO.
Although none of Anthropic’s venture capital investors holds more than a 5% stake in the company, the IPO is a massive windfall for its numerous backers. Investors who own approximately 1% of the company reportedly include Sequoia, as well as former Google CEO Eric Schmidt. Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC also holds about a 1% stake in the company, according to a person familiar with the matter. Other backers set to make billions are Iconiq, Menlo Ventures, Coatue, and Sound Ventures, a firm launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher. Spark Capital, the only VC firm known to hold a board seat at the company (it was the first institutional investor in the company, leading its $450 million Series C round in 2023 that valued the company at $4.5 billion), also stands to make a fortune off its early investment in Anthropic.
Some of the Anthropic’s existing investors, namely Sequoia, Iconiq, Lightspeed, Accel, and Altimeter Capital Management, are so enthusiastic about Anthropic’s future that they are reportedly planning to buy billions of dollars’ worth of the company’s shares in the IPO.
Yet the investors’ holdings in Anthropic pale in comparison to those of the company’s strategic partners Amazon, which owns nearly 15% of the company, and Google, which holds almost 14%. A group of major tech companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners, have also agreed to purchase $26 billion worth of non-voting shares through a private placement alongside the IPO.
The company’s seven co-founders, including CEO Dario Amodei, each sold nearly 3.4 million shares in the IPO, according to the S-1 filing, bringing in about $282 million for each.
This post has been updated with the number of shares sold and IPO proceeds.

articles.title: Retro Kickstarter speaker can play soundtracks directly from original Game Boy cartridges — Retro Song Bird supports over 1,900, with physical controls for media
articles.text:
Retro Kickstarter speaker can play soundtracks directly from original Game Boy cartridges — Retro Song Bird supports over 1,900, with physical controls for media
Turns old Game Boy cartridges into a chiptune jukebox.
A new device on Kickstarter claims to make Game Boy cartridges relevant again by playing soundtracks from your favorite classic Nintendo games. The Retro Song Bird is a box-shaped speaker that supports Game Boy and Game Boy Color cartridges, with support for over 1,900 games. Simply inserting a cartridge into the speaker gives you access to all soundtracks and sound effects, which can be controlled using onboard physical controls including next, previous, and volume.
The Retro Song Bird also comes with a 3.5mm stereo line-out and a USB Type-C port in case you want to connect to other audio equipment. According to the developer, it offers accurate, register-level sound emulation and can be used to sample and remix music from your Game Boy cartridges. It exposes all four audio channels (two square, wave, noise) as separate USB audio streams that can be imported into a DAW. This allows you to isolate individual melodies, waveforms, and sound effects from old games to create your own melodies. There’s even support for LSDj for playing saved chiptune tracks, while two Retro Song Bird units can be synced for DJ-style performances using Game Boy cartridges instead of traditional records.
In addition to playing retro video game soundtracks, the Retro Song Bird also supports the Game Boy Camera, allowing you to use it as a webcam offering a glorious 128×112 pixels resolution and 5 frames per second speed. Other features include the ability to back up and restore save files, ROMs, flash writable carts, and export any soundtrack or sound effect as WAV onto your PC. The listing also includes other abilities, including an Alarm Mode, a record of every cartridge you've ever plugged in, an open API for developers, and over-the-air updates.
The Retro Song Bird is currently available to back on Kickstarter, with the standard model starting at $79. The introductory $59 Early Bird offer has already sold out, while the developer is also offering a two-unit bundle for $150. Shipments are expected to begin in April 2027.
The developer notes that only a handful of hand-assembled prototypes currently exist and that the hardware and design still need some refinements. The project also faces potential manufacturing challenges, including component availability, finding suitable manufacturing partners, and producing injection-molded enclosures. Like any other Kickstarter campaign, delivery timelines are subject to change, and backers should be aware that there is no guarantee the finished product will ship as planned.

articles.title: Nigeria’s Payaza secures Central Bank of Kenya licence - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian payments infrastructure company Payaza has been authorised by the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) to provide payment gateway services, just weeks after getting regulatory approval in Zambia.
Payaza offers payment collection, payout and merchant tools to businesses in Africa and international markets. It handles card, mobile money and bank payments in more than 40 currencies and operates in more than 27 countries.
The CBK approval allows Payaza to operate as a licensed payment service provider in Kenya. It can now serve local merchants directly with online checkout and payment acceptance. The licence does not cover deposit-taking or customer wallets.
It comes after the Bank of Zambia gave Payaza a Certificate of Designation of a Payment System. The company has also recently picked up payment licensing milestones in China, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
“Kenya is the heartbeat of East Africa’s digital economy, and we are entering it the right way: fully licensed,” said Seyi Ebenezer, Payaza’s group CEO. “Coming so soon after our Bank of Zambia approval, this licence from the Central Bank of Kenya connects East, West and Southern Africa on one regulated platform.”
Payaza says it will now speed up merchant onboarding, build closer ties with banks and mobile money operators, and seek more licences across Africa, especially in East Africa. Nigeria makes up about 35 per cent of its revenue.

articles.title: Juanjo, español viviendo en Japón: “Los japoneses han normalizado vivir en 15 o 20 metros cuadrados”
articles.text:
Aunque son muchos los edificios grandes que podemos encontrar en Tokio, también existen algunos que son mucho más pequeños. En un vídeo de YouTube, Juanjo Dalmau muestra algunos de estos espacios.
“Desde fuera parece una ciudad superfuturista con edificios enormes, que lo es, pero mucha gente vive en pisos diminutos de 20, 25 e incluso 9 metros cuadrados”, comenta el creador de contenido. En él muestra cómo se aprovechan los espacios y cómo están organizados.
“Los japoneses han normalizado que vivir en 15 o 20 metros cuadrados”. Así valora la forma de vida que puede encontrarse en Tokio.
Las dimensiones son lo primero que llama la atención, pero el recorrido permite fijarse también en la distribución. La cocina, el lugar de trabajo y la zona de descanso deben encajar en una superficie que deja poco margen para separar unas actividades de otras.
Una cocina, una mesa de trabajo y hasta un balcón
En uno de los apartamentos que muestra, tenemos una cocina con dos fogones; también hay una mesa de trabajo y, en el área de estar, tenemos un sofá y un televisor.
Además, este apartamento cuenta con un balcón exterior. Por más que sea pequeño, ofrece un espacio abierto fuera de la estancia principal.
La visita permite ver el apartamento con sus muebles y sus usos cotidianos. La mesa sirve para trabajar y el sofá permite disponer de una zona de estar, aunque ambos tengan que compartir los pocos metros disponibles con el resto de la vivienda.
Para que entendamos cómo es posible que sean tan pequeños, Dalmau menciona el alto precio del suelo y el número de personas que habitan en la ciudad.
También es importante el hecho de que pasen mucho tiempo fuera. Para algunos de ellos el apartamento es solo un sitio para dormir.
Así se entienden las casas que muestra. En los pocos metros que tienen, han de estar presentes todas las funciones de una casa. El resto del día se pasa fuera.

articles.title: GTA 6 va voler des millions d’heures aux autres jeux, à Netflix… et même à votre travail
articles.text:
Plus que quelques heures avant de rejoindre Vice City. GTA VI sort ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series, et ses précommandes ont déjà pulvérisé tous les records. D’après le suivi des ventes tenu par Sensor Tower, le jeu de Rockstar totalisait le 17 novembre 15,88 millions de copies numériques précommandées, remboursements déduits, pour 1,54 milliard de dollars de recettes. La PS5 représente à elle seule 75 % des ventes. Ces estimations ne comptent ni les boîtes vendues en magasin, ni la commission prélevée par les boutiques en ligne, mais elles suffisent à situer l’ampleur du phénomène. Dans un rapport publié à la veille de la sortie, le cabinet s’est surtout penché sur une autre question : où les joueurs vont-ils trouver le temps d’y jouer ?
Fortnite et les grands jeux solo en première ligne
Chaque grosse sortie prend des joueurs quelque part et Sensor Tower a mesuré la fréquentation du reste du catalogue PlayStation dans le mois suivant cinq lancements majeurs récents. Après Monster Hunter Wilds, le nombre de joueurs quotidiens sur les autres jeux a reculé de 7,6 %, et la baisse a atteint 6 % après Oblivion Remastered ou encore 4,7 % après Resident Evil Requiem. Pour GTA VI, le cabinet prévoit une chute de plus de 10 % sur l’ensemble des jeux « qui ne s’appellent pas GTA VI », ce qui en ferait l’impact le plus important jamais mesuré.
Fortnite et les grands jeux solo seraient les plus exposés. L’étude relève que 42 % des joueurs ayant GTA V installé sur PlayStation ont aussi Fortnite, contre 22 % de l’ensemble des joueurs PlayStation. Roblox, en revanche, devrait mieux résister : sa fréquentation a progressé après plusieurs des lancements étudiés, son public étant moins attiré par les grandes productions solo. Le cabinet s’attend aussi à ce que GTA VI retienne ses joueurs pendant des mois, à la manière de Baldur’s Gate 3 ou d’Elden Ring.
Le rapport confirme au passage l’efficacité du marketing de Rockstar. Les précommandes, qui rapportaient entre 2,4 et 3,8 millions de dollars par jour en août, ont bondi à 16,3 millions de dollars le lendemain de la diffusion de « An Extended Look » sur Netflix, soit six fois plus.
Le smartphone ne quittera pas la main des joueurs
GTA VI ne va pas pour autant faire disparaître le smartphone, qui devrait plutôt servir de second écran. Aux États-Unis, Sensor Tower prévoit 60 millions d’heures supplémentaires passées sur les réseaux sociaux le premier mois, pour discuter sur Discord, consulter des guides sur Reddit ou regarder des extraits de parties, ainsi que 100 millions de sessions en plus sur les applications de musique et de podcasts, et 50 millions sur les applications de livraison de repas et de fast-food. Le joueur type serait à 72 % un homme, âgé de 34 ans en moyenne, et nettement plus adepte de Discord, de TikTok et de Twitch que la moyenne des mobinautes.
Ce temps sera forcément pris ailleurs, comme l’explique le cabinet. Ce dernier anticipe 20 millions d’heures de moins sur les jeux mobiles et 6 millions d’heures de moins sur les applications de streaming vidéo. Plus inattendu, les applications professionnelles pourraient perdre 180 millions de sessions durant le mois de lancement, en raison des congés posés pour l’occasion, de la distraction en journée et des « GTA sick days », ces arrêts maladie pris pour jouer. Ces prévisions portent uniquement sur les smartphones Android aux États-Unis, et le profil des joueurs est modélisé à partir des joueurs de consoles et des jeux GTA sur mobile, mais elles donnent une idée de l’onde de choc attendue.

articles.title: Vélo électrique ALSO TM-B : les livraisons suspendues en urgence à cause d’un souci de batterie
articles.text:
Le TM-B d’ALSO a déjà connu un lancement compliqué. Cette start-up de vélos électriques, née chez le constructeur américain Rivian, a levé 150 millions de dollars (environ 137 millions d’euros) cet été. Elle avait aussi repoussé plusieurs fois la livraison de son vélo, jusqu’à début novembre pour les clients de l’édition de lancement.
Un problème logiciel au niveau de la charge
Or, ALSO a annoncé à ses clients, dans un message relayé ce mercredi 18 novembre par Electrek, qu’elle suspendait temporairement ces livraisons, le temps de corriger plusieurs problèmes logiciels qui touchent notamment la charge. Ceux qui attendent encore leur vélo vont devoir patienter un peu plus, alors que les premiers exemplaires sont déjà arrivés chez les clients il y a moins de deux mois.
« Nous avons identifié quelques problèmes logiciels, notamment au niveau de la charge, qui affectent certains vélos », explique l’entreprise dans ce message. Ses ingénieurs travaillent sur une mise à jour du micrologiciel, le logiciel embarqué qui fait fonctionner le vélo, et ALSO estime pouvoir reprendre les envois dans environ deux semaines. Cette pause forcée concerne à la fois les dernières livraisons de l’édition de lancement (Launch Edition) et le démarrage de celles de l’édition Performance, qui arriveront toutes les deux plus tard que prévu.
Début octobre, ALSO prévoyait encore de lancer les expéditions de la version Performance en novembre, pour livrer l’essentiel des commandes d’ici décembre. Le TM-B, présenté le 22 octobre 2025, était même promis à l’origine pour le printemps 2026.
Un vélo où tout passe par le logiciel
Pourquoi un tel bug de charge bloque-t-il toutes les livraisons ? Parce que le TM-B ne fonctionne pas comme un vélo électrique classique. Avec son système DreamRide, présenté sur la page officielle du TM-B, il n’existe aucune liaison mécanique entre le pédalier et les roues. Le pédalage entraîne un générateur qui produit de l’électricité, stockée dans la batterie, puis le logiciel d’ALSO décide comment le vélo avance.
Le TM-B reprend le principe de l’hybride en automobile, où le moteur sert uniquement à produire du courant ; ici, ce sont les jambes du cycliste qui jouent ce rôle. De fait, la gestion de la batterie compte bien plus dans la conduite que sur un vélo à chaîne équipé d’un simple moteur électrique.
Ces soucis n’arrivent pas totalement par surprise. Electrek avait déjà signalé des comportements inhabituels de charge et de décharge sur le TM-B. Pour autant, ALSO n’a pas précisé l’étendue des problèmes et n’a pas confirmé qu’ils étaient liés à ces signalements.
Un nouveau point prévu le 24 novembre
ALSO fera un nouveau point le mardi 24 novembre ; d’ici là, l’entreprise s’en tient à son estimation d’environ deux semaines. En attendant, son site continue de prendre des commandes : la version Performance, affichée à 4 500 dollars (environ 4 100 euros hors taxes), indique une expédition estimée au début de l’année 2027. Le TM-B n’est toujours pas vendu en Europe.

articles.title: Dossier mobile et accoudoirs articulés : ce que propose cette chaise Sihoo à 385,39 euros pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Avec huit heures devant un écran lors d’une journée de travail, on change sans cesse de position. On se rapproche du bureau pour écrire, on recule pour une visioconférence, puis on s’incline pendant une pause. Ces mouvements modifient la position du dos et des bras par rapport aux appuis du fauteuil.
Avec sa Doro C300 Pro V2, Sihoo associe un dossier mobile à plusieurs appuis réglables, pour accompagner les mouvements tout en permettant d’ajuster le siège à sa morphologie et à ses habitudes.
À l’occasion du Black Friday, ce modèle profite d’une offre valable pendant le mois de novembre. La Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 noire sans repose-pieds est proposée à 385,39 euros avec le code SihooNM, contre 409,99 euros avant application du code, soit une réduction supplémentaire de 24,60 euros. Ce tarif s’applique uniquement sur le site officiel de Sihoo.
Un dossier qui accompagne le passage du travail à la pause
Sur la Doro C300 Pro V2, Sihoo regroupe sous le nom DynaCore le fonctionnement coordonné de quatre zones d’appui : la tête, le dos, les lombaires et les bras. L’objectif est de conserver le même soutien, quelle que soit la position de l’utilisateur, notamment lorsque celui-ci incline le dossier.
SyncroFlex, quant à lui, constitue la partie mécanique du système. Sa structure utilise des doubles ressorts et des doubles rails pour permettre au dossier de suivre les mouvements du corps. La chaise accompagne par ailleurs parfaitement le bas du dos au cours de ces changements de posture.
Si vous terminez de taper un texte, par exemple, et que vous vous inclinez pour le relire à l’écran, le dos change d’angle, les épaules reculent et les avant-bras quittent leur position au-dessus du clavier. Le dossier et les accoudoirs accompagnent cette bascule, pour maintenir des appuis dans la position inclinée.
Le mécanisme d’inclinaison adapte également sa résistance au poids de l’utilisateur. Il intervient dans la bascule comme dans le retour du dossier.
Des réglages pour le bas du dos et les avant-bras
Si la mobilité du dossier est un point crucial pour le confort de votre dos, elle ne fait cependant pas tout. La position et l’intensité des appuis comptent aussi, notamment au niveau des lombaires.
Le soutien lombaire dynamique 2.0 dispose d’une surface d’appui élargie et de trois positions. Selon le réglage choisi, il propose un soutien ferme, plus doux ou davantage orienté vers le sacrum, à la base de la colonne vertébrale. L’utilisateur peut ainsi choisir à sa convenance, la façon dont le fauteuil soutient le bas de son dos.
Les accoudoirs 8D, quant à eux, se règlent en hauteur, en profondeur, en écartement et en orientation. Leurs parties articulées permettent d’adapter les appuis à la position des avant-bras et à l’activité en cours.
Au clavier, on peut les placer à hauteur du bureau et ajuster leur écartement. Pour tenir une console portable ou consulter un téléphone, on peut rapprocher les appuis et les orienter vers l’intérieur. Ces ajustements évitent de conserver la même position d’accoudoirs pour des usages qui ne sollicitent pas les bras de la même manière.
Les accoudoirs suivent également l’inclinaison du dossier. Une fois le fauteuil basculé vers l’arrière, ils restent donc associés au mouvement du siège. C’est l’un des atouts du système DynaCore : le soutien des bras évolue avec celui du dos.
Ce que comprend la version proposée à 385,39 euros
La Doro C300 Pro V2 permet aussi de régler la profondeur de son assise sur 4 centimètres. Ce réglage sert à adapter la surface d’assise à la longueur des cuisses et à ajuster l’espace entre son bord avant et l’arrière des genoux.
Sihoo indique que la Doro C300 Pro V2 convient aux personnes mesurant entre 150 et 190 centimètres. Dans cette plage, les réglages du dossier, de l’assise, des accoudoirs et du soutien lombaire servent à affiner la position.
L’appuie-tête large, réglable en 3D, complète les possibilités d’ajustement. Le revêtement en maille laisse quant à lui circuler l’air à travers l’assise et le dossier. Un atout en été, quand vous passez de longues heures en short devant votre ordinateur.
Pendant le mois de novembre, le code SihooNM fait passer le prix de la Sihoo Doro C300 Pro V2 de 409,99 à 385,39 euros. L’offre est exclusivement valable sur le site officiel de Sihoo et concerne le modèle noir sans repose-pieds.
