articles.title: Si tienes una tarjeta NVIDIA, este error oculto podría estar dañando tu SSD sin que lo notes
articles.text:
Un fallo en los controladores de NVIDIA podría estár desgastando los SSD en Windows. Una serie de reportes en los foros de NVIDIA y Dell afirman que algunas versiones de los drivers de GeForce realizan escrituras constantes en el disco, incluso cuando el ordenador permanece inactivo. El ciertas condiciones, el controlador escribe más de 500 MB de datos en apenas cinco minutos.
De acuerdo con Neowin, la alerta surgió luego de que se detectara un problema similar con los drivers de AMD. Varios usuarios con una tarjeta gráfica de NVIDIA detectaron un comportamiento anómalo con el archivo nvlog.nvlgstg, el cual utilizan los componentes de registro y telemetría. Según los reportes, este archivo se reescribe continuamente por el proceso NVDisplay.Container.exe, lo que significa que tu SSD trabaja más de la cuenta.
En un hilo de soporte en los foros de NVIDIA, un usuario reveló que el controlador GRD 621.14 escribió 512 MB de datos en cinco minutos, algo que no ocurría con la versión 621.01:
"NVDisplay.Container.exe reescribe continuamente el archivo de registro binario en C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg, lo que provoca escrituras pesadas en SSD mientras el PC está inactivo", mencionó en su publicación. "El Monitor de Recursos mostraba NVDisplay.Container.exe escribiendo entre 4,6 y 5,2 MB/s en este archivo, sin que ningún juego se ejecutara".
El usuario añadió que el archivo crece más rápido luego de que se elimina y que el contador SMART del SSD coincide con los informes de escritura de Windows. Este fenómeno provoca un desgaste del SSD, que escribe unos 3 GB por hora mientras el ordenador está en reposo.
Un controlador defectuoso de NVIDIA está matando el rendimiento de tu PC
Otros reportes afirman que esta escritura constante genera tirones a la hora de ejecutar un juego o reproducir vídeos. En algunos casos, el fallo provoca que el cursor de Windows se mueva de forma errática cuando la actividad de escritura se incrementa.
En otra publicación de los foros de NVIDIA, un usuario reportó hace dos años este problema con el controlador 566.36 en su Dell XPS 9570. La función de telemetría de NVIDIA hacía que se escribiera en nvlog.nvlgstg cada 30 segundos, aunque no al mismo nivel que ocurre ahora. En esa ocasión, el archivo alcanzaba los 15 MB tras ocho horas de uso.
Hasta ahora no existe una solución oficial para resolver el problema en el controlador 621.14. Algunos usuarios descubrieron que detener el servicio NVIDIA Display Container LS, eliminar el archivo nvlog.nvlgstg y reiniciar el servicio, reduce la cantidad de datos que se escriben en el SSD. La más efectiva es volver a una versión anterior del controlador, como el 621.01 que no sufre de este fallo.
Si optas por lo segundo, lo recomendable es hacer una instalación limpia con DDU (DisplayDriverUninstaller). Para lograrlo, primero necesitas descargarte el controlador GeForce 621.01 desde la web de NVIDIA y la versión más reciente de DDU desde la web de Guru3D. Una vez hecho, descomprímelo y reinicia tu ordenador en Modo Seguro para ejecutar la herramienta y evitar errores.
Una vez que desinstalas el controlador defectuoso, reinicia tu PC en modo normal e instala la versión anterior. De este modo tendrás un driver limpio y sin problemas de escritura constante en el SSD.

articles.title: How Stretto built an AI voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
How Stretto built an AI voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
This post is co-written with Danya Gordin from Stretto and Marcelo Wzorek from CI&T.
Before Stretto built an AI voice agent, consumers considering bankruptcy on its Bankruptcy.com site filled out a web form with a few fields: debt amount, attorney status, and contact information. These form-generated leads carried thin margins.
The gap between a web form lead and a fully qualified lead is significant. Bankruptcy attorneys place more value on a lead that includes detailed financial data: debts, assets, vehicles, real estate, employment history, and prior filings. The web form could have been extended to capture that detail, but the longer it got, the more visitors abandoned it partway through. A phone interview would have drawn the information out naturally, because people are more willing to share financially sensitive details in conversation, but staffing and training a human intake team to run those interviews was cost-prohibitive.
Stretto saw an opportunity: replace the web form with an AI voice agent that conducts the intake interview by phone. The agent would guide callers through the full bankruptcy questionnaire conversationally and extract structured data in real time. It would then sort leads against attorney-defined rules to support attorney decision-making.
The challenge was finding a voice AI solution that could handle sensitive financial conversations naturally, with low latency, clean interruption handling, and emotional awareness, at a cost that made the unit economics work.
In this post, we walk through how Stretto worked with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center and CI&T (an AWS Partner) to build Tara, an AI voice agent powered by Amazon Nova 2 Sonic, a speech-to-speech model in Amazon Bedrock. Tara conducts multi-phase bankruptcy intake interviews and sorts leads against attorney-defined rules. We cover the architecture, the phased build from validation through production deployment, and how the team tested voice quality for sensitive conversations.
Solution overview
Tara is an AI voice agent that conducts bankruptcy intake interviews over the phone. When a caller dials the Bankruptcy.com number, Tara picks up, introduces herself, and guides the caller through a structured conversation. She collects personal information, financial details, asset inventories, and employment history while adapting her tone to the caller’s emotional state. At the end of the call, Stretto’s system applies attorney-defined rules to sort the lead as qualified, disqualified, or needs-more-information for attorney review.
The solution is built on Amazon Nova 2 Sonic, a speech-to-speech foundation model (FM)available through Amazon Bedrock. It processes speech input and generates speech output natively in a single model rather than chaining separate speech-to-text, language model, and text-to-speech components. This architecture is designed to reduce latency and produce more natural-sounding conversations, both critical for the sensitive nature of bankruptcy intake calls. Building on Amazon Bedrock gave the team both Amazon Nova 2 Sonic and Anthropic’s Claude through one managed service, with no model infrastructure to run. It also brought AWS security and governance controls to a workload that handles sensitive financial data. Access to both models is governed by AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Traffic to Amazon Bedrock stays on the AWS network through virtual private cloud (VPC) endpoints (AWS PrivateLink). Amazon Bedrock doesn’t use prompts or model outputs to train models (for details, see Data protection in Amazon Bedrock). Because the models run in the same AWS environment as the voice bridge, the database, and Amazon CloudWatch monitoring, the team could secure and operate the whole solution with one set of tools. Amazon Nova 2 Sonic and Amazon Bedrock are not available in all AWS Regions. For current Region availability, see Amazon Bedrock supported Regions.
The team chose Amazon Nova 2 Sonic over the previous voice solution for three reasons:
- Cost: Stretto reports a 95 percent reduction in per-minute voice cost compared to its previous solution, based on Amazon Bedrock on-demand pricing in us-east-1 as of April 2026.
- Latency: In Stretto’s testing, the previous solution exhibited time-to-first-audio latency above 500 milliseconds, creating awkward pauses. Amazon Nova 2 Sonic is designed for low latency to support natural conversational flow.
- Interruption handling: Callers in stressful situations need to interject, correct themselves, and ask clarifying questions. The previous solution handled barge-in poorly, often breaking the conversation flow. Amazon Nova 2 Sonic is designed to handle interruptions without breaking the session.
The following figure shows the end-to-end architecture.
A caller reaches Tara through Twilio, which opens a WebSocket connection into AWS. Traffic passes through AWS WAF and an Application Load Balancer to the voice bridge on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate, which streams audio with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic (accessed through Amazon Bedrock). After the call, Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) with a dead-letter queue hands the transcript to an asynchronous processor. The processor uses Anthropic’s Claude 3 Haiku on Amazon Bedrock to extract structured fields, which persist in Amazon Aurora Serverless v2. Qualified leads route to attorneys by jurisdiction. Supporting services include NAT gateways, VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink), Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR), AWS Secrets Manager, and Amazon CloudWatch.
Stretto used Twilio for telephony because Tara’s intake is fully automated, with no human agents taking calls, and because Stretto wanted a direct integration with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic that kept its existing AWS backend in place. Twilio Media Streams delivers the caller’s raw audio over a WebSocket, which is the input the voice bridge needs, and CI&T had already integrated it with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. For contact center workloads that route calls among human agents, Amazon Connect also supports Amazon Nova 2 Sonic.
The architecture uses the following AWS services:
- Amazon Nova 2 Sonic (through Amazon Bedrock): The speech-to-speech foundation model that powers Tara’s voice conversations. It handles both speech recognition and response generation in a single pass, supporting tool calling for structured data collection during the interview.
- Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate: A serverless compute engine that runs the voice bridge containers connecting the telephony layer to Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. The voice bridge tasks run continuously across three Availability Zones for high availability.
- Amazon Aurora Serverless v2: A PostgreSQL-compatible serverless relational database deployed in Multi-AZ configuration. Stores caller profiles, intake responses, qualification results, and session metadata. The serverless scaling of Aurora matches the variable call volume patterns.
- Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic’s Claude 3 Haiku): Handles structured data extraction from conversation transcripts. After Amazon Nova 2 Sonic generates a transcript, Claude 3 Haiku extracts typed fields (names, dollar amounts, addresses, vehicle details) into the relational schema.
- Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) with dead-letter queues: Manages asynchronous webhook processing for post-call events, preserving failed messages for retry.
- AWS WAF, VPC Endpoints, and Application Load Balancer: Security and networking layers that help protect API endpoints, route traffic across Availability Zones, and provide private connectivity to AWS services.
Building and validating the voice agent
The team took a phased approach: validate voice quality first, build the production integration, then expand the questionnaire scope after proving the system worked with real callers.
Validating voice quality for sensitive conversations
Bankruptcy conversations are emotionally charged. Callers are often stressed, hesitant, or embarrassed. The voice agent needs to sound empathetic and natural, not robotic or transactional. Before writing any integration code, the team spent a dedicated week testing the voice quality of Amazon Nova 2 Sonic against several caller scenarios.
The validation covered:
- Voice quality across caller emotional states (calm, stressed, hesitant, frustrated).
- Time-to-first-audio latency benchmarks against the previous solution’s over 500 ms baseline.
- Barge-in and interruption handling: can a caller interject mid-sentence without breaking the conversation?
- Emotional tone adaptation: does the agent adjust its pace and tone when a caller sounds distressed?
This validation step produced a comparison report documenting the performance of Amazon Nova 2 Sonic against the previous solution across each dimension. The report became the go/no-go gate for proceeding to integration.
Deploying to production with real callers
With voice quality validated, the team built the end-to-end integration over three weeks. The call flow works as follows:
- A caller dials the Bankruptcy.com number. Twilio’s telephony layer receives the call and opens a WebSocket connection to the voice bridge running on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate.
- The voice bridge streams audio bidirectionally between the caller and Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. Tara introduces herself, collects consent, and begins the intake interview.
- After the call, the full transcript feeds into an extraction pipeline powered by Anthropic’s Claude 3 Haiku on Amazon Bedrock. The pipeline extracts the fields from the conversation and stores them in Amazon Aurora.
The full attorney-designed intake can run 15–20 minutes, which is longer than the maximum duration of a single Amazon Nova 2 Sonic streaming session (for the current value, see Getting started with speech-to-speech). The team treated that session duration as a design parameter and implemented the session continuation pattern, an approach that carries conversation context across session boundaries. The voice bridge tracks how long each bidirectional stream with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic has been open. Shortly before the limit, it opens a new stream with the same system prompt and tool configuration and sends the conversation so far as text history. When Tara finishes her current response, the bridge switches the caller’s audio to the new stream and closes the old one, so the conversation continues smoothly for the caller.
The initial deployment covered the existing 13-field intake form, collecting the same data points the web form captured but through natural conversation. This gave the team a production baseline to measure against before expanding scope.
Expanding the intake and lead qualification
With the production pilot running, the team expanded the questionnaire to the full attorney-designed intake over four weeks. This was a significant increase in scope:
- Over 18 intake categories with conditional branching, where the questions Tara asks depend on the caller’s previous answers.
- Complex relational data: Vehicles (year, make, model, financing status, monthly payment per vehicle), real estate properties, individual debt line items, multiple employment and income sources, and prior bankruptcy filings.
- Rules-based lead sorting: Stretto applies attorney-defined rules to each lead, and attorneys make the final decision. Because a voice agent collects richer, conditional data than a static web form, it gives Stretto more flexibility to apply those rules and qualify leads accurately.
- Lead routing: Qualified leads are routed to bankruptcy practitioners, while callers who do not meet the qualification criteria are directed to alternative resources.
The Amazon Aurora schema expanded to a full relational data model supporting one-to-many relationships. A single caller record might include four vehicles, two properties, and dozens of individual debt line items.
Measuring results and optimizing
The final phase focused on collecting production data and tuning the system based on real caller behavior. The team tracked key performance indicators including call volume, average duration, intake completion rate, profile completeness, conversion rate, and drop-off points.
Insights from production data drove several optimizations: reordering questions to reduce early drop-offs, adjusting conditional branching to collect high-value fields earlier in the conversation, and modifying qualification thresholds based on attorney feedback. The following table shows two key production metrics.
| Average call duration (completed calls) | ~8 min | 
| Data extraction accuracy | ~96% | 
Testing for quality and compliance
Deploying a voice agent that handles sensitive financial data requires more than functional testing. The AWS Generative AI Innovation Center (GenAIIC) advisory team guided the development of a comprehensive testing framework spanning four categories:
- Happy path testing: Complete end-to-end intake interviews with cooperative callers across the full questionnaire. These calls confirm that the over 18 categories collect accurate structured data and that the qualification rules produce correct results.
- Adversarial testing: Callers who provide contradictory information, change answers mid-conversation, refuse to answer certain questions, or attempt to manipulate the qualification outcome. The agent needs to handle the ambiguity and keep the conversation coherent.
- Compliance testing: Consent collection, disclosure delivery, and data handling workflows. The team verified that the agent delivers disclosures accurately and collects consent before proceeding, because bankruptcy intake involves sensitive financial information.
- Barge-in scenario testing: Callers interrupting at various points in the conversation, including during disclosures, mid-question, and during the agent’s responses. Tara should recover without losing context or asking the caller to repeat information.
Responsible AI controls in production
The team treated responsible AI as a production control, not only a testing step. Amazon Nova 2 Sonic includes built-in safety protections, described in the AWS AI Service Card for Amazon Nova 2 Sonic. On top of those, the solution keeps consequential decisions out of the model: lead sorting runs on explicit attorney-defined rules after the call, and attorneys make the final decision. Consent and disclosures are delivered and logged before intake begins, and the adversarial test suite checks that attempts to manipulate the conversation don’t change lead outcomes. Beyond model inference, the solution uses the Amazon Bedrock bidirectional streaming API for real-time audio, tool use for structured data capture during the interview, and private connectivity to Amazon Bedrock through VPC endpoints.
The GenAIIC advisory team also provided guidance on prompt engineering best practices for voice-specific applications, including techniques for managing conversational state across session continuation boundaries and structuring system prompts that maintain consistent agent personality across long interviews.
Results
After roughly three months in production, Stretto reported the following results:
- Per-lead value: Fully qualified leads with complete intake data are significantly more valuable to bankruptcy attorneys than web form leads, which capture only a few basic fields.
- Lead conversion: Stretto’s early production results show a 20 percent relative increase in conversion rate compared with the web form, even before the solution has been rolled out broadly across additional districts.
- Data quality and call length: Stretto reports that Tara extracts structured fields at approximately 96 percent accuracy in its testing, and completed calls average about 8 minutes.
- Voice solution cost: Stretto reports a 95 percent reduction in per-minute voice cost compared to its previous solution.
        “I’m incredibly grateful to the AWS GenAI Innovation Center team. Their expertise helped bring our voice agent, Tara, to life, driving a 20 percent increase in our lead conversion rate.”
— Danya Gordin, Principal AI Architect, Stretto
        “As one of the partners in the AWS Generative AI Partner Innovation Alliance, we can confirm that the GenAIIC program is a true catalyst, bringing customers and partners together to solve real problems and deliver business impact. With Stretto, that meant taking a voice agent to production in a matter of weeks and transform the bankruptcy intake process”
— Marcelo Wzorek, Executive Manager, CI&T
Conclusion
Stretto’s journey from web form leads to AI-assisted intake interviews illustrates what becomes possible when voice AI reaches the quality bar for sensitive use cases. By combining the speech-to-speech capabilities of Amazon Nova 2 Sonic with a well-designed architecture on AWS, the team built a voice agent that is natural enough for callers discussing personal financial hardship and cost-effective enough to deliver meaningful savings at scale.
The phased approach, validating voice quality first, deploying a minimal intake to production, then expanding scope based on real-world data, reduced risk at each step. The team built on validated assumptions rather than projections.
If you are exploring AI voice agents for your own use case, here are some resources to get started:
- Learn about Amazon Nova 2 Sonic and speech-to-speech capabilities.
- Get started with Amazon Bedrock to access foundation models including Amazon Nova 2 Sonic.
- Explore AWS Fargate for serverless compute for containers.
- Learn about the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center for advisory support on your generative AI initiatives.
If you are weighing voice AI for a sensitive, high-value intake process, your AWS account team and the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center can help you scope and build it.

articles.title: Wüstensand als Gedächtnis fremder Welten – wie Dünen die Windstärken auf dem Mars verraten
articles.text:
Fremde Welten: Wie Sanddünen auf der Erde die Windgeschwindigkeiten auf dem Mars verraten
Wissenschaftler der Stanford University im US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien haben nachgewiesen, dass die mittlere Korngröße des Sandes in Dünen auf der Erde und dem Mars Rückschlüsse auf die Geschwindigkeit jener Winde zulässt, welche die Formationen aufgebaut haben. Wie aus einer in der Fachzeitschrift „Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences“ veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, können Forscher:innen den Sand dadurch wie einen Geschwindigkeitsmesser für heutige und vor Milliarden Jahren versteinerte Dünen im Sonnensystem nutzen.
In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten hatten Raumsonden und Teleskope vom Wind geformte Dünen und Rippelmarken auf der Venus, dem Mars, dem Saturnmond Titan sowie auf einem Kometen entdeckt. Anhand der äußeren Form und Ausrichtung dieser Strukturen konnten Planetenforscher:innen zwar die Richtung und die Beständigkeit der Winde bestimmen, nicht jedoch deren konkrete Geschwindigkeit am Boden.
Stanford University: Wie Korngröße und Windgeschwindigkeit in Sanddünen zusammenhängen
Der Erstautor Colin Marvin und der Seniorautor Mathieu Lapôtre von der Fakultät für Erd- und Planetenwissenschaften der Stanford University belegen in ihrer Untersuchung, dass Dünen auf der Erde und dem Mars überwiegend von Winden geformt werden, die gerade stark genug sind, um die Sandkörner am Boden in Bewegung zu setzen. Da größere und schwerere Körner einen stärkeren Luftstrom benötigen, um über diese physikalische Transportschwelle gehoben zu werden, gibt der mittlere Durchmesser der Sandkörner einer Düne Auskunft über die vorherrschende Windstärke.
In der Geologie wird dieser Vorgang, bei dem Wind einzelne Körner vom Boden abhebt und in kurzen Sprüngen vorwärtstreibt, als Saltation bezeichnet. Zwar bewegen seltene Stürme kurzfristig große Mengen an Material, doch über lange Zeiträume hinweg leisten die deutlich häufigeren Winde knapp oberhalb der kritischen Bewegungsschwelle den größten Beitrag zum Aufbau einer Düne.
Laut einer Mitteilung der Stanford University bezeichnet Colin Marvin, der inzwischen als Postdoktorand an der US-amerikanischen Brown University forscht, Dünen daher als einen „großartigen Datenspeicher für das, was auf der Oberfläche eines Planeten geschieht, und insbesondere für die Wechselwirkungen zwischen den Vorgängen in der Atmosphäre eines Planeten und den Prozessen an der Oberfläche“. Dass sich Dünenfelder auf ein solches Gleichgewicht nahe der Transportschwelle einpendeln, hatten zwei Wissenschaftler der US-amerikanischen University of Pennsylvania bereits im Jahr 2010 anhand weniger Stichproben als Hypothese formuliert.
Da diese Annahme seither nicht systematisch an einer größeren Zahl von Wüsten oder auf anderen Himmelskörpern überprüft worden war, werteten Marvin und Lapôtre nun Wetterdaten aus einem Zeitraum von 30 Jahren sowie Messungen der Korngrößen aus 24 weltweit verteilten Dünenfeldern mit unterschiedlichen Formen und Ausmaßen aus. Die Berechnung, welche Windgeschwindigkeiten im Laufe der Zeit am meisten Sand bewegten, bestätigte vom Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park im US-Bundesstaat Utah bis hin zur Namib-Wüste im afrikanischen Namibia durchgehend das vermutete Verhältnis zwischen Korndurchmesser und Windstärke.
Vom Mars bis zur frühen Erde: Klimamodelle mit versteinerten Sanddünen prüfen
Anschließend übertrugen die beiden Wissenschaftler ihre Berechnungsmethode auf die Messdaten eines Dünenfelds auf dem Mars, obwohl sich der Planet bei Atmosphärendruck, Schwerkraft und der Dichte des Sediments deutlich von der Erde unterscheidet. Da sich auch dort dieselbe statistische Korrelation zeigte, gehen die Autoren davon aus, dass Winddünen auf allen Himmelskörpern nach demselben Prinzip entstehen, sofern ausreichend loses Sediment vorhanden ist und starke Stürme seltener auftreten als schwächere Winde.
Weil sich historische Dünen über geologische Zeiträume zu Sandstein verfestigen und die Korngrößen darin erhalten bleiben, ergänzt die Methode eine frühere Untersuchung desselben Forschungsteams im Fachmagazin „Geology“ und erlaubt auch Berechnungen für die frühe Erdgeschichte, wie Mathieu Lapôtre erläutert: „Das funktioniert bei heutigen Dünen ebenso wie bei Sandsteinen, die bis zu drei Milliarden Jahre alt sind.“ Mit diesen aus versteinerten Dünen gewonnenen Werten wollen Forscher:innen künftig Computermodelle zur atmosphärischen Zirkulation auf der frühen Erde und dem Mars überprüfen.
Grenzen der Methode für die Planetenforschung auf Mars und Titan
In der praktischen Anwendung unterliegt das Verfahren der durch die US-amerikanische Forschungsstiftung National Science Foundation geförderten Studie allerdings deutlichen Einschränkungen. Um aus der Korngröße eines Dünenfelds auf einem anderen Himmelskörper die Windgeschwindigkeit abzuleiten, müssen zunächst Daten über den mittleren Durchmesser und die Materialdichte der dortigen Sandkörner vorliegen.
Während Kameras auf Raumsonden im Orbit zwar die großflächigen Formen von Dünen auf dem Mars, der Venus oder dem Saturnmond Titan erfassen, lassen sich millimetergroße Partikel aus der Umlaufbahn nur indirekt und mit Unsicherheiten über thermische Messungen abschätzen. Verlässliche Berechnungen setzen daher im Regelfall Messungen durch Lander oder Rover direkt vor Ort voraus und liefern selbst dann nur Durchschnittswerte der häufigsten Winde, während seltene Extremwetterereignisse im Sand kaum dauerhafte Spuren hinterlassen.
! Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: GTA 6 réclame jusqu’à 212 Go : pour le Black Friday ce SSD SanDisk 1 To officiel PS5 passe à 259,15€
articles.text:
GTA 6 sort le 19 novembre et demande jusqu’à 212 Go d’espace libre sur PS5, de quoi pousser les joueurs à libérer de la place. Amazon vend le SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 850P 1 To, sous licence officielle PS5 et livré avec son dissipateur, à 259,15 € au lieu de 331,99 €, mais nous ne l’avons pas testé et sa facture reste élevée face à des SSD sans licence.
Le SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 850P est un SSD M.2 NVMe PCIe 4.0 conçu pour l’emplacement d’extension de la PS5 et de la PS5 Pro. Amazon propose la version 1 To à 259,15 € au lieu de 331,99 €, soit 72,84 € de remise et 22 % d’économie, dans le cadre de son offre Pré-Black Friday. Le dissipateur thermique est livré avec le disque, un accessoire que Sony exige sur les SSD M.2 de sa console.
Amazon annonce cette offre jusqu’au 30 novembre. Elle s’adresse aux joueurs qui veulent installer GTA 6 sans effacer le reste de leur ludothèque, à condition d’accepter un tarif supérieur à celui de SSD sans licence.
Le SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 850P 1 To est à 259,15 € au lieu de 331,99 € chez Amazon, licence PS5 et dissipateur compris.
Pourquoi choisir le SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 850P 1 To ?
- Une licence officielle PS5 : Le fabricant destine ce SSD à la PS5 et à la PS5 Pro sous licence officielle, un repère rassurant quand on achète un disque tiers pour sa console.
- Un dissipateur déjà fourni : Sony en exige un sur les SSD M.2 de la PS5, et celui-ci arrive avec le disque. Aucun accessoire à ajouter au panier.
- Jusqu’à 7 300 Mo/s : Le fabricant annonce cette lecture séquentielle pour les capacités de 1 à 4 To, bien au-dessus des 5 500 Mo/s minimum recommandés par Sony.
Installer GTA 6 sans trier sa ludothèque
GTA 6 réclame jusqu’à 212 Go libres selon la console, soit un peu plus d’un cinquième de ce 1 To. Le reste de la capacité accueille vos autres jeux. L’emplacement M.2 de la PS5 accepte les SSD NVMe PCIe 4.0 de 250 Go à 8 To, ce qui couvre ce modèle.
Il convient à un joueur dont la console est déjà pleine et qui veut y ajouter GTA 6 en gardant ses autres titres. Il compte moins si vous jouez à peu de jeux, ou si vous n’avez pas besoin de plus d’espace tout de suite. Nous n’avons pas testé ce SSD : les débits cités sont ceux annoncés par le fabricant.
Face aux SSD sans licence, une facture plus lourde
Ce SanDisk coûte plus cher que les SSD NVMe sans licence PS5. Nous relayions le 10 novembre le Corsair MP600 Core XT 1 To à 178,87 € chez Amazon, un SSD livré nu, qui impose d’acheter un dissipateur à part. L’écart de 80,28 € se justifie donc en partie par la licence et le dissipateur, sans qu’on puisse dire en totalité. Pour situer ce modèle face au marché, notre comparatif des meilleurs SSD détaille les références que nous recommandons, avec le WD Blue SN5000 comme meilleur choix.
✅ Les points forts
- Licence officielle PS5 et PS5 Pro
- Dissipateur thermique livré avec le disque
- Jusqu’à 7 300 Mo/s annoncés en lecture séquentielle
- 72,84 € de remise sur le prix barré par Amazon, soit 22 %
- Vendu par Amazon, en stock lors du relevé du 18 novembre
❌ Les limites
- Tarif élevé face à des SSD sans licence, comme le Corsair à 178,87 € relayé le 10 novembre
- Modèle non testé par Clubic
- 1 To seulement, dont plus d’un cinquième pour GTA 6
- Prix barré fourni par Amazon, sans plus bas sur 30 jours vérifié
Offre Pré-Black Friday annoncée par Amazon jusqu’au 30 novembre, en stock lors de notre relevé du 18 novembre : le SSD SanDisk 1 To à 259,15 €.
À 259,15 €, ce SSD répond à un besoin précis : ajouter un téraoctet à sa PS5 avant GTA 6, sans rien acheter d’autre puisque la licence et le dissipateur sont fournis. La remise de 72,84 € est calculée sur le prix barré par Amazon. Elle ne change pas la position du produit : c’est un SSD haut de gamme pour la console, pas un SSD à petit prix.
Si votre budget prime, un SSD sans licence laisse environ 80 € d’écart pour acheter un dissipateur. Si vous préférez un disque pensé pour la console et prêt à installer, cette offre tient la route. Gardez en tête que nous n’avons pas testé le SanDisk, et vérifiez que le prix affiché sur Amazon est toujours celui de notre relevé du 18 novembre.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?

Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Pas fan de GTA ? Le prix de Battlefield 6 s’effondre sur PS5
articles.text:
Battlefield 6 est actuellement proposé à 25,31 € sur PS5, alors qu’on le trouve habituellement autour de 35 €. Plusieurs enseignes s’alignent sur ce prix.
- Battlefield 6 à 25,31 € chez Amazon
- Battlefield 6 à 25,31 € chez Leclerc, avec le retrait gratuit en magasin
- Battlefield 6 à 25,31 € chez Cdiscount
Tout ce qui tient debout peut tomber
Battlefield 6, c’est le retour de la série à ce qui a fait sa réputation. Des batailles à grande échelle, des chars, des hélicoptères, et des décors que l’on peut réduire en miettes. Un immeuble gêne la progression de votre escouade ? Quelques roquettes bien placées suffisent à changer la carte, et la partie avec. Rien n’est scripté, ce sont les joueurs qui créent le chaos, si bien qu’aucune partie ne ressemble à la précédente.
Les sensations suivent. L’arsenal est très fourni, chaque arme se personnalise en profondeur et les tirs ont un vrai impact. Les combats sont nerveux sans tomber dans la frénésie, et les quatre classes emblématiques (Assaut, Ingénieur, Soutien, Éclaireur) gardent tout leur intérêt pour qui joue en équipe. Les véhicules ont aussi trouvé leur place, avec des hélicoptères qui rappellent les meilleurs souvenirs de Battlefield 4. Les nostalgiques retrouveront même une version modernisée d’Opération Tempête de feu, l’une des cartes cultes de Battlefield 3.
Ce retour aux sources a visiblement parlé aux joueurs. Battlefield 6 s’est écoulé à plus de 7 millions d’exemplaires en trois jours, ce qui en fait le plus gros lancement de l’histoire de la série selon Electronic Arts.
Les saisons se sont enchaînées avec leur lot de nouvelles cartes et de nouvelles armes, et un battle royale gratuit, Battlefield REDSEC, est venu s’ajouter fin octobre 2025. Le mode Portal permet aussi de créer ses propres parties, et même ses propres cartes. De quoi largement rentabiliser l’achat.
Le bon moment pour monter au front ?
Le jeu était sorti à 79,99 € en octobre 2025, et il se vendait encore 64,99 € chez Amazon et Leclerc au moment de notre test. À 25,31 €, il coûte environ trois fois moins cher qu’à son lancement. Seule la Fnac reste un peu au-dessus, à 29,99 €.
Avec un 8/10, notre test le considère comme une proposition très solide. On aurait simplement aimé, au moment du test, un peu plus de variété entre les modes de jeu, qui reposent souvent sur le même principe de capture de zones, et quelques cartes plus marquantes. Depuis, les saisons successives sont venues étoffer l’offre.
Pensez aussi que le multijoueur en ligne demande un abonnement PlayStation Plus, comme pour la plupart des jeux sur PS5. Mais pour retrouver le grand spectacle qui a fait la réputation de la série, à ce prix-là, il y a peu de raisons d’hésiter.
Chez Leclerc, l’offre est disponible jusqu’au 6 décembre 2026. Le jeu se retire gratuitement en Click & Collect ,

articles.title: Ultraviolette X-47 Venom review: An electric crossover that makes more sense on the road?
articles.text:
Ultraviolette X-47 Venom review: An electric crossover that makes more sense on the road?
Ultraviolette’s X-47 Venom gets a 20kg weight reduction, improved battery cooling, more technology and better road manners, making it a compelling electric crossover. Here’s what we think.
Ultraviolette's X-47 was an interesting attempt at combining the performance of an electric motorcycle with the versatility of a crossover. With the new X-47 Venom, the company hasn't reinvented the motorcycle but has made a series of engineering and feature upgrades that could make it a more rounded proposition.
The biggest change is underneath the visuals. The Venom gets a new 100V VX-100 electrical architecture, an updated SRB-11 battery pack, a lighter motor and controller, and an improved battery thermal management system. Depending on the variant, it is around 13-17kg lighter than its predecessor, while offering larger battery options and a higher claimed range. Ultraviolette also claims faster heat dissipation, improved acceleration and a higher top speed.
There are some noticeable changes to the equipment list, too. The older 5-inch instrument display makes way for a 7-inch touchscreen TFT console, while cruise control, updated camera-assisted parking features and radar-based rider assistance systems add to the technology package.
But do these changes make the X-47 Venom a better motorcycle? We spent time riding it on a go-kart track, city roads and some gravel stretches to find out.
Design: Familiar territory, but lighter on its feet
The overall design remains unchanged, as do the motorcycle's dimensions. Swing a leg over and there is little to distinguish the new X-47 Venom from its predecessor in terms of ergonomics. However, once you kick off the stand, the reduction in weight becomes evident.
Ultraviolette hasn't made any significant changes to the styling or the core structural components, including the suspension and wheels. The chassis remains the same, apart from a few tweaks to improve its structural strength.
The Venom retains its crossover proportions, block-pattern tyres and upright riding stance. It may not look dramatically different, but the weight reduction is arguably more important than a cosmetic update, particularly for a motorcycle that has to balance battery capacity with everyday usability.
Features: A technology showcase
On the features front, the X-47 Venom continues to run on 17-inch alloy wheels at both ends, with USD forks at the front and a monoshock at the rear, both preload-adjustable. Braking duties are handled by disc brakes at both ends, supported by dual-channel ABS.
The technology package, however, is where the Venom gets more interesting. The first thing to catch one's eye is the new 7-inch TFT instrument console, replacing the older 5-inch display. It is touch-operated and allows riders to access a host of settings, including traction control levels, regenerative braking, tyre pressure information and ABS modes.
One feature I particularly appreciate is that the touchscreen functionality is disabled when the motorcycle is moving. Riders can only toggle between regenerative braking levels and riding modes while on the move. All other operations require the motorcycle to come to a complete halt. It is a sensible safety measure that prevents unnecessary distractions.
Other notable features include onboard front and rear cameras with parking assistance, along with radar-based systems such as rear collision warning, lane change assist, overtake alert and blindspot detection. Cruise control is another useful addition, particularly for longer highway rides, where maintaining a constant speed can help reduce rider fatigue. The company also claims better range when cruise control is used, however, this is something to test when we have the motorcycle for longer.
Underneath, the new SRB-11 battery pack gets an upgraded thermal management system. Ultraviolette claims up to 50% faster heat dissipation and twice the cooling performance compared with the earlier system. The company also says the battery can return to its optimal operating temperature in 15 minutes, against 30 minutes previously. These are interesting claims, especially for Indian riding conditions, although our short test ride wasn't long enough to evaluate the battery's thermal performance.
The new electrical architecture also brings improvements to performance. The UV LIGHTFURY motor delivers a claimed output of around 40hp and 550Nm of wheel torque, while top speed has increased to 155kmph. The 7.5kWh version offers an IDC-certified range of 227km, while the larger 11kWh variant claims 343km. Ultraviolette also says the Venom can accelerate from 0-100kmph in 5.9 seconds. While acceleration has definitely improved, real-world range is another aspect that we could not test.
Ride and handling: More at home on the road than on the racetrack
We had a go on the X-47 Venom at the Velocity go-kart track, before taking it out into the natural settings where this electric crossover is likely to spend most of its life: city roads, highways and some mild off-roading.
On the racetrack, the motorcycle reminds you that you are riding an EV. As I tipped it into corners, the transition felt like a small step rather than the seamless lean that conventional motorcycles offer. It did not feel quite as natural when changing direction quickly.
This could partly be down to the battery pack and how its weight influences the motorcycle's dynamics, or perhaps the block-pattern tyres, which are designed to offer versatility across different surfaces rather than outright track grip. The chassis, however, remains identical to the older X-47, with no fundamental changes apart from a few tweaks to improve its structural strength.
Move away from the racetrack, though, and the X-47 Venom begins to make much more sense.
On the road, the motorcycle felt completely natural. The rider triangle is excellent, with the rider sitting on top of the electric crossover rather than feeling enclosed within it. The handlebars are comfortably positioned and offer an easy reach, making the riding posture suitable for everyday use as well as longer journeys.
The acceleration is typical Ultraviolette. Riders can choose between a more linear power delivery and the sharper response of Ballistic mode. Regardless of the mode, the acceleration does not disappoint. The instant torque makes overtaking and quick bursts of acceleration effortless, while the different riding modes allow the rider to decide how aggressively the motorcycle responds.
Having shed weight compared with the older motorcycle, the Venom feels lighter and brisker. This is particularly noticeable when negotiating city traffic and changing direction on ordinary roads. The suspension also does a commendable job of soaking up Bengaluru's pothole-ridden roads. The experience remains reasonably composed even with a pillion, although the rear seat could do with better cushioning and comfort, particularly for longer rides.
The braking is predictable, and ABS intervention is not particularly intrusive during normal riding conditions. The motorcycle inspires confidence under braking without the system constantly making its presence felt.
Since our test rides were relatively short, we could not assess the battery's heating and cooling performance or the charging capabilities. However, one aspect worth noting is that the Venom comes with an onboard charger. This means riders only need to carry a charging cable, which does not take up too much space in a backpack. It is a practical addition, particularly for those planning longer journeys.
Off the road, the 200mm ground clearance provides enough confidence to tackle gravel tracks and uneven surfaces. The Venom is capable of handling mild off-roading, but it would be unfair to compare it with purpose-built adventure motorcycles.
It does not have the same off-road credentials as the KTM 390 Adventure R, its sibling, the 390 Enduro R, or the Royal Enfield Himalayan. These motorcycles are designed to handle considerably more demanding terrain. The Venom, instead, is better understood as a road-focused electric crossover that can take the occasional gravel trail or broken road in its stride.
Would I recommend it?
My answer is yes, provided you understand what the X-47 Venom is designed to do.
If your riding primarily involves city commutes, occasional highway runs and limited off-roading, the Venom makes sense. The lower weight, improved acceleration, larger battery options and added convenience features make it a more rounded proposition than its predecessor.
However, if you are looking for a serious adventure motorcycle that can tackle demanding trails, rough terrain and extended off-road journeys, KTM and Royal Enfield remain the more appropriate choices.
As a second motorcycle in the garage, though, the X-47 Venom is a fun proposition. It offers the performance and instant acceleration associated with Ultraviolette, while adding a degree of everyday practicality and versatility.
The Venom may not have changed dramatically on the outside, but the engineering updates make it a more appealing electric crossover. It is not trying to replace a conventional adventure motorcycle. Instead, it makes a case for being a versatile, technology-packed electric motorcycle that is enjoyable on everyday roads.

articles.title: Réseau mobile : l'Arcep désigne le meilleur opérateur entre Orange, SFR, Free et Bouygues
articles.text:
L’Arcep (l’Autorité de régulation des communications électroniques, des postes et de la distribution de la presse) vient de publier son étude comparative des réseaux mobiles d’Orange, SFR, Bouygues Telecom et Free Mobile pour 2026. Cette étude a été menée entre mai et août 2026 dans tous les départements de France métropolitaine. Au total, plus d’un million de mesures ont été effectuées durant cette période, dans des zones urbaines et rurales, dans les transports en commun et à bord de TGV. L’étude porte par ailleurs sur les réseaux 2G, 3G, 4G et 5G NSA. La 5G Standalone (SA) n’a quant à elle pas été prise en compte. Alors, quel bilan tirer de cette étude comparative ? Autant dire qu’Orange tire son épingle du jeu.
Débits mobiles : Orange en tête, les zones rurales restent mal couvertes
Tout d’abord, l’Arcep a comparé les performances des réseaux mobiles des quatre opérateurs français, dans toutes les zones, selon trois seuils : un débit dépassant 3 Mbit/s (usages peu exigeants, comme la navigation web), un débit dépassant 8 Mbit/s (usages courants, comme le visionnage de vidéos) et un débit dépassant 30 Mbit/s (pour des usages plus exigeants).
Comme nous pouvons le voir sur le graphique ci-dessus, Orange est en tête sur les trois seuils (94 %, 90 % et 82 %), tandis que les trois autres opérateurs sont au coude-à-coude.
Ensuite, l’Arcep a comparé les performances des réseaux mobiles des quatre opérateurs selon les trois seuils de débit mentionnés plus haut (3 Mbit/s, 8 Mbit/s et 30 Mbit/s), et selon trois types de zones : rurales, intermédiaires et denses.
Sans grande surprise, les performances de l’Internet mobile diminuent fortement en zones rurales (seuls 53 à 60 % des tests dépassent 30 Mbit/s). Dans ces zones, Orange tire son épingle du jeu pour les seuils de 3 Mbit/s (86 %) et de 8 Mbit/s (78 %), mais se retrouve ex æquo avec Free Mobile (60 %) pour le seuil de 30 Mbit/s. En zones intermédiaires et denses, les performances sont assez similaires, mais Orange se démarque tout de même sur le seuil de 30 Mbit/s avec 91 % en zone intermédiaire (contre 84 % pour Free Mobile) et 95 % en zone dense (contre 85 % pour Free Mobile). Pour rappel, l’Arcep avait déjà relevé la faible couverture des réseaux mobiles en zones rurales dans son rapport de 2025.
D’excellents résultats dans les métros, mais la situation reste compliquée dans les TGV
Dans son rapport de 2026, l’Arcep fait état d’une qualité élevée des réseaux mobiles sur les routes et dans les métros. Sur les routes, les résultats sont les suivants : SFR (93 %), Bouygues Telecom (92 %), Orange (92 %) et Free Mobile (88 %). Sur le réseau RER et Transilien, l’Arcep conclut que « les quatre opérateurs sont ex æquo, avec 87 % à 90 % d’appels réussis et maintenus ».
En revanche, la situation se complique pour les appels passés dans les TGV, avec seulement 30 % à 44 % des appels en qualité parfaite. Là aussi, Orange tire son épingle du jeu avec 44 %, contre 30 % à 34 % pour ses concurrents. Si l’on prend en compte les appels réussis et maintenus pendant deux minutes, Orange obtient même un score de 77 %, contre 67 à 68 % pour les trois autres opérateurs.
En ce qui concerne la navigation sur Internet dans les TGV, Orange est également en tête du classement : 79 % des pages web se chargent en moins de cinq secondes, contre 67 % chez Free Mobile. Selon les résultats de l’enquête de l’Arcep, Orange semble donc être le meilleur opérateur pour les personnes voyageant souvent en train.

articles.title: Microsoft’s Agent Framework PyPI package compromised to steal credentials
articles.text:
Hackers compromised Microsoft's official Agent Framework Python package on PyPI, publishing two malicious versions designed to steal cloud credentials and other sensitive information from developers' systems.
Microsoft Agent Framework is Microsoft's open-source toolkit for building AI agents and coordinating them in workflows. It's a fairly popular tool with roughly 200,000 monthly downloads on PyPI.
The malicious releases, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on November 17, 2026, and contained a credential stealer that executed automatically during normal Python startup in affected environments, even when the Agent Framework package was not imported.
Both versions retained their dependency on the legitimate agent-framework-core 1.26.0 package, allowing the framework to function normally while the malware ran in the background.
Multiple security firms discovered and documented the attack, including Socket, Step Security, and Ox Security.
Version 1.26.1 contained a credential stealer that harvested secrets from environment variables, local configuration files, and other running processes where permissions allowed, targeting Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face, OpenAI, and other services.
The malware also attempted to obtain Azure managed identity access tokens and Azure DevOps OIDC tokens, potentially giving attackers access to additional cloud resources.
Version 1.26.2 added GitHub Actions OIDC token requests and searches of GitHub runner directories.
According to Socket and StepSecurity, the first malicious release used agent_framework_meta.pth to execute the credential stealer in agent_framework_meta/_telemetry.py during Python startup.
The second release restored the original package initializer and moved the malicious code into af_runtime_diag.pth and af_runtime_diag.py.
Both versions exfiltrated collected data to the same attacker-controlled endpoint, https://webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb.
PyPI quarantined the first malicious release, but the attacker published a second version roughly 2.5 minutes later, which was also quarantined about eight minutes afterward. The second release indicates that the attacker still had publishing access after the initial quarantine.
It remains unclear how the attacker gained access to publish malicious releases under Microsoft's official PyPI project.
BleepingComputer has contacted Microsoft to learn what the point of breach was, but we have not received a response by publication time.
Developers who installed either malicious version should isolate affected environments, avoid running Python or pip until they are secured, and rebuild from a known-clean environment using the safe 1.26.0 release.
Any potentially exposed credentials that were within the reach of the compromised environment should be rotated immediately.
To determine the exact level of compromise, investigators should look for the specific webhook URL path in egress logs and distinguish blocked requests from completed transfers.

articles.title: "Aquí están los 4 trabajos que resistirán a la Inteligencia Artificial". Las predicciones de Bill Gates y el plan de Microsoft.
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial va a cambiar bastante el mercado laboral, pero Bill Gates cree que hay terrenos en los que las personas seguirán siendo necesarias, y señala cuatro: la programación, la biología, la energía y el deporte profesional. Y es que, aunque la automatización asuma cada vez más tareas, eso no implica que los trabajadores vayan a desaparecer de todos los ámbitos.
El deporte, para las personas. Gates puso ese ejemplo en The Tonight Show en 2025. Cuando el presentador le preguntó si seguiremos necesitando a los humanos, contestó que no para la mayoría de las cosas, pero añadió que eso lo decidiremos nosotros: “Como el béisbol. No vamos a querer ver a ordenadores jugando al béisbol”. Vamos, que hay actividades cuya gracia está en que las hacen personas.
La IA como acelerador. En las otras tres áreas, la tecnología haría de acelerador más que de sustituto. Gates ha hecho múltiples declaraciones declarando que la IA ya puede generar código, pero los programadores siguen siendo necesarios para detectar y corregir errores y para hacer avanzar la propia IA. De hecho, en una entrevista con Axios Gates defendió que conviene seguir aprendiendo a programar aunque los ordenadores lo hagan muy bien, para entender lo que hay debajo.
Biología y energía. La misma recopilación le atribuye la idea de que la IA diagnostica bien enfermedades y analiza el ADN, aunque le falta la creatividad que piden la investigación biológica y los descubrimientos científicos, mientras que la energía sería un campo demasiado complejo para automatizarlo del todo.
Lo que sí se automatizará. En la misma charla con Fallon en Tonight Show, Gates avanzó que “en lo que respecta a fabricar cosas, moverlas y cultivar alimentos, con el tiempo serán problemas básicamente resueltos”, lo que afecta a la industria, la logística y la agricultura. Eso sí, también dejó claro que “habrá algunas cosas que nos reservaremos”, así que tocará decidir como sociedad qué tareas queremos seguir dejando en manos de personas.
Las salidas voluntarias de Microsoft. El debate coincide con los ajustes de plantilla de las grandes tecnológicas. Microsoft anunció el 26 de octubre de 2026 un programa de salidas voluntarias por tiempo limitado, con apoyo económico y recursos para planificar la carrera profesional, dirigido a empleados elegibles de los equipos que participan en Estados Unidos, Canadá, Reino Unido e India, pudiendo acogerse a él unos 60.000 empleados, más de una cuarta parte de la plantilla.

articles.title: AWS PrivateLink Tunnel Endpoints Open a Whole CIDR Range to Another Account
articles.text:
AWS has published a technical walkthrough of tunnel endpoints, a VPC endpoint type launched in September that lets an application in one VPC reach every address in a CIDR range shared from another account, instead of one resource at a time. The provider shares a CIDR-type resource configuration through AWS Resource Access Manager and the consumer creates a tunnel endpoint against it. From then on, anything inside the range is reachable, including resources that did not exist when the share was made.
Bruce Pinsky and Ashish Kumar of AWS frame it as a vendor-access problem, for "a vendor or service provider whose software must reach applications and resources in a customer's network." Until now, that meant a separate PrivateLink resource configuration per database or host, which breaks down when the resources are ephemeral, or the customer does not want to enumerate them. With a CIDR configuration, the customer defines a perimeter in address ranges, and "resources located outside the perimeter can't be reached by the vendor." Two further properties come with the design: the consumer and provider VPCs can use overlapping CIDR blocks, and connections "can start only from the consumer VPC, not from the provider network."
(Source: AWS Networking & Content Delivery blog)
On the r/aws thread about the September launch, the first question was what this does that VPC peering does not, from a self-described veteran of AWS's advanced networking components. The answers that followed are the use cases: a peering connection exposes the whole VPC in both directions, while a tunnel endpoint shares a subset of the address space in one direction only; one commenter at a bank wrote that "peering with unregulated partners is a massive no-no, the auditors will rip you to shreds for it." Another pointed to clusters that do client-side load balancing, such as self-managed Kafka or Aerospike, which until now needed port-based routing on a Network Load Balancer and a separate port-mapping horizon for connections arriving over an interface endpoint. The same thread drew the line against VPC Lattice itself: Lattice services work at layer 7, tunnel endpoints at layer 4 without a resource configuration per target.
The unusual part is on the consumer side: the application's traffic has to arrive at the tunnel endpoint wrapped in GENEVE, the encapsulation protocol defined in RFC 8926, over UDP port 6081 and in the same Availability Zone. The endpoint strips the header, checks that the inner destination falls inside the shared range, rewrites the source to a resource gateway address, and forwards a plain packet into the provider VPC. Linux can do the wrapping in the kernel. The walkthrough creates an ip link add ... type geneve id 0 device inside its own network namespace with a default route through it, which sends the provider's ranges into the tunnel and leaves the instance's other traffic alone. On the far side, the resources see the resource gateway as the client, so the post advises security groups that reference the gateway's security group or subnet rather than a single address.
The documentation lists the constraints. Inner traffic must be TCP, with UDP permitted only for DNS, so ICMP and ping do not work, and IP fragments are dropped. Private DNS names are not supported on tunnel endpoints. The endpoint's subnets must sit in Availability Zones that overlap with the resource gateway's, or the association shows as inaccessible. A resource gateway's DNS setting cannot be changed after creation. And the access logs identify the consumer's endpoint but carry no field for the inner source address, so a provider can attribute traffic to a vendor and not to a workload behind that vendor's endpoint. The post also warns that sharing 0.0.0.0/0 grants access to everything the provider VPC can route to, including networks behind VPC peering, Direct Connect or a Site-to-Site VPN, and recommends sharing the narrowest ranges that work.
Both points have been tested in practice. Ryo Suzuki of the Japanese consultancy Classmethod connected two VPCs that both use 10.0.0.0/16 and got HTTP through, but only by running a GENEVE relay as root on the client, by routing a /32 per destination host, or by putting an HAProxy or NAT instance in front, each of which adds a hop or a single point of failure; his conclusion was that "route management according to the number of destinations is required." In a second experiment, he shared 0.0.0.0/0 from a VPC with a NAT gateway and reached the internet from a VPC with no gateway at all, which confirmed AWS's warning from the other side; he judged it workable as a temporary path and "difficult to use in a permanent production setup."
Pricing is an hourly charge per tunnel endpoint plus a per-GB charge for data processed, under PrivateLink pricing, with the provider side billed per GB through the resource gateway under VPC Lattice pricing, and the feature is available in 28 regions. Terraform support followed from the community: a contributor request opened two days after launch was implemented by another contributor and shipped in version 6.71.0 of the AWS provider, as a Tunnel endpoint type on aws_vpc_endpoint and a cidr_resource block on the Lattice resource configuration.

articles.title: Pennsylvania high school disables AI weapons detector after it keeps mistaking everyday items for guns
articles.text:
Facepalm: It's no secret that AI often gets things wrong, with varying degrees of consequences. It can be pretty serious when the system in question is supposed to detect weapons being sneaked into an educational facility. But that's the situation in one Pennsylvania high school, which has deactivated its AI-powered weapons detector after it kept identifying everyday items as potential threats.
Hempfield Area High School is one of several schools across Pennsylvania that agreed to help train Wi-AI. Developed by CurvePoint, a Carnegie Mellon University spinout, Wi-AI uses Wi-Fi signals to look for concealed weapons.
Small sensors called SensePods, installed near school entrances, measure how people and the objects they carry change the way radio waves bounce around them. The software looks for patterns it associates with a weapon and can alert staff by text, email, or through a dashboard. The system works without cameras, and CurvePoint says it can also track movement and occupancy without storing information that identifies individuals.
During the pilot program, the system continued to collect training data on students once they had entered the building, but it had trouble telling the difference between a weapon and the usual items carried by kids, such as binders, metal water bottles, and battery packs, resulting in a high number of false positives.
It had been hoped that the model would achieve an accuracy rate of 95%, which could have made it the primary security system at the high school. But Superintendent Dr. Mark Holtzman told WTAE-TV (Channel 4), "It's not near 95%, I could tell you that much."
Skip Smith, co-founder and CEO of CurvePoint, said, "Hempfield has served as a testing and evaluation site for our school safety technology, rather than an operational deployment."
"We're continuing to develop and evaluate the technology, but we are not currently supporting operational deployments, and we don't have a deployment date to announce."
Smith blamed the WiAI's problems on "environmental challenges that affect reliability and consistency."
The school district will get back the money it paid for the detectors because the program wasn't launched full-time, though Holtzman said Hempfield was open to testing CurvePoint's technology in the future. For now, the school is sticking with its long-used OpenGate walk-through weapons detector.
This isn't the first time a school's AI-powered security system has been less than perfect. Last year, a 16-year-old high school student at Kenwood High School in Baltimore County, Maryland, was swarmed and handcuffed by police after an AI linked to the school's security cameras mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun.

articles.title: It shouldn’t be this easy to pedal 25 mph: Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo
articles.text:
I’ve had only one experience of pedaling an e-bike after it ran out of juice, but it was enough to make checking the battery display an anxiety-driven habit: “Can I afford to use the highest assist level up this hill? Should I switch to eco mode to preserve power and make sure I have enough to get home with the bike lights on?”
These aren’t fun questions to have rattling around in your head while riding home in the dark.
But those intrusive thoughts never crossed my mind while I was testing Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo. I didn’t experience range anxiety, even while blowing through city streets at 25-plus mph (40.2 kph). The bike has so much juice (840 watt-hours) and power (810 watts of peak power and 105 newton-meters of torque) from Specialized’s 3.1 motor system that I could ride as far and as fast as I wanted without worrying about having enough battery to get back home.
Given my preference for biking over driving, I need a bike that can get me across town at a decent clip without draining an entire charge. That’s exactly what the Evo delivered on my longest rides.
What sold me on the bike was a 24-mile round trip that took 83 minutes and used just 56 percent of the battery. According to Specialized’s app, which connects to the bike over Bluetooth, I averaged 235 W of assist power while moving an average of 17 mph, though I was generally closer to 20 mph on stretches where I didn’t have to slow down. I also hit a max speed of 27.3 mph with little effort.
Power and comfort
The bike is a beast, weighing around 70 pounds for the large-size frame I tested. Despite being the heaviest e-bike I’ve ridden, the Evo makes pedaling easier than ever. The bike lacks a throttle, so it takes a few rotations to get moving, but once the assist kicks in, it’s remarkable how easily you can reach the 18–20 mph range.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos aseguró que estuvo involucrado en elegir el nuevo papel de Robert Pattinson: “él es James Bond”
articles.text:
Jeff Bezos afirmó que participó de forma directa en la elección de Robert Pattinson como el nuevo James Bond, después de que Amazon MGM Studios asumiera el control creativo de la franquicia. El fundador de Amazon señaló que el equipo redujo una lista amplia de aspirantes a cinco finalistas y resolvió la selección el pasado viernes.
La revelación ofrece una mirada poco habitual al proceso detrás de uno de los papeles más codiciados del cine. Pattinson será el próximo agente 007 bajo la dirección de Denis Villeneuve, mientras Amazon MGM Studios prepara una etapa nueva para una saga que, durante décadas, cambió de intérprete sin perder presencia internacional.
Jeff Bezos describió pruebas de pantalla con cinco finalistas
Bezos habló sobre la búsqueda del protagonista durante el evento Silicon Valley & The World, organizado por Semafor en California. Según explicó, el proceso terminó con cinco candidatos que participaron en pruebas de pantalla con condiciones similares a las de una producción cinematográfica.
Cada actor interpretó tres escenas con vestuario completo, decorados reales y otros intérpretes. El objetivo era observar cómo funcionaban dentro del universo de James Bond, más allá de sus trabajos anteriores o de su nivel de popularidad.
“Seguimos un proceso muy riguroso y tomamos la decisión final el viernes (13 de noviembre de 2026)”, afirmó Bezos. El empresario añadió que pasó varias horas junto con un grupo de trabajo, incluido Villeneuve, revisando las interpretaciones de los finalistas.
Entre los actores que, según se informó, llegaron a realizar pruebas para el papel figuraban Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor, Jack Lowden y Nicholas Hoult. Bezos no confirmó sus nombres durante su intervención.
Pattinson convenció al equipo pese a que ya era una figura conocida
El fundador de Amazon indicó que la búsqueda comenzó con una preferencia por un intérprete menos conocido. El grupo consideraba que la fama previa podía condicionar la recepción del próximo 007, una preocupación que ha estado presente en otros relevos dentro de la franquicia.
Pattinson, sin embargo, alteró esa evaluación durante las pruebas. “Había algo especial en Rob y en sus interpretaciones”, explicó Bezos. “No hubo debate alguno. Todos nos inclinamos por Rob”. Más tarde, resumió el resultado con otra frase: “En las pruebas de pantalla era tan evidente: él es James Bond”.
El actor señaló que asumir el papel representa “el honor de toda una vida”. En un comunicado difundido tras el anuncio, sostuvo que calificar el proyecto como un sueño cumplido resultaba insuficiente.
La elección coloca a Pattinson en una lista formada por Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan y Daniel Craig. Varios de sus predecesores llegaron al personaje con una carrera más vinculada al teatro, la televisión o producciones de menor alcance.
La carrera de Robert Pattinson pasó de Crepúsculo a producciones de autor y grandes estudios
Robert Pattinson alcanzó reconocimiento internacional durante su adolescencia por su papel de Edward Cullen en la saga Crepúsculo. Antes había interpretado a Cedric Diggory en Harry Potter.
En los años posteriores, combinó películas independientes con producciones de gran presupuesto. Entre sus papeles más visibles figura Bruce Wayne en The Batman, una interpretación que lo situó al frente de otra franquicia de alcance mundial.
También trabajó recientemente con Villeneuve en Dune: Parte Tres, donde interpretó a un asesino capaz de cambiar de forma. Esa colaboración previa conecta al actor con el director que tendrá a su cargo la próxima película de Bond.
El guion estará escrito por Steven Knight, creador de la serie británica Peaky Blinders. Por ahora, no hay fecha de estreno ni título confirmado para la nueva entrega.
Brad Pitt y Florence Pugh mostraron interés en el papel del villano
La elección de Pattinson abrió preguntas sobre el resto del reparto. Una de las incógnitas pasa por la identidad del antagonista, y dos actores expresaron públicamente su interés en participar.
Brad Pitt, citado por Complex, dejó un mensaje dirigido a Villeneuve: “Apúntenme. Pónganme al teléfono con Denis Villeneuve”. Florence Pugh fue más directa y escribió al cineasta para felicitarlo por encontrar a su Bond.
La actriz preguntó si existía espacio para una “villana femenina de 5,4”, una referencia a su estatura de 163 centímetros. Pugh aparecerá antes de terminar 2026 en Dune: Parte Tres y Vengadores: Doomsday.
Pitt, por su parte, estrenará Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth, una película junto a Quentin Tarantino y David Fincher. Ninguno de los dos forma parte oficialmente del reparto de 007.
Amazon MGM Studios todavía debe anunciar el resto de los personajes, el inicio del rodaje y la fecha de llegada a los cines.

articles.title: Why Canadian tech is standing against Bill C-22
articles.text:
The Canadian government has picked a particularly inconvenient time to make the case that companies should introduce backdoor vulnerabilities and retain more user data, for longer.
Much of the digital world seemingly broke this past week. A hacker injected malicious JavaScript code into more than 100 major websites; systems like US air control and banks experienced widespread outages; Microsoft Outlook and Copilot crashed; and a cyberattack hit a Norwegian energy giant. Not all of the disruptions were caused by hacks—many appeared to be problems with outdated code—but, as a whole, the incidents contributed to the growing sense that we’re in a precarious moment for cybersecurity.
It was in the shadow of that chaos that Canada’s Senate held a committee meeting to hear from tech leaders and civil liberties advocates on Bill C-22, the controversial lawful access legislation. Leaders at companies including Meta, Tailscale, Signal, and Animikii took the floor to stress that without significant changes, the proposed bill will either force their companies to stop serving Canadians or, in the case of Tailscale, create risks for their customers abroad.
David Shipley, CEO and Founder of New Brunswick-based cybersecurity firm Beauceron Security, urged the government to focus on building up secure systems first, before opening even more holes in it that bad actors could access.
“When parliament set out to protect critical systems, [the legislation] stayed narrow. Hospitals, food supply, water systems remained dangerously exposed … When it set out to access systems for spying, the reach became nearly limitless, down to, in theory, a daycare. We are cautious when protecting Canadians, but expansive when surveilling them. It must be the other way around,” Shipley urged senators during Monday evening’s meeting.
The invite to speak at committee also apparently went out to critics at the last minute, a move Citizen Lab director Ron Deibert called “fundamentally unserious.” It’s not entirely unusual for Senate meeting requests to come at short notice, but it raises an eyebrow when paired with the bill’s passing in the House in a fast-tracked vote this summer with limited debate. It appears as if the government is readying to hand law enforcement (and potentially other actors) the keys to Canadians’ communication—at a time when the locks are already looking flimsy.
Sarah Rieger,

articles.title: OneTrust's Fall '26 Release expands AI visibility, privacy and third-party risk tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OneTrust’s Fall ’26 Release expands AI visibility, privacy and third-party risk tools
Governance platform provider OneTrust LLC today announced its Fall ’26 Release, a set of platform updates said to bring governance into the workflows where business decisions are made.
Building on OneTrust CORIE, a shared intelligence layer for governing artificial intelligence agents introduced at the company’s TrustWeek conference in September, the release covers AI visibility, privacy, consent and third-party risk management.
Leading the list of updates is a revised AI inventory, which is designed to reflect changes across a customer’s environment on a continuous basis. According to OneTrust, the change is needed because many organizations running complex networks of AI systems and agents have only limited visibility into how those systems operate. Model associations, potential matches and deprecation indicators from providers are now pulled into the inventory from a curated library of foundation models.
Relationships among AI systems, models, agents, projects, risks, controls and workflows can be explored through an interactive AI lineage view. AI performance and operational dashboards, added in the release, bring usage, associated risk, evaluation coverage, outbound personally identifiable information discovery and token consumption into one summary.
Ryan Karlin, vice president of product management at OneTrust, said knowing which AI systems are in the business “is just the starting point.” According to Karlin, teams also need visibility into the activity and dependencies of those systems “alongside the privacy and third-party risks they already manage.”
On the third-party risk side, a workflow rule that launches a risk assessment can now trigger OneTrust’s Deep Research AI skill. The in-depth research report that the skill compiles from public data sources is then used to answer the assessment questionnaire. OneTrust claims the integration can cut the time needed to complete a third-party risk assessment from weeks to minutes.
Drawing on previous assessments and supplier documentation, the company’s expanded AI Document Scanning and Inventory Response Analysis features can now also answer questions about the business engagement tied to a third party.
For privacy teams, the release adds protections against automated abuse of data subject request web forms. Growing volumes of those automated requests are straining team workloads, according to OneTrust. To filter out the abuse, enhanced CAPTCHA options now work alongside cross-site request forgery token controls to block suspicious submissions.
In the company’s consent management platform, navigation, configuration, scanning, publishing and geolocation management have also been brought into a single workflow under a modernized interface.
Rounding out the release are reporting updates. Enhanced assessment reporting and application programming interfaces are said to give privacy teams more insight into what drives risk scores. New risk hierarchy visualizations, which show how individual risks across business units aggregate into enterprise risk categories, are aimed at helping teams prioritize risk treatment.
OneTrust is sharing availability details for the Fall ’26 Release through an overview webinar.
OneTrust has raised $1.13 billion to date, including $150 million in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Investors in the company include Insight Partners LP, Coatue Management, Technology Crossover Ventures LP, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 LP, Franklin Resources Inc., Generation Investment Management LLP and Sands Capital Management.

articles.title: Meta anuncia novo app de mensagens; Direct é baseado nas DMs do Instagram • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Meta anuncia novo app de mensagens; Direct é baseado nas DMs do Instagram
Aplicativo de mensagens está em testes na Turquia e na Tailândia. Não é necessário ter uma conta do Instagram para logar.
A Meta revelou seu novo app Direct, uma espécie de DM independente do Instagram. O mensageiro é mais uma alternativa ao WhatsApp oferecido pela empresa, que também tem o já tradicional Facebook Messenger. Aqui, o diferencial fica por conta de recursos como desenhos, figurinhas e efeitos de voz – ou seja, não muda muita coisa em relação aos outros.
A empresa de Mark Zuckerberg também promete segurança reforçada, mas sem grandes novidades. Segundo o comunicado da Meta, o Direct restringe as mensagens aos seus contatos e permite bloquear, restringir e reportar pessoas. Eles garantem ainda que “vão agir se alguém infringir as regras”, e que o app utiliza “tecnologia para detectar interações inapropriadas com usuários jovens”.
O acesso não requer uma conta no Instagram: é possível logar com um e-mail ou celular que não esteja cadastrado, por exemplo. O aplicativo também é proibido para menores de 13 anos, sendo necessário fazer uma verificação de idade para manter a conta.
Por enquanto, o Direct está disponível em celulares Android e iPhone (iOS) na Turquia e na Tailândia. Não há detalhes sobre a chegada ao Brasil.
A Meta destaca algumas funcionalidades que incrementam a troca de mensagens no aplicativo. Entre as “novidades” estão a possibilidade de enviar desenhos, criar notas (as mesmas do Instagram), gerar figurinhas e enviar efeitos de som. Também será possível personalizar o fundo das conversas.
Já em termos de segurança, as promessas passam por garantias padrão de apps do tipo, como a possibildiade de remover contatos, identificação de mensagens inapropriadas e controles parentais como ferramentas de supervisão e configurações para controlar o tempo de uso do aplicativo. Ou seja, nada muito diferente do que já é feito na própria DM ou nos outros mensageiros da empresa.
O Direct é, no final das contas, uma forma de acessar mais rapidamente as DMs do Instagram – como o Facebook Messenger se propõe a ser, por exemplo.
O acesso pode ser feito tanto pela sua conta da Meta quanto via e-mail ou celular. Nesse último caso, você só pode trocar mensagens e criar grupos com seus contatos salvos.
