articles.title: From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents
AWS Quick User Group DC inaugural meetup recap
Many organizations are asking how to move beyond static reporting dashboards and begin using generative and agentic AI. But before an AI agent can answer questions or help teams act, it requires a trusted data foundation.
On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, data leaders, developers, and practitioners gathered at the AWS Skills Center in Arlington, Virginia, for the AWS Quick User Group DC meetup. The session brought together founders, software engineers, and enterprise leaders, among them a team from Financial Independence Group (FIG). Attendees explored practical strategies for modernizing legacy architectures, preparing structured data for agentic workflows, and automating routine tasks with no-code tools.
        User groups like this provide a forum for peer-to-peer learning and collaborative problem-solving. The event offered attendees an inside look at how organizations are putting AWS Quick to work to drive productivity gains.
What’s new with AWS Quick: Agents, skills, and connectors
For many in the room, this meetup was a first look at what agentic AI looks like in practice with AWS Quick.
The meetup kicked off by exploring the latest product capabilities across AWS Quick, focusing on its evolution into a unified AI assistant for work. Rather than functioning solely as a traditional business intelligence visualization tool, AWS Quick unifies analytics, natural-language interaction, and multi-step task orchestration.
- AWS Quick agents and skills: Turn natural-language questions into multi-step reusable actions that aid in decision making across enterprise data.
- Third-party connectors: AWS Quick includes built-in integrations that connect tools like Salesforce, Slack, Google Drive, and Microsoft 365, breaking down data silos.
- Unified workspace: A cohesive environment that bridges research, automated visual generation, and business artifact creation (presentations, documents, and spreadsheets) directly where users work.
Real-world innovation: Moving to AI analytics and agentic systems
The core of the day highlighted a real-world customer journey showing how one enterprise is rethinking its data architecture so AI agents can work from governed, trusted data.
Financial Independence Group: Innovating at the pace of technology
Vanessa Gonzalez, Vice President of AI at Financial Independence Group (FIG), shared how FIG keeps pushing past what’s possible today. They’re adopting new tools and platforms as technology changes, and building toward AI-powered analytics and agentic systems on top of their data with AWS Quick.
Technology is changing fast, and FIG wants to be at the front of that change. Building on its existing analytics, FIG moved to AWS Quick, a platform that brings AI into its dashboards, reporting, and analytics. AWS Quick is FIG’s “single front door” for enterprise analytics. It brings together structured data such as customer relationship management (CRM) systems, databases, and finance data. It also pulls in unstructured content such as internal knowledge bases, policy documents, and collateral, through a governed data layer. That gives FIG a base for AI-powered insights and agentic workflows built on its own data.
- The AI analytics loop: Moving from reporting on what already happened to a continuous cycle: Ask → Analyze → Automate → Act.
- Centralized discovery: An analytics portal organized by business area (sales, operations, marketing, commissions), with built-in AI chat assistants so teams can talk directly to their documents and datasets.
- Democratized insights: Self-service exploration tools for non-technical business users, plus a learning hub that builds prompt engineering and AI skills across teams while keeping proper governance in place.
Hands-on: Building apps and no-code flows
Attendees worked through two hands-on exercises:
- Build an AWS Quick app in 50 minutes: Every attendee in the room successfully designed and launched a custom application in AWS Quick. This showed how fast non-technical users and developers alike can deploy purpose-built decision tools without writing code.
- AWS Quick Flows workshop: A subset of six participants dove deeper into workflow automation. They built multi-step, event-triggered flows that handle repetitive data tasks, replacing manual reporting handoffs with automated, repeatable pipelines.
One of the key takeaways is how quickly teams can go from an idea to a working solution with AWS Quick. New ideas now take hours or even minutes to build, not weeks or months.
Looking ahead and getting involved
| Figure 6: Attendees during the closing group discussion | The event concluded with an open group discussion where attendees shared practical observations on bridging the gap between legacy infrastructure and generative AI. As organizations move toward agentic architectures, the consensus from the DC user group was clear: successful AI adoption isn’t only about selecting a foundation model. It starts with intentional data design, unified access, and empowering teams to build practical automations. Building fast isn’t only about tools. It also means learning from each other, which is why events like this matter. | 
Next steps
Ready to try it yourself? Start with the AWS Quick product page and the AWS Quick user guide, then connect a data source you already use and ask your first question. From there, try building an app or an AWS Quick Flows automation for a task your team repeats every week.
Join the community
- Connect with peers: Stay up to date on upcoming meetups and presentations by joining the AWS Quick User Group on LinkedIn and participating in the AWS Quick Community.
- Explore upcoming sessions: Keep an eye out for details on our next DC-area meetup, featuring detailed hands-on architectural sessions and customer lightning talks.

articles.title: From Deepfakes to Helpdesk Impersonation: Why Stronger Verification Matters
articles.text:
In 2024, an employee at engineering firm Arup was tricked into transferring $25 million after attending a fake video conference featuring deepfake versions of their colleagues.
A year later, Marks & Spencer (M&S) suffered a major cyberattack after attackers used social engineering to gain access through a third-party helpdesk.
More recently, attackers have impersonated IT support staff to convince employees to hand over remote access to their devices.
While the tactics differ, these incidents raise an important question for IT and security teams: how can organizations be confident that someone requesting access or authorizing a sensitive action is who they claim to be?
We examine these attacks and explore how stronger identity verification and more secure workflows can help organizations defend against similar threats.
The Arup Deepfake Fraud
A finance employee at engineering firm Arup's Hong Kong office received an email in January 2024 that appeared to come from the company's UK-based CFO, requesting a series of transactions. Initially suspicious, the employee was convinced the request was genuine after joining a video conference featuring what appeared to be the CFO and several colleagues.
However, the meeting was a deepfake. According to Hong Kong police, the attackers had used publicly available video and audio to create a convincing pre-recorded conference.
The employee subsequently made multiple transfers, losing approximately HK$200 million (US$25.6 million).
The M&S Cyberattack
In April 2025, British retailer Marks & Spencer (M&S) suffered a major cyberattack that disrupted operations for weeks. Online orders were suspended, contactless payments and Click & Collect services were affected, and customer data was stolen.
M&S initially estimated the incident would reduce its 2025/26 operating profit by around £300 million before mitigation.
The attack was linked to the Scattered Spider cybercriminal group, known for using social engineering to gain access to corporate networks.
M&S later confirmed that attackers had gained entry by deceiving employees at a third-party contractor, rather than exploiting a technical vulnerability in its systems.
Secure your Active Directory passwords with Specops Password Policy
Verizon’s Data Breach Investigation Report found stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches. 
Effortlessly secure Active Directory with compliant password policies, blocking 4+ billion compromised passwords, boosting security, and slashing support hassles!
Fake IT Support
Microsoft recently reported a cyberattack campaign in which threat actors impersonated IT support staff through Microsoft Teams, tricking employees into handing over remote access to their devices.
The attackers contacted employees through external Teams messages or calls, posing as internal IT personnel. Using convincing pretexts such as urgent technical issues, they persuaded employees to grant remote control through screen sharing or legitimate support tools like Quick Assist.
Once connected, the attackers used PowerShell to install malicious software, establish persistent access and gather information about the compromised network.
Microsoft also observed attempts to move laterally towards critical infrastructure, including domain controllers and certificate authorities.
The Common Thread: Trust Replacing Verification
Impersonation Exploits Familiar Trust Signals
Social engineering has long been a key technique in attackers’ arsenals. They don't need sophisticated malware or technical exploits to compromise an organization if they can convince someone that they're a trusted colleague.
Deepfake technology makes this particularly concerning, as familiar faces and voices can be recreated.
But even without AI, attackers can use convincing pretexts and trusted communication platforms to make fraudulent requests appear legitimate.
Trusted Processes Can Become Attack Vectors
Password resets and remote IT support are routine activities, but they can also give attackers opportunities to gain access if requests aren't properly verified.
Third-party providers expand the potential attack surface; organizations may have strong controls over their own systems but less visibility into how external support teams verify identities and authorize sensitive actions.
Employees Can't Be Expected to Spot Every Impersonation Attempt
Security awareness training helps employees recognize suspicious requests, but even well-trained staff can be deceived by convincing impersonation attempts.
Attackers will carry out reconnaissance beforehand to gather information that makes their social engineering attempts appear like routine requests.
Organizations need reliable verification processes that support employees when they're asked to make security-sensitive decisions, rather than leaving them to judge whether someone can be trusted.
How Can Organizations Mitigate These Risks?
Strengthen Identity Verification at the Service Desk
Rather than relying on security questions or personal information that attackers may have obtained, service desk teams should use trusted authentication methods to confirm callers' identities.
Specops Secure Service Desk helps organizations build this verification into their service desk processes. Agents can verify callers using more than 15 MFA factors, including options that don't require a phone, with integrations for existing identity platforms such as Duo and Okta.
This helps ensure that sensitive account recovery actions are supported by reliable identity checks, reducing opportunities for attackers to exploit service desk procedures.
To see it in action, explore our interactive walkthrough and discover how agents can securely verify callers before carrying out sensitive account actions.
Build Verification Into Business Workflows
As organizations introduce self-service portals, internal chatbots and automated IT processes, it's important that these systems follow the same verification standards as traditional support channels.
A password reset request made through an internal chatbot, for example, should still require strong identity verification before the request is processed.
It’s here that solutions like the Specops Authentication API can help, by allowing organizations to add secure workforce authentication and identity verification to their existing applications, automated processes and business workflows.
By integrating verification directly into these processes, organizations can apply consistent security checks at critical points without relying entirely on manual intervention.
Independently Verify Sensitive Requests
For financial transactions, privileged access, and other sensitive requests, organizations should require independent confirmation through trusted channels.
This might include contacting the requester using previously verified details or introducing additional authentication into approval workflows.
Verify IT Support Requests Before Granting Access
Where support processes are managed through internal applications or automated workflows, additional identity verification can help ensure that sensitive requests are made by authorized users.
These measures should be supported by broader security controls like phishing-resistant MFA and least-privilege access, while monitoring for suspicious account activity.
Make Strong Verification Part of Everyday Security
As social engineering tactics become more convincing, organizations can't rely on employees recognizing every fraudulent request. Strong identity verification, independent approval processes and clear security procedures can help reduce the risks.
By building these checks into service desks, applications and everyday workflows, organizations make it harder for attackers to turn a convincing impersonation into a successful compromise.

articles.title: PesaLink’s bank owners remain split on what it should cost
articles.text:
Gituku Kirika runs a payments network owned by Kenya’s banks, but he cannot dictate what they charge customers.
This constraint defines PesaLink’s efforts to win everyday payments from mobile money services. Launched in 2017, PesaLink allows customers to send up to KES 999,999 ($7,700) instantly between bank accounts at different financial institutions. The network is operated by Integrated Payment Services Limited (IPSL), which Kirika leads. The Kenya Bankers Association (KBA), the industry body representing the country’s lenders, is its sole shareholder.
PesaLink says it processes an average of KES 4 billion ($30.8 million) daily, up 24% from 2025. Monthly transaction value has reached KES 110 billion ($846.5 million), up 41% year on year. The company reports a transaction success rate of about 98%.
This year, IPSL has been encouraging banks to adopt a common transfer fee: free for transactions of KES 1,000 ($7.70) or less, and a flat KES 20 ($0.15) for larger transfers, up to KES 999,999 ($7,700). Sending KES 50,000 ($384) between bank accounts costs just KES 20, compared with KES 108 ($0.83) through M-PESA or Airtel Money.
KCB, Co-operative Bank, NCBA, Absa and Stanbic have adopted the flat-fee model. Equity Bank, Standard Chartered and I&M have not, leaving their customers on tiered pricing, where transfer fees rise with the amount sent.
Kirika says PesaLink can only recommend a price, not impose one, but he expects all banks to switch before the end of 2027.
He spoke to TechCabal on Wednesday in Balaclava, Mauritius, a day before the AfricaNenda Foundation, a non-profit that helps African central banks build instant payment systems, released its annual report. He discussed PesaLink’s bank ownership, the lenders yet to adopt its proposed pricing model, competition from M-PESA, merchant payments, and the network’s plans to move beyond bank-to-bank transfers.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
PesaLink is owned by the banking industry, but could its owners also be its biggest constraint?
PesaLink was established by the banking sector. All the banks set it up under the Kenya Bankers Association, so the KBA holds sole ownership of IPSL. PesaLink is available across all banks today. Different banks use the platform differently, based on their strategies and customer segments. As we support more use cases, you will see PesaLink more across the banking world.
If PesaLink transfers can be cheaper than mobile money, why hasn’t the platform pushed that advantage more aggressively?
At PesaLink, we champion lower payment costs, inclusivity, and affordability, and we are passionate about seeing payment costs come down. But we don’t dictate prices to our customers. Banks, microfinance banks, Savings and Credit Cooperative Organisations (SACCOs), and telcos. We do share with them what we believe is the right approach to pricing instant payments. The banks make decisions based on their strategies and budgets. We’ve seen most banks adopt the new KES 20 ($0.15) price this year, and I’m confident many more will do so next year. I expect that before the end of next year, all banks will have changed their price.
Mobile money has built customer habits, merchant acceptance and an extensive distribution network. What is PesaLink doing to make customers choose it without their banks having to push them towards it?
We are a mobile money-native country when it comes to instant payments, and PesaLink also offers instant payments through its different participants. We still need much more work to build awareness of PesaLink. People already have mobile money as an option, but we believe it’s important to have different options. We are working on awareness together with the PesaLink participants who are on board.
As we increase the use cases PesaLink supports, people will learn more about it. Everyday use cases such as person-to-merchant payments will help drive that. The more relevant PesaLink becomes day to day, the more awareness will grow, and next year you will see a huge change.
More participants with large consumer bases are also coming on board. Airtel Money, for example, has now joined PesaLink, so a lot more people will see and hear about it. We look forward to a significant increase in awareness.
Can PesaLink become a payment option at shops and supermarkets?
First, 50% of the payments we process today either terminate at a business or originate from one, so person-to-business payments are already happening. What you’re asking about, though, is person-to-merchant payments. That will follow the approach we’re all familiar with: a merchant number, which we call a till number or paybill, or a QR code. We have now gone live with that use case. As we speak, we are live with Equity Bank and SBM at Quickmart, and we look forward to scaling across other merchants and PesaLink participants.
As PesaLink extends its reach through SACCOs, fintechs, telcos and agent networks, is its ambition to become Kenya’s underlying payment infrastructure, including for transactions that do not originate from bank accounts?
Our agenda is simplifying life through instant, affordable payments for everyone, everywhere, every time. For payments to be affordable, our own costs have to be affordable. And for payments to reach everyone, everywhere, every time, we have to break down the silos created by closed-loop ecosystems.
If you are with your bank, your mobile money operator, or your SACCO, and you can’t use or access that money without moving it to another ecosystem, we consider you in a closed-loop ecosystem. For example, if you’re in the mobile money world and you come across a merchant served by a bank, where you have to pay by card, you’re in a closed loop.
We’re working to reduce barriers to moving money by breaking down those silos and ensuring real interoperability. One way to do that is to reduce the effort it takes for two parties to move money between each other. Today, for a bank, a telco or a SACCO to move money to one another, they have to go through lengthy, time-consuming and expensive arrangements, from technology work to contract negotiations. PesaLink can cut all of that out if every participant is a member.
Can PesaLink become a gateway for cross-border payments into Kenya?
PesaLink is integrated with the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS), so people can now send money into Kenya from other PAPSS-enabled countries. We’re happy to be powering inbound remittances through PAPSS. But we’ve been doing this for a long time: many international money transfer operators, both banks and non-banks, use PesaLink for last-mile delivery of money into the country. We look forward to powering many more of these transactions.

articles.title: Luis Tosar, actor, 54 años: “Me produce mucha tristeza que ahora haya niños por ahí hablando de Franco, reivindicando su figura”
articles.text:
La infancia de Luis Tosar fue un poco de descampados y de fábricas abandonadas. Cuando habla de sus hijos, le preocupa el mundo en el que están creciendo. En su charla con Ana Trasobares se lamentaba del panorama actual. “A mí me produce mucha tristeza que ahora haya niños por ahí hablando de Franco, reivindicando su figura”.
“Niños, cuyos padres ni siquiera han vivido el franquismo y, aun así, están en ese discurso”. En un contexto de polarización de redes, Tosar lamentaba que hubiera jóvenes reivindicando al dictador.
“No se dan cuenta de que este señor se alzó en armas el 18 de julio y acabó con un gobierno legítimo. Es increíble”. Se refería al día que se produjo la sublevación militar de los militares contra la Segunda República (que derivaría en la Guerra Civil).
De los descampados de Lugo a la crianza de sus hijos
Por otro lado, la conversación tocaba también el tema de la infancia de Tosar. Cómo era su entorno. Vivió en un ambiente rural, pero luego su padre empezó a trabajar en Lugo y entonces se mudaron a esta ciudad. Vivían en un barrio del extrarradio. “Era un mundo urbano, pero a medias”.
En este periodo recuerda haber tenido una infancia “superdivertida”. Él era un niño “gamberro, pero no más que los demás”. Jugaban a piratas y a Indiana Jones. También descubrió el breakdance. “Recuerdo que nos íbamos a bailar a las fábricas abandonadas y nos creíamos que estábamos en Nueva York porque aquello parecía el Bronx”.
La paternidad de Tosar también le ha cambiado. Aunque admite que a veces es sobreprotector, intenta que sus hijos se relacionen con el campo. Además, viven fuera de Madrid. Por eso pueden “descubrir” todo lo que les rodea. “Me gusta que investiguen las texturas de las plantas, de las tierras, de los metales”.
La conversación partía de “Golpes” (de Rafael Cobos), la historia de dos hermanos divididos por las circunstancias y con un difícil reencuentro.
El actor cree que España no está totalmente reconstruida desde la Guerra Civil. Todavía quedan algunas heridas por curar. Sin embargo, tiene cierta confianza en el resto. “Me parece que la especie humana, a estas alturas, ya debería estar extinta por las cosas que hacemos. Sin embargo, aún hay gente capaz de arrancarnos del abismo. Es de agradecer”. Resumiendo: “Menos mal que existe toda esa gente buena, porque si no este mundo ya habría desaparecido”.

articles.title: Google Keep prépare une nouveauté très attendue pour enfin retrouver vos notes en un clic
articles.text:
Si vous utilisez Google Keep régulièrement, vous savez qu’il n’est pas toujours simple de retrouver une note en utilisant simplement la barre de recherche ou le système d’étiquettes manuelles. Google semble conscient du problème si l’on en croit nos confrères d’Android Authority qui ont trouvé une nouveauté très intéressante dans le code de la version 5.26.461.01.90 de l’application qui intègre désormais des filtres sous forme d’onglets.
Des onglets pour trier vos notes Google Keep
Placés juste en dessous de la barre de recherche principale, ces nouveaux filtres ont évidemment pour but de faciliter la navigation. La vue par défaut, intitulée « Tous », conserve l’affichage classique en plaçant les notes épinglées en haut de liste, suivies immédiatement par les notes les plus récentes. En sélectionnant l’option « Cette semaine », l’application isole uniquement les notes rédigées au cours des sept derniers jours, ce qui évite d’avoir à trop faire défiler l’écran.
Source : Android Authority
Le filtre « À faire » rassemble quant à lui l’ensemble des notes associées à des tâches et des rappels. De son côté, l’onglet « Listes » filtre uniquement les notes au format à puces. L’onglet « Partagés » permet également de retrouver en un clic les documents partagés avec d’autres utilisateurs. Pas mal de filtres supplémentaires, donc, qui devraient aider à la navigation sur Google Keep.
Quelques changements d’interface au passage
En plus de ces nouveaux outils de tri, cette version v5.26.461.01.90 de Google Keep cache quelques changements visuels sur la page d’accueil. Les notes épinglées n’apparaissent ainsi plus sous une section dédiée, mais affichent désormais une icône d’épingle discrète dans leur coin supérieur droit.
Source : Android Authority
À lire : Google Keep ne plaisante plus avec ces deux nouveautés
Enfin, le texte qui se trouve dans chaque carte sur l’écran d’accueil profite désormais d’un effet de fondu progressif vers le bas. Toutes ces nouveautés étaient fonctionnelles en manipulant le fichier APK, mais ne sont pas encore déployées sur la version stable de l’application. Reste maintenant à savoir quand Google se décidera à les déployer.

articles.title: Debate brews over Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models; Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here
articles.text:
Debate brews over Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models; Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here
Token Factory is an inference platform, which provides the computing infrastructure required to run trained AI models and generate responses.
Dear Reader,
Sarvam hosts Chinese AI models on Indian infrastructure. The move has sparked debate over AI sovereignty. More on this later in the edition.
Speaking of AI, Nvidia’s board has no intention of reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, chair Harvey Jones said on the chipmaker’s earnings call on Wednesday. His remarks came hours after Huang said he would be honoured to return if the board believed it was in the company's best interest.
As for its earnings report, the company also said its net income more than doubled to $65.3 billion for the quarter ended October 25, 2026, from $31.9 billion a year earlier.
Apollo Hospitals is using an AI agent developed with Microsoft to speed up reviews of patient falls, medication errors and readmissions. The hospital says the system has coincided with fewer recorded incidents, although this does not establish that AI alone caused the decline.
The newly-developed Daily Tiered Huddle agent supports clinical-governance teams. It brings together hospital records, flags cases, builds patient timelines and prompts clinicians for missing details. The agent also suggests assessments for doctors to check and amend.
In other news, domestic and global institutional investors such as Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund and BlackRock have increased their stake in Groww by acquiring shares worth Rs 1,905 crore, per block deal data on NSE.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Debate brews over Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models
- Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here
Here’s your trivia for today: Originally named DMA Design when it created the first Grand Theft Auto in 1997, the Scottish studio behind the franchise is now known as Rockstar... what?
Artificial intelligence
Debate brews over Sarvam hosting Chinese AI models
With its newly-launched Token Factory offering access to models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Z.ai, alongside its own models and Google’s Gemma, Bengaluru-based Sarvam AI is positioning itself as an AI developer and an inference provider.
The move has attracted criticism from those who believe a company backed by public resources should prioritise original Indian research.
Key takeaways:
- Token Factory is an inference platform, which provides the computing infrastructure required to run trained AI models and generate responses.
- The criticism about Sarvam AI centres on the distinction between hosting AI and developing it.
- Hemant Mohapatra, a partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the launch, pointing out that international inference providers are already making money by hosting foreign models in India.

Gaming
GTA VI is finally here
More than 13 years after the release of Grand Theft Auto V, GTA VI is finally here. The game is exclusive to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, with no release planned for PC, PS4, or Xbox One.
PlayStation India lists the Standard Edition at Rs 5,999 and the Ultimate Edition at Rs 7,499. Both come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription service.
Game on:
- Indian players do not have to wait for a courier. Quick-commerce platform Blinkit announced on its official account that GTA 6 is now available on its app, with delivery in minutes.
- Pre-loading opened on 12 November. On the PS5, the game needs at least 212 GB of free space, according to PlayStation's store page.
- Rockstar has not announced a PC version. That matters in India, where many serious gamers play on PCs and gaming laptops because consoles are expensive.

- Lofty ambitions: Edtech firm PhysicsWallah has set an ambitious revenue target of Rs 9,000–10,000 crore by FY30. The goal will test whether an online-first education business can sustain rapid growth while expanding its offline network and improving margins.
- Profits: Public shareholders in Paytm’s parent company, One 97 Communications, have seen their investments grow roughly 1.7x over the past five years. The rally, which pushed the fintech giant's shares to a new high, reflects a major expansion in both retail ownership and institutional backing since its market debut.

articles.title: Timing terrible: le PlayStation Network flanche à quelques heures de la sortie de GTA 6

Le timing ne pouvait guère être plus mauvais pour Sony.
Mercredi 18 novembre en début de soirée, les signalements de dysfonctionnement du PlayStation Network (PSN) se sont envolés sur Downdetector, la plateforme qui recense les incidents déclarés par les utilisateurs.
Cela se passe à quelques heures seulement du lancement de Grand Theft Auto VI, prévu à minuit heure locale sur PS5.

Ces difficultés n’ont pourtant rien de surprenant, tant l’attente autour de GTA 6 est forte et tant les serveurs de Sony risquent d’être sollicités par des millions de joueurs au même moment. articles.title: Acer Nitro V 16 AI : ce laptop gamer Ryzen 9 + RTX 5070 perd 650 € pour le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Trouver une configuration gaming sérieuse à prix raisonnable devient compliqué : la hausse du prix de la RAM et la pénurie sur les composants graphiques tirent les tarifs vers le haut. Pour le Black Friday, l’Acer Nitro V 16 AI, un 16 pouces pensé pour le jeu avec Ryzen AI 9 et RTX 5070, bénéficie de près de 30 % de remise.
L’Acer Nitro V 16 AI, c’est quoi ?
- Un écran WUXGA de 16 pouces à 180 Hz
- Un combo Ryzen AI 9 + RTX 5070 pour les jeux exigeants
- Une configuration solide : 32 Go de RAM et 1 To de SSD
Au départ proposé à 2 299 euros, l’Acer Nitro V 16 AI s’affiche désormais à 1 649 euros sur Amazon, soit 650 euros d’économie.
Sécurisez vos achats durant Black Friday avec la meilleure offre de l’année. Dénichez les bonnes affaires, Bitdefender s’occupe des arnaques.
Un châssis gaming qui reste transportable
Face aux PC gamer plus massifs de la gamme Predator, ce Nitro V 16 AI reste sobre avec son châssis noir. Il conserve des mensurations raisonnables pour un 16 pouces : 2,43 kilos sur la balance pour une épaisseur comprise entre 16,1 et 24,5 millimètres. Il pèse plus lourd qu’un ultrabook, mais se glisse sans souci dans un sac à dos.

articles.title: Optimizely hack made Zoom, CNN, BBC, and 175 other sites serve crypto-stealing malware
articles.text:
What we know so far: Most big websites load a handful of scripts they didn't write themselves, from analytics tags to A/B testing tools. On Monday, one of those tools was turned against them. Attackers slipped malicious code into Optimizely's experimentation platform. For most of the day, it pushed a crypto stealer and card skimmer to visitors of Zoom, CNN, the BBC, and roughly 175 other organizations.
Optimizely is best known for letting companies A/B test their web pages on real visitors. Customers embed a small snippet that pulls each project's code straight from Optimizely's servers. So whoever controls that code effectively decides what runs in every visitor's browser.
That's exactly the kind of power the attacker grabbed. To see how far it reached, Report URI's Scott Helme and his team checked 1,611 Optimizely snippets. The malicious code turned up in 188 of them. Those belonged to 178 organizations, including Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM and even hardware wallet maker Ledger. Embarrassingly, Optimizely's own websites were serving it too.
As for how it happened, Optimizely told Gizmodo that someone exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow. The attacker then wrote code into each customer's "Project JavaScript" field. That setting runs on every page, so Optimizely's servers delivered the malware just like any legitimate experiment.
Strangely, the company hasn't explained how a signup bug let an outsider edit other companies' live projects. Even so, Optimizely says it has blocked the vulnerable path, deployed a fix, and notified affected customers.
Once loaded, the payload hunted for crypto wallet addresses across eight blockchains and replaced them with the attacker's own. It even rewrote addresses copied to the clipboard, so anyone pasting a wallet address from an infected page could end up paying a stranger. A card skimmer joined in partway through the day, lifting card numbers, expiry dates and CVVs from checkout forms.
On iOS 18.6 and earlier, the code also quietly loaded the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits – the same leaked tools criminals have used to raid iPhones this year.
By that evening, Helme estimated the attacker's wallets had pulled in about $7,040. But in its own analysis, StepSecurity says that figure undersells the damage. Stolen cards and hacked iPhones simply don't show up on the blockchain.
For visitors, Helme recommends updating iPhones to at least iOS 18.7.3 or iOS 26.3. Any card entered on an affected site on November 16 should be treated as exposed, too.
Optimizely's customers aren't the first to get burned this way, either. Just this July, Adform's tracking script was rigged to swap crypto addresses in much the same way. Two years earlier, the Polyfill.io takeover pushed malicious code to more than 100,000 websites.

articles.title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
articles.text:
Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet from legacy self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by re-pointing existing EBS volumes at new pods, rather than streaming data between nodes. A blog post by the site reliability team details a migration. It covered about 90 production clusters. There was zero downtime for customers and no data loss. The largest cluster, a 54-pod user-data store, took about 12 hours end to end.
Yelp had already moved its stateless workloads to EKS through its PaaSTA deployment layer, but Cassandra stayed behind. Kubernetes has no built-in way to migrate StatefulSets and their persistent volumes across clusters. The usual approach is to add nodes to the new cluster and shut down the old ones. This would temporarily double compute capacity but also lead to data transfer costs. For the largest clusters, streaming alone could have taken weeks. Yelp also considered a regional failover and rebuild, and a new Cassandra datacenter in EKS, but rated both as less transparent to customers.
Yelp's "Rolling PV Transplant" relies on the fact that an EBS volume is bound to an Availability Zone, not to a Kubernetes cluster, and that a PersistentVolume is effectively a pointer to a volume ID. The team pre-creates PVs and PVCs in EKS that reference the existing volume IDs, then creates an identical StatefulSet there, whose pods wait in ContainerCreating. The automation then deletes one pod at a time on the legacy cluster, waits for the volume to detach, and lets the EKS pod claim it. The pod rejoins the ring with the same data and token range, and the process repeats for the next pod. Cassandra's replication tolerates the few minutes each node is offline.
Yelp set a skipReconciliation: true flag on the custom resources in both clusters. This was done because two operators managed the same logical ring during the migration. The flag helped prevent them from conflicting over pod state. The flag was cleared on the EKS side at the end.
Across roughly 1,000 pods, about 1,000 TiB moved by pointer rather than over the wire. No node was ever decommissioned from the ring, so rollback was the same operation in reverse. Yelp used it a handful of times, for a missing subnet definition and a certificate mismatch, and restored pods within minutes. After a week of manual dev runs and a week of automation, one engineer ran the production rollout in about three weeks, migrating three to six clusters on a typical day.
The team had Claude generate the orchestration script, roughly 800 lines of bash, from its validated manual runbook, rather than asking it to design the procedure. The script needed minor adjustments after two days of testing.
The approach relies on a previous Container Storage Interface migration by Yelp's Compute Infrastructure team. This work gave the Data Infrastructure team confidence in the volume detach and attach process. Yelp also used the technique for Kafka clusters, and says it applies to any AZ-pinned stateful workload on Kubernetes. The legacy clusters are now retired.
The one failure specific to this technique was a stale VolumeAttachment object left behind by the AWS CSI controller after pod deletion. The EKS pod sat in Pending with no error, and deleting the object on the legacy cluster fixed it. Yelp advises building explicit timeouts for stalled detach and attach operations into any automation. Two other findings were unrelated to the mechanism. Backups failed with IAM AccessDenied errors for 48 hours because a new -eks role was not yet being assumed by scheduled jobs, and the alert only filed a ticket instead of paging. Pausing repairs for the migration also exposed one cluster whose repairs had been silently disabled for three months, leaving accumulated data inconsistencies. Teams planning a similar move should audit repair state, backup IAM roles and alert severity before starting.
Yelp's approach is not the only way to move Cassandra between EKS clusters. Monday.com's engineering team describes a different one in a post on zero-downtime Cassandra migration between EKS clusters. K8ssandra-managed clusters had to move without any downtime or data loss. So, the team created a workflow to add new Cassandra data centers, safely transfer data, and remove the old ones. That is the streaming model Yelp considered and rejected. The new cluster is brought up alongside the old one and receives data over the network, and the original is retired only afterwards. The team believes success relied more on control, automation, and handling failures than on speed. They automated long tasks like rebuilds and planned the migration in stages based on operator behavior.
The two migrations differ in what they trade away. Yelp's disk transplant skips data transfer and extra compute. It allows for a rollback by swapping the pointer. However, it relies on EBS volumes being linked to an Availability Zone, not a cluster. Monday.com's approach does not rely on that property, and it keeps the old environment intact until the end. The cost is a longer migration and the capacity to run both sides at once, which Yelp calculated would have taken weeks for its largest clusters.
Despite the different mechanics, the post-migration lessons are similar. Monday.com devotes part of its write-up to verifying that backups work after the migration, along with monitoring, dashboards and alerts. Yelp's own backups failed on an IAM role mismatch within 48 hours of its first production clusters landing in EKS. Teams planning either approach should treat those checks as part of the migration plan, not as cleanup afterwards.

articles.title: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
articles.text:
United Launch Alliance said Wednesday that the failure of its Vulcan rocket during a launch on Sunday was caused by inadequate fuel supply.
“ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday,” the company said in a statement. “While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines.”
The new information released by ULA confirms reporting from Ars Technica on Tuesday that the rocket’s failure was not due to the performance of the vehicle’s main engines, which are provided by Blue Origin.
This represents an important revelation from ULA and will provide some major relief to different parts of the US aerospace community, particularly Blue Origin and NASA.
Big for Blue
That’s because the BE-4 engine is also the bedrock of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This powerful rocket uses a similar but slightly more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. New Glenn experienced its own catastrophic failure in May during a ground test, a failure that was later attributed to a main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines.
After this anomaly, Blue Origin retrofitted the main oxygen valve, including for Vulcan missions. Now it’s clear that this retrofit was not implicated in the Vulcan accident. With the preliminary Vulcan investigation having largely exonerated the BE-4 engine, Blue Origin can press ahead with its return-to-flight mission with New Glenn, which could occur as soon as January.
“Following the Vulcan anomaly, Blue Origin immediately worked alongside ULA to review flight data and support the investigation,” Blue Origin said in a statement Wednesday. “Together, we identified that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines. ULA is a valued partner, and we look forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.”

articles.title: “La demanda de IA está creciendo. Creo que la industria estará bien”: Sam Altman sobre la salida de Jensen Huang de Nvidia
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, sostuvo que la salida de Jensen Huang como CEO de Nvidia no frenará el avance de la inteligencia artificial (IA). “Es difícil imaginar la revolución de la IA sin Jensen y la compañía que ha construido”, declaró Altman durante el evento Silicon Valley & The World.
Aun así, descartó que su salida provoque una alteración en el mercado: “Hay tanta demanda, y está tan claro que la IA es real y que la gente quiere usarla y que los ingresos y la demanda están creciendo con tanta fuerza, que creo que la industria estará bien”.
La renuncia de Huang como consejero delegado se produjo tras conocerse una relación extramatrimonial con una presunta espía china. El cofundador de Nvidia dejó el cargo en medio de una campaña pública que reclama su restitución y de cuestionamientos desde Washington sobre el futuro liderazgo de la empresa.
Qué relación hay entre Nvidia y OpenAI
Nvidia comprometió hasta 105.000 millones de dólares para respaldar el proyecto de centros de datos de OpenAI en Ohio, sumado a otros negocios compartidos. Esa relación convirtió la salida de Huang en un foco de inquietud para los mercados, ante la posibilidad de que se revisaran compromisos vinculados a la expansión de la inteligencia artificial.
Altman consideró que la dimensión de la empresa permite sostener sus garantías financieras incluso sin su fundador al mando. “Nvidia es una empresa gigantesca”, enfatizó. “Creo que la gente sigue confiando mucho en sus garantías”.
El dirigente de OpenAI definió a Huang como un “héroe” personal y señaló que “los héroes tienen defectos”. Su respaldo estuvo acompañado por una referencia a su propia destitución temporal al frente de OpenAI en 2023, experiencia por la que dijo sentir una profunda empatía hacia la situación de Huang.
Cuál ha sido la postura de otros líderes tecnológicos sobre el caso de Jensen Huang
La cautela de Altman contrasta con la posición de otros referentes tecnológicos. Elon Musk, director ejecutivo de SpaceX y Tesla, Tim Sweeney, director ejecutivo de Epic Games, y Garry Tan, presidente de Y Combinator, firmaron una carta abierta para pedir a la junta directiva de Nvidia que reincorpore a Huang como consejero delegado.
La petición reunió más de 165.000 firmas, incluidas las de más de 7.500 empleados de Nvidia, una cifra equivalente a más del 15% de la plantilla. Entre los adherentes figura Travis Kalanick, cofundador de Uber, quien escribió que Huang “erró, sí, errar es humano, pero no creo que nada de lo que hizo alcance el umbral para separarlo de su compañía”.
Qué presión hace Silicon Valley para la restitución de Jensen Huang en Nvidia
Un aliado de Huang confirmó a Financial Times que un grupo de ejecutivos de Silicon Valley organizó un “cuartel de guerra” para impulsar su regreso y reunir respaldo en la Casa Blanca.
“Todos los que importan en el sector tecnológico fuera de los laboratorios de vanguardia admiran a Jensen”, afirmó esa persona, quien añadió que el propio Huang respalda esas gestiones.
La posibilidad de un reintegro de Huang a Nvidia enfrenta resistencia dentro del Gobierno de Estados Unidos. El secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, pidió una “reorganización drástica” en la conducción de Nvidia y sostuvo que la compañía debería buscar a su próximo director fuera de la empresa.
Hace poco, Huang manifestó que estaría dispuesto a retomar el cargo si la junta directiva considera que esa decisión beneficia a los accionistas, los empleados, Nvidia y Estados Unidos. “Si el consejo considera que mi regreso beneficia a los accionistas, a los empleados, a la empresa y a Estados Unidos, me sentiría honrado de atender esa petición y volver a ejercer como director ejecutivo”, señaló.

articles.title: Industry leaders want Canada to choose whether it builds its own fusion future, or buys it from abroad | BetaKit
articles.text:
As the global race to develop commercially viable nuclear fusion power intensifies, a trio of the field’s leading Canadians entrepreneurs says it is time for the country to prioritize investment in the industry.
Daedal Systems founder and CEO Henry Gould, General Fusion CEO Greg Twinney, and Stellarex Energy co-founder and CEO Spencer Pitcher made the argument on stage yesterday at the MaRS Climate Impact conference in Toronto during a panel on commercial fusion.
Many global players are competing to harness fusion, the same physical process that powers the sun, to generate abundant, carbon-free energy. Pitcher, who leads the fusion-focused and Toronto-based Princeton University laboratory spinoff Stellarex, argued that Canada now needs to follow the same path it took when it began investing heavily in nuclear energy after World War II.
“If we don’t make this decision now, we’ll buy our devices from other countries for a very long time.”
Spencer Pitcher, Stellarex
“Seventy-five years ago, our grandparents—in some cases, your great-grandparents—made a decision that Canada would have a clean source of nuclear energy based on heavy water, moderated reactors, and unenriched uranium,” Pitcher said. “This was a really bold decision made by politicians, engineers, bankers, and investors … It [has been] the foundation of energy supply in [Ontario] for two generations, and will probably continue for another few generations.”
Pitcher thinks Canada would benefit from adopting the same “can-do attitude” today. “Fusion is the ultimate source of energy,” he added. “It’s the primary source of energy in the universe. Nothing comes after it; it’s the end game. If we don’t make this decision now, we’ll buy our devices from other countries for a very long time.”
Twinney and Gould agreed. “We need Canada to acknowledge this opportunity in a real way,” Twinney said.
Gould noted that the last two decades of fusion and plasma development in Canada “have been lacklustre, basically non-existent, with the exception of General Fusion,” his previous employer.
He thinks the path forward entails focusing on tritium systems, where he said Canada has a competitive advantage. Canada is a global leader in the production, processing, and handling of tritium, a radioactive isotope of hydrogen and a key ingredient in the fuel for nuclear fusion, which could soon become a key strategic resource.
“Do we only sell fuel-handling systems to this emerging industry for value to be captured elsewhere, or do we leverage that competitive advantage, do more with it, bolster reactor developers and other parts of the supply chain?” Gould asked.
RELATED: Ex-General Fusion employee raises $4 million USD for fusion diagnostics startup Daedal
Gould believes a three-pronged approach is in order: doubling down on tritium systems, supporting fusion developers, and filling tech gaps in the industry, such as in measurement instruments like the ones Daedal is building.
Twinney said Canada lags the United States and United Kingdom on a regulatory framework for fusion, and ought to follow in those countries’ footsteps.
Though Canada recently launched a national nuclear energy strategy that listed fusion as one of the innovative forms of power the federal government intends to support, Twinney thinks the country could use a dedicated national fusion strategy, something General Fusion advocated for but did not receive in the federal government’s latest budget.
“We have some of the best fusion companies—even though there’s a small group of us—in the world … These companies are going to be successful one way or the other, and we should keep them in Canada,” he added.
An open approach to combat “Theranos-type risk”
Moderator Zoltan Tompa, partner and team lead of BDC Capital’s Climate Tech Fund, noted that establishing credibility is “critical” when it comes to fusion development. Tompa asked the panellists whether they see potential “Theranos-type risk” in the sector, highlighting that some unnamed firms have been making “extraordinary claims” lately that they may not be able to support and could ultimately chill market interest in fusion.
“In the scientific community, we’ve been worried about this for several years,” Pitcher said.
Gould also sees potential for fraud to create a chill in fusion. “It’s deep tech,” he said. “There’s long development cycles. There [are] these thorny physics and science problems that are difficult for the investment community to understand … It’s a long path to revenue.”
RELATED: General Fusion “pleased” with public-market debut after redemption-heavy SPAC deal
With capital providers investing in fusion based on tech development milestones rather than actual sales, assessing true value creation can be more difficult, especially for the less technically savvy.
To build trust, Pitcher argued that companies could disclose two key performance metrics, their “fusion triple product” and their recirculating power requirement, without threatening their intellectual property or “special sauce.”
Twinney agreed with the sentiment. “Sharing the science basis of your approach and what you’ve achieved, and allowing peers and industry [to evaluate it], this is common practice and a great way to establish your own credibility, to get feedback from [third parties], and also make sure that you are bringing the people along that you need to bring along.”
“We believe an open approach is the best approach,” he said.
Feature image courtesy MaRS.

articles.title: Molecular discovery speeds up at Texas A&M supercomputing - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI and supercomputing merge as universities build GPU clusters at cloud-provider scale
Universities racing to build AI infrastructure are learning that raw compute changes the pace of science itself, from molecular discovery to materials engineering.
AI and high-performance computing are converging, and campus technology leaders are now building like cloud operators. The Texas A&M University System is standing up two major clusters for researchers across its 12 universities and eight state agencies, according to Vince Kellen (pictured), chief information officer of The Texas A&M University System.
“A lot of it is going to be related to molecules, molecular discovery, and the size of these computers lets researchers go through their research program in a fraction of the time. What would normally take five months now gets done in a week,” Kellen said. “That’s a big deal for the scientists. It lets them do more exploration more frequently.”
Kellen spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how the system’s supercomputing clusters are speeding up molecular discovery, the security and operational demands of running them, and the convergence of AI and supercomputing. (* Disclosure below.)
Molecular discovery at supercomputer speed
The system’s VISION supercomputer, an Nvidia Corp. DGX H200 SuperPOD, ranked No. 66 on the June 2026 Top500 list, making it the most powerful university supercomputer in the U.S. — with a second cluster on the way, according to Kellen. The Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station selected Dell Technologies Inc. to build IGNITE, a platform running Advanced Micro Devices Inc. GPUs in an Equinix Inc. data center in Dallas. With some research tied to highly secure federal contracts, protection tops the policy agenda.
“On the policy side, our main concern is security. Are we doing this in a secure way?” Kellen said. “Are we vetting the employees who are coming into the platform to make sure that they’re properly credentialed to come in?”
Texas A&M is working through those access questions as it brings more computing power to researchers across the system, but faster molecular discovery is only the first payoff. Materials engineering, fluid dynamics and other engineering disciplines are next in line, and the system has no plans to slow its buildout, according to Kellen.
“We already know that AI and supercomputing are one and the same,” he said. “That trajectory is going to continue in Texas for some time.”

articles.title: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: 'It's time to start running' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated technology systems can defend against them, Palmer Luckey warned at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. Addressing the recent spate of tech outages, the Oculus founder and Anduril Industries co-founder argued that older systems are struggling to keep pace with the new hacking capabilities enabled by AI and warned it was time to quicken the pace of securing our defenses.
“We’re seeing the natural effects of a lot of these advanced AI tools allowing for the creation of various exploits,” he said.
While government officials largely attributed the latest set of technical issues to companies rushing to patch their systems to protect against the new vulnerabilities AI has discovered, Luckey focused on the underlying security challenges facing organizations using outdated technology.
Luckey explained that U.S. adversaries are currently exploiting the mismatch between new attack capabilities and our defense capabilities. These attacks are being carried out for both strategic and financial reasons, and North Korea was particularly involved, he added.
The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, noted that U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance had canceled his appearance at the Times’ conference this week because of the recent tech outages, saying he now had to attend meetings about the matter.
Given the situation, Sorkin asked Luckey how worried we should be about all this.
“It depends on how well prepared you are,” was Luckey’s answer. (He then ominously warned, “You guys are going to find out what’s going on soon enough.”)
The tech executive argued that AI could ultimately give defenders the upper hand, but they’d have to move more quickly.
“In the long run, the advantages are going to accrue to the side that is most effectively using AI for defense,” Luckey said. “With the people who say that everything can be hacked — they are right, for now. That actually may be the case with certain new techniques that are coming along. But as of right now, there’s a mismatch between the attackers who are very fast-moving and using technology and old, outdated systems that are not able to adopt technology as quickly as it is developed,” Luckey continued.
“And I think … people are going to have to pick up the pace,” he said. “It’s time to start running.”

articles.title: SSDs, laptops, and phones may get cheaper as consumer NAND spot pricing drops 20% — Bank of America expects contract price drops, report cites oversupply in consumer market amid declining demand and growing Chinese competition
articles.text:
SSDs, laptops, and phones may get cheaper as consumer NAND spot pricing drops 20% — Bank of America expects contract price drops, report cites oversupply in consumer market amid declining demand and growing Chinese competition
A small but welcome potential reprieve for PC builders and consumers.
Solid-state drives, phones, laptops, and tablets have all gotten substantially pricier in the last couple of years. Beyond the stratospheric prices of DDR5 memory, prospective PC builders and consumer electronics buyers have had to deal with upcharges on SSDs of all sizes thanks to the AI boom. That may be changing soon, as spot pricing for consumer NAND chips is reportedly dropping, according to a new report from Seoul Economic Daily (SED).
The report observes a 20% drop in spot pricing for NAND chips over just the last month. Its conclusions are bolstered by information from a Bank of America note from Nov. 13, wherein industry sources tell that institution that NAND is due for a market correction.
SED says that according to that note, 512 Gb NAND wafers saw a 32% drop to $14.30 apiece on the spot market, while 1 Tb wafers fell 19% to $24.90. SED quotes another industry source that says: "NAND cannot sustain the steep price gains seen so far."
Those decreases may be hard to square in a time when enterprise SSDs are getting pricier by the day, but SED notes that the rise in phone and PC prices has led customers to delay upgrades, resulting in a 20% year-on-year decline in shipments for phones alone and making for the lowest third-quarter volumes in 14 years. Meanwhile, PC shipments have also fallen 22.5% year-on-year, according to a Gartner report.
In the face of those consumer decisions, device makers are letting their existing stock drain out and are presumably stocked with NAND chips for the short term, thus resulting in lower prices for new fab shipments on the short-term spot market.
Another factor in the consumer NAND market is that not all flash is equal. Both RAM and NAND makers have been redirecting their chip output to serve the ongoing AI boom, converting their consumer-grade production lines to make higher-spec silicon. Memory factories have been converting DDR5 capacity to HBM at a steady pace, as parts of the process are shared across both types.
But according to the Bank of America note that SED cites, things are different in the NAND world. High-density flash now sits at around 300 layers, and its production requires substantially different tooling compared to the lower-grade silicon deemed suitable for us mere mortals. So the continuing growth in NAND demand from AI data centers may not translate directly into reduced consumer supply.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Beyond those factors, added supply from Chinese NAND maker YMTC is creating additional downward price pressure in the NAND market. SED notes that YMTC has taken a 14% chunk from major players in the NAND market in the second quarter of this year alone.
On net, these forces could result in a bit of relief for consumer tech. SED says Bank of America expects consumer NAND prices for PCs and smartphones to fall 5% to 10% on the longer-term contract market in the first quarter of 2027, while enterprise NAND contract prices are expected to hold more or less steady.
Whether those declines translate to lower prices for finished devices and components like SSDs will remain to be seen, and products with those chips inside will require some time to reach the market. But in the ongoing AI supply crunch, any potential relief is worth celebrating.

Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

Prices have been sitting at an inflated high for the last year now. Look at the prices of GPUs versus MSRP and that should give you a tiny indication of how completely screwing the pricing is today. Reply

articles.title: Hackean una herramienta de Microsoft y la convierten en malware para robar tus datos
articles.text:
Una herramienta de Microsoft ha sido comprometida para distribuir malware y robar credenciales. Investigadores de seguridad descubrieron que dos versiones del framework para Python que se utiliza para desarrollar agentes de IA fueron vulneradas. Los hackers la aprovecharon para distribuir malware que puede robar credenciales, secretos corporativos y tokens de acceso a servicios en la nube.
De acuerdo con The Register, el incidente afecta a las versiones 1.26.1 y 1.26.2 del paquete agent-framework publicado en PyPI, el repositorio más importante para Python. Los expertos encontraron que las versiones infectadas se distribuyeron desde la cuenta oficial asociada al proyecto de Microsoft, por lo que sospechan que el atacante comprometió las credenciales de alguien con permisos de publicación.
Según OX Security y OpenSourceMalware, el código malicioso se diseñó para ejecutarse de forma automática al momento que Python se iniciaba en un equipo infectado. A diferencia de otros ataques similares, los usuarios no tenían que importar la librería en sus proyectos para que se activara el malware. Bastaba con instalar alguna de las versiones del paquete para que el proceso se activara en segundo plano.
El malware de Python podía robar credenciales y tus tokens de desarrollo
Una vez que se activaba, el malware recopilaba variables de entorno, archivos de configuración y credenciales almacenadas localmente. Debido a que el ataque estaba enfocado hacia los desarrolladores, el malware también robaba secretos relacionados con servicios como Azure, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face, npm, PyPI y otros ecosistemas de desarrollo. Por último, la información se comprimía antes de enviarse a un servidor controlado por los hackers.
Debido a la naturaleza del ataque, el malware que infectó a esta herramienta oficial de Microsoft no se limitaba a robar solo la información de tu ordenador. Los investigadores descubrieron que también pedía nuevos tokens de autenticación en plataformas como GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps y distintos servicios de Azure. De este modo, los hackers podían obtener acceso temporal a recursos o APIs antes de que expiraran.
Uno de los factores que complicó la detección fue que el malware cargaba componentes legítimos de la herramienta de Microsoft, por lo que los desarrolladores seguían trabajando sin sospechar que el paquete infectado estaba robando sus datos. Afortunadamente, Microsoft detectó el problema y retiró algunos repositorios, mientras que PyPI puso en cuarentena la cuenta que publicó estos paquetes comprometidos.
Los investigadores de OX Security encontraron que el proyecto registró más de 190.000 descargas mensuales antes de que se tuviera conocimiento del ataque. Aunque esta cifra no representa todas las instalaciones con el paquete malicioso, una fracción tuvo que lidiar con el problema.
Cómo eliminar el malware de la herramienta de Microsoft
Si un ordenador tuvo instaladas las versiones 1.26.1 o 1.26.2 de agent-framework, los investigadores recomiendan asumir que el sistema quedó comprometido. Eliminar el paquete puede ser la solución más simple; sin embargo, OpenSourceMalware recomienda seguir estos pasos:
- Eliminar las versiones afectadas de agent-framework y reemplazarlas por una versión verificada.
- Buscar y eliminar los archivos maliciosos en el entorno de Python:
  - agent_framework_meta.pth
  - agent_framework_meta/_telemetry.py
  - af_runtime_diag.pth
  - af_runtime_diag.py
- Eliminar el entorno afectado y reconstruirlo a partir de imágenes o dependencias conocidas y verificadas.
- Rotar inmediatamente todas las credenciales potencialmente expuestas.
- Revocar tokens temporales y sesiones activas obtenidas mediante GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps u otras identidades federadas.
- Revisar los registros de actividad de Azure y otros servicios cloud para detectar accesos sospechosos.
- Buscar conexiones salientes al webhook de los atacantes para determinar si hubo exfiltración de datos.
La buena noticia es que el malware no es persistente a nivel de sistema operativo, ya que no instala servicios o tareas programadas. Solo operaba mientras los archivos permanecían en el directorio site-packages de Python.

articles.title: Bell to remove 10K Aeroplan point bonus from some plans
articles.text:
Bell is set to cut a perk from one of its most expensive plans that netted customers tons of Aeroplan points ahead of Black Friday.
The carrier launched the Aeroplan perk back in July, offering 10,000 points to customers who signed up for one of the carrier’s Ultra plans. The points are rolled out over the course of a year, with the first installment coming 60 days after a plan is activated.
However, per a new notice on Bell’s website, the company’s cheaper Ultra plan will lose the Aeroplan bonus on Nov. 23, just in time for Black Friday.
The new end date is listed on the company’s $90/mo Ultra plan, while the more expensive $100/mo Ultra plan had no end date at the time of writing. The main difference between the two plans is that the latter includes international roaming, while the $90 option only has Canada, U.S., and Mexico roaming included.
While 10,000 Aeroplan points maybe aren’t the most enticing bonus, it’s a bummer to see Bell remove a bonus from one of its plans. Especially at the prices Bell charges, you need every bonus you can get.
To put Bell’s plan in perspective, you could get a $45/125GB plan from Freedom that also has CAN/US/MEX data and international roaming features built in. Sure, technically the Bell plan has faster data with no cap, but for half the price, the Freedom plan is a lot more compelling to me.
Notably, Bell is one of the few carriers that hasn’t yet launched any Black Friday deals. So perhaps this change is in preparation for some stellar offers to come. But I’m not sure I’d bet on it.

articles.title: Pour rivaliser avec ChatGPT et Claude, Microsoft dévoile 7 nouvelles IA à prix cassé
articles.text:
Microsoft veut s’émanciper de ses partenaires dans le monde de l’IA. Lors de sa conférence Ignite organisée à San Francisco, le géant américain a présenté sept nouveaux modèles d’intelligence artificielle conçues par ses propres équipes. Chaque modèle s’attaque à une tâche bien précise, comme le codage informatique, la cybersécurité, ou encore la création d’images.
À lire aussi : Le chercheur en guerre contre Microsoft dévoile une 16ᵉ faille Windows, elle peut désactiver votre antivirus
Des modèles spécialisés à la place d’une IA géante
Microsoft mise sur une approche bien différente de celle de ses rivaux. Plutôt que de construire une seule IA capable de tout faire, le groupe américain mise sur des modèles « spécialistes ». Cette approche permet à Microsoft de réduire le coût de fonctionnement de ses intelligences artificielles.
Selon Microsoft, MAI Code 2, son IA de programmation, offre 96 % de performances plus élevées que Claude Opus 5.5, le modèle phare d’Anthropic, pour seulement 5 % de son prix. Côté cybersécurité, MAI Cyber 2 Flash, un modèle dédié à la chasse aux failles, ferait mieux que GPT-6 Astra, l’IA cyber d’OpenAI, tout en coûtant moins cher. Notez que ces comparaisons ont été réalisées par Microsoft lui-même, en prenant en compte sa remise promotionnelle de 50 %.
Microsoft complète sa gamme d’IA avec des modèles dédiés à la voix, à la transcription et à la prise de décision. Pour Mustafa Suleyman, patron de Microsoft AI, « c’est un système, une machine à progresser que nous avons construite, qui optimise à la fois la performance et le prix ».
À lire aussi : Microsoft corrige une faille critique au coeur d’un outil de gestion ultra sensible
S’émanciper d’OpenAI et d’Anthropic
Microsoft avait déjà esquissé les contours de sa stratégie d’émancipation quelques mois plus tôt. En juin dernier, Microsoft avait déjà dévoilé sept modèles maison, dont MAI-Thinking-1, une IA capable de « raisonner » qui rivalisait selon lui avec Claude Sonnet 4.6. Pour rappel, Microsoft a bâti une grande partie de son offre d’IA sur les modèles d’OpenAI, dans lequel il a investi 13 milliards de dollars.
Par la suite, l’éditeur a misé sur Anthropic avec un investissement de 5 milliards de dollars. Par la suite, Microsoft a pris des décisions destinées à s’émanciper des laboratoires d’IA. En juin, Mustafa Suleyman expliquait que l’enjeu n’est autre que « l’autonomie à long terme de Microsoft ». Le groupe veut désormais pouvoir maîtriser les IA qui font tourner ses propres services, comme son assistant Copilot ou GitHub Copilot.
Une super IA en préparation chez Microsoft
Microsoft ne compte pas s’arrêter à ces sept nouvelles IA. Le patron de la division IA de Microsoft assure que ses équipes travaillent sur une IA généraliste de pointe, capable de rivaliser avec ChatGPT ou Claude sur tous les terrains.
« Mon équipe construit une véritable superintelligence », affirme-t-il, sans évoquer la date de sortie de cette intelligence artificielle.
Le patron de Microsoft AI promet de ne pas sacrifier la sécurité sur l’autel de la performance. Après plusieurs dérapages récents des agents IA, il assure faire de l’« alignement », c’est-à-dire la capacité d’une IA à respecter les intentions de ses créateurs, sa priorité absolue. Le modèle de cybersécurité annoncé lors de la conférence Ignite doit d’ailleurs venir renforcer Project Perception, son arsenal contre les cyberattaques.

Source : Microsoft

articles.title: Amazon lanzó un nuevo Kindle Colorsoft por 299,99 euros, pero este otro cuesta la mitad y es la compra inteligente este Black Friday
articles.text:
Dentro de apenas una semana tendrá lugar, como cada año, el Black Friday, en la que se espera que sea la mayor campaña de rebajas de todo 2026. Pero muchas tiendas ya han comenzado sus Black Friday anticipados y no hace falta esperar al viernes 27 de noviembre para aprovechar toda clase de chollos.
Kindle Colorsoft de Amazon 16 GB
Amazon es una de ellas. Porque aunque no será hasta esta medianoche cuando dará su pistoletazo de salida al Black Friday 2026, ya tiene rebajados algunos dispositivos propios como los lectores Kindle. Y entre ellos, el modelo Colorsoft de la pasada generación tiene ahora su mejor precio hasta la fecha: 164 euros.
Con pantalla a color y 16 GB de capacidad
Decimos "de la pasada generación" porque recientemente Amazon renovó parte de su catálogo de lectores Kindle, entre los que se encuentra una revisión del Colorsoft: algo más fino pero prácticamente idéntico en especificaciones al anterior Colorsoft. Aunque, eso sí, a un precio de 299,99 euros. Casi el doble de lo que cuesta (ahora que está en oferta) este otro.
De modo que, si vamos buscando el mejor precio posible, la compra inteligente pasa por el Colorsoft original, lanzado al mercado hace un par de años y ahora casi a mitad de precio. Porque con él nos ahorramos un buen pellizco a la par que nos llevamos un excelente dispositivo para leer libros, novelas gráficas y cómics.
Cuenta con una pantalla a color de 7 pulgadas a 150 ppp, que alcanza los 300 ppp cuando se establece en blanco y negro. Con una capacidad de 16 GB que da de sobra para una biblioteca de cientos de libros y una autonomía de semanas con una sola carga. Todo ello, con luz integrada ideal para leer a oscuras en la cama y también resistencia al agua, para hacer lo propio en el baño, la playa o la piscina.
