articles.title: Como desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Como desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok
Se você desbloquear alguém no TikTok, a pessoa voltará a ter acesso ao seu perfil, enviar mensagens e interagir com seus vídeos
Se você mudou de ideia e quer desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok, o processo pode ser feito pelo aplicativo no celular ou pela versão web. No app, basta acessar as configurações de privacidade para gerenciar as contas restritas, enquanto no PC é preciso localizar o perfil desejado para desfazer a restrição.
Após o desbloqueio no TikTok, o usuário recupera o acesso ao seu perfil, podendo visualizar seus vídeos e interagir novamente nas publicações abertas ao público. Vale lembrar que a plataforma não restabelece o vínculo de seguidores automaticamente, exigindo que ambos voltem a se seguir para retomar o contato antigo.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te explica como desbloquear alguém no TikTok pelo celular e pelo PC.
Você consegue desbloquear uma pessoa no TikTok pelo aplicativo, acessando a lista de restrições nas configurações da conta. Veja o passo a passo no celular Android ou iPhone.
Abra o aplicativo do TikTok no seu smartphone e toque em “Perfil”, no canto inferior direito da tela.
Toque no botão de três riscos, no canto superior direito, e selecione a opção “Configurações e privacidade”.
Navegue até a seção “Visibilidade” e toque na opção “Contas bloqueadas”.
Encontre o usuário restrito na lista e toque no botão “Desbloquear”. Assim, ele poderá voltar a ver seu perfil nas buscas e seus vídeos publicados no TikTok.
Você pode desbloquear alguém no TikTok pelo PC acessando diretamente o perfil do contato restrito. Para isso, siga os seguintes passos:
Ao desbloquear alguém no TikTok, você remove imediatamente as restrições impostas anteriormente, mas a plataforma não restaura automaticamente o vínculo entre os perfis. Veja o que muda após essa ação:
Não, o usuário não volta a seguir você automaticamente após o desbloqueio. Como a ação de bloquear alguém no TikTok rompe o vínculo entre os perfis na base de dados da rede, é preciso clicar em “Seguir” novamente para restabelecer o contato.
Se o seu perfil no TikTok estiver configurado como uma conta privada, o usuário desbloqueado precisará enviar uma nova solicitação para acompanhar suas publicações. Nesse caso, o acesso ao seu conteúdo só será liberado após a sua aprovação manual nas notificações.

articles.title: Snapchat now lets developers build AR Lenses with AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Snapchat announced on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Snapchat Lenses, which are a core part of the social network’s platform, are AR effects that let users alter their appearance, add digital objects to their surroundings, or interact with animated experiences through the camera.
The company is introducing Easy Lens CLI, which builds on its existing Easy Lens tool, which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on the web and mobile. Easy Lens CLI brings that same idea into developers’ existing workflows, allowing AI assistants to handle the technical work while creators focus on the vision for the Lens itself.
The launch indicates that Snapchat is looking to lower the barrier to creating AR content, while making its platform more accessible to developers who are increasingly using AI coding assistants. Instead of requiring creators to learn how to use Snapchat’s own development tools, the company is bringing Lens creation into the AI coding workflows they already use, which could in turn expand the pool of people who build for Snapchat.
Developers enrolled in Snapchat’s Lens+ Payouts program can earn from the Lenses they create with Easy Lens CLI. Snapchat says it paid out $1.8 million to Lens+ community creators last month.
Lens creators can describe the Lens they want in plain language, and their AI assistant handles the process from start to finish, Snapchat says. That includes building with more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, generating previews, and publishing them to Snapchat and tracking their performance.
With Easy Lens CLI, Snapchat says developers can create everything from Web Lens games with leaderboards to camera effects and beauty filters.
AI assistants can generate assets, build and test Lenses, address errors, and send updated versions directly to the creator’s phone. The new capability can take a game from an initial idea to a published Lens in a single day, without developers having to write code themselves, Snapchat says.
The tool is aimed at different types of creators. The company notes that game developers can bring existing browser games to Snapchat as Web Lenses, while AI creators can use assets from their preferred tools to build Lenses in their own style. Additionally, agencies and brands can turn existing campaign videos, images, and other brand assets into AR experiences with less production time.
Easy Lens CLI runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

articles.title: Online shoppers can save $65 in fees at Rogers, Fido right now
articles.text:
Rogers and flanker brand Fido are back to offering free shipping on phones as we head into the holiday shopping season. Moreover, Rogers is waiving its $40 device setup charge for online orders.
Previously, Rogers and Fido charged $25 for shipping. However, as of Nov. 17, both providers’ websites now list shipping costs as free. Further, a banner at the top of the websites notes that customers who buy online also skip the device setup fee.
It’s a notably change, both for the consumer savings as well as Rogers’ recent history with both these fees.
Rogers first launched the $25 shipping fee back in 2024 just ahead of that year’s iPhone launch. The fee stuck around for a while until it received some scrutiny from the CRTC earlier this year. Rogers briefly lowered the fee to $9 in July, only to increase it back to $25 in September.
The device setup fee, on the other hand, was a new charge Rogers introduced in response to the CRTC’s ban on junk fees. Rogers wasn’t the only one, with Bell also introducing a similar $40 device fee. The CRTC is still reviewing the fees to determine if the carriers violated the new rules.

articles.title: US-IT-Chaos: Wie du erkennst, ob es sich um Ausfälle oder Cyberangriffe handelt
articles.text:
Nach IT-Chaos in den USA: Wie du erkennst, ob es sich um Ausfälle oder Cyberangriffe handelt
In den USA häufen sich seit Mitte November 2026 IT-Ausfälle, von denen Millionen Nutzer:innen weltweit betroffen sind. So fielen mehrere Cloud-Dienste von Microsoft aus, darunter Outlook und Teams. Auch bei der US-Luftfahrtbehörde FAA, dem US-Geheimdienst NSA oder Online-Diensten von Apple kam es zu Störungen.
USA sehen keine Belege für Cyberangriffe
Beobachter:innen spekulieren aufgrund der Häufung und vor dem Hintergrund von tatsächlichen Cyberangriffen auf Supermärkte, Dienstleister und Behörden in Europa über entsprechende Attacken von Hacker:innen. US-Außenminister Marco Rubio erklärte dagegen am 17. November 2026, dass es „keinerlei Belege oder Gründe für diese Annahme“ gebe, wie das ZDF berichtet.
Die Kolleg:innen von Wired haben einen Guide mit verschiedenen Fragen erstellt, die sich Nutzer:innen stellen können. Die Beantwortung soll dann dazu beitragen, besser einschätzen zu können, ob es sich um Ausfälle oder Cyberattacken handelt.
Suche nach technischen Fehlern
Zunächst einmal sollte die Suche nach technischen Fehlern Priorität haben. IT-Expert:innen gehen jedenfalls davon aus, dass fehlerhafte Softwareupdates, Änderungen an der Konfiguration oder beschädigte Kabel oder Geräte deutlich häufiger vorkommen als Cyberangriffe.
Doug Madory vom IT-Sicherheitsunternehmen Infoblox schätzt gegenüber Wired, dass bei den von ihm beobachteten Netzwerkausfällen nur einer von tausend auf einen Hackerangriff zurückging. Danach sollten Nutzer:innen die Statusseiten und offizielle Mitteilungen von Betreibern betroffener Dienste prüfen. Je mehr Firmen auf große Cloud-Anbieter wie AWS setzen, desto mehr Dienste und Kund:innen können von einem dort auftretenden Problem betroffen sein.
Mithilfe von Diensten wie Cloudflare Radar lässt sich zudem einfach ermitteln, ob nur ein Anbieter oder mehrere Netzwerke in der Region von Ausfällen betroffen sind. Daran kann man ablesen, ob es sich um ein fehlerhaftes Update bei einem Betreiber oder etwa um ein beschädigtes Glasfaserkabel handeln könnte.
Bekennerschreiben von Ransomware-Gruppen
Hinweise auf Cyberangriffe liefern dagegen mögliche Bekennerschreiben, etwa von Ransomware-Gruppen. Diese sind allerdings mit Vorsicht zu genießen, da solche Behauptungen übertrieben oder erfunden sein könnten, wie Wired warnt. Eine Bestätigung können Mitteilungen der betroffenen Organisation, von Behörden oder unabhängigen Sicherheitsforscher:innen liefern.
Einen weiteren Anhaltspunkt kann auch die Dauer des Ausfalls liefern. Geht es um ein fehlerhaftes Update, ist das oft innerhalb von Minuten oder Stunden geregelt. Bei einer Ransomware-Attacke kann es dagegen Tage, Wochen oder Monate dauern, bis ausgefallene Dienste wieder normal funktionieren.
Technik wird immer komplexer
Im Fall der aktuellen IT-Ausfälle in den USA kommt noch ein weiterer Punkt dazu, der eine genauere Betrachtung verdient: die zeitliche Nähe der Angriffe. Experte Madory erklärt allerdings, dass die Serie an Störungen auch schlicht zeigen könnte, wie komplex die Technik geworden sei.
„In unserer Gesellschaft läuft alles über internetbasierte Dienste. Und die fallen von Zeit zu Zeit aus“, so Madory gegenüber Wired. Solche Ausfälle ließen sich nie ganz verhindern. Wichtig sei zu verstehen, was jeden einzelnen Ausfall ausmache und was man daraus lernen könne.

articles.title: TechCabal expands SA coverage with launch of TC Mzansi
articles.text:
TechCabal is launching TC Mzansi, a weekly newsletter dedicated to South Africa’s technology and innovation economy, as the pan-African technology publication deepens its editorial presence in one of the continent’s largest technology markets.
Tomiwa Aladekomo, CEO of Big Cabal Media, TechCabal’s parent company, announced the newsletter at Africa Tech Festival in Cape Town on Wednesday. The first edition is scheduled to reach subscribers’ inboxes on November 23, extending the publication’s coverage of South Africa and the wider Southern African Development Community (SADC) region.
The launch reflects TechCabal’s push to build a stronger regional newsroom presence and give South Africa’s technology industry more dedicated coverage. While the publication has reported on African technology for 13 years, starting in Lagos, Nigeria, it has expanded its operations in South Africa with a Johannesburg-based editorial team.
“We have hired an A-team here, and next week we’re launching a new newsletter focused on South Africa. It’s TC Mzansi,” Aladekomo said during a fireside chat moderated by Jessica Hope, founder and chief executive officer of public relations firm Wimbart.
He said the newsletter would focus on telling stories about innovation in South Africa, including the journey from university research and technological development to commercial products, as well as connecting the country’s technology ecosystem with the rest of the continent.
TC Mzansi will cover developments across South Africa’s startup and technology industries, including funding, acquisitions, telecommunications, digital payments, artificial intelligence and policy. Its coverage will also extend to SADC markets, particularly developments with implications for South African businesses and investors.
The newsletter is designed to go beyond a roundup of headlines. Its editorial format will combine important regional developments with deeper reporting and analysis of the businesses, investments, people and policy decisions shaping the technology economy.
Each edition will include a selection of major headlines, a closer look at a major development, technology business moves, relevant industry data, and developments readers should watch.
“Super excited about that and about telling the stories of innovation here, the bridge between research and technology in universities and what becomes end products, and connecting South African tech with the rest of the continent,” Aladekomo said.
The launch comes as South Africa’s tech ecosystem navigates a period of significant change. Telecommunications consolidation, the expansion of digital financial services, artificial intelligence adoption and renewed investment in digital infrastructure are reshaping the competitive landscape.
Aladekomo said connecting South African technology with the wider continent was an important part of what made the market exciting for TechCabal.
TC Mzansi joins TechCabal’s existing newsletter portfolio, which includes TC Daily, its weekday briefing on Africa’s technology ecosystem; The Next Wave, which examines innovation and the future of the industry; and Francophone Weekly, which covers technology developments in French-speaking Africa.
The launch is also part of a wider refresh of Big Cabal Media’s newsletter products, including a redesigned TC Daily and the introduction of Crypto by TC, a vertical focused on cryptocurrency developments, deals and regulation across Africa.

articles.title: Confirmada la calificación por edades de 'Avengers: Doomsday': será la película más violenta de los Vengadores
articles.text:
Marvel ya ha recibido la calificación por edades de su próxima película, Avengers: Doomsday. Y lo cierto es que la cinta ha marcado un hito en la historia de la compañía. Algo que ha provocado que la expectación y la tensión aumenten aún más entre los fans, ansiosos por ver qué les deparará a sus héroes favoritos en esta aventura. Durante meses se ha hablado de que la cinta supondrá una verdadera masacre para los personajes. Y ahora, parece que esta dirección se confirma.
Porque resulta que la MPAA (Motion Picture Association of America) le ha otorgado a Avengers: Doomsday una calificación por edades de PG-13. Es decir, no es apta para menores de 13 años. Concretamente, el organismo señala las causas como "violencia/acción, imágenes sangrientas y lenguaje soez". Y es aquí donde el filme destaca dentro del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel.
Hasta ahora, el aviso de "imágenes sangrientas" era algo que jamás se había visto en Marvel con la evidente excepción de Deadpool y Lobezno (que tenía calificación R). El resto de películas de los Vengadores, aunque también tuvieran una calificación de PG-13, nunca había tenido ese aviso. Este detalle anticipa lo que ya parece inevitable para los Héroes más Poderosos de la Tierra. Que Avengers: Doomsday va a ser una escabechina.
Qué pasará en Avengers: Doomsday
En Avengers: Doomsday, evidentemente sabemos que el gran villano que tendrán los héroes de Marvel enfrente será el Doctor Doom de Robert Downey Jr. Apenas hemos podido verle en acción hasta ahora, más allá de los tráileres de la película y de algunas escenas post-créditos en otros proyectos recientes de la saga. Pero gracias a estos pequeños vistazos y a su enorme legado de los cómics sabemos que se trata de uno de los personajes más poderosos de La Casa de las Ideas.
De esta versión, concretamente, ya hemos visto cómo es capaz de parar un golpe del Stormbreaker de Thor con tan solo dos dedos, sin inmutarse. También le hemos visto levantar todo un ejército de enormes Centinelas robóticos. Y, para colmo, sus fuerzas aliadas no dejan de crecer. Gracias a los paneles y puestos promocionales en distintas convenciones alrededor del mundo sabemos que el Doctor Doom contará con unas misteriosas mujeres con él. Y todo apunta a que se trata de algún tipo de hechiceras. Pero lo realmente grave ha sucedido en los últimos meses.
En el reestreno de Avengers Endgame Encore se añadió una nueva escena en la que Doom secuestraba a Bruce Banner, escondido tras la catástrofe provocada por Hulk en Spider-Man: Brand New Day. A buen seguro, el villano va a tener entre sus filas al forzudo Gigante Escarlata bajo su control. Y hace solo unos días, en la escena post-créditos de VisionQuest, vimos cómo el Doctor Doom resucitaba y reclutaba también a la mismísima Bruja Escarlata, considerada por muchos como el personaje más poderoso del UCM hasta el momento. Con tantas alianzas en su bando, los Vengadores lo tienen realmente difícil en Avengers: Doomsday. Por los avisos en su calificación por edades, parece que muchos de ellos no saldrán con vida de la película.
Avengers: Doomsday se estrena en cines el 18 de diciembre.

articles.title: Elon Musk tries to explain what’s going on with Ukraine and Starlink
articles.text:
Elon Musk said Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is lying about disruptions to Starshield in Ukraine and that he’s trying to misuse SpaceX’s consumer service, Starlink, for military purposes. Musk made the comments at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday as he tried to explain the conflict following weeks of back and forth between Zelenskyy, Musk, and the US government.
Elon Musk tries to explain what’s going on with Ukraine and Starlink
The SpaceX CEO claims that Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is ‘lying’ about using Starshield.
“From the beginning, I’ve said that Starlink is a civilian system,” Musk said. “It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government. But do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions.”
Musk also said that “if they want to do something that’s an offensive military action, it needs to be the Starshield system where the kill decision is that of the War Department, perhaps ultimately the president, and not mine.”
The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, said that President Zelenskyy refers to the system as Starshield and is claiming that is the system that was slowed down. “That’s false,” Musk said, claiming that Zelenskyy is “not always truthful.”
Sorkin asked, “So when President Zelenskyy talks about using Starshield, he is not using Starshield, or he’s lying?”
“He is lying,” Musk said. “What he is actually saying is he wants to use Starlink for offensive military operations.”

articles.title: What Is Driving Silicon Wafer Demand Recovery?
articles.text:
The high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.
Global silicon wafer shipments are forecast to grow 11.8% in 2026, according to the Q3 2026 SEMI Silicon Wafer Market Monitor. This increase is primarily due to strong demand for AI, which is projected to drive shipments through 2029.
Alongside AI, rising process material sales are also supporting recovery. The positive correlation between material sales and silicon wafer demand not only reflects growth in manufacturing complexity, but it also points to greater material consumption per wafer.
Finally, increases in memory demand, precautionary inventory building, and global fab capacity expansions are boosting silicon wafer shipments as well.
To better understand today’s landscape, it’s helpful to revisit past silicon wafer demand curves. From 2018 to 2019 and from 2022 to 2023, silicon wafer shipments rose ahead of major increases in memory work-in-process (WIP) inventories, or unfinished memory chips undergoing fabrication. However, shipments lagged at the same time WIP inventory peaked. Because fabrication lines were already producing at full capacity, their need for silicon wafers slowed.
While this pattern provides historical context for today’s demand recovery, the high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.
Silicon Wafer Shipments and Memory WIP: Historical Lead–Lag Pattern. Both series use four-quarter moving averages. Sources: SEMI SMG and financial disclosures from Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and Micron. Data for 3Q26–2Q27 are forecasts.
SEMI’s fab investment outlook predicts continued growth in planned equipment spending beyond 2026. So long as investment plans remain broadly on track, ongoing equipment installation and capacity ramps are likely to support silicon wafer demand. The report also demonstrated a widening gap between YoY growth rates for semiconductor fab equipment spending and silicon wafer manufacturing equipment spending, suggesting that investment support for wafer demand may persist longer than initially expected.
This also helps explain why the historical relationship between wafer shipments and WIP does not necessarily imply an imminent slowdown. Wafer procurement momentum can moderate before WIP inventories peak, although investment support may slow if moderation becomes visible in wafer shipments.
Investment Spread: A Signal of a Later Wafer-Cycle Slowdown. Spread between the YoY growth rates of semiconductor fab equipment spending and silicon wafer manufacturers’ equipment spending, compared with silicon wafer shipment trends. Sources: SEMI Silicon Wafer Shipment Statistics and SEMI WWSEMS. Shipment data are updated through 2Q26, while equipment spending data are updated through August 2026.
SEMI projects continued wafer shipment growth in 2027, although growth will likely be more moderate than it was in 2026. As inventory stockpiles subside, ongoing production will be important for sustaining demand. If planned capacity expansions continue and customers buy the resulting chips, semiconductor companies can gradually reduce their wafer inventories while also maintaining their purchase rate. However, investment delays or weaker demand for semiconductors would slow this absorption and increase the risk of declining silicon wafer orders.
While AI-related investment is a critical source of support, broader semiconductor recovery is still uneven. Because of this, the key to maintaining demand growth will be how quickly fabs can use wafers purchased in advance. Doing so will help shape the duration of this recovery period and the depth of any subsequent wafer inventory adjustments.

articles.title: XPRIZE launches $6m competition to tackle foundational learning crisis in Africa, India - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Global non-profit XPRIZE has launched XPRIZE Accelerate Learning, a two-year, US$6 million competition seeking tech-driven solutions that help first graders in Sub-Saharan Africa and India master foundational reading and maths.
XPRIZE is an established global leader in designing, launching, and executing large-scale competitions to solve humanity’s greatest challenges.
The competition, which takes place in Rwanda, aims to cut the time it takes children to learn reading and maths skills from four years to one, at a cost as low as US$10 per child, and to reach nearly one million students in target communities. In Sub-Saharan Africa, nine in 10 children cannot read and understand a simple sentence by age 10.
Startups, non-profits, universities, corporates, government agencies and individuals can enter one or both of two tracks. The Core Track, worth US$5 million, seeks end-to-end solutions that improve mastery by at least 25 percentage points at under US$10 per child per year. Up to eight finalists will deploy at school district scale, with the winner taking home US$2.5 million.
The Last Mile Moonshot track, with separate US$400,000 purses for Sub-Saharan Africa and India targets a 50 percentage point improvement at under US$40 per child. Finalists will test their solutions in a six-month randomised controlled trial.
Teams will be paired with local schools or districts to co-design and test their solutions, so that governments can adopt them long term.
“Rwanda’s Vision 2050 depends on a skilled and productive workforce, and that journey begins with children who can read, understand and apply what they learn,” said Joseph Nsengimana, Rwanda’s Minister of Education. “We welcome XPRIZE as a partner in accelerating solutions and invite Rwanda’s innovators, educators and researchers to help transform learning outcomes for every child.”
Partners include the Republic of Rwanda, the African Union Development Agency-NEPAD, Equity Group Foundation, ShikshaNext and IDinsight. Qualified teams will be announced in 2027, and winners in 2029.

articles.title: Silvia Intxaurrondo, periodista, 46 años: “De Iñaki Gabilondo aprendí que si nos tomamos treinta segundos para pensar lo que estamos contando, podemos afinar la información”
articles.text:
“Si nos tomamos treinta segundos para pensar lo que estamos contando, podemos afinar la información”, explica Silvia Intxaurrondo. “En ese tiempo te da tiempo a reflexionar, a ubicarte y pensar quién lo puede contar mejor”.
Así lo ha explicado durante una entrevista en la promoción de la publicación de su primera novela “Solas en el silencio”. Sobre el aprendizaje de Gabilondo, explica que uno debe pararse a pensar en lo que va a contar. Trabajó con Iñaki Gabilondo en “Hoy por hoy” y luego en el telediario de noche de Cuatro.
Silvia Intxaurrondo (Barakaldo, 1979) ha trabajado en la Cadena SER, CNN+, Cuatro, ETB y Telemadrid. Ahora presenta “La hora de La 1” en Televisión Española. También ha sido en Noticias Cuatro donde ha coincidido durante cuatro años con Gabilondo en la presentación de la edición nocturna.
“Porque a veces en esos treinta segundos, podemos confirmarla, rechazarla o determinar que es un bulo”.
Unos segundos para consultar a quien sabe
Intxaurrondo vinculaba ese margen con el propio oficio: “A veces esos treinta segundos o un minuto son el tiempo diferencial entre un periodista y el que no lo es. Treinta segundos para que pienses y te hagas unas preguntas”.
También es posible que haya que recurrir a otro para resolver alguna duda. Intxaurrondo explica que a veces es necesario pedir ayuda. No siempre tenemos todas las respuestas.
“En ese tiempo te da tiempo a reflexionar, a ubicarte y pensar quién lo puede contar mejor”. Tras recordar el aprendizaje de Gabilondo, ha añadido otro de los aspectos que debe cumplir un buen periodista: “Eso es lo más importante que me enseñó. Y el trabajo duro”.

articles.title: Windows 11 : pourquoi certaines de vos applications risquent bientôt de refuser de démarrer
articles.text:
La sécurité dans Windows 11 est sur le point de subir une évolution majeure. Microsoft vient en effet d’introduire sa nouvelle Windows Baseline Protection, un nouveau système de protection qui laissera chaque application installée sur votre PC décider si votre configuration est suffisamment sécurisée pour qu’il puisse s’exécuter.
Un nouveau bilan de sécurité unique pour Windows
Concrètement, cette Windows Baseline Protection consiste à regrouper huit fonctionnalités de sécurité matérielle et logicielle du système sous la forme d’une simple vérification binaire. Contrairement au passé, où la sécurité d’un PC consistait à un assemblage d’options séparées qui devaient être vérifiées individuellement, ce nouvel outil, va regrouper huit modules de protection du système au sein d’un bilan de sécurité unique qui fournira un résultat simple.
Windows contrôlera alors votre puce TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, la sécurité basée sur la virtualisation (VBS), l’intégrité de la mémoire, la signature des pilotes (pour empêcher le chargement des pilotes de périphériques non identifiés), les pilotes certifiés Windows, la protection contre le débogage du noyau, et enfin le blocage des pilotes vulnérables.
Au démarrage de votre PC, tous ces éléments de sécurité seront ainsi vérifiés par Windows qui indiquera si « oui » ou « non » votre machine est correctement protégée.
Ce signal unique sera ensuite annoncé aux applications installées sur votre ordinateur qui pourront alors décider des mesures à prendre en fonction du niveau d’exigence respecté par votre PC.
Un manque de sécurité pourra bloquer certaines applis
Avec ce nouveau système de protection intégré à Windows 11, Microsoft veut laisser aux éditeurs d’applications le choix de la réaction à adopter en cas de manquement côté sécurité.
Vos applications pourront ainsi afficher un simple message d’avertissement à l’écran. Elles pourront aussi choisir de restreindre l’accès à certaines de leurs fonctionnalités, avec dans les cas les plus extrêmes, de bloquer complètement leur lancement si la sécurité requise n’est pas atteinte.
Plusieurs grands éditeurs sont d’ores et déjà en train de tester ce système, à commencer par Adobe. L’éditeur de Photoshop aurait ainsi une nouvelle solution pour lutter contre le piratage et les logiciels contrefaits ou modifiés. Battle.net (Blizzard) testerait également ce système de protection pour renforcer la lutte contre la triche dans les jeux vidéo. D’autres éditeurs, comme Schoolyear (pour vérifier la sécurité du PC d’un étudiant avant d’autoriser le début d’un examen en ligne), 1PassWord et Raycast (pour garantir la protection des mots de passe et des interactions avec l’IA) testeraient également cette technologie.
Comment vérifier si votre PC est correctement protégé ?
Pour savoir si votre machine est conforme aux critères de sécurité de Microsoft, vous pouvez vous rendre dans les Paramètres de Windows 11, puis dans la section Sécurité, entrer dans le module de Protection de base.
Un indicateur visuel indiquera l’état de votre PC. Un bouclier vert sera ainsi affiché lorsque « Tout est protégé », tandis qu’un bouclier jaune sera affiché si « une attention est requise » de votre part. Dans le cas où une option de sécurité manquerait à l’appel, Microsoft affichera un bouton pour réactiver celle-ci et redémarrer votre PC.
Et si toutefois l’un des paramètres du BIOS/UEFI devait être modifié, Microsoft affichera un QR Code à scanner avec votre smartphone pour accéder à un guide d’utilisateur décrivant la marche à suivre pas à pas.
Ce nouveau système de sécurité est pour l’heure en cours de test auprès des Insiders. Microsoft n’a pour l’instant donné aucune date de déploiement dans la version stable de Windows 11.

articles.title: British Scattered Spider hacker sentenced to 6 years in prison
articles.text:
A leader of the Scattered Spider cybercrime collective has been sentenced to six years in prison in the United States for stealing millions in cryptocurrency and conspiring to hack a dozen companies.
US prosecutors charged 24-year-old British man Tyler Robert Buchanan and four other suspects in November with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft in relation to a series of phishing attacks between September 2021 and April 2023.
According to court documents, their victims include companies across a wide range of industries, such as telecommunications, technology, business process outsourcing (BPO), entertainment, and information technology (IT) suppliers, as well as virtual currency providers, cloud communications providers, and individuals.
Buchanan and his accomplices sent hundreds of SMS phishing messages to victim companies' employees' phones (while impersonating the companies or a contracted IT or BPO supplier) to trick them into entering sensitive information (including credentials and personally identifiable information) into phishing pages that looked like their employers' legitimate websites.
The stolen information was used to steal over $11.6 million of virtual currency after compromising victims' cryptocurrency accounts and wallets via Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) swaps (also known as SIM swapping attacks).
"Those thefts had severe, life-altering consequences for many victims and underscore both the seriousness and far-reaching impact of this conspiracy," the prosecutors argued in a sentencing memorandum.
"In April 2023, on a digital device found at Buchanan's Scotland residence, he possessed the names and addresses of numerous individual victims, including a text file that contained cryptocurrency seed phrases and login information for one victim's account," the US Justice Department added.
Buchanan was arrested in Palma de Mallorca, Spain, in June 2024, has been in US federal custody since April 2025, and pleaded guilty to crypto theft charges in April.
Three of his accomplices (Evans Onyeaka Osiebo, Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy, and Joel Martin Evans) were also charged in November 2024 with wire fraud, wire fraud conspiracy, and aggravated identity theft and are now serving multi-year prison sentences after pleading guilty.
Noah Michael Urban (also known online as Sosa and Elijah), a fourth conspirator and another Scattered Spider key member, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to wire fraud and conspiracy charges in April 2025.
Scattered Spider hacking collective
The Scattered Spider gang (also tracked as 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Octo Tempest, Starfraud, UNC3944, and Muddled Libra) is a loose-knit group of young, English-speaking threat actors that orchestrates attacks through Telegram channels, Discord servers, and hacker forums.
Scattered Spider has also partnered with several Russian ransomware operations since early 2023, including BlackCat/AlphV, Qilin, and RansomHub.
This cybercrime group was previously linked to breaches at multiple high-profile companies and organizations, including Caesars, Riot Games, MailChimp, Twilio, DoorDash, and Reddit.
According to the FBI, they're using a wide range of tactics to breach corporate victims' networks, including social engineering, multi-factor authentication (MFA) bombing (targeted MFA fatigue), phishing, and SIM swapping.
Some Scattered Spider members have also previously been linked to "The Com," another hacking collective behind violent incidents and cyberattacks.

articles.title: GTA 6 n’est pas parfait : ce que lui reprochent les tests les plus sévères
articles.text:
Quand les « pires » notes attribuées à un jeu vidéo sont des 8 et des 9 sur 10, on comprend vite que GTA 6 est en train d’écraser la concurrence. Pourtant, au milieu du concert de louanges qui accompagne la sortie du titre ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X/S, les critiques de PlayStation LifeStyle et de ScreenHub ont le mérite de pointer du doigt les limites bien réelles du jeu de Rockstar. Leurs reproches portent sur la fluidité, le rythme du début de partie et l’obligation d’entretenir physiquement les personnages.
1. Le plafond technique des 30 images par seconde (et l’absence de mode Performance)
C’est le principal reproche formulé par PlayStation LifeStyle, qui qualifie pourtant le jeu de « titre le plus ambitieux techniquement jamais créé » avant de lui retirer un point pour sa fluidité. Sur PS5, GTA 6 vise 30 images par seconde (avec des baisses à 20 FPS), sans mode Performance à 60 images par seconde. Le testeur a joué sur une PS5 classique, mais précise que la PS5 Pro est elle aussi limitée à 30 images par seconde avec des
Pire encore, le nombre d’images par seconde chute régulièrement dans certaines zones très denses de la carte, au point que le journaliste avoue avoir fini par éviter certains quartiers pour ne pas subir ces ralentissements. Pour un joueur habitué à 60 ou 120 images par seconde, l’adaptation prend du temps. Le testeur compare l’expérience au fait de « regarder la trilogie Le Seigneur des Anneaux sur un iPhone ». L’œuvre reste grandiose, mais le support ne lui rend pas justice. Il réserve son 10/10 à une future version PC ou PS6.
2. Un début de partie beaucoup trop lent et bavard
De son côté, ScreenHub attaque le jeu sur un terrain bien plus sensible : le rythme et l’écriture de GTA 6. La journaliste confesse s’être « complètement ennuyée pendant les douze premières heures ». Loin du chaos immédiat et débridé attendu d’un GTA, le premier chapitre ressemble selon elle à un « simulateur de bon petit ami » très dirigiste, dans lequel Jason passe son temps à rendre service à Lucia pendant et après son passage en prison.
Selon le média australien, il faut attendre le chapitre 3 (soit environ 25 heures de jeu) pour que l’aventure s’ouvre vraiment et devienne amusante, et même 47 heures (au chapitre 4) pour avoir enfin l’impression de jouer l’histoire plutôt que de la regarder. ScreenHub pointe aussi une écriture inégale, visiblement écrite et réécrite par de nombreuses mains pendant des années. Le jeu hésite, selon la critique, entre la satire potache qui a fait la réputation de la licence et un drame social sérieux sur la pauvreté en Amérique, sans réussir ni l’un ni l’autre.
3. Des mécaniques de survie et de sport jugées pénibles
Enfin, ScreenHub épingle une mécanique de gameplay de GTA 6 directement héritée de Red Dead Redemption 2 et GTA : San Andreas : l’obligation d’entretenir physiquement ses personnages. Pour garder Jason et Lucia en forme, endurants et musclés, le joueur doit régulièrement les nourrir et leur faire faire de l’exercice au quotidien (tractions, shakes protéinés, alimentation équilibrée).
Une contrainte jugée fastidieuse et peu gratifiante par la critique, qui avoue avoir détesté devoir s’occuper du régime alimentaire et des séances de musculation de Jason depuis son canapé. Ces reproches n’ont pas empêché les deux médias de saluer l’État de Leonida, le duo formé par Jason et Lucia et le niveau de détail du monde ouvert.

articles.title: Sur Windows 11, Copilot pourra bientôt vous aider à comprendre pourquoi votre PC fait des siennes
articles.text:
Microsoft prépare une nouvelle fonction de diagnostic permettant à Copilot d'examiner l'état du PC et d'aider à identifier l'origine d'un dysfonctionnement, sans modifier les paramètres du système.
Un casque Bluetooth qui ne donne plus signe de vie, une connexion Internet qui se traîne sans raison apparente… Quand Windows 11 fait des siennes, trouver l'origine du problème peut vite se transformer en jeu de piste. À l'occasion de sa conférence Ignite 2026, Microsoft a dévoilé une nouvelle capacité de Copilot qui pourrait nous éviter quelques heures de recherches et de dépannage à l'aveugle.
Copilot pourra examiner Windows, mais pas le réparer
Microsoft avait déjà commencé à explorer cette piste avec PC Insights, une fonction expérimentale apparue en juillet 2026, qui permet à Copilot de consulter des informations sur l'état du PC, comme l'utilisation du processeur, la batterie ou les périphériques connectés. À l’Ignite, la firme a annoncé vouloir pousser l'exercice plus loin, en permettant à l'assistant de rechercher les causes possibles d'un dysfonctionnement.
Il suffira de décrire le problème rencontré pour que Copilot puisse lancer une analyse du système en lecture seule, examiner les informations pertinentes et suggérer des pistes de dépannage, sans obliger les utilisateurs et utilisatrices à déchiffrer eux-mêmes les données techniques.
Cette fonction ne permettra toutefois pas à l'IA de modifier la configuration de Windows ou d'appliquer des correctifs. Microsoft n'a pas détaillé la nature des données de diagnostic auxquelles Copilot pourra accéder, ni les autorisations nécessaires pour les consulter.
Cette nouvelle capacité fait partie des fonctions locales annoncées à l'Ignite dans le cadre de la stratégie d'intelligence hybride de Microsoft. Elle doit arriver prochainement sur les Copilot+ PC, sans date de lancement plus précise ni confirmation d'une disponibilité sur les autres ordinateurs Windows 11.

articles.title: PhysicsWallah targets over Rs 9,000 Cr revenue by FY30
articles.text:
PhysicsWallah targets over Rs 9,000 Cr revenue by FY30
At its first Investor Day in Mumbai on November 18, the company targeted average annual revenue growth of about 25% or more between FY27 and FY30 and a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin above 20%.
Edtech firm PhysicsWallah said it is targeting Rs 9,000-10,000 crore revenue by FY30, an ambition that will test whether an online-first education business can keep growing while lifting margins and expanding its physical network.
At its first Investor Day in Mumbai on November 18, the company targeted average annual revenue growth of about 25% or more between FY27 and FY30 and a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin above 20%.
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA is its non-GAAP measure of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. Online operations are expected to contribute about two-thirds of revenue by FY30.
The target more than doubles FY26 revenue of Rs 3,900 crore. Revenue from operations reached Rs 1,242 crore in the latest quarter ended 30 September. H1 FY27 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin was 8.3%, against 18.8% in Q2. The company has noted that exam-related enrolments and course-fee recognition affect the timing of reported revenue.
Co-founded by Alakh Pandey and Prateek Maheshwari, PW began as a YouTube teaching channel in 2016 and became an education platform in 2020. Its offerings span test preparation, skilling, higher education and education-abroad programmes, delivered through digital content, an app and physical centres. It listed in November 2025.
Pandey said, “We started PW so that no family has to choose between its savings and a child's education.”
Redseer estimates India’s test-preparation market at $14.8 billion in FY26, rising to $23-$26 billion by FY30 at annual growth of 12-15%. PW’s 25%+ target is faster. Redseer says families increasingly judge providers on teaching quality and reliable results, not reach alone.
Allen expanded from 43 cities in FY22 to 78 by FY26, taking coaching into smaller cities and adding AI-supported assessment tools. In September, upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy, highlighting consolidation after the pandemic-era boom.
Meanwhile, regulation is tightening. Central guidelines circulated in 2024 address coaching-centre registration, fees, infrastructure and student welfare. Several states have since introduced rules or laws. Consumer-protection guidelines also prohibit misleading coaching advertisements and the use of successful students’ testimonials without written consent.
CFO Amit Sachdeva said, “Our FY30 ambition is about profit growing faster than revenue. We will stay disciplined with capital and report our progress every year.”

articles.title: Ethiopian Airlines reports cyberattack a week after Air Botswana
articles.text:
Ethiopian Airlines on Wednesday warned customers that some of their information may have been exposed in a recent cyberattack, weeks after Air Botswana disclosed a suspected ransomware incident on its internal systems.
In an email notice sent through its frequent-flyer programme ShebaMiles, the Addis Ababa-based carrier said the incident was “of limited scope” and said there was “currently no evidence” that customers’ financial information was accessed.
Ethiopian Airlines did not provide the date of the intrusion or the customer data and gave no estimate of how many people might be affected. It also did not say whether the breach was confined to the loyalty programme or whether bookings and flight operations were affected.
The breach at Ethiopian Airlines underscores the risks facing carriers as they rely on third parties to handle everything from customer enquiries to airport check-in. An intrusion can expose millions of passenger records without grounding a flight, as Qantas found last year, while an attack on a shared check-in provider can disrupt operations at several airports at once.
“We are treating this matter with the utmost seriousness and are working closely with our cybersecurity partners and relevant authorities to investigate the incident and assess its full impact,” the airline said. “As a precaution, we encourage you to remain vigilant against any suspicious or unsolicited communications.”
ShebaMiles had more than 5.38 million members when Ethiopian Airlines announced a partnership with Etihad Airways’ loyalty programme in 2025. The airline group carried about 19 million passengers and generated $7.6 billion in revenue in its 2024/25 financial year.
Aviation attacks
The Ethiopian Airlines disclosure follows a series of incidents that have exposed the aviation business, from employee records and loyalty accounts to the software airports use to check in passengers.
Air Botswana said it detected unauthorised access on November 3 to systems containing employee and internal information. The state-owned carrier described the incident as suspected ransomware and said passenger bookings, aircraft systems and flight operations were not affected. It has yet to disclose whether any data was copied.
At Qantas, an attacker gained access to a third-party customer service platform used by one of the airline’s call centres in 2025. The Australian carrier said the breach compromised some personal information belonging to 5.7 million customers, including names, email addresses and frequent-flyer details. Qantas said the incident had no impact on its operations.
An attack on Collins Aerospace two months later showed how disruption at a single supplier could spread across airports. The ransomware attack knocked out automated check-in and baggage drop at several European airports, including Heathrow, affecting dozens of flights.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.text:
AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
- Date:
- November 14, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Berkeley
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
- Share:
More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. By comparing the electrical patterns recorded in these scans with information from death certificates, the researchers taught an AI system to recognize subtle differences between healthy individuals, patients with known heart risks, and people who eventually died from sudden cardiac causes.
The team then evaluated the technology using thousands of additional patient records from the United States and Taiwan, testing whether the patterns could reliably identify people at heightened risk in different populations.
AI Detects Hidden Heart Risks That Standard Tests Miss
The results suggest that AI can identify vulnerable patients more effectively than the conventional tests doctors typically rely on. Current screening methods largely focus on how much blood the heart pumps with each contraction, a measurement used to assess whether someone might benefit from an implanted defibrillator.
Using these traditional measurements, doctors can identify a group of patients with an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 4.6%. The AI system, however, identified a group with an annual death rate of 7%, demonstrating a greater ability to distinguish patients facing serious danger.
Importantly, the algorithm also recognized a broader population of people at elevated risk, including thousands who would not normally raise concerns under existing medical guidelines. Most of these individuals would have been classified as relatively low risk using conventional methods.
Another major advantage is that the AI system works with ordinary EKG images, which are already routinely collected in hospitals and medical centers around the world. This means the technology could potentially improve screening without requiring an entirely new type of medical test.
The findings, published in Nature, could eventually help physicians make more informed decisions about who should receive an implanted defibrillator. They also raise an intriguing scientific question about what changes inside the heart produce the electrical patterns that AI has learned to recognize.
"Medical decisions are really hard, and I think that's why AI is so exciting for me," said Ziad Obermeyer, an associate professor at UC Berkeley's School of Public Health and the study's lead author. "We can not only make better decisions, but also start to understand what's actually going on with these patients before their heart stops."
Why Sudden Cardiac Death Is So Difficult to Predict
Sudden cardiac arrest is different from a heart attack. A heart attack happens when blood flow to part of the heart becomes blocked or severely restricted. Cardiac arrest, by contrast, results from a failure of the electrical signals that coordinate the heartbeat.
Immediate CPR and an electrical shock from an automated external defibrillator can sometimes restore the heart's rhythm. However, roughly 90% of people who experience sudden cardiac arrest outside a hospital die within minutes, making early recognition of those at risk especially important.
For Obermeyer, an emergency physician whose research combines artificial intelligence, medicine, and health policy, sudden cardiac death remains one of medicine's most frustrating unsolved problems.
Because victims often die without warning, researchers have limited opportunities to observe what happens inside the heart immediately before it stops. An autopsy may uncover blocked blood vessels, hardened tissue, or other structural abnormalities, but it cannot fully reveal how the heart was functioning in the moments leading up to death.
"One thing that makes the problem very tragic, but also very well suited for AI, is that we have the cure for this problem," Obermeyer said. "If you knew you were one of the people who was going to drop dead, you would go to a cardiologist and you'd get a defibrillator implanted. The problem is that doctors can't figure out who needs one before it's too late."
The Problem With Current Heart Risk Screening
Doctors currently rely heavily on a measurement of how effectively the heart pushes blood out with each beat. Patients whose hearts pump below a specified threshold may be considered candidates for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator, a device that can deliver an electrical shock when a dangerous heart rhythm develops.
But obtaining this measurement generally requires a more extensive medical evaluation. Many people who eventually experience sudden cardiac arrest never receive such testing because they have no obvious reason to suspect they are in danger.
The approach also has limitations for patients who are identified as high risk. About two-thirds of implanted defibrillators in these patients never need to deliver a shock. As a result, many individuals undergo expensive, invasive procedures for potentially fatal emergencies that may never occur.
At the same time, thousands of people who are not recognized as being at risk die unexpectedly each year.
"In some fraction of those people, we could have prevented those deaths if we had just known it in time," Obermeyer said. "There are a lot of lives being lost from people who are dropping dead of sudden cardiac death that are preventable if we just had better AI tools to find these things."
The researchers hope that identifying more accurate warning signs could help doctors direct preventive treatments toward the patients most likely to benefit.
How Researchers Trained AI to Recognize Deadly Heart Patterns
Developing the algorithm required three independent collections of medical data gathered from different parts of the world.
The researchers began with six years of EKG recordings from Sweden's unified healthcare system. By linking these scans to death certificates, they could examine the electrical patterns of patients who later experienced sudden cardiac death and compare them with those of other patients.
The AI learned to identify combinations of spikes, waves, and other characteristics in the recordings that appeared to be associated with increased risk. Once the system had been trained, the team tested it against two additional datasets: two years of anonymized EKG records from a San Diego hospital system and a separate collection of patient data from Taipei.
This international testing helped researchers evaluate whether the algorithm's predictive abilities extended beyond the Swedish population used to develop it.
"Good AI starts with good data," said Obermeyer, who is also part of the joint UCSF-UC Berkeley Computational Precision Health program. "Unfortunately, data like the ones we used for this study are incredibly hard to access. It's a big part of why there's so little clinical AI in use today."
Obtaining and organizing the information was itself a massive undertaking. According to Obermeyer, assembling the datasets took approximately 10 years and involved contributions from two organizations he helped establish, Dandelion Health and Nightingale Open Science. Both organizations work to advance medical research through better access to data and artificial intelligence.
"It's one of the tremendous luxuries of being at Berkeley," Obermeyer said. "You can pursue these projects that just are a slow burn and then have -- hopefully -- a big return when they get over the finish line."
From Hidden Heart Signals to Lifesaving Treatments
The researchers have already begun exploring how the system might be used in actual healthcare settings.
Obermeyer is collaborating with medical systems in Sweden, Taiwan, and the United States to introduce the algorithm into hospital EKG databases. The goal is to examine existing heart scans for signs of elevated risk and identify patients who may benefit from additional monitoring.
Under the proposed approach, physicians would contact patients whose EKGs receive a high-risk assessment and offer them the opportunity to wear a patch that continuously records their heart's electrical activity.
These longer recordings could provide valuable clues about the biological processes responsible for the warning signals detected by the AI. Understanding those processes could help researchers explain why certain hearts are more vulnerable to suddenly developing fatal electrical disturbances.
For some patients, the additional information might ultimately support a recommendation to receive an implanted defibrillator, potentially preventing a sudden and otherwise unexpected death.
Obermeyer has also created a website where people interested in learning about their own risk can provide basic personal information and an email address. The research team can then contact them about EKG analysis when the technology becomes more widely available.
Could AI Reveal New Secrets About the Human Heart?
Beyond its potential to improve the prevention of sudden cardiac death, the discovery highlights how artificial intelligence could help scientists investigate medical mysteries that have resisted conventional approaches.
Rather than simply identifying patients who might need treatment, the algorithm has uncovered patterns in heart activity that researchers do not yet fully understand. Studying those signals could lead to new insights into the electrical disturbances responsible for sudden cardiac death and potentially reveal additional opportunities for prevention.
Obermeyer believes this ability to uncover previously unrecognized biological patterns could become one of AI's most important contributions to medicine, opening new directions for research while helping physicians make better decisions.
"There is also going to be a new way of doing science that comes out of these tools," Obermeyer said, "and it's fun to think about how that starts happening."

articles.title: General Motors planea usar 20% más robots en sus fábricas de Norteamérica para 2028
articles.text:
General Motors prevé aumentar 20% el uso de robots y otras formas de automatización en sus fábricas de Norteamérica hasta 2028, según dos personas con conocimiento del asunto citadas por la agencia Reuters. La automotriz busca contener el aumento de los costos laborales y los gastos de producir en territorio estadounidense.
La meta de 20% y la fabricación propia de robots no se habían divulgado antes, según Reuters. GM desarrolla sus equipos y los ensambla en su planta de Kokomo, Indiana. Su prioridad son los robots móviles autónomos, máquinas que trasladan piezas de un punto a otro dentro de las plantas sin conductor.
Las automotrices usan robots desde hace décadas para soldar paneles de carrocería o mover insumos entre estaciones. Ahora buscan sumar más robótica y más inteligencia artificial a la línea de producción para elevar la productividad, en un momento de costos más altos por las materias primas y por el traslado de las cadenas de suministro a Estados Unidos.
GM sigue comprando equipos de robótica a proveedores externos mientras desarrolla los propios. Según Reuters, la compañía declaró el año pasado que tenía unos 100 especialistas en robótica, ingeniería de IA y hardware dedicados a sistemas avanzados.
GM exige automatización a sus proveedores
Otras dos fuentes de la cadena de suministro dijeron a Reuters que GM pide a los fabricantes de autopartes que compiten por nuevos contratos que presenten planes para automatizar sus propias operaciones. La empresa califica esos planes con una tabla de puntajes y toma en cuenta el resultado al adjudicar los contratos.
GM no respondió de inmediato al pedido de comentarios de Reuters. Antes había afirmado que usa la automatización para mejorar la seguridad, la calidad y la eficiencia. “A medida que se intensifica la competencia global, seguimos poniendo estas tecnologías a trabajar de maneras que apoyan a nuestros equipos de manufactura”, señaló la empresa.
El sindicato United Auto Workers (UAW), que representa a unos 50.000 trabajadores de fábrica de GM, calificó la estrategia como una forma de recortar empleos. “Su idea de ser más eficientes es recortar a las mismas personas que crean su producto y sus ganancias”, dijo en un comunicado el vicepresidente del gremio, Ryan Hiestand.
“No necesitamos más robots para que GM haga otra recompra de acciones”, agregó Hiestand. En junio, el presidente del sindicato, Shawn Fain, había advertido en una convención que los frutos del trabajo se multiplicaron como nunca sin que los trabajadores los cosechen, y que si la IA se usa como cómplice de ese robo, “hay que detenerla”.
Costos laborales y presión política
Desde que el UAW logró ganancias récord en el contrato de 2023 con GM, Ford y Stellantis, las automotrices estadounidenses aumentaron la automatización para contener costos. GM calculó que ese contrato sumaría unos USD 575 por vehículo en costos laborales, y Ford estimó USD 900. Entonces, analistas ya preveían que las empresas recurrirían a más robots para compensarlo.
La política del presidente Donald Trump de traer trabajo industrial de vuelta al país también presiona los costos de producción. Las automotrices estadounidenses sostienen desde hace tiempo que sus costos laborales superan los de rivales extranjeros y los de competidores nuevos como Tesla, cuyas fábricas en Estados Unidos en su mayoría no tienen sindicato.
Laurie Harbour, socia de la firma de asesoría Wipfli especializada en el sector automotor, dijo a Reuters que el objetivo final es dedicar menos horas de trabajo a cada vehículo para ser más eficientes y rentables. Añadió que más automatización puede aliviar la escasez de mano de obra de las automotrices.
La automatización será probablemente un tema central en la próxima negociación del UAW con GM, Ford y Stellantis, cuyos contratos vencen en la primavera boreal de 2028, el mismo año fijado por GM para su meta de 20%.

articles.title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
articles.text:
In the one light-day that humanity’s most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.
Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a “commemorative phonograph record,” in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.
About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs’ overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.
“So much has been written about the contents of the record—the message in the bottle, so to speak—whereas I was more interested in the hardware, the bottle itself, because so very little is known about that,” Swanson, former chief historian for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and founding editor of Quest: The History of Spaceflight Quarterly, said in an interview.
Historian Glen Swanson (right) with his wife, anthropologist Deana Weibel (center), and Jon Lomberg, space artist, science journalist, and design director for the Voyager Golden Record.
Historian Glen Swanson (right) with his wife, anthropologist Deana Weibel (center), and Jon Lomberg, space artist, science journalist, and design director for the Voyager Golden Record.
Credit:
Glen Swanson via collectSPACE.com
With the 50th anniversaries looming for the launches of both Voyager probes, Swanson and Jon Lomberg, the design director of the Golden Record, recently set about writing Voyager’s Golden Record: An Enduring Reflection, which will be released by the University of Chicago Press in August 2027.
“There isn’t a whole lot of information, and some of the information is somewhat contradictory,” said Swanson of the existing resources and publications. “So it is kind of refreshing to look back and see what exactly went on.”
Meanwhile, the Voyagers continue to travel outward, still communicating with Earth. On November 18, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth—the distance a particle of light travels in 24 hours—giving Swanson an occasion to share details from his and Jon Lomberg’s pending book.
Under cover
Within the immense scale of the Universe, Voyager 2 is barely even a block from its home. Were an intelligent species to find it today—some 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) away from Earth—they might not need anything contained on the Golden Record to trace its origins back to our planet.
But that was never the intention of the Golden Record’s designers, who created the archive to last and be relevant for a much more distant encounter.
“They are pretty confident that it’s going to last a long, long, long time based on the data; the probabilities of the impacts from micrometeorites and things like that,” Swanson said.
Historian Glen Swanson rediscovered that the designers of the Voyager Golden Record repeated the operating instructions on the inside of its protective cover.
Historian Glen Swanson rediscovered that the designers of the Voyager Golden Record repeated the operating instructions on the inside of its protective cover.
Credit:
Glen Swanson via collectSPACE.com
When most people think of the Golden Record, says Swanson, what often comes to mind is not the disc itself, but its protective cover. In addition to being inscribed with the now-iconic Pulsar map of the location of our Sun as earlier flown on the Pioneer 10 and 11 probes, hieroglyphs lay out how to play the record and access the data (e.g., photos) also contained on the disc.
The cover also shields the record from possible damage, but nothing protects the protector.
“The designers recognized that the outside of the cover was going to wear down. It just would,” Swanson told collectSPACE. “Even small amounts of dust are eventually going to wear down the inscriptions to the point perhaps where they are not going to be readable.”
It is a catch-22: The instructions needed to be on the outside so whoever finds Voyager easily finds what to do. But if the hieroglyphs are damaged or are eroded away, the disc inside might forever go unplayed.
The solution may seem obvious, but it’s unclear whether the designers thought of it back then.
“It makes a whole lot of sense that they repeated the instructions on the inside of the cover, because when someone or something finds Voyager, they might only be able to make out a little bit on the outside,” said Swanson.
There were hints that this backup existed in photographs of the covers taken before the Voyager probes were launched, but they were either not clear enough or had other objects (e.g., a bag) in the way to make out what was there. It was not until Swanson found and referenced the original blueprints that he could confirm the instructions were on the inside, too.
The schematics for the Voyager Golden Record’s protective cover confirmed the “reduced size” instructions to be added to the interior side, just as Glen Swanson found.
Credit:
Glen Swanson/NASA/JPL
The schematics for the Voyager Golden Record’s protective cover confirmed the “reduced size” instructions to be added to the interior side, just as Glen Swanson found.
Credit:
Glen Swanson/NASA/JPL
There is another reason why the record’s designers may have felt they needed to repeat the instructions, according to Swanson.
“What’s the best way to convey the importance of those instructions? You repeat them,” he said. “You have them on the outside, and you have them on the inside.”
Limited edition
Initially, the Voyager Golden Record was a limited edition of just three—one to fly on each spacecraft and a flight backup.
“Later, meaning maybe a month or so after the launches, there’s correspondence indicating that NASA said to go ahead and make 10 extras,” said Swanson, noting that the count included the spare. “How they came up with that number, I am not 100 percent sure, other than maybe they were to make as many as they could based on the hardware and funding available.”
Over the years, various reports have either lowered the total number to as few as six or raised it as high as 14, for reasons unexplained. What is for certain—as Swanson also verified—is that the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Pasadena, California, retained and displays the flight spare.
In the process of his research, Swanson was also able to verify that original duplicates are held today at the United Nations in New York; the US Library of Congress, NASA Headquarters, and Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Washington, DC; the Johnson Space Center in Texas; the Kennedy Space Center in Florida; Langley Research Center in Virginia; Glenn Research Center in Ohio; and Goddard Space Flight Center in Maryland.
“Interestingly enough, NASA Headquarters was not given one originally, so how they obtained their copy is not certain,” said Swanson. “It may be that President Carter turned his copy over to NASA HQ since records indicate that he had one. Archivists at the Carter Presidential Library and Museum confirmed that they never received a Golden Record, so Carter most likely gave it back to NASA at some point.”
In 2024, SpaceX founder Elon Musk replied to a social media post, saying, “I have one,” without offering any other details. It is believed he was referring to a replica, not one of the NASA-produced duplicates.
This duplicate of the Voyager Golden Record was transferred to the National Air and Space Museum in 1978. (Smithsonian)
Credit:
Smithsonian
This duplicate of the Voyager Golden Record was transferred to the National Air and Space Museum in 1978. (Smithsonian)
Credit:
Smithsonian
Due to rights issues and material challenges, no complete versions have been offered for sale. The audio tracks have been collected on vinyl, CD, in playlists, and even a CD-ROM, which was produced for the visuals. Full- and smaller-size replicas of the cover have also been made.
Swanson and Lomberg are working on a full-size replica of the copper record to be released in conjunction with their book. But even that, as now planned, will not be playable.
“I think humanity is delighted that there were 10 spares made, because now we have those to study and look at, as the two that were flown are now well out of our reach,” said Swanson.
Robert Pearlman is a space historian, journalist and the founder and editor of collectSPACE, a daily news publication and online community focused on where space exploration intersects with pop culture. He is also a contributing writer for Space.com and co-author of "Space Stations: The Art, Science, and Reality of Working in Space” published by Smithsonian Books in 2018. He is on the leadership board for For All Moonkind and is a member of the American Astronautical Society's history committee.

articles.title: Canada’s economy could gain billions if more businesses pushed past $3 million in revenue: report | BetaKit
articles.text:
A new report by the Business Development Bank of Canada (BDC) has found $3 million in annual revenue to be a crucial “tipping point” for the productivity of small businesses and Canada’s economy.
The study used Statistics Canada data to analyze how growth affected productivity, investment, and profitability in 1.2 million businesses over two decades. It found that businesses making less than $3 million in annual revenue have a harder time improving their productivity, and that these businesses need to reach a certain size to be able to invest in tech and automation to benefit from economies of scale, BDC chief economist and vice president of research Pierre Cléroux told BetaKit in a Tuesday interview.
“We need to encourage businesses to get a bit bigger.”
“We need to encourage businesses to get a bit bigger, to get to this optimal size,” Cléroux said, adding that these businesses find it much easier to invest in themselves to improve productivity and profitability.
According to the report, on average, businesses with less than $3 million in revenue generate less than $10,000 in annual profit. Meanwhile, businesses in the next tier up, with revenues between $3 million and $10 million, are far more productive, earning more than $100,000 in annual profit.
Still, the vast majority (88 percent) of Canadian businesses generate less than $3 million annually, with only around two percent moving into a higher revenue tier each year. BDC says businesses within “striking distance” of $3 million in revenue should make the leap, because failure to do so increasingly puts a business at risk. To pull this off, Cléroux suggested finding operational efficiencies, adopting technologies, and potentially even merging with another business.
RELATED: BDC launches two entrepreneur-led AI programs to make small businesses, and itself, more productive
“When you make an acquisition, our research is showing that the new business, which is a bit bigger, is really benefiting from that,” Cléroux said.
Crossing the tipping point will benefit more than just the businesses themselves. The report states that increasing the number of businesses crossing the $3-million tipping point by just 0.5 percent, or around 6,500 businesses per year, could boost the Canadian economy by $15.5 billion.
“If we look at the macro level, productivity in Canada is low compared to the US or other developed economies,” Cléroux said. “So we need to increase our productivity; we also need to have bigger businesses.”
Feature image courtesy Unsplash. Photo by Annie Spratt.

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks to Buy AI Startup Applied Compute for $4.5 Billion
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW) said Wednesday it has agreed to acquire AI infrastructure company Applied Compute in an all-stock transaction valued at $4.5 billion, subject to adjustments.
Applied Compute’s platform lets companies adapt existing open-weight AI models to their own data and run them in production. Palo Alto Networks plans to offer the platform to its security customers, with deployment options in public clouds and sovereign environments. Applied Compute will continue serving its existing customers.
The acquisition gives Palo Alto Networks a role in how enterprises build and deploy AI, expanding its reach beyond the security tools those companies use to protect their deployments. Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora said he expects businesses to use a mix of open-weight and proprietary models. Palo Alto Networks evaluated Applied Compute as a prospective customer, and its Unit 42 team assessed the platform’s security, Arora said.
Applied Compute co-founder and CEO Yash Patil will become co-chief AI officer at Palo Alto Networks after the deal closes. The startup’s research team will also join the company and help train proprietary AI models for use across its products.
The deal is expected to close in its fiscal third quarter of 2027, pending regulatory clearance and other customary closing conditions.
In September, Palo Alto Networks acquired Console, an AI-native platform designed to help organizations build agentic workflows and automate operational tasks using natural language.
Separately on Wednesday, Palo Alto Networks reported that revenue for its fiscal first quarter ended October 31 rose 39% year over year to $3.44 billion. Next-generation security annual recurring revenue climbed 66% to $9.73 billion. GAAP net income increased to $482 million, or $0.57 per diluted share, from $334 million, or $0.47 per share, a year earlier.
The company also raised its full-year outlook and now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $14.52 billion to $14.57 billion, up 26% to 27% year over year.

articles.title: Spend management platform Payhawk announces $280M raise, 2B valuation | TechCrunch
articles.text:
U.K.-based fintech Payhawk announced a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted. The round values the company at $2 billion, bringing its total funding to more than $500 million to date.
Founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents. Speaking to FinTech magazine, Payhawk’s co-founder and CEO, Hristo Borisov, said the company saw “an incredible growth opportunity and room to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls.”
Payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and says it operates in 33 countries. Notably, the company said it still has 70% of the $100 million it raised in 2022, a round that valued the company at $1 billion. This fresh capital will support its global expansion. Other investors in the round include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED.

articles.title: Distributed inference turns stranded power into AI compute - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
From store outlets to methane leaks: AI’s hunt for power
AI factories are outgrowing traditional data centers as models grow and distributed inference moves from concept to deployment. The infrastructure behind those models now has to span racks, sites and even scattered pockets of power.
Dell Technologies Inc. is betting that the answer lies in building complete systems rather than components, from rack-scale management to fully liquid-cooled designs. The size of modern AI clusters dwarfs anything high-performance computing has handled before, according to Ihab Tarazi (pictured), senior vice president and chief technology officer of AI, compute and networking at Dell.
“The difference with AI is the scale is massive: tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands of GPUs that are all on a single fabric. It may be multiple clusters, but they end up being a single fabric at the end of the day,” he said.
Tarazi spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and host Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed Dell’s 100% liquid-cooled networking system, distributed inference and turning stranded energy into AI capacity. (* Disclosure below.)
Liquid cooling sets the stage for distributed inference
Dell’s latest move takes liquid cooling beyond the graphics processing unit. The company is shipping what it calls the first 100% liquid-cooled networking system, with switches, optics and cabling pretested in its factory and delivered as a single rack, Tarazi explained.
“The fact that it’s pretested as a single-rack system means [that] instead of having to assemble hundreds of pieces on-site and take maybe two weeks or three weeks to find the bugs, it all comes in, you install it [and] we turn it up in hours,” he said.
The networking launch follows Dell’s debut of liquid-cooled storage for AI racks. Compute, networking and storage can now operate within a common cooling and power architecture.
“Instead of building two data centers — one for GPU, one [for] network — being able to do one is a massive reduction in time and cost for us,” he said.
Software is the next lever for distributed inference. Customers want a single control plane that can work across different GPUs and CPUs and link as many as 1,000 small sites, each with some spare power, Tarazi noted. That approach turns stranded energy into AI capacity for companies that can’t quickly build a massive data center.
“You’ll be surprised what power availability means,” he said. “It doesn’t mean just that you have power in your store. It could also mean methane coming out — every source of power possible. People are going backwards to say, ‘How do I leverage that power for compute and enable inferencing in a distributed manner?'”
