articles.title: $3.26 million in SpaceX AI data center revenue will be pumped back into the City of Memphis — up to $25,000 on offer to low-income residents for repairs and home improvements
articles.text:
$3.26 million in SpaceX AI data center revenue will be pumped back into the City of Memphis — up to $25,000 on offer to low-income residents for repairs and home improvements
The city is making its first major investment through the Community Benefit Ordinance, using a portion of the tax generated by SpaceX AI's Colossus 1 facility for the benefit of residents.
The City of Memphis has announced that it will make its first major investment as part of its new Community Benefits Ordinance. The fund will use revenue generated by taxing SpaceX AI's Colossus 1 facility to fund various initiatives within the South Memphis neighborhoods around that data center. The fund will help with the costs associated with housing, neighborhood improvements, and services, with the first $2 million allocated for the Memphis HOPE Initiative — a new home repair assistance program that helps residents make vital repairs as well as improvements that will make their homes more accessible.
The HOPE Initiative will provide low- and moderate-income homeowners and even renters with up to $25,000 for qualifying repairs and improvements. Eligible improvements include structural repairs as well as plumbing, heating, and air conditioning repairs. Roof repairs and replacement, accessibility improvements, and some exterior improvements like painting, fencing, and landscaping are also eligible. Funds will be provided as a deferred, interest-free, forgivable loan with zero monthly payments. Any required lien will be recorded after repairs are completed and forgiven after three years.
SpaceX AI's Colossus 1 data center became fully operational in May 2025, packing 220,000 GPUs and 300 megawatts of compute capacity. A year later, in May 2026, it was announced that Anthropic had signed a lease that would see it take over the entire facility in an effort to ease usage bottlenecks across Claude's paid-for ecosystem. The company said that the additional compute afforded by Colossus 1 would enable higher Claude Code limits, the removal of throttling for Pro and Max customers, and increased API request limits for Claude Opus models. But none of that will matter to those benefiting from the Community Benefits Ordinance, of course.
The full breakdown of the $3,259,282 allocation includes:
- $2 million for home repair assistance
- $309,282 for community grants supporting public safety, youth, workforce development, and other services
- $250,000 for paid neighborhood cleanup and beautification jobs
- $250,000 for property board-ups and demolitions
- $150,000 for blight mitigation and remediation
- $125,000 for cooling and air quality equipment for residents
- $100,000 for environmental education
- $50,000 for grants to health care-focused organizations
- $25,000 for Memphis City Beautiful
Today's news comes hot on the heels of SpaceX AI CEO Elon Musk telling employees that the company will increase the power capacity of its data centers by 7x to 10 gigawatts by late 2027. The move would see those data centers rake in between $300 billion and $500 billion per year, according to Musk. Perhaps notably, the claim also comes as SpaceX's market capitalization dropped by nearly $570 billion in less than two months.

articles.title: Jogamos GTA 6! Veja nossas primeiras impressões do novo jogo da Rockstar
articles.text:
Depois de 13 anos de espera, finalmente chegou o momento de colocar as mãos em Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6). A convite da KaBuM!, o Olhar Digital participou do evento de lançamento do jogo na Galeria Magalu, onde tivemos a oportunidade de conhecer em primeira mão o novo título da Rockstar Games.
E, depois de jogar, uma coisa ficou clara: GTA 6 é tudo aquilo que prometia ser — e ainda mais.
Desde os primeiros minutos, o jogo impressiona pela qualidade visual, pela riqueza de detalhes e pela sensação de estar explorando um mundo que realmente existe. Leonida e Vice City não são apenas cenários bonitos: são ambientes que parecem reagir a cada movimento do jogador.
Mas o que mais surpreende não é apenas o salto gráfico em relação a GTA 5. É a maneira como todos esses elementos se combinam para criar uma experiência envolvente, que prende a atenção desde o início.
GTA 6 impressiona pelo realismo de Vice City
É difícil falar das primeiras impressões de GTA 6 sem começar pelos gráficos. A Rockstar Games conseguiu criar um mundo visualmente impressionante, com um nível de realismo que chama atenção em praticamente todos os momentos.
A ambientação de Leonida é um espetáculo à parte. Cada movimento, cada detalhe dos cenários e cada interação contribuem para a sensação de estar dentro daquele universo.
Vice City está linda. Mas, mais do que isso, a cidade parece viva.
Durante a experiência, foi possível perceber como o jogo oferece diferentes possibilidades de interação com o ambiente. Lugares, objetos, animais e personagens não jogáveis (NPCs) fazem parte de um mundo que convida o jogador a experimentar, observar e descobrir.
Essa liberdade é um dos maiores atrativos de GTA 6. Não se trata apenas de seguir missões ou percorrer o mapa, mas de sentir que sempre existe alguma coisa interessante acontecendo ao redor.
É o tipo de experiência que faz você querer parar a missão principal por alguns minutos simplesmente para explorar.
Lucia e Jason conquistam desde o começo
Outro grande destaque das primeiras horas é a dupla de protagonistas.
Lucia é extremamente cativante. Sua personalidade chama atenção desde o início e faz com que seja fácil se envolver com a história.
Jason, por sua vez, entrega aquilo que esperamos de um protagonista de GTA: um personagem com a postura e a personalidade de um criminoso que parece pertencer perfeitamente àquele universo.
Juntos, os dois formam um casal de vigaristas cuja dinâmica desperta curiosidade desde os primeiros acontecimentos da campanha.
A história consegue prender a atenção rapidamente, fazendo com que o jogador queira descobrir o que acontecerá com os protagonistas e quais serão as consequências de suas escolhas.
Mesmo em uma experiência inicial, já é possível perceber que a relação entre Lucia e Jason será um dos elementos mais interessantes da narrativa.
E esse talvez seja um dos maiores acertos do jogo: além de oferecer um mundo gigantesco para explorar, GTA 6 apresenta personagens pelos quais realmente queremos continuar jogando.
Jogabilidade mantém a essência de GTA 5, mas amplia as possibilidades
Quem está acostumado com GTA 5 provavelmente vai se sentir em casa ao começar GTA 6.
A dinâmica dos confrontos é bastante semelhante à do título anterior, assim como a condução dos veículos. Isso torna a adaptação relativamente natural para quem já conhece a franquia.
A Rockstar não parece ter buscado reinventar completamente essas mecânicas. Em vez disso, manteve uma base familiar e ampliou a experiência com novas possibilidades de interação. Os comandos são similares, e durante a primeira hora de jogo não foi encontrado nenhum bug.
E é justamente nesse aspecto que GTA 6 começa a mostrar sua evolução.
A quantidade de elementos com os quais podemos interagir chama atenção. O mundo não funciona apenas como pano de fundo para perseguições e tiroteios, mas como parte fundamental da jogabilidade.
A sensação é de que existe muito mais para descobrir do que seria possível observar em uma única sessão.
Afinal, GTA 6 vale toda a expectativa?
Depois de tantos anos de espera, trailers, especulações e expectativas, seria natural imaginar que GTA 6 teria dificuldade para corresponder a tudo o que foi construído ao redor de seu lançamento.
Mas nossas primeiras impressões foram extremamente positivas.
O jogo é visualmente deslumbrante, oferece um mundo aberto impressionante e apresenta protagonistas que conseguem despertar interesse desde os primeiros minutos.
A familiaridade dos confrontos e da direção de veículos não diminui a experiência. Pelo contrário, ajuda a manter a identidade da franquia enquanto os avanços de ambientação e interação mostram o quanto a Rockstar evoluiu.
Ainda é cedo para fazer uma avaliação definitiva da campanha, do desempenho ao longo de dezenas de horas ou de todos os sistemas disponíveis. Essas conclusões exigem uma experiência mais extensa.
Mas, pelo que jogamos durante o evento da KaBuM!, GTA 6 não apenas corresponde às expectativas: consegue superá-las.
Saí da Galeria Magalu com a sensação de que havia conhecido apenas uma pequena parte de tudo o que Leonida tem para oferecer — e com uma vontade enorme de voltar a jogar.
Se a proposta era fazer o público se apaixonar novamente pelo universo de Grand Theft Auto, a Rockstar começou muito bem.

articles.title: Nuevo hito para la Voyager 1, el primer objeto humano a un día luz de la Tierra
articles.text:
Casi 50 años después de su lanzamiento, la Voyager 1 continúa haciendo historia. La sonda espacial ha alcanzado un nuevo hito al convertirse en el primer objetivo construido por humanos en alcanzar una distancia de un día luz de la Tierra, ha confirmado la NASA.
Hoy, miércoles 18 de noviembre de 2026, la Voyager 1 logró este registro. El mismo se produjo a las 05:16, hora del Este de Estados Unidos; es decir, a las 11:16, hora peninsular española. Esto significa que el vehículo se encuentra a unos 26.000 millones de kilómetros de nuestro planeta.
La Voyager 1 ya era el objeto humano más alejado de la Tierra, pero con este nuevo récord agiganta todavía más su leyenda. Recordemos que la sonda se lanzó en 1977 y junto con Voyager 2, su hermana gemela, ha dedicado las últimas cinco décadas no solo a estudiar el sistema solar, sino también a navegar hacia los confines de lo desconocido. En 2012 ingresó en el espacio interestelar y actualmente sigue enviando datos que captura con los instrumentos que aún tiene encendidos.
¿Pero qué implica realmente que Voyager 1 esté a un día luz de distancia de la Tierra? El Laboratorio de Propulsión a Chorro de la NASA (JPL) ha publicado un breve vídeo explicándolo de modo sencillo. La agencia espacial estadounidense indica que una partícula de luz demora 24 horas en viajar unos 26.000 millones de kilómetros, la distancia a la que hoy se encuentra la Voyager 1.
Esto quiere decir que cualquier comando que se envíe desde la Tierra demora 24 horas en llegar a la Voyager 1. En tanto que las respuestas desde la sonda hacia nuestro planeta requieren exactamente la misma cantidad de tiempo para llegar a la NASA. De modo que cualquier comunicación de ida y vuelta con la nave hoy requiere de dos días completos.
La Voyager 1 ahora está a un día luz de la Tierra
El nuevo hito de la Voyager 1 es una prueba más (como si hiciera falta) de la inmensidad del espacio. La sonda ha requerido 49 años, 2 meses y 11 días para recorrer un día luz de distancia desde la Tierra. En el caso de la Voyager 2, cuyo lanzamiento se produjo unos días antes, no se espera que esté a un día luz de distancia de nuestro planeta hasta 2035.
La Voyager 1 continúa con su trayectoria hacia la estrella Gliese 445, que está a más de 17 años luz de distancia de la Tierra. Volando a una velocidad que supera los 61.000 kilómetros por hora, la sonda podría estar relativamente cerca de dicho cuerpo (a 1,6 años luz de distancia, aproximadamente) recién dentro de 40.000 años.
Pase lo que pase con el vehículo, la Voyager 1 ha superado con creces las expectativas de la NASA y toda la comunidad científica. En los últimos años, la agencia espacial estadounidense ha logrado mantenerla con vida a pesar de su longevidad y lejanía. La sonda ha experimentado varios problemas técnicos, incluyendo interrupciones de comunicación con la Tierra, pero hasta aquí siempre se ha logrado superarlos.
Tanto la Voyager 1 como la Voyager 2 viajan equipadas con los icónicos discos de oro que sirven como un mensaje de paz para cualquier posible civilización extraterrestre que los pueda encontrar.

articles.title: France Is Blaming Iran for the Fridge Cyberattack - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
France Is Blaming Iran for the Fridge Cyberattack
U.S. intelligence agencies have recently reached a “low confidence” assessment that Iran was responsible for the attacks in France, according to three U.S. officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive intelligence. A “low confidence” assessment generally means that there is some intelligence that points in a certain direction but is fragmented, and that the assessment could change as more information is collected.
The agencies’ judgment on the French incidents linked those attacks to Iran generally and not to a specific group such as the Revolutionary Guards, two of the officials said. They added that Iran was also seen as probably responsible for other similar attacks around Europe, but that those investigations were in their early stages.

articles.title: Youtube krempelt die View-Zählung um: Co-Views werden ab sofort mitgezählt
articles.text:
Youtube zählt ab jetzt Co-Views: So verändert sich die View-Zählung
Die Videoplattform Youtube hat ein großes Update für die View-Zählung in petto – schon wieder. Erst im Sommer wurde eine Metrikanpassung für die View-Zählung vorgestellt. Seit dem 24. August genügt auf Youtube schon der Start eines Videos, damit ein View gezählt wird. Jetzt kommt eine Neuerung für die Integration von Co-Views im öffentlichen View-Count hinzu.
Was Co-Views auf Youtube sind und wie die Plattform sie einordnet
In einem Video für den Creators Insider Channel erklärt Rene Ritchie von der Youtube-Liaison, was es mit den Co-Views auf sich hat. Dabei handelt es sich um einen geschätzten Wert für die Anzahl der Personen, die auf TV-Geräten zusammen Youtube-Inhalte schauen. Diesen Wert generiert Youtube nicht durch die Überwachung der User, betont Ritchie darauf, sondern auf Basis von Statistiken, demografischen Daten und Sehzeiten in Kombination mit Daten aus Panels. Er führt aus:
Youtube doesn’t use devices, cameras, microphones or anything like that. Co-views are estimated using a privacy safe statistical mode, developed by Google research scientists, based on factors like demographic patterns and viewing times, calibrated against ground-truth data sources like industry panels
Die errechneten Co-Views sollen künftig direkt in den öffentlichen View-Count einfließen. Sie werden bei allen Inhalten angezeigt, Shorts, Longform-Videos und Live Content. Historische View-Counts bleiben davon aber unberührt. Das gilt aber nur für die TV-Rezeption, Desktop und Mobile sind davon nicht betroffen. Hierfür kann Youtube keine Schätzwerte zur Co-Rezeption ermitteln, wenngleich sie ebenso bei diesen Geräten möglich ist. Da aber Youtube-User schon mehr als eine Milliarde Stunden Content auf Youtube pro Tag auf TV-Geräten anschauen, möchte die Plattform die Co-Views als Metrik mehr in den Fokus stellen. Bisher gab es nur eine Private Views (Co-Viewed)-Metrik im Youtube-Studio. Diese wird im Mai 2027 eingestellt.
Bei der Analyse von Co-Views wird Youtube als Zusatzmetrik eine Co-View Rate einführen. Diese offenbart, wie viele Views es ohne Co-View für Inhalte gab. In der Aufteilung nach Gerätetypen im Youtube-Studio können die Creator diese Rate mit den Views gegenchecken. Für Views via Mobile und Desktop wird die Co-View-Rate immer 1,0 sein, da dort keine Co-Views gemessen werden können.
Für die Creator dürfte zudem noch von besonderem Interesse sein, dass die Co-Views die Werbeeinkünfte und die Hürden für das YouTube-Partnerprogramm nicht beeinflussen. Einkünfte, Auszahlungen und die Qualifizierung für das Programm bleiben an qualifizierte Views und gesehene Stunden geknüpft.
And while co-views also don’t impact metrics like Thumbnail Impressions, Click Through Rate, and Average View Duration – Watch Time will be consistent with the updated public view counts to reflect the co-view audience watching together,
schließt Rene Ritchie. Du kannst dir seine Ausführungen im X‑Post im Wortlaut durchlesen.
Der Artikel stammt von Niklas Lewanczik aus der OnlineMarketing.de-Redaktion und wird im Rahmen einer Content-Kooperation auf t3n veröffentlicht.

articles.title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
articles.text:
The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
MIT Technology Review’s highly subjective take on the latest buzz about AI
Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack.
You go to the movies and see Sam Altman being played with nauseating intensity by Andrew Garfield, and go back home to find that Elon Musk has released a Grok-fied version of The Odyssey. You try to watch it, but it feels like a long, unskippable mobile ad. In a way, the whole world kind of feels that way now: Like a modern Odysseus, you are cursed to roam AI-infested waters, dueling with machine gods and monsters, trying to find your way back to somewhere that feels like home.

articles.title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
articles.text:
New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president of education, told the Times that, “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” and that schools that turn off Google’s AI features “will not have access to Search.”
The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
Google is trying to force Gemini on schools, and they’re not thrilled.
Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Google’s behavior “extortion.” Mamdani had recently announced a policy that barred 2-K-8 students from using AI in the classroom. In a statement to the Times, New York City schools chancellor Kamar H. Samuels said, “If Google doesn’t reconsider their position, we will explore other search options.” Chicago’s public schools have also reportedly told Google that if it can’t provide a version of Search without AI, “the district will look to other search solutions.”
In a statement to The Verge, Google spokesperson Laura Breen said, “We hear parents and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to shortcut learning, and we share the same goal: help students learn. To improve Search for the classroom, we’re starting to pilot Guided Learning capabilities in Search this month to walk students step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers. Next year, we’re also updating our approach to controls for schools to address feedback we’ve heard from educators, so Gemini app, Gemini Notebook and Search will be off by default until schools decide which services to enable. We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers.”
Educators are wary of AI’s effect on students’ critical thinking skills, and some studies have shown that students who use AI generally perform worse on tests. There are also concerns about the mental health effects on children who develop relationships with chatbots at a young age. But Google is deeply embedded in classrooms across the US, which rely on Google Classroom, Chromebooks, and other services, and going fully Google-free might prove difficult.

articles.title: Budget-friendly gifts for gamers — keyboards, mice, and more under $80
articles.text:
Budget-friendly gifts for gamers — keyboards, mice, headsets, and more under $80
The best budget-friendly gifts for gamers.
The gamers in your life might be hoping for a $7,000 graphics card (I know I am), but that doesn't mean they won't still appreciate some solid, significantly cheaper gaming peripherals. While $80 doesn't go quite as far as it used to, there are still plenty of awesome accessories that any gamer would be thrilled to receive — including headsets, mice, keyboards, microphones, mouse pads, and even an Elgato Stream Deck.
Budget-friendly doesn't mean compromising on quality or convenience, either. While you won't be able to find all the bells and whistles at the sub-$80 level, there are both wired and wireless headsets, mice, and keyboards at this price point, including some last-generation flagship products. Razer's DeathAdder V3 Pro is currently on sale for $64.99, and remains one of the best-feeling mice we've ever tested — and its shape was so good that Razer kept it, exactly, in the newer DeathAdder V4 Pro. HyperX's Cloud III gaming headset is basically identical to our favorite Cloud III S headset — the only real difference is that the Cloud III is wired, while the Cloud III S is wireless.
The HyperX Cloud III is a wired gaming headset with a detachable microphone. It features 53mm drivers and virtual surround sound support.
This wireless lightweight over-ear headset weighs just 212g and is very comfortable. It features very good embedded beamforming mics and gets up to 24 hours of battery life on a single charge.
The G203 is now on sale for under $19 and is a great option for a budget mouse. It has six programmable buttons, and an 8K DPI optical sensor. There's also a RGB strip that wraps around the backside and shows off the Logitech "G" for a bit of bling.
Sporting a 12K sensor, a 99g weight, and a 250-hour battery rating on a single AA battery, Logitech's G503 wireless isn't an ultra-light 8K polling elite gaming mouse. But it solid experience while gaming and working. Unless you're playing competitive titles on an elite level, it just might be all the gaming mouse you really need.
Save an incredible 47% and get the Logitech G309 Lightspeed on sale for only $42.50. The G309 connects via Bluetooth or Wireless, uses a Hero 25K DPI sensor, six programmable buttons, and Lightforce mechanical switches.
The DeathAdder V3 Pro is a lightweight wireless gaming mouse with a fantastic shape, Razer's Focus Pro 30K optical sensor, and up to 90 hours of battery life. It weighs just 63g and is perfect for a range of gamers.
This Razer wireless gaming mouse features the company's Focus Pro 30K DPI optical sensor. It has a battery life of 280 hours using a single AA battery.
A wired membrane keyboard that punches above its weight: features SteelSeries' Whisper-Quiet membrane switches, 8 zones of RGB lighting, and a compact TKL form factor. It's also water- and dust-resistant.
Hexgears Immersion A3 combines the small footprint of a TKL keyboard with low-profile keycaps and switches, and multi-connectivity with 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, plus a wired connection. There's even a small TFT screen to monitor battery life or host a personalized GIF.
The Logitech G413 TKL SE Mechanical Gaming Keyboard is a wired device with backlit keys. As the name suggests, it has a tenkeyless form factor so there is no numeric pad. The keys are mechanical with tactile switches.
This budget-friendly gaming mic features a unique ball shape and sounds fantastic out of the box. It comes with a sturdy desktop stand and features two mounting points so you can mount it at an angle, as well as a cardioid polar pattern and fun RGB lighting.
A USB condenser mic with a cardioid polar pattern, excellent sound out of the box, and a built-in desktop stand with a mounting point on the bottom. It also has a large tap-to-mute button on the top, and a red indicator light so you know when the mic is recording.
These 2.0 desktop speakers have a unique, round pebble shape with angled drivers so the sound hits your ears just right. They feature both wired and Bluetooth connections, have impressive bass for their size, and they've even got customizable RGB lighting around the base.
The Stream Deck Mini features six buttons but is otherwise compatible with the full suite of Stream Deck tools from Elgato.
SteelSeries' classic QcK gaming mouse pad is fairly basic — featuring a micro-woven cloth surface and a nonslip rubber backing, and measuring 12.6 x 10.8 inches (320 x 270mm) and just 2mm thick — but it's a solid option if you're looking for a no-frills mouse pad to up your mouse accuracy.
This XL extended mouse pad has a cloth surface that feels great — almost like a cooling pad. It features a non-slip rubber backing and a gunmetal gray pattern that may not be for everyone.
SteelSeries' performance-specific mouse pads are designed for specific scenarios — the balance mouse pad has a soft cloth surface designed to give you a mix of speed and precision.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar at its best and most frustrating
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI feels both refreshingly new and stuck in the past.
On the one hand, Rockstar’s long-running open-world crime franchise has finally grown up thanks to a more mature and emotionally-charged narrative. But on the other hand, some dated mechanics and mission design make the experience drag in places. Still, it’s a remarkable accomplishment that’s greater than the sum of its parts — the sort that certainly none but Rockstar could make.
Above all else, GTA VI succeeds on the strength of its leads. It’s a sweeping 60-hour Bonnie & Clyde-style epic that focuses on veteran-turned-drug runner Jason Duval and gig worker and recent inmate Lucia Caminos. Notably, the latter is the series’ first non-optional female protagonist, and she is every bit the star as Jason. In fact, she’s easily the more compelling of the two.
Where Jason can sometimes feel overly stoic and passive, Lucia is vivacious, determined and thoughtful. An early mission, which lets you see what led to her incarceration, depicts her as a sympathetically desperate lead who you want to root for even as she continues to make questionable life choices. All the while, her actress, who I wasn’t permitted to reveal per (excessive) embargo restrictions even though she was just nominated for a Game Award, delivers a wonderfully charismatic and effortlessly naturalistic performance.
It’s through Jason and Lucia that Rockstar’s noted Red Dead Redemption II inspirations are most pronounced, with GTA VI‘s dense five-chapter structure really allowing you to fully live with the duo. In between their criminal exploits in the main missions, you’ll be able to take on pretty much every activity in the sprawling Florida-inspired state of Leonida with both characters. This includes everything from intense bank robberies (more on those later) to minigames like mini golf and billiards and even simply sitting on the couch and chatting.
As I guide Jason and Lucia through their daily routines, they truly feel like living, breathing people. The way that they lean in for a passionate kiss or playful love tap. The way that they work out together, cheering each other on as they power through gruelling reps, before sharing two protein shakes for recovery. The way that watching TV or taking a shower can sometimes spontaneously turn into lovemaking.
The GTA games have always been about satirical deconstructions of the so-called “American Dream,” but getting to inhabit Jason and Lucia so intimately during their everyday lives makes those themes more meaningful than ever. It’s so effective, in fact, that I sometimes found that the main story was getting in the way of that lovely dynamic. For one, the supporting cast of characters is largely disposable, the sorts of thinly written caricatures you encountered in previous games. Take Jason’s old friend Dre’Quan; I spent so many missions helping him with his nightclub business, yet there’s nothing more to him or their relationship. Similarly, Jason’s boss, Brian, is just a generic drug runner whose only memorable quality is that there’s a great character actor playing him.
GTA VI can get so caught up in some of these subplots that it occasionally loses sight of the main driving force behind the narrative. At a certain point, the story can feel meandering, taking numerous detours from Jason and Lucia’s end goal — which I’m also not allowed to reveal — in favour of forgettable side characters. This can feel even more like a slog during extensive walk-and-talk sequences where your character simply moves forward at an incredibly glacial pace while someone else is chatting with them. The worst example of this, a mission that is structurally similar to several others, consisted largely of me escorting a whiny rich guy around a packed nightclub as Jason. Outside of one series of shootouts at the end, this was it — walking back and forth at a snail’s pace. “Cinematic,” sure, but not exactly engaging.
This relative lack of interactivity also pops up in some of the bigger setpieces. During one bank heist mission, moments of gunplay would be interspersed with quick cutscenes of characters moving locations or police entering the building. And in another infiltration mission, I watched a cutscene in which characters prepared a zipline before I was prompted to hold down on the stick to rappel down, only for a second cutscene to play immediately after. These constant cinematics are frustrating; yes, the game is undeniably stunning to behold, but I would like to actually play some more of these moments myself. If nothing else, the campaign does come together rather beautifully in its final stretch, which is refreshingly tighter and more stirring. I just wish the lead-up to get there felt better paced.
But of course, many people likely won’t even “roll credits” on GTA VI, and if they do, it will be over a much more stretched-out period than I had for this review. Indeed, this being an open-world game means that scores of players will sink countless hours into exploring Leonida without touching much, if any, of the story, and thankfully, that experience is a resounding success. It’s here that you get glorious, unfettered freedom, a welcome reprieve from the sometimes painfully on-rails moment-to-moment gameplay of the campaign.
From the lively, bustling streets of the Miami-esque Vice City to the sweltering flooded grasslands of the Everglades-inspired Grassrivers, GTA VI features easily one of the densest and most exquisitely detailed open worlds of all time. (Even if, rather glaringly, the game feels bizarrely out of time in how it completely refuses to even touch on the modern Trumpian climate of the U.S. in any real way outside of some cartoonish NPCs who will yell the kind of hateful language you’d hear from your average Fox News viewer.)
If anything, GTA VI really comes to life through its economy system. For various main and side missions, you’ll sometimes need a certain amount of money to progress, but how you obtain that is entirely up to you. Do you want to sneak into a trailer park and snatch some drugs from a local dealer for quick, low-risk cash? If you’re feeling a need for speed, you could always jack a high-value car and return it to a wanted buyer. Or maybe you want to do something safer and more law-abiding, like helping a farmer with his crop by flying a miniplane to hose down his fields.
But my favourite activities, without question, are heists. You start off small, only being able to rob convenience stores, pawn shops and similar small businesses. But over time, you’ll gain new equipment like sticky bombs for safes and special lights to counter marked bills that allow you to tackle bigger hits like banks. Here, the Jason and Lucia dynamic truly sings, with one of them handling crowd control while the other tries to grab as much cash as possible.
This is also where the laborious Red Dead Redemption 2-style animations actually enhance the experience, creating a rich sense of tension as your character slowly loads stacks of cash one-by-one into a duffel bag as your partner anxiously calls on you to hurry up because the police are on their way to catch you. It creates an electrifying risk-reward element, challenging you to weigh when enough is enough — whether you sneak out earlier with a smaller haul for a potentially clean getaway or dare to take more and end up facing the cops guns a-blazing.
These heists lead to some truly dynamic sequences that make full use of the meticulously crafted open-world. In fact, one of my favourite GTA VI memories so far stems from what I thought would be a simple bank robbery in Vice City. Strapped for cash, I risked having Lucia stay longer in the vault to nab some extra dough, much to Jason’s chagrin. After I finally loaded all of the bags and handed one to Jason to better manage the load, we rushed outside to our getaway vehicle just as police arrived and started shooting at us. But because I waited too long, the cops had set up roadblocks that funnelled us to a pier area, forcing us to abandon our ride and hide in a mini yacht.
Unfortunately, it moved slower than molasses, so the Coast Guard quickly discovered us, leaving us to mow down a nearby police cruiser and steal that. To escape the large police search radius, I frantically steered us to the next landmass, which I soon realized was a small rich person’s island completely disconnected from land. Amid police radio chatter saying they tracked the stolen vehicle to this island, we snuck around the guards and found a ferry, ultimately taking us to the mainland where I was able to use my phone to hail a ride to a contact where I could fence the stolen cash for a huge profit. Naturally, we ended the day with a well-earned night of R&R at the crib. All in all, it was an absolutely thrilling experience, and one that came organically from me reacting on the fly to the game’s intricate open-world design and wanted systems.
Those highs are ultimately what define my 80-plus hours with GTA VI. The larger story could be uneven, but it’s that relationship between Jason and Lucia that I came to really love. From the quiet moments of them going about their days to their pulse-pounding, action-packed criminal escapades, I couldn’t get enough of seeing these two together. And with Leonida itself being such a phenomenal setting, I can’t wait to keep going back for many more years to come.
GTA VI launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19.

articles.text:

                                                                Simulation of Plasma Chambers for Predictive Simulation of Semiconductor Manu...                                                    
Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Linking plasma chamber simulation with feature-scale process modeling to predict etch profiles, evaluate wafer uniformity, and optimize plasma etching processes.
								November 19th, 2026 - 
								By: Silvaco
								
							
Plasma etching and deposition processes increasingly determine the manufacturability of advanced semiconductor devices, where smaller features, more complex geometries, stricter wafer-uniformity requirements, and new chemistries demand predictive control of ion fluxes at the wafer surface. Kinetic plasma simulation provides a physics-based route to this control by resolving sheath dynamics, ion-neutral transport, and ion angular and energy distributions that cannot be captured reliably with bulk fluid approximations alone. VSim Plasma applies Particle-in-Cell modeling with Monte Carlo collisions to compute self-consistent electromagnetic fields, charged-particle motion, collisions, and current deposition. Validation against inductively coupled plasma measurements shows strong agreement for electron temperature and plasma potential, reasonable density agreement, and consistent electron energy probability function behavior. Coupling plasma-derived ion angular and energy distributions into Victory Process enables feature-scale etch simulation, linking chamber conditions and waveform design to process variability and profile evolution.

articles.title: La tele QD-Mini LED de Xiaomi se adelanta al Black Friday con un nuevo precio mínimo histórico

El Black Friday, tanto el Viernes Negro como las semanas previas, es ideal para renovar el televisor dado el gran número de ofertas que solemos encontrar. Este año no iba a ser diferente y ya estamos viendo precios tan atractivos como el que tiene el Xiaomi TV FX Mini LED, que ahora mismo se encuentra en Amazon por 399 euros.
Xiaomi TV FX Mini LED (55 pulgadas)

articles.title: Weitreichende Systemausfälle: Warum KI nur indirekt das Problem sein könnte
articles.text:
Weitreichende Systemausfälle: Warum KI nur indirekt das Problem sein könnte
In den vergangenen Tagen legte eine Reihe schwerer Ausfälle mehrere kritische Systeme in den USA lahm. Die Auswirkungen gingen aber weit über die Vereinigten Staaten hinaus. Teilweise waren Nutzer:innen weltweit betroffen. Laut einem Bericht der Washington Sun, der sich auf drei anonyme Quellen beruft, wurden Abgeordnete des US-Kongresses inzwischen über die Gründe informiert. Demnach seien die Ausfälle darauf zurückzuführen, dass mithilfe von KI entdeckte Schwachstellen geschlossen werden sollten.
Nutzer:innen weltweit von Ausfall betroffen
Ein Beispiel ist die Störung von Outlook. Laut Microsoft wurde diese aus einem Zusammenspiel mehrerer Faktoren ausgelöst. Am Abend des 12. Novembers hätten auf dem Höhepunkt der Störung mehr als 80 Prozent der zuständigen Rechner nicht mehr reagiert. Grund war eine im Juli aufgespielte Software-Änderung an einer zentralen digitalen Eingangstür für den Datenverkehr von Microsoft 365, die mehr als drei Monate unauffällig lief. Die Tests hätten den Fehler nicht angezeigt, da sie vorwiegend ältere Technik nutzten. Er trat aber vor allem auf neueren Servern auf.
Zwei zusätzliche Belastungen ließen den Fehler am vergangenen Donnerstag zur US-Hauptnutzungszeit ausbrechen. Einerseits hatte Microsoft kurz zuvor Teams planmäßig auf dieselbe Hauptinfrastruktur umgeschaltet, was den Datenverkehr erhöhte. Andererseits fielen wegen eines anderen Problems knapp 14 Prozent der Server-Kapazitäten vorübergehend aus. Als die ersten Server unter der Last ausfielen, wurden Anfragen automatisch auf die verbliebenen Rechner umgeleitet. Das löste denselben Fehler auch dort aus. Dieser Dominoeffekt erfasste innerhalb von unter zwei Stunden fast das gesamte System.
KI zwingt veraltete Systeme in die Knie
Microsoft war nicht das einzige Unternehmen mit einem solchen Ausfall. Auch Wells Fargo, die Bank of America und der gesamte US-Flugverkehr waren betroffen. Die Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) verhängte am Freitagabend ein landesweites Startverbot. Grund dafür war eine Störung der Radar- und Telekommunikation der Flugsicherung. Laut dem Wall Street Journal fielen mehr als 20.000 Flüge aus. Markwayne Mullin, Minister für Innere Sicherheit, erklärte am Dienstag gegenüber CNBC, er sei zu 98 Prozent überzeugt, dass hinter den Störungen keine Cyberangriffe steckten.
Öffentlich wollten die betroffenen Unternehmen und Behörden die KI-bezogene Software-Problematik aber nicht als Ursache bestätigen. Das gilt unter anderem für die FAA. Auch Microsoft führte die Störung bei Outlook offiziell auf einen technischen Defekt zurück. Die NSA, die ebenfalls betroffen war, räumte am Dienstag ein, dass es in einigen ihrer Netzwerke zu einer Beeinträchtigung infolge geplanter Wartungsarbeiten gekommen sei, wie Politico berichtete. In der öffentlichen Erklärung der Behörde wurden KI-generierte Patches ebenfalls nicht als Ursache genannt.
Weitere Ausfälle sind wahrscheinlich
Laut Washington Sun installieren Unternehmen, Behörden und Finanzinstitute eilig Software-Patches, nachdem KI-Modelle potenziell schwerwiegende Schwachstellen in ihren Systemen aufgedeckt haben. Dies habe einige Systeme überlastet und Ausfälle ausgelöst. „Diese Modelle identifizieren massive Schwachstellen, und das erhöht die Dringlichkeit, sofort Patches zu installieren“, erklärte ein über die Angelegenheit informierter Kongressbeamter gegenüber der Washington Sun. „Sie versuchen, eine Vielzahl von Patches auf einmal durchzusetzen – mehr, als das System bewältigen kann.“
Der Einsatz von KI zur Aufdeckung von Schwachstellen stellt Unternehmen und Behörden vor eine neue Herausforderung. Die Verantwortlichen müssen diese schnell beheben – zumal Angreifer:innen möglicherweise ähnlich leistungsfähige KI nutzen. Auch Mullin vermutet, dass neue Technologien in veralteten Computersystemen unerwartete Probleme verursachen könnten. „Sie setzen neue Technologien auf wirklich alte Computersysteme ein, und das scheint das System einfach zu überfordern“, sagte er gegenüber CNBC. „Wir werden noch mehr davon sehen, wenn neue Technologien eingeführt werden.“
))))) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Botswanan startup SocialLight brings local depth to Southern African media monitoring - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Botswana-based startup SocialLight is helping organisations keep track of what is being said about them across Southern Africa, with a focus on the print and radio coverage that international monitoring platforms tend to miss.
Founded in 2014 by Tony Mautsu, SocialLight tracks coverage of organisations, their competitors and their industries across print, radio, TV, online news and social media, turning it into alerts, reports and analysis for decision-makers. Its platform monitors more than 1,300 print publications and over 158 broadcast stations across the region, alongside online and social channels.
“Clients choose the keywords that matter to them, such as their brand, executives, competitors or regulatory issues. Every morning they receive alerts and regular reports showing where they were mentioned, what the tone was, and what it means for them,” Mautsu told Disrupt Africa.
“We have integrated AI into the platform so we can process large volumes of coverage quickly. Our in-market analysts then add the local context that software alone misses. The simplest way to put it – you find out first, while it is still a decision and not a crisis.”
The business has unusual origins. In 2012 and 2013, Mautsu volunteered at the Diacore marathon in Gaborone.
“My actual job was managing the toilets and the environment. I saw an opportunity to add more value and prove my worth, so I offered to run the event’s social media,” he said. “That experience became SocialLight, which I registered in 2014.”
The company started out as a social media management agency, and its appetite for bringing new technology into the local market took it into livestreaming and even holograms. The turning point came in 2018, when Mautsu took his first flight to a conference in South Africa.
“Honestly, I was scared of South Africa at the time. At that conference I was introduced to media monitoring. I immediately saw how much it was needed back home, so I built partnerships to bring it into the Botswana market,” he said.
Media monitoring has since become SocialLight’s core business. The startup went through the Botswana Innovation Hub’s First Steps Venture programme, and Mautsu was named on the Forbes 30 Under 30 Africa list in 2020. This year, he was recognised among the Top 10 Men in PR in Botswana. SocialLight saw a gap left by the international providers that dominated the market.
“Most media monitoring providers serving our market were international, and they did not fully understand the landscape. They assumed everyone was online. In Botswana and much of the region that is not true,” Mautsu said. “Power cuts, high data costs and patchy connectivity mean traditional media is still dominant.”
The team tested that belief on the ground, spending time at taxi ranks and other public spots to watch how people consumed news.
“I once took a bus from Gaborone to Lusaka, and for most of that journey people were not on their phones. They were listening to the radio and reading newspapers,” he said. “If you only monitor online and social media in this region, you miss a huge part of the conversation that shapes reputations.”
Mautsu said SocialLight’s edge over international platforms is the depth of its local coverage, especially print and radio, combined with in-market analysts who understand the languages, the politics and the context. “We are globally African and locally unmatched,” he said.
B2B uptake in Botswana has been strong, with SocialLight working with major brands in mining and banking, as well as regulators. It has also served multinational brands monitoring their presence in the region.
“These are sectors where reputation and early warning are critical,” Mautsu said.
The startup is now opening up its platform so organisations can sign up and use it online, with prospective clients able to request a free media assessment and a 14-day trial. It is also building strategic partnerships with PR agencies and other monitoring companies across SADC, some of which use SocialLight’s coverage to strengthen their own offerings.
SocialLight monitors media across most of SADC and currently has clients in Botswana, South Africa and Zambia. It plans to grow in Lesotho, Eswatini, Namibia and Malawi through strategic partners, and to enter Kenya and Nigeria within the next year, also via partnerships.
“Our model is to partner with established local agencies rather than build offices everywhere. They bring the relationships, and we bring the coverage and the technology,” Mautsu said.
The company makes most of its money from subscription retainers for media monitoring, priced mainly on the number of keywords a client tracks and the media types they need, with broadcast monitoring offered as an additional service. It also earns from custom reports and analysis, revenue-share arrangements with partner agencies that resell its platform, and its social media management services. It has been bootstrapped from day one.
“The business has funded its own growth since 2014, through retainer clients in banking, mining and the regulatory space, without outside investment,” Mautsu said. “I believe in starting where you are with what you have, and that is what we did.”
He said the biggest challenge has been finding the right in-country partners.
“They need to share our standards and see media monitoring as a long-term business, not a side offering. Finding that partner in each country takes time, and we have learned to be patient rather than rush into a market with the wrong one,” he said.
The cost of running the platform is another hurdle, with monitoring across multiple countries requiring constant spending on servers, data processing, digitising traditional media and AI tools.
“As a bootstrapped company, we carry all of that ourselves. That forces discipline, and it is why we have built much of our technology in-house rather than relying on expensive third-party tools,” Mautsu said. “Access to capital for SMEs in Botswana is difficult, so every stage of growth has had to pay for itself.”

articles.title: Exclusive: Wherobots AI agents automate complex spatial data engineering - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Wherobots AI agents automate complex spatial data engineering
Cloud-native spatial analytics and artificial intelligence startup Wherobots Inc. today introduced an artificial intelligence agent that enables users to build and deploy spatial data pipelines using natural-language instructions, reducing the need for specialized programming expertise.
Called Waldo, the agent can discover data sources, generate queries, perform analysis, visualize results and schedule recurring operations. It’s designed for applications involving location-based information such as satellite imagery, road networks, GPS tracking data and geographic features.
Spatial data presents unusual processing challenges because it combines multiple data types, including geographic coordinates, imagery and geometric shapes. Analyzing this information at scale often requires specialized tools and scarce technical expertise.
A recent survey by Global Marketing Insights Inc. concluded that the global geospatial workforce is 10 to 15 years behind in building the skill levels employers need.
Wherobots, which was founded in 2022 by the creators of the open-source Apache Sedona spatial analytics engine, said Waldo can compress development projects that traditionally take weeks into days.
“Waldo is our new agentic interface,” said Damian Wylie, Wherobots’ head of product. Unlike general-purpose AI coding assistants, he said, Waldo can invoke specialized computational engines that can process enormous geographic datasets.
“We’re not deploying some net-new [large language model] under the hood,” Wylie said. “We’re connecting existing LLMs to our product and also giving it the context it needs to speed up that spatial data workflow.”
The agent orchestrates several components of Wherobots’ platform. Its Havasu spatial data and knowledge catalog discovers and prepares public geographic datasets alongside customers’ private information. RasterFlow, Wherobots’ serverless Earth intelligence and inference engine, processes satellite and aerial imagery using computer vision models to identify features such as buildings, roads and land-use changes.
WherobotsDB executes the resulting analysis using more than 300 spatial functions, while Wherobots Maps visualizes the results. Completed pipelines can be scheduled to refresh automatically as new data arrives.
The distributed processing platform uses existing cloud storage and enterprise data catalogs, including Amazon Web Services Inc.’s Glue and Databricks Unity Catalog, eliminating the need for customers to migrate their data, Wylie said.
In a demonstration, he showed how Waldo could identify the drainage area surrounding Montana’s West Boulder River using geographic and elevation data. The agent located relevant datasets, constructed a geographic representation of the watershed and displayed the results on a map.
The resulting geometry could support subsequent analysis of snowfall, water runoff or changing environmental conditions, Wylie said. Waldo can also process satellite imagery using specialized machine learning models, including Meta Platforms Inc.’s Segment Anything Model 3.
Potential commercial applications include identifying delivery vehicles that deviate from planned routes, assessing weather-related transportation disruptions and analyzing advertising impressions based on billboard locations and mobility patterns.
Wherobots said customer Action Engine Inc. is using the technology to build recurring fleet analytics pipelines and reports that it can deliver new spatial analyses two to three times faster that was possible with manual processes. Another customer used the platform’s distributed computing architecture to reduce a large-scale data-joining operation from approximately a week to less than an hour, said Benjamin Pruden, Wherobots’ go-to-market executive.
Waldo isn’t intended to eliminate human oversight, executives said. Users can inspect generated queries, review geographic visualizations and create Jupyter notebooks to examine individual processing steps. Wylie acknowledged that the technology can’t guarantee accurate results from every prompt.
“That’s an area we’ll invest,” Wylie said. “We’re not at the stage where we’re going to say every prompt is the best quality you’ll ever get.”
Waldo is available in public preview, with agent tokens currently included at no additional charge in Wherobots Professional Edition. Customers pay primarily for the computational resources they consume, with controls to select processing capacity and monitor costs.

articles.title: Mira el genial tráiler final de 'Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth', la secuela de 'Érase una vez en Hollywood' con Brad Pitt
articles.text:
La secuela de Érase una vez en Hollywood, titulada Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth, está a punto de estrenarse y acaba de lanzar su esperado tráiler final. La película volverá a contar con Brad Pitt como el intrépido protagonista. Un papel que, recordemos, le valió el Oscar en la cinta de Quentin Tarantino. Esta vez, el que no regresa es el propio director, que cede el testigo a nada menos que a David Fincher.
Tal y como vemos en el avance, esto no es más que otro verano en Hollywood. Estamos en 1977, ocho años después de que Cliff Booth se cruzara con la familia Manson en el Hollywood de 1969 de Érase una vez en Hollywood. Ahora, en el tráiler de Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth, el cuento de hadas ha terminado. Los Ángeles ya no necesita a un doble de acción que se encargue de los hippies como antes.
Pero Hollywood siempre tendrá problemas, y algunos solo puede resolverlos alguien con las habilidades únicas (y, en ocasiones, al margen de la ley) de Cliff. Cuando no se gana la vida como camarero o proyeccionista, Cliff Booth es todo un solucionador de problemas: se ocupa de los conflictos de los peces gordos de Hollywood. Y, a veces, también de los que no lo son tanto.
Mira el tráiler de Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth
David Fincher dirige Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth pero, eso sí, lo hace a partir de un guion del propio Quentin Tarantino. Tampoco regresan Leonardo DiCaprio ni Margot Robbie, por lo que el filme será más bien un spin-off centrado exclusivamente en la vida del personaje de Brad Pitt ocho años después.
El reparto lo componen, además del propio Pitt, nombres de la talla de Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, Karren Karagulian. La película se estrenará en exclusiva durante dos semanas en salas IMAX el 25 de noviembre de 2026, antes de llegar a Netflix el 23 de diciembre de 2026.

articles.title: Democrats skip a vote on adding Brendan Carr’s adviser to the FCC
articles.text:
Senate commerce committee Chair Ted Cruz (R-TX) began a meeting Wednesday meant to confirm President Donald Trump’s nominee to the Federal Communications Commission with a lopsided dais. To his right sat all 14 Republican members of the panel, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD). To his left were about a dozen empty chairs — every Democratic member of the panel was absent.
Democrats skip a vote on adding Brendan Carr’s adviser to the FCC
Trump is stacking the FCC with Republicans, even as the Democrats boycott.
Cruz said he’d learned the night before that Democrats intended to boycott the vote, though Democrats say they’d repeatedly raised their concerns about advancing a Republican FCC nominee without a Democratic one. “The administration has shown it’s willing to move Democrats,” Cruz said, pointing to Senate votes scheduled on bipartisan pairs of nominations to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission. And even though the Supreme Court confirmed his power to do so, Cruz said, Trump has not moved to fire any Democrats from the FCC, as he did at the Federal Trade Commission. “This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party,” Cruz said.
“This is an ordinary nomination to fill a vacancy previously held by someone in the same party”
But in statements and comments to reporters outside the committee room, Democrats said that the process has been far from normal. Senate committees often vote on nominations to historically independent agencies in bipartisan pairs. Confirming Danielle Thumann Severs, senior counsel to FCC Chair Brendan Carr, to become a commissioner at the agency would put the FCC at four total members — three Republicans and one Democrat, Anna Gomez. Gomez’s term has technically expired, though she can remain on the commission through next year unless she’s replaced. But Democrats fear that by confirming a third Republican to the FCC, Trump might finally fire Gomez, because he’d no longer need her present for a quorum to vote on key actions.
Democrats asked for Thumann’s confirmation vote to be withheld until her nomination could be paired with a Democratic nomination. One way to do that would be to renominate Gomez. But so far, the president has not offered any Democratic nominees for the commission. Democrats said they made their concerns clear to Cruz, and added, “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In addition to the procedural concerns, Democrats worry about Thumann’s work as an adviser to Carr, and whether she was truthful about the matters she worked on. In a letter asking Cruz to delay her confirmation vote, Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-NM) detailed his concerns. At the November 10th hearing where Thumann answered committee members’ questions, she testified that she had “not worked with the Chairman on any media-related issues,” Luján noted in the letter. But documents obtained via a Freedom of Information Act request show that Thumann was “looped in” on various media matters, and “helped draft Skydance’s commitments that facilitated the 2 FCC’s approval of the Skydance-Paramount merger,” Luján wrote. “She also played a role in processing informal complaints related to CBS 60 Minutes alleged news distortion and she apparently orchestrated the Commission’s response to consumers regarding the Jimmy Kimmel controversy.” The FCC did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the matter.
Even Cruz admitted concerns with Carr’s handling of Kimmel’s comments in the aftermath of conservative activist Charlie Kirk’s killing. But at Wednesday’s meeting, he said he “emphatically agree[s]” that Thumann had resolved any lingering worries about that. He added that his JAWBONE Act, which the committee previously passed, could directly address First Amendment violations by government agencies of either party. The bill would let individuals sue government officials if they illegally try to compel social media or broadcast companies to remove their speech. Sen. Jerry Moran (R-KS), who’d similarly expressed concern over the Kimmel incident, said he found Thumann’s responses on the subject “comforting,” including in a phone call earlier that morning where he said he’d expressed his “serious interest in how the FCC protects and promotes free speech, including free speech on broadcast.” On the call, he said, “she was able to satisfy me once again in her answers, including an explanation for her role at the FCC and her lack of engagement on this type of issue as the FCC made decisions.”
“If she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?”
Speaking to reporters outside of the hearing room ahead of the meeting, Luján accused Thumann of lying to the committee. “The questions that I have is if she was lying about this, what else is she lying about and what else is she hiding?” he said. Luján said he wants both Thumann and Carr to appear before the committee by the end of the year to answer lawmakers’ questions. Asked if he’d support using the committee’s subpoena power or even pursuing impeachment against Carr when Democrats regain power next year, Luján said his vote to confirm Carr as a commissioner under President Joe Biden is among his biggest regrets, and that while he hopes Carr will testify voluntarily, “everything should be on the table here to be able to get answers for the American people.”
When it came time to vote on whether to advance Thumann’s nomination for a final step of a vote on the Senate floor, all 15 Republicans voted “aye.” That gave Thumann enough votes for her nomination to advance to the Senate floor, where it’s expected to pass along party lines once scheduled. Still, the clerk listed off the names of the 13 Democratic committee members whose seats remained empty. There was no response.

articles.title: The Download: AI learns to smell and hydropower struggles
articles.text:
The Download: AI learns to smell and hydropower struggles
Plus: The wave of outages has reached the US government and Apple.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
In a New Jersey lab, researchers are trying to sniff every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with chemical analyses to train what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. Its goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”
Wiltschko claims the model has already achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence” and is helping fragrance brands design new scents. But Osmo has bigger ambitions, from detecting counterfeit goods to diagnosing diseases. Not everyone is convinced its technology can deliver.
How far could an AI-powered sense of smell really take us?
—Amit Katwala
Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.
Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. But an extreme, prolonged drought has left water levels dangerously low in the region's two largest reservoirs—and climate change is adding to the pressure.
Find out how climate change is threatening a vital source of renewable power.
—Casey Crownhart
MIT Technology Review Narrated: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of the US grid, helping move power efficiently across long distances. But they’re complicated and in short supply, and their basic design hasn’t changed much in about a century.
As electricity demand rises from EVs, data centers, and more, plans are emerging to modernize these grid staples. Solid-state versions could help ease supply concerns and cut power losses. The technology is still in development, but it could become a crucial part of our future grid.
This is our latest story to become an MIT Technology Review Narrated podcast, which we publish each week on Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Just navigate to MIT Technology Review Narrated on either platform, and follow us to get all our new content as it’s released.
The must-reads
I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
1 The wave of outages has reached the US government and Apple
The agency’s classified communications network has gone down. (CNN)
+ An update disrupted Apple Music, App Store, and AppleCare. (AP)
+ The issues join a recent flood of outages at critical services. (CNBC)
+ Marco Rubio says they’re unrelated and not hostile acts. (Guardian)
+ But AI is accelerating the discovery of vulnerabilities. (Vox)
+ And making online crimes easier. (MIT Technology Review)
2 Measles is officially endemic again in the US
Scientists blame persistent gaps in vaccination coverage. (Guardian)
+ This year’s outbreak is the deadliest since 1991. (Nature)
+ Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles elimination status. (DW)
+ Other infections could be next. (MIT Technology Review)
3 Only nine countries have backed COP31’s AI climate pledge

articles.title: Avec Rubin HPC, NVIDIA dévoile un monstre de plus de 50 000 cœurs, mais AMD a déjà pris une longueur d’avance
articles.text:
Simulations scientifiques, recherche assistée par l’IA et calcul haute performance sont au programme du nouveau GPU de NVIDIA. Prévu pour 2028, il devra notamment rivaliser avec l’Instinct MI430X d’AMD, attendu dès l’année prochaine.
Les agents IA vont devoir passer leurs idées au banc d’essai. NVIDIA a présenté le 16 novembre dernier, lors de la conférence Supercomputing 2026 à Chicago, Rubin HPC, une déclinaison de sa plateforme Vera Rubin consacrée au calcul haute performance. Sa mission est d’accélérer les simulations et l’analyse de données qui permettent aux chercheurs d’évaluer des molécules, des matériaux ou des conceptions industrielles suggérés par l’IA.
Un Rubin rééquilibré pour le calcul scientifique
Premier changement, Rubin HPC dépassera les 50 000 cœurs CUDA par GPU, contre 28 672 pour la version classique de Rubin. À titre de comparaison, une carte graphique GeForce RTX 5090 en compte 21 760 et une RTX 5080, 10 752. NVIDIA prévoit aussi une accélération du traitement des données éparses pour que les unités de calcul passent moins de temps à attendre les informations dont elles ont besoin. La liaison entre GPU passera au NVLink de septième génération, contre la sixième sur Rubin classique.
L’enjeu tient notamment à la double précision, ou FP64, employée dans de nombreuses simulations scientifiques. Rubin classique privilégie les formats de faible précision utilisés par l’IA avec un débit FP64 vectoriel de 33 téraflops, contre 40 pour Blackwell. NVIDIA revendique jusqu’à 200 téraflops pour certaines opérations matricielles FP64 obtenus par émulation sur ses Tensor Cores. Cette technique exploite des unités conçues pour des calculs moins précis, mais ne remplace pas les capacités FP64 natives dans tous les usages scientifiques.
Interrogé par The Register, Dan Ernst, responsable du supercalcul chez NVIDIA, a également évoqué des capacités matricielles FP64 natives pour le matériel HPC du groupe. Les performances exactes de Rubin HPC, sa capacité mémoire et sa bande passante n’ont cependant pas été communiquées.
AMD a déjà un rival et des clients
NVIDIA trouvera sur sa route l’Instinct MI430X d’AMD, attendu dès 2027. Détaillée le 12 novembre à l’approche de SC26, cette puce basée sur l’architecture CDNA 5 doit embarquer 432 Go de mémoire HBM4, avec une bande passante pouvant atteindre 23,3 To/s et jusqu’à 288 téraflops en FP64 natif. AMD affiche ainsi ses ambitions dans le calcul scientifique, avec un calendrier plus serré que celui de son rival. Pour confronter les promesses des deux fabricants, il faudra toutefois que NVIDIA dévoile les performances de Rubin HPC.
Les centres de calcul, eux, passent déjà commande. Aux États-Unis, le laboratoire d’Oak Ridge a choisi le MI430X pour Discovery, le supercalculateur qui succédera à Frontier. En France, la puce d’AMD équipera Alice Recoque, le premier supercalculateur exascale du pays. Il faudra attendre 2028 pour mesurer ce que vaut Rubin HPC face à son rival. Pour ces deux machines, le choix est déjà fait.
La FP64 (64 bits) augmente la précision numérique des calculs, ce qui limite les erreurs d’arrondi quand une simulation enchaîne des milliards d’opérations. Elle est essentielle en modélisation physique, chimie, mécanique des fluides ou climat, où une petite dérive peut fausser un résultat final. Beaucoup de charges HPC sont donc jugées sur leur débit FP64, généralement exprimé en téraflops (TFLOPS). À l’inverse, l’IA privilégie souvent des formats moins précis (FP16, BF16, FP8) plus rapides et moins coûteux en énergie. Un GPU orienté science doit donc proposer une FP64 solide, pas seulement des accélérations ponctuelles.
La FP64 native signifie que le GPU dispose d’unités matérielles capables d’exécuter directement des opérations en double précision, avec un comportement et des performances prévisibles pour les codes scientifiques. La FP64 émulée via des Tensor Cores consiste à s’appuyer sur des unités optimisées pour des calculs matriciels moins précis, en recomposant des opérations FP64 pour certains types de multiplications de matrices. Cette approche peut donner de très bons débits dans des cas bien cadrés (algèbre linéaire dense, kernels adaptés), mais elle ne couvre pas tous les besoins HPC. En pratique, de nombreux logiciels utilisent un mix d’opérations (vectorielles, irrégulières, non matricielles) où l’émulation ne remplace pas toujours la FP64 native. C’est pour cela que les annonces distinguent souvent « pic théorique » sur matrices et performance FP64 réellement exploitable sur des codes variés.
La HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) est une mémoire empilée très proche du GPU, conçue pour fournir une bande passante massive, bien plus élevée que la GDDR des cartes grand public. En HPC, beaucoup de workloads sont limités non par la puissance de calcul brute, mais par la vitesse à laquelle le GPU peut lire et écrire des données (gros tenseurs, grilles de simulation, matrices, champs 3D). La bande passante (exprimée en To/s) aide à alimenter les unités de calcul et à réduire le temps passé à attendre les données, surtout quand les accès mémoire sont nombreux. La capacité (en Go) compte aussi : elle conditionne la taille des modèles ou des simulations qui tiennent en mémoire sans découpage coûteux. HBM4 est une nouvelle génération qui vise à augmenter à la fois capacité et débit, ce qui est central pour les systèmes exascale.

articles.title: Si vous voulez un robot cuiseur avant les repas de fêtes, Lidl fait baisser son Monsieur Cuisine Smart
articles.text:
Velouté de potimarron, pâte à brioche, risotto qui se remue tout seul : le Monsieur Cuisine est le robot cuiseur que Lidl vend sous sa marque maison Silvercrest. On le cite souvent comme l’alternative au Thermomix de Vorwerk. Sa version Smart Black Edition, connectée au Wi-Fi, baisse de prix.
Pour le Black Friday, Lidl affiche son robot cuiseur à 399 € au lieu de 549 €, soit 150 € de moins.
C’est quoi, ce Monsieur Cuisine Smart Black Edition ?
Un robot cuiseur chauffe et mixe dans un même bol. Celui-ci est en inox, avec une contenance de 4,5 litres dont 3 litres utiles. La puissance maximale atteint 1 200 W, avec 1 050 W pour la chauffe et 1 000 W pour le moteur. La température se règle de 37 à 130 °C. Les lames tournent entre 125 et 5 500 tours par minute, sur 10 vitesses avec une fonction turbo. La rotation à droite hache les ingrédients. La rotation à gauche remue un ragoût ou un risotto sans réduire les aliments en purée. Une balance intégrée pèse jusqu’à 5 kg directement dans le bol.
16 fonctions et programmes automatiques sont présents, parmi lesquels le pétrissage, la cuisson vapeur, les smoothies, la fermentation, la cuisson lente et la cuisson sous vide. Cette dernière cuit à basse température un aliment emballé hermétiquement. L’accessoire vapeur fourni empile les niveaux de cuisson : un poisson au-dessus, les légumes en dessous, et le repas se prépare en une fois. Vous trouverez aussi un fouet, un panier de cuisson et une spatule. Tous les accessoires passent au lave-vaisselle.
La partie « Smart » repose sur un écran tactile de 8 pouces et une connexion Wi-Fi. Le robot embarque plus de 1 000 recettes guidées pas à pas, dont certaines en vidéo, et ajuste le nombre de portions sur une sélection d’entre elles. Google Assistant permet de le commander à la voix, à condition que le Wi-Fi soit actif. L’application ajoute un planificateur de menus hebdomadaire et une liste de courses.
À ce prix, le Monsieur Cuisine Smart est-il une bonne affaire ?
Avec 150 € de remise, le robot perd un peu plus d’un quart de son prix et passe sous la barre des 400 €. C’est un très bon prix pour un appareil qui remplace à la fois le blender, la balance de cuisine et le cuiseur vapeur. Le Thermomix de Vorwerk, qui reste la référence du secteur, coûte nettement plus cher pour un principe similaire.
Deux réserves avant de vous décider. Avec environ 45,7 x 37 x 29 cm, le robot prend de la place sur un plan de travail. Ses fonctions les plus avancées dépendent aussi de l’écosystème de recettes de Lidl et d’une connexion Wi-Fi. Si vous cuisinez souvent maison, les 150 € économisés couvriront largement les premières courses pour les gros repas de fin d’année.

articles.title: Google AI Ultra inclut YouTube Premium Famille : faites près de 360 € d’économie par an — Frandroid
articles.text:
Google a annoncé ce mercredi 18 novembre, sur le forum communautaire de Google One, une évolution de ses forfaits d’intelligence artificielle haut de gamme. Jusqu’ici, les abonnés à Google AI Ultra profitaient d’un abonnement YouTube Premium Individuel, réservé à une seule personne. Désormais, ils ont droit à YouTube Premium Famille, sans supplément.
D’après Google, la bascule se fait automatiquement dans les pays éligibles, dont la France fait partie. Les abonnés existants n’ont donc aucune démarche à faire. Selon Android Police, plusieurs d’entre eux ont d’ailleurs indiqué sur Reddit avoir reçu ces derniers jours un e-mail les informant du changement.
Une condition s’applique toutefois. Pour partager l’avantage, l’abonné Ultra doit être le gestionnaire du groupe familial Google. Les personnes invitées doivent en outre vivre sous le même toit et avoir au moins 13 ans, précise la page de l’offre.
Si le groupe familial Google du foyer est déjà géré par une autre personne, l’abonné Ultra peut créer son propre groupe pour partager l’avantage. Notez toutefois que Google ne permet de changer de groupe familial qu’une fois tous les 12 mois.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Ce que comprend la formule Famille
La formule permet d’ajouter jusqu’à cinq membres du foyer, soit six utilisateurs au total. Chacun garde son propre compte Google, et donc son historique, ses recommandations et ses abonnements.
Les avantages sont ceux de YouTube Premium : vidéos sans publicité, téléchargements pour un visionnage hors ligne et lecture en arrière-plan. YouTube Music Premium est également inclus, tout comme la fonction Ask Music.
À titre de comparaison, le forfait AI Pro, facturé 21,99 euros par mois en France, ne propose que YouTube Premium Lite, qui exclut YouTube Music. L’écart entre les deux paliers se creuse ainsi un peu plus.
Les forfaits Ultra regroupent par ailleurs d’autres services : 20 ou 30 To de stockage selon la formule, Google Home Premium Advanced et Google Health Premium. Ils incluent en outre Gemini dans Gmail et Docs, des limites relevées dans Flow, l’accès à Project Genie et aux modèles Gemini 4 Argon et Carbon, ce dernier étant réservé à Ultra. Dans l’application Gemini, les limites d’usage atteignent 5 ou 20 fois celles d’AI Pro. Certaines fonctions ne sont toutefois pas disponibles en France, comme la navigation automatique de Gemini dans Chrome (proposée aux États-Unis et en Inde) et AI Inbox dans Gmail (États-Unis uniquement, en anglais).
En France, la formule Ultra 5x, avec 20 To de stockage, coûte 99,99 euros par mois, et la formule Ultra 20x, avec 30 To, 219,99 euros par mois. Google a ajouté ce premier palier en juin 2026. Avant, l’offre Ultra unique était facturée 274,99 euros par mois.
On comprend que pour Google, l’idée est d’être plus compétitif que les abonnements à 100 et 200 dollars de ChatGPT et de Claude qui vient de rentrer en bourse.
Un gain qui dépend du prix de l’abonnement séparé
Pour mesurer l’économie, il faut regarder le prix de YouTube Premium vendu seul.
En France, le forfait YouTube Premium Individuel coûte toujours 12,99 euros par mois, tandis que le forfait Famille est passé de 23,99 euros à 29,99 euros en juillet 2025. Un abonné Ultra qui payait la formule Famille séparément économisera ainsi près de 360 euros par an.
Pour un foyer qui n’est pas encore abonné, le calcul est différent : la formule Ultra 5x revient à près de 1 200 euros par an, soit plus de trois fois le prix de YouTube Premium Famille seul (359,88 euros). L’avantage YouTube compte donc surtout pour ceux qui utilisent déjà beaucoup Gemini ou qui ont besoin d’un gros espace de stockage.

articles.title: Ha entrado en vigor: los propietarios que vendan la vivienda deberán indemnizar a los inquilinos que residan en ella
articles.text:
Al vender una vivienda con inquilinos, hay que atender qué pasa con el alquiler existente. Por un lado, cambia el titular de la renta y, por otro, al comprar la vivienda, se adquieren ciertas obligaciones respecto al inquilino.
Debemos tener en cuenta la duración del contrato y el estado registral. En función de estos, puede haber que respetar el alquiler hasta cierto momento y puede ser necesario que el vendedor indemnice.
Esto viene regulado en el artículo 14 de la LAU. También existe la posibilidad de que haya que indemnizar. Esto sucede cuando el contrato es de más de 5 (o 7) años y el comprador cumple con ciertos requisitos.
Comprador debe respetar el alquiler
Los 5 primeros años (o 7 si el anterior arrendador era una persona jurídica, como por ejemplo una empresa), el nuevo dueño es sustituto del anterior arrendador. No podemos desahuciar al inquilino ni modificar unilateralmente lo que se ha firmado por el hecho de comprar el piso.
Deben contarse a partir de la fecha de inicio del contrato. Es decir que debemos respetar el tiempo que falta para llegar a los 5 (o 7) años.
En el caso de que se haya pactado un plazo mayor, la norma general es que el comprador también se vea afectado por todo el plazo. Hay una excepción en la que sí hay que indemnizar. Para ello es necesario que el comprador cumpla con los requisitos del artículo 34 de la Ley Hipotecaria (compra de buena fe y por precio a quien aparece en el Registro con facultades para transmitir, además de inscribir el derecho). No basta con que se quiera disponer de la casa.
Cuándo tiene que indemnizar el vendedor
En el caso de excepción, el comprador solo tendrá que aguantar el alquiler hasta que pasen los 5 (o 7) años. El vendedor deberá compensar al arrendatario por el tiempo restante.
La ley indica que será de una mensualidad de la renta actual por cada año que quede más allá de los 5 (o 7) años. Quien paga la indemnización que indica este artículo es el vendedor. No se trata de sumar los gastos de mudanza o relacionar el precio del alquiler con el de otra vivienda.
Por tanto, en el caso de que se firme un alquiler de 10 años y posteriormente se venda, es preciso saber si el comprador debe aguantar todo el plazo o si estamos en una situación de excepción. No basta con que la venta sea antes de tiempo.
Es importante comprobar el contrato y cómo hemos pactado con el casero. Los contratos anteriores a esta regulación siguen sometidos al régimen que les corresponda (salvo que se haya acordado una válida adaptación entre las partes).
