articles.title: Ya es oficial: el servicio universal de internet será diez veces más rápido en 2027 y beneficiará a mucha más gente
articles.text:
Ya es oficial. El Consejo de Ministros ha aprobado el Real Decreto que aprueba el Reglamento del Servicio Universal de telecomunicaciones. Se han incluido todos los cambios que conocimos en el Proyecto de Orden que publicó el Gobierno hace unas semanas y que entrarán en vigor el próximo 1 de enero.
En primer lugar, el nuevo reglamento libera a Telefónica de la obligación exclusiva de garantizar este servicio y la hace extensible al resto de operadores. También multiplica por diez la velocidad mínima de la banda ancha fija, que pasa de 10 a 100 Mbps.
Y además, permite a muchos más usuarios beneficiarse de tarifas asequibles de telefonía fija e internet. Entre ellos, todos los perceptores del Ingreso Mínimo Vital, las pymes o las ONGs.
Qué es el Servicio Universal de telecomunicaciones. Dicho en pocas palabras, es la obligación por ley de garantizar los servicios básicos de telefonía fija y acceso fijo a internet con una calidad determinada y a un precio asequible para cualquier ciudadano español, independientemente de su ubicación geográfica o su situación económica.
Las prestaciones de este servicio universal han ido evolucionando con el paso de los años y, del mismo modo que en su día se eliminaron las cabinas y las guías de teléfonos, también se empezó a considerar como servicio básico la conexión fija a internet con una velocidad mínima. Actualmente, son 10 Mbps, pero con la nueva normativa, que entrará en vigor el 1 de enero de 2027, se incrementa la velocidad mínima a 100 Mbps. Diez veces más.
Tarifas baratas para más gente. Otra novedad importante del Real Decreto es que podrán acceder a las tarifas asequibles todas aquellas unidades de convivencia perceptoras del Ingreso Mínimo Vital (unos 800.000 hogares). Si un operador no dispone de las tarifas asequibles que establece la CNMC, deberá ofrecer un 25% de descuento a los beneficiarios del Ingreso Mínimo Vital respecto al precio medio de mercado.
Además, el Real Decreto amplía el "tipo" de usuarios que pueden beneficiarse del Servicio Universal. A partir del 1 de enero, no sólo podrán solicitarlo los consumidores, sino también las microempresas, las pymes o las organizaciones sin ánimo de lucro (ONGs).
Buenas noticias para Telefónica. Ante la falta de interés del resto de operadores, la CNMC lleva casi 30 años designando a Telefónica como única compañía encargada de garantizar ese servicio. Pero eso también va a cambiar. La última adjudicación finaliza el próximo 31 de diciembre, de manera que, a partir del 1 de enero, todos los operadores atenderán solicitudes en las zonas donde ofrezcan cobertura.
De lo que no se librará Telefónica es de seguir ofreciendo las ofertas vigentes del actual Abono Social, que aplican una bonificación para jubilados y pensionistas a la hora de contratar una línea de telefonía fija o una línea fija con conexión a internet.

articles.title: Apollo, Microsoft turn to AI to help hospitals learn from medical errors
articles.text:
Apollo, Microsoft turn to AI to help hospitals learn from medical errors
The partnership aims to turn fragmented hospital records into faster incident reviews and shared lessons.
An artificial intelligence system developed by Apollo Hospitals with Microsoft is being used to speed up reviews of patient falls, medication errors and readmissions. Apollo said the system has coincided with fewer recorded incidents, although the evidence published so far does not establish that AI itself has reduced patient harm.
Apollo and Microsoft developed a Daily Tiered Huddle agent to support clinical-governance teams. It brings together hospital records, flags cases, builds patient timelines and prompts clinicians for missing details. It also suggests assessments for doctors to check and amend. The tool is in production at some Apollo hospitals.
“For anyone to process 600 cases per month with incomplete data and come up with a meaningful decision is difficult,” said Dr Rohini Sridhar, Apollo’s chief of medical services. The agent is intended to reduce the time spent assembling records, leaving clinicians more time to investigate complex cases.
Apollo said more than 60% of cases reviewed by its huddles were closed within three days in November 2026. It also noted fewer falls and medication errors in July-September than in the same quarter of 2025. Dr Sridhar said staff satisfaction with error handling improved by almost 30%, based on the hospital’s annual safety-culture survey.
These are hospital-reported results published in a Microsoft case study. The account does not provide incident counts, patient-volume-adjusted rates or an independent assessment.
The system is also designed to identify patterns across departments, although Apollo said this analysis is still being developed. It flagged a cluster of central-line-associated bloodstream infections in a bone marrow transplant unit. Juliet Joji Varghese, Apollo’s director of nursing in Chennai, said the system helps staff learn from incidents elsewhere in the network.
Beyond the Apollo and Microsoft push, there are other initiatives that reflect the expanding use of AI in routine healthcare operations and diagnostics.
In April, AstraZeneca and the Telangana government agreed to introduce Qure.ai’s AI-supported chest X-ray screening in 20 public health facilities. The technology is intended to flag high-risk lung nodules for further assessment. Manipal Hospitals has also worked with Google Cloud on a generative AI tool for nurse handovers, which Google said had been rolled out across 23 hospitals by July 2025.
India is also beginning to establish a framework for responsible adoption. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, launched in 2021, laid the foundation for interoperable digital health records. In February 2026, the Centre launched the Strategy for AI in Healthcare for India, and the Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI (BODH).
Developed with IIT Kanpur and the National Health Authority, BODH is intended to evaluate AI models using diverse health data while protecting patient records.
The World Health Organization, in a July 2026 report, highlighted ethical and oversight challenges arising from AI in health research, including risks that existing review systems may not adequately address.

articles.title: Oppo Reno 17 Pro: Price, release date and full specs
articles.text:
Table of contents
Oppo announced the Reno 17 Pro in China on November 16, 2026, with sales starting November 20. Priced at CNY 4,199 (about $591), the phone packs a 200MP main camera into a compact 6.32-inch body.
For the first time in the series, the Pro is the smaller model. The standard Reno 17 has a larger 6.56-inch display, reversing last year’s arrangement, when the China-exclusive Reno 16 Pro came with a 6.78-inch screen.
Oppo has yet to announce an international launch. This guide covers the Reno 17 Pro’s price, specifications, expected availability outside China, and its comparison with the Reno 16 Pro.
Oppo Reno 17 Pro release date
Here is how the China launch played out:
- Pre-orders: Oppo opened blind pre-orders on October 30, 2026, through its official Weibo account.
- Launch event: Oppo unveiled the phone on November 16, 2026, at 7 pm China time (12 pm in Lagos), alongside the standard Reno 17.
- Sale date: The phone goes on sale in China on November 20, 2026.
- Model number: The China model is PND110.
Will the Oppo Reno 17 Pro launch globally?
Oppo has not said when the phone will launch in other countries. A few signs suggest the Pro may stay in China, at least for now:
- Tipster Yogesh Brar told Smartprix that Oppo plans to bring the Reno 17 to India without the Pro.
- Thailand’s telecom regulator has certified the standard Reno 17 and the Reno 17 F for global markets. No global model number for the Pro has shown up in any certification so far.
If the Pro does go global, past launches give you a rough idea of timing:
- The Reno 15 launched in China on November 17, 2025, and went global on January 2, 2026, about six and a half weeks later.
- The Reno 16 launched in China on May 25, 2026, and went global on June 25, 2026, exactly one month later.
If Oppo follows either pattern, a global Reno 17 launch would land between mid-December 2026 and late January 2027. The Pro may not be part of it.
Is the phone coming to Nigeria?
Oppo Nigeria has not announced a Reno 17 Pro launch. The recent track record is mixed. Oppo launched the Reno 15 and Reno 15 F in Nigeria, but excluded the Pro model. For the Reno 16 series, Oppo never confirmed a Nigerian launch, as we noted in our Oppo Reno 16 price and specs guide.
So if you want this exact phone in Nigeria, you will most likely have to buy an imported China unit. Read the buying risks further down before you do.
Oppo Reno 17 Pro price
The phone comes in three memory options in China. Here is what each one costs:
| Variant | China price | USD (approx.) | Naira (approx.) | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 8GB + 256GB | CNY4,199 | $591 | ₦802,000 | 
| 12GB + 256GB | CNY4,599 | $648 | ₦879,500 | 
| 12GB + 512GB | CNY4,999 | $704 | ₦955,500 | 
| With China subsidy | From CNY3,699 | $521 | China residents only | 
Naira figures use the official CBN rate of ₦1,357.19 to $1 on November 16, 2026. At the Lagos parallel rate of ₦1,445 to $1, the range is about ₦854,000 to ₦1,017,000.
Keep these points in mind:
- These are straight currency conversions. They exclude shipping costs and customs duty, so an imported unit will cost more.
- Oppo has not set a Nigerian price. Treat any naira price you see online as a guess.
For context, the global Reno 16 Pro launched at €1,099 in Europe and £899 in the UK for 12GB + 512GB. China prices are usually much lower than European prices, so don’t expect the Reno 17 Pro to cost half as much if it reaches your market.
Oppo also sells the upgraded OPPO Bubble for CNY 399 (about $56) in China. It is a small 1.73-inch round screen that sticks to the back of the phone with magnets. You use it to see yourself while you take selfies with the main camera.
Detailed specs
1. Design and build
- Size: 151.21 x 72.42 x 8.32mm (8.50mm for the cat edition)
- Weight: about 192g (194g for the cat edition)
- Build: metal frame with a glass back
- Water and dust: IP66, IP68, IP69 and IP69K, with the phone able to sit in 1.5m of water for 30 minutes
You can pick First Snow White or Cocoa Brown, plus a special cat edition called Encounter Cat. Oppo has only published Chinese names so far, so these English names are translations.
The cat edition has a 3D cat that floats inside the glass back. Its outline and shadow shift as you tilt the phone. The bezels around the screen are as thin as 1.2mm.
2. Display
- 6.32-inch flat OLED with a 2640 x 1216 resolution (460ppi)
- Up to 120Hz refresh rate and 240Hz touch sampling
- 800 nits normal brightness and 1,800 nits in high brightness mode
- 10-bit colour with full DCI-P3 coverage, protected by OPPO Crystal Shield Glass
The refresh rate drops from 144Hz on the global Reno 16 Pro to 120Hz here. Most people will not notice it in daily use, but gamers might.
3. Performance
- Chip: MediaTek Dimensity 8550 Super (4nm), up to 3.4GHz
- Graphics: Arm Mali-G720 MC8
- Memory type: LPDDR5X RAM and UFS 3.1 storage
- Cooling: a 4,400mm² vapour chamber
Oppo claims a benchmark score of about 2.49 million and 120fps in supported games. It uses the same chip as the global Reno 16 Pro, so don’t expect a big speed jump.
4. Cameras
- Main: 200MP, f/1.8, with optical image stabilisation (OIS)
- Ultrawide: 50MP, f/2.0, 116-degree view, with autofocus
- Telephoto: 50MP periscope, f/2.8, 3.5x optical zoom with OIS, up to 120x digital zoom
- Selfie: 50MP, f/2.0, with autofocus
You can record 4K video at up to 60fps on both the rear and front cameras. The phone also takes 4K Live Photos of up to six seconds on every rear lens.
Oppo added new colour tools too. A Live Colour Palette lets you change a photo’s tone after you take it, and an AI portrait fill light brightens faces in dim scenes.
5. Battery and charging
- 7,250mAh silicon-carbon battery (7,020mAh rated)
- 80W SuperVOOC and 80W UFCS wired charging
- Reverse wired charging, so you can top up another device
- No wireless charging
The China box comes with an 80W charger and a case.
6. Software
- ColorOS 17 based on Android 17
- AI tools such as AI Snap, AI Writing, an AI call assistant and AI ID photos
Oppo says the phone will stay smooth for six years, but it has not shared how many Android updates you get. For comparison, the global Reno 16 series gets five Android updates and six years of security patches.
7. Memory and storage
- 8GB or 12GB of RAM
- 256GB or 512GB of storage, with no memory card slot
8. Connectivity
- 5G (including the n77 and n78 bands) and 4G LTE
- Dual Nano-SIM, with no eSIM listed
- Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.4
- NFC and an IR blaster
- In-display fingerprint sensor and face unlock
- Stereo speakers and a USB-C port, with no headphone jack
Oppo Reno 17 Pro vs Oppo Reno 16 Pro
This comparison uses the global Reno 16 Pro, the 6.32-inch model sold in Europe and Asia. The China Reno 16 Pro was a different, bigger phone with a Dimensity 9500s chip.
| Spec | Reno 17 Pro (China) | Reno 16 Pro (global) | 
|---|---|---|
| Launch | November 16, 2026 | June 25, 2026 | 
| Starting price | CNY4,199 (8GB + 256GB) | €1,099 / £899 (12GB + 512GB) | 
| Display | 6.32-inch OLED, 120Hz | 6.32-inch AMOLED, 144Hz | 
| Chip | Dimensity 8550 Super | Dimensity 8550 Super | 
| Main camera | 200MP with OIS | 200MP with OIS | 
| Telephoto | 50MP 3.5x periscope | 50MP 3.5x periscope | 
| Battery | 7,250mAh | 6,700mAh (6,000mAh in Europe) | 
| Charging | 80W wired, no wireless | 80W wired, no wireless | 
| Water and dust | IP66, IP68, IP69, IP69K | IP68, IP69K | 
| Software | ColorOS 17, Android 17 | ColorOS 16, Android 16 | 
| Size and weight | 8.32mm, 192g | 8.2mm, 188g | 
| SIM | Dual Nano-SIM | Nano-SIM plus eSIM | 
Here’s what’s new on the Reno 17 Pro:
- A bigger battery, up to 550mAh on the global model and 1,250mAh on the European one
- Android 17 with new photo tools such as six-second Live Photos
- Two extra water ratings, IP66 and IP69
- A cheaper 8GB starting option
The chip and all the cameras carry over unchanged. The screen also takes a small step back, with a lower refresh rate and lower peak brightness. If you own a Reno 16 Pro, you have little reason to upgrade.
Where you can buy the Oppo Reno 17 Pro
1. In China
- Oppo Mall, on the opposhop.cn website and the Oppo Store app
- Oppo-authorised online stores and Oppo experience stores
2. In Nigeria
As of November 17, 2026, the phone has no listings on Jumia, Slot, Konga, or Jiji. Expect imported units to show up after the China sale date of November 20.
Be careful with websites already quoting a Nigerian price. Some of them list made-up specs, such as the wrong chip and Android version.
3. What to check before you buy an imported unit
- Google apps: China units usually ship without Google Play services, and Oppo has not said otherwise for this phone.
- Warranty: The warranty covers China only. Oppo Nigeria may not repair it.
- Network: The phone supports the n78 band that MTN and Airtel use for 5G. It lacks 4G bands 7 and 20, so ask your network if that affects coverage in your area.
- Extras: OPPO Pay and other NFC payment features work only in China, and the charger has a Chinese plug.
If you would rather not wait or import, check our list of OPPO phones you can buy right now. You can also follow OPPO’s full 2026 release timeline to see what else is coming.

articles.title: GTA 6 sur PS5 : vous devez absolument installer cette mise à jour pour pouvoir y jouer
articles.text:
Le compte à rebours est lancé avant la sortie de GTA 6. Mais avant de pouvoir lancer le titre dès minuit ce 19 novembre, vous devez obligatoirement passer par la case mise à jour si vous possédez une PS5 ou une PS5 Pro. Dans un message officiel publié par le compte @PS_Support_US sur X, le constructeur japonais vous presse en effet de ne pas attendre la dernière minute pour mettre à jour votre console.
Une mise à jour de sécurité nécessaire pour jouer à GTA 6 sur PS5
Portant le numéro de version 26.07-14.23.00, cette mise à jour système pèse environ 1,3 Go. C’est plus lourd qu’un patch mineur, mais le journal de modifications officiel fourni par Sony reste particulièrement succinct. L’entreprise japonaise y indique simplement avoir apporté des « correctifs de sécurité au logiciel système », sans détailler la moindre optimisation ou fonctionnalité spécifiquement conçue pour GTA 6.
 Sony Interactive has issued a PS5 system software update that is required before playing Grand Theft Auto VI. Players should download this update prior to midnight on November 19 so that they’re ready to play on launch day, November 19.
— PlayStation Support US (@PS_Support_US) November 18, 2026
Ce manque de précisions a de quoi interpeller, d’autant qu’il s’agit du second patch axé sur la sécurité déployé coup sur coup par le constructeur, juste après la version 26.07-14.22.00. Si Sony n’a pas expliqué pourquoi le jeu exige impérativement cette version du firmware, le déploiement intervient dans un contexte assez tendu face aux tentatives de jailbreak et d’exploits logiciels ciblant la PS5. Ceci explique donc peut-être cela.
Vérifier et installer la mise à jour manuellement pour éviter les blocages
Pour éviter d’être pris de court lors du déverrouillage du jeu le 19 novembre à minuit, il est donc conseillé d’anticiper l’installation. Si le téléchargement automatique ne s’est pas déclenché en tâche de fond, vous pouvez effectuer une vérification manuelle dans l’interface de votre console. Il vous suffit de vous rendre dans : Paramètres > Système > Logiciel système > Mise à jour et paramètres du logiciel système.
Découvrez : Comment jouer à GTA 6 avant tout le monde sur Xbox Series S / X
Si vous avez acheté le jeu et que vous l’avez préchargé pour pouvoir y jouer dès ce soir, ce serait bête de rester bloqué ou simplement retardé à cause d’une simple mise à jour. Dites-nous en commentaire si oui ou non vous avez précommandé GTA 6 et si vous comptez y jouer dès minuit ce 19 novembre.

Instead of digging through system folders to delete these files one by one, you can use Advanced SystemCare to detect and wipe out the clutter automatically. The software also goes past simple file deletion to handle day-to-day upkeep, sweeping away browser tracking data, broken shortcuts, registry bloat, and sluggish background tasks. Part 4: How to Reclaim Gigabytes of Storage With Advanced SystemCare?

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review
articles.text:
Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort.
This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.
The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.
Just another day in a thrilling life of crime.
Rockstar
Just another day in a thrilling life of crime.
Rockstar
The family that moves furniture together stays together.
Rockstar
The family that moves furniture together stays together.
Rockstar
Just another day in a thrilling life of crime.
Rockstar
The family that moves furniture together stays together.
Rockstar
But it’s the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.
Taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game’s two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content.
Grand Theft Auto VI never lets you get too settled with a budding life of crime or a budding family life. And it’s all the better for it.
The couple you love to love
A large part of why this works so well is Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists whose relationship drives the story. While that relationship starts off a bit awkwardly—thanks chiefly to Lucia’s brief prison stint—it quickly develops into a true criminal and life partnership. Both sides of the relationship are driven by a mutual desire to move up in the criminal world and eventually settle down to a legit family life, if they can just earn enough from the next big score.
I can’t tell who’s in this screenshot because of the bandanas.
Rockstar
I can’t tell who’s in this screenshot because of the bandanas.
Rockstar
The love of a good woman makes the dull Jason downright tolerable.
Rockstar
The love of a good woman makes the dull Jason downright tolerable.
Rockstar
I can’t tell who’s in this screenshot because of the bandanas.
Rockstar
The love of a good woman makes the dull Jason downright tolerable.
Rockstar
Of the two, Jason is definitely the duller partner. An ex-military meathead with a ripped body and a dull, affect-free vocal delivery, a decent chunk of Jason’s lines essentially boil down to “Yeah, sure, that’s fine.” While the game struggles to expose a bit of a tender and thoughtful side hiding underneath Jason’s cool demeanor, the writing can’t quite break through the emotionless masculine facade that Jason wears as a semi-permanent mask.
Lucia is much more interesting as a vivacious and amiable Latina eager to grab any opportunity presented to her. The game takes some time to dig into the difficulties of Lucia’s underprivileged youth and highlight her strained relationship with an unreliable mother, helping to add some important depth to her chip-on-her-shoulder journey of self-improvement. And even the boring Jason seems that much more appealing seen through the lens of Lucia’s good-natured teasing and genuine affection.
While Jason and Lucia can and do operate independently—and the game lets you change between them frequently—it’s their moments of togetherness that really stand out. There’s an easy, rom-com comfort to their time together, whether they’re discussing their future on the couch (“I feel like I haven’t done anything normal in a minute”), taking some time for quick romance (the game cuts away before things get too hot and heavy), or laying down covering fire for each other during a firefight (the lack of a co-op mode for these missions feels truly baffling).
You jump, I jump, Jack. Er, Jason.
Rockstar
You jump, I jump, Jack. Er, Jason.
Rockstar
It’s important that your significant other be a good hang.
Rockstar
It’s important that your significant other be a good hang.
Rockstar
You jump, I jump, Jack. Er, Jason.
Rockstar
It’s important that your significant other be a good hang.
Rockstar
There’s a minor relationship simulation component to the game, with a simple “heart level” that can rise or fall based on some basic decisions. Don’t expect a lot of dating-sim style drama, though; as long as you make the completely obvious choices when they’re presented, it’s hard to let the relationship fall apart. That’s a good thing, too, because this is a relationship that’s easy to root for, even when the participants are literally getting away with murder.
Hitting and missing
In true Grand Theft Auto fashion, Jason and Lucia’s particular way of chasing The American Dream is through a life of crime. Their travels through the criminal underworld start off kind of slow, as Lucia’s begging gradually compels Jason to reluctantly introduce her to the two-bit operators with which he’s found himself involved.
For the first half of the game, the pair are constantly interacting with a rogues’ gallery of new criminal acquaintances, each more over-the-top than the last, and all of them having specific needs that somehow only Jason and Lucia can fulfill. Many of the missions these small-time crooks have on offer end up feeling like the criminal equivalent of errands—drive here, take that, lose the cops, repeat.
And while a few standout characters develop complex interpersonal relationships with Jason and Lucia over multiple missions, most of these early side characters feel like one-note caricatures that can be distilled to a few tropey traits.
It isn’t until the back half of the game that the main storyline really starts to focus on what it does best: integrating Jason and Lucia into a persistent ring of professional criminals working toward bigger and bigger scores. Here, the missions build on each other, with characters going undercover, casing targets, and learning new skills that eventually come together in some truly tense and bombastic heists. These missions also do the best job of showing off the dual protagonist system, frequently shifting the perspective between Jason and Lucia to highlight their different skills and views on how things are going down.
Ah, great, who are these yahoos…
Credit:
Rockstar
Ah, great, who are these yahoos…
Credit:
Rockstar
Outside of this core plot, though, many of the missions and side stories in GTA VI make Jason and Lucia feel like side characters in their own story. I found myself beginning to tune out during some of the many missions in which one or both protagonists serve as glorified security props or overpaid getaway drivers amid other characters’ contrived turf wars. And even dozens of hours into the game, there were still missions that felt like tutorials, seemingly built around the opportunity to introduce some new simulation system or control scheme.
Through it all, the game can’t seem to totally shake the style of sophomoric humor that feels a lot less “edgy” today than it did when Grand Theft Auto III hit back in 2001 (for players who are old enough to remember that release, at least). There are countless extended bits where the entire joke seems to boil down to “Man, kinky sex is weird, isn’t it?” or “Hey look, it’s a male penis (or something that looks similar to one).” And the game seems to take particular pleasure in forcing Jason into uncomfortable situations with plenty of T&A, much to Lucia’s good-natured bemusement.
A word of warning for parents: This is a game that definitely earns a hard “M for Mature” rating and shows how standards for that rating have shifted since GTA: San Andreasearned an AO re-rating for hiding a single sex scene amid its legacy code.
Grand Theft Auto VI gets a lot less safe for work than this, let me tell you (but not show you).
Credit:
Rockstar
Grand Theft Auto VI gets a lot less safe for work than this, let me tell you (but not show you).
Credit:
Rockstar
There are moments where GTA VI’s satire cuts a bit deeper. I especially liked a couple of side stories that skewered buzzword-spewing crypto bros and multi-level marketing schemes with some welcome over-the-top excess. Overall, though, the game’s warmed-over one-liner takes on “wokeness” felt about as fresh as jokes about mothers-in-law and TV dinners, without much in the way of thought-provoking statements on society as a whole in 2026.
What do you want to do?
Grand Theft Auto VI has a gift for finding excuses to lure you into an expertly designed space and then throwing together a reason for why you have to shoot/punch your way out. That might sound snarky, but I actually mean it more or less sincerely; I was frequently surprised by the scenarios the writers dreamed up to turn what seemed like a routine trip to some beautiful locale into a firefight with way more armed goons than seems strictly necessary.
The moment-to-moment shooting will feel very familiar to Grand Theft Auto fans, by which I mean it’s dead simple to hide behind convenient cover and pop up to pick off relatively stupid enemies one by one with a dizzying array of available weaponry. The rare enemies that do manage to flank you seem to have incredibly bad aim, even at close range, and both Jason and Lucia can take a whole lot more punishment than the average quick-to-crumble grunt.
*Making car engine revving noises with my lips* BRRRRRRRRRRRMMMMMM!
Rockstar
*Making car engine revving noises with my lips* BRRRRRRRRRRRMMMMMM!
Rockstar
Eyes on the road, Lucia!
Rockstar
Eyes on the road, Lucia!
Rockstar
*Making car engine revving noises with my lips* BRRRRRRRRRRRMMMMMM!
Rockstar
Eyes on the road, Lucia!
Rockstar
Driving around town is significantly more exciting—you’ll be darting between cars in heavy traffic to chase down antagonists, avoid the police, or simply get where you’re going faster. It’s still a blast to sample as many vehicles as you can, from zippy but easy-to-wreck sports cars to tank-like trucks that can plow through traffic, tiny motorbikes that can squeeze through tight spaces, and off-road vehicles that can explore off the beaten path.
Driving through the city also offers ample opportunities to get distracted from your main goals by dozens of side activities that dot the map. Even as I struggled to work through the story on deadline, I found myself getting sucked in for hours trying to master drone racing, chasing gold medals in countless mud-splattered rally races, or hunting for one of the many meditation spots hidden in out-of-the-way corners.
While most of these side activities offer money or improve character stats, some are simply there to be experienced. Completionists will have a bear of a time tracking down every single hidden collectible, rare car, robbable location, and beautiful landmark the developers have placed throughout the city. Grand Theft Auto VI seems set to be one of those games you can just load up to hang out in long after the main story missions are done.
A technical marvel
Even with a fast vehicle, much of that “hang out” time can be spent simply crossing the game’s massive map. Getting from the depths of the wilderness in the north to the tip of the keys in the south is a six-plus-mile trip (measured at an apparently real-world-accurate scale) that can take 10 minutes to weave your way across on a good traffic day. During these cross-city treks, the tenor of the city’s architecture morphs noticeably as you pass from rich gated communities through the glitzy skyscraper-laden downtown and on to downtrodden neighborhoods, backwoods swamps, and laid-back island beach communities.
As nice as Vice City’s outdoor architecture is, GTA VI’s interiors are where the game’s developers really show off. Practically every story mission seems to introduce a new cavernous indoor space that’s fully furnished and lovingly crafted to look naturally lived-in and also utterly unlike anything you’ve seen before. And while you can’t go into every one of the thousands of buildings you pass on the streets of Vice City, you can enter a surprisingly large number, each with its own distinct layout and decorations.
I dare you to try to count the number of people in this scene.
Credit:
Rockstar
I dare you to try to count the number of people in this scene.
Credit:
Rockstar
Another element that makes all these spaces feel lived-in is the game’s surprisingly detailed crowd system. Grand Theft Auto VI sometimes packs over a hundred non-player characters into a single space, with no two characters looking or acting alike in size, shape, dress, or animation. Working your way through these crowds can be integral to some of the game’s missions, but even when you’re just casually exploring, it’s fun to take advantage of eavesdropping opportunities, listening in on individual conversations that build into overlapping chatter (realistically muffled through walls and over distance).
Grand Theft Auto VI’s spaces also seem specifically designed to show off the game’s incredible lighting system, which really shines on a PS5 Pro. The effect is most apparent at night, when car headlights streaming through a window or the rotating blue-and-red of a cop car can cast the entire world in an otherworldly glow.
But even in “normal” lighting conditions, I’d occasionally find myself slack-jawed at the details: a laptop screen partially reflected in a character’s glasses, the way rotating pyrotechnic laser effects played across dancers in a crowded club, the fluttering shadows cast by a leafy tree near sunset, or the finger smudges visible on your cell phone in bright sunshine.
Dance Floor Jason is activated by purple light.
Rockstar
Dance Floor Jason is activated by purple light.
Rockstar
Just another day in paradise.
Rockstar
Just another day in paradise.
Rockstar
Look at that headlight halo. Just look at it!
Rockstar
Look at that headlight halo. Just look at it!
Rockstar
Just another day in paradise.
Rockstar
Look at that headlight halo. Just look at it!
Rockstar
I know we said we wanted to shoot your photograph in natural light, but maybe we could go somewhere different?
Rockstar
Check out those long shadows as the sun gets low.
Rockstar
I could watch these clouds crawl across the sky all day.
Rockstar
#nofilter
Rockstar
I could go on and on about the little “attention to detail” touches that add up to a more engaging world simulation. Characters who fall in the dirt get dust on only the specific parts of their clothes that hit the ground. Older characters look distinctly wrinkly, with veins that show through their thinning skin. Fabric and hair flow naturally in the wind and as characters move. Rain beads on car roofs and drips off overhangs during a storm.
Through it all, one moment really stood out to me. As I prepared for an upcoming firefight, I had Lucia start eating some chips to buff her health. Halfway through the bag, I had her pick up a nearby soda, too. At first, Lucia held the chip bag in one hand and used the other to pick out individual chips. But once that other hand was occupied with a soda, she started shaking the bag above her head to pour the chips directly into her mouth.
When I thought about the effort that went into coding and recording that specific animation for such a highly specific edge case, I thought about the millions of man-hours that went into making Grand Theft Auto VI the ultimate expression of this kind of urban crime/life sim. It might be a long time before we see this level of focused effort on a singular interactive vision again.
Kyle Orland has been the Senior Gaming Editor at Ars Technica since 2012, writing primarily about the business, tech, and culture behind video games. He has journalism and computer science degrees from University of Maryland. He once wrote a whole book about Minesweeper.
E.g. light gets distorted when it passes through the water in (some) drinking vessels, open glass doors show the reflection of things which are not currently visible to the player, hair looks and moves realistically, etc.
Lots and lots of ray tracing and complex physics, all running in realtime at 30ps on a six-year old platform with the (rough) equivalent of a 2-year old mid-range GPU bolted onto it.
View: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ULM2OIj5o0I
GTA6 may look like a high-end CGI rendering, but the breadth of what they're achieving within that game engine is impressive, and goes a long way to explaining both the time and cost needed to build GTA6.

articles.title: Vero Security Raises $11 Million for AI Security Engineering Platform
articles.text:
Vero Security, founded in 2025 by IDF 8200 alumni Elad Tessler (CEO) and Daniel Meirov (CTO), has raised $11 million in a seed funding round led by TLV Partners. The firm is building a platform for AI Security Engineering (ASE) – the process of securing AI tools and agents – and will use the funding to advance the platform and grow its go-to-market presence in the United States.
AI Security Engineering is a new, and as yet ill-defined, security discipline. Its purpose is to secure the AI tools and agents that are increasingly being adopted, used, and modified in-house by company employees. This is happening at pace and volume – so the object of ASE is a moving target; and is a security requirement that is different to and separate from cybersecurity.
ASE policy is defined by security teams. Vero turns these policy definitions into enforced controls, automatically updates them as the AI tools evolve, and refers only those enforcement decisions that require a human judgement to the security team.
Vero’s idea is to bring a new approach to securing AI. “CISOs have seen enough dashboards and tables that tell their teams what’s wrong and leave the work to them. AI Security Engineering deserves a better operating model, designed for AI rather than borrowed from other areas of security,” commented Elad Tessler, Co-Founder and CEO of Vero Security. “We’re working alongside the first generation of AI security leaders and building Vero around what they actually need: a platform that does the work, keeps protections current as AI changes, and brings them only the decisions that require human judgment.”
The core technology within the platform is Vero’s AI Runtime Governor. It puts security decisions into effect as AI operates, enforcing approved policies and blocking agent actions that trigger unauthorized behavior. If a change requires a new risk decision, Vero brings the analysis and recommended action to the responsible security professional.
In parallel with developing its AI Security Engineering platform, Vero is establishing AISecurityEngineering.org, an open community and knowledge center featuring practical field guides, workshops and the ASE credential track. ASE is new, rapidly growing, and different to existing mainstream cybersecurity.
“Our own weekly count of open roles titled ‘AI Security Engineer’ went from 367 on 25 October to 451 on 14 November, up 23% in three weeks,” Tessler told SecurityWeek. “Demand is arriving before the discipline has been written down.”
He added, “Security disciplines that have lasted, like AppSec and detection engineering, grew a shared body of knowledge before they had standard job titles. AI Security Engineering needs that too, and right now!”
Vero is bringing order to the evolving and disorganized security requirement of AI Security Engineering. While the new open community will help to define and establish the discipline, Vero’s own platform will assist the ASE role to perform the operational work.
“The Vero platform undertakes the impossible part of the ASE work, leaving the human engineer in situ to make judgement calls where necessary,” explained Tessler. The impossible part is the volume (dozens of tool changes every week, each one mapped to every control they touch), and tempo (agents act in seconds, so defenses must be in place before the action, not reviewed after it) of AI tool changes. “The human part is deciding what the business will accept, which exceptions make sense, and when a new tool is worth the risk.”
“We’re betting on more AI security engineers, not fewer,” said Tessler, “which is why we’re building AISecurityEngineering.org to train them. Without Vero, keeping up with AI in a large company takes a team. With it, one person, or a security leader taking it on alongside their job, can stay ahead.”
Vero is adding flesh to a newly emerging security requirement: AI Security Engineering. The Vero platform and AI Runtime Governor automates much of the mechanics of securing AI tools and agents used in-house, by continuously discovering, assessing and securing enterprise AI. Additionally, launching the separate AISecurityEngineering.org open community will help establish a body of subject knowledge to sustain and grow the new discipline.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.text:
Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
By treating qubits like individual molecules, scientists can now predict their behavior faster and more accurately
- Date:
- November 13, 2026
- Source:
- Princeton University
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.
- Share:
A new computational technique could accelerate the search for diamond materials capable of powering future quantum computers and highly sensitive sensors. Developed by a researcher at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the method makes it much easier to identify promising materials for quantum technology, potentially opening the door to advances across many areas of science.
The approach has already revealed new candidates for quantum computing and sensing applications. The findings were recently published in ACS Central Science and have attracted attention from other researchers in the field.
One of the biggest challenges in developing quantum technology is finding materials that can maintain delicate quantum states under practical conditions. Many candidates require extremely low temperatures to function reliably. Diamond materials stand out because certain quantum properties can remain useful even at room temperature.
This capability could help advance technologies that are important to national research priorities and the development of next-generation computing. Quantum sensors promise levels of sensitivity and precision beyond those of conventional instruments, while quantum computers could eventually solve certain extraordinarily complex problems much faster than today's most powerful supercomputers.
Why Imperfect Diamonds Could Be the Key to Quantum Computing
Although diamonds are made of carbon atoms, a flawless diamond crystal is not enough to create a useful quantum computing system. The key lies in tiny irregularities within the crystal structure.
These imperfections, known as defects, can occur when a carbon atom is absent from its normal position, when another element replaces a carbon atom, or when both changes occur together. The atoms surrounding these defects can form qubits, the basic units used to store and process quantum information in quantum computers and sensors.
Finding the most useful defects, however, has been difficult. Accurately modeling their quantum behavior traditionally requires enormous computational resources, making it challenging to evaluate large numbers of possible candidates.
A Simpler Way to Discover Better Diamond Qubits
Mark Martirez, a staff research scientist at PPPL, developed a way to dramatically reduce the complexity of these calculations. Instead of simulating a much larger diamond structure, he isolates a small region containing just 16 to 30 atoms around a defect.
By "carving out" this tiny atomic cluster and treating it like a separate molecule, Martirez can use powerful computational methods that chemists have spent decades refining. These established techniques make it possible to analyze the quantum properties of diamond defects much more efficiently without sacrificing the high level of accuracy needed for the calculations.
"Because we're treating the qubits as molecules, the cost of calculating these defects is equivalent to the cost of just modeling a simple molecule," Martirez said. "This method really opened the floodgates" in terms of how qubits can be assessed.
The new technique allows researchers to calculate how different qubits respond to laser light and microwave pulses far more quickly than before. Using this approach, the team identified promising defects involving boron and oxygen that could serve as new types of qubits.
New Diamond Defects Reveal a Spectrum of Quantum Colors
Light plays an important role in how scientists interact with diamond qubits. Researchers use lasers and microwave pulses to manipulate their quantum states and retrieve stored information.
Much of the previous work in this area has centered on a defect known as the nitrogen-vacancy center. This structure forms when a nitrogen atom takes the place of a carbon atom in a diamond crystal, while an adjacent position that would normally contain another carbon atom remains empty.
Under laser illumination, this type of defect can emit red light when it occupies a particular quantum state.
The newly investigated defects offer different optical properties. Oxygen defects can produce blue light, while those involving boron emit ultraviolet light.
These differences could make it possible to combine several types of qubits within a single quantum device. Because each type responds differently to light, researchers might be able to interact with one group of qubits without disturbing another.
"One could imagine, then, combining different qubits of different responses, so you can basically probe one qubit but not the other," Martirez said.
Beyond identifying new candidates, the findings suggest a broader change in how researchers approach quantum technology. Diamond qubits have traditionally been studied primarily through physics, but understanding their underlying chemistry could provide additional ways to design them.
Martirez believes that researchers could eventually engineer qubits for particular functions using principles similar to those applied when chemists create specialized molecules, including compounds designed for new medications.
How Quantum Chemistry Could Transform Future Research
The potential benefits extend well beyond the development of quantum computers themselves. Martirez sees an intriguing possibility in which advances made possible by quantum chemistry eventually lead to quantum technologies that help improve the field of chemistry.
In other words, quantum chemistry could develop the very tools needed to "enrich itself" in the coming decades.
A practical quantum system containing multiple qubits could make molecular calculations substantially more accurate. That would allow scientists to study increasingly complex chemical structures, including large biological molecules and proteins, with a level of detail that is difficult to achieve using conventional methods.
"We could describe larger molecules, biomolecules, proteins and everything like that in a more accurate way, and that could improve all the chemical-adjacent industries, such as pharmaceutical science and materials science. Even our fundamental understanding of molecular systems could be enriched."
Such improvements could have far-reaching implications for pharmaceutical development, materials research, and the fundamental study of how molecules behave.
Martirez also hopes the research will encourage more chemists to explore solid-state physics. Although building advanced quantum computers is often viewed as a challenge primarily for physicists, he argues that chemistry offers valuable expertise that could help accelerate progress.
"At this moment in time, there's a great emphasis on building the first state-of-the-art qubit computer," he said. "But it's not just physicists who should be participating in this research. Chemists have decades of developed intuition about chemical systems that could be easily translated into understanding defects in solids as well."
By bringing these disciplines together, scientists may be able to develop more effective ways to discover, understand, and eventually engineer the quantum materials needed for future technologies.
The research was funded through PPPL's Laboratory Directed Research and Development program under prime contract number DE-AC02-09CH11466, with additional support from the DOE Office of Science, Office of Fusion Energy Sciences.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Princeton University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- John Mark P. Martirez. A Chemist’sGuide to Solid-State Qubits: DiamondColor Centers as Embedded Vacancy-Centered Molecules. ACS Central Science, 2026; 12 (10): 1578 DOI: 10.1021/acscentsci.6c00548

articles.title: GTA VI llegó con casi la nota máxima de la crítica y 16 millones de reservas estimadas
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI, el videojuego más esperado de los últimos años, salió con una nota de 99 sobre 100 en Metacritic, el sitio que promedia reseñas de la prensa y con unas 16 millones de reservas, según estimaciones de la firma Sensor Tower.
Sensor Tower calculó que el juego ya había generado unos USD 1.540 millones en preventas Los analistas sostienen que podría superar los récords de ventas de GTA V, aunque ninguna de esas cifras fue confirmada por Rockstar Games, la desarrolladora.
El lanzamiento es escalonado: comenzó en Nueva Zelanda y avanza por zonas horarias, porque el juego se habilita a medianoche local del 19 de noviembre en todos los países.
Solo se vende para PlayStation 5 y para Xbox Series X y S. Las copias en caja traen un código de descarga y no un disco, según la BBC. La versión estándar cuesta USD 79,99 y la edición Ultimate, USD 99,99.
Dos calificaciones de GTA VI perfectas entre los críticos
Cuando terminó el plazo que Rockstar fijó para publicar reseñas, el puntaje de Metacritic salió de 114 críticas. IGN y GameSpot le pusieron 10 sobre 10, y Giant Bomb, cinco estrellas. El crítico de IGN Luke Reilly lo llamó el “videojuego más impresionante” que jugó.
GameSpot sí marcó un reparo: ciertas exigencias para avanzar interrumpen a veces el ritmo de la historia. Los críticos de The New York Times y Polygon destacaron la relación entre los dos protagonistas y la sátira de la sociedad estadounidense.
En The Verge, Andrew Webster dijo haber pasado casi 80 horas en Leonida, la versión ficticia de Florida donde transcurre el juego. Los protagonistas, Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos, son dos delincuentes de poca monta inspirados en la pareja de Bonnie y Clyde.
Webster señaló fallas: el combate sigue siendo torpe, la rueda de armas lo hizo equipar una linterna en lugar de una escopeta y vio errores menores, como un cadáver que se sacudía. Aun así, escribió que en una consola PS5 de lanzamiento el juego funcionó bien.
También, describió un sistema de puntos de control que reduce la repetición de escenas tras un fracaso, y la posibilidad de saltar una misión si el jugador falla demasiadas veces.
Lo que conviene saber antes de jugar GTA VI
GTA V vendió más de 230 millones de copias en 13 años, una cifra que explica la expectativa por la secuela, que además pasó por filtraciones y retrasos antes de llegar a las tiendas.
Quien reservó el juego digital puede descargarlo antes de la hora de salida. Polygon calculó que hacen falta 212 GB libres, más 1 GB para la primera actualización. El juego no permite partidas cruzadas entre PlayStation y Xbox y se limita a 30 cuadros por segundo en todas las consolas.
Es una experiencia para un solo jugador. GTA Online, el modo multijugador, funciona por separado, según Polygon.
Rockstar no ha anunciado una fecha para la versión de computadora.
Campañas de fraude por el lanzamiento de GTA VI
ESET advirtió sobre campañas de fraude y malware que aprovechan la expectativa por el lanzamiento de GTA VI, con sitios falsos que prometen accesos anticipados, versiones beta, descuentos o copias filtradas del videojuego.
Mario Miucci, investigador de Seguridad Informática de ESET Latinoamérica, afirmó que circularon supuestas imágenes del nuevo título en internet, pero que no existen pruebas de una versión auténtica y jugable que haya sido filtrada. “Lo que sí encontraron fueron campañas de malware diseñadas para aprovechar la demanda”.
Según la empresa de ciberseguridad, algunas campañas imitan la comunicación oficial de Rockstar Games, mientras otras ofrecen archivos que aparentan contener el juego completo. También detectaron tiendas online fraudulentas que comercializan productos inexistentes, como accesos anticipados, betas o reservas exclusivas.
La telemetría de ESET identificó miles de dominios vinculados con términos relacionados con GTA 6 o que suplantan la identidad de Rockstar. Parte de esos sitios reúne información de fanáticos, aunque otros pueden buscar obtener dinero, datos bancarios o credenciales de acceso de los usuarios.
“Los estafadores aprovechan esta familiaridad para hacer que las ofertas inexistentes parezcan creíbles”, explicó Miucci. Las páginas pueden utilizar logotipos, imágenes inspiradas en Vice City, autos de lujo y contenido generado con inteligencia artificial, junto con mensajes de urgencia o exclusividad.
Las recomendaciones para evitar estafas con GTA VI
ESET recomendó comprar el juego solo en comercios reconocidos y plataformas oficiales, sin ingresar desde enlaces de anuncios, redes sociales o correos electrónicos. También, aconsejó desconfiar de rebajas excesivas, contadores regresivos y mensajes que alertan sobre un supuesto stock limitado, ya que las copias digitales no se agotan.
Antes de pagar, conviene verificar los datos de contacto, las condiciones de venta y la política de devoluciones de la tienda. La compañía sugirió evitar criptomonedas, tarjetas de regalo u otros medios sin protección al comprador.
Rockstar anunció GTA VI para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, sin beta, demo ni acceso anticipado. Por eso, una oferta para PC o dispositivos móviles debe considerarse una señal de alerta.

articles.title: Google's AI feature in Search gets its own incognito mode | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s search engine has long offered an incognito mode for all those search queries you don’t want logged or associated with your account. Now, Google’s AI Mode in Search is getting a similar feature. In a blog post, the company announced a new feature that brings “temporary threads” to AI Mode, where the conversations you have won’t be resurfaced later in areas like your search history or recommendations.
Many leading AI chatbots already offer the option for temporary chats, Google Gemini included. However, there was not yet an option to have a temporary chat when you’re searching Google and are dropped into its conversational interface, known as AI Mode.
Google says that users won’t have to adjust their settings to take advantage of the new option. Instead, they’ll be able to click a temporary threads icon in the upper right corner of AI Mode to engage in a temporary chat. This essentially works the same as a temporary chat would in the stand-alone Gemini chatbot.
The option could be convenient to use at those times when you start digging deeper into a particular topic via AI Mode and realize that you don’t want the discussion to become a part of your search history because of its personal nature.
Once the temporary thread is started, the session becomes detached from your account, Google says. This means that the responses the AI provides won’t be informed by past preferences, nor will they impact future personalization. That could also be useful for those times when you want to learn about something as more of a one-off, but don’t want Google to start to think of the topic as one of your main interests.
When you close out of the thread, you will return to searching as usual.
The company says the option to engage in temporary chats in AI Mode is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile across all supported languages.

articles.title: Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are spreading malware through dark web scam bundle, NordVPN warns
articles.text:
Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are spreading malware through dark web scam bundle, NordVPN warns
A plug-and-play cybercrime kit targets eager PC gamers with cookie stealers, crypto drainers, and hidden miners
- NordVPN discovered a fake GTA 6 kit spreading malware on the dark web
- The scam exploits the lack of an official PC release date
- Rockstar is releasing GTA 6 only on consoles on November 19
Scammers are preparing to cash in on the massive hype surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 with ready-to-run malware packs sold on the dark web.
Discovered by NordVPN’s Threat Intelligence team on November 16, the toolkit is built to fleece eager gamers just days before the game's November 19 console launch.
The illicit package costs $200, payable only in Bitcoin or Tether. That flat fee gives entry-level crooks everything they need to start stealing data without writing code.
While setting up the best VPN protects your connection on public networks, software tools cannot stop you from opening an infected file yourself. Security researchers have already warned that cybercriminals are using GTA 6 hype to spread malware, and this new listing lowers the barrier to entry.
"We’ve been watching scammers use GTA 6 for months, but this is a different level," says Marijus Briedis, CTO at NordVPN. "Someone has packaged the whole scam and is selling it to anyone with $200. You don’t need any technical skills anymore. Criminals can just buy the kit and wait for launch day."
NordVPN – the best VPN overall 
NordVPN came out on top in our 2026 round of VPN tests. We think it's the best VPN for most people. We’re confident that virtually anyone can sign up for NordVPN and get what they need from it. It’s easy to use, very secure, fast enough for gaming, and offers flawless streaming service unblocking.
Subscriptions start from $3.49 per month, and you can try it out risk-free with a 30-day money-back guarantee.
How the fake GTA 6 PC port scam works
Every piece of the bundle uses a fake PC release as bait. GTA 6 is arriving strictly on consoles, leaving PC players waiting without a confirmed launch date.
"People who play on PC have been waiting for news, and any link promising an early PC version will get clicks," says Briedis. "There is no PC version on November 19. If you see one, it's a scam."
The kit contains multiple traps. It includes a crypto wallet drainer that targets Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, and Polygon networks, netting sellers an estimated $100 to $500 per drained wallet.
Victims who download the payload get hit with a cookie stealer disguised as "GTA6 Keygen.exe". This program grabs browser session tokens to take over accounts without needing passwords. The kit also installs XMRig to secretly mine cryptocurrency in the background, while an automated bot pushes links on YouTube Shorts to drum up traffic.
Industry reports confirm that fake GTA 6 malware is on the rise. Criminals recognize that scammers do not need to break into Rockstar to steal your details; they simply exploit consumer impatience.

Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.

How to avoid GTA 6 launch day malware
Does using an antivirus or privacy app stop you from losing your money? Not if you manually approve a transaction or willingly run an unverified installer.
Steer clear of any site offering a GTA 6 PC build. Rockstar has not published a PC version of the game. Any file, torrent, or archive claiming to deliver a playable PC port is malicious.
Never run key generators or cracks. Files labelled with names like "GTA6 Keygen.exe" deliver malware rather than game access. Buy your games only through the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, or Rockstar's platform.
Keep crypto wallets disconnected from unknown domains. A video game installer will never require access to Web3 assets. If your computer fans spin at top speed or your machine stutters while idle, open Task Manager and run a scan to detect rogue miners.

articles.title: Supercomputing needs rack-scale management, Dell says - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Scripts can’t run AI factories: Dell moves cluster management from the server to the rack
As artificial intelligence clusters grow to supercomputing scale, the hard part of the AI factory is no longer buying hardware. It is keeping racks, switches, GPUs and cooling running once they are switched on.
That operational burden is reshaping what infrastructure providers sell. Dell Technologies Inc. has spent the past year pushing its AI Factory beyond servers and storage, and customers are now asking for best practices and better tools to stand up and run what they buy, according to Andrew Vaz (pictured, left), vice president of product management for the Telecom Systems Business at Dell.
“What we are seeing is a fundamental shift from procuring supply to actually standing up and running these very complicated AI clusters and data centers,” Vaz said. “One of the interesting things that we’ve seen is it’s actually now impossible to manage these things with just a few scripts, manually, in an old world manner. The toolsets are becoming more important.”
Vaz and Saurabh Kapoor (right), director of product management and strategy for AI compute and networking solutions at Dell, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed supercomputing, rack-scale management, AI observability and why networking sits on the critical path for AI clusters. (* Disclosure below.)
Rack-scale management for the supercomputing era
Dell used the conference to introduce Dell OpenManage Rack Scale and Dell Fabric Manager, two tools for running AI infrastructure from deployment through daily operations. OpenManage Rack Scale manages 100,000 devices in its first release, up from 8,000 servers for its predecessor, OpenManage Enterprise, Kapoor explained. Systems such as Nvidia Corp.’s NVL72 racks bundle compute, power shelves, switches and coolant distribution units into one unit.
“OpenManage Enterprise, the previous product we had, was perfect for servers. Server was the unit of compute,” Kapoor said. “But you have seen in the last 18 months, the world has moved very quickly to larger ecosystems and infrastructures. Rack is the new unit of play.”
Visibility is the other half of that equation. Dell’s iDRAC controller pulls more than 320 metrics from every server, and an AI-assist chatbot can query that telemetry through local large language models, according to Kapoor. A single cooling leak can damage millions of dollars of gear, so every layer has to report in, Vaz noted.
“It could be something as simple as, ‘Hey, this transceiver’s about to die that you can’t diagnose with metrics you have today,'” Vaz said. “You need to use AI to go look at it. You need telemetry off the system to go collect all of that, correlate it, run your algorithms on them, train it and understand what’s happening.”
The network is where those pressures concentrate. Dell Fabric Manager turns validated designs built with Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. into deployable blueprints across different network operating systems and silicon. Agentic AI is also reshaping traffic, and enterprise bandwidth is outrunning a projected 3.5-fold increase, Vaz noted.
“We’re getting blown away by it. It’s more like nine to 10x,” Vaz said. “It’s going everywhere: east, west, north, south.”
