articles.title: Absolute Batman can save DC Studios
articles.text:
With James Gunn and Peter Safran out as the co-heads of DC Studios following Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, it’s unclear what will become of the cinematic universe that was building around movies like last year’s Superman. Though Gunn’s Man of Tomorrowfeature might still come out, it seems like his larger vision for the DC Universe may be tossed out by DC Studios’ newly appointed CEO, Jeremy Latcham. Gunn was taking his time fleshing out the DCU with relatively less high-profile characters like Peacemaker, Supergirl, and Clayface. But Latcham has reportedly received a mandate from Skydance CEO David Ellison to fast-track a new version of the Justice League featuring more popular heroes like Wonder Woman and the Green Lantern.
Absolute Batman can save DC Studios
Skydance’s cinematic superhero universe could get back on track through DC’s progressive Absolute Universe comics.
This drastic shift in priorities will likely change what the DCU looks like in the coming years as Skydance attempts to parlay its comics IP into projects that can help it get on top of the $80 billion of debt the company is now responsible for after acquiring WBD. Ellison’s instinct to whip out the A-list superheroes is probably right from a business perspective. Most casual DC movie fans are more interested in stories about the Trinity than obscure characters like Gorilla Grodd. But after two iffy attempts at creating interconnected DC movie franchises, that audience might not have much of an appetite for yet another full-on reboot.
Rather than starting from scratch, DC Studios should probably keep some of the things that worked well during Gunn and Safran’s tenure, like presenting Superman as a compassionate person with a strong moral compass. But if the studio really wants to take this franchise in a new direction that gets people excited, it should also be thinking about tapping into the energy of some of DC’s most successful recent comics. Though the WBD merger prompted Skydance to begin laying off almost 2,000 employees last month, DC Comics — which Skydance gained control of as part of the deal — was reportedly left unscathed because the publishing arm’s business has been performing surprisingly well. Much of that success seems to have been driven by strong sales of comics created by DC’s Absolute Universe imprint.
Launched in 2024, the Absolute Universe comics reimagine DC’s heroes and villains as wildly different versions of their classic selves. Absolute Wonder Woman is a witch raised in Hell, Absolute Superman first arrives on Earth as a teenager who remembers his childhood on Krypton, and Absolute Batman is a working-class civil engineer rather than a socialite born into immense wealth. The Absolute characters’ worldviews and approaches to enacting justice are all distinct from their mainstream universe counterparts. But as much as the Absolute comics diverge from established canon, they each capture the essence of what makes their central characters iconic pillars of the DC brand.
Wonder Woman aside, there have been so many cinematic portrayals of DC characters based on their classic selves that it has often seemed like Warner Bros. was stuck in a kind of rut. There have been slight stylistic differences between the various big-screen iterations of Superman and Batman over the years, but for the most part, they have all come across as the products of a studio that’s averse to trying new things.
Absolute Batman is compelling because it inverts the established power structures that define most classic Batman comics.
That’s part of what made Matt Reeves’ The Batman— which didn’t bother to rehash Bruce Wayne’s tragic origin story — feel somewhat like a breath of fresh air when it debuted in 2022. Robert Pattinson will reprise his role as the Dark Knight in The Batman Part II, but it’s not really clear whether that version of the character will have any bearing on the DCU’s future.
Between Reeves’ Batman films existing in their own universe (similar to Todd Phillips’ Joker features) and Pattinson presumably being busy now that he’s been cast as Amazon’s new James Bond, it doesn’t seem likely that that version of the character will be incorporated into the DCU. Ellison obviously intends to put out more projects featuring Batman, though, and DC Studios could tell a riveting story if it took some cues from the hero’s Absolute incarnation. What makes Absolute Batman such a compelling series is the way it inverts the established power structures that define most classic Batman comics. In those books, Bruce Wayne is part of Gotham’s marginalized underclass, while the Joker is a moneyed elite whose villainy is highlighted in the way he manipulates various industries.
This inversion puts Absolute Batman in a position to operate as a vigilante with a much deeper connection to the ordinary people he has sworn to protect. Monstrous supervillains like Poison Ivy and Bane are still major threats, but the comics also spend time pitting Absolute Batman against more ordinary evils like corrupt police departments infested with white nationalists fixated on terrorizing minorities. Absolute Batman’s progressive political overtones might not gel with Ellison’s personal sensibilities, and the comic’s brutality probably doesn’t align with Latcham’s approach to making films. But Absolute Batman’s phenomenal sales have made it abundantly clear that readers are enjoying these stories, which is likely a big part why DC Studios announced earlier this year that it has plans to produce an animated series based on the comics.
Those plans might change in the wake of Skydance acquiring WBD, but an Absolute Batman series would give DC Studios an organic way to introduce the character into its tentpole films. Having characters jump back and forth between TV and the big screen was one of the stronger ideas Gunn introduced to the DCU, and it’s a strategy that could continue to benefit DC Studios under Latcham’s leadership. Turning Absolute Batman into the next flagship Bruce Wayne would be a bold move on Skydance’s part. But if the studio really wants to prove that this megamerger was the right decision, it needs to show the public that it has the guts to take exciting chances.

articles.title: Actualiza ya tu PS5 o 'GTA 6' no arrancará, confirma Sony
articles.text:
GTA 6 ya está llegando a los países que cruzaron la barrera de la medianoche y ya transitan el tan anhelado 19 de noviembre. Para muchos otros, todavía faltan algunas horas para que puedan poner sus manos sobre el anhelado juego de Rockstar Games, cuyas primeras reseñas son tan positivas como se esperaba (y tal vez más). Pero mucho ojo si planeas jugarlo desde una PS5, pues antes de ejecutarlo tendrás que instalar sí o sí una actualización de sistema.
Sony ha lanzado un parche de software para la PS5 que es obligatorio si quieres acceder a GTA 6. Se trata de la actualización de firmware 26.07-14.23.00, que pesa casi 1,3 GB. La misma inició su despliegue en la mañana de ayer. No obstante, no fue hasta bien entrada la madrugada europea de hoy que se confirmó que su instalación era un requisito ineludible para acceder a Grand Theft Auto VI.
Los motivos oficiales detrás de la actualización de la PS5 antes del debut de GTA 6 apuntan solamente a la resolución de fallos de seguridad. Se especula con que Sony en realidad está tratando de cerrar cualquier puerta a posibles intentos de hackear el software de la consola y de piratear lo nuevo de Rockstar Games.
Si quieres jugar GTA 6, actualiza tu PS5 al firmware 14.23
La PS5 se ha convertido en noticia últimamente por los avances en jailbreaking que se han dado con el apoyo de IA generativa. En los últimos días, un hacker presumió de supuestamente dumpear el binario de un juego en una consola usando la versión 14.22 del firmware. ¿Esto qué significa? Que aparentemente pudo extraer los archivos originales de un videojuego, un paso crucial para piratearlo. Si bien no se brindaron más precisiones sobre la veracidad del caso, es lógico pensar que Sony ha tomado recaudos para evitar sorpresas desagradables con GTA 6.
Pese a la falta de detalles, se cree que Sony está cortando el acceso a PlayStation Network a las PS5 con firmware anterior a 14.23. De modo que si quieres acceder a GTA 6, no tienes otra alternativa más que instalar la actualización en cuestión en tu consola.
"Sony Interactive ha lanzado una actualización del software del sistema de PS5 que es necesaria para jugar a Grand Theft Auto VI. Los jugadores deben descargar esta actualización antes de la medianoche del 19 de noviembre para estar listos para jugar el día del lanzamiento", dice el escueto mensaje compartido en X (Twitter) a través de un perfil de soporte. La cuenta principal de PlayStation lo republicó con un emoji de ojos para llamar la atención de cualquier jugador desprevenido.
Si bien en buena parte de Occidente todavía restan algunas horas para que GTA 6 llegue a manos de los jugadores, muchos han optado por el viejo "truco de Nueva Zelanda" para reducir al mínimo posible la brecha de disponibilidad. Se espera que el 19 de noviembre tenga una de las tasas de ausentismo laboral más altas de la historia reciente. Un dato acorde con el lanzamiento más importante alguna vez visto en la industria de los videojuegos.

articles.title: Gemini-Nutzer können jetzt KI-Training untersagen, aber Verlauf behalten
articles.text:
Mehr Datenschutz bei Gemini: Nutzer können jetzt KI-Training untersagen, aber Verlauf behalten
Gemini-Nutzer:innen, die ihre Chats länger behalten wollten, stimmten damit bisher auch zu, dass Google diese Inhalte zum Training seiner KI-Modelle nutzt. Die entsprechende Einstellung ließ sich unter dem Menüpunkt „Aktivitäten speichern“ aktivieren.
Googles Datenschutz-Update bei Gemini
Wer dem KI-Training nicht zustimmen wollte, konnte die eigenen Chats nicht länger als 72 Stunden speichern lassen. Diese Zeit nahm sich Google für Antworten und „Sicherheitsmaßnahmen in Gemini“. Mit einem Update der Datenschutzeinstellungen der Gemini-App ändert Google diese Vorgehensweise jetzt grundlegend.
Auf der einen Seite sollen temporäre Chats und Chats mit deaktiviertem Verlauf künftig statt 72 Stunden etwa zwei Monate lang im Konto der Nutzer:innen gespeichert bleiben. Google erklärt das in seinem aktualisierten Privacy-Hub mit dem Schutz von Nutzer:innen und Öffentlichkeit sowie der Möglichkeit, zu antworten und Feedback zu verarbeiten.
Die längere Speicherzeit soll etwa sicherstellen, dass die Chats „im Falle eines Systemausfalls verfügbar sind“. Zudem soll Gemini sie bei Antworten als Kontext verwenden können. Warum dafür eine deutliche Ausweitung der Speicherzeit notwendig sein soll, erklärt Google nicht.
Datennutzung für KI-Training untersagen
Dafür schließt Google in seinen aktualisierten Datenschutzeinstellungen jetzt aus, temporäre Chats oder jene mit deaktiviertem Verlauf automatisch für das Training seiner KI-Modelle zu verwenden. Geben Nutzer:innen allerdings Feedback, kann Google die Chats der vergangenen 24 Stunden verwenden, um die Gemini-App entsprechend zu verbessern.
Dabei greift das Unternehmen nicht nur auf in den Chats enthaltenen Text, sondern auch auf mögliche Uploads oder Daten aus verbundenen Apps zu. Ähnliches gilt für die Speicherfunktion bei aktiviertem Verlauf. Die gespeicherten Chats enthalten dann etwa auch Audioaufnahmen, Gemini-Live-Videos und Bildschirmfreigaben, Prompts, Tasks und Toolaufrufe sowie Daten von besuchten Websites.
Außerdem geht es auch um den ungefähren Ort des für die KI-Chats genutzten Geräts, die IP‑Adresse sowie die im Google-Konto hinterlegten Privat- und Arbeitsadressen. Bei eingeschalteter History-Funktion (Verlauf) speichert Google die Daten bis zu 18 Monate. Mit der Aktualisierung ermöglicht es Google Nutzer:innen jetzt, selbst zu entscheiden, ob sie diese Daten für das KI-Training bereitstellen wollen oder nicht.
ChatGPT und Claude speichern kürzer
Die Konkurrenz setzt übrigens auf deutlich kürzere Speicherzeiträume, wie Techcrunch berichtet. Bei OpenAI werden temporäre Chats in ChatGPT für bis zu 30 Tage gespeichert. Denselben Zeitraum gibt auch Anthropic für Inkognito-Chats bei Claude an. Es ist allerdings möglich, dass beide KI-Anbieter einige Daten aus rechtlichen Gründen länger aufbewahren, etwa um Verstöße von Richtlinien zu untersuchen.
)))))) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
World model accuracy starts with high-quality, diverse training datasets. Yet capturing rare defects, nighttime incidents, and other challenging scenarios is costly and time-consuming. Turning raw data into training-ready datasets adds complexity, particularly when using disconnected tools and manual processes for curation, labeling, generation, and evaluation.
NVIDIA technology is helping developers more easily build high-quality, diverse training datasets at scale for physical AI. NVIDIA Cosmos is an open platform of frontier models, datasets, frameworks, and skills for world model development. As part of this platform, NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory (CDF) is a collection of five cloud-native blueprints and six composable skills to accelerate data curation, processing, and synthetic data generation (SDG). Frontier AI agents can be used to orchestrate these blueprints, enabling prompt-to-data without human steering.
This post walks you through how to curate and augment datasets or create anomalous events for physical AI model training with just two prompts in Cosmos. It features five different use cases.
Set up and configure Cosmos blueprints and skills: Prompt 1
Cosmos Data Factory contains five reference blueprints for common tasks. All five blueprints run using the CDF Orchestration core skill, which coordinates workflow steps, deploys the required services, and manages execution on your cluster.
To set it up, enter the following prompt into your coding agent:
| Example prompt: “Clone the CDF Orchestration repository, then run orchestration preflight and setup.” | 
|---|
Preflight checks your environment without making changes and flags anything missing. Once those checks pass, setup prepares your environment to run the blueprints.
Run the blueprint for your training data use case: Prompt 2
This section features five training data use cases for running the blueprint, including example prompts:
- Generate driving scenarios for autonomous vehicle (AV) training
- Augment image attributes for search and re-identification
- Augment videos across weather, lighting, and environments
- Generate rare event videos for model training
- Generate defect images for visual inspection
If you already have footage or images and need to curate and add more variety, the first use case in this section covers generating driving scenarios, varying clothing attributes in person images, and transforming videos across weather, lighting, and environmental conditions. The augmentation use cases expand the variety in your existing data, but some training gaps call for creating entirely new events or defects.
Your model might need to recognize a leaking product or a defective circuit board, but your dataset may contain few examples or none. Waiting to capture enough rare cases can take years, and staging them can be dangerous or expensive. The last two use cases cover generating rare event videos and defect images from images or 3D assets to fill these gaps.
Use case 1: Generate driving scenarios for AV training
The Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation blueprint helps you search large databases of driving scenarios and generate novel datasets for downstream model training and validation tasks. NVIDIA Cosmos Curator extracts metadata for your video dataset inputs, and NVIDIA Cosmos Dataset Search finds relevant videos through those embeddings. The retrieved videos are passed to NVIDIA Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video style transfer, and Cosmos Evaluator checks the generated videos for physical plausibility.
| Example prompt: “Search for driving scenes similar to our input video.mp4, transform them into rainy, snowy, and foggy while preserving layout and motion, and check physical plausibility.” | 
|---|
Use case 2: Augment image attributes for search and re-identification
The Image Attribute Augmentation reference blueprint generates variations of person-crops with controlled attribute changes such as clothing type, accessories, and color. An LLM turns your selected attributes into structured modification prompts, used to generate the augmented variations of the source image. Cosmos Evaluator confirms that the requested clothing attributes appear. The blueprint then auto-labels the results with clothing attributes and search queries for person search and re-identification.
| Example prompt: “Augment the person crops in <input-bucket>, three clothing variants per person, and write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
Use case 3: Augment videos across weather, lighting, and environments
The Video Data Augmentation reference blueprint transforms your existing footage across weather, lighting, and environmental conditions while preserving scene structure. A vision language model (VLM) describes your source video and combines that with your requested conditions into a structured prompt, which Cosmos3-Nano uses to generate the augmented variant.
Cosmos Evaluator checks each generated clip for motion artifacts that aren’t in your source, confirms that the conditions you asked for actually appear, and scores whether the motion is physically plausible. Next, the blueprint auto-labels both your source and generated videos with detection, tracking, and captions. It then provides you with a training-ready dataset.
| Example prompt: “Run video data augmentation on the videos in <input-bucket>, create 3 augmentations for yellow lighting, dim lighting and red table. Write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
Use case 4: Generate rare event videos for model training
The Event Video Generation reference blueprint uses a source image to create videos of rare events, such as fires, falls, or shoplifting. A VLM combines its description of your scene with your requested event into a structured prompt. Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video generates the clip while preserving the source viewpoint and layout.
Cosmos Evaluator checks whether the event appears and whether motion looks physically plausible, retrying failed clips. Passing clips are auto-labeled with detections, tracks, captions, and semantic annotations for downstream training.
| Example prompt: “Run the Event Video Generation blueprint on the image in <input-bucket> to generate 3 clips: normal traffic, stalled vehicle, and collision at the intersection. Write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
Use case 5: Generate defect images for visual inspection
The Defect Image Generation reference blueprint creates defective examples from clean inspection images or 3D USD assets of parts such as circuit boards, glass panels, or metal surfaces. For 3D assets, NVIDIA Isaac Sim renders inspection images and masks, and Qwen-Image-Edit creates realistic clean reference images, called golden images.
Cosmos 3 Super uses these images, defect masks, and your requested defect types to generate defects while preserving the surrounding part. It ships fine-tuned for printed circuit boards (PCBs), glass, and metal, with further fine-tuning skills available for other use cases. You get golden images, synthetic defect images, and manifests tracing each result to its source and generation settings.
| Example prompt: “Run the Defect Image Generation blueprint and generate shift structural defects for images in <input-bucket> with full board coverage. Write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
How to use core agent skills and tools for specific tasks like curation, search, and labeling
The blueprints outlined in the previous section are built from six core agent skills: Auto Labeling, AnomalyGen, Augmentation, Curation and Retrieval, Simulation, and Orchestration. You can use these skills independently or combine them to build a workflow around your own data and goals.
- Auto Labeling: Turns raw video and images into annotated datasets with detection, tracking, captions and scene understanding.
- AnomalyGen: Creates realistic defect images from a handful of examples, with masks, for visual inspection.
- Augmentation: Generates visual variations of your video and images using Cosmos models, for conditions you can’t capture.
- Curation and Retrieval: Finds clips and images in a large collection, using Cosmos Curator and Cosmos Dataset Search.
- Simulation: Renders photorealistic, fully labeled images from 3D scenes using Isaac Sim and Omniverse Replicator.
- Orchestration: Runs reference blueprints on your cluster, deploying the services each one needs and scaling them.
| Example prompt: Clone the auto labeling repo https://github.com/NVIDIA/cdf-auto-labeling/tree/main. Perform video auto-labeling to label my videos at <input-bucket>. Save outputs to <output-bucket>. Use the locally deployed model at <endpoint> for VLM and LLM.  | 
|---|
For workflows focused on curation and retrieval, use Cosmos Curator to process and auto-label raw video and multimodal data, and Cosmos Dataset Search to find targeted training scenarios across large datasets. Cosmos Curator now supports multicamera video, IMU, and GPS inputs, plus initial lidar support in its sensor library. Reusable Python processing components and Managed Ray on Slurm orchestration help teams connect sensor observations, test curation strategies, and use spare GPU capacity.
Planned expansion includes additional lidar devices, radar, and other sensor types. Cosmos Dataset Search, now open source under the Apache 2.0 license, combines metadata, scene semantics, spatial relationships, and temporal behavior through multi-embedding retrieval and adaptive agentic reranking (early access). Its modular APIs and agent skills retrieve relevant video segments for training datasets or the augmentation blueprints above.
Generate training data up to 60x faster and 45x cheaper
Cosmos Data Factory skills and blueprints turn hard-to-collect training data into a compute workload you control. The NVIDIA team measured daily throughput on a cloud server with eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Series GPUs at roughly $40 per server-hour, or $960 per day, then divided daily cost by output to estimate cost per asset.
- AV dataset generation: Generates ~130 edge-case clips/day at $2.66 in GPU compute per clip, about 45x cheaper than a fleet crew costing $125 per scenario collected on the road.
- Image attribute augmentation: Augments ~42,649 annotated image pairs/day at $960/day, or $0.023 per pair, about 10x cheaper than the $0.25 average for third-party purchased data.
- Video data augmentation: Augments ~305 annotated clips/day at $3.15 per ~5-minute clip, about 7x cheaper than the $22 average we’ve paid for third-party data.
- Defect image generation: Dropped dataset assembly time from two months to one day, a 60x speedup.
- Event video generation: Generates ~384 annotated clips/day at $2.50 each and ~4 minutes per clip, creating scarce training examples of fires, fights, and falls without waiting for or recreating dangerous real incidents.
With Cosmos, training gaps become generation jobs with a measurable compute budget. Note that these figures cover compute only; source data preparation, setup, agent use, storage, and human review may add costs.
What results and projected outcomes are organizations reporting with Cosmos?
Several organizations are using Cosmos skills and blueprints to improve testing, detection, and search accuracy across autonomous vehicles, visual inspection, and robotics while targeting lower costs and effort.
- Improving recall on real-world anomalies by up to 24% with synthetic data and estimated 1,400x return on data-generation cost at an offshore oil and gas site.
- Targeting up to 85% less manual engineering effort in automated optical inspection (AOI) program generation – with 40% fewer false calls.
- Reducing repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shortening AI regression test cycles by up to 85% (expected).
- Going to market in under two weeks with Cosmos Curator compared to an estimated six months (time required to build an equivalent pipeline in-house).
Get started with NVIDIA Cosmos
To accelerate data curation, processing, and synthetic data generation for your application, check out NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory blueprints and composable skills. Start with a blueprint that matches your use case, follow the setup guide, and use your AI agent to run the workflow with your data. Customize your pipeline with individual skills to generate high-quality, annotated training datasets.
To learn more, join us on November 19 for the livestream, Build Training-Ready Datasets in Two Prompts. Learn how to use Cosmos to curate and augment datasets for AVs, robotics, and vision AI agents. Featuring Voxel51 and Encord, the livestream will highlight how Porsche uses Cosmos Data Factory through the Voxel51 platform and how Encord worked with ANYbotics.

articles.title: Detachable Fiber Connectors Pose New Challenges For Photonics
articles.text:
Multiple designs are emerging for CPO and NPO, but standardization and high-volume manufacturing are still not ready.
Key Takeaways:
As photonics shifts from pluggable optical transceivers toward near- and co-packaged optics (NPO, CPO), engineers are devising new ways to attach fibers to the photonics chips on a board. Several different designs exist today, but so far there is no common interface.
With pluggable photonics, lasers and connections are attached at the server faceplate, with the board itself housing only electronic components. Yet long electrical connections to the faceplate mean higher power and longer latency. Fibers would need to move onto the interior of the board to solve that. That eliminates the need for pluggables, but it requires new solutions.
“With the rapid growth of generative AI, AI data centers are required to process enormous volumes of data faster and more efficiently than ever before,” said Yoshimasa Bando, principal scientist at Mitsubishi Chemical. “To meet this demand, further improvements in communication speed and energy efficiency have become critical challenges.”
The goal of CPO and NPO is to reduce reliance on long electrical connections.
Long lines
One reason for maintaining faceplate pluggables is that lasers are not always reliable. Using a pluggable module makes it easy to replace the laser.
“What we are focused on has the laser on the faceplate, because the laser is the highest reliability risk,” said Vishal Chandrasekar, director of product management at Ayar Labs.
All connections, whether they have a laser or not, happen in pluggable modules today. That means the signals those fibers carry must travel electrically from their origin to the edge of the board. Bandwidth necessitates serial lines driven by serializer/deserializer (SerDes) circuits. Driving those signals over that distance requires high power.
CPO aims to reduce system power by eliminating those long electrical lines and bringing fiber into the processor or switch packages. “CPO unlocks the token economics that everyone cares about,” said Chandrasekar. “The major bottlenecks are compute, memory, and moving data back and forth. If you’re trying to make step changes in hardware every one or two years, the way you make 5× or 10× kinds of improvements is by having new hardware. How do you use that hardware intelligently? How do I ensure that whatever hardware I have, I’m using it for the most important problem so my utilization is good?”
Fig. 1: With co-packaged optics, an optical engine is placed inside a package along with other chiplets. The laser remains outside the package for thermal reasons, and in the near term it will remain pluggable. Source: Bryon Moyer/Semiconductor Engineering
Photonics plays a key role in this effort. “You’re trying to reduce copper, so you’re trying to bring the PIC [photonic integrated circuit] closer to the processor or the switch,” said David Harame, COO at AIM Photonics, which operates with NY Creates (New York Center for Research, Economic Advancement, Technology, Engineering, and Science). “The industry is still very much using pluggables; you plug in the front panel. So there’s a lot of copper going between this [and the processor]. The next step is to move the optical transceiver closer to the switch by putting it on the PCB and reducing the copper line length to the switch. This is called near-packaged optics. Essentially, it moves the optical pluggable connector further inside the box on the PC board, so the optical-to-electrical connection takes place closer to the switch.
CPO is yet another variant of advanced packaging. “And all the challenges in advanced packaging are the same for co-packaged optics, except for fiber coupling and getting the PIC closer to the target chip,” noted Harame.
CPO receives the bulk of the near-term optical development efforts.
Fig. 2: In near-packaged optics, the optical components lie on the board near where their signals originate. Lasers will remain pluggable for now. Source: Bryon Moyer/Semiconductor Engineering
Unknown fiber length
Both CPO and NPO share the need to connect fiber directly to components on the board. One straightforward way is to attach a nominal length of fiber to the chip package and ship it that way, with the system integrator connecting the other end of the fiber directly to the destination.
The challenge there is that chip producers have no way of knowing how long that fiber will need to be. If it’s long enough for designs that require long runs, it will be too long for the many designs that don’t. That said, there are ways of dealing with extra fiber.
“The fiber goes into a fiber management tray, and there are spool points on the board,” said Nick Harris, CEO of Lightmatter. “They’re neatly managed for airflow.”
Others agree. “Usually, you’ll have some kind of excess fiber management,” explained Obie Roy, vice president, strategic commercial development at Senko. “But depending on the system that you’re building, you could cut it to length and terminate it once you know the exact application.”
Some engineers see this as a non-issue, which may be true if one is fusing the fibers or having the integrator attach a connector. “The fiber length is irrelevant,” said Professor Amr Helmy at the University of Toronto. “You connect a strand of fiber to the chip. With the other end, you can connectorize it, cut it, or fuse it with another fiber to make it longer. Fusing is one approach, but each one of these fibers can come with a connector depending on the amount of loss appetite you have.”
For ease of assembly, some means of attaching and detaching a fiber would also be helpful, such as a fixture or clip on the end to which another fiber can attach. But several considerations make this decision about more than simply adding wire connections as shown in the figures above.
Moving beyond the die edge
Today, fibers typically are placed using well-established V-groove technology, where the fibers exit out the side of a photonic chip. This attachment method works at low volumes and low total fiber counts, but it lacks the modularity and convenience needed for high-volume automation.
“The V-groove is a great concept, but the fibers are attached,” explained Gerard John, senior director, chiplets/FCBGA business unit at Amkor. “When being assembled onto a board, if one of them breaks, there’s no rework. People are generally thinking in terms of detachables and moving away from V-grooves.”
In addition, attachment space is bound by shoreline, which is essentially the real estate on the edge of the die. With metal connections, it might include the first few rows of bumps on the package, but fiber footprint is bigger and can chew up a lot of shoreline.
“The fiber diameter is 10 µm, but you have all the cladding around it, making it 125 µm,” John said. “So if you’re putting, let’s say, 16 cables like that, even if it’s staggered you will use a lot of real estate.”
Nevertheless, this is the predominant approach today. For example, Senko has put together a LEGO-like connector, with one part glued to the chip and the other attached to a fiber. This is one of many approaches underway at different companies.
There are three configurations for bringing fiber out (see figure 3, below). One takes the light from a waveguide, reflects it upward 90°, and sends it horizontally to a connector. These connectors would be situated around the periphery of the die.
Another is simply to run the waveguide to the edge of the die and have a connector butt up to the die to capture the light and route it to a fiber. The number of such connections is also determined by the perimeter.
A third approach moves the light vertically but then connects to the top surface rather than going out horizontally. This makes the entire area of the chip available for connections, providing more “shoreline” than the other two schemes.
“You have the waveguide shooting out laterally, and then it hits a mirror at a 45° angle,” said John. “It shoots upward, and once you get it upward, you put a connector with all the fibers on it.”
Fig. 3: The three ways of getting a waveguide signal into a fiber — horizontal-to-vertical-to-horizontal, fully horizontal, and horizontal-to-vertical. Source: Bryon Moyer/Semiconductor Engineering
But vertical approaches must avoid any heat sinks or other elements attached to the top. “When you send it vertically, you may get in the way of your thermal solution,” said Ravi Mahajan, fellow at Intel Foundry. “So if you have a solution that does both vertical and lateral, then you have more flexibility. In cases where thermal is a potential problem, go horizontal. In cases where you don’t worry about it, you can go vertical.”
The problem with pigtails
As depicted above, these connectors could be short pieces of fiber — pigtails — that are affixed firmly to the die and with some sort of clip connector at the end. A matching connector clip could then be plugged in to make the connection. Such a clip would likely cause some insertion loss, but if managed well, it can work. And it can be made to be sturdy.
“We have taken a part with a pigtail and banged it on the desk to convince a VP that it doesn’t come off,” said Mahajan. “We expose it to temperature cycles, to a little bit of moisture, and bake it for a long time, and it doesn’t come off.”
But the greater concerns are the high-volume manufacturing implications. Even without considering how the fiber attaches to the die, a more immediate question is how these chips would be packaged in bulk for test and delivery. The same issue holds for shipping a longer fiber and cutting it to order during integration.
Today, chips go into trays, and automated handling equipment can pick and place them onto boards or into test heads or anywhere else they’re needed. What happens if it’s no longer just a chip in the tray pocket, but potentially a chip wrapped with pigtails?
“If you have a pigtail, it’s very difficult to wrap that pigtail around and put it in a tray, and you probably won’t have many parts on the tray,” said John. “So our choice is to have a detachable connector, and it also makes sense from a manufacturing perspective.”
In addition, it is inconvenient to try to place a chip with pigtails into such a tray in an orderly, repeatable way. And then, when pulling the chip out of the tray, it will have dangling pigtails floating about, potentially interfering with whatever operation the equipment is attempting. Then, presumably, those pigtails would be manually connected.
This arrangement, while suitable at low volumes, may not work in high-volume production.
“I understand people being worried about a pigtail dangling off the edge, so we decided, ‘Why not just bring it to the edge of the die,’” said Mahajan. “Then an integrator just attaches it [to the fiber].”
Fig. 4: A fiber plugs into the side of a package. Source: Intel Foundry
Old habits change slowly, however. “Pigtails are probably still more common because people are trying to make incremental changes,” noted Sanjay Gangadhara, senior architect at Synopsys.
Scaling volumes also must address the assembly of any connector on the package. “Terminating a fiber is complex,” said Badri Gomatam, CTO of STL. “You’ve got to make it low cost, high yield, and repeatable. You’ve got hundreds of connections. No speck of dust can be allowed, and the assembly has to survive high-temperature reflow and all the other growth steps.”
Alignment concerns
One of the unique and challenging characteristics of photonics is that where two conductors meet, as much light as possible must get from one to the other. That applies to assembly and test.
Today, this is done through active alignment, where a tool measures the light exiting a waveguide and positions a fiber to maximize the captured light. This is a six-degree-of-freedom problem, where the aligner must be able to move in three linear dimensions as well as three angles of approach. It can take time.
With the pigtail configuration, presumably the clips would be designed to provide the alignment, but you still need to affix the stationary end of the pigtail during assembly. Given the downsides of pigtails, an alternative is to build the connector into the package itself. That way, nothing is hanging off the package, and it can be handled like other chips.
But alignment is still necessary. One method places a lens over the optical TSV to focus the light into an attached fiber while the other connection hardware aligns.
“One of the advantages when you have a lens is that, even if you do have some misalignment, the lens can correct for some of that because it’s focusing the light into a common region,” said Synopsys’ Gangadhara. “So this idea of using micro-optics, whether in a vertical-coupling or an edge-coupling architecture, is becoming more and more common.”
The Senko technique, for instance, provides passive mechanical fine alignment and restraint when snapped together. Roy explained that the snap-on structure provides the fine alignment, but you need something to hold it down. “We have screws and a structure that pushes it down into the fine alignment. This is the mechanical latching.”
It’s one thing to perform alignment during assembly, but it’s another to require it when attaching system fibers to the chip. Magnetic connectors, such as those used by Apple on iPhones, are being considered. Once the receiver end is built into the package, someone (or an automated handler) attaching the fiber must first align it roughly in place. From there, the magnet pulls it into the necessary precise location.
Unfortunately, some magnetic connectors are easily damaged. Any acceptable CPO fiber connection must be firm.
Stronger magnets could help, and this is an active area of development, possibly along with a mechanical restraint (such as Senko’s screws). What’s unclear, however, is how strong that magnetic field would be and whether it may adversely affect surrounding components such as MRAMs.
“When you design your system board, are you going to put sensitive memory close to these devices?” mused John.
As a result, any mechanical alignment would likely also be supplemented with a latch.
Serviceability and testability are critical
One way to connect fibers, common in long-haul optical applications, is to literally fuse them together. This permanent attachment method does not allow detachment, so it provides poor serviceability if a photonics chip fails.
“People have this concern about any kind of failure,” said Gangadhara. “How do you replace it? That serviceability part of the RAS requirement becomes a challenge.”
Serviceability, reliability, and availability make up the RAS feature that’s in high demand these days. It means components at greater risk of failure must be easy to replace, so you don’t have to throw out an entire expensive module or server.
“Once you attach a pigtail, if it gets damaged during shipment, the whole thing needs to be thrown out,” said John.
Roy agreed. “You need to make it detachable because if you permanently attach it and the fiber breaks, you have to fail the entire module out, which is very expensive,” he said.
Testing is heavily affected by these connector types, especially without standards. “An important aspect is making sure your solution is testable in real life,” noted Roy.
Addressing testability, especially for future high-volume manufacturing, means collaborating with test-equipment manufacturers. “We worked with Advantest and developed a test connector made out of tungsten carbide,” explained Roy. “It has the same bumps [as the LEGO-like connector] on the other side, and so it can come down, align precisely, and test very quickly. And you can scale it to test one at a time or a row of these things.”
Critically, the connection doesn’t require active alignment, saving test time. “We demonstrated 10,000 matings with very little variation in the loss [through the connection],” said Roy.
The connectors themselves must be reliable enough, but only up to a point. “Ideally, you’re not detaching and reattaching frequently,” noted Gangadhara. “If these things are up and running and working, then they’re running for thousands or tens of thousands of hours. Meta published a study last year where they had done serviceability/reliability analysis of some CPO devices, and they showed 10,000 hours of constant usage without any degradation of signal integrity or performance.”
Settling on a common design
Connector attachment is a textbook case of a development that needs standards so that any user can plug into anyone else’s photonics chip. At present, there are numerous pigtail-based designs and no standards. Likewise, no magnetic (or other) pigtail-less approach has been standardized or proven in high volumes. Customer requirements also appear to vary in ways that may make standardization difficult.
Consider the mechanical latching of Senko’s solution, for example. “Each of these parts is custom, depending on the ganging requirements and the mechanical sizes that are important to avoid — cooling plates and thermal elements and such,” Roy said. “Our vision is to take the receptacle part [that gets attached to the package], make that a common interface of the chip, and then sell the cover plate to any FAU manufacturer.”
For that to become an actual standard, however, typical licensing will presumably need to be reasonable and non-discriminatory (RAND). That’s a situation where different connector companies will work closely with photonics companies to find an approach that works functionally and is suited to high-volume manufacturing. That means compatibility with handling equipment.
These efforts will likely continue until standards (or at least multi-source agreements, or MSAs) are put in place, removing one major photonics volume barrier once the solution is established.

articles.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
articles.text:
This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
Osmo’s smell model is already being used in the fragrance industry. But are medical diagnostics and threat detection a sniff too far?
In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”
“Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”
In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.
Wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko says, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.
A lot of the company’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.
Mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko says. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.)
The company also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.
Osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo launched, later gave the company a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.
But not everyone is convinced by the technology or the company’s big claims. Avery Gilbert, a smell scientist and author of What the Nose Knows, has been sharply critical of Osmo on his Substack, arguing that some of its marketing claims are undocumented, and that its patent filings still rely on human sensory panels and perfumers, rather than AI. “This heavy reliance on human sensory judgments seems odd for a company premised on super-cool AI,” he wrote in March. A representative for Osmo did not respond in time for publication.
Michael Schmuker, a former professor of neural computation at the University of Hertfordshire who has previously consulted for Osmo, says the company’s technology is an achievement. With colleagues, he created an open-source, reverse-engineered version of Osmo’s 2023 model, but it lacks the reams of data the company has collected since.
But even with all this smell data, Osmo may be missing some of the factors that make human olfaction unique, Schmuker says. “Smell is super complex. Context is very important for smell. The same molecule may evoke a different association depending on context,” he says. “[The smell of] a French cheese like Camembert is partly the same molecule as in used nappies. You don’t confuse the two because of the context.”
In a controlled setting like a fragrance lab, this lack of context may not matter so much. But it could have an impact if Osmo’s technology becomes, as Wiltschko suggests, the “olfactive channel” for AI world models. Imagine a machine that could sniff out spoilage in food on a production line, or detect tumors through smell the way dogs have been trained to do in pilot studies.
For that to happen, sensor technology will need to get a lot better, Schmuker says. The models will need to keep improving. Medical diagnostics is the biggest prize.
“There’s a lot of history of companies that have gone directly at that mountain peak and, unfortunately, not been successful, because it is very expensive and it is very difficult,” Wiltschko says. "So what we’re doing is building this foundation at the foothills of all these mountains. We’re sending expeditions up to the mountains, doing explorations, and basically smelling the whole world.”

articles.title: WhatsApp veut vous faire oublier Google Drive, mais son offre gratuite risque de vous laisser sur votre faim
articles.text:
WhatsApp va bientôt proposer son propre espace de sauvegarde en ligne, avec 2 Go seulement à la clé.
Les développeurs de WhatsApp ne manquent pas d’inspiration pour améliorer leur produit. Récemment, ils ont créé un accès express aux médias récents, qui n’a pas reçu l’accueil escompté. Ils ont également testé un outil de retouche IA sur iPhone et lancé un réglage pour permettre aux utilisateurs d’avoir un meilleur contrôle sur la visibilité de leur numéro de téléphone. Un nouveau projet, déjà évoqué en avril dernier, prend enfin forme sur Android.
WhatsApp tourne le dos à Google Drive
WABetaInfo a repéré dans la version bêta 2.26.46.4 de WhatsApp une petite nouveauté qui devrait faire grand bruit : il est désormais possible de sauvegarder son historique d’échanges directement dans les serveurs de l’application. Pour l'instant seule une poignée de testeurs a accès à cette nouvelle fonctionnalité. Elle devrait être proposée plus largement dans les prochaines semaines. Aucune date précise n’a toutefois été dévoilée.
La nouvelle option se cache sur l’écran de sauvegarde des discussions : elle donne à l’utilisateur le choix d’utiliser Google Drive ou le stockage de WhatsApp. Ce dernier peut changer d’avis à tout moment.
WhatsApp mise plus que jamais sur la sécurité. Le chiffrement de bout en bout doit être activé dès la première copie et il est impossible de le désactiver. Le dispositif s’appuie sur une clé d’accès, mais on peut aussi passer par une clé de 64 chiffres, si cette solution ne nous convient pas. En procédant ainsi, ni WhatsApp ni Meta ne peuvent consulter le contenu de ces archives. On ne va pas s’en plaindre.
Une capacité de stockage un peu légère
Côté capacité de stockage, WhatsApp se montre un peu radin : l’application fournit seulement 2 Go aux utilisateurs gratuits. C’est bien loin des 15 Go proposés par un compte Google, même s'ils sont partagés entre Drive, Gmail et Google Photos. Les abonnés payants sont mieux lotis : ceux qui possèdent un abonnement WhatsApp Plus bénéficient de 100 Go d’espace disponible et les formules Meta One vont jusqu’à 4 To.
- Chiffrement de bout en bout.
- Appels audio et vidéo gratuits.
- Compatibilité multiplateforme.
Une autre information qui a son importance : ceux qui souhaitent renoncer à leur forfait payant auront 4 mois pour récupérer leurs sauvegardes. Quand ce délai sera passé, les archives disparaîtront définitivement si aucun renouvellement n’est intervenu entre-temps.
Derrière ce pied de nez à Google, on devine que Meta recherche surtout une nouvelle stratégie de monétisation pour sa messagerie instantanée. Les utilisateurs mordront-ils à l’hameçon ? L’avenir nous le dira.

articles.title: Le vrai frein à l'achat d'une voiture électrique n'est pas celui que l'on croit
articles.text:
La voiture électrique a un problème d’image, et l’industrie (certains constructeurs plus spécifiquement) ne l’a pas aidée avec des discours ambivalents et de fausses promesses. Pour ceux et celles qui en conduisent une, le premier coupable est pourtant ailleurs. Le Global EV Alliance (GEVA), un réseau de 71 associations de conducteurs électriques présentes dans 41 pays, a publié ce mardi 17 novembre 2026 son enquête annuelle.
Chez les 29 547 conducteurs de 34 pays interrogés, les idées reçues ou fausses informations arrivent en tête des freins à l’adoption (74 % à l’échelle mondiale et 79 % en France), devant le prix d’achat (49 %) et la recharge en immeuble (47 %). Et les mythes autour de la batterie sont ceux qui reviennent encore le plus régulièrement chez les non-possesseurs d’électrique.
La batterie fait moins peur quand on roule avec
72 % des sondés entendent dire que les batteries de voitures électriques ne durent pas, 58 % que la voiture prend feu plus facilement à cause de la batterie.
Chez les propriétaires, cette crainte s’est largement dissipée. 65 % d’entre eux ne s’inquiètent pas de la durée de vie de leur propre batterie, contre 18 % qui s’en soucient.
Ellen Hiep, membre du comité de pilotage du GEVA, rappelle que les batteries sont souvent garanties 8 ans et durent en général plus longtemps que la voiture. Plusieurs études autour de la fiabilité des batteries l’ont déjà démontré, et ce peu importe la technologie choisie.
Une perception biaisée ?
Pour autant, prenons des pincettes. Comme le relève InsideEVs, ce sont ici des propriétaires qui expliquent ce qui retient les autres de passer à l’électrique : l’enquête ne mesure donc pas directement ce qui fait hésiter les acheteurs.
Il convient aussi de préciser que ces sondés ont été recrutés par des associations et des passionnés, un public forcément acquis à la cause de la voiture électrique. Néanmoins, les possesseurs de voitures électriques restent les premiers ambassadeurs de cette forme de mobilité : ils sont en première ligne. Ils sont aussi les mieux placés pour faire tomber les préjugés de ceux qui n’en possèdent pas encore.
Ils sont quand même 49 % à juger qu’il est difficile de convaincre leurs amis et leur famille de choisir un véhicule électrique à cause des idées reçues, contre 22 % qui ne voient pas cette désinformation comme un problème pour convaincre leurs proches.
Au-delà de cette bataille contre les idées reçues, le prix et la recharge en immeuble restent de vrais obstacles soulevés. Enfin, un dernier chiffre retient aussi l’attention dans l’étude : 46 % des possesseurs ne voient aucun inconvénient à l’électrique, et ce chiffre atteint même 60 % à l’échelle de la France. Les résultats détaillés, pays par pays, sont consultables sur le site de l’enquête.

articles.title: Fritzbox als Netzwerkspeicher: Diese Möglichkeiten bietet dein Router
articles.text:
Fritzbox als Netzwerkspeicher: Diese Möglichkeiten bietet dein Router
Fritzboxen bieten eine Vielzahl von Features. Einige davon dürften die meisten User:innen gar nicht auf dem Schirm haben. Schließlich ist der Router schnell vergessen, wenn er seine Dienste reibungslos erledigt und Internet in jeden Bereich der Wohnung bringt. Eine dieser oftmals übersehenen Funktionen ist der Netzwerkspeicher der Fritzbox.
Es gibt zwei Wege, um auch von anderen Geräten im Netzwerk auf Dateien zuzugreifen, die per USB-Stick oder Festplatte an die Fritzbox gekoppelt sind. Einziger Nachteil: Die beiden Methoden schließen einander aus. Solltest du etwa den USB-Fernanschluss für die Fritzbox aktiviert haben, funktioniert der Netzwerkspeicher nicht mehr. Was die Unterschiede sind und wie du beide Varianten einrichtest, erfährst du in den jeweiligen Abschnitten.
Fritzbox: So funktioniert der USB-Fernanschluss
Der USB-Fernanschluss ist die einfachste Methode, um die Fritzbox in einen Netzwerkspeicher zu verwandeln. Die Einschränkung dabei ist, dass nicht alle Geräte im Netzwerk auf den USB-Stick oder die Festplatte zugreifen können, die am Router angeschlossen wurde. Beim USB-Fernanschluss stellst du nur die Verbindung zwischen der Fritzbox und einem oder mehreren Windows-Computern her. Wem das reicht, bekommt damit eine schneller umsetzbare Lösung als beim Medienspeicher.
Um den USB-Fernanschluss einzurichten, benötigst du einen PC mit Windows 7 oder höher. Dazu kommt ein passender USB-Stick oder eine Festplatte. Welche Geräte mit deiner Fritzbox kompatibel sind, entnimmst du dabei am besten dem Handbuch, da sich die Spezifikationen von Modell zu Modell unterscheiden können. Hast du den USB-Stick mit dem Router verbunden, kannst du zunächst in deiner Fritzbox-Benutzeroberfläche mit den Vorbereitungen starten.
USB-Fernanschluss in der Fritzbox aktivieren
- Öffne die Benutzeroberfläche der Fritzbox über die Webadresse „fritz.box“ oder über die werksseitig eingestellte IP „192.168.178.1“.
- Klicke in der linken Seitenleiste auf „Heimnetz“ und wähle dort „USB / Speicher“ aus.
- Wähle den Reiter „USB-Einstellungen“ aus.
- Aktiviere am unteren Ende der Seite den Haken bei der Option „USB-Fernanschluss aktiv“.
Windows-PC mit USB-Fernanschluss ausstatten
- Öffne wie oben beschrieben den Bereich „USB-Einstellungen“ in der Fritzbox-Oberfläche.
- Im unteren Bereich findest du einen Download-Button für das Programm „AVM Fritzbox USB-Fernanschluss“.
- Klicke im Anschluss doppelt auf die heruntergeladene Datei, um sie zu installieren.
USB-Fernanschluss unter Windows nutzen
- Klicke im System-Tray von Windows unten rechts auf das kleine USB-Symbol des Fernanschlusses.
- Trage in der Anmeldemaske das Kennwort deiner Fritzbox ein. Solltest du dich bei deiner Fritzbox mit einem Benutzernamen anmelden müssen, trage diesen ebenfalls ein. Andernfalls kann das Feld leer bleiben.
- Wähle „Aktualisieren“ und anschließend per Rechtsklick den angeschlossenen USB-Stick aus.
- Klicke auf „Verbinden“.
Künftig sollte der USB-Speicher, der mit deiner Fritzbox verbunden ist, genauso in Windows angezeigt werden, als wäre er an den PC selbst angeschlossen. Willst du auch mit anderen Windows-Geräten darauf zugreifen, wiederholst du einfach auf den Endgeräten die Installation des Programms und das Verbinden des Sticks.
Fritzbox: So wird der Router zum Netzwerkspeicher
Um den USB-Speicher an der Fritzbox im kompletten Netzwerk nutzen zu können, musst du zunächst, wie oben erwähnt, den USB-Fernanschluss deaktivieren. Der Vorteil im Gegensatz zur ersten Variante ist, dass du auch mit einem Smartphone oder Tablet auf den Speicher zugreifen kannst. Der Zugriff über Windows-PCs ist ebenfalls möglich, genauso wie über andere Betriebssysteme wie macOS.
Fritzbox-Benutzer einrichten
Um die NAS-Funktion an der Fritzbox nutzen zu können, müssen ein Benutzer samt Kennwort festgelegt werden. Das ist zum Glück vergleichsweise schnell erledigt.
- Öffne die Benutzeroberfläche der Fritzbox über die Webadresse „fritz.box“ oder über die werksseitig eingestellte IP „192.168.178.1“.
- Klicke in der linken Seitenleiste auf „System“ und anschließend auf „Fritzbox-Benutzer“.
Du kannst einen vorhandenen Benutzer bearbeiten und bei ihm im Bereich „Berechtigungen“ den Haken bei „Zugang zu NAS-Inhalten“ setzen. Gibt es noch keinen Benutzer oder willst du ein separates Konto für den NAS-Zugang mit eigenem Passwort, kannst du einen neuen Benutzer über den Knopf „Benutzer hinzufügen“ erstellen.
Bei beiden Varianten kannst du nach dem Aktivieren von „Zugang zu NAS-Inhalten“ festlegen, ob der Benutzer vollen Zugriff auf alle Inhalte haben soll oder nur einen Lesezugriff erhält. Über die Option „Individuelle Einstellungen“ und „Zugriffsberechtigung einstellen“ kannst du auch einzelne Ordner für den Zugriff freigeben, während der Rest verwehrt bleibt.
NAS in der Fritzbox aktivieren
- Öffne die Benutzeroberfläche der Fritzbox über die Webadresse „fritz.box“ oder über die werksseitig eingestellte IP „192.168.178.1“.
- Klicke in der Seitenleiste auf „Heimnetz“ und anschließend „USB / Speicher“.
- Wähle im Reiter „Heimnetzfreigabe“ die Option „Zugriff auf Netzlaufwerk (SMB)“ aus.
Darunter kannst du dann einen Namen für den Netzwerkspeicher festlegen, damit du ihn später zuordnen kannst. Zudem siehst du eine Liste aller Benutzer, die NAS-Zugriff haben. So kannst du direkt prüfen, ob das Erstellen aus dem vorherigen Schritt korrekt funktioniert hat. Nach einem letzten Klick auf „Übernehmen“ sind schon alle Voraussetzungen für den Netzwerkspeicher der Fritzbox getroffen. Allerdings gibt es noch Unterschiede bei der Art des Zugriffs.
So kannst du auf deinen Fritzbox-Speicher zugreifen
Mit Geräten, die einen Browser nutzen können, kannst du nach dem Setup über die Adresse „fritz.nas“ auf deinen Netzwerkspeicher zugreifen. Über mobile Geräte wie Smartphones und Tablets kannst du hingegen die Myfritz-App nutzen. Etwas komplizierter ist das Ganze, wenn du über den Datei-Explorer auf Windows-PCs oder über den Finder auf macOS auf den Netzwerkspeicher deiner Fritzbox zugreifen willst.
Unter Windows
- Öffne den Datei-Explorer und gib in der Leiste „\\fritz.box“ ein.
- Gib in der Anmeldemaske die Login-Daten des Benutzers ein, der Zugriff auf den Speicher hat, und aktiviere die Option „Anmeldedaten speichern“.
- Klicke mit der rechten Maustaste auf den Ordner, den du als Netzwerklaufwerk einrichten willst, und wähle „Netzlaufwerk verbinden“ aus.
- Klicke auf „Fertigstellen“.
Unter macOS
- Öffne den Finder und klicke in der Menüleiste auf „Gehe zu“.
- Wähle „Server verbinden“ aus und gib als Adresse „smb:\\fritz.box“ ein.
- Klicke auf „Verbinden“ und gib die Login-Daten des Netzwerknutzers ein.
- Wähle den Ordner aus, der freigegeben werden soll, und klicke im Menü auf „Ablage“, gefolgt von „Alias erzeugen“.
- Ziehe das Alias in den Bereich „Favoriten“ des macOS-Finders.

articles.title: Amazon Prime : bonne nouvelle, vous pouvez partager votre abonnement avec quelqu'un d'autre
articles.text:
Ce 17 novembre, Amazon lance Amazon Family en France, une fonction réservée jusqu’à maintenant aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, en Italie, au Canada et en Irlande. Elle permet de partager ses avantages Prime avec un autre compte Amazon. Mais attention aux petites lignes : on ne peut pas tout partager et pas à n’importe qui.
Partager ses avantages Prime gratuitement : Amazon Family est là
Si vous êtes abonné à Amazon Prime et que vous allez dans « Gérer votre Famille Amazon », vous pouvez désormais cliquer sur « Partager vos Avantages Prime ». Il permet d’ajouter un compte Amazon d’un adulte et l’inviter à profiter aussi des avantages inclus dans l’abonnement Amazon Prime. De quoi éviter de repayer 69,90 euros par an sur un deuxième compte : une belle économie potentielle.
Dans son communiqué de presse, Amazon annonce que tous les avantages ne sont pas partagés, mais il y a tout de même la livraison Prime gratuite, les offres exclusives sur Amazon, le service de streaming audio Amazon Music Prime, la SVoD avec Prime Video (avec les publicités uniquement) ainsi que le service de cloud gaming Amazon Luna. Manquent donc à l’appel certains avantages assez limités, comme Prime Photos qui permet de stocker des photos dans le cloud ; Prime Reading qui permet de lire via Kindle à des centaines de livres.
L’avantage est que chacun peut garder son compte avec son historique de commandes, ses parties sur Amazon Luna, ses recommandations sur Prime Video, etc. Bien qu’il existe déjà un système de profils sur les services d’Amazon, il faut à chaque fois partager un même compte Amazon. Mais avec Amazon Family, plus besoin de demander le code de la double authentification envoyé par mail.
Le « foyer » : une notion floue pour Amazon, mais qui doit permettre d’éviter les abus
Dans sa communication, Amazon parle d’un foyer au sein duquel un compte abonné à Prime peut partager ses avantages. L’idée derrière cela est d’éviter que certains partagent leur compte à quelqu’un d’autre : un ami, de la famille éloignée, etc. Un foyer pour Amazon, c’est une résidence principale à la même adresse pour deux comptes : « il s’agit de l’adresse que vous considérez comme votre domicile et où vous passez le plus clair de votre temps », peut-on lire sur le site de support.
On imagine qu’un compte pourra être retiré de la famille Amazon s’il n’est pas suffisamment présent à la même adresse que le compte abonné. Pour le moment, Amazon n’indique rien à ce propos sur son support. Par ailleurs, un compte qui quitte une famille Amazon devra attendre 12 mois pour rejoindre une autre famille. Là encore, c’est un moyen d’éviter les fraudes.

articles.title: Paytm public-market investors earn 1.7x returns in five years as shares hit record high
articles.text:
Paytm public-market investors earn 1.7x returns in five years as shares hit record high
An analysis of the company's shareholder base shows that public investors have collectively acquired around 41.5 crore shares at a weighted average price of Rs 1,092 apiece.
Public shareholders in One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, have earned returns of approximately 1.7 times their investment over the past five years, as the fintech company's shares climbed to a new high, reflecting a significant expansion in public ownership and institutional participation since its stock market debut.
An analysis of the company's shareholder base shows that public investors have collectively acquired around 41.5 crore shares at a weighted average price of Rs 1,092 apiece. Based on the National Stock Exchange's closing price of Rs 1,903 on November 17, 2026, this translates into an annualised return of approximately 17%.
The stock closed at Rs 1,888.30 on Wednesday.
The calculation includes both investors who subscribed to Paytm's initial public offering (IPO) in November 2021 and those who subsequently purchased shares from pre-IPO shareholders in the secondary market.
However, investors who received shares in the IPO at Rs 2,150 apiece are still trading at approximately 0.9 times their initial investment, underscoring the difference between returns for the original IPO allotment cohort and those for public-market investors who entered at lower prices.
The analysis, based on NSE and BSE block deals, bulk deals and disclosed open-market transactions, also shows that pre-IPO shareholders have sold approximately 34.6 crore shares since listing at a weighted average price of Rs 832 apiece.
At the November 17 closing price, these shares are valued at around 2.3 times their average selling price, translating into an annualised return of approximately 40.4% for investors who acquired them at the reported average price.
Paytm's shareholder composition has undergone a significant shift since its market debut, with the company's free float increasing from around 15% at listing in 2021 to approximately 68%.
Domestic institutional ownership has also risen substantially, increasing from 1.3% in September 2022 to 29.5% in September 2026.
Mutual funds now hold around 21.2% of the company's equity, while insurance companies account for another 6.2%, indicating a larger institutional presence in its shareholder base.
The increase in institutional participation comes as Paytm has worked through regulatory and business challenges while focusing on its core payments operations, merchant ecosystem and financial services distribution.
Under founder and Chief Executive Vijay Shekhar Sharma, the company has continued to invest in technology, expand its merchant network and strengthen its financial services offerings, alongside efforts to improve operational efficiency and build a more sustainable business model.
Paytm's operating performance has also improved, with the company reporting six consecutive quarters of profitability.
For the second quarter of FY27, the company reported revenue of Rs 2,648 crore, up 28% year-on-year, while EBITDA increased 90% to Rs 270 crore. Its EBITDA margin reached 10% for the first time, while profit after tax stood at Rs 225 crore.
The improvement in financial performance reflects higher operating leverage and the company's continued focus on profitable growth, as it seeks to strengthen its position in India's digital payments and financial services market.
The expansion in domestic institutional ownership and the rise in public shareholding mark a significant change in Paytm's investor profile since its listing.

articles.title: Comment faire une recherche IA sur Google sans laisser de traces — Frandroid
articles.text:
Après la navigation incognito, voilà que Google déploie la recherche incognito. Ou plutôt, le prompting incognito. Dans un billet de blog publié le 17 novembre dernier et repéré par Techcrunch, la firme de Mountain View a annoncé qu’un bouton allait apparaître dans l’interface de recherche par IA pour garder certains échanges privés.
Ces « discussions temporaires », comme l’entreprise les appelle, concernent spécifiquement le mode de recherche par IA qui est offert sur la page d’accueil de Google, mais fonctionne exactement comme celles intégrées à Gemini.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Des recherches privées, pas anonymes
Activer le prompting incognito demandera juste de cliquer sur le petit bouton en forme de crayon en haut à droite dans le mode IA. Ce dernier n’est pas encore disponible, mais « est en cours de déploiement dans le monde pour tous les langages pris en charge par le mode IA », indique la firme.
Ces « sessions » de discussions ne seront pas liées à votre compte Google et pas enregistrées dans votre historique. Cela signifie aussi qu’elles ne seront pas « contextualisées » grâce aux restes de vos recherches et avec ce que l’IA sait déjà sur vous. Cela peut être aussi utile si vous voulez éviter que Google commence à penser que Dora l’Exploratrice et Bluey sont des centres d’intérêt majeurs de votre vie.
Ces informations ne seront pas non plus « utilisées pour améliorer l’IA de Google » si l’on en croit l’entreprise, mais rien ne dit par contre qu’elles ne serviront pas au ciblage de publicités. Comme pour la navigation incognito, cela ne laisse pas de traces sur la machine ou dans l’historique, mais cela ne signifie pas que personne n’est en mesure de lier ces données à vos habitudes de navigation.
Gemini et le mode IA, bonnet blanc et blanc bonnet ?
Pour accéder au mode IA, il faut soit cliquer sur le bouton dédié dans la page d’accueil, soit interagir avec les réponses générées par IA après une recherche.
    Pour aller plus loin
Google veut imposer son mode IA, quitte à envahir votre écran
            
Avec cet ajout, le mode IA de la recherche Google se rapproche encore un peu plus de ce que propose le véritable chatbot de la firme et la distinction commence à être difficile à justifier. Gemini est certes plus complet et propose plus de fonctionnalités, mais, pour la plupart des recherches, les résultats sont très similaires.

articles.title: Alfonso, funcionario de la Seguridad Social: “Quien retrase un año su jubilación podrá recibir un pago de 8.500 euros”
articles.text:
Explica Alfonso Muñoz Cuenca que uno de los incentivos que tienen los trabajadores que deciden continuar trabajando tras alcanzar su edad ordinaria de retiro es el de poder acceder a un pago único de 8.000 o 8.500 euros. Es decir, se trata de un incentivo que puede pagarse si se retrasa un año la jubilación. Depende de la situación de cada trabajador.
Con la jubilación demorada, el trabajador puede optar por retrasar de manera voluntaria su acceso a la pensión a cambio de un complemento económico. Este complemento puede ser en forma de incremento de la pensión mensual o bien a tanto alzado. También puede haber una mezcla de ambos. En este caso sí que hace falta que se haya retrasado un mínimo de dos años completos. Es decir, que si solo se retrasa un año, no se puede pedir la opción de pago mixto.
Este pago se calcula de manera individual. Depende de la cantidad de la pensión y de los años cotizados que tenga el trabajador en el momento de alcanzar la edad ordinaria de jubilación. Por ello, en algunos casos, los 8.500 euros de los que habla Muñoz pueden ser superiores. De hecho, en algunos casos pueden llegar a ser superiores a los 10.000 euros por año de demora. En los ejemplos que pone el organismo ya se contempla esta posibilidad. Es el caso de las personas que tienen una carrera de cotización más larga y una pensión más alta.
Qué hay que decidir al solicitar la pensión
Esta elección solo hay que hacerla una vez. Es decir, en el momento de solicitar la pensión (cuando se adquiere el derecho al complemento). Una vez elegida la opción, no se puede cambiar (artículo 210.2 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social). Como insiste Muñoz, el trabajador tiene estas opciones:
Es importante pensar si queremos recibir el dinero en un solo pago (al jubilarnos) o si preferimos que nos aumenten nuestra pensión mensual. Hay que saber que podemos trabajar y cobrar pensión si cumplimos los requisitos de compatibilidad y que tenemos estos incentivos por retrasar nuestro retiro.
También es relevante pensar en cómo afectará a nuestros impuestos. Este pago único se considera rendimiento del trabajo (por ello tributa en el impuesto sobre la renta de las personas físicas (IRPF)). La Agencia Tributaria contempla una reducción del 30 % en el caso de que se cumplan los requisitos. Hay que saber que el importe bruto del complemento no es necesariamente equivalente al importe neto.
Muñoz también apunta a que hay que pensar en otros aspectos. Por ejemplo, en nuestra salud. O en las características de nuestro puesto de trabajo. También es importante pensar en la calidad de vida.
Además, debemos tener en cuenta nuestros proyectos personales. Saber que existe este incentivo económico nos va a permitir tenerlo en cuenta en nuestra planificación de la jubilación. También hay que tener en cuenta aquellas circunstancias que hacen más o menos viable continuar trabajando.
