articles.title: Miden taps Visa’s network to bring virtual cards to African businesses
articles.text:
Miden, a Y Combinator-backed Nigerian payments infrastructure startup, has partnered with payments giant Visa to help mid- to large-sized African businesses issue virtual cards and manage company spending through a single platform.
The partnership will connect Miden’s card-issuing infrastructure to Visa’s global payments network, allowing eligible businesses to create and distribute virtual Visa cards to employees, teams, suppliers, and projects. The cards will feature programmable spending controls that let companies restrict transactions by merchant, spending category, and location, Miden said.
The deal extends Miden’s efforts to build a card infrastructure for businesses that extends beyond issuing virtual cards. In March, the startup introduced tap-to-pay functionality to its card product, letting customers use their cards through digital wallets such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay.
“By integrating with Visa, we are removing unnecessary intermediaries from the equation,” Dom Okiemute, Miden’s chief executive officer and cofounder, said at the launch event in Lagos. “This gives our partners access to the world’s leading digital payments network alongside the precision card controls required to manage spend securely and at scale.”
Founded in 2022 by Okiemute and Ini Udoh, Miden builds payment infrastructure that allows businesses and fintechs to issue cards and manage collections and payouts through application programming interfaces (APIs). In 2024, the startup joined Y Combinator’s Winter batch. Since then, Miden has expanded beyond card issuance to support disbursements, collections, global payments, and treasury operations.
Under the Visa partnership, Miden provides the card management technology, monitoring, spending controls, and automated reconciliation infrastructure, while Visa provides access to its global card network. Participating financial institutions issue the cards and businesses can configure and distribute them through Miden’s platform or an API.
Miden said it is also rolling out granular spending controls alongside the direct Visa integration. Businesses will be able to restrict transactions to approved merchants, set merchant category code (MCC) limits for expenses such as software, logistics, travel, and procurement, and define geographical boundaries for card usage.
A company could issue its IT department a virtual card specifically for cloud infrastructure expenses. The card could be restricted to an approved provider such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), with a fixed monthly spending limit. Attempts to use it elsewhere would be declined, Miden said.
According to the company, its platform will also provide spending analytics showing where money was spent, by whom, and for what purpose, alongside reporting, transaction categorisation, and accounting integrations. The company said these features will help reduce manual reconciliation and give finance teams better visibility into corporate spending.
Miden says its direct technical integration with Visa removes some intermediary processing layers, allowing transactions to reach Visa’s infrastructure through a shorter route. The company expects this to reduce latency and improve approval rates.
The company operates in a competitive African payments infrastructure market that includes Flutterwave, Interswitch, and Paystack, as well as spend-management platforms such as Sava. While these companies overlap with Miden in merchant payments, card issuing, disbursements, and expense management, Miden says its proposition combines card issuing, banking infrastructure, treasury services, and payment operations in one platform.
It operates a business-to-business (B2B) infrastructure model, earning a share of interchange and per-transaction processing fees on card spending. It also charges API subscription fees from enterprises and fintechs using its financial infrastructure.
The initial rollout of the direct Visa integration covers its operating markets in Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and South Africa, with plans to extend the infrastructure into additional markets across sub-Saharan Africa.
In 2023, Visa partnered with South Africa’s Direct Transact to expand multi-currency card solutions for banks, fintechs, and businesses across Central Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Visa has also partnered with African fintechs such as Pesapal and MFS Africa to expand digital payments and card access across the continent.
“At Visa, we are committed to powering next-generation financial infrastructure to drive business growth and digital transformation,” Andrew Uaboi, vice president/cluster head, Visa West Africa, said in a statement. “Our collaboration with Miden is an important step forward in expanding access to secure digital issuing rails, and we are excited to see how this collaboration unlocks new efficiencies for African businesses.”

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
- November 12, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
- Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.

articles.title: Russian APT Poses as Employee of Hacked Firm to Breach Another US Organization
articles.text:
Russia-linked APT Star Blizzard hacked a US organization by impersonating an employee at another US organization it had previously compromised, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reports.
Also tracked as Callisto, Cold Relic, Cold River, UNC4057, and Gossamer Bear, and active for over a decade, Star Blizzard has been formally associated by the US with Russia’s intelligence service FSB.
The APT is known for mounting sophisticated phishing and malware campaigns to collect information relevant to the Russian government, and to use victims’ data in attacks on subsequent targets.
Star Blizzard “has been highly successful at compromising high-value targets (including government officials, defense contractors, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) across Europe and North America) while maintaining a consistent operational tempo,” Google says.
In a recent attack against a US organization, Star Blizzard impersonated an employee of another organization it had breached months earlier. Google, which tracks the group as Cold Relic, believes the hackers likely used contact and relationship information obtained during the earlier intrusion to select and deceive their new target.
The first organization was hit in late 2025, using the compromised credentials of a super admin account. The APT leveraged a residential proxy network close to the victim and relied on multi-factor authentication (MFA) push notification fatigue to register a device to the victim’s tenant.
Next, the group downloaded the organization’s entire cloud storage drive, accessed the admin console to fingerprint defenses and remove evidence of the initial intrusion, exported full employee lists, and launched a domain-wide export.
According to Google, the group used passkeys, rogue MFA devices, and MFA backup codes to maintain persistent access to the victim organization for several months. It also exfiltrated emails and targeted cloud drive documents containing information of interest.
“When the threat actor was removed from the victim organization’s infrastructure, GTIG observed Cold Relic leveraging email accounts impersonating employees of the victim organization. These impersonated accounts were used to target both internal employees and associates within the same professional circles with renewed social engineering attempts,” Google says.
The APT impersonated an employee at the victim organization to establish communication with the second victim organization via a secure messaging application.
Ultimately, it shared phishing links designed to steal credentials and Entra ID authentication tokens, and used the secrets to register a new MFA device to the second organization’s SSO solution to retain access to the compromised account.
“By impersonating someone known in the same professional circles as the new target, Cold Relic increased their chance of phishing success. Ultimately, in this case, Cold Relic was able to obtain credentials to the organization and perform bulk download of files accessible in the compromised user’s cloud drive,” Google says.
To maintain persistence, the APT registered rogue MFA devices, passkeys, and MFA backup codes, conducted aggressive data collection and exfiltration, and searched for credentials, employee information, email archives, documents, and any other information it could use in subsequent spear-phishing attacks.
The threat actor also changed its profile name in the secure messaging application used in this intrusion, likely to reuse it in another attack.
“Cold Relic’s campaigns demonstrate the convergence of human-centric social engineering and cloud identity abuse. By obtaining access to strategic personnel rosters and operational documents, Russian intelligence services turn legitimate business communications into attack vectors against trusted partners,” Google notes.

articles.title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
articles.text:
Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”
The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.
The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.
All about agents
Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability.
Also announced as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a company’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

articles.title: Estados Unidos evalúa obligar a las empresas a avisar en sus sitios web si usan IA china
articles.text:
El gobierno de Donald Trump evalúa obligar a las empresas estadounidenses a informar públicamente cuándo usan modelos de inteligencia artificial de China, según tres personas que hablaron con la agencia Reuters. La medida busca desalentar esa dependencia sin imponer prohibiciones nuevas que puedan molestar a la industria o a Beijing.
El Departamento del Tesoro y la Oficina de Política Científica y Tecnológica de la Casa Blanca discutieron el plan, que alcanzaría a compañías como Airbnb. La plataforma de alquileres usa Qwen, un modelo de la china Alibaba, para su agente de atención al cliente.
Según el plan, firmas como Airbnb tendrían que publicar esa información en sus sitios web. Las fuentes no aclararon si la idea gana respaldo dentro del gobierno ni si pasaría a un proceso formal de reglamentación.
La Casa Blanca, el Tesoro, Alibaba y la embajada de China en Washington no respondieron de inmediato a los pedidos de comentarios de Reuters. Airbnb declinó opinar.
Reuters describió la propuesta como una campaña de señalamiento público (en inglés, name and shame), compatible con la postura general del gobierno contra regular la inteligencia artificial.
Modelos chinos más baratos y cada vez más usados
Los modelos en cuestión son de “pesos abiertos”: sus componentes centrales son públicos y cualquiera puede descargarlos y adaptarlos. Entre ellos están Kimi, de Moonshot AI, DeepSeek y Qwen. De acuerdo con la agencia Reuters, las empresas estadounidenses los adoptan porque cuestan menos que las herramientas de OpenAI y Anthropic y rinden lo suficiente.
Los sectores más duros con China temen que Beijing use esos modelos para volver dependientes a las compañías de Estados Unidos, escribió la agencia. En octubre, los tres modelos más usados en OpenRouter, una plataforma que mide el uso de IA, fueron chinos. La medición se hace por tokens, las unidades de texto que procesa y cobra un modelo.
Los modelos abiertos de origen estadounidense incluyen Muse Glimmer, de Meta, Nemotron, de Nvidia, y Beam, de Reflection AI.
Una investigación en el Congreso y amenazas de sanciones
Los republicanos Andrew Garbarino, de Nueva York, y John Moolenaar, de Michigan, presidentes de los comités de Seguridad Nacional y del comité especial sobre China de la Cámara de Representantes, abrieron este año una investigación sobre el uso de IA china por empresas estadounidenses. Enviaron cartas a Airbnb, a Anysphere y a DoorDash.
Anysphere, creadora de la herramienta de programación Cursor, construyó su modelo Composer 2 sobre una versión de Kimi. Un cofundador de DoorDash dijo que la empresa deriva algunas tareas de un sistema interno hacia Kimi. Moonshot, DoorDash y SpaceX, que compró Anysphere, no respondieron a Reuters.
En julio, el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, dijo que el gobierno podría sancionar a empresas chinas de IA si se comprueba que robaron propiedad intelectual mediante la “destilación”: entrenar modelos pequeños con las respuestas de otros más grandes. En abril, el director de esa oficina de la Casa Blanca, Michael Kratsios, acusó a China de robar esa propiedad “a escala industrial”.
La propia administración también usó IA china: Reuters informó en septiembre que un sitio web del gobierno federal empleaba un modelo de Alibaba para buscar regulaciones propuestas, aunque el FBI acusó a su desarrollador de copiar la tecnología de Anthropic.
Hasta ahora, según Reuters, los funcionarios no restringieron ni sancionaron a las empresas chinas de IA. La nota enmarca el debate en el escándalo del director ejecutivo de Nvidia, Jensen Huang, y su relación con una presunta espía china, que reavivó los pedidos de una postura más dura.
La propuesta refleja una disputa que combina competitividad tecnológica, seguridad nacional y costos empresariales, mientras Estados Unidos busca limitar la influencia de China sin cerrar el acceso a modelos de inteligencia artificial más económicos.

articles.title: Así está el mercado laboral de tecnología: una de cada seis ofertas pide IA, solo uno de cada 60 programadores la pone en su currículum
articles.text: Imagen de una oficina con varias desarrolladoras. El 98% de los programadores españoles usa ya la IA cada día y el 86% dice que así es más productivo. Esa presencia cotidiana inunda inexorablemente el mercado laboral tecnológico: una de cada seis ofertas ya pide IA, pero solo uno de cada sesenta perfiles tiene algo de IA en su currículum. La aparición de la IA es la que más crece en las ofertas, ya aparece en el 15,7%, y las que mencionan agentes de IA se han multiplicado por ocho. La IA también provoca ya la creación de roles propios, como el “ingeniero de IA”, que reúne varios perfiles anteriores y que tiene 20 veces más demanda que en 2023. “Para la gran mayoría de profesionales tech del país, incluir la IA en su currículo va a ser prácticamente una obligación si quieren encontrar oportunidades”, destaca el nuevo informe de Manfred, del que salen los datos citados. articles.title: CloudBackend grabs €6.6M to turn AI-generated prototypes into productive business applications - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
CloudBackend grabs €6.6M to turn AI-generated prototypes into productive business applications
Just about anyone can knock up a working prototype application these days using artificial intelligence coding tools, but what happens when they want to turn that app into a viable business?
That’s the question that Swedish AI infrastructure startup CloudBackend AB thinks it can answer after raising €6.6 million ($7.25 million) in seed funding today. Leading the round was the family office of Carl-Henric Svanberg, formerly chairman of the Swedish government’s AI Commission, with participation from M2 Asset Management.
CloudBackend says it’s targeting the parts of application development that can’t be whipped up in seconds by generative AI tools. While vibe coding platforms such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex can deliver a working application, they can’t go the whole hog and turn it into a revenue-generating product.
The problem is that although vibe coding tools are great at generating application logic and user interfaces, they don’t know much about building the backend infrastructure. There’s a lot to do, because applications can’t just function – they also need robust security in place, the ability to scale up to thousands of users, they need to provide customer support, and they must work reliably in every situation. There’s also the question of how to monetize the app, getting insights from users, pricing considerations and marketing operations.
All of this is what CloudBackend’s Operations Platform is designed to handle, founder and Chief Executive Daniel Arthursson (pictured) told SiliconANGLE. It provides all of the backend infrastructure needed to turn any AI-generated prototype into a viable and profitable business within a single, accessible environment. “AI has made it much easier to build the first version of an application, but the challenge comes when customers sign in and expect the service to be secure, reliable and available every day,” he said.
Arthursson said the Operations Platform has five key components, including the extremely flexible Singularity Database that unifies relational data, object storage, caching and user files within a single platform. It offers robust identity and access controls integrated at the data layer, so users don’t have to stitch together multiple services to secure their application data.
Another key component of CloudBackend’s platform is “Build,” which allows skilled developers to create application frontends using declarative XML or native software development kits and then bind them to live data and deploy them in cloud environments without a continuous integration and deployment pipeline. Then there’s “Run,” which provides built-in tools for user subscriptions, customer relationship management and support, and revenue tracking within a single interface.
CloudBackend also offers collaboration tools that allow apps to keep their user’s data in perfect synchronization so multiple users can work together on projects. Finally, there’s a data sovereignty component that’s aimed at European organizations that must ensure all customer data is stored in Europe.
“We’re building the AI cloud infrastructure that helps creators make the leap from prototype to production without extensive technical knowledge,” Arthursson said. “It’s a new type of infrastructure designed for applications built with AI.”
CloudBackend’s infrastructure has been up and running with early access users so far, and with today’s funding round under its belt, it’s now planning to open it up to more users, with selected creators to begin onboarding to its beta program on November 24. The money from today’s round will also help CloudBackend to build deeper integrations with select vibe coding tools and large language models, Arthursson said.
The long-term vision, according to Arthursson, is to make the backend infrastructure and business operations as simple as the generative AI coding process has become.
Hans Lindroth, CEO of the Svanberg Family Office, said there will be lot of demand for what CloudBackend is offering, because it makes generative AI coding tools much more attractive when anyone can use them to start a business.
“AI makes it easier to build applications, but turning them into production-grade solutions for businesses is a different challenge,” he said. “We see a growing need for infrastructure that helps businesses to operate securely, serve customers reliably and expand their offerings. Daniel and his team have the experience and expertise to address that need and that’s why we chose to lead this round.”

articles.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.
AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.
But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.
“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”
JPMorgan and Bank of America, the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. And PNC, the eighth largest bank, changed its terms today.
Citi’s update goes beyond telling customers that they are responsible for anything their agents may do; it also informs them that if the AI tool leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer will be responsible for anything hackers do with their account. Banking giant Citizens similarly emailed its customers this week, warning that they are also on the hook for anything their AI assistant does, according to an email seen by TechCrunch.
As AI startups look for more revenue, breaking into personal finance presents an attractive opportunity for companies to add value for customers and wet their beaks in the stream of fees generated by the sector. But if consumers are already leery of sharing their email or chat records with an AI agent, bank and brokerage accounts offer a new trust challenge.
Anthropic’s approach is telling: The personal finance tool it launched earlier this month is explicitly billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”
Beyond cybersecurity concerns, banks also view efforts to enter their franchise as a competitive threat. Markets shuddered briefly in reaction to the prospect of AI tools making it easier for consumers to avoid unnecessary fees or low-interest deposit accounts that pad bank margins. But if AI agents become an important way to interact with financial decisions, banks will fight to control that pathway. Citi’s terms note that AI agents it provides can be used by customers without worrying about additional liability.
The reaction by banks is part of a broader trend among businesses of all stripes: AI labs promise that their agents will revolutionize the way people engage with a variety of service providers, then the service providers say “hold on a minute.” We’ve seen it in everything from car-hailing to food service, and how these relationships play out will help determine which AI investments pay off.

articles.title: GTA 6 chegou! Veja preço, onde comprar, história e tudo sobre o lançamento
articles.text:
A espera acabou! Depois de 13 anos desde o lançamento de Grand Theft Auto V, a Rockstar Games lança nesta quinta-feira (19) Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), um dos jogos mais aguardados da indústria dos videogames.
O novo título leva os jogadores de volta a Vice City, agora em uma versão mais detalhada e integrada ao estado fictício de Leonida. A aventura acompanha Jason e Lucia, dois protagonistas envolvidos em uma história de crimes, perseguições e sobrevivência.
Além da nova campanha, GTA 6 promete avanços gráficos, mudanças na inteligência artificial dos personagens, sistemas policiais mais elaborados e um mundo aberto com mais possibilidades de interação.
Para quem pretende começar a jogar no lançamento, reunimos as principais informações sobre plataformas, preços, história, mapa, desempenho e primeiras avaliações.
Quanto custa GTA 6 no Brasil?
GTA 6 chega ao Brasil com preços a partir de R$ 449,90 nas lojas digitais do PlayStation e Xbox. O jogo está disponível em duas edições:
| Edição | Preço | 
| Standard Edition | R$ 449,90 | 
| Ultimate Edition | R$ 549,90 | 
A edição Standard inclui o jogo completo. Já a Ultimate Edition oferece conteúdos adicionais, com uma diferença de R$ 100 em relação à versão básica.
Na PlayStation Store, a edição Standard também inclui o Pacote Vintage Vice City e um mês de GTA+ como benefícios de pré-venda.
Para quem prefere comprar no varejo, lojas como Amazon e Magazine Luiza comercializam a versão de PS5 em caixa com código de download, sem disco físico. Os preços podem variar conforme a loja e a forma de pagamento.
Em quais plataformas GTA 6 está disponível?
No lançamento, GTA 6 está disponível para:
O jogo não possui versão de lançamento para PlayStation 4 ou Xbox One.
A Rockstar Games também não anunciou uma data oficial para a chegada de GTA 6 ao PC.
Onde comprar GTA 6?
Os jogadores podem procurar GTA 6 nas lojas digitais oficiais das plataformas:
- PlayStation Store: para PS5 e PS5 Pro;
- Microsoft Store: para Xbox Series X|S.
Também é possível verificar a disponibilidade de cópias físicas em varejistas brasileiros. Nesse caso, é necessário observar a plataforma, o preço e as condições de entrega.
Para compras digitais, o jogo fica associado à conta utilizada na loja correspondente.
Qual é a história de GTA 6?
GTA 6 acompanha Jason e Lucia, dois personagens que acabam envolvidos em uma trama criminosa no estado de Leonida.
A história explora a parceria entre os protagonistas enquanto eles enfrentam as consequências de suas decisões em um ambiente marcado pelo crime.
A relação entre Jason e Lucia é um dos elementos centrais da narrativa e também foi destacada nas primeiras avaliações da imprensa especializada.
A campanha mantém a proposta característica da franquia, combinando missões principais, exploração livre, atividades paralelas e situações inesperadas pelo mapa.
Onde GTA 6 se passa? Qual é o tamanho do mapa?
GTA 6 se passa em Leonida, um estado fictício inspirado na Flórida, nos Estados Unidos.
Seu principal cenário é Vice City, cidade que retorna à franquia com uma nova representação de suas praias, avenidas, áreas comerciais e bairros.
O mundo aberto também inclui regiões fora do centro urbano, com estradas, áreas rurais e diferentes ambientes naturais.
Segundo a análise técnica da Digital Foundry, GTA 6 apresenta o maior mapa já desenvolvido pela Rockstar Games, acompanhado de uma densidade de detalhes superior à de seus títulos anteriores.
O tamanho exato em quilômetros quadrados, entretanto, não foi divulgado. Por isso, comparações numéricas com o mapa de GTA 5 exigem medições verificadas.
Quais são as principais novidades de GTA 6 em relação a GTA 5?
Além da mudança de cenário e protagonistas, GTA 6 introduz sistemas que ampliam as interações com o ambiente.
Entre os recursos destacados pela Digital Foundry estão:
- Sistema policial mais elaborado: agentes respondem a ocorrências a partir de diferentes pontos do mapa, e o reconhecimento de suspeitos considera fatores como roupas, veículos e aparência.
- Maior interação com personagens: jogadores podem conversar, cumprimentar ou ameaçar civis, que apresentam diferentes reações.
- Veículos mais detalhados: automóveis possuem sistemas de segurança, combustível e danos que influenciam a dirigibilidade.
- Ambientes interativos: é possível consumir alimentos e bebidas, utilizar determinados objetos e interagir com diferentes estabelecimentos.
- Comportamento dos NPCs: pedestres reagem a acidentes, tiroteios e outras situações de maneira mais dinâmica.
- Novas atividades: corridas de rua, competições off-road e outras opções de entretenimento ampliam as possibilidades de exploração.
Essas mudanças procuram tornar Leonida mais reativa às ações do jogador, indo além do aumento na quantidade de atividades disponíveis.
Como são os gráficos e o desempenho de GTA 6?
O desempenho de GTA 6 é um dos pontos que mais chamaram atenção nas primeiras análises.
De acordo com a Digital Foundry, o jogo utiliza uma resolução-base de 1440p tanto no PS5 convencional quanto no PS5 Pro, mas apresenta diferenças importantes na reconstrução da imagem.
No PS5 Pro, a tecnologia PSSR é utilizada para produzir uma apresentação visual próxima de 4K. O console também oferece sombras com ray tracing, enquanto o PS5 convencional utiliza uma solução diferente para esse recurso.
Ambas as versões analisadas trabalham com uma meta de 30 quadros por segundo (fps), sem modo de desempenho a 60 fps identificado nas avaliações citadas.
Segundo a Digital Foundry, o PS5 Pro mantém os 30 fps de maneira consistente durante a maior parte da experiência. Já o PS5 convencional pode apresentar quedas em situações mais exigentes, especialmente em cenas com explosões e durante algumas perseguições.
Entre os avanços gráficos estão iluminação global com ray tracing, reflexos mais realistas, efeitos climáticos localizados, cabelos com simulação física e ambientes urbanos mais detalhados.
O que dizem as primeiras avaliações de GTA 6?
As primeiras análises de GTA 6 destacam principalmente a qualidade do mundo aberto, a ambientação de Vice City e a relação entre Jason e Lucia.
Segundo levantamento publicado pelo TalkEsport em 18 de novembro, o jogo alcançou 99 pontos no Metacritic, com base em 100 avaliações, e 98 pontos no OpenCritic, considerando 52 análises. Os números representam o momento do levantamento e podem mudar conforme novas avaliações sejam adicionadas.
Veículos como Push Square, VGC, GamesRadar+, TechRadar e Screen Rant elogiaram diferentes aspectos da experiência, incluindo a exploração, os personagens e a quantidade de acontecimentos espalhados pelo mapa.
A Digital Foundry também destacou a qualidade técnica do jogo, especialmente a iluminação, os reflexos e a complexidade dos ambientes.
Por outro lado, a limitação a 30 fps aparece entre as principais críticas. Alguns avaliadores também apontaram trechos mais lentos da campanha e problemas pontuais de interface e desempenho.
As estimativas iniciais indicam que a história principal pode levar aproximadamente 60 horas para ser concluída, enquanto a exploração de atividades secundárias pode ampliar consideravelmente esse tempo.
Com a chegada oficial de GTA 6, os jogadores poderão conferir se a nova aventura da Rockstar corresponde às expectativas construídas ao longo de mais de uma década.
Rachele Victoria é formada em Letras, MBA em Inovação e atua há 10 anos com comunicação e conteúdo gamer.

articles.title: Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
articles.text:
President Donald Trump was greeted by no less than five beauty queens when he landed in the Philippines on Tuesday, according to local news outlet Rappler. As he stepped onto the tarmac, a child handed him small US and Philippine flags. A band played “YMCA,” a staple at Trump rallies, as more girls in traditional bell-sleeved blouses and young men in wide-brimmed hats danced to the song.
Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
Facing opposition at home, Trump is eyeing the former US colony to build chip fabs and data centers.
Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
Facing opposition at home, Trump is eyeing the former US colony to build chip fabs and data centers.
Outside the airport, hundreds of protesters packed streets bearing signs — and at least one prop casket — saying “Trump out.” Others say “Reject Pax Silica,” the name for the US-led international initiative to secure chips and critical minerals used in the hardware fueling the AI boom.
Peace and prosperity for whom?
“Pax” comes from the Latin word for “peace, stability, and long-term prosperity,” the Pax Silica website proudly says. Yet the unspoken question — peace and prosperity for whom? — explains the whiplash between the Philippine government’s warm welcome of Trump and the public fury raging outside.
Trump says he wants to “win AI” — whatever that means. As such, the US needs data centers full of GPUs to do it. With Americans increasingly opposed to data centers and chip factories being built in their communities, the US is now recruiting less affluent nations to take up some of the slack. Lawmakers from both the US and the Philippines are promising a slice of the riches that advances in generative AI are supposed to create. And that’s supposed to be worth the land razed, homes destroyed, and natural resources lost in the name of technological progress. In the Philippines, that’s taking the shape of a proposed 1,620-hectare (4,000 acres) hub for chip factories, processing plants for critical minerals, and data centers.
At least two dozen countries have signed on to the Pax Silica initiative, and Trump was expected to pressure more to join while in the Philippines for events related to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit. With Pax Silica, the US aims to insulate itself from China’s dominance in manufacturing semiconductors and processing critical minerals needed to make those chips. Trump held a bilateral meeting with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen to meet with China’s President Xi Jinping and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin.
Philippine and US officials are expected to sign a framework agreement by the end of the year for the jointly developed Pax Silica Economic Security Zone. The details are still murky and shrouded in NDAs. The Philippines’ Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) overseeing the plan expects an economic boom from minerals processing and chip manufacturing, with perhaps a data center or two on site. Meanwhile, human rights advocates who oppose the project warn that it will displace Indigenous residents, cutting them off from water resources on which they rely.
“How do we give up our burial grounds, our church, our livelihood?”
“We do not want to give up our community,” Petronila Capiz-Muñoz, chieftain of the Indigenous Aeta Hungey tribe, told Human Rights Watch. “How do we give up our burial grounds, our church, our livelihood? This is where we source our water, this is where we plant.” Capiz-Muñoz said BCDA officials have told residents that they’ll need to relocate by December to make way for development. Small farmers are also afraid the semiconductor hub will push them off their lands, according to Lian Buan, Southeast Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch.
There are layers of land-grabbing to unpack here.
The Aeta are among the first people to inhabit the Philippines, believed to have arrived around 30,000 years ago. And yet the Aeta Hungey tribe has been trying since 1994 to secure an official certificate recognizing its ancestral domain in one of the areas now facing industrial development. But since the tribe hasn’t been granted that certificate, the BCDA can still claim the AI hub will be built “outside titled ancestral domains.”
The agency says the project will be on public land located at the former Clark Air Base built in the early 1900s when the Philippines was a US territory. The Philippine constitution now only allows its own citizens to own private land. But the BCDA can offer leases lasting as long as 99 years to foreign developers. The agency expects to rake in close to $1 billion USD (about 60 billion in PHP Peso) from lease income over the first 25 years.
There are layers of land-grabbing to unpack here
The BCDA was in talks with around 30 different companies interested in setting up shop in Clark’s proposed AI hub, then-BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang told reporters in July. He couldn’t name names, he said, because of NDAs — creating the same kind of opacity that has turned Americans against data centers on their home turf.
He did mention, however, that an American energy company was conducting a feasibility study into building a liquefied natural gas (LNG) line and plant to meet the hub’s enormous electricity demand. Bingcang called LNG a clean fuel, but that’s provably false. LNG is primarily methane, a smog-forming pollutant that is an even more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.
Bingcang said in September that the Philippine government wanted to invite Nvidia, TSMC, and Apple. While one or two data center developers had expressed interest, according to Bingcang, most of the companies interested were “high tech” manufacturing firms. He has also described chip manufacturing as a “clean” industry, echoing corporate spin that’s been around since the start of Silicon Valley.
At the first chip fabs in California, workers — many of them Filipino immigrants — donned “bunny suits” to assemble sensitive chips in environmentally controlled “clean rooms.” Little did they know that the gear they wore offered little protection against the harsh chemicals used in manufacturing, which also leaked out of storage tanks to contaminate soil and groundwater. When studies came out in the ’90s documenting disproportionately high rates of miscarriages among workers, companies pledged to phase out some of the chemicals linked to reproductive health risks. Around the same time, chip manufacturing started to move out of the US to Asia, where similar health problems stemming from the same chemicals cropped up even decades later.
Chipmakers say their fabs have gotten much safer over the years, in part because more work is automated. Even so, the BCDA estimates that the AI hub will create up to 190,000 direct jobs. The BCDA, White House, and Philippine’s Malacañang Palace did not immediately respond to questions from The Verge.
“I don’t want to date myself, but I knew your parents very well. They were great,” Trump told President Marcos during his visit. Marcos’ parents are estimated to have stolen up to $30 billion from government coffers over decades of rule before a people power movement ousted the current president’s father from the same office in the 1980s. But public memory, it seems, can be short.
And skyrocketing demand for more powerful chips used for generative AI has raised fears among environmental and labor groups that history might repeat itself. Companies move fast and break things, leaving a toxic mess in their wake. And when Americans decide they’ve had enough in their own back yards, the industry sets up shop somewhere else where they think their customers aren’t paying attention and politicians are happy to look the other direction.

articles.title: Geely trae a España el Monjaro EM-i Ultra: su nuevo SUV híbrido enchufable de más de 300 CV
articles.text:
Monjaro EM-i Ultra. Quédate con este nombre de nuevo SUV de Geely Auto, puesto que va a dar mucho que hablar, tanto por prestaciones como por precio. El fabricante trae a España su SUV híbrido con una carta de presentación bastante interesante: 334 CV, tracción total eléctrica, un motor 1.5T y tres motores eléctricos, desarrolla 667 Nm de par y una aceleración de 0 a 100 km/h en 5,8 segundos... todo ello a un precio bastante competitivo.
Con la llegada del Monjaro EM-i Ultra, Geely ya suma en España cuatro modelos disponibles en su catálogo, aunque este SUV que acaba de presentar la marca es sin duda su buque insignia y su tope de gama, al menos de momento. Es un modelo bastante interesante, teniendo en cuenta que se trata de UN SUV de 4.800 mm de longitud, 1.895 mm de anchura y 1.700 mm de altura, con una distancia entre ejes de 2.845 mm, bastante en línea con las medidas que busca el conductor español que busca un coche de este segmento.
En este sentido, el Monjaro EM-i Ultra tiene una altura libre al suelo de 189 mm y ángulos de ataque y salida de 19° y 18°, todo ello dentro de un diseño enfocado a la seguridad, tanto en carretera como en caminos y terrenos más exigentes. Monta llantas de 20 pulgadas optimizadas aerodinámicamente y remata su diseño exterior una suerte de trazado ascendente de las luces diurnas, un voladizo delantero corto y una firma LED a lo ancho del vehículo en la zaga que dejan clara la presencia de este nuevo SUV.
Híbrido, más de 300 CV y mucha tecnología
Respecto a lo que lleva bajo el capó, el Geely Monjaro EM-i Ultra usa el sistema EM-i Super Hybrid, que según la compañía es uno de los sistemas híbridos enchufables más sofisticados del mundo. En el caso del Monjaro, se compone de un motor turbo de gasolina de 1,5 litros desarrollado específicamente para aplicaciones híbridas enchufables, tres motores eléctricos, una transmisión automática 3DHT, una batería LFP de 29,8 kWh y sistemas inteligentes de gestión y recuperación de energía.
Con todo ello, desarrolla una potencia combinada de 246 kW (334 CV) y un par máximo de 667 Nm, 0 a 100 km/h en 5,8 segundos y una velocidad máxima de 190 km/h (169 km/h en modo eléctrico), con un consumo de combustible ponderado de 2,4 l/100 km en ciclo urbano WLTP.
El Geely Monjaro EM-i Ultra estará disponible en Blanco Imperial (de serie), Negro Volcánico, Gris Titán, Ámbar y Azul Glaciar para su aspecto exterior y en Negro Onyx, de serie, y Arena para el interior. ¿Su precio? Desde 37.990 € en su modalidad al contado.

articles.title: I spoke with our GTA 6 reviewer about the game’s “unbelievable” immersive audio, and these are the soundbars I’d recommend for getting the very best out of your escapades in Vice City on PS5 or XBox
articles.text:
‘You want to be immersed in it as you would be in an IMAX movie’: a soundbar can totally bring the sprawling soundscape of GTA 6 to life, and these are the models I’d recommend — with options for every budget from JBL, Sony, and more
Turn up that radio
Grand Theft Auto 6 is here, and it’s accomplished the extremely daunting task of meeting our steep expectations after an epic 13-year-long wait, earning a perfect five-star review from us here at TechRadar Gaming.
Now that its release date has finally arrived, millions of people are finally getting started with the game, but I spoke with someone who’s already had the chance to sink countless hours into Rockstar’s smash hit. TechRadar Gaming’s Managing Editor, Rob Dwiar, penned our GTA 6 review, and we sat down to discuss everything from the game’s technical performance to its standout moments.
But there was one topic that we kept coming back to: its incredible sound design. In a title filled with crazy car chases, bustling urban zones, and rich natural areas, you’d really hope that the audio makes you feel a part of the world, and Rob felt it did just that.
The absorbing audio of GTA 6 seemed to be crucial to his enormously enjoyable experience with the game, something that became apparent as he recounted high-octane car chase segments. “There have been multiple times where things like knowing where sirens and the cops are coming from when travelling at high speeds around the city has been really key when trying to plan an escape to get out of trouble fast”.
But even if you fail in doing so, and find yourself in a spot of bother, Rob told me that weapon noises engage you in the action far more than they did in Grand Theft Auto 5. “There’s a lot of the best of Red Dead Redemption 2’s audio in that respect,” he said. “Car engines, noises, screeches, smash-ups, and the destruction of scenery — they are in the audio itself rather than just a subject of it”.
With Dolby Atmos audio available for Xbox players and Tempest 3D Audio harnessed for the PS5 version, we cannot understate the sheer scale and depth of the sound available in GTA 6. Indeed, Rob told me, “There’s lots going on, which is great, but you want to make sure you hear everything…it’s cinematic, and you want to be immersed in it as you would be in an IMAX movie”.
But how can you make sure that you truly “hear everything”, as is Rob's recommendation, and get the very best out of your time with the game? Well, for me, one of the greatest options available is a soundbar.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You don’t want to miss out on the spacious sound of GTA 6, and you certainly don’t want tinny audio when bumping tunes on the radio — something that your basic TV speakers will likely subject you to. So, I’ve compiled a list of the best soundbars for GTA 6 by combining Rob's thoughts on the audio and sound design of the game with my own years of testing audio-visual gear, with plenty of amazing options for everyone — no matter your budget. Without further ado, then, let’s get right into my top picks.
The best soundbars for GTA 6: my personal recommendations
1. The budget-friendly bar: Sony HT-SF150
I can’t even count the number of times I’ve recommended this soundbar on both hands — and if I could, I’d have an alarmingly high number of fingers.
The Sony HT-SF150 (known as the Sony HT-S100F in the US) is a budget soundbar done right in every sense. Rather than attempting to cram the fanciest features, like Dolby Atmos support or ultra-powerful bass, into a cheap and compact package, it mainly focuses on the fundamentals — which it gets absolutely spot on.
You’ll never have to second-guess what Lucia or Jason say thanks to this soundbar’s excellent handling of dialogue, and there are plenty of sound modes, including a Night option for playing in the early hours of the morning. And although this unit won’t provide palpable bass, I was impressed with the quality of its low-end output thanks to the built-in bass reflex speaker, which will give a bit more oomph to explosions than your basic TV sound.
One of my favorite things about this model, though, is its use of Sony’s S-Force Front Surround virtual processing, which endeavors to emulate “cinema-style surround sound”. This is great for adding a bit more width to the sound of GTA 6’s vibrant world, and will help the soundbar to map the movement of the on-screen chaos more effectively.
This soundbar is often available for less than $100 / £100, and it’s far better than most of the competition in this price range, so if you want to upgrade your audio setup for GTA 6 without breaking the bank, this is the model to go for.
2. The sonically stellar step-up: Klipsch Flexus Core 100
As much as I love the previous entry, it's admittedly an entry-level option, so why don’t we take things up a notch, eh? And the Klipsch Flexus Core 100 feels like a very natural step-up.
You can often scoop this one up for less than $300 / £300, which is still relatively affordable. But there are a lot of big improvements to be found here, including Dolby Atmos support and considerably stronger bass output.
Yes, when I tested the Klipsch Flexus Core 100, I was wowed by this lil’ soundbar's seismic bass output, with a deep rumble that filled every inch of our testing room. Its powerful bass will be excellent for GTA 6’s firefights, but also for its soundtrack, as Rob explained: “Background music during missions can be quite synthy with prominent beats and bass, and this complements the action really, really nicely — especially when you’re going through, sneaking about or breaking into places”.
Powerful bass never comes at the expense of crystal-clear dialogue, though, and Atmos effects are well-replicated considering the absence of dedicated up-firing drivers. This means that you may not get the almost-tangible height effects that a soundbar with ‘true’ Atmos provides, but the Flexus Core 100 still plates up sound with delicious depth and multi-dimensionality.
3. The premium yet compact option: Sonos Beam Ultra
This next entry currently reigns supreme in our guide to the best soundbars, and for good reason. The Sonos Beam Ultra is, without doubt, one of the greatest soundbars I’ve had the pleasure of testing, offering a brilliant blend of cinematic sound, exquisite design, and wonderful value for money.
Like the previous two entries, this soundbar is still a compact, single-box model, but it provides a huge jump in quality. First of all, the Beam Ultra has dedicated up-firing drivers, meaning you get true Atmos, and the verticality of sound — as well as the width — that this soundbar provides is absolutely sensational. It's perfect for truly immersing yourself in the shenanigans of Vice City.
For such a small soundbar, the bass on offer is astonishing. Whether I was gaming or watching Dolby Atmos movies, I was stunned by the bar’s ability to reach down to the deepest depths with a confident and regimented delivery.
The Beam Ultra can also get seriously loud while still maintaining its composure with movies and music alike, which is ideal for an audio-visual spectacle like GTA 6. Rob spoke to me about a particular montage that's teamed with a famous Dire Straits song, where visual and audio are matched perfectly to the song's beats, and this, he said, is “something you can’t imagine listening to quietly”.
This soundbar is incredibly feature-rich, with a top-class speech enhancement mode, Wi-Fi streaming for high-res music listening, and a companion app for adjusting height effects, EQ, and more. Sure, at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099, it’s by no means cheap, but there aren’t many soundbars in this price category that get close to the Beam Ultra in terms of all-round quality.
4. The multi-box maestro: Samsung HW-Q800F
As amazing as the Sonos Beam Ultra is, it’s still a single-box solution — but what if you want to take things further? Well, the Samsung HW-Q800F could be the perfect pick, as it also delivers sublime sound and Dolby Atmos capabilities, and packs in a separate sub.
With a standalone sub, you’ll feel like you’re playing GTA 6 in a movie theater — forget the living room. The sub packs in almighty low-end power, giving every bass hit, blast, and thump serious venom. Said sub is also paired right out of the box, so you won’t have any confusing set-up processes to sift through.
Beyond its raucous bass, the HW-Q800F is a marvel. It supports both Dolby Atmos and DTS:X and whips up an imposing sense of space, with the noise of gunfire sure to sound as if it's firing into the corners of your room as you play. That’s perfect for the moments where you want to be aware of cops running up on you, or simply want to enjoy the gorgeous sounds of nature in wild areas.
Something else that this 5.1.2 channel model has over the aforementioned entries is HDMI passthrough. This means that you can plug your PS5 or Xbox directly into the soundbar without any trade-offs to picture or audio — a big plus given that you’ll already be taking up a precious HDMI slot to use the soundbar itself.
Mix in some awesome customization options in the SmartThings app, surprisingly strong music playback over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, and the ability to pair compatible surround speakers, and the Samsung HW-Q800F is more than worthy of the five-star score I bestowed upon it. Despite a seemingly high launch price, you can often find it now for less than $600 / £500 — bargain!
5. The ultimate surround sound system: JBL Bar 1300MK2
It's all been building to this: the most luxurious, powerful, three-dimensional, and glorious soundbar on this list: the JBL Bar 1300MK2.
This soundbar is one of the most feature-rich, sonically gifted systems that money can buy, with a main soundbar, sub, and detachable rear speakers which are fully wireless (and can even be used as standalone Bluetooth speakers). It’s the most powerful soundbar I’ve tested by a mile, with a gargantuan maximum power output of almost 2,500W across a total of 29 drivers.
When it comes to surround sound performance, this model is hard to beat, with top-tier Atmos effects and MultiBeam 3.0 technology, which uses beamforming and digital processing to create ultra-immersive audio.
Again, there’s a Night mode, which uses the detachable speakers for late-night gaming sessions; there are loads of connectivity options for playing GTA 6 or listening to music; and there are loads of ways to personalize sound to your specific tastes in the soundbar’s companion software.
This bar supplies rippling bass, word-perfect dialogue, and has a great handling of dynamics for more sudden in-game sounds. It’s also amazing for music, which Rob would undoubtedly appreciate, as he shared that his favorite moments from GTA 6 came from “listening to 80s music while driving around at night under the neon lights”.
As our sit-down came to an end, Rob told me that GTA 6 is “one of the coolest games I’ve ever played, one of the most technically accomplished games I’ve ever played, and one of the best games I’ve ever played”. So, if you want that generational experience to truly blossom, then the JBL Bar 1300MK2 is all you need. I’ve spotted it going for less than $1,200 / £1,200 lately, and for the sheer versatility, might, and talent of this model, it's worth every last penny.
I'm a Senior Reviews Writer here at TechRadar, where I cover a blend of audio-visual gear as well as the latest gaming software and hardware releases.
I've spent years testing soundbars and have reviewed everything from compact budget-friendly models to premium multi-box surround sound systems, meaning I know exactly what makes a standout model.
All of the soundbars in this list have been tested by me personally in our dedicated TV testing space at Future Labs, so they've truly had to impress me to earn a spot on this list.
Rob is the Managing Editor of TechRadar Gaming and Streaming. He joined in 2023 as the Deputy Editor of TechRadar Gaming (TRG), and was a Commissioning Editor and writer at sister-site GamesRadar+ for nearly five years before then, and has multiple years of games media and games writing experience under his belt, with a variety of bylines at games publications, but also in the world of gardens and landscapes.
He has spent around 100 hours playing Grand Theft Auto 6 and wrote our review, awarding it a five-star rating. You'll find his thoughts on the sonic wonders of Rockstar's blockbuster hit scattered throughout this guide.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Harry is a Senior Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He reviews everything from party speakers to wall chargers and has a particular interest in the worlds of audio and gaming. Harry has a background in business tech journalism, particularly around the telecoms industry.

articles.title: Last of Five Defendants Sentenced in US Scattered Spider Hacking Case
articles.text:
A British Scattered Spider hacker will spend six years in a US federal prison for his part in a conspiracy to hack companies and take at least $11.6 million in cryptocurrency from individuals across the US.
Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, from Dundee, Scotland, was arrested in Spain in May 2024 and has been held by US authorities since April 2025. He pleaded guilty in April 2026 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft.
Between September 2021 and April 2023, the Scattered Spider group texted hundreds of phishing lures to staff at telecommunications, technology, interactive entertainment, cloud communications, and cryptocurrency companies.
Links in the texts pointed to phishing websites where recipients were tricked into entering credentials and personal information. Login details captured by the cybercriminals ended up in a Telegram channel managed by Buchanan and an accomplice.
With the stolen credentials, the hackers broke into employee accounts and company systems and took confidential information. That information helped them pinpoint and access cryptocurrency accounts and wallets owned by individuals.
To defeat two-factor authentication, they took over victims’ phone numbers through SIM swaps, moving the numbers to devices under their control.
The theft total has grown from the $8 million cited at the time of Buchanan’s plea. The court will hold a restitution hearing on December 11.
Buchanan is the final defendant in the five-person case to receive a sentence. Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy and Evans Onyeaka Osiebo, both of Texas, were each given 45 months in September and August, respectively.
Noah Michael Urban is serving 10 years in federal prison, while Joel Martin Evans received a two-year term.
Earlier this year, two other Scattered Spider members, Thalha Jubair and Owen Flowers, were sentenced to jail in the United Kingdom for a cyberattack targeting Transport for London (TfL).
