articles.title: Sam Altman warns against a future where AI, not humans, calls the shots | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI co-founder and CEO Sam Altman believes that people should stay in charge of the future when it comes to how AI technology impacts the world and everyone’s lives. Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the AI executive referred to discussions in Silicon Valley about whether there will be a gradual handover to AI — meaning AI will eventually become the decision-making authority across every major industry and institution.
“One thing we’ve been talking a lot about recently is there’s been this thing in Silicon Valley that seems almost ridiculous to have to fight against, but we both believe very deeply that people need to stay in control of the future, and there’s increasing talk about, well, there is either going to be or there should be this sort of gradual handover to AI. And I — we both — agree that that’s a terrible idea,” said Altman, who was sharing the stage with OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman.
The hand-off theory stems from the idea that as AI models become increasingly more powerful, they will learn to improve themselves — a concept known as “recursive self-improvement” or RSI. As existing AI technology builds newer, smarter generations, those will eventually become a superintelligence that humans can no longer control, the belief goes.
Altman explained that he and Brockman only disagree over how to best accomplish the goal of keeping humans in control, or what sort of challenges we should expect to face along the way. However, Altman characterized this as more of a debate between two people who share the same larger views.
“The question of how to actually prevent [handover] from happening — how to actually ensure that we will, given all of the various pressures and given what other companies may try to do — that we are going to actually ensure that people stay in control of the future in a very deep way, and we don’t have this either accidental or intentional handover — I think we can both agree on that,” Altman said.
Brockman added that, as the models improve, there’s an increasing responsibility for alignment, safety, and security, which may require changes in how things are currently done.
“Monitoring is a good example of something where I think we are going to need new … technology,” he said.
Today, AI researchers monitor the model’s chain of thought, where the AI writes out what it’s thinking as it works through problems and performs tasks. But in Brockman’s view, that may not always be the best way to monitor more advanced AI that’s being built now.
“As the models have gotten more capable, they can do more within just the forward path without having to actually write out that thinking, which means we need a new approach to monitoring,” Brockman said. “We’re going to need to deliver that, and I think that there will be points where we need to really think about, as the capabilities get to a certain point, chain-of-thought monitorability is degraded,” he continued, adding that all the problems were technical ones to be solved.
OpenAI had committed to increased chain-of-thought monitoring after the incident where an OpenAI model escaped containment and hacked into the AI model repository Hugging Face. In Wednesday’s interview, Brockman noted that the company told 25% of its production engineers to stop building things and work on securing the AI technology after the hack.
But despite the high-profile breach, he argued that forward progress was still critical to fight bad actors.
“I think to realize that if you look to the level of capabilities of models in the world, and you see cyber models that are coming from that are now … in the hands of threat actors everywhere, that I think that it’s really important that defenders use the most capable models to defend,” he said.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Neon: conheça a nova IA do Google para programação e análise
articles.text:
O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Neon, novo modelo de inteligência artificial (IA) desenvolvido para lidar com tarefas complexas de programação, análise de dados e atividades profissionais. A ferramenta consegue processar diferentes formatos de informação em mesma solicitação e foi projetada para executar trabalhos longos, que envolvem várias etapas e arquivos.
O modelo começou a ser disponibilizado nesta quarta-feira (18) pela API do Gemini no Google AI Studio e no Gemini para empresas. Assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra também terão acesso pelo aplicativo Gemini e pela plataforma de desenvolvimento Google Antigravity.
Um dos principais destaques do Gemini 4 Neon é sua janela de contexto de até um milhão de tokens. Na prática, isso permite que o modelo trabalhe com grandes volumes de informações em mesma tarefa, combinando planilhas, documentos PDF, gráficos, áudios e vídeos para produzir resultados estruturados.
Segundo o Google, a proposta é atender a trabalhos que exigem análise aprofundada e execução de várias etapas, em vez de se limitar a responder perguntas ou produzir textos curtos.
Gemini 4 Neon promete avançar na programação
- O novo modelo foi desenvolvido para lidar com projetos de programação que envolvem diversos arquivos e sessões prolongadas de trabalho. Entre as aplicações estão a identificação de problemas em códigos, a realização de alterações em diferentes partes de um projeto e a reorganização de sistemas existentes;
- Em avaliações divulgadas pelo Google, o Gemini 4 Neon alcançou 65,2% no Terminal-Bench 4.1, teste que avalia a capacidade de modelos de IA de executar tarefas em ambientes de terminal. No FrontierCode 2.0, voltado à avaliação de habilidades de programação, o resultado foi de 46,2%;
- A empresa também destaca o desempenho do modelo em atividades profissionais. No Vals Index, avaliação voltada a tarefas de trabalho, o Neon alcançou 70,9% e ficou na segunda posição;
- Já no Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, que compara modelos de diferentes empresas, obteve pontuação 61 e ficou em terceiro lugar, segundo os dados apresentados pelo Google.
Leia mais:
- Gemini agora permite editar PDFs, documentos e planilhas dentro do chat
- Gemini chega ao Apple CarPlay e permite conversar com IA enquanto dirige
- Google lança IA para programar que promete ser 2,5 vezes mais rápida
Quanto custa usar o Gemini 4 Neon?
O modelo também está disponível por meio de estrutura de cobrança baseada no processamento de tokens, unidades utilizadas pela IA para interpretar e gerar informações.
Os preços anunciados pelo Google são:
- Entrada: US$ 3 (cerca de R$ 17,43) por milhão de tokens;
- Saída: US$ 15 (cerca de R$ 87,15) por milhão de tokens;
- Entrada em cache: US$ 0,15 (cerca de R$ 0,87) por milhão de tokens.
A cobrança varia conforme a quantidade de informações enviada ao modelo e o volume de conteúdo produzido. Por isso, o custo final depende da complexidade e da duração das tarefas realizadas.
Google prepara versão do modelo para segurança cibernética
Outra aplicação prevista para a tecnologia envolve a segurança digital. O Google anunciou versão especializada, chamada Gemini 4 Neon for Cyber, que será disponibilizada nos próximos dias a profissionais de defesa cibernética selecionados.
A ferramenta poderá auxiliar na identificação, validação e correção de vulnerabilidades em códigos. A proposta é ajudar equipes de segurança a encontrar problemas em softwares e desenvolver soluções para proteger sistemas.
O acesso inicial será restrito a integrantes elegíveis do programa Fairwind, iniciativa voltada a profissionais de defesa cibernética.
A novidade amplia a presença da IA nas atividades de segurança digital, área na qual a identificação rápida de falhas pode fazer diferença na proteção de sistemas e infraestruturas.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Can AI Agents Really Shift Chip Design Left?
articles.text:
Agentic AI promises to automate more of the chip flow, but integration with EDA tools and capturing decades of engineering expertise are non-trivial.
Key Takeaways:
Experts at the Table: AI agents are moving into more parts of the chip design flow, but connecting them across different tools and processes remains a challenge. Questions also remain about how to capture decades of engineering expertise, protect proprietary design data, and keep costs manageable. Semiconductor Engineering sat down to discuss these issues with Frank Schirrmeister, executive director of strategy programs and system solutions at Synopsys; Ronen Laviv, vice president of business development and strategic partnerships at Hiveware; Jack Berg, vice president of business development at Silvaco; Ashish Darbari, founder and CEO of Axiomise. What follows are excerpts of that conversation. To view part one of this discussion, click here. Part two is here.
L-R: Silvaco’s Berg; Synopsys’ Schirrmeister; Axiomise’s Darbari; Hiveware’s Laviv.
SE: If AI agents are modifying code, and you keep updating AI models and agents, how much can you really shift left?
Darbari: This is going to be a new methodology direction the industry will be taking, much like UVM, where you combine these different flows together. How do you combine all the agents together? I don’t get a sense that anybody really knows today how this combination is going to work. From what I have seen in different presentations, they’re still looking at how these things unfold. A lot of agentic AI companies lack the field experience of having seen these problems firsthand, so what they’re building is not what the consumer wants. In many cases, the big consumers are building their own stuff because they know what they want. They have the field experience. They have data from many years. So, where will the big EDA vendors go to streamline this, and how will that shape the end use? I don’t know.
Laviv: One of the challenges with emulation is that when running in co-simulation mode, the simulation slows down. Maybe, instead of having UVM or other languages that slow it down, AI will get its own language and get SystemVerilog RTL synthesizable code that you can put in the machine. Then you’ll need less of the software, and you can run faster in emulation. I’m not sure yet if the methodology would change quickly, but UVM might not stay forever.
Darbari: That’s what Nvidia’s head of GPU said at DVCon U.S., isn’t it? The formal is replacing simulation, or is going to replace simulation. I’m less interested in how each of these individual technologies works with each other, but I’m very interested in whether all of this adoption will lead to a coherent story.
Schirrmeister: You have lifecycle, manufacturing, digital implementation, functional verification, and you have specification engineering. Making sense of it is the light bulb — making sure it works, getting it to layout, getting it into the actual physical silicon and 3D, and then observing it during the lifecycle. Each of these flows has many sub-components. Functional verification to emulation is like one of the five. There is virtual prototyping, formal, simulation, emulation, and prototyping. Everybody gets their own agent. So you have an agent doing something localized. Now you start getting an agent that orchestrates these things together as a functional thing, and then you get an agent that connects to the front end. This is an onion of agents, with more and more layers on top. EDA vendors are all saying we have Level 5 stuff, and there’s truth to that within the scope of the operating domain.
Berg: This is very much about hierarchy.
Darbari: But who’s going to pay for all this? Do the small companies have the budget to tokenize their banks and run all of this?
Schirrmeister: Do you mean the guys building the product, or the guys building the tools?
Darbari: The ones running the product. These are the consumers. They would need to pay for the tokens. I have a feeling that only the big companies will be able to afford this. They’ve been running it full-on, saying they haven’t written any code. All of this is agents. But it would get very interesting if the cost of doing all of this could be significantly reduced.
Schirrmeister: What’s exciting about this is that all the smaller designs that used to be difficult because you had to go through all of this will benefit. If you want to be an Nvidia competitor, you still cannot do this out of your garage. That still has to be a big company.
Berg: You’ve got levels of agents at this point, and a Level 5 orchestrating the whole thing. The industry is going to work on building each of these and then iterating and improving them. That’s the only way in which you’re going to get agents to learn and replace large groups of engineers doing the grunt work that’s necessary here.
SE: But that hierarchy needs to start with whatever shifts left to include in each one of these different blocks, right? You need to at least define, in general, what you’re going to be doing.
Berg: You’re going to have information being fed back to ensure that when they go to the specification of the functional, there are constraints placed here. That way, you can improve the probability of manufacturability.
Schirrmeister: Can I have an agent model and predict that path?
Berg: Yes, you can.
Schirrmeister: But you want to check, right? You need to make sure early on what the multi-physics effects of what you’re doing will be.
Berg: Yes, and without that, it will be dead on arrival in manufacturing.
Schirrmeister: So now the question becomes, ‘How much can you really abstract?’
Laviv: AI is doing a great job on, say, 80% of the challenges. But then you have experience from individuals who have been in the industry for 30 years with unique skills that AI doesn’t have. We had a discussion where we talked about 250 different skills for power, emulation, format, and verification. AI doesn’t have those skills today. The industry needs to figure out how to gather those skills in order to really get to a flow where an agent can talk to an agent and has all the decades of experience that is hidden in Apple, Qualcomm, and Intel.
Berg: It took 50 years, but in 2024, the Nobel Prize in chemistry was given in part to a software called AlphaFold, which predicted with uncanny certainty how proteins fold. Proteins are much more complicated than the crystalline structures that we deal with on a daily basis. But it took 50 years to get there. That said, it’s a proof of concept. Whether or not you believe it can be done in semiconductors, it’s going to happen.
Laviv: The difference is that with proteins, everything is open.
Schirrmeister: Yes. Where does the data come from? Simon Davidmann (currently a professor at the University of Southampton) framed it as, ‘We have the big three. They have the base tools, and they build agent stacks on it. That’s why you have a chip stack, or super stack, or whatever.’ We are doing the same thing at Synopsys, and we’ll see who has the best traditional EDA. People who know AI well found EDA. But they need to learn EDA first, rather than the other way around, and they don’t have access to the data they need. The users have access to the data. Samsung talked about optimizing the quality of service for a network-on-chip. They had a fast classic engine, an SoC simulator, an emulator, and they built their own LLM to feed all the data in there. That’s their company data, and it’s not going out to anybody. That’s why they’re doing it themselves. Cognichip said you need LLMs that are trained with real chip designs and people, which is why they hired chip designers and built chips.
SE: They’re also using that intelligence for the LLMs rather than the agents, right?
Schirrmeister: Exactly. And that’s the balance you need.

articles.title: WoW Forever : Blizzard suspend des comptes après l'exploitation d'un bug à 100 pièces d'or par heure
articles.text:
DansWorld of Warcraft Forever, tout coûte cher, surtout quand on n’a pas beaucoup d’or. Et le jeu n’est vraiment pas généreux quand il s’agit de donner des récompenses en validant des quêtes. Du coup, les joueurs et les joueuses courent après l’argent pour se payer la monture épique, monter leurs métiers et s’équiper décemment.
Blizzard avait déjà reconnu que l’économie du jeu posait problème. D’ici à un éventuel ajustement, les braves qui arpentent Azeroth cherchent des astuces pour se remplir les poches facilement et rapidement. En lisant des guides en ligne, en se passant des astuces, en faisant des affaires à l’hôtel des ventes… et parfois en abusant de bugs.
Il y avait justement une gruge que des petits malins avaient fini par voir : dans le Repaire des Noiregueules (Blackmaw Hold), un donjon de niveau 55 à 60, il a été découvert une salle d’une trentaine d’ennemis non élites (des monstres ordinaires, censés rapporter peu) dans laquelle on pouvait obtenir par erreur le butin d’un ennemi d’élite.
D’après les calculs du site spécialisé Wowhead, en enchaînant ces combats en boucle, il était tout à fait possible de dépasser les 100 pièces d’or par heure, et certains acharnés ont prétendu en avoir ramassé des milliers. Au regard de l’économie de WoW Forever, ces centaines ou ces mille pièces d’or constituent une vraie fortune.
Cette arnaque a existé jusqu’au week-end des 14 et 15 novembre, jusqu’au moment où Blizzard a publié un correctif pour faire sauter le bug au cours du 16 novembre.
Quelques centaines de comptes gelés
Mais le studio américain ne s’est pas arrêté là.
Dans un message publié ce mardi 17 novembre sur ses forums, Kaivax, responsable communautaire, a indiqué que les fonctions économiques des comptes de « quelques centaines de joueurs » qui avaient compris qu’il s’agissait d’un bug et farmé ces ennemis pendant des heures, c’est-à-dire tués en boucle pour amasser du butin.
Les sanctions ne s’arrêtent pas là : Blizzard est aussi en train de retirer cet or excédentaire des comptes ou de l’hôte des vente, y compris celui tiré de la revente des objets. Quant à celles et ceux qui ont vraiment trop abusé de ce bug, Blizzard a également appliqué des suspensions ponctuelles. Il n’est pas précisé si des suspensions définitives ont été décidées.
Il faut dire que la pression était forte : sous l’article de Wowhead comme sur Reddit, beaucoup réclamaient le retrait de l’or. Des internautes suspectaient même des streamers de couper leur diffusion pour farmer tranquillement, à l’abri des regards et pour éviter de partager l’astuce, et accessoirement pour ne pas attirer l’attention de Blizzard.
En revanche, ceux qui ont fait le donjon quelques fois sans rien savoir ne risquent rien.

articles.title: « Je vois tout » : le système testé par l'armée de Terre prédit les déplacements ennemis
articles.text:
Le 152e régiment d'infanterie fabrique désormais ses propres drones et s'est doté d'une section dédiée. Mise à l’épreuve fin juin au camp de Mourmelon, elle illustre la mue de l’armée de Terre face aux nouvelles menaces.
Dans le dernier numéro d'Esprit défense, un magazine du ministère des Armées paru le 16 novembre 2026, une partie est consacrée au fameux 152e régiment d'infanterie, qui dispose désormais de sa propre section drone. Le ministère revient sur ses débuts au camp de Mourmelon, cette année. Le magazine des Armées revient sur un camp d'expérimentation mené en juin et juillet derniers, destiné à valider la transformation engagée par le régiment trois ans plus tôt. Des drones, radars, missiles et industriels étaient réunis, avec l'ambition de mettre l'innovation au service de la victoire.
Ce régiment de l’armée de Terre fabrique désormais ses propres drones
Alors que certains pays « s'engagent sur la voie de la domination », selon les mots du magazine, les unités opérationnelles musclent leur outil de défense, et le 152e RI ne fait pas exception Sa vedette est la Section drone régimentaire (SDR), inaugurée quelques jours avant la manœuvre du 25 juin. Chez les Diables rouges, surnom du 152e RI, elle assure la reconnaissance et la frappe à longue portée. Et tout est allé vite, au régiment comme dans le reste de l'armée de Terre. « Le régiment a acquis son premier drone en 2019. Aujourd'hui, il en fabrique », résume le lieutenant-colonel Benoît, son chef opérations. Le reportage montre aussi des drones FPV, pilotés en immersion totale grâce à une caméra haute définition couplée aux lunettes de l'opérateur, utiles pour la reconnaissance avancée mais aussi pour neutraliser un objectif.
Ce jeudi-là, la compagnie d'appui a une mission. Elle doit arrêter une progression ennemie, à deux kilomètres seulement de la ligne adverse. Le drone du soldat de première classe Landry décolle, et en quelques secondes, un blindé est neutralisé. L'explosif est fictif, exercice oblige, mais le système qui l'emporte a bien été conçu par les dronistes du régiment, une trouvaille maison encouragée par la cellule dédiée à l'innovation. « Notre métier évolue avec son temps », savoure le soldat, qui trouve « exaltant » de participer à ce changement.
Mais il n'est pas question pour autant de tout miser sur la machine. « Le drone seul ne suffit pas pour vaincre », prévient le lieutenant-colonel Benoît. Selon lui, l'engin s'inscrit dans un système de combat global qu'il reste à définir et à ériger en doctrine. Et le matériel ne fait pas le soldat. « L'intégration technologique ne se limite pas à une question d'équipement », insiste l'officier. Il faut former, entraîner, sans sacrifier les savoir-faire fondamentaux du fantassin.
Guerre électronique : quand le radar voit venir l'ennemi
Avant de frapper, vous serez d'accord avec nous pour dire qu'il faut voir. Pour la section de reconnaissance et de guerre électronique (SRGE), l'exercice est lui aussi celui des premières fois. Elle teste le radar à impulsion Murin, doté d'une fonction d'aide au tir, qui détecte une compagnie adverse sur engins blindés à trois kilomètres. Elle teste aussi Vénus, l'interface de pilotage du radar, qui affiche et transmet les informations en temps réel. « Je vois tout », s'exclame le sergent Aymeric, chef de groupe. D'après lui, l'outil estime le type, l'allure et le nombre d'engins, et il « prédit leur déplacement ».
Il faut encore confirmer. Alors, le chef de section fait appel au système Esus, encore en expérimentation, situé à 500 mètres du groupe, qui détecte et sectorise les ondes militaires. Le renseignement est validé, l'ordre de frappe part vers la SDR, c'est la frappe de Landry. Son équipe a tout juste le temps de se replier qu'Esus signale une nouvelle menace, un véhicule de combat d'infanterie armé d'un canon. Un drone Parrot Anafi s'élance d'un abri pour le reconnaître, puis un binôme met en place un missile moyenne portée (MMP). Le missile antichar fait mouche, sous l'œil de tireurs d'élite quasi invisibles, prêts à riposter.
Rien de tout cela ne s'est fait en vase clos. La SRGE a été formée par le 54e régiment de transmissions et la 785e compagnie de guerre électronique, deux spécialistes de la guerre des ondes. Le régiment travaille avec des industriels, notamment Thales, Airbus et Procomm. Certains étaient présents sur le camp pour former les fantassins et récolter leurs retours en temps réel, afin d'ajuster si besoin les équipements. Le général Maxime Do Tran, qui commande la 7e brigade blindée, estime que les armes des premières phases de la guerre moderne, comme les drones, seront sans doute les plus technologiques, et celles des dernières phases relèveront du combat rapproché. Comme il le dit si bien, « la guerre allie innovation et rusticité. »

articles.title: GTA 6 : le PSN a flanché la veille, tenu à minuit, puis rechuté au réveil — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le scénario que redoutaient les joueurs PS5, un PlayStation Network à terre au moment du déblocage de GTA 6, ne s’est pas produit. Ce mercredi 18 novembre au soir, pourtant, le réseau de Sony a donné des sueurs froides. Les signalements ont grimpé vers 18 h 30 sur Downdetector, avec un pic autour de 19 h. Les joueurs décrivaient des échecs de connexion, des messages d’erreur et des difficultés à lancer jeux et applications.
Sony a déclaré un incident à 19 h 58 sur sa page d’état, sur le service « Jeux et réseaux sociaux ». Vers 20 h 30, cette même page affichait de nouveau tous les services comme opérationnels. Le constructeur n’a en revanche rien dit de l’origine de la panne.
    Pour aller plus loin
GTA 6 est disponible en France : suivez le lancement du jeu en direct
            
Un contexte explosif
Le moment rendait l’incident particulièrement sensible. Sony venait de déployer sur PS5, ce mardi 17 novembre, une mise à jour système obligatoire pour lancer GTA 6, la version 26.07-14.23.00, et de nombreux joueurs avaient déjà préchargé les 212 Go du jeu. Rien n’indique officiellement un lien direct avec GTA 6, mais le calendrier alimente forcément les soupçons. Avant l’ouverture, les joueurs craignaient ainsi que leur console ne parvienne pas à vérifier la licence du jeu au moment crucial.
La pression sur le réseau est à la mesure de l’événement. Selon Jeuxvideo.com, GTA 6 est le jeu le plus précommandé de l’histoire du PlayStation Store. Aux États-Unis, l’opérateur Comcast a en outre constaté que les 48 premières heures de préchargement avaient représenté le plus gros pic de trafic de son histoire.
Minuit, le réseau a tenu
À minuit, quand GTA 6 est devenu jouable en France, le réseau a pourtant tenu. Le PSN est resté stable à l’ouverture, sans panne notable. Le jeu tournait d’ailleurs depuis midi (heure de Paris) en Nouvelle-Zélande, puis depuis l’après-midi en Australie, au Japon et en Corée du Sud.
Nouvelle alerte au petit matin
Le calme n’a pas duré toute la nuit. Ce jeudi 19 novembre, vers 6 h 30, quelques minutes après le déblocage du jeu aux États-Unis et au Canada, la page d’état de Sony a de nouveau signalé des perturbations sur « Jeux et réseaux sociaux », en Amérique comme en Europe. En outre, le PlayStation Store était indiqué totalement hors service sur notre continent. Peu après 7 h, les problèmes de connexion aux jeux étaient résolus, mais la boutique restait en panne en Europe au moment où nous écrivons ces lignes.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelle console acheter pour jouer à GTA 6 le 19 novembre ?
            
Le plus dur reste à venir
Il serait donc prématuré de crier victoire. La vraie épreuve arrivera dans la journée et ce soir, quand ceux qui ont travaillé ou dormi se connecteront en masse. Le jeu sort sans mode multijoueur, mais il n’existe qu’en version numérique, même en boîte (qui ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement). Le PSN et le PlayStation Store restent donc un passage obligé pour activer son code, télécharger le jeu ou récupérer ses mises à jour.
Les bons réflexes en cas de panne
En cas de souci, consultez d’abord la page d’état de PlayStation. C’est la référence officielle, même si elle réagit souvent avec un temps de retard sur les remontées des joueurs. Recoupez ensuite avec Downdetector avant de toucher aux réglages de votre console. Si le jeu refuse de se lancer, la restauration des licences (Paramètres > Utilisateurs et comptes > Autre > Restaurer les licences) peut débloquer la situation, à condition que le PSN réponde.
    Pour aller plus loin
GTA 6 débloqué sur Xbox : tout le monde peut le télécharger, même sans l’acheter
            
Notez aussi que l’option Partage de console et jeu hors ligne (Paramètres > Utilisateurs et comptes > Autre) permet à la PS5 sur laquelle elle est activée de lancer les jeux achetés et téléchargés sans passer par le PSN. Sony n’a toutefois pas précisé si cela suffit pour GTA 6 le jour de sa sortie.
Pour l’instant, Sony sort donc plutôt indemne de ce premier test, malgré la fausse note de ce matin. Reste à voir si cette stabilité survivra au week-end, qui s’annonce comme le véritable crash-test du réseau.
Tout savoir sur GTA 6 (gameplay, trailer, précommandes)
Les choses accélèrent du côté de Rockstar depuis le début des précommandes pour GTA 6. Prix officiel en France : 80 euros. Surtout, la troisième bande-annonce de GTA 6 est enfin sortie sur Netflix et YouTube à la fin du mois d’août pour montrer de nombreux éléments de gameplay dans le cadre d’un aperçu large très attendu.
Nous avons d’ailleurs décortiqué les 27 minutes de vidéo pour vous résumer tout ce qu’il fallait retenir du gameplay de GTA 6.
Pour aller plus loin, voici, ci-après, quelques lectures intéressantes.
- Ce qui cloche avec l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6.
- Les multiples pannes provoquées par l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6.
- Pourquoi il vous faut forcément un compte pour regarder le trailer sur YouTube.
Rendez-vous enfin le 19 novembre pour la sortie officielle de GTA 6 qui n’a que trop souvent été repoussée.

articles.title: Senkung der Stromsteuer: Die Koalition verschiebt die Probleme nur
articles.text:
Senkung der Stromsteuer: Die Koalition verschiebt die Probleme nur
Na bitte, geht doch, könnte man nach dem Gezerre um die Stromsteuer sagen. Die Koalition hat in einer stundenlangen Sitzung beschlossen, die Stromsteuer auch für Privathaushalte auf das europäische Mindestmaß zu senken. Für Unternehmen gilt eine solche Regelung schon länger.
Dass ein durchschnittlicher Haushalt dadurch lediglich vier bis acht Euro im Monat sparen wird – geschenkt. In diesem Fall ist schon die Geste viel wert. Alles andere wäre nämlich ein Desaster gewesen: für Friedrich Merz persönlich (er hatte die Senkung gefordert), für die Glaubwürdigkeit der Koalition (die Senkung wurde im Koalitionsvertrag versprochen) und für die gesamte Energiewende sowieso (Elektrifizierung ist ein entscheidender Hebel zur Senkung der Emissionen).
Stromsteuer-Senkung ist mehr ein Provisorium als gesichert
Doch die Koalition wäre nicht die Koalition, wenn sie nicht an entscheidender Stelle wieder nur ein halbgares und halbherziges Provisorium angerichtet hätte. Die Steuersenkung ist nämlich nur auf das Jahr 2027 befristet. Alles darüber hinaus steht unter Finanzierungsvorbehalt.
Man darf sich also darauf einstellen, dass das einmal Erreichte bei jeder neuen Haushaltsverhandlung wieder infragegestellt wird. Dabei sehnen sich Unternehmen und Privatpersonen vor allem nach Planungssicherheit. Wer jetzt vor der Entscheidung steht, sich eine Wärmepumpe oder ein E-Auto anzuschaffen, dem ist mit dem aktuellen Kabinettsbeschluss wenig geholfen. Seine Lenkungswirkung dürfte überschaubar bleiben.
Geld für fossile Brennstoffe sitzt lockerer
Dass die Koalition sich auch schnell und geräuschlos einigen kann, hat sie schon mehrfach gezeigt. Leider bei den falschen Dingen. Bei den beiden Tankrabatten in diesem Jahr waren die Milliarden beispielsweise hopplahopp da. Das Geld für fossile Subventionen sitzt offenbar immer etwas lockerer als das für die Unterstützung der Energiewende.
Ein anderes Beispiel ist die Gasspeicherumlage. Bisher wurde sie von den Gaskunden bezahlt. Doch im Herbst 2025 beschloss die Koalition, sie mit Steuergeldern zu begleichen. Das hört sich zwar nach einer Verschiebung von der linken Tasche in die rechte Tasche an, doch das täuscht: Steuern zahlen praktisch alle Bürger und Bürgerinnen, aber nicht jeder verbraucht auch Gas. Die Summe der Steuerzahlenden subventioniert also den Gaskonsum einer Teilgruppe. Ähnliches gilt auch für Stromsteuer und Tankrabatt: Jeder verbraucht Strom, aber nur eine Minderheit fährt Auto.
Senkung der Stromsteuer ließe sich für ein Jahr gegenfinanzieren
Wenn die Koalition also wieder mal verzweifelt nach Milliarden sucht: Geld wäre genug da. Die wirklich knappe Ressource ist politischer Mut, sich an die Subventionen für fossile Brennstoffe zu wagen. Ansgar Heveling, Präsident des Bundesrechnungshofes, beziffert diese auf 17 Milliarden Euro pro Jahr. Zum Vergleich: Die nun beschlossene Senkung der Stromsteuer kostet den Fiskus etwa 5,4 Milliarden Euro. Allein durch den jüngsten Tankrabatt (rund 2,5 Milliarden Euro) und durch die Gasspeicherumlage (3,4 Milliarden Euro) ließe sich die Senkung der Stromsteuer für ein Jahr gegenfinanzieren. Von den steuerlichen Privilegien für Diesel, Kerosin und Dienstwagen ganz zu schweigen.
))) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Este pueblo madrileño ha encontrado la fórmula para dar prioridad a sus vecinos en vivienda pública: exige llevar 10 años empadronado
articles.text:
Mientras miramos con recelo el modelo de Praga, la vivienda en Madrid vive subidas históricas (el alquiler medio va camino de los 2.130 euros al mes, superando con mucho el salario base). Pues bien, esta es la nueva fórmula con la que la Comunidad de Madrid planea reservar el 75% de su parque de viviendas: que optar a un piso protegido de alquiler en Guadarrama implique haber vivido al menos diez años allí. El problema es que los vecinos que el mercado ya expulsó del pueblo no cuentan, y los que más necesitan una vivienda protegida son, justamente, los que no han podido quedarse.
La fórmula. 58 viviendas son las afectadas a este convenio de protección pública en alquiler. El lugar, Las Laderas. Son 24 pisos de dos dormitorios y 34 de tres, con un presupuesto de 14,2 millones. Seguirán como alquiler al menos otros 20 años. Los ingresos del hogar han de situarse entre 1,5 y 5 veces el IPREM.
Con un IPREM de 600 euros, eso es entre 900 y 3.000 euros al mes. Las obras ya empezaron, pero no hay fecha de adjudicación. Un 75 % de los pisos (43), se reservará a quien demuestre más de diez años de empadronamiento en Guadarrama. El resto se adjudicará siguiendo la normativa general.
No es solo Guadarrama. La Comunidad firmó el mismo día seis convenios con Guadarrama, Villa del Prado, Móstoles y Valdemoro. Es decir, este criterio se está extendiendo. Y suman 676 viviendas y 138 millones, de los que el Gobierno regional pone más de 113. En los cuatro municipios, el 75% se reserva a quien lleve diez años en el padrón local. En Guadarrama gobierna el PP gobierna en coalición con Vox, y el convenio se firma tras el rechazo al borrador regional. Esta política, por tanto, responde al motto Madrid para los madrileños de siempre.
¿Y a quién esperan? Literalmente, el argumento oficial es proteger al vecino de siempre. El alcalde, Diosdado Soto, presume de que el pueblo llevaba años sin oferta: habló de 12 en 2023 y de más de 20 en la nota de este mes. Quiere que esta promoción sea “la primera de otras”.
Sin embargo, ¿quién entra en el 75%? Porque cumple el filtro quien ya aguantó diez años en el pueblo, como decíamos, no quien se marchó porque no podía pagar, ni el joven que se emancipa, ni quien llegó hace cinco años a trabajar. Y hablamos de un salto interanual de casi el 17% en julio y subiendo. En este desplazamiento gobierna el padrón, no el trabajo.
10 años, como la nacionalidad. Es el mismo plazo que España exige para nacionalizarse por residencia. En Canarias, un decreto pide 12 años de arraigo para vivienda pública y ya tiene la primera demanda, al ser tachado de irrazonable: en una década la vida de una persona puede virar de recién emancipado a casado con hijos.
En Madrid, la propia Comunidad tanteó el mismo camino en el borrador del nuevo reglamento de vivienda protegida de marzo. Exigía 10 años de padrón en la región para comprar y 10 para alquilar. Tras el rechazo social, rebajó el alquiler a 5. Más Madrid denunció que la norma trataba como ciudadanos de segunda a cientos de miles de personas llegadas de otros países o provincias.
Paradoja comarcal. El borrador regional sigue sin aprobarse: debe pasar por la Comisión Jurídica Asesora y volver al Consejo de Gobierno. Los convenios de Guadarrama reclaman el doble de plazo que los de la Comunidad. Algo parecido ocurre con el Plan Vive, que ya subió de tres a cinco años el padrón o vínculo laboral exigible en el municipio. La vara de medir sube a medida que bajan los pisos disponibles.

articles.title: Karnataka picks 8 startups for government projects worth nearly Rs 2 crore
articles.text:
Karnataka picks 8 startups for government projects worth nearly Rs 2 crore
Karnataka has picked eight startups to pilot solutions with government departments, with the Praja Seva Department and BWSSB committing projects worth nearly Rs 2 crore.
Karnataka is looking to bring startups closer to the people who use public services.
The state government has selected eight startups under its Government First Initiative, allowing them to deploy their technology within government departments and address public sector challenges.
Announced on the opening day of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), the selection covers four startups each for the Praja Seva Department and the Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB).
The two departments have a combined committed project value of nearly Rs 2 crore, inclusive of GST.
The initiative, launched by the Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology (IT & BT), Government of Karnataka, aims to make government departments potential customers for startups.
Rather than limiting innovation to demonstrations and proof-of-concept projects, the programme gives selected companies an opportunity to test market-ready solutions in real government environments.
Startups tackle citizen service challenges
The Praja Seva Department received 76 applications across four problem statements, covering AI-enabled grievance management, a unified citizen call centre, e-Office workflows and the availability of citizen-facing government IT services.
Four startups were selected, with a total committed project value of Rs 99.78 lakh, inclusive of GST.
SanMejora was selected for AI-enabled grievance management and redressal, while VTT AI Private Limited will work on the unified citizen call centre. Datafrontier Innovations Private Limited was chosen for the e-Office and officer workflow challenge, and Nife Apps Labs Pvt Ltd for ensuring the uptime of government IT services.
BWSSB received 74 applications across five challenge areas. These included reducing non-revenue water, planning treated wastewater reuse, intelligent asset management, GIS-enabled revenue and operational intelligence, and digital twins for integrated water management.
The selected startups are Smart Terra, UniaX Technologies, Krishi Hrudya Private Limited and Calypsion Innovations LLP. Each has been allocated Rs 25 lakh, taking the department's total committed project value to Rs 1 crore, inclusive of GST.
Selected startups could receive work orders of up to Rs 25 lakh
The programme allows selected startups to pilot, test and validate their solutions in partnership with the respective government departments. Subject to technical evaluation and programme guidelines, they will be eligible for direct work orders of up to Rs 25 lakh each.
The selection process involved five stages: application submission, eligibility screening, evaluation by the selection committee, discussions with officials from the respective departments, and final budget discussions.
Applications were invited between October 8 and October 23, 2026. Proposals were assessed on innovation, technical soundness, product readiness, relevance to government requirements, scalability and integration capabilities.
Speaking at the announcement, Shri Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home and Information Technology, Biotechnology and E-Governance, Government of Karnataka, said, "The Government First Initiative reflects our commitment to making government an active partner and customer of Karnataka's startup ecosystem.
We want to create opportunities for startups to take their innovations beyond the proof-of-concept stage and demonstrate their solutions in real-world governance settings."
He added that connecting startups with government departments could help translate homegrown innovation into measurable public impact and create opportunities for wider adoption.
Through the initiative, Karnataka aims to give startups a route to government procurement while helping public departments adopt technology-led solutions. The pilot deployments will also allow the government to assess how these products perform against actual administrative and infrastructure challenges.

articles.title: Bitcoin: cuál es el valor de esta criptomoneda
articles.text:
El bitcoin, la primera moneda virtual lanzada al mercado, fue creado por Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudónimo) en 2008 tras la crisis financiera que afectó al mundo; esta divisa digital tenía como base un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales.
Conocido en el mundo de los mercados bajo las siglas BTC, el bitcoin utiliza la criptografía para garantizar que su gestión sea descentralizada, es decir, que no pueda ser regulado por ninguna institución u organismo bancario, lo que a su vez hace que las criptomonedas sean volátiles.
Pese al avance y alcance que ha tenido el Bitcoin y otros activos digitales de gran talla como Ethereum, organismos como el Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) y el Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) aún se muestran dudosos sobre los "pros" de este tipo de criptomonedas.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El precio de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 64063.59 dólares. Esto quiere decir que la moneda digital presentó un cambio de -1.31% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
Bitcoin alcanzó su máximo histórico
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: DycoVue wants to make sure your hospital never loses your X-ray
articles.text:
If you’ve ever had a brain scan, the strange noises of the machine might be the first thing to scare you. Staying still while it makes its clanging noises is another challenge, but what really gets you is the anxiety of waiting for a radiologist to interpret the images and tell you what is happening inside your head. In Nigeria, where radiologists are in short supply, getting that report can be another hurdle.
During her five years as an advanced nurse practitioner in the United States, Kafilat Shobajo had encountered several cases where radiology reports missed fractures or other abnormalities she could identify from examining patients and reviewing their X-rays. In the two years before speaking to TechCabal in November, she said she had caught at least five errors that could have changed a patient’s diagnosis or treatment. The experiences made her question how much room there was for such oversights in a healthcare system that struggles with a shortage of specialists.
A 2025 study published in BMC Medical Education estimated that Nigeria had fewer than 700 radiologists, or roughly one for every 660,000 people. Shobajo’s own assessment of the facilities she spoke with revealed that some radiologists were working across at least three hospitals.
However, the shortage of specialists was only part of the problem. Before building a product, Shobajo mentioned that her team conducted a three-month pilot to understand the needs of diagnostic centres and clinics. They found that many facilities were not properly storing the medical images they produced.
“During our pilot, the majority of the facilities had their images stored on WhatsApp or Telegram,” Shobajo said.
She told TechCabal that her first instinct had been to build an artificial intelligence tool that could help radiologists and frontline clinicians interpret medical images. However, medical AI models are only as useful as the data they learn from, and Shobajo was concerned that models trained on images from other populations might not produce accurate results for African patients.
“Our tumours are larger, so chances are if they bring that model here, it’s not going to be accurate,” she said. “What DycoVue does is we build the infrastructure for clinics in digital imaging. So before you can start saying you’re going to use AI to help interpret your medical images, hospitals need to store their data first.”
This led her to build DycoVue, a healthtech startup developing software that helps healthcare facilities manage their medical imaging records, including storing, organising, retrieving and sharing the images with the healthcare professionals involved in a patient’s care, in 2025.
How DycoSuite works
The company’s main product is DycoSuite, an imaging management system built around a technology known as a Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS). PACS systems allow healthcare facilities to store, retrieve and share medical images digitally. DycoSuite is designed to replace the scattered films, CDs and images shared across messaging apps with a central system where a patient’s imaging records can be stored and retrieved when needed.
Shobajo says the system is designed to fit into a clinic’s existing imaging workflow, rather than requiring staff to manually upload every scan. When a diagnostic centre signs up, DycoVue’s engineers visit the facility to connect its imaging equipment to the platform. Once the connection is set up, images are transferred to the system as they are produced.
“It automatically goes to the cloud. We have engineers that can come and ensure that. If clinics are interested in using DycoVue, we would come to their clinic, do a demo for them to see the product, our engineers will make the connection, and that’s it,” Shobajo said.
The company also said it provides ongoing technical support after installation. Shobajo says this is important because deploying software is only useful if clinics can rely on it when they need it. Patients are shared a link that contains the images from the scan.
Once images are stored centrally, clinicians can retrieve earlier scans and compare them with newer ones. A patient who returns with the same complaint would not have to rely on a physical film or remember which facility holds an earlier image, as the doctor would be able to access the previous scan from the cloud. Shobajo said the platform also allows radiologists to review images remotely instead of being physically present at the diagnostic centre. Shobajo says DycoVue wants to reduce the time patients spend waiting for their results, with a target of delivering them within 15 minutes.
DycoSuite is also intended to bring imaging and laboratory information together under a patient’s record. Shobajo argues that diagnosing and monitoring a condition can involve several tests, and the results should be accessible together rather than scattered across different systems.
“Whatever they’re doing, whether it’s images or labs related to the same issue, the same patient information should be under one bucket,” she said.
DycoAtlas, the company’s second product, is a needs-assessment and mapping tool intended to help governments, healthcare planners and philanthropies understand where diagnostic facilities and equipment are located, what services they offer and what prevents them from operating effectively. So far, the team has surveyed 240 facilities across four states, according to Shobajo. The team also records facility coordinates because it found that some diagnostic centres it visited were not listed on Google Maps.
Building the infrastructure for AI-assisted imaging
DycoVue has been operating since 2025 and has so far funded its operations without external investment, according to Shobajo. The company currently has five team members, split between Nigeria and the United States. Shobajo said the startup recently signed its first paying user, a private diagnostic centre in Nigeria, where the team is deploying the product. She did not disclose how the company charges facilities.
According to the company, its pilot helped two facilities digitise more than 100,000 medical images covering about 600 patients, with records dating from 2023 to 2026.
Shobajo explained that DycoVue’s priority is to get the product into more facilities and demonstrate that clinics can use it to manage their imaging records. Shobajo says the company is considering raising capital in 2027 to improve its existing products and expand its reach. The company wants to connect DycoSuite to electronic medical record (EMR) systems already used by healthcare providers, creating a more connected record of patients’ diagnostic history.
That groundwork is also central to the company’s plans for AI-assisted medical imaging. Shobajo says DycoVue hopes to begin developing this capability in 2027. She argues that storing images over time is important for tracking how a patient’s condition changes and for building datasets that can support AI models.

articles.title: 800 V et 660 km d'autonomie : la Leapmotor B05 fait un bond de géant… mais pas pour nous !
articles.text:
Fraîchement lancée chez nous, la Leapmotor B05 s’apprête déjà à recevoir des améliorations de circonstance en Chine. La marque a en effet confirmé l’arrivée d’une version optimisée de sa compacte électrique au Salon de l’Automobile de Guangzhou, qui se tiendra le 27 novembre prochain. Outre un équipement enrichi, c’est surtout la technique qui fait un bond de géant, avec l’adoption d’une plateforme 800 V.
Les temps de recharge seront donc logiquement revus à la baisse. Rappelons que le modèle actuel annonce un 10 à 80 % de batterie en 27 minutes grâce à une puissance de charge de 174 kW avec l’accumulateur de 67,1 kWh. Ce n’est déjà pas si mal, les autres modèles du groupe effectuant plutôt le 20 à 80 % en 30 minutes… Aucune information n’a cependant été communiquée sur les nouvelles performances à la borne.
Jusqu’à 660 km d’autonomie : un rayon d’action en nette hausse
On devrait probablement glisser sous les 25 minutes, ce qui renforcera encore l’attractivité du modèle. Passer moins de temps à recharger, c’est bien. Aller plus loin ensuite, c’est encore mieux ! Bonne nouvelle, l’autonomie progressera aussi, avec jusqu’à 660 km sur le cycle CLTC. Cela correspondrait à environ 500 km sur notre norme WLTP, ce qui reste supérieur aux 482 km d’autonomie du modèle actuel.
Côté équipement, cette B05 révisée gagne un affichage tête haute en réalité augmentée, un écran tactile agrandi à 17,3 pouces, des sièges zéro gravité et 14 haut-parleurs. L’habitacle est sinon identique à la version sortante, avec une planche de bord toujours aussi impersonnelle. Et de dehors aussi, la compacte ne change guère. Son design assez standard ne bascule pas outre mesure dans la folie.
Une arrivée en Europe déjà compromise par la stratégie de la marque
Sauf à prendre la version Ultra, qui n’est malheureusement pas disponible chez nous : celle-ci ajoute une lame avant, des jupes latérales, un diffuseur et un aileron plus généreux. La garde au sol a aussi été abaissée d’un petit centimètre. A défaut d’avoir la variante Ultra, avons-nous donc plus de chances de voir cette B05 améliorée arriver en Europe ? Pas vraiment pour des raisons d’ordre stratégique.
Il suffit de voir ce qui s’est passé avec le B10 pour anticiper le même scénario avec la B05. Des responsables voyaient mal remplacer aussi tôt un véhicule fraîchement commercialisé chez nous. Ils évoquent notamment une dynamique d’achat sensiblement différente entre la Chine et l’Europe, où les nouveaux modèles se présentent à intervalles réguliers. Nul doute donc qu’il faudra aussi attendre un cycle de quelques années pour espérer voir une B05 améliorée.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.text:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.
Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds
Understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.
However, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.
At RUN, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.
Tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.
To appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.
Making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.
Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling
To observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.
In the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.
The researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.
Simon Maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "By varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond."
This approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.
What makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.
This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.
"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.
A Surprising 500-Attosecond Delay
To understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with Prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit."
Their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.
At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.
For example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit."
The team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.
The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.
A Hidden Tradeoff Between Space and Time
Raffael Spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "The more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially."
In other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.
To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.
This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.
Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.
The findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.
Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?
Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.
One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.
Transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.
Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.
"In the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains Prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.
The implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.
"In the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant CMOS technology," adds Prof. Rupert Huber.
That possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.
For Repp and Huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Regensburg. Original written by Karoline Stürmer. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- S. Maier, R. Spachtholz, K. Glöckl, C. M. Bustamante, S. Lingl, M. Maczejka, J. Schön, A. Riedel, K. Richter, F. J. Giessibl, F. P. Bonafé, M. A. Huber, A. Rubio, J. Repp, R. Huber. Tracking electrons at the space-time limit. Nature Photonics, 2026; 20 (8): 961 DOI: 10.1038/s41566-026-01932-0

articles.title: Al menos el 10% de la población mundial sufre un uso problemático del internet: “Hay que priorizar la salud pública frente a la industria”
articles.text: Una mujer consulta Instagram en su teléfono móvil. Existe un término. Se inventó durante la década de los noventa y se llama “adicción al internet”. Pero ya no es suficiente, se ha quedado obsoleto. Por ello, la Comisión de la prestigiosa revista The Lancet Psychiatry ha decidido emplear otro: “Uso problemático del internet” (PUI, en inglés). Y las razones no son muy halagüeñas. En un documento publicado este jueves , la Comisión estima que el PUI afecta al menos al 10% de la población mundial. Una situación que abarca desde los trastornos por apuestas y videojuegos en línea , pasando por el consumo adictivo del porno , hasta llegar a conductas “emergentes” como la cibercondría —los hipocondriacos de siempre, solo que ahora potenciados por las infinitas y aterradoras posibilidades de la red—. Los autores del artículo urgen a los gobiernos y a todas las instituciones involucradas a “priorizar la salud pública por encima de los intereses de la industria”. Seguir leyendo

articles.title: Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
articles.text:
Instagram’s latest update will allow you to edit your Stories without losing your views, likes, or replies. You can now edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings for up to 15 minutes after sharing your Story, Instagram head Adam Mosseri has announced.
Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
You can edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings in your Stories for up to 15 minutes after sharing.
Reverse engineer Alessandro Paluzzi first spotted Instagram working on this feature in April, but now it’s official. Previously, you had to delete and repost your Story to fix a typo or add a song that you forgot to include.
You can edit your post by opening your Story and selecting the three-dot menu in the bottom-right corner. From there, tap “Edit Story” to start making changes.
In addition to editable Stories, Instagram announced that it’s launching new fonts, colors, and shapes for stickers, as well as presenting them on sticker sheets that are supposed to be easier to browse. The platform is also making changes to the way you select multiple photos and adding new blur, colors, and gradient background options.

articles.title: MPT processa 99 e pede R$ 100 milhões por programa para motoristas
articles.text:
O Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) entrou na Justiça contra a 99 Tecnologia para tentar suspender o programa Taxa Zero, que permite aos motoristas pagar antecipadamente para trabalhar sem descontos por corrida. O órgão também pede a devolução dos valores desembolsados pelos profissionais e indenização de R$ 100 milhões por danos morais coletivos.
A ação civil pública foi ajuizada após o lançamento da modalidade, em 9 de junho deste ano, em 25 cidades brasileiras. Na ocasião, a empresa informou que poderia ampliar o programa para outras regiões do país.
O Taxa Zero funciona como uma espécie de assinatura. Em vez de pagar uma porcentagem à plataforma a cada viagem, o motorista antecipa um valor para utilizar o aplicativo sem a cobrança da taxa de serviço.
Existem duas modalidades: uma com validade de 24 ou 72 horas e outra vinculada a um limite de faturamento. Nesta segunda opção, o profissional paga antecipadamente para trabalhar sem taxas até alcançar o valor estabelecido pela empresa.
Para o MPT, porém, o modelo transfere aos trabalhadores riscos que deveriam ser assumidos pela plataforma. Isso porque pagar pela adesão não garante que o motorista receberá corridas suficientes para recuperar o investimento.
MPT questiona cobrança e distribuição de corridas da 99
- Um dos principais argumentos da ação envolve o funcionamento do algoritmo da plataforma. Pelos próprios termos do programa, a distribuição das viagens continua sendo feita pelo sistema da 99 e também pode contemplar motoristas que não aderiram ao Taxa Zero;
- Na avaliação do Ministério Público, isso significa que o profissional pode pagar para trabalhar sem taxas, mas não tem garantia de receber quantidade mínima de corridas ou obter receita suficiente para compensar o gasto;
- A ação também questiona o mecanismo de cobrança. Segundo o MPT, quando o motorista não possui saldo para quitar o valor devido, a plataforma pode reter automaticamente remunerações futuras;
- Para os procuradores, essa dinâmica pode gerar uma situação de dependência econômica e endividamento permanente. O órgão sustenta que o mecanismo pode configurar servidão por dívida, prática associada pela legislação brasileira ao trabalho em condição análoga à escravidão.
“O mecanismo de cobrança do Taxa Zero cria estrutura objetiva de endividamento permanente: o motorista que não possui saldo suficiente tem suas futuras remunerações retidas automática e integralmente pela ré”, afirmam os procuradores na ação.
O procurador Marcello Ribeiro Silva, responsável por assinar o processo, argumenta que a prática pode caracterizar trabalho em condição análoga à escravidão.
O coordenador nacional de combate às fraudes trabalhistas do MPT, Rodrigo Castilho, também criticou o programa. Segundo ele, a cobrança pode fazer com que motoristas iniciem suas jornadas já devendo à plataforma.
Leia mais:
- USP e 99 anunciam parceria para pesquisas em IA no Brasil
- 99 lança app de recarga elétrica no RJ que reúne postos de diferentes redes e oferece até 20% de desconto
- 99Premier chega para disputar mercado com Uber Black; veja o que muda
Contrato também é alvo de questionamentos
Outro ponto levantado pelo Ministério Público envolve as condições de adesão ao Taxa Zero. De acordo com a ação, o contrato foi elaborado unilateralmente pela 99, sem possibilidade de negociação pelos motoristas.
O documento também permitiria que a empresa alterasse as regras do programa a qualquer momento e desativasse um passe já adquirido sem devolver os valores pagos.
Para o MPT, o modelo ainda pode prejudicar a concorrência entre aplicativos de transporte. A justificativa é que motoristas que desembolsam dinheiro para aderir ao programa tendem a concentrar suas atividades na 99 para tentar recuperar o investimento.
Na avaliação do órgão, isso funciona como forma indireta de fidelização, reduzindo a liberdade dos trabalhadores para alternar entre plataformas em busca de melhores condições de remuneração.
MPT quer acesso ao algoritmo da 99
Além de pedir a suspensão imediata do Taxa Zero, a devolução dos valores pagos pelos motoristas e a indenização de R$ 100 milhões por danos morais coletivos, o MPT solicitou acesso ao código-fonte do algoritmo da empresa.
O objetivo é examinar os critérios utilizados pela plataforma para distribuir corridas, definir preços e calcular os valores repassados aos trabalhadores.
O processo será analisado pela 1ª Vara do Trabalho de Goiânia.
O que diz a 99
O Olhar Digital entrou em contato com a 99 e aguarda uma resposta oficial sobre o tema.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says it's 'hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI industry is entering a new era, and not just because of its constant stream of new model releases and discoveries. The AI community must now push forward without one of its most influential figures, Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down last week amid several scandals involving affairs with two employees and an alleged Chinese spy, raising potentially far-reaching national security concerns.
Speaking onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and President Greg Brockman each revealed that they had spoken privately with Huang as the embattled former CEO’s public image continued to unravel.
“Jensen took one of the earliest big bets on us. We took a big bet on Nvidia,” Altman said. “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”
OpenAI has worked closely with Huang over the years. Nvidia invested $30 billion in the company earlier this year and designs the chips that power OpenAI’s technology.
Brockman added that he and his wife are friends with Huang’s family, so the couple had reached out “personally, just to be there for him and his family at this time.”
“I think it’s obviously a tough time for everyone, but again, I think Nvidia is such an incredible company,” Brockman said. “I think that… what Jensen has built there, it clearly is built to last, and so we’re excited to keep partnering and looking to the future.”
Huang’s impact on Nvidia and the broader AI industry has been so profound that nearly 200,000 people, including Elon Musk and other influential CEOs, have signed a petition calling for the chipmaker to reinstate him. Nvidia executives said during the company’s earnings call on Tuesday that they do not have plans to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return.
Altman was reticent to weigh in on Huang’s future at Nvidia. When asked whether he thought Huang could return, Altman replied, “One thing I did not appreciate was everybody on Earth speculating with some random theory.”
“I will say, I wish Jensen the best. I wish Nvidia the best,” Altman said. “I don’t think the world needs another set of random opinions on what’s going to happen here.”

articles.title: Chief AI Officers are now a common sight in businesses — but new study finds they often don't really have any power
articles.text:
Chief AI Officers are now a common sight in businesses — but new study finds they often don't really have any power
CAIOs don't actually have much independent responsibility
- IBM study finds CAIOs have become 3x more common in UK businesses in just one year
- Only 16% say they have full control over AI investments
- Successful CAIOs are using business outcomes to identify key investment areas
Chief AI Officers (CAIOs) have become far more common in recent months, with over three-quarters (78%) of UK businesses now having one appointed - compared with a tiny 26% in 2025, according to IBM's latest 2026 CEO Study.
But even though they're given C-suite titles, that doesn't always mean anything, as despite how commonplace the CAIO role has become, only 16% say they have full control over AI investment decisions, with even fewer (11%) having full control over their AI-related workforce strategies, implying other C-suite execs are still holding the reins.
IBM found CAIOs are generally unsatisfied with their business' overall AI readiness too, slating slow action and limited access to resources.
CAIO roles are commonplace, but responsibilities still lie elsewhere
AI policies were also slated in the report – four in five (79%) say their organization has finally defined situations in which human oversight is non-negotiable, but enforcement is lacking with just three in five (58%) saying these are consistently applied.
"Giving AI leaders greater influence over investment, workforce and operating decisions will be critical to turning ambition into action," IBM Consulting UK&I Managing Partner Rhodri Arrowsmith said, stressing the importance of clear and enforced governance.
IBM's report is also one of a long list reporting that AI ambitions could be outpacing actual readiness, with 29% of UK CAIOs worried their organizations have not yet made the changes needed to prepare for widespread transformations. Three in four (73%), as a result, worry that their company could fall behind competitors.
The study also found that the most successful CAIOs were able to reinvest productivity gains back into their wider transformation strategy while also using business outcomes to determine which AI initiatives should receive additional investment in the first place.

articles.title: Chrome 158 Patches 204 Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Google on Tuesday announced the release of Chrome 158 to the stable channel with patches for 204 vulnerabilities, including six critical-severity bugs.
The critical flaws include three use-after-free issues in WebView, GarbageCollection, and WebAudio, out-of-bounds write defects in GPU and ANGLE, and a buffer overflow in Media.
No bug bounty reward will be paid for any of these. In fact, no reward will be handed out for 163 of the security weaknesses. Google and Xinyang Ge discovered 145 and 15 of them, respectively.
Of the remaining vulnerabilities, 62 are high-severity issues, 82 are medium-severity, and 54 are low-severity.
Google says it handed out $11,000 in rewards for five of the vulnerabilities reported by external researchers and has yet to determine the amounts to be paid for 36 flaws.
The most common type of vulnerability patched in Chrome 158 is use-after-free (51 occurrences), followed by incorrect authorization (34), missing authorization (16), out-of-bounds write/read (15), uninitialized resource (14), information leak (11), UI misrepresentation (10), improper input validation (9), and race condition (8).
Google makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to update their browsers as soon as possible.
The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out as versions 158.0.8127.36/.37 for Windows and macOS, and as version 158.0.8127.36 for Linux.

articles.title: Blog Review: Nov. 18
articles.text:
PCIe and trust; rack-scale co-design; heterogeneous scaling; AI data center primer; on-device balancing; EU semi trends.
Cadence’s Rajesh Pamujula considers how to establish trust when sensitive data, proprietary models, cryptographic keys, and confidential workloads increasingly traverse PCIe links.
Synopsys’ Neeraj Paliwal argues that extreme co-design, where silicon, interface IP, memory, cooling, and power are designed together as one system, is needed for efficient racks that are capable of running increasingly demanding AI workloads.
Siemens’ Kevin Rinebold and Andras Vass-Varnai examine the evolving semiconductor design landscape shaped by the shift from monolithic scaling to heterogeneous architectures and consider how to navigate the complexities of AI-driven 3D-IC and chiplet technologies.
Keysight’s Linas Dauksa provides a primer on the technologies that power AI data centers, how they handle training and inference workloads, and why they’ve become the backbone of modern AI.
Arm’s Michael Gamble checks out how to enable gaze-based interactions in lightweight smart glasses by running fast, sensor-dependent AI on-device while larger workloads stay where more compute is available.
SEMI’s Sitong He chats with Patrick Vandenameele of imec about the trends reshaping the semiconductor industry, why collaboration matters more than ever, and the role Europe can play in global competitiveness.
